David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that ISMAEL ROMAN, also known as “Poochie, ” 47, of Hartford, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Sarah F. Russell in New Haven to 60 months of imprisonment and four years of supervised release for a cocaine trafficking offense and for violating the conditions of his supervised release from a prior federal conviction.

According to court documents and statements made in court, in January and February 2026, an investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Hartford Task Force revealed that Jose Colon, also known of “Uncle Benny,” was attempting to purchase several kilograms of cocaine and was in possession of a large amount of cash to complete a purchase. Investigators arranged a meeting with Colon at his residence on Pearl Street in Hartford on February 19, 2026. Prior to the meeting, investigators observed Roman, who was carrying a backpack, and an associate enter Colon’s apartment. Colon, Roman, and their associate were arrested a short time later after a court-authorized search of the residence revealed approximately $52,000 in cash, which had been concealed in a small cooler within the backpack.

Roman has been detained since his arrest. On June 1, 2026, he pleaded guilty to attempting to possess with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of cocaine.

In October 2022, Roman was sentenced in Hartford federal court to 41 months of imprisonment for a cocaine trafficking offense and he was on federal supervised release at the time of his arrest in this case.

Colon pleaded guilty and awaits sentencing.

This investigation is being conducted by the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Hartford Task Force, which includes personnel from the DEA Hartford Resident Office, the Connecticut State Police, and the Bristol, Hartford, East Hartford, Enfield, Manchester, New Britain, Rocky Hill, Wethersfield, and Windsor Locks Police Departments. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Reed Durham.

DOJ’s Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI Expose More than $490M in Tax Fraud in National Tax Enforcement Surge
The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), along with the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation, today announced a nationwide series of enforcement actions targeting tax fraud.
Between early September and today, the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country participated in the Department’s first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge. The surge of nationwide resources resulted in prosecutorial actions against 76 defendants whose alleged and proven crimes intended an estimated loss of revenue to the federal government of more than $490,000,000.
“Every dollar stolen through tax fraud is a dollar taken from the American people,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “What we uncovered during this concentrated surge is only the tip of the iceberg. The Department of Justice is committed to expanding our investigations and exposing schemes designed to evade accountability, because there is no safe haven for fraudsters.”
“The Fraud Division is resolved to protect American taxpayers from criminal actors on every frontier of fraud, including tax fraudsters seeking to steal the wealth of America,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “Over six weeks, the Fraud Division’s Tax Section, 35 U.S. Attorneys' Offices, and IRS Criminal Investigation took action against over 70 defendants who sought more than $490 million from the Treasury. Today’s results send a clear message to fraudsters: those who intentionally lie to steal the money of the American people should expect to answer for their conduct in federal court.”
“This enforcement surge delivered results for taxpayers,” said IRS CEO Frank J. Bisignano. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are working across government to go after fraud, hold bad actors accountable, and protect the integrity of our nation’s tax system.”
“If there was ever any question whether criminal tax enforcement remains a priority, today’s actions should dispel all doubt. These cases send an unmistakable message that individuals and businesses who deliberately cheat the tax system will be held accountable,” said Jarod Koopman, Chief of IRS Criminal Investigation and Chief Tax Compliance Officer. “The investigations announced today involve hundreds of millions in identified tax losses to the United States, funds that should have supported the programs and services Americans depend on every day. When taxpayers evade their legal obligations, the burden does not disappear, it is shifted to law-abiding Americans.”
The Department’s prosecutors returned 23 actions with new charges against 31 defendants. The estimated intended loss to the public fisc arising from the allegations against these defendants exceeds approximately $350,000,000. In addition to returning these new charges, the Fraud Division’s Tax Section and the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices partook in around 39 other enforcement actions — trials, guilty pleas, and sentencings. These events affected another 45 defendants whose actions produced an estimated intended loss of nearly $140,000,000.
National Tax Enforcement Surge Map
Notable Cases
1) United States v. Martin Navarrete (Indictment) – $2,800,000 – District of Maryland
According to the indictment, Navarrete, who served as sole owner and sole corporate officer of Navarrete Brothers Construction Inc. (NBC), exercised significant control and authority over NBC’s finances. Among his responsibilities, Navarrete was tasked with collecting trust-fund taxes, accounting for employment taxes by filing Forms 941 with the IRS and paying the IRS the trust-fund taxes for NBC’s employees.
From September 2020 through December 2025, Navarrete allegedly willfully failed to truthfully account for and pay over the trust-fund taxes owed to the IRS on behalf of NBC’s employees. Additionally, Navarrete willfully failed to file U.S. Corporate Income Tax Return and Individual Tax Return forms for calendar years 2020–2024.
2) United States v. Sherita Booker (Information) – $11,806,165 – Northern District of Ohio
On Sept. 30, Sherita Booker, of Cleveland, was charged with aiding or assisting in the preparation of false and fraudulent federal income tax returns. She allegedly prepared false returns and obtained large, fraudulent refunds for hundreds of clients, primarily using three programs: (1) COVID-19 sick leave credits for non-existent businesses and employees; (2) Refunds of purported fuel taxes paid for off-road (farm) use; and (3) Claims for refunds of taxes purportedly overpaid in previous years.
3) United States v. Marty Allen Linville (Sentencing) – $2,595,679 – Western District of Arkansas
Since at least 2010, Marty Allen Linville, age 58, owned and operated Malco Inc., a trucking business located in De Queen, Arkansas, where he had employees and paid them wages. Linville provided his employees with Forms W-2 that reported withholdings paid to the IRS on their behalf. However, Linville did not separately file the Forms W-2 with the Social Security Administration or make the required tax deposits. More than one employee reported to Linville that their tax return refunds were frozen because no Form W-2 was on file with the IRS. Linville pled guilty to 2 counts of Willful Failure to Account for and Pay Over Trust Fund Taxes. Linville was sentenced to 20 months imprisonment and ordered to pay restitution, including penalties and interest, in the amount of $3.8 million.
4) United States vs. Duncan John MacDonald, Sarah Duren, Richard Ronald Cayce, and Thomas Weickgenant (Indictment) – $200,000,000 – Northern District of Texas
Four Texas residents charged with conspiracy to defraud the United States and other crimes for promoting an illegal tax shelter. According to the indictment, the defendants promoted and sold a fraudulent trust scheme that was used to shelter more than $1.5 billion of income, causing an estimated tax loss to the IRS of more than $200 million. The defendants allegedly sold clients the tax shelter for fees that often exceeded $100,000 by fraudulently telling clients that they could assign their income to sham trusts to defer paying taxes in perpetuity, all while continuing to enjoy the benefit and control over their assets and income. The defendants also allegedly encouraged some clients to backdate their trusts and file amended income tax returns claiming refunds for prior years’ taxes.
5) United States v. Ephantus Mwangi (Sentencing) – $1,500,000 – District of Kansas
A Kenyan national and Missouri businessman was sentenced to 51 months in prison for willfully failing to pay over employment taxes to the IRS on behalf of the credit-card processing services companies he owned and operated. During this time, he spent more than $200,000 on loan payments for various luxury vehicles, including a Hummer H2, a Cadillac Escalade, two Range Rovers, two Mercedes, and a Lexus. He also willfully failed to file individual income tax returns for the years 2017 and 2020, and he filed 2018 and 2019 individual income tax returns after the deadline had passed.
6) United States v. Nelai Mitchell (Sentencing) – $13,800,000 – Eastern District of North Carolina
Nejlai Mitchell, an owner of a North Carolina tax return preparation business was sentenced to 60 months in prison for conspiring to prepare false returns claiming fraudulent refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits. From approximately April 2022 through May 2023, Mitchell and seven employees filed false tax returns seeking fraudulent refunds based on the paid sick and family leave credit, a credit passed by Congress to aid struggling businesses during the COVID-19 global pandemic. The conspiracy resulted in a total of approximately $23.9 million in fraudulent tax refund claims. The IRS paid out approximately $13,890,697 of that amount.
Five other return preparers were sentenced for their roles in the scheme. On Sept. 3, Tiffany Moody was sentenced to 26 months in prison. On July 8, Shaneen Ray was sentenced to 18 months in prison, Eyoubo McBurney was sentenced to 18 months in prison, and Sylvia Swindell was sentenced to 16 months in prison. On July 9, Katrena Stanback was sentenced to six months in prison.
7) United States v. Gustavo Rojano Salazar, Gabriel Rojano Salazar, and Andres Huerta Rendon (Indictment) – $74,000,000 – Northern District of Georgia
Two brothers and a third man were charged with conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, mail fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering, all arising out of a $74 million scheme to defraud the IRS through the filing of fraudulent tax returns. According to the indictment, the three men, who are Mexican citizens, obtained Mexican identification documents in the names of third parties. They used these identification documents to obtain Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN) with the IRS used by an individual who was required to file a federal tax return, but who did not have or was not eligible to receive a Social Security number. After receiving the ITIN information, the co-conspirators prepared and filed fraudulent tax returns in the names of the Mexican ITIN holders. Each of these returns resulted in refunds, which the co-conspirators directed to be mailed to post office boxes they controlled. The co-conspirators then collected the resulting U.S. Treasury refund checks issued in the names of the Mexican ITIN holders and cashed them using a check cashing company. In total, the three co-conspirators and others cashed more than 16,000 U.S. Treasury tax refund checks worth over $74 million.
8) United States v. Pedro Cabrajal (Indictment) - $4,900,000 – District of New Jersey
New Jersey man charged with willful failure to account for and pay over employment taxes, tax evasion and willful failure to file income tax returns. According to the indictment, from 2012 to 2020, Pedro Carbajal, of Sparta, New Jersey, operated Option Staffing Services LLC, an employee-leasing business that was nominally owned by another individual. During this period, Carbajal allegedly did not file quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS or pay the required trust fund and unemployment taxes on behalf of his company’s employees. Carbajal allegedly failed to pay over a total of approximately $4.9 million in taxes to the IRS.
9) United States v. Jose Da Costa Gomez (Indictment) – No public loss announced – Southern District of Florida
Business owner charged with conspiracy to defraud the United States, filing false tax returns with the IRS, wire fraud conspiracy and wire fraud. According to the indictment, Da Costa Gomez was the owner of a series of businesses Da Costa Gomez and his family members allegedly used the companies’ funds to pay tens of millions of dollars of personal expenses and failed to report those payments as income to the Internal Revenue Service. Da Costa Gomez and others also allegedly evaded Florida sales and use taxes on purchases by having items shipped out of Florida and then surreptitiously bringing them back to the state or submitting false resale certificates to sellers.
10) United States v. John Labee (Indictment) – $6,900,000 – Western District of Texas
Defendant charged with conspiring to file false claims and filing false claims. From approximately October 2021 through July 2022, Labee and co-conspirator Andrea Dotson allegedly agreed to have Labee prepare and file false tax returns on behalf of Dotson’s business, Divine Grinde. Although Divine Grinde had minimal operations and no employees, Labee and Dotson allegedly conspired to file nine false tax returns that falsely claimed the Employee Retention Credit and the Sick and Family Leave Credit based on completely fabricated wage and tax figures. Dotson previously pleaded guilty on March 10, 2026, for her role in the offense. In total, Labee and Dotson’s fraudulent claims sought refunds of approximately $6.9 million, of which the IRS paid over $1.1 million. Dotson kept a portion of the tax refunds for herself and allegedly provided the remainder to Labee.
11) United States v. Pacifique Kashosi (Trial) – Loss to be determined at sentencing – District of Arizona
Phoenix tax preparer convicted at trial for aiding and assisting in the filing of false tax returns and filing false personal income tax returns. Kashosi prepared false tax returns for his clients that reported false Covid tax credits, false fuel credits and false business losses. The false tax returns claimed thousands of dollars in fraudulent refunds. In cases like this one, the intended loss is often millions of dollars and can result in significant prison time.
12) United States v. Marquis Al Bey (Guilty Plea) – $35,000,000 – District of Maryland
Marquis Al Bey, of Forney, Texas, pleaded guilty on Sept. 17, for his role in a tax refund fraud conspiracy that sought to obtain more than $35 million in fraudulent refunds through the filing of false tax returns. Bey prepared tax returns for clients, including clients located in Maryland, that sought large tax refunds that the individuals and entities listed on the returns were not entitled to receive. Bey charged clients for his tax return preparation services and, in some cases, required that clients agree to pay him a percentage of any resulting refund. As part of his plea, Bey admitted to preparing seven false returns between 2017 and 2021 for his co-defendant and another individual in Maryland that collectively sought more than $35 million from the Internal Revenue Service. Two of those returns resulted in the IRS issuing refunds totaling more than $10 million to Bey’s clients.
13) United States v. LaMar Dazjar Burgess and LaMar Javis Burgess (Guilty Pleas) – $9,200,000 – District of Minnesota
Father and son, LaMar Javis Burgess and son LaMar Dazjar Burgess, participated in a scheme to fraudulently obtain tax refunds by filing false income tax returns based primarily on COVID-related sick and family leave credits, fuel tax credits, and false withholdings. For tax years 2022 and 2023 Javis and his son prepared and/or filed at least 300 false income tax returns claiming at least $9.2 million in fraudulent refunds.
14) United States v. Ronald Chrichlow and Gordon Chrichlow (Guilty Pleas) – $978,126 and $1,643,172 – District of New Jersey
Two brothers plead guilty to stealing more than $978,126 and $1,643,172, respectively, in tax refunds. Ronald Chrichlow and Gordon Chrichlow both filed a false 2022 Form 1041, U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts, on behalf of their trusts. These Forms 1041 falsely reported that the trusts made tax payments to the IRS when they had not and claimed refunds as a result. In response to IRS collection efforts, the Chrichlow brothers mailed forms to the IRS on which they falsely claimed not to be residents of the United States and falsely claimed that their 2022 income was tax exempt pursuant to a tax treaty. The Chrichlow brothers also failed to file their personal income tax returns in some years, despite earning income and being legally obligated to file.
15) United States v. Lakeibia Fannin (Sentencing) – $1,400,000 – District of Nevada
Illinois woman sentenced to 13 months in prison for conspiring to defraud the United States by making false claims for refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits. Lakeibia Fannin conspired with others, including Candies Goode-McCoy, from June 2022 through November 2023 to file tax returns seeking fraudulent refunds based on false Employee Retention Credits and Sick and Family Leave Credits. Fannin and her businesses were not eligible to receive these refundable credits in the amounts claimed. In total, Fannin claimed more than $3.5 million in fraudulent refunds, of which more than $1.4 million were paid.
16) United States v. McDonald Preval (Sentencing) – $4,200,000 – Southern District of Florida
Florida man was sentenced to 36 months in prison for filing a false tax return on behalf of a trust he controlled as part of a $4.2 million refund fraud scheme.
McDonald Preval, of Miami, filed a number of false tax returns for himself and trusts he claimed to control. The trust tax returns reported that the trusts had earned significant income and made tax withholding payments to the IRS, purportedly entitling the trusts to large tax refunds. In fact, the trusts did not have the claimed income and did not make payments in the amounts claimed on the returns and therefore were not entitled to the refunds Preval claimed. He also filed tax returns for 2023 that did not include the income from his employment. The false tax returns Preval caused to be filed on behalf of purported trusts and himself collectively sought tax refunds totaling more than $4.2 million. Preval obtained more than $580,000 from his scheme, which he used to pay off the mortgage loan on his house and other personal expenses.

RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced that a jury has convicted Brandon Brave Heart, age 42, of Kyle, South Dakota, of Assault by Striking, Beating, or Wounding and Simple Assault following a two-day jury trial in federal district court in Rapid City, South Dakota. The verdict was returned on October 8, 2026.

The charges carry a maximum penalty of one year in custody and/or a $100,000 fine, one year of supervised release, and a $25 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Brave Heart was indicted for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury and Assault with a Dangerous Weapon by a federal grand jury in September 2024.

On July 23, 2024, shortly before 7:30 pm, the victim and his family were at the Common Cents convenience store located at Sharp’s Corner near Kyle, SD. The victim had his back to the door when Brave Heart entered the store. Brave Heart walked towards the victim from behind and struck him with a closed fist in the back of the head. The victim fell to the ground, and Brave Heart continued to strike the victim. During the assault, Brave Heart used fists to punch the victim and his tennis shoes to kick the victim twice in the face.

This matter is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office because the Major Crimes Act, a federal statute, mandates that certain violent crimes alleged to have occurred in Indian Country be prosecuted in Federal court as opposed to State court.

This case was investigated by the Oglala Sioux Tribe Department of Public Safety Criminal Investigations Division. Assistant U.S. Attorney Abby VanDenBerg prosecuted the case.

A presentence investigation was ordered, and a sentencing date has yet to be set.

ATLANTA – Dye’Shuan Green, who pressured girls as young as nine years old to send him sexually explicit photos and videos online, has been sentenced to nearly 17 years in federal prison for production of child sexual abuse material.

“The Court’s sentence holds a predator accountable for his reprehensible acts and ensures he won’t victimize another child for most of the next two decades,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg, “This case also serves as a reminder to parents and caretakers about the dangers deviant criminals like Green pose to young people online.”

“Posing as a child and then pressuring children, among the most vulnerable members of our society, to produce sexually explicit and harmful material is unconscionable,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “The FBI, alongside our local, state, and federal partners, will relentlessly work to bring justice to the victims and their families.”

According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: In 2022, a mother in Columbus, Georgia reported to the Columbus Police Department that her daughter had been manipulated by a man, who was posing as a child online, to send nude images of herself. The FBI then conducted a multi-year investigation, which revealed that Green had preyed on young girls across the country.

The investigation established that Green targeted young girls on social media and gaming sites and pretended that he was a boy their age. Green befriended them, convinced them that he loved them and wanted a relationship with them, and discussed having sex with them. Green then relentlessly begged and threatened victims to produce sexually explicit photos of themselves to send him, and many girls sent nude images to him. A review of Green’s phone and social media accounts showed that he chatted online with hundreds of young girls as part of his scheme.

On October 13, 2026, U.S. District Judge Sarah E. Geraghty sentenced Dye’Shuan Green, 23, of College Park, Georgia, to 16 years, 10 months in prison to be followed by 15 years of supervised release. Green pleaded guilty to one count of production of child sexual abuse material and four counts of enticement to create child sexual abuse material on June 29, 2026.

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with valuable assistance provided by the Columbus Police Department.

Assistant United States Attorneys Matthew R. LaGrone and Leanne M. Marek prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood. In February 2006, the Attorney General launched Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from online exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices around the country, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov.

For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga .

ICYMI: Director Kupor Discusses Responsible SI Leadership on Fox News’ Saturday in America
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Director Scott Kupor, Vice Chair of the Super Intelligence Task Force, joined Kayleigh McEnany on Fox News’ Saturday in America to discuss the task force’s work, the importance of U.S. leadership in SI, and the responsibility of technology companies to develop and release safe products.
On the task force’s dual mandate:
“We’ve got a dual mandate here. The President has been very clear that this is a race we are winning and need to win, and that it’s critical to Americans’ economic and national security for Americans. But he’s also said we have to do so responsibly. That’s a lot of what we’ve been discussing at the task force: How do we allow the technology to continue in and appropriate way while also protecting the best interests of the American people? I’m absolutely confident we can square those two goals.”
On addressing SI safety risks:
“Those very same people were also predicting a jobs apocalypse about 18 months ago. The opposite has happened: We’ve actually had a huge increase in jobs as a result of SI.
“Nonetheless, we take this seriously. The answer, though, is not to slow down or pause. That’s the absolute worst thing we can do. All that does is inure to the benefit of our adversaries, China foremost among them.
“We’ve been very clear with [model providers] that they have a key fundamental responsibility to put out safe products. If they deem a product isn’t safe, the answer is to slow its release, not put it out and just pray for good times.”
On company responsibility and incident response:
“Companies have a responsibility from a technology perspective to develop the security tools. Second, they have an obligation to respond and notify the government when these things happen. In cases like the Philadelphia one you mentioned, those are things that should have happened immediately. We’ve been very clear with those vendors that they need to do that and be an active part of remediation if something happens.
“A lot of this is about setting the right expectations with companies, making sure the government has all the information it needs, and making sure other critical infrastructure providers, like financial services companies, are fully in the loop if something happens.”
On the risk of falling behind:
“We believe this is the most important economic and national sovereignty tool that will govern international relationships for the next 30, 40, 50 years. If we lose this race to China, or suspend or slow down our efforts, all we do is encourage an adversary to have economic control over our future, as well as control over our national sovereignty and security control.
“I’m confident there’s a way to square these two problems: winning the race and doing so in a responsible way.”
title: ICYMI: Director Kupor Discusses Responsible SI Leadership on Fox News’ Saturday in America

text:
Navy Flies Drones Without GPS, Lands Autonomously on Moving Ships
NAVAL AIR WARFARE CENTER AIRCRAFT DIVISION, PATUXENT RIVER, Md. — The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) successfully proved an unmanned system can navigate missions and land aboard Navy ships without GPS or pilot control.
“In contested areas where satellites and communications are jammed, autonomy gives significant advantage to our sailors,” said NAWCAD Commander Rear Adm. Todd Evans. “Breakthroughs like this help us scale unmanned capability fast and affordably across a distributed fleet.”
The live-flight demonstration proved that a tactical drone can fly mission tasks and execute recoveries on a pitching vessel at sea – even when satellite navigation is jammed or unavailable – by using its own commercial-standard cameras, motion sensors, and electronics.
“In a high-end maritime conflict, GPS is the first operational link an adversary attempts to sever,” said NAWCAD aerospace engineer Peter Arslanian. “By developing a modular adaptable system and putting it directly onto a UAS, we expand where and how the fleet can deploy unmanned systems with a simple software upgrade rather than expensive modifications to space-constrained ships.”
Traditional UAS landings rely on multimillion-dollar radar systems, recovery gear for the flight deck, and ship modifications that can take months to install. NAWCAD’s software-driven approach replaces that hardware by pairing an unmanned system’s mission sensors such as cameras with advanced guidance, navigation, and control software developed by the warfare center’s Maritime Autonomous Guidance-Navigation-Control Intelligent Coupled Systems Lab.
In flight, the UAS uses its camera to recognize a ship’s shape and visual cues to guide its flight path like a human pilot, while its guidance and control algorithms predict the ship's rising and falling deck in real time so the aircraft can touch down smoothly. The software works with nearly any UAS computer hardware and can scale across unmanned systems of all sizes, from small tactical quadcopters to large, combat-class aircraft.
With initial flight demonstrations complete, the software is ready for operational testing on fleet platforms. NAWCAD plans to scale the technology to larger unmanned systems, including tactical resupply drones, and is working with program offices to transition the capability into acquisition pipelines at the Navy’s Small Tactical Unmanned Aircraft Systems program office, the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program, and DARPA’s EVADE project.
The project was funded through the Naval Innovative Science and Engineering Program and the Office of Naval Research.
NAWCAD employs military, civilian, and contract personnel to operate test ranges, laboratories, and aircraft in support of test, evaluation, research, development, and sustainment for all Navy and Marine Corps aviation platforms. Based in Patuxent River, Maryland, NAWCAD also has major sites in St. Inigoes, Maryland; Lakehurst, New Jersey; and Orlando, Florida.
#
title: Navy Flies Drones Without GPS, Lands Autonomously on Moving Ships

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Josh Riley (NY-19) introduced the Ad-Free Means Ad-Free Act, legislation to crack down on streaming companies that promise customers commercial-free viewing, then change the rules and force them to sit through advertisements.
Many digital streaming platforms that built massive user bases on promises of commercial-free viewing have later added advertisement to their default tiers for both live and on-demand programming. For example, RedZone – the NFL’s popular streaming service – recently announced it would broadcast advertisements for the first time in its 17-year history. Outraged fans viewed the change as a bait-and-switch that fundamentally breached the ad-free experience they had already purchased.
“If you pay for ad-free, you should get ad-free. It’s that simple,” Riley said. “For years, football fans were promised seven hours of commercial-free football. Now the big streaming companies are moving the goalposts to squeeze even more money out of hardworking people. Upstate New Yorkers are sick and tired of getting ripped off. My bill makes these companies honor their promises and gives fans what they paid for.”
RedZone is not alone in its change from an ad-free model. Across the industry, major streaming platforms are introducing commercials into previously ad-free tiers, often forcing users to pay an additional surcharge to restore the uninterrupted experience they originally signed up for. The Ad-Free Means Ad-Free Act would prohibit streaming services from adding commercials to paid subscriptions originally advertised or offered as commercial-free within one year or the length of the original contract.
The Ad-Free Means Ad-Free Act is endorsed by the Sports Fans Coalition.
“If sports fans pay extra to watch games without additional commercial interruptions, they should get what they pay for – no ads. We thank Congressman Josh Riley for throwing the flag on the bait-and-switch some streaming services are pulling on fans,” said David Goodfriend, Chair of the Sports Fans Coalition.
You can read the text of the legislation HERE.
###
title: RILEY TAKES ON STREAMING GIANTS WITH BILL TO END AD-FREE BAIT-AND-SWITCH

text:
Congressmen Carter, Thompson Visit Nation’s Largest Permanent ICE Migrant Detention Facility
NATCHEZ, MS – Today, Rep. Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, and Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA), Committee Member, released the below statement on their surprise oversight visit yesterday to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facility at Adams County Correctional Center (ACCC) in Mississippi, the nation’s largest migrant detention facility.
“One of Congress’ primary responsibilities is oversight of federal agencies, and we exercised that power – and legal right – in an unannounced visit to ACCC after a summer of crises, protests, and power outages. We wanted an unvarnished look at the institution to make sure that facility problems highlighted in correspondence our offices and in public inspection reports are being addressed, and that everyone in the facility has access to their constitutional due process rights. Regardless of a person’s station in life, they are still human and deserve safe shelter with adequate, sanitary food and water, and access to health care.
“We continue to have concerns that detainees aren’t able to obtain access to adequate mental health services, a full understanding of what crimes they are charged with, and transparency and accountability for when ACCC staff fail in upholding their constitutional rights. As the Trump administration continues to weaponize ICE against communities across the country, we will continue rigorous oversight of immigrant detention facilities so that the law is followed and immigrants have access to their full constitutional rights.”
Background
Adams County Correctional Center (ACCC), operated by the private prison company CoreCivic, is the largest permanent immigration detention facility in the U.S. and detains an average of 1,878 men daily.
In the past six months, ACCC and the men detained there have experienced multiple crises. In May 2026, ICE’s Office of Detention Oversight inspected ACCC and downgraded the facility from a “Superior” rating to “Acceptable/Adequate,” with only 24 of 28 standards met. In July, nearly 70 detainees submitted a petition to the warden demanding an end to the practice of placing three detainees in cells meant to hold two people. During the week of August 10, 2026, a lengthy power outage at ACCC left detainees without air conditioning for two days in nearly 100-degree heat. On August 22, 2026, around 100 male detainees started a protest over poor living conditions, spoiled food, and meager rations.
title: Congressmen Carter, Thompson Visit Nation’s Largest Permanent ICE Migrant Detention Facility

SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) and Emily Randall (WA-06) are leading Members from Washington and Oregon in demanding answers and transparency into ongoing efforts by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to purchase existing immigration detention centers currently owned and operated by private prison companies like GEO Group and CoreCivic. Currently, the GEO Group contract with the Northwest Detention Center (NWDC) is set to expire in October 2026.
Earlier this summer, ICE purchased two CoreCivic detention centers in California for $1.5 billion and facilities in Kansas and Minnesota for $734 million. Despite these facilities having been purchased by ICE, CoreCivic will continue managing operations. In October, ICE purchased three detention facilities in Adelanto, California, from GEO Group for $950 million. Similarly, GEO will continue running the facilities and says ICE is considering buying 10 facilities or more from the company.
“We are deeply concerned about the potential purchase of these facilities, as it appears to be an attempt to circumvent oversight and accountability at detention facilities. Both GEO Group and DHS have stated that acquiring these facilities is aimed, at least in part, at circumventing attempts by states to conduct oversight at immigration detention centers located within their borders,” wrote the Members.
Any attempt to dodge oversight is particularly troubling at the NWDC, as Washington State recently had to go to court to ensure access to the facility for state Department of Health officials. There is serious cause for concern if this purchase is being made to shield ICE and GEO from oversight efforts by putting the facility under federal ownership.
There are also troubling financial incentives. Under the Trump administration, GEO and CoreCivic have reaped enormous financial benefits. In 2025, both companies received an additional $2 billion in profit each, a 13 percent increase in revenue, and there has been a revolving door between the Trump administration and these companies — including border czar Tom Homan and Acting ICE Director David Venturella, who were previously employed by GEO.
“As of March 2026, the Washington State Department of Health received over 3,500 complaints about [NWDC]. Individuals have reported being sexually assaulted by an officer in their unit; unsanitary conditions, including unclean drinking water, worms, hair, and metal in food, and black mold in showers; and insufficient medical care. State oversight is an essential way to help ensure that the people detained in these facilities at U.S. taxpayer expense are being treated with dignity. Attempting to circumvent such oversight by purchasing substandard detention facilities and continuing to allow such inhumane conditions to persist is unacceptable,” continued the Members.
The full text of the letter can be found here.
The letter was also signed by Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle S. Bynum (OR-05), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Kim Schrier (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10).
Issues: Immigration
title: Jayapal, Randall Lead PNW Members in Demanding Answers on NWDC Contract

text:
Proposed Rules Implement Working Families Tax Cuts Reforms to Prevent Fraud and Abuse of the Premium Tax Credit
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) issued proposed regulations to implement President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts reforms to the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), a refundable tax credit that helps eligible American taxpayers afford health insurance purchased through the Health Insurance Exchanges.
“Hardworking American taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize health care for people who are ineligible under federal law,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Today’s proposed rules implement the common-sense reforms enacted by the Working Families Tax Cuts to close eligibility loopholes and ensure taxpayer-funded Premium Tax Credits are reserved for eligible Americans. Under President Trump, this Administration is cracking down on fraud and corruption; holding bad actors accountable; lowering health care costs for Americans; and restoring integrity to our tax code and health care system.”
“The proposed rules protect eligible taxpayers while strengthening the integrity of the Premium Tax Credit,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “The enhanced verification measures are designed to curb improper claims, ensuring these vital tax benefits go strictly to the hardworking Americans who qualify for them.”
“The Trump Administration’s whole-of-government approach to fighting fraud, waste, and abuse is built on the idea that an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “Ensuring health programs serve only those who are eligible is one of the most effective ways to protect these programs and the taxpayers who support them. With today’s proposed rules, the Treasury Department is taking another step forward in our collaborative effort to protect taxpayer dollars by shutting down waste and fraud before a single dollar leaves the building.”
PROTECTING TAXPAYER-FUNDED BENEFITS FOR ELIGIBLE AMERICANS
The proposed rules put the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Premium Tax Credit reforms into effect which strengthen eligibility checks, close gaps in the verification process, and help ensure taxpayer-funded subsidies go only to eligible American taxpayers.
The Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud exposed the need for stronger safeguards to protect the integrity of the Federal Marketplace. As part of that work, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced the removal of more than 760,000 unverified “phantom” enrollees from the rolls of the Affordable Care Act (ACA), resulting in $2.2 billion in savings and sending nearly 1 million Americans $500 each who had been overcharged for their Obamacare coverage by the Biden Administration.
The Treasury and IRS proposed rules:
- Strengthen Eligibility Standards: Beginning in 2027, ensures taxpayer-funded health insurance subsidies go only to Americans who qualify under federal law.
- Protect Taxpayer Benefits for Eligible Americans: Restricts PTC eligibility to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and certain lawfully present noncitizens.
- Close Verification Gaps: Applies commonsense PTC eligibility checks and adds new verification criteria for any advance PTC payments.
The proposed regulations are available here.
The changes to Exchange procedures and operations necessary to implement the verification requirements are expected to be addressed in parallel proposed regulations issued by HHS under related provisions of the same statute.
###
title: Treasury and IRS Move to Protect Health Care Benefits for Eligible Americans

text:
FBI Operation Summer Heat 2.0 Nets Thousands of Violent Crime Arrests
In four months, the violent crime initiative also seized enough fentanyl to kill 52 million people
The FBI and its law enforcement partners are announcing the results of Summer Heat 2.0, a four-month violent crime initiative that resulted in 8,927 arrests, the seizure of deadly fentanyl and cocaine, and 5,013 dangerous illegally possessed weapons taken off American streets.
“This year’s Summer Heat was our second straight nationwide offensive to crush violent crime all over the country, and the results were outstanding,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Even after last year’s unprecedented numbers, all 56 FBI field offices stepped up and delivered even higher numbers this year—arresting almost 9,000 subjects, up 3% from Summer Heat last year; seizing 63% more fentanyl; identifying or locating 1,410 children, 34% higher than last year; and recovering over 5,000 weapons, up 120% from 2025. Major cities across America saw increases as high as 80% in arrests compared to last summer alone. When this FBI elevated ‘crushing violent crime’ to one of our top priorities, we moved 2,000 FBI personnel out of Washington and permanently into the field—making the decisive call to go on offense. This FBI isn’t waiting for violent criminals, drug traffickers, and weapons dealers to devastate our communities any longer. As a result, under the Trump administration’s leadership, we have achieved the most prolific reduction in violent crime in U.S. history.” 
Between June 1 and September 20, the FBI and its 56 field offices surged resources alongside state and local partners to execute federal warrants on violent criminals and fugitives, dismantle violent gangs and transnational criminal organizations, identify and rescue child victims, and resolve violent crime cases in Indian Country.  
The FBI’s Summer Heat 2.0 initiative achieved additional victories with 687 kilograms of fentanyl seized: an amount equal to 52 million lethal doses. Of the 8,927 arrests, more than 5,900 arrests fell under the FBI’s violent crime and gang program.
A Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) takedown across two states, Operation Turf War, kicked off the FBI’s 2026 Summer Heat initiative. FBI Pittsburgh, in coordination with West Virginia’s HSTF, netted 32 narcotics and weapons-related arrests. In a separate effort in July 2026, FBI Los Angeles executed 17 federal arrest warrants and 49 search warrants in connection with Operation Hard Ball. The operation united FBI Los Angeles with law enforcement from Canada and Europe to investigate an organized crime group accused of a litany of criminal acts. And in yet another example of the success of Operation Summer Heat, FBI San Juan and its partners led Operation Taking Back West, which resulted in the indictment of 81 members of a violent criminal gang.  
The FBI first launched the Summer Heat initiative for three months in 2025 to deploy a multi-pronged offensive to crush violent crime. The announcement of Operation Summer Heat 2.0 results follows on the heels of historic drops in crime across the U.S., according to the FBI’s 2025 UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation.
title: FBI Operation Summer Heat 2.0 Nets Thousands of Violent Crime Arrests

Today, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) announced the next step in its work to advance President Trump’s fight against the debanking of businesses and individuals on the basis of their constitutionally protected rights, including support of President Trump, MAGA, pro-life causes, and industries disfavored by the Left. The CFPB will address any consumer harm caused by the nation’s largest banks in response to the Report on debanking practices by Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The OCC report, “Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans,” found that the nine largest national banks under its supervision – JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo Bank, U.S. Bank, Capital One, PNC Bank, TD Bank, and BMO Bank – maintained policies or engaged in practices that denied or restricted financial access on the basis of Americans’ political or religious beliefs or a customer’s otherwise lawful business activities. The OCC report provides excerpts from bank documents, including emails, revealing this biased and discriminatory decision-making. The report shows that entire sectors were victims of debanking, most notably those related to firearms, oil and gas, and tobacco.
“It is appalling that these banks targeted American consumers for their political, social, or religious beliefs that did not align with the Biden Administration or its leftist allies. Many of those targeted were supporters of President Trump. These thuggish tactics, which were also a defining feature of the Biden-Chopra CFPB, have no place in America,” said CFPB’s Acting Director Mark Paoletta. “We thank the Department of the Treasury and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for conducting its review to shed light on these shameful practices. The CFPB will fully investigate whether the institutions featured in OCC’s report and others have complied with federal consumer financial laws and take appropriate action.” The CFPB holds primary supervisory and enforcement authority for banks with over $10 billion in assets, including these banks, as well as certain nonbank financial institutions to assess their compliance with federal consumer financial laws.
The CFPB’s announcement is part of the agency’s latest undertaking to implement Executive Order  14331, “Guaranteeing Fair Access to Banking for All Americans,” and advance its priority to vigorously remedy debanking. The CFPB evaluates financial institutions for compliance with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) and Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), particularly the adverse action notice requirements under these laws, and Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices (UDAAP), and opens investigations when warranted. Previously, the CFPB reviewed its Examination Manual, guidance, regulations, and other materials used to regulate or examine financial institutions under its authority to ensure that they do not contain reputation risk concepts that could result in unlawful debanking. The CFPB has also been reviewing consumer complaints, as well as supervisory and enforcement data, for evidence of potential unlawful debanking, and is pursuing its own investigations, based on that data.
The CFPB recently updated its website and complaint portal with information to raise awareness about debanking, and continues to encourage consumers to submit complaints if they believe they have been debanked.
title: CFPB Announces New Initiative to Address OCC-Uncovered Debanking by Large Banks

Tennessee Woman Pleads Guilty to Preparing False Tax Returns
A Tennessee woman pleaded guilty today to preparing false tax returns for others and willfully failing to file her own tax returns.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Lynette Hogue prepared and filed with the IRS false income tax returns for clients of the tax preparation business where she worked. These tax returns contained false and fraudulent items, which generated refunds the clients were not entitled to receive. Hogue also willfully failed to file her own tax returns, even though she earned substantial income from her tax return preparation business and was required by law to file. In total, Hogue’s conduct caused a loss to the IRS of $4.1 million.
Hogue pleaded guilty to one count of willfully aiding and assisting the filing of a false tax return and one count of willfully failing to file an individual tax return. She is scheduled to be sentenced on January 15, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of three years in prison for aiding and assisting the filing of a false return and one year in prison for filing a false individual return. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant for the Western District of Tennessee made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorneys Isaiah Boyd III and Matthew C. Hicks of the Fraud Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Carroll L. André III for the Western District of Tennessee are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Tennessee Woman Pleads Guilty to Preparing False Tax Returns

Memphis Safe Task Force Arrests 34 Tuesday, Recovers 6 Guns
For immediate release
Office of Public Affairs
Usms.mediadesk@usdoj.gov
MEMPHIS - The Memphis Safe Task Force (MSTF) on Tuesday executed 34 arrests, including one man who had an outstanding warrant for aggravated rape, and recovered six illegal firearms.
Of note:
Christopher Harris, 38, was arrested in the 3800 block of Democrat Road on an outstanding warrant for aggravated rape. Harris was with a woman who claimed he’d kidnapped her and who told MSTF officers that Harris was in the process of raping her before they arrived. A search warrant for the vehicle was prepared and charges for kidnapping and rape are pending. Harris was transported to the Memphis Police Department (MPD) for interview by the MPD sex crimes unit.
Jalen Pierce, 25, was arrested at the intersection of Roland Street and Fleetwood Avenue and charged with aggravated assault /theft of property. MSTF recovered an unknown amount of marijuana, drug paraphernalia, and a Glock 19 handgun outfitted with a Machine Gun Conversion Device, which is illegal throughout Tennessee.
Paul Guy, 52, was arrested at the intersection of West Byfield and Horn Lake Road on an outstanding warrant for possession of cocaine. Subsequent search warrants yielded more than 70 pounds of marijuana and $40,000 in cash.
Juan Leal-Nunez, 25, was arrested at the Greyhound bus station and charged with possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine after he gave consent to MSTF to search his luggage which revealed approximately 43.5 pounds of methamphetamine. Leal-Nunez was booked at Shelby County jail.
Dontavious Simpson, 32, was arrested at an apartment complex in the 6500 block of Ballantrace Court, charged with possession of a controlled substance with intent to manufacture/deliver narcotics. Officers recovered approximately 2 pounds of marijuana, approximately $1,150 in U.S. currency, a Glock 27 handgun and various firearms components (conversion kit and high-capacity magazines). Simpson was processed at the Shelby County Sheriff's Office.
On Monday night, MSTF conducted a traffic stop at Overton Crossing and Pamela Drive of a vehicle for a moving violation that was also suspected of containing narcotics. At the stop, Tennessee Highway Patrol officers interviewed the driver and secured the driver’s license. Upon return to the suspect’s vehicle, the trooper discovered him to be unresponsive. CPR was performed by personnel on scene and medics were requested. The suspect was transported to the hospital where he was later pronounced deceased. A K9 unit made a positive alert on the vehicle, and a subsequent vehicle search led to the discovery of 3 pounds of marijuana, which was seized.
Since the launch of the Memphis Safe Task Force initiative, officers have made 13,569 arrests, including 142 for homicide, 1,460 for controlled substances, 1,335 for firearms violations, and 126 for sex offenses. Of those arrested, 433 were juveniles and 1,518 were known gang members. The task force has seized 2,283 illegal firearms. These enforcement actions reflect a sustained commitment to reducing violent crime and removing dangerous weapons from Memphis neighborhoods.
The Memphis Safe Task Force is a multi-agency initiative established via a Presidential Memorandum signed by President Donald Trump on Sept. 15, 2025. Aimed at addressing violent street crime, the task force coordinates federal, state, and local law enforcement and includes mobilized members of the Tennessee National Guard. The MSTF is focused on arresting violent criminals, clearing warrants, seizing firearms, and locating missing children. Since the operation began, the MSTF has located 196 missing children.
This operation reflects the MSTF’s commitment to coordinated enforcement efforts and its mission to identify, apprehend, and hold accountable those who pose a threat to public safety.

NAPERVILLE, Ill. — The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has begun a special inspection at the Dresden Nuclear Power Station in Morris, Illinois, after plant staff found a corroded battery connection that broke during maintenance. Constellation Energy operates the two-unit plant.
The battery is part of a backup power system that supports equipment used to safely shut down the reactor. The issue did not affect public health and safety.
The NRC determined a special inspection was warranted because the damage was not caught during routine checks, and similar battery problems have occurred at other nuclear plants.
“An independent NRC review will help us understand how this battery issue developed and whether improvements are needed,” Region III Administrator Mohammed Shuaibi said. “We’re committed to ensuring the plant’s oversight processes remain strong and that similar problems are prevented at other facilities.”
A team of two NRC inspectors will look at how the damage happened, whether the plant’s regular inspections should have found it sooner, how the plant responded, and whether other plants could face a similar issue.
Once the inspection is complete, NRC inspectors will document their findings in a publicly available inspection report, which will be distributed electronically to listserv subscribers and posted on the NRC website.
title: NRC Begins Special Inspection at Dresden Nuclear Power Plant

Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) highlighted the awarding of $142,330,091 in federal funding to Massachusetts through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP). The early allocation follows Trahan’s request for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to release Massachusetts’ LIHEAP funding before the end of the month to combat surging home heating costs.
“No family in Massachusetts should have to choose between heating their home and affording groceries or medicine,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “With heating oil prices up nearly 75 percent from last year, that choice is becoming a reality for far too many households. Releasing these funds early will help families prepare for the winter ahead. But this year’s allocation falls short of last year’s at a time when the need is greater than ever. Congress must act to restore and strengthen this lifeline.”
This year’s $142.3 million allocation is nearly $4 million less than Massachusetts’ initial allocation last year, which totaled $146 million. The drop is driven by the expiration of the five-year LIHEAP increase included in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which delivered an additional $6.4 million to the Commonwealth last year alone over the baseline $139.6 million allocation.
Crude oil prices have topped $100 per barrel multiple times this year, most recently on September 15. Because heating oil is refined from crude, those spikes hit Massachusetts households hardest. State utility shutoff moratoriums protect many families through the coldest months, but they do nothing for households that must pay in full before a heating oil delivery.
The LIHEAP program has long been underfunded. On average, just 20 percent of eligible households receive assistance each year. In 2023, Trahan led an effort to increase federal LIHEAP funding. Earlier this month, Trahan, Senator Elizabeth Warren, and Congressman Stephen Lynch led 24 of their colleagues in pressing the Department of Energy to act on soaring heating oil costs and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP, which it has tried to eliminate.
Massachusetts residents can learn more about and apply for heating assistance HERE.
###
title: Massachusetts Awarded $142 Million in Federal Home Heating Assistance Funds

View the complete list of fourth quarter projects here.
VA obligated all the $4.8 billion that was available in FY 2026. Maintenance projects approved in the fourth quarter of FY2026 include:

- $938 million for major building upgrades like elevators, electrical systems, and boiler plants.
- $560 million for maintenance and modernization of facility infrastructure to support future electronic health record system updates.
These investments are one of many ways the Trump Administration is making VA work better for Veterans. Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:

SAN BRUNO, CA – Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15), who has been demanding answers from the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) and authored the National Archives Protection Act, issued the following statement in response to California Attorney General Rob Bonta announcing a lawsuit to block the closure of the San Francisco National Archives, located in San Bruno, CA:
“The National Archives and Records at San Bruno tell the important story of what has happened here in the Bay Area and local communities have every right to want direct access to their history. The National Records and Archives Administration (NARA) failed to conduct any kind of public input process and didn’t engage with stakeholders who are impacted before making a decision to close this facility and relocate fragile, sensitive documents over 1,500 miles away.
I am glad to see California Attorney General Rob Bonta file a lawsuit to stop NARA’s closure of the facility, and emphasizing how important it is for state agencies, university researchers and tribes to have access to these records.
While I’m pleased to see the Attorney General take action today, I am also pushing for federal legislation with the National Archives Protection Act and will be doing everything in my power to prevent the closure through other means like the federal budget process.
The fact that we have developed a bipartisan, nationwide coalition of federal lawmakers interested in preserving these archives demonstrates the unique and irreplaceable value they hold. These archives aren’t just boxes of paper — they hold the stories, memories, and history of generations of Americans. Families whose ancestors immigrated through Angel Island can track their lineage, those whose loved ones served in the Navy and were stationed in the Pacific can learn about their legacy, and Native Americans whose history is documented over generations are all able to learn more by visiting this national archive.”
In June 2026, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) announced it would be closing the San Francisco (San Bruno) and Chicago facilities, which are two of just 13 regional archives across America. The local facility in San Bruno houses culturally-significant archives from not only California but also Nevada, Hawaii, Pacific island territories, and Tribes. Its records hold deep value to the community including Angel Island immigration files, Chinese Exclusion Act and Japanese Internment records, Native American and indigenous history documents, and much more.
Read more about Rep. Mullin’s National Archives Protection Act, and NARA’s dismissive response to a letter he co-authored with Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) along with 37 federal lawmakers, urging them to stop the closure.
###
title: Reaction to California Attorney General’s Lawsuit to Protect National Archives in San Bruno

Tallahassee, Florida – Timeka Griffin, 42, of Tallahassee, Florida, was sentenced to five years in federal prison for her role in a conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and cocaine, distribution of cocaine and methamphetamine, and possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This local drug trafficking ring has been dismantled thanks to the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners and this successful prosecution by my office. Our citizens deserve safe, drug-free streets, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute anyone caught peddling deadly narcotics in this district to ensure we deliver on that promise.”

Court documents reflect that in July 2025, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Leon County Sheriff’s Office received information regarding the trafficking of cocaine in Leon County. Through investigation, law enforcement identified Edward Lee Cromartie and Griffin as a source of supply for cocaine and methamphetamine. Law enforcement also identified a suspected drug stash location, and upon execution of a federal search warrant at a storage unit shared by Cromartie and Griffin, seized approximately 1.6 kilograms of methamphetamine, along with multiple firearms, including a stolen handgun.

In March 2026, Cromartie was sentenced to 12 years in federal prison for his role in the drug trafficking conspiracy, distribution, and possession with intent to distribute charges.

“Dealers of Methamphetamine in North Florida should know DEA is coming for you,” said Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Our agents will bring criminals who distribute this poison in our communities to justice.”

The case involved a joint investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration and Leon County Sheriff’s Office. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

BOSTON – Former Massachusetts state official, Lamar Cook, has been arrested for fraudulently obtaining Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits, receiving over $500 per month, while on court ordered pretrial release in connection with a pending state indictment for alleged cocaine trafficking and firearm offenses.

Lamar Cook, 46, of Springfield, Mass., was arrested today on a criminal complaint charging him with one count of SNAP fraud and wire fraud. Cook will appear in federal court in Boston later today.

In 2023, the Governor of Massachusetts appointed Cook to serve as the Western MA Deputy Director in Springfield, Mass. Cook was terminated in October 2025 after he was detained at the Springfield State Office building and later charged by the Hampden District Attorney’s Office for alleged drug and firearm offenses. According to court documents, Cook earned a yearly salary of $130,227 and was later paid $22,374.29 in net pay for accrued vacation leave following his termination. The Commonwealth later “realized an error in paying Mr. Cook for accrued vacation leave time, the Commonwealth attempted to reverse the direct deposits, but it could not do so due to insufficient funds available in the accounts.”

According to court filings in the federal criminal case, Cook’s bank account continued to hold balances of approximately $13,000 as of January 2026 and over $8,800 in April 2026.

Cook also allegedly received a federal and state tax refund in May 2026 from his employment with the Governor’s Office for the 2025 calendar year in the amount of $2,497.88. Additionally, according to court documents, Cook’s mother won approximately $1 million in the Massachusetts Lottery in early 2026. Cook’s mother allegedly made numerous Zelle payments to him totaling approximately $12,000 between May and June 2026.

According to the charging documents, Cook applied for SNAP benefits on April 6, 2026 and falsely claimed zero income, less than $100 in his bank account, and to be living in a two person household consisting only of himself and his minor child. According to the affidavit, Cook in fact maintained at least one bank account that held more than $8,800 on the date of his SNAP application and received thousands of dollars in additional deposits, including the payments from his mother. It is further alleged that Cook failed to disclose that his fiancée and her mother lived with him at his Springfield residence and his fiancée earned income exceeding $80,000 annually from the City of Springfield Public Schools.

“The alleged conduct is simply egregious. SNAP benefits are intended to put food on the table for struggling families who cannot make ends meet, not for those who allegedly hide income to circumvent the financial requirements, much less travel to Disney World. Mr. Cook allegedly lied about his income and the makeup of his household in order to receive over $540 per month in SNAP benefits. All this occurred while Cook was on pretrial release for charged state drug and firearm offenses,” said U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley. “What kind of system allows for someone like this defendant to receive taxpayer funded benefits? I find it disturbing that the Commonwealth of Massachusetts could not prevent this from happening, nor could it recover the ill-gained $22,000 payment for earned vacation time -- which was also paid out with taxpayer money.”

All this occurred while Cook was on pretrial release for charged state drug and firearm offenses,” said U.S. Attorney Leah B. I find it disturbing that the Commonwealth of Massachusetts could not prevent this from happening, nor could it recover the ill-gained $22,000 payment for earned vacation time -- which was also paid out with taxpayer money.”

“It is an unconscionable betrayal of the public trust for a former state official with a pending indictment for drug and gun offenses to then also steal SNAP benefits from the American taxpayer – food assistance benefits intended for low-income Americans,” said U.S. Department of Agriculture, Inspector General John Walk. “This former state employee lied about his income and family situation to cheat the program. He will now face justice.”

“Fraud against public benefit programs is ultimately a theft from taxpayers and from the beneficiaries these programs are intended to serve,” said Roberto Coviello, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “HHS-OIG remains committed to protecting the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs and ensuring that those who seek to exploit them for personal gain are held accountable.”

Cook received approximately $546 per month in SNAP benefits. Cook’s SNAP benefits were allegedly used regularly at grocery and retail stores in Massachusetts and on a July 2026 trip to Florida. Retail surveillance and transaction records show Cook’s fiancée frequently used his EBT card to make purchases for the household, despite not being listed as a member of his household on Cook’s SNAP application.

According to court documents, at the time Cook submitted his application for SNAP benefits, he was on release for a pending Hampden County Superior Court indictment charging him with trafficking more than 200 grams of cocaine, conspiracy and firearm offenses stemming from an October 2025 investigation.

The charge of SNAP fraud provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of wire fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

U.S. Attorney Foley; USDA IG Walk; and HHS IG Coviello made the announcement. Valuable assistance Massachusetts State Police, Hampden County District Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations in New England and the Springfield Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip A. Mallard of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case.

On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621).

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. RepresentativesYassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) demand answers from GardaWorld Federal Services (GWFS) following its latest $1.2 billion contract to expand immigration detention facilities in Florence, Arizona. The lawmakers also pressed the company to answer questions it failed to address in a previous inquiry related to the Surprise warehouse facility.
The new contract, awarded September 21, raises fresh concerns about transparency and coordination with local governments. According to reporting, the Town of Florence was not notified of the planned expansion and had no additional information about the contract.
"It is deeply concerning that, despite the significant scale of these projects and their potential impact on surrounding communities, local governments continue to learn about them only after contracts have been awarded," the lawmakers wrote.
The letter also presses GWFS on questions left unanswered from the lawmakers’ March 2026 inquiry into its contract with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to convert a warehouse in Surprise into an immigration detention facility. In its April response, GWFS deferred many questions to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and failed to address basic questions about its own detention experience, staffing, facility assessments, and subcontracting plans. The lawmakers are demanding full answers.
The lawmakers also raised concerns about GWFS' previously undisclosed role in the environmental review of the Surprise warehouse. The City of Surprise revealed that a company representative had requested information for the assessment, despite neither GWFS nor federal agencies publicly disclosing its involvement.
The lawmakers are requesting written responses within 15 business days of receipt of the letter, including answers about:
- Experience and staffing: GWFS' qualifications to manage both projects, personnel overseeing operations, and plans to subcontract construction, medical care, staffing, or facility management.
- Facility safety: Structural and code-compliance assessments of the Surprise warehouse, including plans for ventilation, extreme heat mitigation, fire safety, and medical care.
- Environmental review: GWFS' role in the Surprise environmental assessment and its experience conducting comparable federal reviews.
- Florence expansion: Specific projects, facilities, and task orders planned under the $1.2 billion contract, including their scope and cost.
- Local coordination: Consultations with Surprise, Florence, Maricopa and Pinal counties, school districts, and public safety agencies.
- Taxpayer costs: Whether GWFS or DHS will cover increased demands for emergency medical services, fire protection, and law enforcement rather than shifting those costs to local taxpayers.
"The communities surrounding the Surprise and Florence facilities deserve transparency," the lawmakers concluded.
Read the full letter HERE.
title: Ansari, Stanton, Grijalva Press GardaWorld Over Unanswered Questions After Company Secures New $1.2 Billion ICE Contract
