Pou Reveals New Details of Massive Data Center Diesel Spill
More than a month later, questions remain over missing oil, environmental damage, and cleanup
PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) today revealed new details about the September 11, 2026 diesel spill at a data center in Secaucus, including a more than seven-hour delay in reporting the incident to state authorities and unanswered questions about its environmental impact.
These findings, obtained after Pou sought answers from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection, were shared in a letter to Secaucus Mayor Michael Gonnelli as the state continues investigating the roughly 5,500-gallon spill.
On October 2, 2026, Congresswoman Pou wrote to NJDEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak seeking a full accounting of the spill, including how it occurred, a timeline of the disaster, the extent of the damage, and what safeguards would be put in place to prevent similar catastrophes.
“Although approximately 4,000 gallons of the diesel have been recovered from waterways and canals, a full accounting of the remaining fuel and cleanup is still outstanding. NJDEP reports that its daily inspections have found no evidence that diesel reached the Hackensack River. However, the agency has acknowledged reports of discoloration in vegetation along the southeast edge of the river, downstream of the tributary where the spill occurred. Although Equinix and NJDEP have stated that an unspecified amount of fuel was absorbed by cleanup materials deployed around the tributaries, I remain deeply concerned about diesel that may remain in the surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways,” Congresswoman Pou writes Secaucus Mayor Gonnelli about the data center damage around his community.
Key Findings from the NJDEP’s Preliminary Investigation
- Approximately 4,000 gallons of diesel have been recovered from the storm sewer line and drainage canals: NJDEP reports an unspecified amount was absorbed by cleanup materials. How much diesel remains in surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways is unknown.
- No evidence was found that diesel reached the Hackensack River: But NJDEP acknowledged reports of “discolored vegetation along the river’s southeastern edge, downstream from the affected tributary.” NJDEP is investigating if the discoloration was caused by the diesel spill.
- The data center falls below the threshold for certain state safeguards against major facilities. NJDEP determined that the facility is not subject to New Jersey’s major-facility discharge prevention requirements, including secondary containment systems, physical security measures, and visual inspections.
- Cleanup efforts continue, and Equinix has taken corrective measures. NJDEP has confirmed that emergency responses were undertaken following the spill. According to separately published reports, Equinix has reportedly terminated a facility site engineer and suspended automatic fuel polishing operations nationwide.
- The state probe remains ongoing with no completion date announced. The agency has committed to releasing its final report publicly and will evaluate appropriate enforcement actions.
Secaucus and surrounding communities have lived with pollution for decades. Contamination from industrial sites and landfill runoff led the Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River a Superfund site in 2022. Now as a major cleanup is underway, the September 11 Equinix spill has seen over 5,000 gallons of diesel released into the local environment.
The Secaucus spill comes amid growing national attention to the environmental impact and public costs of rapidly expanding data centers.
Timeline of the September 11, 2026 Diesel Spill
12:20PM: The spill may have begun as early as just after noon, following a failure of the overfill protection system on generator #4’s fuel tank during an internal fuel transfer.
~4:00PM: Equinix’s fuel polishing process stopped although diesel continued leaking.
6:36PM: An Equinix guard discovered the spill, approximately six hours after it may have begun.
6:46PM: Within 10 minutes of discovering the spill, Equinix isolated the fuel lines and halted the generator.
7:06PM: Spill containment kits were deployed.
7:11PM: Equinix contacted its emergency contractor.
7:43PM: Equinix notified NJDEP of the spill, more than seven hours after it may have begun. The Secaucus Fire Department arrived around the same time.
9:45PM: Equinix’s emergency contractor arrived at the facility, more than three hours after the spill was discovered.
September 12, 6:07AM: Secaucus and the local health department received electronic notification of the spill, nearly 18 hours after it may have begun.
The text of Congresswoman Pou’s letter to Secaucus Mayor Gonnelli is below.
Dear Mayor Gonnelli:
I write to share new information over the recent data center fuel spill in Secaucus that released over 5,000 gallons of diesel fuel into waterways near the Hackensack River. On October 2, I wrote to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (“NJDEP”) demanding answers about the spill at the Equinix facility, including a timeline of events and information about its environmental impact. NJDEP responded to several of my questions. Although more information is forthcoming, I want to share what we have learned so far, including additional details Equinix recently provided to my office and to NJDEP.
On September 11, 2026, Equinix conducted an internal fuel transfer operation, during which the overfill protection system on generator #4’s fuel tank failed. Equinix has stated that the spill may have begun as early as 12:20 PM and continued until approximately 4:00 PM when fuel polishing stopped. After roughly six hours of diesel fuel leaking, an Equinix security guard discovered the spill at approximately 6:36 PM. Within 10 minutes, the facility isolated the fuel lines and halted the associated generator. Around 7:06 PM, spill kits were deployed and by 7:11 PM, Equinix contacted its emergency environmental contractor. Equinix reported the incident to the NJDEP Hotline at 7:43 PM—over seven hours after the spill began. Around that same time, the Secaucus Fire Department arrived at the facility—Equinix’s own emergency environmental contractor arrived roughly two hours later at 9:45 PM. NJDEP also directed environmental booms to be deployed to stop the diesel fuel from spreading into the drainage tributary for the Hackensack River. NJDEP also directed the use of additional equipment to vacuum and clean up the spill.
More than a month after the spill, important questions remain unanswered. Although approximately 4,000 gallons of the diesel have been recovered from waterways and canals, a full accounting of the remaining fuel and cleanup is still outstanding. NJDEP reports that its daily inspections have found no evidence that diesel reached the Hackensack River. However, the agency has acknowledged reports of discoloration in vegetation along the southeast edge of the river, downstream of the tributary where the spill occurred. Although Equinix and NJDEP have stated that an unspecified amount of fuel was absorbed by cleanup materials deployed around the tributaries, I remain deeply concerned about diesel that may remain in the surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways.
NJDEP continues to investigate the incident, including whether the vegetation discoloration was caused by the fuel spill, but has not provided a timeline for completing its probe. NJDEP has promised to provide me with additional information as it becomes available. The agency has committed to making its final report public so our community can understand the full extent of any damage. Once the report is completed, NJDEP will evaluate appropriate enforcement actions.
Importantly, within a week of the spill, NJDEP inspected the Equinix facility and determined that its fuel storage capacity falls below the threshold for New Jersey’s major facility discharge of petroleum and other hazardous substance prevention requirements. These requirements include having physical security measures, impermeable secondary containment and diversion systems, and visual inspections and monitoring.
While NJDEP has confirmed that appropriate emergency responses were undertaken following the spill and that cleanup efforts continue, and although Equinix appears to have terminated an employee serving as a facility site engineer and has halted automatic fuel polishing nationwide, more must be done to keep our communities safe. My office will continue to work with you, the Town of Secaucus, state agencies, and federal regulators to address the aftermath of this incident and prevent similar spills in the future.
Sincerely,
Nellie Pou
Member of Congress
###
title: Pou Reveals New Details of Massive Data Center Diesel Spill

BOSTON – An associate of the Lynn Chapter of the Trinitarios and drug supplier to the gang with connections to a Mexican drug cartel pleaded guilty on Oct. 7, 2026 to racketeering and drug charges, including organizing an attempted murder that the Trinitarios undertook on behalf of the cartel.

Janoy Batista, a/k/a “El Viejo,” 47, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to conduct enterprise affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity, more commonly referred to as RICO conspiracy and drug conspiracy. U.S. Senior District Court Judge Nathaniel M. Gorton scheduled sentencing for Jan. 7, 2027. Batista was arrested and charged in February 2025 with other leaders, members and associates of the Trinitarios.

The Trinitarios is a violent criminal enterprise comprised of thousands of members across the United States. The Trinitarios adhere to a Magna Carta, employ an internal hierarchy to coordinate and execute violence, and undertake extensive efforts to maintain the secrecy of the organization and its members.

During the plea hearing, Batista admitted that he was an associate of the gang and that he supplied the gang with drugs from Cartel Jalisco Nuevo Generacion (“CJNG”). CJNG would ship large quantities of cocaine and fentanyl to Batista in Lynn, Mass. utilizing car transport trucks. Batista would supply members of the Trinitarios with cocaine and fentanyl received from CJNG.

Batista further admitted that in November 2023, CJNG tasked him with killing a local drug contact who the cartel believed had stolen a large quantity of drugs. CJNG indicated that Batista would be required to kill the drug contact in order to continue receiving shipments. In November 2023, Batista organized a failed murder attempt of the drug contact utilizing a Trinitarios member’s vehicle. During the incident in Salem, Mass., two shooters opened fire on the drug contact as he sat in his driveway, striking him multiple times. Batista picked up the shooters and driver involved in the attempted murder and drove them to an apartment controlled by the Trinitarios. The drug contact survived the incident.

In February 2025 , federal racketeering charges were unsealed against 22 leaders and members of the Trinitarios. The charges were the result of a multijurisdictional investigation, which began in the aftermath of four murders as well as a series of attempted murders and shootings that took place in Lynn in 2023, allegedly committed by the Trinitarios criminal enterprise and its members. On June 9, 2026 , additional federal racketeering and drug charges were unsealed charging 26 additional leaders, members and associates of the Lawrence, Haverhill and Boston Chapters of the gang. According to court documents, the Trinitarios have allegedly participated in five additional murders in Essex County since 2017, bringing the total of federally charged murders to 11, and the total number of federally charged defendants to 56.

The charge of conspiracy to conduct enterprise affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity (also known as “racketeering conspiracy” or “RICO conspiracy”) provides for a sentence of up to life in prison, five years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; Essex County District Attorney Paul F. Tucker; Massachusetts State Police Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble; and Lynn Police Chief Christopher P. Reddy made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Manchester, N.H. Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip A. Mallard of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Boston is comprised of agents and officers from HSI, FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS, IRS-CI, USPIS, DOL-OIG and DSS, as well as several state and local law enforcement agencies, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces and Project Safe Neighborhood .

Reps. Carter, Moskowitz Introduce the Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education Act to Strengthen Campus Resilience
WASHINGTON, D.C. – In the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA) and Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), Co-Chairs of the Disaster Preparedness and Recovery Caucus, introduced the Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education Act. This legislation authorizes $100 million in annual federal funding for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to distribute to higher education institutions. These grants would improve institutions’ capacity, planning, and facilities to better prepare for, and respond to, disasters and other emergencies that directly impact students, administrators, and staff. The need for greater disaster preparedness was evident when Hurricanes Katrina, Ida, and Irma devastated universities in Louisiana and Florida, and when wildfires forced evacuations of California campuses.
“Our climate crisis makes extreme weather events more frequent and severe, so we need to ensure uniquely vulnerable communities, such as our colleges and universities, have the support and resources they need to prepare for and respond to disasters and emergency situations,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m partnering with Rep. Moskowitz to introduce this legislation and take necessary steps toward preparing our institutions of higher education for protecting the lives, housing, property, and futures of our young adults and the staff that support them before disaster strikes – not after a storm has already arrived.”
“As Florida’s former emergency management director, I know that the time to prepare for a disaster is before it strikes. No student should be left wondering where to go or whether their campus can keep them safe when a disaster hits,” said Congressman Moskowitz. “Families send their children to college trusting that their safety is a priority. That responsibility starts long before the first evacuation order.”
Background
American colleges and universities function as small communities, often housing tens of thousands of students, staff, and researchers in concentrated areas, making them uniquely vulnerable to a range of natural disasters and other emergencies. Campus shootings and other acts of violence, from Virginia Tech to Michigan State, have shown that institutions need well-rehearsed active-threat plans and protocols, reliable mass-notification systems, trained threat-assessment teams, and coordination with local law enforcement. Additionally, climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of hurricanes, wildfires, floods, extreme heat, and other events that can shut down campuses, displace students, and damage infrastructure.
Institutions have a duty of care for the many students who live on campus far from family, including international students, students with disabilities, and low-income students who face additional challenges. Investing in comprehensive emergency planning, resilient infrastructure, continuity-of-operations strategies, accessible communication, and other resources protects lives, preserves academic and research missions, and limits financial impacts. As these threats become more frequent and often overlap, campuses need additional support to make preparedness a core institutional responsibility.
The Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education strengthens higher education resilience by establishing a $100 million annual FEMA grant program to help eligible higher education institutions create or expand emergency management and preparedness capacity.
Eligible uses of grant funds include personnel costs to expand emergency preparedness; creating or updating comprehensive institutional emergency management plans; infrastructure and facility construction or improvements for emergency operations centers or areas of refuge; and equipment and technology to enhance interagency coordination.
Read the full bill text here.

Navy Child and Youth Programs Partners with United Through Reading to Keep Military Families Connected Through Storytime
WASHINGTON DC (Oct. 14, 2026) — Navy Child and Youth Programs (CYP) has launched an enterprise-wide partnership with United Through Reading (UTR), a nonprofit that strengthens military families’ emotional bonds, literacy, and well-being through shared reading experiences, regardless of distance.
Under the banner “Read, Record, Connect: Keeping Military Families Connected Through Storytime,” the partnership will equip Navy installations with books, literacy resources, mobile story stations, and digital tools to help families stay connected during periods of separation while supporting children’s early literacy and development.
Military life often requires families to spend extended periods apart due to deployments, Individual Augmentations (IAs), extended duty shifts, underways, temporary duty assignments (TDYs), and Permanent Change of Station (PCS) relocations. These demands can also separate families from the extended support networks they rely on. By helping children see and hear their parent reading a familiar story, the partnership reinforces meaningful family connections, supports consistent reading routines, and makes shared story time possible from thousands of miles away.
“Military life can place unique demands on families, from deployments and extended duty hours to frequent relocations that take Sailors away from home. Maintaining strong family connections is essential to Sailors’ well-being and their families’ resilience,” said Vice Adm. Brad Collins, Commander, Navy Installations Command. “Our partnership with United Through Reading reflects CNIC’s commitment to improving Quality of Service by giving military families practical ways to stay connected, even when duty keeps them apart.”
Beginning in fall 2026, the eight-month initiative will deliver literacy resources and family engagement opportunities to Navy CYP facilities and military households, including:
- 24,850 Books for Children and Youth: A diverse selection of titles for all ages, from baby board books and picture books to early and leveled readers, chapter books, middle-grade literature, and young adult novels.
- 165,000 Bookmarks: Specially designed bookmarks to encourage daily reading habits, featuring creative coloring bookmarks, Halloween-themed editions, and commemorative "Book for the Military Child" bookmarks.
- 100,000 Early Literacy Guides: From Day One: Connecting Through Storytime, practical resources tailored to families with infants and children ages 0–5.
- 65 Specialized In-Person Recording Events: 41 recording sessions staffed by UTR and 24 events using Mobile Story Stations.
- Facility Engagement Materials: Year-round outreach resources, including UTR information cards, parent bookmarks, and front-desk flyers for distribution across all CYP sites.
Flexible Ways to Share Storytime
The partnership combines in-person recording opportunities with a convenient mobile option, allowing service members to record and share stories wherever duty takes them.
Through the self-service UTR smartphone app, service members can record themselves reading a book aloud from virtually anywhere in the world. They can then upload the video and designate a co-parent or caregiver to receive it by email and through the app. Recipients also receive instructions for ordering a free copy of the featured book through UTR, allowing children to follow along with the printed pages as they watch and listen to their parent read.
In addition to the mobile app, families will have access to Local and Command Story Stations, along with on-site recording opportunities for enrolled parents and caregivers. These in-person events will focus on major fleet concentration areas, including Region Northwest, San Diego, Hampton Roads, Naval District Washington, and Florida.
Phased Rollout: 2026–2027
Resources will be distributed in phases:
- October 2026: Distribution of Halloween-themed bookmarks and early childhood literacy guides.
- December 2026: Winter shipment of children's and youth books.
- January 2027: Second distribution phase of literacy guides for ages 0–5.
- March 2027: Spring distribution of books across age categories.
- April 2027: Month of the Military Child-themed bookmarks distributed in celebration of military youth.
Through Read, Record, Connect, Navy CYP and United Through Reading are making it easier for military families to maintain meaningful connections through the simple, familiar ritual of reading together. Whether a Sailor is deployed overseas, underway, or serving far from home, a familiar voice and a favorite story can help children feel connected to their parent. The partnership reinforces CNIC’s commitment to improving Quality of Service by helping Sailors and their families stay connected, supported, and resilient wherever Navy service takes them.
Commander, Navy Installations Command is responsible for worldwide U.S. Navy Shore installation management, designing and developing integrated solutions for sustainment and development of Navy shore infrastructure as well as quality of life programs. CNIC oversees 10 Navy regions, 71 installations, and more than 63,000 employees who are focused on warfighting and manning, training and equipping the Shore to fight and win. Navy installations are warfighting platforms essential to every fleet operation.
title: Navy Child and Youth Programs Partners with United Through Reading to Keep Military Families Connected Through Storytime

WASHINGTON — In response to a Presidential disaster declaration issued Oct. 7, the U.S. Small Business Administration announced the availability of low-interest federal disaster loans to businesses, private nonprofits, and residents affected by severe storms and flooding occurring July 16 – 21.
The disaster declaration covers Pueblo of Zuni, which is eligible for both physical damage loans and Economic Injury Disaster Loans from SBA. Small businesses and most private nonprofit organizations in the following adjacent New Mexico counties of Cibola and McKinley, and the Arizona county of Apache are eligible to apply for economic injury loans.
Businesses and nonprofits are eligible to apply for business physical damage loans and may borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged or destroyed real estate, machinery, and equipment, inventory, and other business assets.
Homeowners and renters are eligible to apply for home and personal property loans and may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property, such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances. Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence.
Applicants may also be eligible for a loan increase of up to 20% of their verified physical damage, for mitigation purposes. Eligible mitigation improvements may include strengthening structures to protect against high wind damage, upgrading to wind rated garage doors, installing a safe room or storm shelter, elevating flood prone structures, adding a sump pump, or French drains to help reduce damage from future storms and flooding.
The SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan program is available to eligible small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofits — including faith-based organizations —impacted by financial losses directly related to this disaster. The SBA is unable to provide disaster loans to agricultural producers, farmers, or ranchers, except for aquaculture enterprises.
Economic Injury Disaster Loans are for working capital needs caused by the disaster and are available even if the business or private nonprofit did not suffer any physical damage. They may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills which could not be paid due to the disaster.
“A presidential disaster declaration opens the door to SBA assistance at a time when families and businesses are facing difficult decisions,” said Chris Stallings, Associate Administrator of SBA's Office of Disaster Recovery. “These loans can help eligible homeowners and renters repair or replace what was damaged while giving businesses and private nonprofits the resources to continue operating as their communities recover.”
Interest rates are as low as 4% for businesses, 3.625% for nonprofits, and 2.875% for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not begin to accrue, and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The SBA determines eligibility and sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant’s financial condition.
To apply online, visit sba.gov/disaster. Applicants may also call SBA’s National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for more information on disaster assistance. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
The filing deadline for returning applications for physical property damage is Dec. 7. The deadline to return economic injury applications is July 7, 2027.
###
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of business ownership. As the only go-to resource and voice for small businesses backed by the strength of the federal government, the SBA empowers entrepreneurs and small business owners with the resources and support they need to start, grow, expand their businesses, or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA Relief Available to Pueblo of Zuni Businesses, Private Nonprofits, Residents Affected by Severe Storms and Flooding

Deluzio Continues October Town Hall Tour in Carnegie, PA
CARNEGIE, PA – Yesterday, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) continued his October Town Hall Tour across Pennsylvania’s 17th District in Carnegie, Pennsylvania. The event was open to the public and the press.
The Carnegie Town Hall covered a wide range of topics, including the Iran War, data centers, healthcare cuts, and more. Constituents had an opportunity to speak directly with their elected representative in Congress, share their opinions, and ask questions. Congressman Deluzio also provided updates from his work down in Washington.
“It was great to hear from more than 85 folks in Carnegie last night on the second stop of my October Town Hall Tour,” said Congressman Deluzio. “It's clear that the good people of Western Pennsylvania are sick of the corruption at the top of our federal government and want an end to the Iran War that’s jacking up costs and making us all less safe. I look forward to continuing the conversation with one last stop in Beaver Falls this Saturday!”
Congressman Deluzio has attended more than twenty similar town hall-style, open Q&A events so far this Congress (2025-2026).

- For Immediate Release:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today expanded the approved use of Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln), given with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG), to include adults with high-grade papillary-only bladder cancer that has not spread into the bladder muscle and has not responded to BCG treatment. Anktiva is the first FDA-approved treatment specifically for patients with BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only disease.
The approval marks a new FDA approach to evaluating treatments for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). The agency based its decision on evidence supporting an earlier approval of Anktiva for adults with another form of NMIBC, carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary tumors, and scientific similarities between CIS and high-grade papillary-only disease.
“We listen to patients, clinicians, and researchers, and we act when the science supports a new approach,” said R. Angelo de Claro, M.D., Director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence. “For Anktiva, our review of the similarities between these cancers allowed us to build on the results in patients with CIS and expand treatment options for people with high-grade papillary tumors alone. This approach may also help guide the development of future treatments.”
NMIBC is bladder cancer that has not grown into the bladder’s muscle layer and can include CIS and papillary tumors. CIS forms flat patches along the bladder’s lining, while papillary tumors grow from the lining into the bladder as small, finger-like projections. CIS is always high-grade, while papillary tumors can be low-grade or high-grade. High-grade cancers are more likely to grow and spread than low-grade cancers.
Treatment for high-risk NMIBC often starts with BCG, which activates the immune system inside the bladder to fight cancer. Sometimes, however, the cancer persists or returns. Adding Anktiva gives the immune system another way to fight the cancer, and the combination can help some people whose cancer was not controlled by BCG alone.
Anktiva’s CIS approval was supported by a trial (NCT03022825) that evaluated the treatment’s effectiveness in 77 adults, some of whom also had papillary tumors. Sixty-two percent achieved a complete response, meaning no high-grade cancer was detected during follow-up assessments, and of those, 58% maintained that response for at least 12 months and 40% for at least 24 months.
For today’s expanded approval, the FDA considered these results alongside clinical and laboratory evidence showing that CIS and high-grade papillary tumors share important features. They often occur together, can be difficult to distinguish under a microscope and carry a high risk of returning or progressing when BCG treatment no longer works. These similarities supported applying the evidence of Anktiva’s effectiveness in people with CIS to those with high-grade papillary-only disease.
To help developers apply this approach, the FDA is working toward finalizing its draft guidance, “Bacillus Calmette-Guérin-Unresponsive Nonmuscle Invasive Bladder Cancer: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Treatment.” The guidance is intended to include discussion of using evidence from studies in patients with CIS to support approval of treatments for BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only NMIBC.
Anktiva is given with BCG directly into the bladder through a catheter. It is given once a week for six weeks, with additional treatment based on how the cancer responds. Treatment may continue for up to 37 months. It should be stopped if the cancer persists after a second six-week course, returns or progresses, or side effects become unacceptable.
The most common side effects and laboratory abnormalities included painful or frequent urination, an urgent need to urinate, blood in the urine, urinary tract infections, muscle or joint pain, chills, fever, and increased blood levels of creatinine and potassium. Anktiva’s prescribing information warns that delaying surgery to remove all or part of the bladder can allow the cancer to spread to other parts of the body, which can be fatal.
The approval was granted to Altor BioScience, LLC.
Additional Resources
The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.
###
title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Certain People With BCG-Unresponsive Bladder Cancer

text:
ICYMI: OPM Director Scott Kupor Discusses the Super Intelligence Force on CNN’s The Lead with Jake Tapper
WASHINGTON, DC – US Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Director Scott Kupor joined The Lead with Jake Tapper on CNN to discuss President Trump’s Super Intelligence Force, the administration’s approach to SI safety and innovation, and how the government can prepare for potential risks and workforce changes.
On President Trump’s use of the term “super intelligence”:
“No. Yes. I can’t protect you, you know. But yes, SI is the new word.”
On whether companies will change their names:
“I don’t know. But you may have seen Elon did, right? So Elon changed the name of his company. He’s now calling it X SI, I believe.”
On whether there will be punishment for using the term “artificial intelligence”:
“I don’t know. You got to ask the President that. I’m not briefed on that to talk to you about today.”
On the industry’s voluntary safety commitments and the task force’s role:
“Yes. I would say a couple of things. First of all, it’s not just, you know, they’re responsible for their own stuff. As part of that contract they signed, they agreed that they would have external third-party auditors reviewing it. And as you probably know, obviously, if you sit on a public company board in particular, outside auditors typically report to the board of directors.
“And so if an outside security auditor comes back to these companies and says, ‘Hey, we got a problem here,’ that board’s going to have to actually respond and do something. So it is truly legally binding in that respect, which is all the traditional fiduciary duties and kind of duties that board owes.
“The second thing I would just add is, look, as I know we’ll talk about, the President put together this SI force that myself and three others—”
“Jay Clayton, Emil Michael, and Andrew Ferguson at the FTC are running. I think you should expect that. Look, we’re not going to sit around and just say, ‘Great, we’re wonderful. We’re thrilled you guys signed this piece of paper,’ and, you know, we should just be done and dusted.
“The whole purpose of this committee is to figure out, OK, what is the comprehensive set of policies that we think meet the dual goals that the President has? Which is, look, the President thinks we should continue to win. I certainly believe this is an important fight and a battle that we should win.
“But he’s also said we need to figure out how to do it in a way that’s responsible to the economic and natural sovereignty needs of the American people. So that’s what we’re going to obviously balance as part of this.”
On reporting incidents involving SI models:
“Yes. So this is definitely one of the things that we are going to take up as part of this task force. We need to make sure we have an appropriate, let’s call it a notification paradigm, for lack of a better word. So, we want to encourage the companies—and you’re seeing this more and more now—we want to encourage the companies to have a paradigm where they say, ‘Look, when we see something, report it to us.’
“And then, look, it’s incumbent upon us as the government then to make sure, OK, what do we do with that information? So is it an FAA issue? So we’ve got to go talk to the Department of Transportation, make sure they know what’s happening. So, again, a lot of what we’re going to try to do is talk to, obviously, the model companies, talk to all the agencies in the government, including the intelligence agencies, figure out what they need.
“We’re also going to go talk to—and this is where I’m going to spend my time—all the various other infrastructure companies, so financial services, oil and gas companies, energy companies, anybody for whom some type of security-related incident might obviously turn into a major issue.
“And we’ve got to figure out a notification system, we’ve got to figure out a communication system, and ultimately action plans to make sure that the American people feel that they can—they’re safe and they can trust the technology.”
On preparing workers for potential changes to the labor market:
“Yes. So one thing I would just note is, look, so far to date, if you rewind the clock about 18 months ago, people like Dario, for example, were actually talking about a coming job apocalypse. So far, actually, if you look at jobs, what all the data has shown is that actually we’ve increased jobs as a result of SI.”
“And I hope that’s true too, right? And that’s—and that’s, as you well know, look, when you look at most technological changes, that’s what happens. But I agree with you, people are concerned about it. What you have seen and what you will see more from the Department of Labor is there are a bunch of retraining programs that are happening, and you will see us address this very, very directly as part of the work that we’re doing in our task force.”
On addressing risks from bad actors and cyberattacks:
“Yes. So I think there’s a couple things, again, that you’ll see us enact as part of this task force. One is there is a whole set of laws and regulations that deal with kind of what you’re describing, the bad actor scenario. So, you know, DOJ has all kinds of criminal statutes, as does the FTC have civil ones.”
“I think there are. I think, look, every corporation has a very basic responsibility to make sure that when they put things out, they put things out that they deem safe and appropriate, you know, for consumer use. Now, look, if a bad actor comes along and takes technology, again, you know, we have the ability, of course, to go after that bad actor through existing criminal laws.
“On the other side, though, what’s really important is, you know, as you mentioned before, we’ve got to protect things on the cyber side as well. So, a lot of what you’re going to see us do is make sure we have a lot more teeth, you know, behind all the activities of the companies themselves. We have notification schemes. We will have, kind of, contingency plans across all the different agencies.
“And the goal will be to make sure that, you know, if it turns out that there’s something there, the government is going to be as well-educated and as well-prepared for this as we can be for any possible scenario.”
title: ICYMI: OPM Director Scott Kupor Discusses the Super Intelligence Force on CNN’s The Lead with Jake Tapper

Trump Administration Delivers Second Year of Savings by Stopping Taxpayer Payments for Duplicate and Deceased Enrollees in Obamacare
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 14, 2026—The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) continue to crush fraud, waste, and abuse in America’s healthcare programs by stopping duplicative enrollment in government health programs, with the potential to save taxpayers approximately $1.5 billion over the next year.
In 2026, CMS identified 189,000 people who had subsidized Obamacare coverage through the Federal Marketplace and either had duplicate Medicare, Medicaid or Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) coverage or were deceased. CMS took swift action to remove Obamacare subsidies for these people to save taxpayer dollars.
“Taxpayers should not foot the bill for duplicate coverage or subsidies for people who have died,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “HHS is identifying improper enrollments, stopping those payments, and making sure federal dollars support the Americans these programs were created to serve.”
“When it comes to program integrity, the Biden Administration was sleeping on the job,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “They paused looking for duplicate Medicaid and Obamacare coverage for four years, creating a backlog of hundreds of thousands of duplicate enrollments. We’ve already saved nearly $6 billion, and we will continue to work hard to restore taxpayers’ confidence that the programs they fund are spending their hard-earned dollars wisely and efficiently.”
The Trump Administration restored duplicate enrollment enforcement in 2025, ending duplicate Obamacare subsidies for approximately 551,000 enrollees already receiving coverage under Medicaid.
Historically, CMS routinely checked to ensure taxpayers were not subsidizing duplicate Obamacare policies on the Federal Marketplace for beneficiaries already on Medicaid or Medicare. It also checked if taxpayers are paying for Obamacare plans on the Federal Marketplace for deceased people.
Federal regulations require Exchanges to periodically examine data for dual enrollments in Medicaid to guard against improper enrollments in subsidized Exchange plans through a process called Medicaid/CHIP Periodic Data Matching (PDM). These essential examinations were strengthened under the first Trump Administration and increased to at least twice a year. However, these checks were paused for Medicaid/CHIP enrollees the duration of the Biden Administration, allowing hundreds of thousands of individuals to be enrolled in multiple federal health insurance programs at once.
Individuals whose records show they receive Obamacare subsidies while also being covered by Medicaid or Medicare are contacted and provided 30 days to dispute that they have duplicate coverage. If such individuals fail to do so, CMS ends subsidies for their Obamacare plan. Even after 30 days, individuals may appeal the determination of duplicate coverage or show that their Medicaid/CHIP coverage is about to lapse and regain Obamacare subsidies.
This process also contacts individuals, or their estate, when federal records say they are deceased. CMS provides 30 days to dispute this record, otherwise their Obamacare subsidy and plan is ended.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

MONROE – On October 8, 2026, United States Chief District Judge Terry A. Doughty sentenced Heath A. Foster , 30, of West Monroe, to 156 months in federal prison for Possession with Intent to Distribute a Controlled Substance, followed by five years of supervised release. Foster previously pled guilty to the charge on June 18, 2026.

According to court documents, investigators with the Monroe Metro Narcotics Unit (MNU) used a confidential informant in August of 2025 to conduct a controlled purchase of 57.2 grams of methamphetamine from Foster for $350 in West Monroe. In November 2025, MNU again used a confidential informant to purchase 58 grams of methamphetamine from Foster for $350 at a different West Monroe location.

Later that same day, MNU received information from a confidential source that Foster was returning to Ouachita Parish with approximately 10 pounds of methamphetamine. Louisiana State Police (LSP) conducted a traffic stop as Foster’s vehicle entered Ouachita Parish. During the stop, an LSP K-9 unit alerted to drugs in the vehicle. A probable cause search revealed a backpack on the front passenger floorboard containing almost ten pounds of methamphetamine packaged in six clear plastic bags.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

The Drug Enforcement Agency, MNU, and LSP investigated this case. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Allison C. Foster with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Emily Favrot.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer, under Case Number 26-00036.

Proposed rules implement Working Families Tax Cuts reforms to prevent fraud and abuse of the Premium Tax Credit
IR-2026-121, Oct. 14, 2026
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service issued proposed regulations to implement President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts reforms to the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), a refundable tax credit that helps eligible American taxpayers afford health insurance purchased through the Health Insurance Exchanges.
“Hardworking American taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize health care for people who are ineligible under federal law,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Today’s proposed rules implement the common-sense reforms enacted by the Working Families Tax Cuts to close eligibility loopholes and ensure taxpayer-funded Premium Tax Credits are reserved for eligible Americans. Under President Trump, this Administration is cracking down on fraud and corruption; holding bad actors accountable; lowering health care costs for Americans; and restoring integrity to our tax code and health care system.”
"The proposed rules protect eligible taxpayers while strengthening the integrity of the Premium Tax Credit," said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. "The enhanced verification measures are designed to curb improper claims, ensuring these vital tax benefits go strictly to the hardworking Americans who qualify for them."
“The Trump Administration’s whole-of-government approach to fighting fraud, waste, and abuse is built on the idea that an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “Ensuring health programs serve only those who are eligible is one of the most effective ways to protect these programs and the taxpayers who support them. With today’s proposed rules, the Treasury Department is taking another step forward in our collaborative effort to protect taxpayer dollars by shutting down waste and fraud before a single dollar leaves the building.”
Protecting taxpayer-funded benefits for eligible Americans
The proposed rules put the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Premium Tax Credit reforms into effect which strengthen eligibility checks, close gaps in the verification process, and help ensure taxpayer-funded subsidies go only to eligible American taxpayers.
The Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud exposed the need for stronger safeguards to protect the integrity of the Federal Marketplace. As part of that work, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced the removal of more than 760,000 unverified “phantom” enrollees from the rolls of the Affordable Care Act (ACA), resulting in $2.2 billion in savings and sending nearly 1 million Americans $500 each who had been overcharged for their Obamacare coverage by the Biden Administration.
The Treasury and IRS proposed rules:
- Strengthen Eligibility Standards: Beginning in 2027, ensures taxpayer-funded health insurance subsidies go only to Americans who qualify under federal law.
- Protect Taxpayer Benefits for Eligible Americans: Restricts PTC eligibility to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and certain lawfully present noncitizens.
- Close Verification Gaps: Applies common sense PTC eligibility checks and adds new verification criteria for any advance PTC payments.
The proposed regulations are available in the Federal Register.
The changes to Exchange procedures and operations necessary to implement the verification requirements are expected to be addressed in parallel proposed regulations issued by HHS under related provisions of the same statute.
title: Treasury and IRS move to protect health care benefits for eligible Americans

Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Senators Edward J. Markey (D-MA), and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Congressman Jim McGovern (MA-02) wrote to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator Bryan Bedford and Amazon.com, Inc. CEO Andy Jassy urging Amazon to work with the FAA to conduct an Environmental Assessment of its proposed drone delivery facility in Westborough, Massachusetts, before launching operations there. Communities have raised concerns about the Amazon Prime Air drone delivery program’s impact on the environment and residents’ quality-of-life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy.
In the letters, the lawmakers wrote, “Despite the noise and environmental risks of Amazon’s drone operations, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has authorized operators such as Amazon to deploy their fleets without completing a site-specific Environmental Assessment (EA) of their impact on the surrounding communities. This decision is especially problematic in Massachusetts localities, given the differences between it and previously studied communities, local opposition, and the inadequate treatment of the risks associated with transporting hazardous-materials.”
The lawmakers continued, “An independent resident survey, with more than 1,200 responses as of early October 2026, found 92 percent of respondents opposed the proposed Westborough facility. At a state level, Massachusetts is one of 15 states currently suing the FAA for its nationwide FONSI. In other words, Amazon is now trying to quickly move drone operations into Massachusetts under a streamlined regulatory process the state itself is challenging. These are precisely the community-specific noise, safety, and quality-of-life concerns a site-specific EA and comment period exist to surface and address.”
The lawmakers urged, “These concerns – applying the FONSI to a community different from those previously assessed by the FAA, significant local opposition, and the limited evaluation of hazardous material risks – warrant requiring Amazon to complete a site-specific EA, with a public comment period, before the FAA authorizes Prime Air operations in Massachusetts.”
A copy of the letter sent to the Federal Aviation Administration can be accessed HERE. 
A copy of the letter sent to Amazon can be accessed HERE.

title: Trahan, Markey, Warren, McGovern Demand Study of Impacts of Amazon’s Westborough Drone Program

California Man Pleads Guilty to Sex Trafficking a Minor
Keynin McGee, 27, of Oakland, California, pleaded guilty to sex trafficking a minor in the Eastern District of California.
According to court documents, McGee met the minor victim in 2021 through Instagram. After months of speaking with her, McGee bought the victim a bus ticket for her to travel to meet him in person. When she arrived, McGee picked the victim up at the bus station, bought her clothing, and took her to a hotel. He then posted photographs of the victim online on a website commonly used to buy and sell sex. McGee then drove the victim to outdoor areas in Oakland and San Francisco known for commercial sex work and instructed her to solicit sex buyers in passing cars. Because of his conduct, the minor victim engaged in commercial sex acts with multiple buyers.
“Exploiting a child for financial gain is reprehensible and heinous,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Yesterday’s guilty plea of Keynin McGee to sex trafficking of a minor, who he lured to meet him in person then trafficked her for commercial sex in the Oakland and San Francisco areas, reflects our commitment to protecting children from the scourge of sex trafficking. The Criminal Division will continue to pursue and prosecute vile individuals who victimize and traffic minors.”
“This guilty plea illustrates the dedicated work of our law enforcement partners and prosecutors to investigate and stamp out sex trafficking and to hold traffickers accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Eric Grant for the Eastern District of California. “Protecting vulnerable victims requires sustained collaboration, thorough investigations, and a commitment to prosecute to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue working together to identify and support victims and bring to justice those who exploit them.”
“Keynin McGee reduced his young victim to a commodity to be bought and sold for his own gain,” said Special Agent in Charge Brian Tosh of FBI Sacramento. “Anyone who seeks to exploit children will face relentless pursuit from the FBI and our law enforcement partners. We will hold traffickers fully accountable for the harm they inflict. Together, we can protect the vulnerable and create a safer future for every child.”
McGee pleaded guilty to sex trafficking of a minor. He is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 19, 2027, and faces a minimum penalty of 10 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
The FBI is investigating the case with assistance from the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation.
Deputy Chief Leah Branch of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney David Gappa for the Eastern District of California are prosecuting the case.
Anyone who has information about human trafficking should report that information to the National Human Trafficking Hotline toll-free at 1-888-373-7888, which is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For more information about human trafficking, please visit www.humantraffickinghotline.org. Information on the Justice Department’s efforts to combat human trafficking can be found at www.justice.gov/humantrafficking.

IR-2026-122, Oct. 14, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service today announced that, in response to the President’s Oct. 5, 2026, Executive Order, Emergency Tax Relief on Diesel Fuel, it will not impose a penalty when dyed diesel fuel is sold for use or used on highways nationwide.
The relief is retroactive to Oct. 1, 2026, and will remain in effect until Dec. 31, 2026. Relief is available to any person that sells dyed diesel fuel or uses dyed diesel fuel for highway use.
Ordinarily, dyed diesel fuel is not subject to tax because it is destined for an exempt use, such as use on a farm for farming purposes; however, it would be taxed if sold for highway use or used to power a vehicle on the highway. Generally, the person liable for the tax is the person who sells dyed diesel fuel at retail or, if the dyed diesel fuel is not purchased at retail, the operator of the motor vehicle (e.g., dyed diesel fuel held in a storage tank on a farm).
During the relief period, ordinary procedures for collection and enforcement will be suspended. All IRS Fuel Compliance Officers will be re-assigned other responsibilities, and no federal inspections of on-road dyed fuel usage will occur. During the relief period, taxpayers need not maintain records necessary to substantiate their eligibility for relief. The IRS will not impose any penalties related to the excise tax for dyed diesel fuel sold for use or used in diesel-powered vehicles on highways nationwide during the relief period. This relief includes penalties for failure to make semimonthly deposits of tax or to maintain adequate records. Sellers and distributors are under no obligation to investigate or document the ultimate end-use of dyed fuel sold during the relief period.
Taxpayers who believe they qualify for relief but receive a penalty notice should follow the instructions in the notice or contact the IRS for assistance.
The IRS anticipates that it will issue further guidance as to the postponement under 26 U.S.C. 7508A of payment of taxes imposed by 26 U.S.C. 4041(a)(1)(A) or by 26 U.S.C. 4041(b)(1)(B), and will explore avenues to eliminate the obligation to pay any amounts deferred. Forthcoming IRS guidance will detail how this relief applies to Form 720 (Quarterly Federal Excise Tax Return) and any other relevant forms.
This relief only applies for federal tax purposes. It has no effect on state fuel taxes and penalties that a state may impose on the use of dyed diesel fuel on the highway. Many, but not all, states have provided similar state excise tax-related relief. Taxpayers are encouraged to refer to their applicable state agencies for the latest guidance on state-level relief.
title: IRS provides dyed diesel fuel relief related to excise tax following President Trump’s Executive Order

Mississippi Man Convicted by Federal Jury of Participating in a Criminal Conspiracy to Distribute Child Sexual Abuse Material
A federal jury convicted Justin Lee Plunk, 39, of Corinth, Mississippi, for conspiring to distribute and distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) for profit on Instagram and Telegram.
“Justin Plunk exploited the most vulnerable members of our society to turn a profit,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva for the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “He operated a business that trafficked in horrific images of the sexual exploitation of children both in America and abroad. The verdict in this case sends a strong message that such horrific and depraved conduct will be met with accountability.”
“Justin Plunk was an active participant in a conspiracy that, for years, preyed upon and sexually exploited children for profit through a variety of online platforms, including popular social media and children’s gaming apps and mobile payment services,” said U.S. Attorney Troy Rivetti for the Western District of Pennsylvania. “Although it can never undo the harm these victims experienced, this verdict holds Plunk responsible for his role in the recruitment and abuse of those minors, and is another example of our office’s commitment to working with our law enforcement partners at all levels to protect children from such crimes and to prosecute to the fullest extent of the law predators who exploit and conspire to exploit minors.”
“Today’s verdict reflects the jury’s clear recognition of the harm caused by those who exploit children for their own profit,” said Special Agent in Charge Richard Evanchec of the FBI’s Pittsburgh Field Office Our children are precious, and their safety must remain our highest priority. We are grateful for the dedicated FBI employees who work every day to protect the most vulnerable among us and to ensure that those who prey on them are brought to justice.”
According to court documents and information provided during the trial, the criminal conspiracy operated online from at least 2021 to 2024. The conspiracy recruited minor girls, including girls as young as 10 years old, to create “packages” of CSAM images and videos and participate in live video calls with customers. The conspiracy operated over numerous platforms, including Instagram, Snapchat, and Telegram. One minor girl was introduced to the conspiracy on Roblox. The conspiracy also used multiple payment methods, including CashApp, Venmo, Walmart, and Roblox gift cards. Investigation revealed that Plunk was connected to the conspiracy in numerous ways, including receiving the proceeds of the conspiracy — in excess of $57,000 — in the form of cash transfers and Walmart gift cards. Plunk had previously been convicted of enticement of a child for sexual purposes in Mississippi in 2016.
Plunk is facing a maximum penalty of 40 years in prison. He is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 26, 2027. A federal district judge will determine the sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
FBI Pittsburgh investigated the case, with assistance from the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.
Trial Attorney Gwendelynn Bills of the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Heidi Grogan for the Western District of Pennsylvania prosecuted the case.
This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit justice.gov/psc. For more information about Internet safety education, please visit justice.gov/psc and click on the “Resources” tab on the left of the page.
title: Mississippi Man Convicted by Federal Jury of Participating in a Criminal Conspiracy to Distribute Child Sexual Abuse Material

HARRISBURG - The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania announced that Deontrae Marquis Jackson, age 35, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was sentenced on October 1, 2026, to 41 months’ imprisonment by United States District Judge Keli M. Neary for straw purchasing firearms.

According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, Jackson worked with others to purchase firearms in the names of women who had no criminal records and were lawfully allowed to buy the firearms. Then, after they got the firearms, they were sold or transferred to felons. In January to February 2021, Jackson and his fellow participants visited federal firearms licensed dealers in Lancaster and York and tried to purchase seven firearms.

When imposing sentence, Judge Neary noted that Jackson had a long criminal history involving drug trafficking and firearms offenses. Additionally, the Judge noted that Jackson fled while the case was pending. Almost two years later, the United States Marshal Service arrested him living in Oregon.

Jackson was found guilty of the conspiracy and providing false statements to federally licensed firearms dealers after a three-day bench trial. Co-defendants Alicia Butler-Sanchez and Olivia Johnson pled guilty and were sentenced in 2022 and 2023. They received probationary sentences.

The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and Explosives investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Michael A. Consiglio is prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

title: Philadelphia Man Sentenced to 41 Months in Prison for Straw Purchasing Firearms

CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE HONORS LOCAL HISPANIC COMMUNITY DURING HISPANIC AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH
Recognizes five local leaders for their outstanding contributions to Rochester through public service, cultural leadership, and community advocacy

Coast Guard offloads over $226 million in illicit drugs interdicted in the Eastern Pacific
Southeast Public Affairs - SoutheastPublicAffairs@uscg.mil
MIAMI — U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Tampa’s crew offloaded approximately 29,600 pounds of cocaine and 3,355 pounds of marijuana, worth an estimated $226.7 million, Wednesday, in Port Everglades.
The seized contraband was the result of six interdictions in international waters of the Eastern Pacific Ocean.
"This crew was phenomenal in successfully stopping a combined 32,000 pounds of contraband from reaching American shores," said Capt. Joshua DiPietro, commanding officer of Tampa. "By honing their maritime skills, standing the watch and working together, they intercepted over $226 million in illicit narcotics. Their resounding teamwork during complex operations is astounding. I commend them on their tremendous tenacity and true camaraderie as they worked through long days and nights to successfully complete difficult cases and continue the disruption of transnational criminal organizations."
The following assets and crews were involved in the interdiction operations:
- U.S. Coast Guard Tactical Law Enforcement Team - Pacific, LEDET 102
- Coast Guard Helicopter Interdiction Tactical Squadron
- USS Gridley
Coast Guard Cutter Tampa’s offload continues the Coast Guard’s mission to interdict, seize, and disrupt transshipment of cocaine and other bulk illicit drugs by sea. The Coast Guard’s persistent operations and rapid response have denied criminal organizations billions in illicit revenue and prevented the flow of dangerous drugs into American communities.
“The Coast Guard continues to leverage its authorities and partnerships across the Western Hemisphere to degrade Transnational Criminal Organizations’ ability to harm American communities,” said Vice Adm. Jo-Ann Burdian, commander Atlantic Area. “Success stories like these highlight our commitment to continuing to control, secure, and defend the nation’s maritime borders and approaches.”
The U.S. Coast Guard works alongside local, state, federal, and international partners to detect, disrupt, and deter transnational criminal organizations and illicit maritime trafficking in support of Operation Pacific Viper. Operating under the Coast Guard’s Title 14 law enforcement authorities, and with critical support from partner nations, these unified efforts span every stage of counter-drug operations from initial detection and monitoring to maritime interdiction and criminal prosecution. Focused on critical regions such as the Eastern Pacific Ocean and the Southwest District's area of responsibility, the Coast Guard is part of a whole-of-government approach to combat transnational organized crime.
Coast Guard Cutter Tampa is a 270-foot medium endurance cutter homeported in Portsmouth, Virginia, under U.S. Coast Guard Atlantic Area Command.

U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02), top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair on the Senate Appropriations Committee, sent a letter to General Services Administration (GSA) Administrator Edward Forst requesting GSA prioritize construction of two stalled border station projects in Northwest Washington. Senator Murray and Congressman Larsen sent this letter on September 22 and have yet to receive response from GSA. 
“It has come to our attention that Washington state’s Kenneth G. Ward and Sumas Land Ports of Entry (LPOE) projects are temporarily prevented from moving forward,” the lawmakers wrote. “We write to express our concern regarding this decision by General Services Administration (GSA).” 
A land port of entry (LPOE) is a federal border facility used to control the entry and departure of people and cargo at a land border. Congress appropriated $3.4 billion to modernize 26 LPOEs across the United States in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law of 2021, which both Senator Murray and Representative Larsen helped become law. As of August 12th, 2026, the GSA has temporarily prevented nine of those projects from moving forward, including the Kenneth G. Ward Land Port of Entry in Lynden and the Sumas Land Port of Entry.  
“Both LPOEs are vital border crossings for Washington state and Canada and play a significant role in trade and economic development that is relevant to the economic vitality of the United States,” the lawmakers continued. “Delaying these projects will have consequential impacts on the nation’s supply chain, labor market, and national security.” 
Rep. Larsen and Sen. Murray stressed the importance of certainty about the status of the border station projects for city officials in Sumas and Lynden to plan for the impact that construction will have to downtown buildings and the local economy. 
“These projects are also key to local development plans in the cities of Sumas and Lynden, where the LPOEs are located,” the lawmakers wrote. “LPOE modernization will impact several existing buildings in Sumas’s downtown core, and Lynden is preparing to take on additional commercial traffic. Prolonged uncertainty on project timelines will only lead to more disruption and delays in economic development of these cities.” 
The lawmakers urged GSA Administrator Forst to prioritize the Kenneth G. Ward and Sumas Land Port of Entry projects when the GSA reassesses the prioritization of the remaining nine LPOEs in the coming months and requested continued updates on decisions regarding the projects. 
The full text of the letter can be read here. 
Larsen and Murray Conduct Oversight of GSA Under the Trump Administration
As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray has led oversight of GSA’s reckless effort to dump federal properties, pressing the Trump administration on why it terminated leases without notifying Congress as required by law, and how veterans, taxpayers, Tribal members, and farmers would still get the in-person help they depend on. Murray continues to hold the Trump administration accountable for skirting the law, keeping Congress in the dark, and cutting off services families rely on.
In a Transportation & Infrastructure Committee oversight hearing in March, Rep. Larsen raised concerns about the GSA’s tumultuous first 14 months under the Trump administration and a memorandum of understanding (MOU) that the GSA signed with the Defense Ministry of Pakistan without providing evidence of the GSA’s legal jurisdiction to enter into the MOU or engage in redeveloping the private hotel.  
This July, Rep. Larsen and Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Ranking Member Greg Stanton (AZ-04) sent a letter to Administrator Forst seeking answers about the agency’s involvement with the renovation of the Roosevelt Hotel and reporting from Bloomberg that the GSA signed a $1.4 million contract with Sullivan & Cromwell—a law firm with significant ties to the Trump administration—to provide legal services regarding the privately-owned property.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a division within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to reimagine the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. As outlined in a new white paper, the Initiative will develop an optimized, fit-for-purpose framework that reflects the realities of rare disease drug development by considering the nuances of each disease, patient needs, product type and the evidence that can be realistically generated in small patient populations.
To solicit feedback on the Rare Disease Framework Initiative from patients and disease advocates, industry, and others, the FDA will host an October 28 meeting at the FDA’s White Oak campus. The meeting will be facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA.
“Americans with rare diseases cannot afford a regulatory system that treats every condition the same,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Under President Trump, FDA is rethinking rare disease drug development by putting patients at the center and matching regulatory requirements to the realities of small patient populations. We will remove unnecessary barriers, embrace cutting-edge science, and accelerate promising treatments while upholding FDA’s rigorous standards.”
“Patients and families living with rare diseases have few or no approved treatment options, and the burden of uncertainty can extend across every part of their lives,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “As we learn more about rare diseases and better understand the breadth of suffering they cause, we must ensure that America’s regulatory system remains at the forefront — prepared to respond to emerging science, anticipate the needs of patients and families, and help bring safe and effective therapies to those who need them. The FDA will fight hard for patients by building a more consistent, predictable, and innovative approach to rare disease drug development while maintaining the rigorous standards Americans expect from the FDA.”
The FDA has long used regulatory flexibility and developed targeted programs to support innovation in the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. These efforts have led to meaningful advances for patients and families. Nevertheless, with only 5% or so of rare conditions having an FDA-approved treatment, the FDA agrees with patients, drug developers, and providers that more must be done to speed the development of safe and effective treatments for rare diseases. In developing the framework, the FDA is committed to the following:
- Providing greater clarity, consistency, and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance and transparent communication.
- Embedding the patient’s voice both early, and at clearly defined milestones, in the drug development and review process.
- Further leveraging external expertise to support customization of regulatory review.
- Building shared resources, robust training, and institutional knowledge on rare disease drug development and review.
- Applying risk-based approaches, particularly to chemistry, manufacturing, and controls review and pre-approval inspections.
- Championing the use of cutting-edge science, novel methods and innovative statistical approaches in rare disease drug development.
The Initiative is led by the FDA’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, partnering with the Office of the Commissioner, the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.
“Patients with rare diseases and their families deserve a regulatory process that addresses the uniqueness of each of their conditions while maintaining the FDA’s rigorous standards,” said the Hub’s Director, Amy Comstock Rick, J.D. “A bold vision to reimagine the framework for rare disease drug development that builds on key learnings and milestones is necessary to meet this moment. This new framework will enhance consistency and predictability for both sponsors and for patients.”
Further opportunities to provide input will follow the public meeting, including sector-specific roundtables, Requests for Information, and internal FDA feedback sessions. This feedback will inform the detailed development of a new framework, which might include potential new or revised guidance, revisions to regulations, staff training, and organizational changes.
Additional Resources
•    FDA Rare Disease Innovation Hub
•    Rare Disease Framework
The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.
###
title: FDA Launches the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to Develop a Holistic, Fit-For-Purpose Framework for Rare Disease Drug Development
