DHS, ICE comment on dangerous consequences of sanctuary policies
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and the ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations Executive Associate Director Marcos Charles commented on the dangers of sanctuary policies following the arrest and shooting of a criminal alien offender in New York City.
“Sanctuary politicians create an environment for criminal activity to thrive, not for American citizens be safe.” said Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “President Trump made it very clear that he was going to restore law and order in our cities, in our towns, and in our states, in spite of sanctuary politicians that put criminals in front of law-abiding citizens. Sanctuary cities and politicians endanger the safety of the public. That is not a secret. That is exactly what takes place.”
On Oct. 8, ICE officers arrested Oscar Bergal, a criminal illegal alien and documented associate of the notorious Trinitario street gang in the Bronx, NY. Bergal’s criminal history includes a conviction for grand larceny as well as charges for multiple counts of robbery, assault, larceny, weapons possession, possession of stolen property, and dangerous drugs. Twice in January of 2026 Bengal had protection orders lodged against him. Both remain active.
“[Bergal] refused to comply with the orders of federal law enforcement officers, ICE officers,” said ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations Executive Associate Director Marcos Charles. “Bergal is the subject of an HSI investigation; he is a known associate of a gang in New York; and he has evaded law enforcement before when we attempted to arrest him before.”
On the afternoon of Oct. 8, ICE ERO New York City officers positively identified Bergal driving his vehicle. Officers used their vehicles to conduct a vehicle stop and approached Bergal’s vehicle on foot. Bergal then rammed the ICE vehicles and appeared that he intended to strike officers on foot. Based on Bergal’s actions, and his vehicle’s proximity to the officers, as well as the rapidly evolving circumstances, ICE officers reasonably believed that they faced an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury. One ICE officer discharged his firearm in self-defense, striking Bergal.
“Bergal refused lawful orders to exit his vehicle. He then accelerated his vehicle smashing into two of our ICE vehicles. He then weaponized his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate his vehicle toward other officers,” Charles said. “Our officer, believing that their life, the lives of their partners and the lives of the general public were in danger, used their training and fired their weapon.”
Bergal was struck in the neck and sustained a superficial injury. ICE officers rendered first aid until the New York Police Department and Emergency Medical Services arrived, evaluated Bergal, and provided additional medical care. EMS transported Bergal to a local hospital for further evaluation and treatment. ICE officers arrested Bergal upon his release from the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Bergal remains in ICE custody.
Bergal illegally entered the United States on an unknown date, at an unknown location, and without being inspected, admitted, or paroled by a U.S. immigration official.
On Dec.7, 2023, NYPD officers arrested Bergal for Robbery-1st: Forcible Theft Armed with A Deadly Weapon. Bergal pled guilty to the lesser charge of Grand Larceny 4th: Property Taken From Person. He was sentenced to five years’ probation.
Bergal has active charges in New York for charges for multiple counts of robbery, assault, larceny, weapons possession, possession of stolen property, and dangerous drugs. Twice in January of 2026 the state of New York issued two protection orders against Bergal on Jan. 29, 2026. Both remain active.
“From January 2025 to September of this year, we have lodged 14,766 immigration detainers in the state of New York. These are for individuals who are locked up, with criminal backgrounds, that the state of New York has in custody,” Mullin said. “We have asked that these 14,766 detainers be honored because these are illegal aliens with criminal records who should never be allowed back on the streets. Silence – absolute silence is what we have heard from New York. These detainers represent 47,750 felony charges. We know that these are the worst of the worst.”

“The men and women of ICE and DHS are out there every day enforcing our nation’s laws,” Mullin said. “We are not picking and choosing which laws to enforce like the sanctuary politicians. CONCORD – Falmouth, Massachusetts resident Leo Anzivino, Jr., 35, pleaded guilty today to a money laundering conspiracy in connection with a more than $6 million health care fraud scheme, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan and Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division announce.

Anzivino pleaded guilty to one count of money laundering conspiracy before U.S. District Judge Landya McCafferty. The Court scheduled sentencing for January 21, 2027. The defendant faces a maximum penalty of ten years in prison. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes that govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

According to court documents and statements made in court, Anzivino conspired with others to launder health care fraud proceeds. Specifically, Anzivino agreed to be the straw or nominal owner of Advanced Medical Supply Corp. (Advanced), located in Rochester, New Hampshire, even though his co-conspirators were in fact the beneficial owners and managers of Advanced. Thereafter, Advanced submitted more than $6 million in claims to Medicare for durable medical equipment (DME) – such as knee braces and back braces – that Medicare beneficiaries did not need and that doctors did not prescribe. Instead, Advanced supported these claims using fake orders from physicians who did not actually write or submit those orders. Medicare paid more than $3 million as a result of these false and fraudulent claims.

Medicare beneficiaries returned boxes of DME to Advanced with notes stating that they had not ordered the products and alleging a fraud or scam, some of which are depicted below.

Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return “Did Not Order” the Medical Products and that it was a “FRAUD!!”

Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that the Medical Products Were Sent “Without Prior Consent of My Physician or Myself”

Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that “This Must Be Some Type of Medicare Scam”

For his part, Anzivino helped hide his co-conspirators’ involvement with Advanced by being listed as the owner of Advanced on the Medicare enrollment paperwork. He also submitted false and fraudulent bank account opening documents to a bank in New Hampshire, falsely certifying that he was the sole owner of 25 percent or more of the equity interests of Advanced when others, including a co-conspirator, were Advanced’s true owners.

Anzivino then laundered the fraud proceeds by, at his co-conspirator’s direction, seeking to transfer more than $1 million from the Advanced bank account in New Hampshire to companies that were affiliated with the co-conspirator. When told by a bank employee that the bank had not reached a level of confidence that the other companies were legitimate, and that Anzivino should do his own research into these companies, Anzivino instead opened a bank account at another bank with branches in Massachusetts.

Anzivino learned that Advanced’s ability to bill Medicare would be revoked for various deficiencies, including an inability to verify proof of his ownership of Advanced. Anzivino then sent messages to another individual discussing that revocation, explaining that “All the ppl who gave me money are going to come back for it now my shits revoked,” stating that his co-conspirator “still wants me to wire him money,” and claiming that “I ain’t wiring shit.” Despite this, over the next five weeks, Anzivino proceeded to wire $1,494,938.09 across three separate transactions.

In 2024, the government seized approximately $353,768.29 in assets tied to the alleged scheme from Advanced’s bank account.

The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Inspector General and the Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case with valuable assistance from IRS-Criminal Investigations and the Department of War Office of Inspector General’s Defense Criminal Investigative Services. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Hunter and Matthew Vicinanzo and Trial Attorneys John Howard and Tiffany Wynn of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit .
title: Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Launder Proceeds of $6 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme

TRENTON, N.J. – An Ocean County man was sentenced for the transportation of a stolen firearm, United States Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Luiz Vargas, a/k/a, “El Biggie,” 26, of Jackson, New Jersey, pleaded guilty on May 26, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Georgette Castner to a one-count Information charging him with transportation of a stolen firearm. Judge Castner imposed the 78-month sentence on October 7, 2026 in Trenton federal court.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

Beginning in January 2025, law enforcement investigated Vargas for trafficking firearms into New Jersey from, among other places, Texas and Maryland. Using a confidential source acting at the direction and supervision of law enforcement, officers conducted four controlled purchases of firearms, which yielded a total of eight firearms: two semiautomatic rifles and six handguns. Two of the handguns were reported stolen out of Texas and Colorado, respectively, and the two semiautomatic rifles had no serial numbers or other identifiable markings on them. On at least one occasion, Vargas provided cocaine to the confidential source after being unable to follow through with a promised sale of firearms. Vargas has never held a federal license to deal or manufacture firearms.

In addition to the prison term, Judge Castner sentenced Vargas to three years of supervised release following Vargas’ term of imprisonment.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the sentencing. He also thanked the United States ICE ERO Newark Field Office, under the direction of Field Office Director Arthur J. Wilson, Jr., the Howell Township Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police John Storrow, the Ocean County Sheriff’s Office, under the direction Sheriff Michael G. Mastronardy, the Asbury Park Police Department, under the direction of Police Director John B. Hayes, the Freehold Borough Police Department, under the Direction of Chief of Police Chris Colaner, the Lakewood Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Gregory H. Meyer, the Little Silver Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Paul Halpin, the Marlboro Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Peter Pezzullo, the Middletown Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police R. Craig Weber, the Monroe Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Griffin N. Banos, and the Wall Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Sean O’Halloran, for their assistance in the investigation.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan S. Garelick of the U.S. Attorney’s Office Criminal Division in Trenton.

While in Iowa, Administrator Zeldin Proposes 100% Reallocation for Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemption Volumes and Opens Markets for American Farmers
WASHINGTON – While in Peosta, Iowa, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin announced revisions to the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) “Set 2” rule volumes to keep the historic and necessary volumes intact and increase target markets for American farmers. In response to the higher than projected 2025 small refinery exemption (SRE) decisions and the needs of American farmers, the agency is proposing two options for revisions, both of which would reallocate 100% of the difference between projected and actual exempted volumes for 2025 SREs.
The Trump EPA understands the importance of providing a predictable and stable market for farmers, refiners, and American consumers to both maintain economic competitiveness and keep energy prices low. The proposal reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensuring America’s hardworking farmers continue to have a robust and growing market for their crops, while also unleashing American energy.
“In each action taken, EPA works to deliver for all Americans. From our farmers to our energy workers, each has an important role to play in growing our economy and ensuring America’s energy independence,” said EPA Administrator Zeldin. “As soon as we got into office, American farmers asked the Trump EPA not to give them handouts but create avenues for them to enter additional markets. As our farmers continue to harvest their crops, today’s proposal is working to maintain a strong and durable market for them to sell to.”
“American biofuel producers have stepped up to the plate to provide record production, helping to fuel our nation and provide more market opportunities for our farmers. I’m thrilled to see Administrator Zeldin act on this growing momentum and provide a path forward to 100% reallocation by 2027,” said U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “The American biofuel industry provides over $100 billion in economic activity and supports over 100,000 American jobs while helping to deliver on President Trump’s energy dominance agenda. The Trump Administration will continue to stand by and deliver results for our farmers.”
“The Trump administration is carrying through on its promise to support Iowa family farmers and biofuel producers. I worked closely with the White House, along with Sen. Ernst and Reps. Hinson, Miller-Meeks, Nunn and Feenstra, to secure full reallocation for all exempted biofuels, and I appreciate the Trump administration following through in a timely fashion. Today’s decision is a major boost for Iowa’s rural economy and the 31,000 Iowa jobs that biofuels directly employ,” said Senator Chuck Grassley (R-IA).
“As farmers continue to harvest their crops across Iowa, we must reaffirm our commitment in providing certainty and reliable markets,” said Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA). “Reallocating the waived small refinery exemption volumes into the 2026 and 2027 Renewable Volume Obligations will strengthen our farm economy, bolster domestic markets, and lower prices for consumers. I thank President Trump and Administrator Zeldin for taking this important step to put farmers first and ensure they have the resources needed to succeed.”
“Farmers across Southeast Iowa are feeling the squeeze, and they need a market they can count on. I’ve worked to make this a reality because Iowa farmers deserve reliable markets for the crops they grow. This announcement helps deliver on that goal, creating more demand for Iowa corn and soybeans,” said Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA-01). “I’m grateful to Administrator Zeldin and President Trump for following through, and I will always fight to put Iowa farmers first.”
“Biofuels should be front and center in any plan to unleash domestic energy production and lower costs at the pump. Earlier this year, the administration announced the strongest biofuels blending targets in history, driving demand for Iowa ag products and new investment in our rural communities,” said Representative Ashley Hinson (R-IA-02). “Today’s proposal reflects the 100% reallocation agreement I helped secure in August—making sure refinery exemptions don’t reduce demand for homegrown biofuels and our farmers and producers are made whole. With farmers facing such difficult conditions right now, getting this across the finish line is a big deal. I’m grateful to Administrator Zeldin for working with me to protect the Renewable Fuel Standard, and I’ll keep pushing relentlessly for Iowa farmers and biofuels producers throughout this process.”
“Homegrown ethanol and biodiesel help us drive down the price of fuel at the pump for families and boost demand for what we grow in Iowa. Our farmers and biofuel producers built this market, and I fought to protect it because it keeps more of that fuel flowing to drivers and keeps the demand with Iowa farmers instead of foreign oil producers. I’ll keep working with Administrator Zeldin to get this rule finalized so families and farmers get the certainty they deserve,” said Representative Zach Nunn (R-IA-03).
When EPA promulgated the “Set 2” rule, the agency estimated the volume of hardship exemptions that small refineries would receive for their 2025 renewable fuel obligations. The August 31,2026, SRE decisions for those 2025 obligations exceeded EPA’s expectations, and an additional 770 million renewable identification numbers (RINs) worth of renewable fuels were exempted from RFS obligations. EPA is now proposing to fully reallocate this volume, to ensure farmers maintain and increase access to their markets. The agency recognizes the importance of getting stakeholder input on the best approach to do so. Therefore, EPA is seeking public comment on two proposed approaches:
- Proposed approach one: EPA would divide the additional 2025 SRE volume equally between the 2026 and 2027 compliance years.
- Proposed approach two: EPA would reallocate all the additional 2025 SRE volume to the 2027 compliance year
EPA will take public comments on the proposal until December 4, 2026.
Additionally, the proposed revision to the 2026 standards may extend the existing 2026 compliance reporting deadline of March 31, 2027. If finalized, this proposal will ensure that all the benefits of the “Set 2” rule will be realized for American farmers.
Today’s announcement is part of the Trump Administration’s all of government approach to opening markets for American farmers. By supporting a strong RFS program, EPA is working to keep generational farmers thriving and rural communities economically rich—Congress’ intent for the program.
Background
Announced on March 27, 2026, by President Trump during the Great American Agriculture Celebration, the historic “Set 2” rule realigned the RFS program with Congress’ original intent of increasing the use of homegrown American biofuels, putting American farmers first. In the 20th year of the RFS program, the final rule sets the highest renewable fuel volumes in the history of the program. With EPA estimating the final rule would generate over $10 billion for rural economies and create over 100,000 new jobs in the agricultural and manufacturing sectors, the Trump EPA’s action created a larger, more stable, and more reliable domestic market for U.S. crops.
title: While in Iowa, Administrator Zeldin Proposes 100% Reallocation for Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemption Volumes and Opens Markets for American Farmers

A federal court has granted the Federal Trade Commission’s request to temporarily halt the activities of Digital Forensics Corporation LLC and its CEO for allegedly defrauding consumers out of millions of dollars using false and deceptive promises relating to “sextortion assistance services.”
Sextortion is a rapidly growing threat to Americans, routinely carried out by foreign scammers who threaten to publish a nude or sexual image of the victim unless the victim pays the criminal.
In a complaint the FTC alleges that Digital Forensics, along with its owner Dmitry Belkin and several affiliated companies, misled victims of sextortion into paying at least $60 million by falsely claiming that it would provide sextortion assistance services.
“Digital Forensics preys on consumers already in crisis, exploiting victims of sextortion by using fear to pressure them into paying thousands of dollars for services that are never provided,” said Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection. “The FTC is committed to protecting consumers from sextortion and other crimes involving non-consensual intimate visual images. That includes taking action against companies that take advantage of consumers experiencing a crisis and engage in deceptive practices that prey on victims’ vulnerability and use abusive tactics that exacerbate the harm.”
The FTC alleged that Digital Forensics pushed victims to purchase a “Phase 1” package of sextortion assistance services, which was supposed to include tracking the sextortionist’s location, communicating with the sextortionist, producing a detailed investigative report and reporting the crime to law enforcement. Despite charging consumers between $1,499 and $20,000, as alleged in the complaint, Digital Forensics, in numerous instances, did not perform the promised services.
After collecting payment for Phase 1, Digital Forensics then pressured victims to pay for “Phase 2” services, which supposedly would include ongoing monitoring of the victims’ accounts and reporting sextortion attacks to law enforcement. The FTC alleges Digital Forensics did not follow through on its promises. To hide these failures and maintain its public reputation, Digital Forensics suppressed negative reviews by its customers and generated thousands of fake positive online reviews, according to the complaint.
The FTC’s complaint alleges that Digital Forensics uses advertisements on search, video sharing and social media platforms such as Google, YouTube and X to target sextortion victims looking for help. The company allegedly advertises that it can “track down cyber criminals across the world [and] beat them” and “identify [perpetrators] with a high degree of success [and] give law enforcement the evidence they need to make arrests.” Instead, Digital Forensics often simply blocked the sextortionist on the victims’ social media accounts—which victims can do themselves—created fake chat transcripts, used made-up investigative information and did not contact law enforcement, according to the complaint.
Consumers are told, the FTC alleges, not to pay the sextortionist but instead to contact Digital Forensics “right away” to let the experts “fight back.” Digital Forensics also allegedly tells consumers not to block sextortionists online and instead let the company handle it by continuing to communicate with the sextortionist, which is contrary to the advice of the FBI and other law enforcement experts.
Specifically, the FTC alleges Digital Forensics unlawfully:
- Made false promises about its sextortion assistance services: Digital Forensics made false promises including that it would communicate with sextortionists on behalf of the consumer, conduct a “tracking campaign” to gather accurate details on the sextortionist and report the sextortionist’s illegal activity to law enforcement to stop the sextortion attack. But the company routinely took little or no action to stop the sextortion attack and faked the data reported to consumers in its “report.” When consumers demanded a refund, Digital Forensics failed to honor its own refund policy.
- Conducted a telemarketing campaign that preyed on victims of sextortion: On phone calls with consumers, Digital Forensics’ telemarketers use scare tactics tailored to consumers’ “pain points” to pressure consumers into paying exorbitant prices for services the company routinely does not deliver. For example, if the victim is a military servicemember, telemarketers warn that the sextortion attack can result in a dishonorable discharge, or if the victim is married, they claim that the sextortionist will target the victim’s spouse and in-laws.
- Collected financial information using false statements: Defendants obtained consumers’ financial information using false statements about their services and charged consumers for services they never completed.
- Generated fake positive consumer reviews: Defendants misled consumers by using employees based in India to write fake reviews, purchasing positive reviews from Uber drivers who had never bought or used Defendants’ services and coercing customers into posting positive reviews before they had actually received any services from Digital Forensics.
The FTC alleges that Belkin, Digital Forensics and affiliated companies violated the FTC Act, the Telemarketing Sales Rule, the Reviews and Testimonials Rule and the Gramm-Leach- Bliley Act.
The Commission vote authorizing the staff to file the complaint was 2-0. The complaint was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio against Belkin, Digital Forensics, 1st All Data Recovery LLC, 1st All File Recovery USA Inc., I & D Belkin LLC, Remote Backup Corp LLC, Digital Cyber Forensics Investigations LLC, Cyber Digital Forensics Response LLC, 1st All Investments LLC, Salon Place LLC, VPR Academy LLC, 21111 Chagrin Investments LLC and 4350 Renaissance LLC.
The FTC thanks the Better Business Bureau Serving Greater Cleveland and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children for their assistance in this investigation.
NOTE: The Commission files a complaint when it has “reason to believe” that the named defendants are violating or are about to violate the law and it appears to the Commission that a proceeding is in the public interest. The case will be decided by the court.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Follow the FTC on social media, read consumer alerts and the business blog, and sign up to get the latest FTC news and alerts.
title: FTC Sues Operator of Sextortion Relief Scheme for Misleading Consumers into Believing it Would Identify Criminals and End Sextortion Attacks

Sixth North Carolina Return Preparer Sentenced in $23.9 Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme
The owner of a North Carolina tax return preparation business was sentenced on October 1, 2026, to 60 months in prison for conspiring to prepare false returns claiming fraudulent refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Nejlai Mitchell owned and operated a tax return preparation business out of Lumberton, North Carolina, and Hope Mills, North Carolina. From approximately April 2022 through May 2023, Mitchell and seven employees filed false tax returns seeking fraudulent refunds based on the paid sick and family leave credit, a credit passed by Congress to aid struggling businesses during the COVID-19 global pandemic. The conspiracy resulted in a total of approximately $23.9 million in fraudulent tax refund claims. The IRS paid out approximately $13,890,697 of that amount.
Five other return preparers have also been sentenced for their roles in the scheme. The co-conspirators prepared federal tax returns for clients that included materially false items. On September 3, 2026, Tiffany Moody was sentenced to 26 months in prison. On July 8, 2026, Shaneen Ray was sentenced to 18 months in prison, Eyoubo McBurney was sentenced to 18 months in prison, and Sylvia Swindell was sentenced to 16 months in prison. On July 9, 2026, Katrena Stanback was sentenced to six months in prison.
Mitchell pleaded guilty to conspiracy and preparing and filing false tax returns. The tax return preparation business’s office manager, Whitnee Leach, pleaded guilty in May 2026 to participating in the same conspiracy and filing false tax returns. The remaining five defendants pleaded guilty to preparing and filing false tax returns for clients. Jeannie Negron pleaded guilty in August 2025 to the same charges.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney W. Ellis Boyle of the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorney Caroline Pearson and Assistant U.S. Attorney Ethan Ontjes of the Eastern District of North Carolina are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Sixth North Carolina Return Preparer Sentenced in $23.9 Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Guangtian Ha, 42, of Haverford, Pennsylvania, was arrested last week and charged by indictment with cyberstalking, arising from threatening online messages that would be reasonably expected to cause substantial emotional distress to the recipient (“Victim 1”) and his family.

At a hearing this afternoon, the defendant was ordered detained in federal custody pending trial.

The indictment alleges that, from on or about October 9, 2025, through on or about May 20, 2026, Ha used at least four anonymous X accounts to direct threatening messages to Victim 1, with the defendant frequently utilizing virtual private networks to obfuscate his internet protocol address and make tracing the source of the messages more difficult.

For example, as alleged in the indictment, in or about January 2026 through in or about February 2026, the defendant, using X account “America1stLM” posted a series of threatening and harassing messages directed at Victim 1, including: “Jew, get the f[***] out of my country”; “Jew pig, get the f[***] out of Lower Merion”; “If jews are so special then they should also be placed in special camps and receive special treatments”; “LM jews are going to have it big time, jew. Remember this. You scums have had it too easy. Goyim are taking America back, blood-guzzling demons.”

On or about May 10, 2026, as further alleged, the defendant, using X account “DlGoyim” posted the following message directed at Victim 1: “@[Victim 1] Eliminate the jewish cockroaches. Exterminate the jewish state. [Victim 1], you will have nowhere to go. Your family has no future in the US. Give it another 10 years, and you shall see a true holocaust.”

In addition, the indictment alleges that at least one of Ha’s messages to Victim 1 included a reference to Victim 1’s minor child — “@[Victim 1] Jew, watch your [Victim 1’s minor child’s true name]. There shall be a sign.” — as well as multiple posts containing Victim 1 and his family’s home address.

In total, Ha allegedly sent approximately 50 messages to Victim 1 using at least four different X accounts.

“This online campaign of antisemitic abuse was not only repugnant, but criminal,” said U.S. Attorney Metcalf. “We will ensure that every citizen deserves to be free from the threatening harassment that took place in this case.”

“Cyberstalking and online harassment are far from harmless. These offenses can cause real harm for victims and their families,” said Wayne A. Jacobs, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Philadelphia. “The FBI and our law enforcement partners are committed to holding those responsible accountable and protecting individuals from threats, intimidation, and harassment, whether online or offline.”

If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum possible sentence of five years in prison.

This case was investigated by FBI Philadelphia’s Newtown Square Resident Agency and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Anthony Carissimi, Sima Kazmir, and Mark Dubnoff.

The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.
title: Delaware County Man Charged With Cyberstalking in Connection With Threatening Messages Sent Via Anonymous X Accounts

text:
Kaptur, Murray: As Families Pay More & More for Energy, Reports Show Trump Energy Department Withholding Billions and Playing Politics
Toledo, OH – Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, released the following statement on the Trump Administration holding back or cutting off Billions of dollars Congress provided the Department of Energy to bring new energy online and lower Americans’ energy costs. Four recent reports detail how, over the last 18 months, President Trump’s policies have raised energy costs for families and delayed and defunded critical energy investments.
“President Trump hasn’t just sent gas prices through the roof with his war with Iran; he and his Administration have systematically held up and cut off energy investments Congress has made that should be lowering families’ energy bills. Congress gave the Department of Energy tens of Billions of dollars to build out the power grid and cut the costs that families pay to heat and cool their homes. But the Trump Administration is still holding that money back and letting politics decide which projects survive. This President’s corruption is already sending Americans’ energy bills higher. The Constitution gives Congress the power of the purse. We will keep pressing until this money reaches the projects and families it was meant for,” said Kaptur and Murray.
Congress provided funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the annual Energy and Water Development appropriations bills for a variety of cost-cutting energy investments. The funding supports power lines, grid upgrades, home energy savings, and bringing more power online. But starting in January 2025, the Trump Administration froze funds for energy programs and kept them frozen after Kaptur and Murray demanded answers. The Department announced the cancellation of 24 awards worth $3.7 Billion in May 2025 and another 321 worth nearly $8 Billion on October 1, 2025. In July 2026, the Department’s lawyers admitted in court that the October cancellations were based solely on the politics of each recipient’s state.
Four reports released recently show the Department of Energy is failing to spend money Congress provided—driving up Americans’ costs—and it is letting politics drive its decisions:
- Recent analysis from Energy Innovation, which includes state-level impacts, found that the Trump Administration’s energy policy changes since January 2025, including the Department’s cancellation of hydrogen hub funding, will cost households an additional $920 Billion for energy from 2026 through 2040, or about $6,500 more in energy costs per household.
- The Department of Energy Alumni Network and Lawyers for Good Government reported that a year after the Department cancelled hundreds of awards, 61 percent of terminated awards remain in limbo, 69 percent of the awards the Department said it would keep have received negligible funding in the past six months, and another 1,731 projects worth $3.9 Billion have heard nothing from the Department.
- The Natural Resources Defense Council published internal Department records, obtained through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit, indicating that DOE’s committee reviewing awards for termination was made up entirely of political appointees and Department of Government Efficiency staff. This follows DOE’s earlier admission in court that its decision to cancel energy projects “was based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state.”
- The EFI Foundation found that 94 percent of the $57.5 Billion Congress provided DOE through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act has still not reached recipients, and $29.3 Billion, or 51 percent, has not been legally committed to any project.

The Energy Department Announces Intention to Support Adding 2.5 GW of Grid Capacity and 800 Jobs
October 13, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced plans to lower electricity costs and strengthen grid reliability by supporting the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in funding 84 transmission and distribution projects across eight states. The projects are expected to add approximately 2.5 gigawatts (GW) of grid capacity to help mitigate outages and create greater grid resilience. The TVA award is for approximately $581 million in total, including $250 million in federal funding and about $331 million in applicant cost-share funding.
As part of the Resilience Amplified: Multi-Market Grid Interconnection Initiative funding award under the Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) project, the investments will help ensure 2.58 million families and businesses have access to the affordable, reliable, and secure power they need. The project is estimated to support about 800 jobs.
“Since day one, President Trump has recognized that years of misguided energy policies under the previous administration left our bulk power system less robust than it should be,” said U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy James P. Danly. “America is blessed with an abundance of natural resources and some of the most advanced technology in the world, but we must have the generation and transmission infrastructure necessary to support our rapidly growing economy and its electricity needs. These investments with TVA will help reduce congestion, improve efficiency, and make better use of our existing transmission system to lower costs for ratepayers while delivering affordable, reliable, and secure energy essential to American prosperity.”
“America's electric grid cannot become a roadblock to economic growth,” said Office of Electricity (OE) Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza. “By bringing TVA and local utilities together, we're helping reduce costly outages and deliver more power where it's needed. That means fewer disruptions for families, more opportunities for businesses, and a stronger foundation for American jobs.”
The award builds on DOE's selection of TVA for the Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades (SPARK) program. Together, the GRIP and SPARK projects for TVA represent nearly $741 million in planned grid investment, including approximately $329.8 million in federal support, and are expected to add more than 4,300 MW of additional grid capacity.
Under SPARK, TVA plans to upgrade about 125 miles of existing transmission lines across Tennessee, Alabama, and North Carolina using advanced conductors and grid-management technology. The $159.7 million project is expected to add approximately 1,900 MW of transmission capacity and reduce congestion.
Final federal funding, project scope, schedules, and other award conditions remain subject to executed DOE agreements and applicable environmental, permitting, regulatory, and Tribal reviews.
title: Energy Department Backs Major Grid Expansion Across Eight States to Strengthen Reliability and Lower Electricity Costs

HONOLULU – Residents of Hawaiʻi County who were impacted by the Kona Earthquake that occurred May 22 may be eligible for rental assistance.
If your primary home is unsafe to live in because of damage caused by the Kona Earthquake, you can apply for FEMA assistance to help pay for alternate temporary housing. FEMA will work closely with households to understand their temporary housing needs and provide assistance.
To request rental assistance, homeowners and renters should contact FEMA and update their application or create one if they haven’t already. This can be done in any of the following ways:
- Visiting DisasterAssistance.gov.
- Visiting a Community Resource Center. Dates, times, and locations can be found at ready.hawaii.gov.
- Calling the FEMA Helpline at 1-800-621-3362. 
  - If you use a relay service, such as video relay, captioned telephone, or another service, please provide FEMA with that number. Phone support is available in many languages, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
- Sending your request to FEMA: P.O. Box 10055, Hyattsville, MD 20782-8055.
FEMA is required to conduct a home inspection to verify damage reported on your application prior to awarding rental assistance.
If approved, you will receive an initial rental award of up to two months of rent. Applicants may be eligible for additional rental assistance beyond the initial two-month period and should keep in touch with FEMA about their housing needs.
The deadline to apply for federal assistance for the Kona Earthquake is November 1, 2026.
title: Rental Assistance Available for those Impacted by Kona Earthquake

INDIANAPOLIS - Andrew Scott Whitaker, Jr., 30, of Indianapolis, has been sentenced to 19.5 years in federal prison, followed by 15 years of supervised release, after pleading guilty to distribution and possession of child sexual abuse material. Whitaker was also ordered to pay restitution to each of 15 identified victims, totaling $47,500.
According to court documents, on December 27, 2024, Whitaker sent multiple images and videos containing child sexual abuse material to several individuals using the social media messaging application Kik. On March 27, 2025, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at Whitaker’s residence and recovered a cellphone containing approximately 2,279 images and 1,109 video files of child sexual abuse material. Investigators also discovered a second Kik account Whitaker used to facilitate the same criminal conduct.
At the time of his 2024 arrest, Whitaker was on federal supervised release stemming from a 2021 conviction in the Southern District of Indiana for possession of and access with intent to view child sexual abuse material.
“This dangerous offender exploited a social media platform to circulate the horrific abuse of the most vulnerable among us, all while already on federal supervised release for the same reprehensible conduct,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Indiana. “Those who gather online to revel in the exploitation of children should know that we will identify you, we will find you, and we will hold you accountable.”
“Distribution and possession of child sexual abuse material is a serious crime that causes significant pain and trauma to victims, families and the community, and it carries significant penalties, as this case demonstrates,” said Special Agent in Charge Ike Barnes, of the U.S. Secret Service’s Indianapolis Field Office. “The U.S. Secret Service is committed to using its resources to pursue those who choose to engage in such nefarious online behavior. Thank you to the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department, the Indiana Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force and the U.S. Attorney’s Office of the Southern District of Indiana for their work in helping to bring this repeat offender to justice.
The United States Secret Service and Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department investigated this case. The sentence was imposed by Chief U.S. District Judge James R. Sweeney, II.
U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys MaryAnn Mindrum, who prosecuted this case.
This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.
If you are a victim of child sexual exploitation, please contact your local police department. Resources for victims of child exploitation can be found on our website at https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdin/project-safe-childhood
This investigation was conducted by the Indiana Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force, a multiagency task force led by the Indiana State Police that investigates and prosecutes persons who use the internet to sexually exploit or entice children. Each year, Indiana ICAC investigators evaluate thousands of tips, investigate hundreds of cases, and rescue dozens of children from ongoing sexual abuse. Visit https://www.internetcrimesagainstkids.com to learn more about their efforts.

text:
News Release 2026-89 | October 13, 2026

Share This Page:

WASHINGTON—The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. (bank), for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. This amount is the largest in OCC history. The bank is also subject to a December 2024 cease-and-desist order (2024 Order), which requires the bank to address its deficient Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering (BSA/AML) compliance program.

“Bank of America, N.A., is the second largest bank in the U.S. and the sixth largest in the world. Every year, it processes hundreds of trillions of dollars in transactions across the globe. It has a high, and increasing, risk profile for money laundering, terrorist financing and other illicit activities. Almost two years ago, the bank signed an order with the OCC and committed to fixing its longstanding BSA deficiencies. Despite its obligation to the American people as a national-chartered, global systemically important bank, the bank’s BSA/AML compliance program continues to reflect widespread breakdowns in internal controls, which threatens U.S. national and economic security” said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould. “The bank’s poor response to its BSA deficiencies is unacceptable. The second largest bank’s egregious and continued BSA violations warrant the OCC imposing its largest CMP ever assessed against a bank. The OCC expects all banks to have an effective BSA/AML compliance program. Those that do not can expect swift and significant action from the OCC.”

The OCC found that the bank’s BSA/AML compliance program has been deficient and ineffective. The bank’s deficient transaction monitoring system resulted in the bank failing to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions. This caused the bank to file large numbers of late suspicious activity reports (SARs) involving billions of dollars. Many of the late SARs had indicia of money laundering. The bank knew for years that it was failing to escalate potentially suspicious activities to investigators for review to determine if a SAR should be filed but failed to correct this serious BSA violation.

In addition, the bank’s BSA Officer and staff lacked sufficient skills and expertise to effectively manage the bank’s BSA/AML program. Key BSA personnel did not receive appropriate training regarding suspicious activity identification, investigation, and reporting, which resulted in the bank filing inaccurate and late SARs. The BSA audit function failed to identify long-standing BSA concerns that examiners subsequently uncovered.

After agreeing to the 2024 Order, the bank still failed to prioritize BSA/AML compliance. The bank did not complete many of the significant steps needed to establish an effective BSA/AML compliance program and its program continues to have significant breakdowns. For example, more than a year after the 2024 Order, the bank still failed to escalate potentially suspicious activities to investigators for review. Additionally, the bank processed potential trade-based money laundering transactions due to a systemic gap in its transaction monitoring program. Bank management failed to ensure the bank had an effective BSA/AML compliance program and continued to minimize the program’s significant deficiencies.

The OCC is taking this action in coordination with an action by the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), which is assessing a $1.2 billion fine that credits the OCC’s $750 million penalty and is requiring remedial action by the bank. The OCC-assessed penalty will be paid to the U.S. Treasury.

Orlando, Florida – Aljunda Jashae Tompkins (33, Orlando) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Anne-Leigh Gaylord Moe to 10 years and 5 months in federal prison for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. He pleaded guilty on June 26, 2026. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court documents and information presented at sentencing, in September 2024, while driving in Orlando, Tompkins was stopped by officers from the Orlando Police Department. Instead of complying with the stop, Tompkins jumped out of his vehicle, attempted to leave the scene, ignored officer commands, and resisted arrest. Officers recovered a loaded firearm from Tompkins’s vehicle. After making bail in his state case, Tompkins became a fugitive. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives joined the investigation, and Tompkins was charged federally. Tompkins was located and arrested shortly thereafter.

Tompkins is a five-time convicted felon, including previous convictions for trafficking controlled substances and firearms offenses. He also has multiple violations of domestic violence injunctions. As a convicted felon he is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition under federal law.

This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Orlando Police Department. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Richard Varadan.

This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: Five-Time Convicted Felon Sentenced to More Than Ten Years for Possessing a Firearm

CVS Agrees to Pay $315M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government
CVS Pharmacy Inc., a Rhode Island-based pharmacy chain, and its related corporate entities (collectively, CVS) have agreed to pay $315 million to resolve allegations that, from October 17, 2013 through December 2, 2025, CVS illegally filled prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances in violation of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA), and then sought payment for many of those invalid prescriptions from Medicare and other federal healthcare programs in violation of the False Claims Act (FCA).
“Not only does this settlement hold bad actors accountable for their fraudulent activities, but Americans are safer because of it,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. “Today’s settlement is a significant milestone in the Justice Department’s efforts to combat the opioid epidemic by cracking down on pharmacies who unlawfully fulfill prescriptions for controlled substances.”
“Today’s settlement requires CVS to implement additional safeguards to ensure that prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances are dispensed only when medically appropriate,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The remedial measures in this agreement — including proactive monitoring of opioid prescribing patterns — will provide critical protections for patients and federal healthcare programs. The Department of Justice will continue to take steps to prevent the unlawful dispensing of opioids.”
“The opioid epidemic has affected families and communities across Rhode Island and throughout the nation,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Charles C. Calenda for the District of Rhode Island. “Pharmacies that dispense controlled substances must maintain effective compliance systems to identify and respond to warning signs that prescriptions may be unlawful or medically unnecessary. This settlement demonstrates the importance of those obligations and the consequences of failing to implement safeguards designed to prevent the improper dispensing of controlled substances.”
The settlement resolves allegations in the government’s complaint, which the United States filed on Dec. 13, 2024, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island, that CVS knowingly filled prescriptions for controlled substances that lacked a legitimate medical purpose, were not valid, and/or were not issued in the usual course of professional practice. The United States alleged that CVS dispensed prescriptions for dangerous and excessive quantities of opioids, opioid prescriptions filled too early, and “trinity” prescriptions, a dangerous and abused combination of an opioid, a benzodiazepine, and a muscle relaxant. CVS also allegedly filled prescriptions for controlled substances from “pill mill” prescribers who issued large numbers of controlled substance prescriptions without any medical purpose. Further, the United States alleged that CVS pharmacists filled these prescriptions despite clear red flags indicating that there was a high likelihood that the prescriptions lacked a legitimate medical purpose, were not valid, or were not issued in the course of professional practice. Many of these prescriptions were ultimately billed to and reimbursed by federal healthcare programs.
The complaint further alleged that CVS’s violations stemmed from corporate-imposed performance metrics, incentive compensation, and staffing policies that prioritized corporate profits over patient safety. CVS failed to employ enough pharmacists to serve patients, comply with CVS’s legal obligations, and meet corporate performance metrics. In addition, CVS’s policies allegedly prevented pharmacists from warning one another about certain problematic prescribers.
In addition to the monetary payment announced today, CVS has entered into a memorandum of agreement with DEA to address its future obligations in dispensing controlled substances. This agreement requires CVS to establish a hotline for both employees and the public to report suspected illegal dispensing of controlled substances, proactively monitor the dispensing patterns of its pharmacies to identify and address potentially illegal dispensing, and establish a process to evaluate prescribers suspected of illegal prescribing.
“This settlement agreement highlights DEA’s commitment to protecting the health and safety of Americans while holding CVS accountable for dispensing unlawful prescriptions and endangering the public,” said DEA Assistant Administrator Cheri Oz. “DEA is unwavering in its commitment to protect public health and ensuring pharmacies adhere to the highest standards of responsible dispensing. We will continue to work closely with law enforcement, regulatory agencies, and the healthcare community to prevent the misuse of controlled substances, and we will hold those who jeopardize the safety of our citizens accountable.”
“Behind every unlawful prescription is a patient who could be put in harm’s way,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG). “The allegations in this case point to warning signs that should never be overlooked. HHS OIG will not tolerate conduct that jeopardizes lives, and we will continue to pursue those who betray the trust placed in them.”
The civil settlement resolves a civil lawsuit filed by Hillary Estright, a former CVS employee, under the whistleblower provision of the FCA, which authorizes private parties to sue on behalf of the United States and receive a share of any recovery. It also permits the United States to intervene and take over such lawsuits, as it did here. The amount to be recovered by the private whistleblower has not yet been determined. The qui tam case is captioned United States ex rel. Hillary Estright v. CVS Health Corporation, et al., No. 22-cv-00222 (D.R.I.).
This year the Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the Administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect, and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s FCA enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. FCA matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s FCA work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the Civil Division’s Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section, and the Enforcement & Affirmative Litigation Branch, along with the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices for the District of Rhode Island, Eastern District of Virginia, Eastern District of Texas, and District of Hawaii. The DEA’s Office of Diversion Control, Los Angeles Field Division, Richmond District Office, and Office of Chief Counsel led this case with substantial assistance from Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General, Defense Criminal Investigative Service, Defense Health Agency (DHA), Office of Personnel Management (OPM), Department of Labor (DOL) Office of Inspector General, and the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
The investigation and resolution of this matter illustrate the government’s emphasis on combating healthcare fraud. One of the most powerful tools in this effort is the False Claims Act. Tips and complaints from all sources about potential fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, can be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services at 800-HHS-TIPS (800-447-8477).
The United States is represented in this matter by attorneys from the Justice Department’s Civil Division Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section (Assistant Director Natalie Waites and Trial Attorneys Claire Norsetter and Megan Engel) and Enforcement & Affirmative Litigation Branch (Deputy Director Lisa Hsiao and Trial Attorneys Kathleen Brunson and Katherine Ho), as well as from the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices for the District of Rhode Island (Assistant U.S. Attorney Rachna Vyas), Eastern District of Virginia (Assistant U.S. Attorney John Beerbower), Eastern District of Texas (Assistant U.S. Attorney James Gillingham), and District of Hawaii (Assistant U.S. Attorney Tracy J. Weinstein).
The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.

text:
Former Tennessee Business Owner Sentenced for Employment Tax Fraud
A former Tennessee business owner was sentenced today to 3 years’ probation and ordered to pay $1,048,840 in restitution to the United States for willfully failing to pay over employment taxes to the IRS on behalf of the company she owned and operated.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Mari Alexander, 52, was the sole owner and president of a mental-health counseling center with multiple locations throughout Tennessee. Alexander controlled the counseling center’s financial affairs and was responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare and federal income taxes from the wages of employees and paying those funds over to the IRS each quarter, as well as filing quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS. From 2015 through 2020, however, Alexander willfully failed to pay over to the IRS the payroll taxes she collected from the counseling center’s employees, and willfully failed to file more than 20 quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS. In total, Alexander caused a tax loss to the United States of more than $1 million.
On April 15, 2026, Alexander pleaded guilty to one count of willful failure to account for and pay over employment taxes.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s Nation Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Braden H. Boucek for the Middle District of Tennessee made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated this case.
Trial Attorney Michael L. Jones of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Former Tennessee Business Owner Sentenced for Employment Tax Fraud

WASHINGTON — Transnational criminal scam networks operating from West Africa suffered major disruptions last week during a coordinated international “Joint Disruption Week,” an effort that produced arrests, seizures, and the largest-ever takedown of fraudulent social media accounts linked to scam centers in the region, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Transnational fraud demands a transnational response,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia, founder of the Scam Center Strike Force. “I have partnered with the NCA and the Crown Prosecutor for England and Wales to push forward cases on both sides of the Atlantic; criminals are not hindered by borders and neither are we. We will deploy our team wherever in the world transnational criminals target innocent victims.”

“Transnational fraud demands a transnational response,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia, founder of the Scam Center Strike Force. “I have partnered with the NCA and the Crown Prosecutor for England and Wales to push forward cases on both sides of the Atlantic; criminals are not hindered by borders and neither are we. We will deploy our team wherever in the world transnational criminals target innocent victims.”

“Criminals beware: Law enforcement from around the world are working together, and with private industry, to find you, stop your schemes, and bring you to justice,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “The Criminal Division’s Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative (CSI) was built for this brand of collaboration. The millions of bogus social media accounts taken down and dozens of arrests that took place as part of Joint Disruption Week are just the beginning. I want to thank the United Kingdom (UK)’s National Crime Agency (NCA) and its Director General, Graeme Biggar, for hosting this effort, as well as everyone who participated. I am especially grateful to the courageous law enforcement officers in Ghana and Nigeria who put themselves in harm’s way to seize evidence and arrest the criminals who prey on innocent people.”

The “Joint Disruption Week” events mark the first coordinated effort focused specifically on West Africa, underscoring the growing global commitment to dismantling increasingly sophisticated transnational scam networks.

The operation included members of the U.S. Department of Justice, the Scam Center Strike Force under the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, FBI, U.S. Secret Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), the UK’s NCA, the Nigerian Joint Case Team on Cybercrimes, the Nigeria Police Force - National Cybercrime Center, Ghanaian Cyber Security Authority, and private sector partners.

Additional participants included law enforcement agencies from Australia, Canada, Ghana, India, New Zealand, Nigeria, along with INTERPOL and additional cybercrime units. Several tech giants also played a key role. The large-scale effort was hosted by the UK NCA in London.

“Thanks to brilliant partnership with the Department of Justice and the private sector, across multiple African countries, we arrested dozens of criminal actors, seized hundreds of devices, identified at least $11 million in potentially freezable funds, and truly saved lives,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “This is what happens when law enforcement executes with precision across the interagency. We are demolishing Scam Centers across the globe and crushing a criminal industry preying on American citizens.”

“Fraud is a global problem and it takes partnership working across international boundaries to tackle it,” said Nick Sharp, Deputy Director of Fraud at the NCA. “Hosting such a rich and dedicated team of law enforcement and technology companies at NCA’s headquarters enabled us to utilize the power of partnerships and strike back at a significant set of criminals who inflict misery on thousands of victims of fraud. Fraudsters can operate from anywhere and will target victims both domestically and globally. The NCA will continue to work with international and private sector partners to tackle fraudsters working upstream, overseas and online. Collaborating in this way sends a clear signal to criminals that the combined capabilities of law enforcement and industry means that we will relentlessly pursue them and the infrastructure they rely on no matter where they operate.”

During the week beginning Oct. 6, investigators and industry partners exchanged real-time intelligence across jurisdictions, enabling rapid identification and disruption of scam centers in Nigeria, Ghana, and other African countries. Many of the targeted operations were tied to schemes victimizing individuals in the United States, UK, and other countries around the world.

Several private industry partners, including Meta, Adobe, Binance, Coinbase, Cyjax, Elliptic, Chainalysis, Flashpoint, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Silent Push, Starlink and TRM Labs collaborated with international law enforcement in the event, and voluntarily took action on their own networks to disrupt scammers using their platforms to perpetrate fraud. These companies reported to the Department that they “removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups targeting people in the U.S., UK and beyond, and shared leads on over 30 suspected scam centers with law enforcement, resulting in dozens of arrests, the rescue of trafficking victims, and cryptocurrency seizures. In total over $11 million dollars in potential freezable funds were identified by the private sector partners. Meta played a key role in coordinating the event and encouraging broad private sector participation to maximize scam compound disruption.

Among the key accomplishments:

A consortium of international law enforcement agencies made 28 arrests of individuals tied to the criminal scam operations, including:

In Ghana, in the Accra suburb of Sasaabi, authorities arrested 19 individuals and seized 303 electronic devices. In addition, authorities identified 117 victims of human trafficking that are now pending repatriation to Nigeria. An additional 89 victims of the scam were identified with an approximate loss of $8.3 million. During the last week of September alone, authorities made scores of arrests at six locations, identified 34 trafficking victims, and seized 129 electronic devices. The Ghana operation was led by the Ghana Cyber Security Authority, Ghana Police Service Criminal Investigation Department, National Security Service, with support from the NCA, FBI, and Nigeria’s Economic and Financial Crimes Commission.

In Ghana, in the Accra suburb of Sasaabi, authorities arrested 19 individuals and seized 303 electronic devices. In addition, authorities identified 117 victims of human trafficking that are now pending repatriation to Nigeria. An additional 89 victims of the scam were identified with an approximate loss of $8.3 million. During the last week of September alone, authorities made scores of arrests at six locations, identified 34 trafficking victims, and seized 129 electronic devices. The Ghana operation was led by the Ghana Cyber Security Authority, Ghana Police Service Criminal Investigation Department, National Security Service, with support from the NCA, FBI, and Nigeria’s Economic and Financial Crimes Commission.

In Nigeria, authorities arrested nine individuals during the enforcement period, and 53 electronic devices.

The disrupted schemes included law enforcement impersonation scams, digital “arrest” extortion schemes, cryptocurrency investment fraud (also known as “pig butchering”), and a variety of other online fraud operations targeting global victims.

According to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), investment scams were reported 72,984 times in 2025, with cryptocurrency investment fraud comprising 72 percent of that category. Reported losses from these scams rose from $3.96 billion in 2023 to $5.8 billion in 2024. Reported losses for investment scams with a cryptocurrency nexus rose 24 percent in 2025 to over $7.2 billion, according to IC3’s released 2025 annual report. Those figures, based largely on victim reports, are believed to significantly underrepresent actual losses, as many victims do not report to law enforcement. According to one government report, a conservative estimate of the annual value of funds stolen by scam syndicates worldwide approached $64 billion as of the end of 2023.

Strengthening Accountability for Transnational Scam Operations

Criminal scam centers operating in West Africa mirror those uncovered in Southeast Asia — highly organized enterprises that recruit workers, train them in social engineering, and deploy multi‑platform fraud campaigns targeting global victims. While technology companies can significantly disrupt online infrastructure used to perpetuate these schemes, true accountability requires sustained law enforcement action against the individuals and organizations behind them.

The FBI, The Scam Center Strike Force, and its international partners remain committed to advancing this model of public‑private collaboration and expanding global efforts to dismantle criminal networks responsible for online fraud.
