Sanctions Disrupt CDN’s Integrated Commercial Operations Supporting Violenceand Cross‑Border Corruption
WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 11 entities connected to the U.S.-designated Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) Cartel del Noreste (CDN). Those designated include individuals and businesses involved in quarter horse racing, construction, trucking, and the oil and gas sector, highlighting the cartel’s diverse commercial footprint. CDN’s evolution from its predecessor, Los Zetas—responsible for some of the deadliest mass‑casualty attacks in Mexican history—underscores the severity of CDN’s continued threat to the United States and the region.
“Today’s action exposes Cartel del Noreste’s exploitation of the horse racing sector to launder illicit proceeds and finance cartel operations,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “This action marks Treasury’s most significant effort to date to disrupt Cartel del Noreste’s financial infrastructure. Treasury, in close coordination with our law enforcement partners, remains committed to protecting the U.S. financial system from misuse by violent cartels.”
CDN’s stronghold sits directly across the border from Laredo, Texas, the busiest port of entry (POE) on the southern border, where nearly 40 percent of all commercial traffic between the United States and Mexico crosses. This deep entrenchment in cross-border industries, combined with CDN’s ability to infiltrate local governments, steer public contracts, and manipulate regional elections, undermines legitimate authority and destabilizes communities on both sides of the border.
In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans in close coordination with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025. OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons.
Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks. OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, including the U.S. Border Patrol, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, as well as assistance from the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the U.S. Marshals Service. OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. Additionally, OFAC coordinated on this action and previous actions against CDN with the Government of Mexico’s financial intelligence unit, the Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF).
The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886 (collectively, E.O.13224, as amended), which targets terrorists and their supporters. This is OFAC’s fourth and largest action to date targeting CDN networks during the Trump Administration. On May 21, 2025, OFAC designated two high-ranking members and arms traffickers of CDN. On August 6, 2025, OFAC designated three high-ranking members and one associate of CDN, including famous narco-rapper El Makabelico. Earlier this year, on April 14, 2026, OFAC designated three entities and three associates of CDN, including Casino Centenario, a casino just miles from the U.S. border, and Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez, criminal advisor to CDN.
CARTEL DEL NORESTE
Based in Mexico directly across from one of the busiest American border crossings, CDN is a violent terrorist cartel founded by the notorious brothers Miguel Angel “Z-40” Trevino Morales and Oscar Omar “Z-42” Trevino Morales. CDN has been involved in the trafficking of narcotics and other illicit drugs, including fentanyl, crystal methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and cocaine. CDN, formerly known as Los Zetas, has engaged in horrific violence over the years. This year marks the fifteenth anniversary of the August 25, 2011 deadly Los Zetas arson attack on a casino in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico. This arson attack killed 52 people and injured dozens more, with a majority of those killed being women. This firebombing became one of the deadliest cartel attacks against civilians in Mexican history.
Z-40 and Z-42 were arrested by Mexican authorities in 2013 and 2015, respectively, but maintained control over the cartel utilizing corrupt attorneys, including Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez, whom OFAC designated in April 2026. The Trevino brothers were transferred from Mexico in February 2025 and are currently facing drug trafficking, racketeering, firearms, and money laundering charges in the District Court for the District of Columbia, with a maximum sentence of life imprisonment. CDN, then known as Los Zetas, was identified by the United States as a specially designated foreign narcotics trafficker on April 15, 2009, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act). On July 24, 2011, Los Zetas was named as a transnational criminal organization (TCO) in the annex to E.O. 13581. On December 15, 2021, OFAC designated CDN pursuant to E.O. 14059. On February 20, 2025, the U.S. Department of State designated CDN as an FTO and as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT).
AMERICAN QUARTER HORSE RACING – A ZETAS TRADITION
CDN has a long history of money laundering through the American Quarter Horse racing industry. Between 2008 and 2012, Z-40 and Z-42 bought and sold racehorses with drug money and trained and raced them in the United States. Over a 30-month period, Zetas-affiliated front persons and shell companies spent $16 million in New Mexico, Oklahoma, California, and Texas to support the operation and laundered upwards of $22 million for the cartel. In June 2012, the U.S. Government seized 455 horses at an Oklahoma horse farm, racing venues, and training farms.
CDN’s involvement in horse racing continues to this day. Club La Molienda (La Molienda) is a horse racetrack, restaurant, and bar located on the outskirts of Nuevo Laredo that is controlled by CDN. As the most prominent racetrack in Nuevo Laredo, La Molienda generates revenue for CDN, charging entrance fees for those racing their horses at the track as well as for spectators.
CDN leaders and members purchase horses, including many from the United States, to race at La Molienda. La Molienda is controlled by Z-40 but is ultimately overseen by various CDN leaders and associates while Z-40 is incarcerated in the United States.
Before a successful bilateral U.S.-Mexico action in April 2026 suspended operations of Casino Centenario, La Molienda and Casino Centenario entered a strategic gambling partnership allowing people to bet on races at La Molienda from the premises of Casino Centenario. In coordination with OFAC’s April 2026 designation of Casino Centenario and related entities, on the same day, Mexico’s UIF took action and the Secretaría de Gobernación suspended the activities of these CDN-linked entities.
OFAC designated La Molienda pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CDN.
INSIDE THE WINNER’S CIRCLE – TRACKSIDE ASSOCIATES OF CDN
Gamaliel Garza Garcia (Garza Garcia) is a Mexico-based businessman, horse racing enthusiast, and an associate of CDN. Garza Garcia is involved in horse racing in both Mexico and the United States, racing at some of the most prestigious tracks in California and New Mexico. Garza Garcia and his horses frequently race at La Molienda.
Garza Garcia’s company, Construcciones y Edificaciones Garza Elias S.A. de C.V. (CEGESA), has been utilized by CDN to funnel money to election campaigns of CDN’s preferred political candidates. Additionally, CEGESA has corruptly obtained government contracts and then sub-contracted that work to CDN-affiliated individuals. CEGESA is a major recipient of government contracts in the north of the country, including from the governments of the municipality of Nuevo Laredo and the state of Tamaulipas.
Garza Garcia created the Nuevo Laredo-based material supply company Concretos y Productos Asfalticos del Norte, S.A. de C.V. (COPASA) to vertically integrate the illicit construction contract scheme. CEGESA performed or subcontracted the work, while COPASA provided the materials. As of early 2026, CEGESA and COPASA were some of the only construction companies authorized by CDN to perform construction work in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas.
Garza Garcia controls Cuadra San Dibanh, an Anahuac, Nuevo Leon-based Quarter Horse racing barn. Cuadra San Dibanh frequently races at La Molienda and other major racetracks throughout Mexico.
Garza Garcia also owns and controls an extensive corporate network of construction and fuel companies in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas. This includes the following six companies, all based in Nuevo Laredo:
- Construaceros del Fuerte, S.A. de C.V., a construction company;
- Inova NLD Desarrollos Inmobiliarios, S.A. de C.V., a construction company;
- Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas company;
- Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas company;
- Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas company; and
- Transportadora de Gas de Nuevo Laredo, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas transportation company.
Gamaliel Garza Elias (Garza Elias), Garza Garcia’s son, is being designated for his role in CEGESA, where he is involved in the day-to-day operations of CEGESA. Garza Elias has also delivered cash to fund election campaigns for CDN’s preferred political candidates in Mexico.
OFAC designated Garza Garcia pursuant to E.O. 14059, for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, CDN. Garza Garcia is also being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, CDN.
OFAC designated CEGESA; COPASA; Cuadra San Dibanh; Construaceros del Fuerte, S.A. de C.V.; Inova NLD Desarrollos Inmobiliarios, S.A. de C.V.; Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V.; Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V.; Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V.; and Transportadora de Gas de Nuevo Laredo, S.A. de C.V. pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Garza Garcia.
OFAC designated Garza Elias pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended,for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CEGESA.
OTHER PLAYERS IN THE NUEVO LAREDO PLAZA
Pablo Cesar Guajardo Alvarez (Guajardo), known as “Takia,” is a current CDN plaza boss of Nuevo Laredo and former leader of CDN’s sicarios. Plaza bosses are in charge of all cartel activity in their area of responsibility. Guajardo was arrested in 2020 for his connection to the January 4, 2017 assassination of Ricardo Martinez Chavez and four public servants, but has since been released. Guajardo has been involved in arms trafficking on behalf of CDN.
OFAC designated Guajardo pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CDN.
Tamex Leasing or Tamex Logistics (Tamex) is a Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas-based trucking company involved in the smuggling of narcotics into the United States. Tamex’s truckyard in Nuevo Laredo has been the originator of at least two cocaine shipments bound for the United States. Seized by law enforcement, these shipments were stored in hidden compartments of the trailers’ brake drums and totaled 52 kilograms. Francisco Javier Inzunza Partida (Inzunza) is a dispatcher for Tamex who was involved in dispatching the two trailers seized for concealed narcotics.
OFAC designated Tamex and Inzunza pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production.
SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS
As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons.
Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions. In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause
U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions. Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.
Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions. OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.
The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

For Immediate Release: October 13, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

Montclair, N.J. — Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) issued the following statement after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers used the parking lot of the federal government's Roxbury Township warehouse facility to stage and process 14 detained individuals on two separate occasions in September.

“DHS has finally admitted what we suspected all along: ICE used the Roxbury property to process and stage detainees on multiple occasions, potentially in violation of a court order restricting its use as an immigration detention facility. After weeks of denying that the property was being used for immigration enforcement operations, DHS has finally confirmed to my office that ICE used the site to process 14 detained individuals on September 4 and 8. Let’s be clear: This was no accident. ICE officers deliberately misled the municipality and state by conducting processing operations with supervisory knowledge. According to communications with my office, only after whistleblowers raised concerns, did they cease activity. The fact that ICE describes potential illegal activity as ‘routine operating procedures’ should alarm every New Jerseyan,” said Congresswoman Mejia.

“ICE does not get to cherry-pick which laws to follow. I will continue to demand answers, pursue oversight, and work with state officials to ensure this property is never again used outside the law. ICE cannot be trusted to police itself. An agency that operates with impunity and answers to a Secretary who encourages suffering in detention must be abolished and replaced with a fair, just, and humane immigration system that respects due process and human dignity,” said Mejia.

title: Rep. Mejia Slams DHS After Agency Admits to Processing Detainees at Roxbury Property

SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A Honduran national pleaded guilty before Federal Chief Magistrate Judge Willie J. Epps, Jr., to the sole count of the indictment charging him with illegally reentering the United States after being previously deported.

Fredy Rolando Rivera-Gonzalez, 31, pleaded guilty to illegal reentry by a previously deported alien, who had been previously convicted of another felony offense. On July 3, 2026, Rivera-Gonzalez was arrested after he was contacted by Pulaski County Sheriff’s Deputies during a traffic stop. During the contact, Rivera-Gonzalez admitted that he had illegally reentered the United States in August of 2024, near Brownsville or McAllen, Texas, after he had been previously deported. On July 3, 2026, Rivera-Gonzalez was found voluntarily in the United States after being previously deported on Nov. 6, 2019, from Huntsville, Texas.

Under federal statute, illegally reentering into the United States after being previously deported is in direct violation of existing federal immigration law and is subject to a sentence of up to two years imprisonment. The maximum statutory sentences are prescribed by Congress and are provided here for informational purposes.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patrick. It was investigated by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement-Homeland Security Investigations and the Pulaski County, Missouri Sheriff’s Department.

Operation Take Back America

These cases are part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Washington, D.C.—Today, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Rick Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Aviation André Carson (D-IN) and 21 Democratic members of the T&I Committee wrote to United States Government Accountability Office (GAO) Acting Comptroller General of the United States Orice Brown requesting an audit of the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) deployment of the AI-based SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories) and FMDS (Flow Management Data and Services) platforms.
“As the Government Accountability Office has previously reported, the Federal Aviation Administration has struggled for decades to modernize the technology and infrastructure supporting the nation’s air traffic control (ATC) system, resulting in outdated systems that undermine the safety and reliability of U.S. aviation,” the members wrote.
“While technological modernization is essential, the FAA’s development and implementation of FMDS and SMART have generated considerable concern from Members of this Committee and key aviation stakeholders. Concerningly, the nation’s frontline aviation safety workforce apparently had little to no input into SMART’s development and have received limited training and information during the current deployment process,” the members continued.
The members also highlighted the need for proper safety guardrails, writing, “The use of artificial intelligence within SMART has rightfully raised serious questions about its reliability and safety benefits, particularly on its potential to interfere with decision-making by experienced air traffic controllers or to hallucinate safety-critical information.”
“Transparency and accountability in the development and deployment of modern, data-driven air traffic control tools are essential to airspace safety,” they continued.
The Members concluded by requesting GAO to assess the FAA’s (1) safety risk management analysis of SMART and FMDS; (2) plans to test, evaluate and certify the platforms for operational use; (3) performance metrics used to determine the safety, effectiveness and reliability of SMART; and (4) deployment strategy, including coordination with key stakeholders.

U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today announced nine recipients of the prestigious Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award for their exceptional contributions to research and development supporting the U.S. Department of Energy’s missions in science, energy, and national security.
October 13, 2026
WASHINGTON—U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today announced nine recipients of the prestigious Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award for their exceptional contributions to research and development supporting the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) missions in science, energy, and national security.
“This year’s Lawrence Award recipients exemplify the ingenuity and determination that drive America’s leadership in science and technology,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “From achieving fusion ignition to advancing critical materials and high-performance computing, these scientists and engineers are tackling some of our nation’s most complex challenges and translating groundbreaking research into real-world capabilities. Their work strengthens our nation’s energy security, drives American innovation, and ensures the United States remains at the forefront of scientific discovery.”
Established in 1959, the Lawrence Award recognizes mid-career U.S. scientists and engineers for groundbreaking achievements across nine scientific and engineering categories. The award is among the longest-running and most prestigious science and technology honors bestowed by the U.S. government.
The 2026 Ernest O. Lawrence Award recipients are:
- Eric J. Schelter, Ph.D. (University of Pennsylvania) – Atomic, Molecular, and Chemical Sciences – Honored for his “fundamental chemical studies of energy-critical metals leading to new methods for their selective and sustainable separations.”
- Patrick Chain, Ph.D. (Los Alamos National Laboratory and New Mexico Consortium) – Biological and Environmental Sciences – Honored for his “pioneering work in genomics and microbiome science, including discoveries of new bacterial-fungal interactions and revolutionizing the field by democratizing access to advanced bioinformatics tools.”
- Samuel W. Williams, Ph.D. (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory) – Computer, Information, and Knowledge Sciences – Honored for his “pioneering contributions in performance modeling, hardware/software design optimization, and novel computer architecture for high-performance computing, enabling modeling of complex computational solutions, and increasing analysis speed, simulation accuracy, and computational efficiency.”
- Thomas Epps, III, Ph.D. (University of Delaware) – Condensed Matter and Materials Sciences – Honored for his “fundamental contributions to chemistry and materials science with applications in the chemical upcycling of polymeric waste, generation of high-performance materials from biomass feedstocks, and development of membranes for lithium-ion battery technologies.”
- Gregg Beckham, Ph.D. (National Laboratory of the Rockies and University of Colorado Boulder) – Energy Science and Innovation – Honored for his “transformative research in the conversion of lignocellulosic biomass and waste plastics via biology, chemistry, and engineering, yielding building blocks for sustainable fuels, chemicals, and materials.”
- Andrea L. Kritcher, Ph.D. (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory) – Fusion and Plasma Sciences – Honored for her “exceptional design efforts leading to the first-ever achievement of fusion ignition in the Laboratory, which is of major scientific impact to institutional and national missions, the private sector, and fusion interests within academia.”
- Charles C. Polly, Ph.D. (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory) – High Energy Physics – Honored for his “exceptional scientific and technical contributions to low-energy precision measurements in particle physics, most notably leadership of the experimental measurement of the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon with the Muon g-2 experiment.”
- Michael Reed, Ph.D. (Nevada National Security Site) – National Security and Nonproliferation – Honored for his “vital contributions to national and international nuclear emergency response through the Advanced Visualization & Integration of Data (AVID) software, which broke existing paradigms by simultaneously fusing all radiological data into a single interface connected seamlessly to world-wide expertise.”
- Lijuan Ruan, Ph.D. (Brookhaven National Laboratory) – Nuclear Physics – Honored for her “outstanding leadership and ingenuity in the design, construction, and operation of novel detector systems in the STAR experiment, transforming dilepton final states into precision probes of heavy ion collisions.”
DOE will honor the recipients at a hybrid award ceremony in Washington, D.C., on November 13, 2026. The ceremony will be broadcast live online, and a recording will be available following the event. Registration is required for both virtual and in-person attendees. Due to space and security requirements, in-person attendance is limited, with registration closing October 30, 2026.
For more information and to RSVP, visit the DOE Office of Science Ernest O. Lawrence Award webpage.
title: Energy Department Announces 2026 Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award Winners

Amo Highlights Rhode Island’s Blue Economy at Roger Williams Oyster Farm and Hinckley Yacht Services
Bristol, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) continued his 2026 Blue Economy Tour today with visits to Roger Williams University’s shellfish farm and research facilities and Hinckley Yachts’ expanded Portsmouth facility, highlighting the research, skilled workers, and businesses driving Rhode Island’s maritime economy.
At Roger Williams, Amo toured the shellfish farm, hatchery, and research labs with faculty and researchers to discuss advances in shellfish production, aquaculture, and blue biotechnology, as well as opportunities to prepare students for careers in the Blue Economy. They also discussed federal policies to support aquaculture, fisheries, and environmental conservation. At the newly expanded Hinckley Yachts facility in Portsmouth, Amo met with workers and discussed the skilled trades and maritime jobs that keep Rhode Island moving.
“Rhode Island’s Blue Economy means cutting-edge research, skilled jobs, and businesses building the future right here in the Ocean State,” said Congressman Gabe Amo. “At Roger Williams, researchers are advancing aquaculture and blue biotech. At Hinckley, skilled workers are building and servicing world-class yachts. PORTLAND, Ore.— A Granite Bay, California, man pleaded guilty today to cyberstalking his ex‑girlfriend and posting sexually explicit photos of her online.

Jason David Campos, 44, pleaded guilty to stalking and aggravated identity theft.

According to court documents, Campos harassed his ex‑girlfriend from 2009 to 2023 by posting intimate images and personal information about her online without her consent. He created social media and forum accounts using her name and, in some cases, encouraged others to contact or harass her.

In 2021, Campos created an email account using the victim’s maiden name and used it to impersonate her and obtain her confidential legal file. Later that year, he sent intimate images of the victim to her attorney from the same account.

In 2022, Campos sent emails to an account belonging to the victim, attempting to confirm her identity and referencing a minor family member whose name he obtained from her legal file. In 2023, he used an instant messaging app to distribute intimate images of the victim to strangers and directed them to contact an email account he controlled that had previously belonged to the victim.

On April 9, 2025, a federal grand jury in Portland indicted Campos on charges of stalking, wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. Under the plea agreement, Campos pleaded guilty to stalking and aggravated identity theft.

Campos has agreed to pay full restitution to the victim and to her attorney for services provided in response to the fraudulent records request.

Campos faces a maximum of five years in prison for stalking and a mandatory two‑year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft, along with fines and supervised release terms.

Sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 1, 2027, before a U.S. District Court judge.

“Today’s plea sends a clear message that those who use the internet to harass, intimidate and exploit others will be held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford. “We remain committed to protecting victims of online abuse and ensuring offenders face the full consequences of their actions.”

The FBI investigated the case, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Gregory R. Nyhus is prosecuting the case, with support from Assistant U.S. Attorney Mira Chernick.
title: California Man Pleads Guilty to Cyberstalking Ex-Girlfriend

BOSTON – A Brockton woman was sentenced on Oct. 5,2026 in federal court in Boston for stealing a nearly $1 million United States Treasury tax refund check.

Lana Ruel, 71, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Allison D. Burroughs to two months in prison, to be followed by two months of supervised release. Ruel may also be ordered to pay restitution at a later date. In June 2026 , Ruel pleaded guilty to one count of theft of government funds. In December 2025 , Ruel was arrested and charged.

Ruel attempted to deposit a United States Treasury tax refund check issued to a healthcare company in Brooklyn, New York. Prior to the attempted deposit, Ruel incorporated a company in Massachusetts and opened a bank account in the same name of the healthcare company that was the payee on the tax refund check. After the attempted deposit, the bank froze Ruel’s account. Ruel then called the bank and said that she could “explain what the check was, where it came from, and what it’s for…”

Over a period of two years, Ruel created four additional companies in Massachusetts that did not have a legitimate business purpose. For one of those companies, Ruel opened an account at approximately 10 different banks. Ruel also received wire transfers in some of the accounts and then wired the funds to different accounts or made cash withdrawals. The banks have since closed all these accounts.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, Boston Field Office; and Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service’s Boston Division made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Saltzman of the Securities, Financial & Cyber Fraud Unit prosecuted the case.

The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Underwood Secures More Than $500,000 in Federal Funding for Child Care, Youth Homelessness, Suicide Prevention, University Research, and More in Northern Illinois
WASHINGTON — This week, Representative Lauren Underwood announced a new round of federal funding she has secured for child care, youth services, university research, and crisis intervention in northern Illinois.
As a member of the Appropriations Committee, Underwood has made securing federal resources for our community a top priority. The following funds will support programs in the 14th District with federal resources:
Lewis University, Romeoville, Illinois – $125,000
Lewis University in Romeoville has been awarded $125,000 in federal funding through the Center for Mental Health Services at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
This grant will help stand up a network of supports to meet the growing mental health needs of Lewis University students. The program will provide screenings, assessments, referrals for services, training, education, and an awareness campaign. Project Safety Net will also help identify students who are at risk for suicidal behavior, increase protective factors that promote mental health, and reduce risk factors for suicide.
Youth Service Bureau of Illinois Valley, Ottawa, Illinois – $235,524
Youth Service Bureau of Illinois Valley in Ottawa has been awarded $235,524 in federal funding through the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
This grant helps create and strengthen community-based programs that meet the immediate needs of runaway and homeless youth under 18 years old. The grant is through the Basic Center Program at ACF, which also works to reunite young people with their families or locate appropriate alternative placements.
Northern Illinois University, DeKalb, Illinois – $34,064
Northern Illinois University has been awarded $34,064 in federal funding through the Office of Public Health and Science at the Department of Health and Human Services.
This grant will fund a project researching the responsible conduct of research into AI, Open Science, and Partnerships.
City of Aurora, Aurora, Illinois – $128,000
The City of Aurora has been awarded $128,000 in federal funding through Office of Justice Programs at the Department of Justice (DOJ).
This grant will fund the City of Aurora’s Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) Training Program Initiative. The purpose of this project is to expand specialized training for public safety personnel to improve responses to individuals experiencing mental illness or behavioral health crises. The project will take place in Aurora, IL and will serve community members who interact with police, school resource officers, dispatchers, and detention personnel. The initiative will train and certify approximately 45 personnel through the Illinois Law Enforcement Training and Standards Board’s 40 hour CIT curriculum.

BECKLEY, W.Va. – Jeremy Lamar Smith, 40, of Beckley, pleaded guilty today to being a felon in possession of a firearm.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on or about April 26, 2023, Smith possessed a Ruger model American 9mm pistol in Beckley.

Federal law prohibits a person with a prior felony conviction from possessing a firearm or ammunition. Smith knew he was prohibited from possessing a firearm because of his prior felony convictions for burglary on November 15, 2005, and possession of a firearm by a prohibited person on February 7, 2022, both in Raleigh County Circuit Court.

Smith is scheduled to be sentenced on February 12, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release, and a fine of up to $250,000.

United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF).

United States Magistrate Judge Omar J. Aboulhosn presided over the hearing. Assistant United States Attorney Amy L. McLaughlin is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

This case is also part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

A federal jury in Phoenix, Arizona, convicted a man for aiding and assisting in the filing of false tax returns, and for filing false personal income tax returns.
Pacific Kashosi, the owner of African Union Tax Services, a tax preparation business, was convicted of 18 counts of aiding and assisting in the preparation of false tax returns for clients of his business and two counts of filing his own false tax returns.
According to the evidence presented at trial, Kashosi prepared false tax returns for his clients that reported false Covid tax credits, false fuel credits and false business losses. The false tax returns claimed thousands of dollars in fraudulent refunds. Kashosi was also convicted of filing false 2022 and 2023 federal income tax returns that did not report any of the nearly $900,000 in return preparation fees he received. Kashosi caused a large portion of the fraudulent refunds claimed on his clients’ returns to be wired into his bank accounts.
Kashosi faces a statutory maximum sentence of three years in prison for each count of conviction along with a period of supervised release, restitution, and monetary penalties. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief Andrew Kameros of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Kevin Rapp of the District of Arizona are prosecuting the case.

US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties
MONROE, NY – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited six construction employers for willful and serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at the site of a planned 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building and proposed a combined $648,094 in penalties.
The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an allegation of struck-by and collapse hazards associated with a large excavation at the Monroe Commons project – also known as Magna Square development – a planned 4-story, approximately 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building with retail, office space, and a 39-room hotel located on an 18-acre site. The excavation had a steep, unstable embankment nearly 75 feet high which was not adequately sloped or shored.
OSHA issued a total of 23 serious and five willful citations to the project’s general contractor and five subcontractors for failing to protect employees from cave-in, struck-by, and chemical hazards; neglecting to shield employees from falling or rolling rock and soil from an excavation face; and not ensuring daily inspections of excavations were conducted by a competent person.
Advanced Plan and Build LLC, and subcontractors Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. – operating as Drip Drop Waterproofing Inc. – and The Paving Masters LLC received citations for willfully exposing employees to cave-in and struck-by hazards from an unprotected excavation. OSHA also cited Advanced Plan and Build and The Paving Masters for their willful failure to ensure that the excavation, which was between 21 and 75 feet deep, was designed by a registered professional engineer.
Subcontractors Century Max Industries Corp., DelValle Contractor, and Prime Structure Inc. were cited for serious violations for failing to protect employees from cave-in and struck-by hazards. DelValle and Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. also received citations for serious violations related to lack of fall protection and chemical hazards.
OSHA proposed the following penalties: Advanced Plan and Build LLC—$175,444; Century Max Industries Corp.—$46,340; DelValle Contractor—$19,151; Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc.—$198,615; Prime Structure Inc.—$19,860; and The Paving Masters LLC—$188,684.
The employers have 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.
Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.
title: US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties

U.S. Marshals Task Force Arrests Dangerous Nashua Fugitive in New York
For immediate release
Andrew Grillo, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Concord, NH – The U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) District of New Hampshire and the New Hampshire Joint Fugitive Task Force (JFTF), working with federal, state and local law enforcement partners, helped locate and apprehend Jacob Reznikow, 39, in upstate New York following a months-long effort to bring him into custody.
The Nashua Police Department requested assistance from the JFTF in late June after Reznikow failed to appear for an arraignment related to his June 10 arrest on a driving under the influence charge. Following that arrest, law enforcement officials brought additional firearms and drug charges against Reznikow stemming from items discovered in his vehicle after it was seized. Reznikow was prohibited from possessing firearms because of a March 2021 conviction for selling controlled drugs in Nashua.
Following his failure to appear, Reznikow took active steps to evade law enforcement, including an incident in which he recklessly fled from officers several weeks ago. Additional charges are pending stemming from the damage caused in the wake of this flight.
“When someone repeatedly evades law enforcement while facing serious firearms and drug charges, it raises significant public safety concerns,” said Nashua Police Department Chief Kevin Rourke. “This arrest demonstrates the importance of working together across jurisdictions to locate dangerous individuals and hold them accountable. We appreciate the dedication and coordination of our local, state and federal partners in bringing this investigation to a safe conclusion.”
The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and New Hampshire State Police provided key investigative resources to help locate Reznikow. Through coordinated investigative efforts, the agencies, working alongside the Nashua Police Department and the JFTF, tracked him to upstate New York.
Friday morning, members of the U.S. Marshals Service New York/New Jersey Regional Fugitive Task Force were able to locate and safely apprehend Reznikow at a McDonald’s restaurant in Rome, New York, without incident.
“Fugitives cannot evade accountability simply by crossing state lines,” said Katherine Burns, the acting U.S. Marshal for the District of New Hampshire. “This case underscores the commitment of the U.S. Marshals Service and our partners to protecting the public and bringing fugitives to justice wherever they may try to run.”
Reznikow was arraigned in New York on Saturday on a fugitive from justice charge. He will be held without bail at the Oneida County Jail pending an extradition hearing tomorrow.
The USMS New Hampshire Joint Fugitive Task Force was formed in the fall of 2002 and is headquartered in Concord. The task force coordinates federal, state, county, and local resources to develop leads, gather intelligence, track and apprehend targeted fugitives. The Task Force receives vital support from Strafford, Merrimack and Rockingham Counties, as well as the cities of Manchester, Nashua and Concord.

Following a comprehensive, multi-phase due diligence review, the Department of War has determined that significant operational and managerial improvements at General Dynamics Bath Iron Works (BIW) have established the capacity and stability necessary to support the potential construction of a second guided-missile destroyer (DDG).
The Department's thorough review evaluated production throughput, schedule adherence, quality assurance benchmarks, supply chain resilience, and workforce optimization at the Bath, Maine shipyard. Based on verifiable performance enhancements and leadership initiatives implemented across the facility, the Department concluded that building an additional Arleigh Burke-class (DDG 51) destroyer at BIW is feasible and strategically advantageous for the Navy's fleet, should Congress secure the necessary funding.
"Our national security requires an industrial base that can respond to demands for increased speed and volume," said Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg. "After a rigorous review, Bath Iron Works has proven it has the capacity and stability to support construction of a second destroyer. While the operational improvements we have seen at BIW are a significant step in the right direction, the shipyard must continue this momentum to fully resolve legacy production challenges – sustained performance is essential. The Department will continue to partner with contractors who prioritize execution, accountability, and the rapid modernization of our forces."
"Today's decision by the Department of War validates the capacity of Bath Iron Works (BIW) and the hard work of its highly skilled 6,800 employees who build the best ships in the world. I have advocated for a second destroyer to be included in this year's budget, and I worked with the Administration during its careful review and repeated visits to BIW to verify the ability of the shipyard to construct another ship while continuing to complete its current workload," said Senator Susan Collins (ME). "This certification will help keep our Navy strong and support BIW as a steady source of good-paying Maine jobs. I will continue to work to ensure our shipbuilders have the resources to meet the Navy's needs at a time when China is relentlessly expanding its fleet."
The decision to certify the shipyard's capacity for a second destroyer aligns with the Administration's broader, aggressive campaign to revitalize the U.S. Maritime Industrial Base and outmatch global pacing threats. To counter aggressive ship-construction timelines by foreign adversaries, the Department is prioritizing long-term stability and capacity-building across the domestic shipbuilding supply chain.
Through targeted modernization investments, workforce development initiatives, and streamlined procurement processes, the Administration is actively expanding America's sovereign shipbuilding capacity. Ensuring that key shipyards like Bath Iron Works can reliably scale and sustain high-rate production is a cornerstone of the Department's strategy to maintain global maritime dominance and protect American interests worldwide.
title: Department of War Certifies Production Capacity for Second Guided-Missile Destroyer at Maine's Bath Iron Works

Secretary Wright issues an emergency order to stabilize the mid-Atlantic grid and mitigate the risk of blackouts
October 12, 2026
WASHINGTON—U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright issued an emergency order to mitigate blackout risks in the mid-Atlantic ahead of a period of elevated demand, a high rate of planned generator outages during the autumn maintenance season, and numerous planned transmission outages. The order directs PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) to dispatch specified units and to order their operation as needed to maintain reliability and authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3. 
PJM is authorized to call upon its Transmission Owners and Electric Distribution Companies to implement the order as needed. The order was issued pursuant to an application from PJM submitted on October 11, 2026. 
“This order will help ensure millions of American families and businesses across the mid-Atlantic have access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity by making additional power generation, including backup power, available to use as needed,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “While past leaders’ energy subtraction policies have made the grid more vulnerable to the risk of blackouts when the sun doesn’t shine or the wind doesn’t blow, this administration remains committed to using every available tool to prevent blackouts.” 
DOE estimates more than 35 GW of unused backup generation remains available nationwide. 
The order is effective October 13, 2026, through October 16, 2026.
title: Energy Secretary Secures Mid-Atlantic Grid Ahead of Anticipated Stressed System Conditions

WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) and the U.S. Department of War (DoW) announced a new memorandum of agreement building on the Smaller War Plants Commission (SWPC) to expand access to strategic capital for small businesses in the defense industrial base. By aligning DoW’s strategic-investment capabilities through its Economic Defense Unit (EDU) with SBA’s lending and investment expertise, the partnership will help defense-critical manufacturers, suppliers, and innovators access more capital to grow production, strengthen domestic supply chains, and deliver for America’s warfighters. The agreement advances the SWPC mission to identify, support, and scale the small businesses essential to America’s military strength.
“The American military is already the strongest fighting force the world has ever known, and President Trump has made clear that we will keep it that way—not by accepting a hollowed-out industrial base, but by building an Arsenal of Freedom that can outproduce, out-innovate, and outlast any adversary,” said Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. “The Smaller War Plants Commission will now be able to surge strategic capital to the small businesses that build the ships, munitions, microelectronics, materials, components, and technologies our warfighters rely on. Together, the Department of War and SBA are restoring the industrial dominance that underwrites America’s military advantage and securing peace through strength.”
“When we established the Smaller War Plants Commission, we committed to putting the full weight of the federal government behind the small manufacturers that comprise 70 percent of America’s defense industrial base,” said SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “Together with the Department of War, we are delivering on that promise by supercharging the flow of strategic capital to American defense suppliers to accelerate growth, innovation, and asymmetric advantage for our warfighters. Thanks to President Trump, we are ending the era of foreign dependence and rebuilding the industrial strength that supports the Arsenal of Freedom and keeps America free and strong.”
Last month, the SBA and DoW established the SWPC as a historic, whole-of-government effort to expand the domestic capacity that supports the world’s strongest military. The Commission draws its name from the World War II-era Smaller War Plants Corporation and the Small Defense Plants Administration, SBA predecessor agencies that connected small manufacturers with the financing, contracting tools, and technical support they needed to scale their critical role in building the Arsenal of Freedom.
Building on the SWPC framework, the agreement creates an integrated capital pathway for qualified small businesses that support America’s defense industrial base by aligning the DoW Economic Defense Unit (EDU) with the SBA Office of Investment and Innovation (OII) and Office of Capital Access. EDU will identify firms with financing needs through its Business Operators for National Defense (BOND) efforts and refer potential loan candidates to SBA, which will leverage its existing 7(a) and 504 lender networks to help connect eligible firms with SBA-backed capital.
The agreement also enables SBA to support EDU’s execution of Department of War-funded redeemable preferred-equity investments in small and medium-sized businesses that create, expand, or restore industrial capacity critical to national security—including munitions, platforms, technological processes, essential materials, and the exploration, development, and mining of strategic and critical metals and minerals. SBA will provide due diligence, underwriting, transaction support, and portfolio-management assistance, while EDU retains responsibility and ultimate decision-making authority for its investments.
Through the new MOA, the agencies will:
- Identify defense-critical businesses: Through the Department of War’s Business Operators for National Defense efforts, EDU will identify small businesses engaged in defense-industrial-base activities that need financing and refer prospective loan candidates to SBA.
- Connect firms to SBA-backed capital: SBA will leverage its existing capital networks to support the financing needs of eligible businesses referred by EDU, consistent with applicable program requirements.
- Deploy strategic preferred equity: EDU may originate and source Department of War-funded redeemable preferred-equity investments for businesses that create, expand, or restore industrial capacity critical to national security.
- Apply SBA investment expertise: SBA will support potential equity investments through legally authorized due diligence, underwriting, investment structuring, transaction documentation, monitoring, and management support—helping ensure investments are disciplined, mission-focused, and positioned to strengthen the defense industrial base.
- Drive results and accountability: The agencies will establish joint investment guidance, conduct quarterly portfolio reviews and resource planning, and collaborate on annual reporting on investment performance and exits.
Under President Trump’s leadership, the SBA and DoW are taking concrete action to expand the domestic industrial capacity that strengthens America’s supply chains, equips our warfighters, and sustains the world’s strongest military. Through the Smaller War Plants Commission, qualified small businesses can connect with federal resources designed to help them grow, innovate, and support America’s defense industrial base. To learn more about available resources, visit www.sba.gov/swpc.
# # #
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of entrepreneurship. As the leading voice for small businesses within the federal government, the SBA empowers job creators with the resources and support they need to start, grow, and expand their businesses or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA, Department of War Sign Landmark Agreement to Supercharge Strategic Investment in America’s Defense Industrial Base

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELERATES VIRGIN ISLANDS-PUERTO RICO FRIENDSHIP DAY

U.S. Virgin Islands—Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett joins our local community in celebrating Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Weekend, culminating today on Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Day. The holiday honors the deep and enduring bonds of family, culture, and shared history between the people of the U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico. Today is also Indigenous Peoples’ Day, a recognition of the first peoples of the Caribbean and the Americas, whose presence and legacy remain woven into the identity of our islands.

“The Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico are bound by far more than the waters between us,” said Congresswoman Plaskett. “From enslaved Africans who escaped the Danish West Indies to find freedom in Puerto Rico, to Puerto Ricans who came to our islands in the early 1900s to cut cane and seek opportunity, to the families who live, work, and worship across our shores today, we share a common thread of resilience, culture, food, faith, and kinship. On this Friendship Day and Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we are reminded that as people of color, telling our own stories is essential. When we tell them with truth and pride, we preserve our history, strengthen our unity, and ensure our children know who they are.”

In observance of Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Day, all of Congresswoman Plaskett’s offices in Washington, D.C., St. Croix, and St. Thomas are closed today, Monday, October 12, 2026. The offices will reopen for regular business hours on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Should you need assistance during those days when the offices are closed, please call 340-778-5900 on St. Croix or 340-774-4408 on St. Thomas, leave a message and someone will respond in short order.

Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Allison Hooker and Japanese Senior Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs Namazu Hiroyuki held the second U.S.-Japan Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) Dialogue on October 12 in Tokyo. The dialogue marked the 10th anniversary of the Free and Open Indo-Pacific vision. The two sides noted continued close alignment on U.S. priorities and Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae’s updated Free and Open Indo-Pacific. They committed to turning that shared vision into concrete results for the American and Japanese people and for the Indo-Pacific region. Under Secretary Hooker and Senior Deputy Minister Namazu discussed how to align their foreign assistance behind strategic infrastructure in priority countries, including the Luzon Economic Corridor in the Philippines and the Japan-U.S. Mekong Power Partnership (JUMPP). They also agreed to coordinate security assistance more closely, especially for maritime security and maritime domain awareness in Southeast Asia and the Pacific Islands.

The two sides reviewed progress on economic security, including critical minerals supply chains, deep-sea mineral development, digital connectivity, and energy security. On regional security, they discussed working more closely with allies and partners in the region, and they welcomed Japan’s growing cooperation with NATO. They noted progress in U.S.-Japan defense industrial cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the immediate resolution of the abductions issue.

Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 16 Individuals for Election Crimes
Today the Justice Department announced charges involving 16 individuals, including an illegal alien, in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes across the country. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of U.S. citizenship in order to register to vote or to vote, voting on behalf the deceased, voting multiple times in the same election, false statements on citizenship applications, and unlawful procurement of citizenship.
Case details are as follows:
District of New Mexico
Patrick Perea, 62, has been indicted by a federal grand jury on one count of fraudulent voting. Perea attempted to cast his deceased wife’s absentee ballot in the November 2024 general election by submitting it to the Bureau of Elections of the Bernalillo County Clerk’s Office in Albuquerque.
Eastern District of Pennsylvania
An illegal alien and three aliens have been charged with voting by an alien.
- Hacina Saadi, 48, an illegal alien from France, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
- Pakistani national Jamil Ahmad, 50, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
- Pakistani national Nighat Jamil, 47, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
- Portuguese national Paulo Silva, 54, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
Southern District of Alabama
Two aliens have been charged with voting as an alien.
- Peruvian national Silvia Delgado Phelps, 78, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with voting as an alien. Phelps allegedly voted in multiple elections in Baldwin County, Alabama, despite not being a U.S. citizen.
- Jamaican national Staciann Pollion Davis, 42, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with voting as an alien. Davis allegedly voted in the November 2024 general election in Clarke County, Alabama, despite not being a U.S. citizen.
Northern District of Alabama
Forrest Scott Woody, 68, of Hendersonville, North Carolina, has been charged with illegally voting more than once. According to the indictment, Woody voted twice in the 2024 general election. In particular, he voted in Calhoun County, Alabama, after having already voted in the same election in Henderson County, North Carolina.
Western District of Missouri
Cuban national Andre’s Garcia, 64, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with two counts of illegally voting in federal elections in November 2022 and November 2024. Garcia knew he was not a U.S. citizen but nevertheless claimed to be one when registering to vote in 2004 and again in 2013. Garcia has allegedly voted regularly for the last 20 years in at least 15 elections, including at least 13 federal elections.
District of Idaho
Canadian national Stanley Walton, 82, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with unlawfully voting in the 2022 general election. Walton allegedly voted even though he was not a U.S. citizen.
District of New Jersey
Lizabeth Almonte Rosa, 24, a naturalized U.S. citizen from the Dominican Republic, has been charged by criminal complaint with voting by an alien in a federal election and unlawfully procuring citizenship. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court, Rosa was not a citizen when she was registered to vote.
Southern District of Ohio
British national Cary Ann Patterson, 59, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. The complaint alleges that Patterson voted in November 2024. According to court documents, in 2005, the Gallia County Board of Elections received a voter registration card for Patterson in which “Yes” was marked in response to the question, “Are you a U.S. citizen?” Based on Gallia County Board of Elections records, Patterson allegedly voted in at least 10 elections as an alien.
Northern District of Ohio
Two aliens have been charged with unlawfully voting in a federal election.
- Pakistani national Arshed Zuberi, 69, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. He allegedly registered to vote in September 2015 and August 2016. On voter registration forms, Zuberi’s signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Voting records from the Cuyahoga County Board of Elections show that he voted in at least six elections.
- Filipino national Eliza M. Moss, 63, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with unlawfully voting in a federal election as an alien. According to voting records, Moss registered to vote in September 2004 and in February 2023. On voter registration forms, her signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Moss allegedly voted in several primary and general elections. According to the criminal complaint, Moss told investigators that the person who helped fill out her registration told her that she could vote despite not being a citizen.
District of Hawaii
Polish national Dawid Nalepa, 45, has been charged by information with unlawfully voting as an alien. Nepela came to the United States in or around 2020 through the Visa Waiver Program, which he overstayed before applying for permanent resident status. Nalepa was not a U.S. citizen when he allegedly cast a vote in the November 2024, general election. Nalepa understood he was not a citizen at the time he cast his ballot.
Western District of Kentucky
Canadian national Sandra Madeline Watson, 59, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegal voting by an alien in a federal election. Watson allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of the President, Vice President, member of the Senate, or member of the House of Representatives, knowing she was not a U.S. citizen.
A complaint, indictment, and information merely contain accusations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 16 Individuals for Election Crimes

Following President Trump’s Executive Order, USDA Urges States to Review Wolf Management Policies and Strengthen Engagement with Ranchers
(Washington, D.C., October 12, 2026) – Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins urged state partners to review their wolf management policies, strengthen engagement with livestock producers, and work with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to address wolf predation. This outreach follows President Trump’s Executive Order 14425, titled “Supporting America’s Ranchers,” and builds on the Trump Administration’s commitment to give producers the tools they need to protect their herds and livelihoods.
“For too long, America’s ranchers have dealt with wolves threatening and killing their livestock, their livelihoods, and the family operations they have spent generations building,” said Secretary Brooke L. Rollins, “As ranchers await federal clarity on this issue, I am urging states to listen to their producers, review state-specific wolf protections, and work with USDA wherever possible to protect livestock, including through lethal removal when requested by the appropriate authorities and authorized by law. The most pro-rancher Administration in history will continue standing with our ranchers and working to rebuild the Great American Cattle Herd.
“American ranchers have been forced to deal with apex predators devastating livestock for far too long despite these protected species exceeding recovery goals long ago,” said Representative Hageman. “Those who work around the clock to keep our shelves stocked and neighbors fed deserve to be fairly compensated for losses from D.C.-protected predators like the grey and Mexican wolf. I am pleased to see President Trump and Secretary Rollins taking steps to relieve our ranchers of unnecessary predators on their lands and deliver due compensation when losses happen.”
USDA is encouraging states to engage directly with ranchers and raise awareness of how to report suspected predation to the appropriate state agencies or the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS). USDA’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) Wildlife Services provides wolf damage management assistance at the request of the appropriate state agencies or the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS). Requests for lethal removal must come from those authorities and be supported by the requisite agreements, environmental analyses, and compliance with state and federal law. APHIS currently supports state and federal partners through more than 40 agreements.
Wolf predation can increase producers’ costs through livestock losses, management expenses, and reduced livestock weights. Under the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, USDA’s Farm Service Agency increased Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP) payment rates for qualifying predation losses to 100% of the determined market value. Eligible producers who lose livestock to qualifying wolf attacks should contact their local Farm Service Agency office for eligibility and application information.
For more information, please visit: https://www.usda.gov/form/ranchers-first

RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts AAPI Roundtable in Palisades Park
Highlights Work to Lower Costs, Protect Communities, Support Small Businesses and Discuss Challenges in the AAPI Community
Above: Gottheimer hosts AAPI Roundtable.
PALISADES PARK, NJ —Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a roundtable with Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) leaders and community members from across North Jersey at the Palisades Park Library to discuss the challenges facing the AAPI community and what Washington can do to help. Joined by local elected officials, community organizations, educators, health care advocates, small business owners, and cultural and ethnic associations, Gottheimer outlined his work on health care, affordability, small business, anti-Asian hate, public safety, immigration, and education, and heard directly from participants about what their neighbors need most.
“The AAPI community represents different ethnicities, languages, faiths, and traditions, but the same drive to strengthen our communities. That’s why I’m working so hard in Washington and across the aisle to support you. But celebrating this community isn’t enough,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).
Across the Fifth District, roughly 127,000 residents are Asian American, or about one in six. This includes nearly half of Englewood Cliffs and more than forty-three percent of Fort Lee. Palisades Park, which has the highest percentage and density of Korean residents of any town in the country, is located within the District.
Gottheimer, a member of the Korea, India, Taiwan, Asia Pacific American, and Pacific Islands Caucuses and Co-Chair of the American Sikh Congressional Caucus, discussed the following priorities and his relevant legislation with attendees:
- Mental Health Emergency Care: Gottheimer secured $2 million to expand the behavioral health emergency department at New Bridge Medical Center in Paramus, growing it from 19 to 49 beds, with 30 beds dedicated to mental health and substance abuse treatment and 50 new clinical jobs. He is also part of the bipartisan push to extend and reform the ACA enhanced premium tax credits.
- Affordability: As Co-Chair of the bipartisan SALT Caucus, he is pushing the SALT Deductibility Act to fully restore the SALT deduction. His Tariff Impact Act would require the Congressional Budget Office to review the economic impact of any new tariff before they take effect.
- Medicaid and CHIP: New restrictions on lawfully present immigrants, part of the OBBB law that he voted against, recently took effect. Roughly 300,000 New Jersey residents could lose Medicaid or fail to get it, mostly because of paperwork.
- Small Business: Under a policy that took effect March 1, 2026, the SBA no longer backs loans to businesses with any non-citizen ownership. Even a green card holder with a 1 percent stake disqualifies a business. In FY2024 alone, the agency backed 8,900 loans worth $7.2 billion to Asian-owned businesses.
- Anti-Sikh Hate: Gottheimer introduced the Sikh American Anti-Discrimination Act with Congressman David Valadao (R-CA) in January 2026. It would create a DOJ Task Force on Anti-Sikh Discrimination, set a federal definition of anti-Sikh hate, develop education programs, and report annually to Congress. New Jersey is home to roughly 100,000 Sikhs.
- Public Safety: Gottheimer announced $42 million in FEMA funding in July 2026, split between $21 million statewide and $21 million for Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties. It covers radios, drones, K-9 units, and security upgrades for houses of worship such as cameras, alarms, guards, and reinforced doors. His bipartisan Invest to Protect Act would authorize $50 million a year for five years to help police departments with fewer than 200 officers with recruitment, training, mental health resources, and body cameras. He invited houses of worship that have not applied for Nonprofit Security Grants to call his office.
- Immigration: More than 1.2 million people are stuck in the employment-based green card backlog, nearly eighty percent from India, with a projected 179-year wait for an Indian EB-2 applicant. He voted to eliminate the per-country caps on employment-based green cards and says the country can secure the border and enforce its laws while treating people fairly.
- ICE Oversight: Gottheimer introduced the ICE Standards Act in January 2026, after the Minneapolis shootings. It would require stronger training, body and dash cameras, clear uniforms and ID, efforts to verify citizenship before detention, and limits on enforcement at schools, hospitals, and houses of worship. - Education: Gottheimer discussed the administration’s freeze of $23 million in English learner funding for New Jersey and cancellation of nearly $1 billion in school mental health grants. He supports doubling the Pell Grant and pointed to the roughly $5 billion the American Rescue Plan he helped write, negotiate, and pass in 2021, and delivered to Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions. He also introduced a resolution recognizing AANAPISI Week.

Congressman Don Davis Joins Congressional Ferry Caucus to Advocate for Eastern North Carolina’s Coastal Communities
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) announced he has joined the Congressional Ferry Caucus. As a member of the caucus, he will join 17 of his colleagues to focus on federal investment in our nation's ferry system.
"Ferries in eastern North Carolina's coastal communities are essential. They connect kids to school, residents to doctor visits, and workers to their jobs," said Congressman Don Davis. "As a new member of the bipartisan Congressional Ferry Caucus, my focus is to advocate for more federal investment in the ferry system so that coastal communities can remain connected."
The State of Washington operates the largest ferry system in the nation, and North Carolina's ferry system follows as the second-largest.
There are a total of seven scheduled ferry routes that link eastern North Carolina communities. Ferries provide access to basic needs and necessities, support the local economy through tourism and trade, and are still a significant part of their daily lives. Ferry transportation is vital to our residents and businesses along the coast.
Representatives Emily Randall (WA-06), Nick Begich (AK-AL), John Garamendi (CA-08), and Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) are the founding members of the caucus, which was created in June 2025 to raise awareness in Washington, D.C., of our nation's ferry system among Congressional members and their staff.
