PHOENIX, Ariz. – During the week of enforcement operations from Oct. 3 through Oct. 9, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona brought immigration-related criminal charges against 345 individuals. Specifically, the United States filed 151 cases in which aliens illegally re-entered the United States, and the United States also charged 172 aliens for illegally entering the United States. In its ongoing effort to deter unlawful immigration, the United States filed 21 cases against 22 individuals responsible for smuggling illegal aliens into and within the District of Arizona.

These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), ICE- Homeland Security Investigations (ICE-HSI), U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF).

Recent matters of interest include:

United States of America v. Favela-Favela. On Oct. 5, 2026, Christina Favela-Favela was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Oct. 4, Favela drove a vehicle with her three children to the San Luis, Arizona Port of Entry seeking admission to the United States. Custom and Border Patrol (CBP) officers referred Favela’s vehicle to secondary inspection. CBP officers subsequently learned that on July 7, 2026, Favela had attempted to cross into the United States via the Lukeville, Arizona Port of Entry with two children and a male alien concealed under personal items. With this knowledge, BPAs used a canine unit on Oct. 4 and found a male passenger hiding in the fetal position under personal items in the cargo area of Favela’s vehicle. CPB officers determined the male was an illegal alien without legal authority to be in the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-1787]

United States v. Luis Angel Diaz-Jimenez. On Oct. 5, 2026, Luis Angel Diaz-Jimenez was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien for Profit. On Oct. 2, Border Patrol Agents (BPAs) attempted to stop a Dodge Charger for an immigration inspection. Instead of yielding to BPAs, the driver, Diaz-Jimenez, accelerated, reaching speeds of approximately 100 mph before leaving the roadway, driving through a fenceline, and coming to a stop in the desert. Three subjects, including the Diaz-Jimenez, then got out of the vehicle and ran. BPAs pursued the subjects on foot and apprehended all three. The two passengers were determined to be citizens of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-10005]

A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

text:
HHS Launches Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit Program to Support Mothers and Babies
MORGANTOWN, WV—OCTOBER 9, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) today launched the Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit (NEST) Program at West Virginia University Medicine Golisano Children’s Hospital in Morgantown, West Virginia, marking the next phase of a federal initiative designed to support mothers and babies during the critical first days and weeks after birth.
Led by HHS through the Office of Intergovernmental and External Affairs (IEA) in coordination with the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), NEST provides families with a one-time kit of essential newborn and postpartum supplies, maternal health items, and trusted information and resources around the time of birth.
“President Trump is putting mothers, babies, and strong families at the center of his health agenda,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Through NEST, HHS is delivering essential supplies and trusted health information directly to families around the time of birth, including in rural and underserved communities. I thank Governor Morrisey for partnering with us to launch this next phase in West Virginia and help more mothers care for themselves and their newborns.”
“West Virginia is proud to help launch NEST and put practical support directly into the hands of mothers and families,” said Governor Patrick Morrisey. “These kits will help new parents get some of the basic necessities they need while easing some of the financial pressure that comes with welcoming a new baby. We appreciate the Trump Administration and our federal partners for working with us to give West Virginia mothers and babies a healthy start.”
NEST builds on the Department’s Newborn Supply Kit initiative, first launched in 2023. In the 2024 evaluation, 99% of surveyed recipients said they would recommend the kit to another new parent, 76% said it helped reduce anxiety, and 72% reported reduced financial stress.
In 2026, Congress provided funding to continue the work of the Newborn Supply Kit. Through HRSA, HHS awarded $5 million in funding to the CDC Foundation to support implementation of NEST. The CDC Foundation also partners with HHS through an established public-private partnership supporting evaluation of the program.
As NEST expands, HHS is emphasizing geographic diversity and reaching areas of greatest need, including maternal care deserts, rural communities, and other medically underserved areas.
“Every child deserves the healthiest possible start in life, and every mother should have the support she needs during pregnancy and after her baby is born,” said HRSA Administrator Tom Engels. “NEST will provide families with essential supplies and trusted resources when they need them most, while helping reach mothers and babies in rural and medically underserved communities. Through this investment, the Trump Administration is strengthening support for families and helping parents care for themselves and their newborns during this critical time.”
Each NEST Kit includes practical supplies for both mom and baby, including diapers and wipes, an infant thermometer, postpartum recovery and breastfeeding supplies, a blood pressure monitor, and other newborn essentials. Families also receive trusted information on postpartum health, infant safety and care, feeding and nutrition, and available programs and resources.
NEST Kits are distributed through hospitals, federally qualified health centers, and other organizations providing maternity care to mothers late in pregnancy or around the time of birth. Through these trusted partners, HHS is working to reach families in communities across the country while prioritizing areas where mothers and babies face greater barriers to care and resources.
Through NEST, HHS is building on what families and healthcare providers said worked: providing useful, high-quality supplies at a moment when families need them most, while connecting mothers with trusted information to help care for themselves and their newborns.
For more information, visit hhs.gov/newbaby.

CFTC Issues Interim Final Rule Excluding Certain Activity from the Definition of Swap
October 09, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today published an Interim Final Rule that codifies the CFTC’s longstanding position that casino-style gambling products, including wagers placed on sportsbooks and casino games, are excluded from the “swap” definition.
“Casino-style gambling products are not derivatives,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Just as the CFTC has done with respect to other products historically regulated by the states, the Commission today provides clarity regarding the limits of its regulatory remit by codifying the exclusion of casino-style gambling products from the ‘swap’ definition.”
The IFR will be effective immediately upon publication in the Federal Register and written comments must be received via Regulations.gov within 30 days of the IFR’s publication in the Federal Register.

Washington, D.C. (October 9, 2026)—Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Jim Himes, Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, are urging Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel to cancel his reported trip to Russia next month, raising urgent national security concerns about his plans to visit Moscow and St. Petersburg as the FBI expands cooperation with Russian and Chinese law enforcement agencies. Patel will reportedly be hosted by Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), the successor to the Soviet-era KGB, which has a documented history of conducting espionage operations against American officials and personnel.
“Winston Churchill described Russia as ‘a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma.’ Now, we have a puzzle buried in a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside that enigma: Why is the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) visiting a hostile foreign power that has been committing war crimes, conducting influence operations against U.S. elections, conducting malicious cyberattacks against our critical infrastructure, and helping our adversaries target and kill American soldiers?” wrote the Ranking Members. “In the interest of national security, we ask you to reconsider. Call off this trip.”
The trip comes amid reports that Patel is personally leading an initiative to forge closer ties between the FBI and Russian and Chinese law enforcement agencies, including personnel exchanges and intelligence sharing. While the Administration strikes a big anti-China pose, Patel has reportedly already provided Chinese officials unprecedented access to American intelligence personnel, diplomatic personnel, government facilities and contractors, despite longstanding warnings that foreign intelligence services will exploit such access to conduct espionage.
The timing raises additional concerns. In the last two weeks, President Trump signed sweeping sanctions targeting Russia’s economy over its war against Ukraine. Meanwhile, Russia continues to conduct espionage and cyberattacks against the United States and its allies, and has reportedly provided Iran with intelligence to help refine aerial attacks on American troops in the Middle East. DOJ also recently revealed a Russian intelligence-linked murder-for-hire plot targeting a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C.
Patel’s hosts are no ordinary law enforcement partners. Russia’s FSB has a documented history of surveilling American officials, planting recording devices and conducting honey trap operations targeting U.S. personnel. Compounding these concerns, Patel received $25,000 for participating in a documentary produced by a filmmaker with Kremlin ties, in which he openly dismissed U.S. intelligence assessments of Russian election interference and claimed Moscow was not among America’s “true enemies.”
The Ranking Members are calling on Patel to cancel his trip and, if he insists on proceeding, are requesting a closed-door briefing on the FBI’s expanding cooperation with foreign adversaries and the security precautions surrounding his odd visit. The briefing must address the FBI’s efforts to increase cooperation with Russia, China and other designated foreign entities; any internal concerns or objections to those efforts; who proposed the trip and why; Patel’s complete itinerary, planned meetings and traveling companions; and precautions to protect against Russian espionage, including technological safeguards, and additional counterintelligence measures.
Click here to read the letter.
title: Ranking Members Himes, Raskin Urge Kash Patel to Abandon Russia Trip Hosted By Putin’s Security Service Amid Espionage Concerns

Liccardo Leads Bipartisan Push to Bring Whale Alerts to West Coast Mariners
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Bay Area Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16) led a bipartisan effort to leverage technology to protect whales on the West Coast. His recent letter to the U.S. Coast Guard, the Federal Communications Commission, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration requests an expansion of Automatic Identification System (AIS) messaging technology to send whale-safety information directly to mariners along the West Coast.
“With at least 145 gray whale collisions already reported along the West Coast in 2026, we must do more to keep both whales and mariners safe,” said Liccardo. “By implementing AIS whale-safety messages, we can give real-time warnings to mariners and help them avoid deadly collisions, without disrupting maritime activities."
Liccardo and his cosigners request the agencies identify areas where AIS messaging could support voluntary speed reductions messages, determine whether existing whale detection programs can transmit information directly to mariners through AIS, and identify ways to streamline approval timelines while maintaining navigation and spectrum safeguards.
On the East Coast, federal agencies and regional partners already use AIS messaging to send vessel location-specific alerts in whale speed reduction zones. Expanding AIS whale-safety messaging to the West Coast would use technology already familiar to mariners to provide additional information about whale activity.
“Expanding this capability is particularly relevant along the West Coast, where vessel traffic and whale activity increasingly overlap,” the lawmakers wrote.
The effort builds on Liccardo’s Save Willy Act, which would establish a “Whale Desk” at the Coast Guard’s San Francisco station to centralize whale sightings and alert vessel operators when whales enter the Bay.
“Using AIS technology to identify high-risk areas and alert mariners in real time can help prevent deadly vessel collisions with whales off California while keeping vital maritime traffic moving safely,” said Geoff Shester, Director of Fishery Innovation and Senior Scientist at Oceana. “This proven technology would give agencies and ship operators a practical, science-based tool to protect whales and improve safety in our busy coastal waters for all who use them.”
“Vessel strikes are a leading cause of death and serious injury for large whales and can result in substantial property damage for mariners as well as pose a significant safety risk to those onboard. IFAW has worked tirelessly in the pursuit of reducing the threat of vessel strikes and strongly supports the use of AIS as a warming system for mariners. We're grateful to Representatives Liccardo, Case, Krishnamoorthi, Min, Moylan, and Pallone for championing the use of AIS to improve mariner safety and help reduce the risk of vessel strikes on whales along the West Coast," said Kathleen Collins, International Fund for Animal Welfare Senior Marine Campaign Manager.
Congressmembers Ed Case (HI-01), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Dave Min (CA-47), Frank Pallone (NJ-06), and James Moylan (Guam) signed the letter.
Read the full letter here.
title: Liccardo Leads Bipartisan Push to Bring Whale Alerts to West Coast Mariners

New York, NY – Rochelle M. Garza, Chair of the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights, moderated the People’s Hearing on Immigration Enforcement in New York on October 8, hearing directly from affected residents, advocates, business owners, and local leaders about the civil rights implications of federal immigration enforcement.
The community-led forum examined immigration enforcement in New York City and Long Island; interactions with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and conditions in detention; uncertainty facing communities with Temporary Protected Status; the economic impact of enforcement; and issues affecting unaccompanied children and their sponsors. Chair Garza served as a moderator alongside Hispanic Federation President Frankie Miranda and former Commission Chair Marty Castro.
In remarks preceding the hearing, Chair Garza emphasized the importance of listening directly to communities and creating a public record of their experiences.
“Our communities are not going to have true healing until we have accountability from the systems that have caused harm,” Chair Garza said.
The New York hearing continued a national series of community-organized forums. Chair Garza has heard from communities in Los Angeles, St. Paul, Chicago, Charlotte, and across Texas. She thanked the Hispanic Federation, Latino Victory, the Texas Civil Rights Project, the Miranda Family Fund, and participating local organizations and individuals for their work to document the effects of immigration enforcement.
Chair Garza participated as part of her continuing response to a congressional request, led by the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, urging the Commission to investigate civil rights concerns related to federal immigration enforcement.
The Commission and its State Advisory Committees have previously examined immigration detention conditions, the treatment of adults and children in federal custody, and related civil rights protections.
See Relevant Commission Reports:
- Civil Rights in Immigrant Detention Centers in New Mexico (2025) – A New Mexico Advisory Committee report examining civil rights concerns in the state’s immigrant detention centers, including due process and unsafe conditions.
- Trauma at the Border: The Human Cost of Inhumane Immigration Policies (2019) – An examination of asylum policies, the detention of children, and related human and civil rights concerns at the southern.
- With Liberty and Justice for All: The State of Civil Rights at Immigration Detention Facilities (2015) – An examination of civil rights and constitutional concerns involving adults and children held in federal immigration detention.

title: Chair Garza Hears from New Yorkers on Civil Rights Concerns Related to Immigration Enforcement

Gainesville, Florida – Denzel Dyshaun Flagg, 27, of Gainesville, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of Hobbs Act Robbery. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This successful prosecution was made possible by the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners, who tracked down this defendant so we could hold him accountable for his role in this violent crime. We owe it to our citizens to protect them from the predations of violent criminals and to seek maximum punishment to hold those offenders accountable and deter future crime.”

Court documents reflect that on February 18, 2025, the defendant participated in the robbery of the Eastside Food Store in Gainesville, Florida. During the robbery, two other individuals entered the store wearing ski masks, and one of them pointed a gun directly at the face of the store clerk before stealing cash from the register. The defendant acted as the getaway driver.

Flagg faces a maximum sentence of twenty years’ imprisonment.

Sentencing is scheduled for November 3, 2026, at the United States Courthouse in Gainesville before United States Chief District Judge Allen C. Winsor.

The case involved a joint investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Alachua County Sherriff’s Office. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Adam Hapner and James McCain.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

Deep learning model using ECGs during sleep studies can predict cardiovascular outcomes
Friday, October 9, 2026
Deep learning model using ECGs during sleep studies can predict cardiovascular outcomes
Integrating ECGs into sleep disorder screening could enhance detection and guide clinical decision-making.
A research team supported by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) has found that electrocardiograms (ECGs) administered during sleep and paired with sleep stage information can be used to determine risk for future adverse cardiac events. The study, which used a deep learning approach, suggests that using ECGs to predict which patients have a greater risk for poor heart-related outcomes could help guide clinical decision-making. The findings were published in the journal Sleep.
“This new approach has the potential to identify individuals at risk for cardiovascular disease years before clinical symptoms arise,” said David Goff, M.D., Ph.D., acting director of NIH’s National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI). “Evaluating whether this information improves traditional risk prediction is an important next step. In the future, proven analytical approaches like this could be integrated into existing diagnostic tests for patients undergoing sleep studies as a screening tool for multiple adverse cardiovascular outcomes.”
Testing conducted overnight during sleep, known as polysomnography, is the standard method of diagnosing sleep disorders such as insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea, which are recognized as cardiovascular risk factors. ECGs are recorded during these tests but are not often analyzed. The research team in this study wanted to see if these recordings could be used to predict 10-year risk of cardiovascular outcomes such as atrial fibrillation, stroke, myocardial infarction, and heart failure, as well as all-cause mortality.
The researchers applied a deep learning system using single-lead ECGs from sleep studies combined with expert-annotated sleep stage data. The model was fine-tuned on a dataset of 15,809 patients at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, and performance was assessed on two datasets that included 9,810 patients from Emory University Hospital in Atlanta and 12,576 patients from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston. Outcomes were derived from electronic health records.
The team found that the model was able to sort people into groups with different levels of long-term cardiovascular risk, showing that people with higher scores were at higher risk. The deep learning model also retained its predictive value when adjusted for common cardiovascular risk factors such as age, sex, BMI, diabetes, and hypertension, as well as sleep-related characteristics such as sleep apnea severity, arousals, and sleep efficiency. The model could predict atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and death from any cause.
The scientists believe that additional optimization of the model is needed to determine prediction for myocardial infarction and stroke. Overall, they found that predicting cardiovascular outcomes from the ECG channel in sleep studies is a promising approach.
“Importantly, we found that adding the score from our deep learning model improved prediction of cardiac outcomes beyond established risk factors,” said Gari Clifford, D.Phil., study author, chair of the Department of Biomedical Informatics at Emory University School of Medicine, and professor of Biomedical Engineering at Georgia Institute of Technology. “Adding these scores into sleep studies has great potential for improving early detection of cardiovascular disease, determining who is most at risk, and being more proactive in patient care.”
In addition, this method, which uses just one ECG lead or electrical signal, is easier to collect than the usual 12-lead setup. Therefore, it offers a simple way to collect useful ECG data in just one night of sleep, making the approach highly accessible through simple, low-cost patches.
About the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI): NHLBI is the global leader in conducting and supporting research in heart, lung, and blood diseases and sleep disorders that advances scientific knowledge, improves public health, and saves lives.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
Reference:
Koscova Z, et al. Prediction of cardiovascular outcomes using ECG from overnight polysomnography. Sleep. 2026. DOI: 10.1093/sleep/zsag229
title: Deep learning model using ECGs during sleep studies can predict cardiovascular outcomes

BOSTON – A Worcester man has been indicted by a federal grand jury for allegedly distributing fentanyl and dealing in firearms without a license.

Omar Ramos-Jimenez, 27, was indicted on two counts of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl, one count of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and one count of dealing in firearms without a license. Ramos-Jimenez was arrested and charged in May 2026 . Ramos-Jimenez was released on conditions following an initial appearance in federal court in Worcester on Sept. 21, 2026.

According to the charging documents, between April 8, 2026 and April 16, 2026, Ramos-Jimenez allegedly sold fentanyl and several firearms including a privately manufactured pistol with no serial number, to confidential informants in Worcester.

The charge of dealing in firearms without a license provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. The charge of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl provides for a sentence of no less than five years in prison and up to life, at least four years of supervised release and a fine of up to $5 million. The charge of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, at least three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $1 million. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Thomas A. Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division; Worcester Police Chief Paul B. Saucier; and Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble, Superintendent of the Massachusetts State Police made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Drug Enforcement Administration; Homeland Security Investigations; the Suffolk County Sherrif’s Department; and the Worcester District Attorney’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan O’Shea of the Worcester Branch Office is prosecuting the cases.

This case was investigated and prosecuted by the Boston Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) as part of Operation Take Back America . HSTFs, which were established by President Trump in Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion, are joint operations led by the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security. Operation Take Back America is a nationwide federal initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces and Project Safe Neighborhood.

The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law.
title: Worcester Man Indicted on Firearm and Drug Distribution Charges

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Ruby Celly Uribe, 37, of Sacramento, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins to two years and five months in prison for unlawfully possession of a machine gun and possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

On May 26, 2026, a jury found Uribe guilty.

According to court documents and evidence presented at a trial, Uribe was assigned to the logistics shop at the California National Guard Headquarters in Mather, and was a member of the Counterdrug Task Force (CDTF). The CDTF supports local, tribal, and federal law enforcement entities in the interdiction of drug trafficking organizations. While assigned to this unit, Uribe leaked information about upcoming drug raids to a person she knew to be involved with drug dealing. Text messages recovered from Uribe’s and the drug dealer’s phones revealed she shared sensitive information about upcoming operations, including the date and location and the number of military vehicles and aircraft involved.

A federal search warrant of Uribe’s residence resulted in the discovery of a short-barreled rifle. The firearm had been modified to fire in full-automatic mode as a machine gun. In addition, it was a privately made firearm with no serial number, commonly referred to as a ghost gun. With certain exceptions, federal law prohibits the possession of machine guns and unregistered rifles with barrels shorter than 16 inches. A search of Uribe’s cellphone revealed that she was also engaged in trafficking other nonserialized, short-barreled machine guns, including to a co-worker on July 20, 2022.

During preparation for trial in this case, the FBI learned of another illegal firearm that Uribe sold in August 2022. The FBI safely recovered that firearm, which is also a machine gun and short-barreled rifle.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives conducted the investigation with assistance from the California Military Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Adrian T. Kinsella and Nicole M. Vanek prosecuted the case.
title: Former National Guard task force member sentenced for illegal firearm possession offenses that came to light during an investigation into leaks of sensitive operational information

AKRON, OH — U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) hosted the 2026 Women in Leadership Conference at the Akron Art Museum, bringing together more than 200 women entrepreneurs, elected officials, labor leaders, and community members from across Ohio's 13th Congressional District. The conference connected local entrepreneurs, innovators, and community members in a collaborative environment to share knowledge, build relationships, and help one another grow.

Sykes. “I'm grateful to every speaker and guest who joined us for honest conversations about leadership, economic empowerment, and public service. I look forward to continuing to build a pipeline of women leaders across our community, and to keep fighting for policies that give every woman the opportunity to thrive.”

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Polish national Dawid Nalepa, 45, was charged yesterday by Information with unlawfully voting as an alien.

Nalepa came to the United States in or around 2020 through the Visa Waiver Program, which he overstayed before applying for permanent resident status. According to court records, Nalepa was not a United States citizen when he cast a vote in the November 2024 general election. Nalepa understood he was not a citizen at the time he cast his ballot.

If convicted, Nalepa faces up to one year in prison, a fine of up to $100,000, and a term of supervised release.

The charge in the Information is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. In the case of conviction, any sentence would be imposed by a United States District Judge based on the statutory sentencing factors and the advisory United States Sentencing Guidelines.

Homeland Security Investigations is investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Arisa Herman is prosecuting the case.
title: Polish National Charged with Unlawfully Voting as an Alien

CONCORD – United States Attorney Erin Creegan announced today that four additional defendants have pleaded guilty to federal firearms offenses in connection with an international firearms trafficking conspiracy that funneled illegally obtained weapons from New Hampshire through the Akwesasne Mohawk Indian Reservation in New York. The investigation uncovered that members of the conspiracy trafficked firearms into Canada while also trafficking narcotics and humans into the United States.

The four latest defendants to plead guilty in the case between the dates of September 26 and October 9, 2026 are all residents of the Akwesane Mohawk Indian Reservation straddling the U.S.-Canada border from New York to Quebec. They are:

Conrad Oakes , 25, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 23, 2027.

Tayson Terrance , 24, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 19, 2027.

Ranonkwatseronhawi Gibson , 22, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027.

Montana Cook , 27, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027.

Oakes, Terrance, Gibson and Cook were among eight defendants indicted in May 2026. Five other defendants, including Justin Jackson, Melissa Longe, Dustin Tuttle, Caleb Wilcott, and Doug Mulligan, had previously pleaded guilty to firearms offenses arising from the investigation.

According to court documents, the investigation began with a firearms trace. A firearm was recovered by the Montreal City Police Department (SVPM) in Montreal, Quebec as part of a search warrant executed in a kidnapping investigation. SVPM recovered a firearm with an obliterated serial number, which they were able to restore. This firearm was purchased by defendant and co-conspirator Dustin Tuttle in New Hampshire. Subsequent investigation revealed a larger conspiracy to smuggle weapons from New Hampshire to Vermont, New York, and ultimately to Canada.

ATF and HSI agents learned that the conspiracy utilized the Akwesasne reservation to cross between the U.S. and Canada. One of the defendants utilized jets skis to smuggle contraband, including straw purchased firearms, from the New York portion of the Akwesasne to Cornwall Island. Once the contraband was on Cornwall Island, a resident would then ferry the contraband through the checkpoint and further into Canada. Through this investigation, the ATF and HSI learned that drugs, humans, and guns were trafficked to and from Canada utilizing Cornwall Island.

ATF and HSI have identified approximately 51 firearms potentially trafficked from New Hampshire to Canada through Vermont and the Akwesasne reservation in New York and Canada, at least ten of which were subsequently recovered at various Canadian crime scenes, in Canada. For example, after an attempted shooting in a parking lot in Montreal, Canadian law enforcement was able to find the discarded firearm which was used. That firearm was purchased by defendant and member of the conspiracy, Melissa Longe, from a Federal Firearms Licensee in Winchester, New Hampshire.

This investigation was led by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). The Ontario Provincial Police (OPP), Sûreté du Québec (SQ), Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Police (SRMTP), Akwesasne Mohawk Police Service (AMPS), New York Department of Corrections and Community Supervision-Office of Special Investigations, Manchester Police Department, and the Keene Police Department have provided valuable assistance.

“These defendants have admitted to operating a sophisticated firearms trafficking network that exploited New Hampshire gun dealers, straw purchasers, and the international border to move dozens of firearms into Canada, facilitating further trafficking crime and violent crimes,” said Erin Creegan, United States Attorney for the District of New Hampshire. “Guns purchased in New Hampshire and traded through this criminal enterprise were later recovered at crime scenes involving offenses such as kidnapping and attempted murder. We are grateful for the partnership between our federal agencies, Canadian and tribal authorities, as well as state and local law enforcement in New Hampshire and New York that helped investigate these crimes and take down this dangerous network.”

“These convictions demonstrate the effectiveness of intelligence-driven policing and cooperative law enforcement efforts in bringing criminal charges against firearm traffickers. Crime gun intelligence connected firearms recovered at different crime scenes in Canada, advancing our Canadian partner’s domestic investigations into violent crime while simultaneously alerting ATF to a transnational firearms trafficking scheme at work in the United States. The guilty pleas hold accountable individuals who exploited that access to firearms and the freedom to travel while undermining public safety in both countries. ATF is proud of our partnerships with our federal, state, local and international law enforcement partners and will continue to work together to build safe communities on both sides of the border,” said Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of ATF Boston Field Division.

“These guilty pleas demonstrate the serious consequences of trafficking firearms across international borders and into communities where they can fuel violent crime. This case is a powerful example of what can be accomplished when law enforcement partners share intelligence, resources, and expertise across jurisdictions and borders. ATF remains committed to identifying, disrupting, and dismantling firearms trafficking networks that threaten public safety. We commend the outstanding work of ATF Boston and ATF New York Albany personnel, HSI New York, Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Police, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire, and our Canadian law enforcement partners whose persistence and collaboration brought these defendants to justice,” said Bryan DiGirolamo, Special Agent in Charge of ATF’s New York Field Division.

The charge of conspiracy to straw-purchase firearms provides a maximum prison term of 25 years, a maximum fine of $250,000, and not more than five years of supervised release. The charge of conspiracy to traffic firearms provides a maximum prison term of 15 years, a maximum fine of $250,000, and not more than three years of supervised release. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Hampshire comprises agents and officers from FBI, HSI, IRS, DEA, ATF, USMS, and DSS with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire.

Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Christopher Marin, Assistant U.S. Attorney Yasir Sadat, and Paralegal Specialist Kristina McNamara are handling the prosecution on behalf of the United States.

NEWARK, NJ – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) and her legal counsel filed a brief requesting that the full U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit hear her case en banc.
The appeal highlights major constitutional problems with the charges the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ) brought against McIver arising out of her May 2025 oversight inspection of Delaney Hall, ICE detention facility in her district. This move for hearing en banc comes after a divided panel of three Third Circuit judges refused to dismiss the case against McIver in August.
By appealing, McIver continues her fight to protect her constitutional and statutory authority to oversee ICE, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and the rest of the executive branch. The full text of the brief can be found here.
“As I have said since last May, oversight is my job. I am pursuing this step in no small part because every single day since last May, we have seen only more terror surrounding Delaney Hall—from brutality outside of its gates to retribution behind its walls and horror stories from the detainees I’ve spoken with on my many visits. What’s happening here and in ICE facilities nationwide only further proves why members of Congress need to be able to do this critical oversight work to protect people—work that Trump’s administration wants to stop by locking me in prison for 17 years,” said McIver. “Members of Congress have a right to do oversight even, and especially, when the administration does not like what they find. I will fight like hell to protect that right. I will continue to oppose these baseless charges and this intimidation, and I will keep doing my job, not without fear, but in spite of it.”
Paul J. Fishman, counsel to McIver, added context about the stakes of the case and the court’s August ruling on the same issues.
“This case is about whether the Executive Branch can interfere with and try to intimidate members of Congress who are doing the oversight the Constitution requires of them. Congresswoman McIver has been incredibly brave in taking on a fight against an administration that targeted lawmakers and others for speaking out when they see abuses,” said Fishman. “The executive branch should not and cannot be allowed to use its power over criminal prosecutions to retaliate against those it would like to silence.”
The charges against McIver stem from an oversight visit she conducted at Delaney Hall, a controversial ICE detention center in her district, in May, 2025. She is the only member of Congress under indictment by the Trump DOJ for performing constitutionally protected oversight of ICE and, if convicted, faces up to 17 years in federal prison.
###
title: McIver Moves For Appeal To Be Heard En Banc By Third Circuit, Refuses to Back Down

FORT WORTH, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a Springtown, Texas, man who repeatedly issued violent threats against the President of the United States and federal immigration officers was sentenced to 33 months in federal prison.

On June 9, 2025, Francisco Jesus Mena, 37, pleaded guilty to one count of threatening a federal official. U.S. Chief District Judge Reed O’Connor imposed the sentence today.

“Threats against the President and federal officers are crimes that my office takes very seriously,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “We will continue to prosecute individuals like the defendant who seek to intimidate, impede or retaliate against federal law enforcement for performing vital national security and immigration related duties.”

“Threats against the President and federal officers are crimes that my office takes very seriously,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “We will continue to prosecute individuals like the defendant who seek to intimidate, impede or retaliate against federal law enforcement for performing vital national security and immigration related duties.”

“This sentence makes clear that conveying violent online threats is a serious criminal offense with substantial consequences, said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “The FBI remains committed to ensuring that individuals who exploit digital platforms to intimidate, coerce, or instill fear are held accountable.”

“The U.S. Secret Service investigates all threats against our protectees,” said Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Secret Service Dallas Field Office Christina Foley. “Threats against the President will not be tolerated. We continue to work alongside our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners to investigate these threats and will hold those who threaten to harm any of our protectees accountable.”

According to court documents, between May 13 and May 25, 2025, Mena made numerous threats against President Trump and ICE agents in a series of online messages posted to social media. The defendant repeatedly threatened to assault and murder the President, writing variations of “KILL TRUMP” across multiple dates and platforms. He also issued threats directed at federal law enforcement officers stating that if ICE agents came to his residence, he would “respond with a gunfight,” and claiming he had previously stabbed an ICE agent and “would love to do this again.”

On several occasions, Mena claimed that ICE personnel would be targeted next and encouraged violence against federal officers and white people, stating that individuals with “blue eyes and white skin will get chopped,” and offering payment or solicitation to harm the President. He further stated he did not need money to “take out Trump” and requested access to a sniper.

The FBI and the U.S. Secret Service conducted the investigation with assistance from local law enforcement. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justin Beck and Ethan Womble from the Fort Worth Division prosecuted the case.

###
title: Local man sentenced to 33 months in federal prison for threatening the President and federal law enforcement officers

text:
Goodlander joins 190 colleagues urging Secretary Kennedy to withdraw proposed rule that would dismantle safeguards for early education, child safety, and health services.
Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) joined House and Senate colleagues this week in urging U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to withdraw a proposed rule that would weaken Head Start standards protecting children and supporting working families across New Hampshire.
The letter opposes the Administration’s proposed “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs” rule, warning that it would remove more than 90 percent of existing program standards and undermine the high-quality early education, health services, and family support that make Head Start a lifeline for families.
“Every child in New Hampshire deserves a safe place to learn, grow, and get a fair shot at success. Head Start helps deliver on that promise while helping hardworking parents stay in the workforce and provide for their families,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “At a time when Granite Staters are struggling to find and afford childcare, Secretary Robert F. Kennedy is brazenly trying to dismantle Head Start, and make it harder for kids and families to get the care they need. That is unacceptable. I’m fighting to protect Head Start and make quality childcare more affordable and accessible for New Hampshire families.”
The lawmakers warn that the proposal would eliminate federal requirements governing staff-to-child ratios and class sizes, weaken staff qualifications and safety training, and roll back standards for developmental screenings, dental care, and mental health services. They also raise concerns that shorter program hours would leave working parents scrambling to find additional childcare, while new documentation requirements would create barriers for families with the greatest needs.
The letter further objects to removing detailed protections for children with disabilities and children experiencing homelessness, and to changes that would undermine instruction for dual-language learners.
Read the full letter HERE.
BACKGROUND ON GOODLANDER’S ADVOCACY FOR CHILDREN AND WORKING FAMILIES
Congresswoman Goodlander is working to lower childcare costs, expand access to early education, and support the educators and programs New Hampshire families rely on.
- Defending Head Start: Goodlander previously joined the Democratic Women’s Caucus in urging Secretary Kennedy to withdraw the same proposed rule, opposing efforts to weaken standards for child safety, early learning, health services, and support for children with disabilities.
- Making quality childcare more affordable: Goodlander helped introduce the Child Care for Working Families Act, which would cap working families’ childcare expenses at seven percent of income, expand the supply of quality care, and increase wages for early childhood educators. The legislation would also support full-day, full-year Head Start programs and higher wages for Head Start workers.
- Helping children and families get to school: Goodlander introduced the bipartisan PATH to Education Act to improve affordable, reliable transportation to Head Start centers and educational institutions. The bill would help connect transit routes to schools and better align transportation schedules with program hours.
- Investing in New Hampshire’s childcare workforce: Goodlander helped secure nearly $1 million for Nashua Community College’s Early Childhood Education Center. The center will help prepare future early childhood educators and expand access to quality childcare, with opportunities for students to observe, collaborate, and teach alongside Head Start teachers.
- Expanding childcare in New Hampshire communities: Goodlander helped secure federal Community Project Funding, including $1 million for Bristol’s Tapply-Thompson Community Center, $688,000 for the Gorham Community Learning Center, and $1.6 million for Sullivan County’s Regional Childcare Enhancement Project. These investments will support a new community center in Bristol, conversion of a vacant bank into a childcare facility in Gorham, and a new childcare center on Sullivan County’s Unity Campus.
###
title: Goodlander Pushes Back Against Trump Administration Plan to Dismantle Head Start, Protects New Hampshire Children and Working Families

Matthew Kashas, age 43, from Sioux City, Iowa, plead guilty October 8, 2026, in federal court in Sioux City, to distribution of child pornography. Kashas was previously convicted in the Northern District of Iowa for distributing child pornography in 2009 and 2016. He previously served 5-year and 10-year prison sentences, respectively, and was currently on supervised release at the time of the offense.

At the plea hearing, Kashas admitted that from May 1, 2025, and December 1, 2025, soon after his release from federal prison, he received, possessed and distributed child pornography. Kashas would access chat sites looking for moms with young daughters willing to engage in sex acts and encouraged the mothers to drug their children and send him photos. This included people from the Sioux City area. Kashas admitted to the conduct in an interview with Sioux City police and described he would routinely destroy his electronics to avoid detection from his probation officer. Law enforcement executed a search warrant on Kashas’ phone and discovered 434 images and 104 videos of child pornography, including images of child pornography saved at the lockscreen and background of his device. The images and videos involved material that portrayed sadistic or masochistic conduct, as well as prepubescent children and toddlers.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC.

Sentencing before United States District Court Judge Leonard T. Strand will be set after a presentence report is prepared. Kashas remains in custody of the United States Marshal pending sentencing. Kashas faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years’ imprisonment and a possible maximum sentence of 40 years’ imprisonment, a $250,000 fine, and at least five years of supervised release following any imprisonment.

The case was investigated by the Sioux City Police Department and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Kraig R. Hamit.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file number is 25-4069. Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.

PROVIDENCE – A former employee of Santander Bank has been sentenced in federal court for stealing more than $125,000 from the bank account of a 78-year-old customer with dementia.

Carlos Bras, 41, of East Providence, was sentenced on October 8, 2026, by U.S. District Court Judge Melissa R. DuBose to 30 months of imprisonment to be followed by 3 years of supervised release and a $200 special assessment. Bras was also ordered to pay $126,000 in restitution. Bras previously pleading guilty to mail fraud and aggravated identity theft.

According to court documents, beginning in or about May 2023, Bras accessed the account of the 78-year-old victim, who resided in an assisted living facility and had a court-appointed conservator in Massachusetts.

Bras admitted that he enabled online banking access to the victim’s account; ordered checks sent to addresses he controlled; obtained a debit card for personal use; and conducted numerous unauthorized transactions, including transfers to accounts controlled by him and his family and multiple wire transfers to a bank account in Portugal.

Investigators also discovered a purported real estate contract in Portugal bearing the signatures of Bras and the victim. The victim’s conservator reported that the victim was unaware of the transaction and that the signature and listed address were not the victim’s.

“Mr. Bras exploited his position at a financial institution and took advantage of an elderly man who could not protect himself,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Charles C. Calenda. “Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of that betrayal and the commitment of our office and our law enforcement partners to safeguard vulnerable members of our community.”

Seattle – Just days before the 25 th anniversary of the unsolved murder of Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas C. Wales, law enforcement leaders again urge members of the public to come forward if they have information that could help solve the case. Wales was shot and killed the night of October 11, 2001, as he worked on a computer in the basement of his Queen Anne neighborhood home. If Wales was killed because of his work as a federal prosecutor, it remains the only unsolved murder of a federal prosecutor because of his work.

The Department of Justice and the National Association of Former U.S. Attorneys are offering a $2.5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of a subject in this case.

“I still remember hearing about this murder twenty-five years ago while I was serving as an Army Judge Advocate at Fort Lewis. This crime had a tremendous impact on the entire U.S. Attorney community and we have not forgotten. The FBI and U.S. Attorney’s Office continue to devote resources to this active investigation,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “We are committed to using all tools available including new computer Super Intelligence to bring those responsible to justice. Now is the time to come forward if you have information that could prove useful in solving this case. The $2.5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction is a real offer and should provide an incentive to do the right thing.”

“For 25 years, the FBI has continued to actively pursue those responsible for the murder of AUSA Wales,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “Tom was one of us and a valued member of this community, which makes this a case that is especially important to both Seattle and law enforcement. An attack on a federal prosecutor is an attack on our entire justice system and the American way of life. If you have information about this case, now is the time to speak up. We are still receiving tips and pursuing all leads so that we can finally bring justice for Tom and his family. Don’t let one of those tips bring the FBI to you before you can report what you know on your own terms.”

Acting U.S. Attorney Floyd and Special Agent in Charge Herrington went to the former Wales home today to get a briefing. Those close to the investigation explained where they believe the shooter stood when firing the shots, what was the apparent escape route, and how the site has changed over the intervening 25 years, altering the landscape.

The Seattle Prosecutor Murder (SEPROM) Task Force is now a joint effort by the FBI, the Seattle Police Department, the Department of Justice, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Washington and the King County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office. The task force is also leveraging emerging and evolving technologies in the effort.

Anyone with information is encouraged to contact the FBI and can do so confidentially by phone at (206) 622-0460 or by e-mail at walestips@fbi.gov . Tips can also be sent to the FBI at 1110 Third Avenue, Seattle, WA, 98101. The FBI Seeking Information poster, details about the tip lines and more can be found at https://www.fbi.gov/wanted/seeking-info/thomas-crane-wales . With more information about the case available here: https://www.fbi.gov/news/stories/wales-investigation-help-us-find-a-killer
title: Wales murder investigation remains active some 25 years after fatal shooting

      WASHINGTON, D.C. – House Military Personnel Subcommittee Ranking Member Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) and Armed Services Committee Ranking Member Adam Smith (WA-09) released the following statement responding to the Department of Defense announcing publicly that it had miscounted the number of U.S. service members who have died in the Central Command Area of Responsibility as part of Operation Epic Fury and other Overseas Operations.
“Today’s public correction in the number of U.S. service members who have died in the Middle East since President Trump launched his disastrous war of choice against Iran was the direct result of congressional oversight. Specifically, this committee discovered a discrepancy in the Pentagon’s reporting of casualty numbers, brought it to the Trump Administration’s attention, and worked to ensure they publicly corrected this incredibly important record.
“There is no excuse for a mistake of this magnitude. While we take seriously our duty to serve as the voice of the American people and hold the executive branch accountable as a co-equal branch of government, requiring Congress to step in to rectify such an egregious error is an embarrassment for the Department. The failure of Secretary Hegseth to immediately take ownership of the problem also does a grave disservice to the men and women putting their lives on the line in service to our country.
“We are glad to see the error has been corrected, and we will continue to fight for transparency and accountability. While this public correction is an important first step, we expect the Department to make the necessary changes to policies and procedures to ensure this mistake is not repeated and that they are more transparent with the public going forward.”
--end--

Pappas, 189 Members of Congress Slam HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start
Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) joined 189 Members of Congress in demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.
The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.
“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”
Since the beginning of the second Trump administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely.
To read the full letter, click here.
title: Pappas, 189 Members of Congress Slam HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start

PHOENIX, Ariz. – Hector Ambrosio Ruiz, 30, of Mexico, was arrested yesterday and charged by criminal complaint for Harboring Illegal Aliens.

On Oct. 7, 2026, agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) executed a federal search warrant at a Phoenix residence suspected of being a stash house for illegal aliens. Upon entering the residence, investigators found twelve individuals hiding in a closet. Ruiz was found among the twelve and was the only one wearing shoes. Law enforcement confirmed that all twelve individuals are citizens of foreign countries without legal authority to reside in the United States.

While searching the residence, investigators found multiple pairs of shoes in the backyard and kitchen and a box in the garage containing 12 cellphones. Investigators also observed that the deadbolt locks on the exterior doors of the residence had been replaced with double-cylinder deadbolt locks requiring a key to unlock the doors from both the interior and exterior of the residence. The kitchen and living room of the residence contained no furniture. Ruiz had his own bedroom and the other 11 illegal aliens slept in one room.

Four of the illegal aliens, Hugo Ipolito Ramirez-Vasquez, Eulogio Perez-Sanchez, Santos Antonio Giron-Castro and Obias Alexander Perez-Perez, were also arrested and separately charged with Re-entry of a Removed Alien. Ramirez-Vasquez, Giron-Castro and Perez-Perez were previously removed from the United States in April 2026, and Perez-Sanchez was previously removed in November 2025.

A conviction for harboring illegal aliens carries a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison, a fine of $250,000 and a maximum term of three years of supervised release.

These cases are part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN).

Homeland Security Investigations is conducting the investigation. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, Phoenix, is handling the prosecution.

A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

CASE NUMBER: 26-MJ-8436, 26-MJ-8429, 26-MJ-8428MJ, 26-MJ-8427, 26-MJ-8433MJ RELEASE NUMBER: 2026-172_Ruiz

Factory Floor Fridays: Chairman Jovanovic Tours Lockheed Martin Aeronautics, Talks with Industry Leaders on Future of U.S. Aviation
FORT WORTH, TX. — Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) Chairman John Jovanovic visited Lockheed Martin Aeronautics’ Fort Worth facility as part of its Factory Floor Fridays initiative. Factory Floor Fridays tell the story of the American Dream through the eyes of the companies and workers building the next generation of American industry, proving with the right tools and support, U.S. innovation can compete and win anywhere in the world.
During the visit, Chairman Jovanovic toured Lockheed Martin Aeronautics’ F-35 assembly facility, met with the plant’s leaders and workers, and discussed the importance of keeping America dominant in the industries of the future. The company employs more than 30,000 highly-skilled professionals around the world and is responsible for the development of high-tech systems that shape the future of U.S. aviation.
“U.S. EXIM is focused on ensuring our advanced manufacturing supply chains are secure, and it all starts with mining,” said Chairman Jovanovic. “Lockheed Martin continues to support America’s mines through strong partnerships. You can’t build the warplane of the future without the critical minerals used to power them. We’re proud to work with them to strengthen supply chains, revitalize manufacturing, and keep future generations of Americans safe.”
“America’s security and economic strength are built on factory floors like this one in Fort Worth,” said Jim Taiclet, Chairman, President and CEO of Lockheed Martin. “We appreciate Chairman Jovanovic’s focus on strengthening U.S. manufacturing, building a resilient industrial base and ensuring America maintains its leadership in aerospace and defense technology.”
“American manufacturers are the backbone of our economic security,” Jovanovic added. “Factory Floor Fridays give everyday Americans the opportunity to hear from businesses large and small—which account for nearly 90 percent of our transactions—and ensure they have the financing tools they need to compete, grow, and win in global markets.”
When EXIM was founded 92 years ago, its mission was simple: support America’s economic recovery from the Great Depression by creating well-paying jobs and rebuilding the nation’s manufacturing base. Under President Trump's leadership, EXIM is once again a frontline economic tool to revitalize America's economy and define a future led by U.S. innovation.
ABOUT EXIM:
As the United States government’s official export credit agency, the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) supports American jobs by facilitating U.S. exports. As an independent agency, EXIM plays a critical role in supporting economic growth, securing critical supply chains, and ensuring American businesses are given a fighting chance. To achieve this mission, EXIM offers financing including export credit insurance, working capital guarantees, loan guarantees, and direct loans. Learn more at www.exim.gov.
title: Factory Floor Fridays: Chairman Jovanovic Tours Lockheed Martin Aeronautics, Talks with Industry Leaders on Future of U.S. Aviation

Chris Kurt, 44, from Lake Park, Iowa, pled guilty October 5, 2026, in federal court in Sioux City, to possessing child pornography.

At the plea hearing, Kurt admitted that from January 1, 2017, through June 23, 2025, he received and possessed over 103 videos and 132 images of child pornography that was backed up to his cloud storage. Law enforcement executed a search warrant at Kurt’s residence and seized several electronic devices. Forensic review of the devices located an additional cache of over 10,000 images and over 1,000 videos of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Some of the depictions involved prepubescent minors, or a minor who had not yet attained the age of 12 years, and involved sadistic or masochistic conduct or other depictions of violence or other depictions of violence or the sexual abuse or exploitation of an infant or toddler. In an interview with law enforcement, Kurt admitted that he would routinely make screen recordings on his phone while visiting websites that contained CSAM. Kurt told agents he did not know how much CSAM would be on his devices because he had downloaded so much over the years.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC.

Sentencing before United States District Court Judge Leonard T. Strand will be set after a presentence report is prepared. Kurt remains in custody of the United States Marshal pending sentencing. Kurt faces a possible maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment, a $250,000 fine, and at least five years of supervised release following any imprisonment.

The case was investigated by the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation, Lake Park, Iowa Police Department, and the Dickinson County Sheriff’s Office and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Kraig R. Hamit.

The case file number is 26-4023. Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.

HHS Announces Up to $27.8 Million for Falls Prevention
WASHINGTON, D.C.— OCTOBER 9, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Administration for Community Living (ACL), today announced the recipients of three falls prevention initiatives totaling up to $27.8 million over three years. The funding will expand proven programs, strengthen connections between health care providers and community organizations, and help states and local partners reach more older adults before a fall leads to injury or loss of independence.
Falls are the leading cause of injury for people 65 and older. One in four older adults falls every year, and a fall is rarely just a fall. It can result in an injury or hospital stay, and non-fatal falls account for an estimated $80 billion in healthcare spending per year. A fall can also shake a person’s confidence and make everyday activities — from walking and shopping to visiting friends — more difficult. Healthcare and aging network providers can help prevent many falls by identifying risks early. They can then connect older adults with programs and support that build strength, improve balance, and make their homes safer.
The three initiatives put prevention first and advance the Trump Administration’s Make America Healthy Again agenda. They will connect screening with community support, expand proven programs statewide, and help organizations deliver and sustain them.
“A fall can change an older American’s life in an instant, and we can prevent many of these injuries,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “HHS is connecting healthcare screening with proven community programs to identify risks earlier, improve strength and balance, and help older adults maintain their independence. These investments will reduce injuries and healthcare costs while helping more Americans remain safely in their homes and communities.”
To reduce that risk, these awards will expand two complementary approaches:
- The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths & Injuries (STEADI) initiative helps health care providers screen for, assess, and address fall risk.
- Stepping On, an evidence-based community falls prevention program, helps older adults improve strength and balance and address risks related to medications, vision, footwear, and home safety. Together, the approaches connect screening with action.
“Knowing someone is at risk is only the first step. What makes the difference is a clear path from screening to support that people can trust and use,” said Mary Lazare, ACL Principal Deputy Administrator. “These awards build that path while giving states and community partners the tools to reach more people and deliver programs that work.”
Three Investments, One Prevention Strategy
Goal: Scaling Through Clinical-Community Partnerships
Program: A Demonstration to Scale Innovative Person-Centered Approaches to Falls Prevention through Clinical-Community Partnerships
Recipient: National Council on Aging, Arlington, VA
Award: $4,781,733
The National Council on Aging will work to scale STEADI and Stepping On through clinical-community partnerships in five geographies. Rapid cycle evaluation will be used to improve the impact of the interventions as they are scaled.
Goal: Expanding Proven Programs Statewide
This funding will help states expand STEADI and Stepping On and address the many factors that increase fall risk. Recipients will strengthen referral networks, prepare more local organizations to deliver the programs, and share lessons with other states and communities.
Goal: Helping Communities Sustain What Works
Program: National Falls Prevention Resource Center
Recipient: National Council on Aging, Arlington, VA
Award: $7,500,000
The National Falls Prevention Resource Center will provide ACL’s aging and disability networks with training, tools, and individualized assistance to deliver and sustain high-quality falls prevention programs. It will also help organizations learn from one another and preserve the elements that make proven programs effective.
Falls Prevention Is a National Priority
Research shows that falls among older adults are preventable through person centered, evidenced based interventions. However, there are gaps in widespread adoption and implementation of these strategies. Through ACL, HHS is coordinating a cross-agency effort, informed by the National Falls Prevention Action Plan. It unites ACL, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Health Resource and Services Administration, CMS’s Center for Clinical Standards and Quality, the National Institute of Aging, and Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. Together, these agencies will move beyond siloed approaches to deliver significant progress in reducing falls over the next three years.
Learn more about ACL’s Falls Prevention Program here.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.
