WASHINGTON, DC — Today, at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, the Trump Administration launched the most ambitious set of science initiatives in decades, representing over $6 billion in investments across the Federal Government, industry, academia, and philanthropy to usher in a New Golden Age of Science.
The Summit builds on Science: A New Golden Age, a report authored by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios to President Trump. The report was written in response to the President’s directive to revitalize the American scientific enterprise. Today, America’s largest Federal research agencies and partners across the science ecosystem launched whole-of-nation efforts to position the United States to lead in a new era of scientific discovery. These initiatives will equip scientists with the tools to harness SI-driven scientific revolution, support the best and brightest American STEM students and early-career scientists, revive the pursuit of ambitious national scientific missions, and encourage the creation of new scientific institutions.
“Today marks the most transformative day for the American scientific enterprise since the reshaping of the Federal research ecosystem following World War II. The efforts announced today will channel billions of dollars across our science ecosystem to realize the new scientific opportunities that now exist.” said Director Kratsios. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are ushering in a New Golden Age of Science powered by super intelligence, a return to merit, and bold national missions that will inspire Americans for generations to come.”
The Trump Administration continues to pursue a whole-of-nation approach to renew American Science for a New Golden Age of Discovery. With today’s announcements, President Trump is forging new partnerships across government, industry, academia, and philanthropy to lay the foundation for the next generation of American scientific leadership.
EQUIPPING AMERICAN SCIENTISTS WITH SUPER INTELLIGENCE: Super intelligence (SI) will be the greatest accelerant of scientific progress in human history and will transform every scientific discipline. President Trump continues to prioritize American scientists by ensuring broad access to the compute and scientific instrumentation needed for SI-enabled scientific research.
- The Trump Administration announced $2.4B in SI for science tools and compute credits for the Genesis Mission Consortium from eleven industry partners, which will support over 15 Federal agencies working towards National Science & Technology Challenges.
  - Industry partner commitments include NVIDIA ($1B), AMD ($500M), OpenAI ($200M), $150M each from Anthropic and Google, $100M each from AMP and Emerald AI, and $50M each from AWS, Armada, Crusoe, and Micron. This follows the expansion of the Genesis Mission in July to over 15 Federal agencies and a $5 billion Federal commitment to support National Science & Technology Challenges across energy, health, space, and more.
- The Trump Administration announced historic investments in scientific computing through state and regional SI infrastructure hubs, making advanced SI resources more widely available to researchers across the country. 
  - More than 14 universities across 10 states launched the Southeast Regional SI Computing Consortium to build and share leadership-class compute infrastructure for scientific research.
  - Universities, industry, and the State of Georgia announced a $1 billion investment in scientific computing and related workforce training efforts for students and faculty.
  - Five universities across North and South Carolina joined together to launch a regional compute hub, unlocking SI-enabled science for researchers across the region.
- The National Science Foundation (NSF) and the Department of Energy (DOE) announced an investment of over $100 million in SI-enabled scientific instrumentation and autonomous laboratories to increase scientific productivity and unlock new modes of research. This follows NSF’s July announcement of a $400 million investment in programmable cloud labs to accelerate and democratize access to science.
REFOCUSING ON THE BEST AND BRIGHTEST: President Trump has replaced DEI with merit across the Federal R&D enterprise, ensuring high-potential American STEM students and early-career scientists receive the resources and support they need early in their careers to pursue ambitious opportunities at the frontiers of science and technology.
- The Trump Administration is announcing new merit-based K-12 STEM opportunities focused on gifted students and meaningful hands-on technical learning. 
  - The Trump Administration revived the NSF Young Scholars Program, funded primarily by philanthropy and inexplicably abandoned in 1996, to invest in students in grades 3-12 on the basis of demonstrated mathematics ability.
  - DOE launched the Battelle-Genesis Mission High School Fellowship to provide advanced high school students with transformative hands-on research experiences at DOE National Laboratories.
- The Trump Administration is strengthening investments in American STEM PhD students, ensuring the STEM PhD remains a desirable pathway for America’s most talented students to continue their technical training.
  - The Trump Administration launched the Genesis Mission Fellowship, a $100 million initiative for students to pursue accelerated four-year PhDs with dual competency in super intelligence and another science or engineering discipline and research experiences embedded in industry and a DOE National Laboratory.
  - NSF launched a 6-year Integrated Bachelors-to-PhD program, enabling promising students to complete doctoral studies on an accelerated timeline, and speeding up their contributions to the American scientific enterprise. This builds off of NSF’s July announcement of an innovative accelerated 4-year PhD program co-funded by industry.
- The Trump Administration launched Generation Discovery, which will bring a hundred exceptional early-career scientists into the NIH’s Intramural Research Program, enabling early-career researchers to do bold, ambitious work at the most pivotal stages in their career. This continues NIH’s FY2026 support for the largest ever cohort of early-stage investigators in history.
BRINGING BACK NATIONAL MISSIONS: From the Manhattan Project to the Apollo Program, some of America’s greatest scientific achievements have come from focused national missions that united the Nation’s brightest minds behind an ambitious common goal. President Trump has brought back National Missions in super intelligence, quantum, fusion, and space exploration that will excite Americans for generations to come.
- NASA and DOE solidified a historic partnership to develop nuclear power and space nuclear fuels. NASA and DOE will collaborate to design, build, and deploy multiple space systems, including NASA’s Space Reactor-1, a nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars expected to launch in 2028, as well as Lunar Reactor-1, the first fission reactor on the lunar surface. This MOU will support implementation of President Trump’s December 2025 Executive Order on “Ensuring American Space Superiority” and NSTM-3 launching a National Initiative for American Space Nuclear Power.
- DOE announced the Quantum Computing Priority Applications, a set of eight key problems that will guide the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, a $215 million initiative to fund teams to demonstrate the world’s first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computers. These challenges will help achieve the goals set out in President Trump’s June 2026 Executive Order “Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation.”
- NSF launched two $33 million Grand Research Challenge (GRC) prize competitions in Quantum+X applications and synthetic multicellularity. These challenges will facilitate multidisciplinary collaboration, attract non-traditional entrants, and form cross-sector teams to spur rapid advances in use-inspired basic discovery.
- This week, the NIH, DOE, and Biohub launched a $1.8B virtual biology initiative to create the data and modeling foundation for virtual cells, which will develop SI models that can better predict how cells and biological systems respond to disease and develop potential interventions. This initiative will support Bio Genesis, a national mission to double the pace of biomedical innovation within the next five to ten years.
BUILDING INSTITUTIONS THAT ACCELERATE DISCOVERY: President Trump is creating new institutions of discovery to enable American Scientists to pursue major scientific and technical objectives that fall outside of disciplines and conventional funding mechanisms.
- The Trump Administration is supporting X-Labs across agencies, a new generation of independent research organizations that give multidisciplinary teams of scientists and engineers the autonomy and resources to tackle specific technical challenges.
  - The Trump Administration launched the X-Labs Consortium with over $310 million in industry and philanthropic commitments to support Federally-funded X-Labs teams with advanced scientific instrumentation and facility space. This builds on the $1.5 billion NSF X-Labs initiative announced in May, which has supported X-Labs across scientific instrumentation, quantum systems, physical SI, predictive biology, and next-generation computation.
- The Trump Administration recognizes that metascience, or applying the scientific method to evaluate how we fund and conduct science, is necessary to evaluate the impact of new experiments and maximize return on Federal investments in research.
  - NSF, DOE, NASA, and DOW launched new metascience initiatives to inform how they fund and conduct science. Agencies will run experiments and analyze data to better identify exceptional ideas, empower talented researchers, reduce unnecessary friction, and accelerate the pace of discovery.
  - The NSF and the United Kingdom Research and Innovation Metascience Unit announced metascience cooperation to measure research impact, improve research review, and test new tools for science, laying the foundation for an International Network of Metascience Units. This announcement builds on the U.S.-led Kyoto Vision for a New Golden Age of Science.
title: Fact Sheet: Trump Administration Announces the Most Ambitious Set of Science Initiatives This Century

text:
LAS VEGAS — Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Core 8 launched Operation Loaded Dice in July 2026. This was a strategic investigative initiative focused on disrupting and dismantling transnational criminal organizations, gangs and other criminal networks involved in illicit firearms and narcotics trafficking, as well as bulk cash smuggling, and associated violent crime in the greater Las Vegas metropolitan area.

Over the course of the approximately three-month initiative, HSTF law enforcement authorities arrested 144 suspects, seized 290 firearms, including machine guns, and seized 1,124 kilograms of narcotics and more than $1 million in cash and other assets. These enforcement actions also led to the initiation of 13 HSTF investigations in coordination with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada.

Through intelligence-driven investigations, coordinated enforcement actions, surveillance, controlled purchases and sustained investigative partnerships, the HSTF disrupted multiple criminal organizations operating within the Las Vegas metropolitan area.

The investigations included networks associated with the Sinaloa Cartel and the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, or CJNG, as well as other regional drug trafficking organizations, gangs, and trafficking networks.

“This coordinated operation is a powerful testament to the relentless dedication of our multiagency task force,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “By removing 144 suspects from our streets, we have dealt a decisive blow to the criminal networks attempting to exploit our community and compromise public safety. Our message is clear: If you threaten the security of Nevadans and our guests, Homeland Security and our law enforcement partners will find you, dismantle your operations and bring you to justice.”

“Strong policing requires true partnership, respect, and community trust,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “By unifying local, state and federal agencies, the HSTF initiative equips law enforcement to tackle crime collectively and save lives.”

“We stand proud of the results achieved by Operation Loaded Dice. This is a vast operation, which has netted more than $1 million in assets, hauled away 290 firearms, and seized 1,100 kilograms of narcotics. Just as significant, we are taking 144 criminals off our streets,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Brandon Lesky of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)'s Las Vegas District Office. “Through our whole-of-government approach, we leveraged each agency’s capabilities and relied heavily on sharp collaboration and open communication. The HSTF initiative empowers partners to continue tackling drug trafficking networks. The ultimate goal is to save lives.”

“Through ATF’s participation in Homeland Security Task Forces, or HSTF, we help to disrupt major criminal organizations and criminal activity while working alongside our local, state and federal partners,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Elliott Prose of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)’s San Francisco Field Division. “By combining our resources through joint task forces and shared intelligence, we effectively and efficiently tackle the violent crime that threatens our communities head on. The investigations conducted thus far in the Las Vegas area serve as examples of the steps HSTF has taken and will continue to take when individuals choose to engage in conduct that endangers the wellbeing of our cities. ATF is proud to be a part of HSTF. We will continue to stay focused on our mission and continue to work in lock step with our partners.”

“We, the U.S. Marshals, are proud to stand with our federal, state and local law enforcement partners in the Homeland Security Task Force against the criminals who prey on our community,” said U.S. Marshal Gary Schofield for the District of Nevada. “We remain relentless in our pursuit of justice. We know we keep Nevada safe.”

“Operation Loaded Dice demonstrates the impact of a unified law enforcement response to the criminal organizations that endanger our communities,” said Special Agent in Charge Erin Burke of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Los Angeles. “By combining our collective authorities, resources, and expertise, the HSTF is identifying and disrupting the networks responsible for trafficking dangerous narcotics, illegal firearms and illicit proceeds. These results represent meaningful progress in protecting the people of southern Nevada and holding accountable those who threaten public safety.”

“Sheriff Kevin McMahill and the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department are thankful for the partnerships we share with the Homeland Security Task Force. This strategic initiative highlights the importance of collaboration in keeping our community safe. Every suspect arrested, firearm recovered or case solved makes a significant impact on the well-being of those who live in Las Vegas.”

“Criminal organizations operate beyond jurisdictional boundaries, making collaboration among law enforcement agencies essential,” said North Las Vegas Police Department Assistant Chief Adam Hyde. “The North Las Vegas Police Department remains committed to working with our federal, state, and local partners to disrupt these organizations and keep our communities safe."

“The Henderson Police Department relies on strong strategic partnerships with local, state and federal law enforcement,” said Henderson Police Chief Reggie Rader. “By sharing resources and intelligence, we're able to target the criminal organizations and keep our communities safe.”

The HSTF was established pursuant President Trump’s Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership focused on eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking networks operating in the United States and abroad. President Trump vowed to make America safe again and by empowering law enforcement agencies and establishing task forces such as HSTF, he is making our nation safer and stronger.

Through interagency collaboration, the HSTF coordinates the capabilities of U.S. law enforcement agencies to identify, investigate, and prosecute the full range of crimes committed by these organizations, which contribute to violence and instability in communities across the country. The HSTF places particular emphasis on organizations whose criminal activity poses a threat to the safety and security of the United States.

The HSTF also uses all available lawful authorities to investigate and prosecute violent criminal offenders and, where appropriate and consistent with applicable law, support their removal from the United States. HSTF Core 8 consists of special agents, officers, analysts, prosecutors, and support personnel from participating federal, state, local, and regional agencies. Federal prosecutions are coordinated with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada.

Homeland Security Task Force Core 8 includes the following federal partners: ATF; DEA; the Diplomatic Security Service; the Federal Air Marshal Service; the FBI; HSI; IRS; the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada; and the U.S. Marshals Service.

State, local and regional partners include the Clark County District Attorney’s Office; the Henderson Police Department; the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department; the Mesquite Police Department; the Nevada Gaming Control Board; the Nevada Highway Patrol; the North Las Vegas Police Department; the Nye County Sheriff’s Office; the Reno Police Department; the Sparks Police Department; the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office; and the White Pine County Sheriff’s Office.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Today at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, President Donald J. Trump presented National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology and Innovation, our nation’s highest honors for exemplary achievement and leadership in science and technology, to six of America’s greatest living innovators.
Since 1963, the President of the United States has bestowed the National Medal of Science on those deserving of special recognition for their outstanding contributions to science in service of the United States. Since it was first awarded in 1985, the National Medal of Technology and Innovation has recognized American innovators whose vision, intellect, creativity, and determination have strengthened America’s economy and improved our quality of life.
President Trump is committed to restoring U.S. global scientific and technological leadership for a New Golden Age, from harnessing super intelligence for scientific discovery to ushering in a nuclear renaissance; from ensuring American space superiority to strengthening America’s quantum advantage.
These medalists have pioneered breakthroughs in science and engineering for the new age of super intelligence, from fundamental advances in general-purpose parallel computing and semiconductor design to engineering and business leadership in building the foundations of hyperscale infrastructure in the U.S., around the world, and even into space. Their work has advanced American global technology leadership for the 21st Century and laid the foundation for a new Golden Age of Science.
The recipients are listed below.
Recipients of the National Medal of Science
- Elon Musk – “For engineering achievements of extraordinary ambition and scale that have pushed the frontiers of space exploration, intelligent systems, communications, and beyond, renewing American technological leadership and opening a new chapter in American manufacturing.”
- Sergey Brin – “For the development of foundational algorithms for information retrieval and data processing that revolutionized how the world accesses information across science, commerce, and in the course of everyday life.”
- Jensen Huang – “For advancing the graphics processing unit into a general-purpose computing architecture through innovations in processor design and software, transforming massively parallel computation and powering breakthroughs in scientific computing and super intelligence.”
- Lisa Su – “For a lifetime of leadership in semiconductor engineering and high-performance computing through innovations in processor architecture and chiplet-based integration that powered the world’s first exascale supercomputer and opened new frontiers in computational performance.”
Recipients of the National Medal of Technology and Innovation
- Michael Dell – “For advancing a vision of widespread adoption of personal and enterprise computing; for his technical and business management skills building a worldwide technology company; and for his support for the next generation of American scientists, engineers, and technologists.”
- Satya Nadella – “For his transformative leadership of a critical American technology company, which led to its rejuvenation for a new era of cloud computing, and for his construction of the hyperscale infrastructure that enabled the training and global deployment of American super intelligence.”
“Each of these medalists has transformed their field or industry, laying the foundations for technologies we already can barely imagine living without,” said Michael Kratsios, Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. “While we in government work to deliver the efforts a New Golden Age of Science will require, we know that scientific progress and technological innovation depend on the insight and character of individuals. Innovators like these six awardees are the architects of the future.”
About the Science: A New Golden Age Summit:
Science: A New Golden Age, released in July 2026 by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, is the first comprehensive rethinking of the U.S. science and technology enterprise since Vannevar Bush’s 1945 Science: The Endless Frontier.
The report observes significant changes to how scientific discovery happens today, particularly the increased role of industry in driving R&D and the close integration of applied and foundational research. It provides concrete recommendations for how government, industry, academia, and philanthropy can seize the opportunities presented by these changes to accelerate scientific discovery and empower the Nation’s best and brightest scientists. Core recommendations include strengthening support for early-career scientists, reviving the national pursuit of ambitious scientific missions, launching new funding and organizational models for transformative research, building the metascience infrastructure to continuously improve the research enterprise, and scaling SI-driven scientific discovery through the Genesis Mission.
The Science: A New Golden Age Summit convenes leading scientists and innovators to examine these changes and translate the report’s ideas into the next chapter of American scientific progress. Throughout the day, the Trump Administration will provide major announcements, in coordination with private sector partners and research institutions, to realize the vision of Science: A New Golden Age and the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science.
title: President Trump Presents National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology and Innovation

Reps. Tlaib and Green lead letter demanding release of DACA recipient in ICE custody
WASHINGTON – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Al Green (TX-09), joined by 21 Members of Congress, demanded the release of Ya’akub Ira Vijandre, who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a year ago as of yesterday. In a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Acting Director David Venturella, the Members pressed for answers regarding Ya’akub’s unconstitutional arrest and prolonged detention after a federal judge allowed his habeas challenge to proceed.
Ya’akub, a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipient, has lived in the U.S. since he was 14 years old. He spent a decade working for American Airlines as a senior safety specialist and was recognized for supporting grieving families after a helicopter crashed into a plane in Washington, D.C. Despite having no criminal record and not being charged with any crime, he was targeted and arrested at gun point for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza and for “liking” a social media post with Quranic verses–both of which are protected by the First Amendment.
“The administration’s stated basis for [Ya’akub’s] detention has been inconsistent and appears to rely substantially on his speech and social media activity,” the Members wrote. “DHS has sought to justify his detention by citing his social media commentary regarding the prosecutions of the Holy Land Foundation Five, his criticism of the treatment of Guantanamo detainees, his advocacy for Palestine, and his engagement with religious Islamic content, including ‘liking’ Instagram posts containing Quranic verses. We are deeply concerned that constitutionally protected political and religious expression is being used as a basis for his continued detention or deportation.”
The letter renews concerns and questions from a letter Rep. Green sent in June. Rep. Tlaib also spoke on the House floor urging for Ya’akub’s release in August.
“We are also concerned by reports, previously flagged in Congressman Green’s June letter, that the FBI approached Mr. Vijandre in November 2023 seeking his cooperation as a confidential informant and that he declined,” the Members continued in their letter. “His DACA status, renewed as recently as May 2024 through May 2026, was subsequently revoked. The proximity and sequence of these events—an FBI approach he declined, followed by a DACA termination and detention grounded largely in the government’s characterization of his religious and political speech—continue to raise serious questions about possible retaliation that Congress has not yet received satisfactory answers to.”
The letter, led by Reps. Tlaib and Green, was signed by 21 other Members of Congress: Greg Casar (TX–35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).
The letter was also endorsed by 38 organizations: American Friends Service Committee, Americans for Justice in Palestine Action, Arab American Caucus of the California Democratic Party, Arlington for Palestine, Asian Americans Advancing Justice – Atlanta, CAIR Action, Center for Constitutional Rights, Codepink, Community Alliance for Peace and Justice, Demand Progress, Havertown-Community Action Network, IMEU Policy Project, Indiana Center for Middle East Peace, Institute for Policy Studies New Internationalism Project, Maine Coalition for Palestine, Majdal: Arab Community Center of San Diego, MARUF CT, Massachusetts Peace Action, Methodist Federation for Social Action, Muslim Advocates, National Political Prisoner Coalition, NE Oakland Indivisible, NH Peace Action, Palestine Legal, Peace Action Montgomery, Peace Justice Sustainability NOW!, Philly Neighborhood Networks, Pittsburgh Palestine Solidarity Committee, Project TAHA, Restore The Fourth – Action, ReThinking Foreign Policy, River Valley for Palestine, The Justice Coalition, United Methodists for Kairos Response, US Campaign for Palestinian Rights Action, Virginia for Palestine, Whistleblower & Source Protection Program at ExposeFacts, Worcester Multifaith for Palestine.

Today, National Labor Relations Board General Counsel Crystal S. Carey has appointed Danielle Lucido as the Regional Attorney for the National Labor Relations Board, Region 32, with its office located in Oakland, California. In her position, Ms. Lucido will serve as the chief legal officer of the regional office and assist Regional Director Christy J. Kwon in the administration and enforcement of the National Labor Relations Act in part of northern California, central California, and Northern Nevada. Ms. Lucido earned her Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) and a Juris Doctor degree from UCLA School of Law. Prior to joining the NLRB, Ms. Lucido served as Chief Counsel for Cal-OSHA managing a statewide legal department and criminal bureau that included 60 attorneys, investigators and support staff and as Chief Counsel for the Engineers and Scientists of California, Local 20, IFPTE.

Established in 1935, the National Labor Relations Board is an independent federal agency that protects employees from unfair labor practices and protects the right of private sector employees to join together, with or without a union, to improve wages, benefits and working conditions. The NLRB conducts hundreds of workplace elections and investigates thousands of unfair labor practice charges each year.

Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H.Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day."
"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Congressman Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."
"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Congressman Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."
"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," Congressman Tonko said. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."
"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Congressman Valadao.
"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.
"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of FCHEA. "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large."
BACKGROUND
National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.
The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power.
U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Representatives Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors.
Senator Richard Blumenthal (CT) led the introduction of the Senate Resolution, with Senators Bill Cassidy (LA), Chris Coons (DE), and Chris Murphy (CT) joining as original cosponsors.
title: Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day

NSF lays the foundation for the next generation of technologies and support for American talent
The U.S. National Science Foundation today announced a series of programs and initiatives to support the ambitious vision articulated in the White House report Science: A New Golden Age and in "NSF leadership in a new golden age of science." These new programs and initiatives combined with the $1.5 billion in investments announced in August will help the agency improve how it evaluates and supports science, harness super intelligence to accelerate discovery, and invest in exceptional students and early-career researchers.
NSF is establishing an Office of Metascience to serve as a testbed for studying how scientific communities respond to novel review and funding mechanisms, applying those lessons learned to NSF programs to accelerate discovery. The office will operate with full transparency, sharing its experiments and findings with academia, industry, and philanthropy. A job announcement for the head of the Office of Metascience will be forthcoming.
In addition, both UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and NSF intend to build on the metascience principles that the United States has outlined in the "Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science," and that both agencies have articulated in, respectively, the "NSF leadership in a new golden age of science" memorandum and the UKRI Strategy 2026-31.
NSF is launching two Grand Research Challenge (GRC) prize competitions to facilitate cross-disciplinary collaboration, attract nontraditional entrants, and form cross-sector teams to spur rapid advances in scientific understanding in crucial areas of science and technology (S&T).
The first is the Quantum+X GRC that will accelerate quantum innovation for sectors like energy, biotechnology, and finance. U.S. participants will be invited to compete and showcase algorithm and application solutions that could redefine what quantum technology makes possible. Through an NSF partnership with industry, competing teams will be able to develop solutions to sector-relevant problems that will not only impact the economy but also advance solutions to fundamental questions in fields such as chemistry, mathematics, and materials science.
The second is the Synthetic Multicellularity Grand Challenge prize, a competition that will transform the ability to design biology. U.S. participants will be invited to compete in a multistage challenge to showcase new computational and experimental approaches in synthetic and engineering biology that expand capabilities to incorporate complexity and regulation into the design of multicellular systems. The results of this competition will advance our understanding of cell biology, development, and aging, and lead to new applications across sectors from medicine to biomanufacturing.
NSF is also launching the new NSF X-Labs Consortium with an initial set of founding partners representing over $300 million in commitments, supporting teams with floor space, instrument access, and direct support. This consortium is designed to provide resources to NSF X-Labs, a new generation of organizations enabling independent teams of researchers, technologists, and entrepreneurs pursuing milestone-based federal funding to solve specific scientific and technological challenges. The founding partners include research institutions, advanced computing centers, philanthropy, and industry, which will provide critical resources such as access to physical space, scientific instruments and infrastructure, and expertise, to catalyze and expedite the impact of the NSF X-Labs initiative.
In addition, in collaboration with several industry and philanthropic partners, NSF will soon release a funding opportunity tied to the NSF Programmable Cloud Laboratories Network (NSF PCLNet) announced in July 2026, with a specific focus on the development of Super Intelligence-Native Instruments (SINI). The eventual SINI awardees will enhance NSF PCLNet by incorporating instruments specifically designed for the modern era of data and super intelligence in their designs and architecture, meaning that the instruments are digital-first. This re-envisioning signals a significant advance in the automation of science and engineering solutions and the era of super intelligence-driven scientific discovery and innovation. NSF anticipates an investment of up to $75 million over the next five years.
"NSF leadership in a new golden age of science" makes clear the imperative for a merit-first approach to identify and develop the exceptionally talented Americans who will serve as the vanguard of U.S. S&T global leadership in the coming decades. To support those goals, NSF is investing in the National Math Stars and NextGen Workforce to open more scientific and technical career pathways for more talented Americans.
NSF's investment of $30 million over four years in National Math Stars, fully matched by private philanthropy, will help grow talent identification and advanced STEM enrichment programs and support the design and testing of a scalable digital platform to assist families in supporting children grades 3–12 to achieve their full potential in math.
The NextGen Workforce program will help students earning STEM doctoral degrees reach the frontier faster than ever before and make STEM Ph.D.s a desirable pathway for America's most talented students. The program will develop new accelerated ;6-year bachelor's to doctoral degree programs and innovative, interdisciplinary graduate training programs that provide direct support for enrolled students and meet critical and emerging national STEM workforce needs.
More details about all these programs and initiatives will be available in the coming days.
title: NSF lays the foundation for the next generation of technologies and support for American talent

Ukrainian-Russian Dual Citizen Pleads Guilty to Running International Money Laundering Organization for Cybercriminals
Oleg Korniev, 42, a dual citizen of Ukraine and Russia, pleaded guilty today to running a sophisticated international money laundering organization that laundered millions of dollars stolen from United States victims by cybercriminals around the world. In total, this international criminal organization recruited over 15,000 U.S.-based money mules to launder at least $10 million stolen by hackers from over 750 U.S. bank accounts.
“Money mules play crucial roles in cybercrime, so the Justice Department pursues mules and their recruiters wherever they operate and however long it takes,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Alongside our international partners, we will dismantle criminal networks that attack Americans. No amount of distance or time puts these criminals beyond the reach of justice.”
“Just because you are outside the borders of the United States does not mean you will get away with defrauding U.S. Citizens and businesses,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson for the Western District of North Carolina. “We will work hard to bring you to justice, as we did in this case.”
“For years, the FBI has worked tirelessly to unravel the layers of this international money laundering operation and bring Mr. Korniev to justice,” said Special Agent in Charge Reid Davis of FBI North Carolina. “This case reflects the Bureau’s enduring commitment to following the evidence — no matter how long it takes, how far it leads, or how deliberately criminals try to hide behind borders and technology. We will continue pursuing those who enable cybercriminals until every responsible individual is held to account.”
According to court documents, Korniev was one of the leaders of Your Mule Cashout (YMCO). YMCO created, maintained, and operated an elaborate and sophisticated system of money mules and internet infrastructure that allowed computer hackers, who had stolen money from the bank accounts of U.S. companies, to conceal the thefts and transfer the stolen money to countries outside the U.S. YMCO’s services operated through online infrastructure that allowed hackers to move the stolen money to countries primarily in Eastern Europe by paying YMCO a percentage of the money stolen.
YMCO provided its money laundering services through money mules who were U.S. residents deceived by YMCO into believing that they were working for legitimate companies and making genuine money transfers. YMCO falsely represented that the money mules’ job was to receive payments from businesses into their personal bank accounts, withdraw the money, and then wire the funds to the fake company’s partners overseas. The money mules instead processed the hackers’ stolen proceeds and wired them out of the country to other YMCO conspirators. The money mules never received payment for their services.
Korniev helped develop YMCO’s policies and procedures; managed, hired, and fired employees; rewarded and punished employees based on performance; and secured illegal services supporting YMCO. As part of his plea, Korniev admitted that YMCO was responsible for over $14.7 million in actual and intended losses by confirmed victims and that he intended to launder over $9.7 million from cybercriminals and did launder at least $7 million. Korniev also agreed to provide full restitution to known victims to compensate them for their actual losses as well as forfeit cash seized from him when he was arrested in the Republic of Georgia.
Korniev pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering, money laundering, conspiracy to commit computer fraud, conspiracy to commit access device theft, and aggravated identity theft. Sentencing will be set at a later date. He faces a minimum penalty of two years in prison and maximum penalty of 50 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine Korniev’s sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors.
Previously, four other individuals involved with YMCO were arrested overseas, extradited to the Western District of North Carolina, and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. They received sentences ranging from around 37 months to 63 months in prison and the court ordered each defendant to pay over $9.1 million in restitution to numerous U.S. victims.
The FBI is investigating the case.
Senior Counsel Matthew A. Lamberti of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Warren for the Western District of North Carolina are prosecuting the case. The Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs, the FBI Office of the Law Enforcement Attache in Tbilisi, and law enforcement authorities in Georgia, including the Prosecutor’s Office of Georgia, provided significant assistance.
CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds.
title: Ukrainian-Russian Dual Citizen Pleads Guilty to Running International Money Laundering Organization for Cybercriminals

Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on USS Lincoln’s Return
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Ranking Member of the Military and Foreign Affairs Oversight Subcommittee, issued the following statement on USS Abraham Lincoln’s return home after the end of a record long deployment.
“I am thankful for the return of the servicemembers aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. They and their families have paid an unnecessary cost for Trump’s endless war of choice with Iran. They deserve all of our respect and support. During the USS Lincoln’s deployment, servicemembers endured a record number of days without a port call. They faced insufficient amounts of food, unfit living conditions, and inadequate mental health support. I will continue to advocate for the respect and safety of our troops. We have a duty to make sure this never happens again by holding the Pentagon accountable, ” said Ranking Member Subramanyam.
In August of this year, Oversight Ranking Member Robert Garcia and Congressman Suhas Subramanyam demanded answers from the Department of Defense (DOD) about conditions on the USS Lincoln. In the letter to DOD Secretary Hegseth, the Ranking Members asked for information on the inventory of food, medical supplies, and other critical resources for the sailors and Marines. They also asked for clarification on the timeline of when the USS Lincoln would be relieved by another aircraft carrier.
The letter can be found HERE and below. 
###
Dear Secretary Hegseth:
We write regarding the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, specifically, the living conditions and access to mental health resources for the sailors. Recent reports have revealed disturbing sanitation conditions, food shortages, and deteriorating mental health among those deployed on the aircraft carrier, including multiple suicide attempts, with one sailor jumping overboard. Our sailors deserve better while they serve our country, and these deplorable conditions negatively impact morale and readiness. As Members of Congress, we have a duty to support our troops, and it is clear that additional oversight is needed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.
The USS Abraham Lincoln holds more than 5,000 sailors and Marines and departed San Diego last November. Now redirected to the Middle East to support the Iran War in Operation Epic Fury, the carrier has been deployed for over 250 days and has spent a record-setting 200 consecutive days at sea. At a town hall with Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, families of those aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln voiced their concerns directly. Among them were food shortages, water contamination, and disruptions in mail.
As the Ranking Members of the Oversight Committee and the Oversight Committee’s Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, we request a classified briefing on the USS Abraham Lincoln’s conditions and answers to the following questions by August 28, 2026:
- What is the current inventory of food aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln?
- Please detail the food supply and delivery schedule over the course of the carrier’s deployment.
- What sanitation issues have been identified aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, including broken bathroom facilities?
- What health care, including mental health care, are available to the sailors aboard?
- What behavioral health care professionals are on board and accessible to those seeking help?
- How quickly can someone on board the ship meet with a behavioral health care professional after seeking help?
- What steps can be taken to mitigate the disruptions to the mail system that sailors have experienced?
- Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao reportedly told family members that the USS Theodore Roosevelt is preparing to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Without jeopardizing national security, what details can be shared about the timeline for the ship’s relief?
The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the principal oversight committee of the House of Representatives and has broad authority to investigate “any matter” at “any time” under House Rule X. If you have any questions about this request, please contact Committee Democratic staff at (202) 225-5051. Thank you for your prompt attention to this request.
title: Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on USS Lincoln’s Return

The Federal Trade Commission is sending more than $15.8 million to consumers impacted by cash advance app company Cleo AI’s deceptive claims about the amounts and timing of available cash advances and the company’s hard-to-cancel subscriptions.
The FTC’s March 2025 complaint alleged that Cleo AI misled consumers with promises of fast money, advertising access to “hundreds of dollars” in cash advances when almost no one received even close to the advertised amounts. The agency also alleged that Cleo charged additional hidden fees for same-day or instant cash advances that often would not arrive until the next day and that the defendant made it difficult for users to cancel their subscriptions.
The FTC plans to send payments to 2,124,796 Cleo AI customers who paid for eligible instant cash advances. Consumers who are eligible for a payment will get an email between now and October 26, 2026. The FTC will begin sending PayPal payments on October 27, 2026. Recipients should redeem their PayPal payment within 30 days.
Consumers who have questions about their payment should contact the refund administrator, Rust Consulting Inc., at 877 788 4958, or visit the FTC website to view frequently asked questions about the refund process. The Commission never requires people to pay money or provide account information to receive a payment.
The Commission’s interactive dashboards for redress data provide a state-by-state breakdown of redress in FTC cases. In 2025, FTC actions led to more than $435 million in redress to consumers across the country.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Pallone Introduces Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act
New Legislation Amends the No Surprises Act to Help Lower Health Insurance Premiums, Rein in Bad Actors, and Ensure Health Care Providers Are Paid Within 30 Days
Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) announced he’s introducing the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act that would fix the No Surprises Act's broken arbitration process, which bad actors have exploited to drive up health insurance premiums for everyday Americans.
“The No Surprises Act has been an overwhelming success when it comes to protecting patients from surprise medical bills. Prior to the law, millions of Americans were on the hook for surprise bills and caught in the middle of payment disputes,” Ranking Member Pallone said. “Today, I’m pleased to say patients no longer receive these outrageous bills, but unfortunately the arbitration process is clearly not working. A few bad actors—largely backed by private equity—are gaming the system, creating backlogs, delaying payments, and driving up premiums. The Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act will replace the broken arbitration system with a fair and timely payment process that lowers people’s health insurance premiums.”
Pallone was one of the authors of the bipartisan No Surprises Act in 2020, which took patients out of the middle of surprise billing payment disputes and established an arbitration process between health care providers and payers. The law established guidelines for determining a fair payment amount, but a series of court decisions in lawsuits have weakened those guidelines, resulting in increasingly large awards that overwhelmingly delay payments and drive up insurance premiums for millions of patients.
Today, a small number of organizations mostly backed by private equity account for the overwhelming majority of disputes filed through the arbitration process. Of the 2.5 million disputes submitted in 2025, approximately 67 percent were submitted by ten provider groups. Taken together, the 15 arbitration firms authorized to handle surprise billing disputes were paid $1.3 billion in fees in 2025 alone, compared to the $885 million these firms received from 2022 to 2024.
Collectively, the 15 arbitration firms awarded nearly $15 billion in payments to providers in 2025, which will result in higher premiums for consumers and employers. According to an analysis in Health Affairs, the arbitration process contributed to an estimated $22.4 billion in total costs over just four years. For instance, the New York State Employee Plan cited the arbitration award amounts as the primary contributor to the 10 percent premium increase this year.
The Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act will amend the No Surprises Act by replacing the broken arbitration system with a fairer payment system based on the median in-network rate and require that payments be issued within 30 days of the claim being filed.
“To help make health care more affordable, Congress needs to close the loopholes in existing law that private equity-backed and corporate firms are exploiting to secure inflated payments — loopholes that ultimately push premiums ever upward,” said Anthony Wright, Executive Director of Families USA. “While the bipartisan No Surprises Act continues to successfully protect patients from unexpected out-of-network medical bills, we need Congressional action to prevent premium increases due to corporate middlemen abusing its arbitration process. Representative Pallone's bill would take commonsense steps to replace the arbitration system with a market-based benchmark that ensures providers receive fair but not inflationary payments that raise costs for everyone. All who worry about health costs need Congress to act urgently to stand up to industry groups that have been profiteering off of the No Surprises Act arbitration process at the expense of consumers."
Legislative text of the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act is available HERE.
###
title: Pallone Introduces Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act

The Federal Trade Commission secured changes to a partnership agreement between T-shirt manufacturer Gildan Activewear SRL and major wholesale T-shirt distributor S&S Holdings LLC that will protect small businesses and consumers from unfair and discriminatory pricing practices. This resolution also furthers the FTC’s efforts to enforce the Robinson-Patman Act (RPA) in cases where price discrimination harms consumers.
The FTC opened an investigation into Gildan and S&S after becoming aware that S&S’s contract with Gildan prohibited Gildan from offering certain pricing and discounts given to S&S to S&S’s competitors.
The FTC investigated Gildan for potential violations of Section 2(a) of the RPA, which prohibits sellers from engaging in certain price discrimination. The FTC also investigated whether S&S violated Section 2(f) of the RPA, which prohibits knowingly inducing or receiving prohibited price discrimination.
In response to the FTC’s investigation, Gildan and S&S modified their agreement, which now provides: “Nothing in this Agreement restricts or restrains Gildan’s discretion to set prices or offer partnership support to any other North American wholesale distributor.”
Given the changes Gildan and S&S have implemented, the FTC has now closed its investigation. The FTC posted a public letter from Gildan confirming that Gildan and S&S have amended the relevant contract.
“Congress has prohibited unfair and discriminatory pricing practices that favor big businesses and box out small businesses, which are the engine of the American economy,” said FTC Bureau of Competition Director Daniel Guarnera. “We will not hesitate to enforce the law when a large, powerful firm insulates itself from competition by forcing sellers to give worse prices to the firm’s competitors. Such pricing policies are bad for consumers and distort competition by making it harder for small firms to compete on the merits of their products and services. We will not tolerate conduct that unfairly alters competition.”
This matter builds on the RPA settlement entered last week with Southern Glazer’s Wine and Spirits, the largest U.S. distributor of wine and spirits. The Southern Glazer’s settlement was the first RPA case resolved by a federal enforcement agency in over 20 years.
Under the RPA, it is generally illegal for sellers to engage in price discrimination that harms competition by charging higher prices to disfavored retailers that purchase similar goods. RPA enforcement seeks to ensure that businesses of all sizes compete on a level playing field with equivalent access to discounts and rebates. Robust competition between businesses of all sizes is beneficial to consumers as it offers shoppers more choice and the ability to access lower prices across all retailers, regardless of their size.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and to protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. You can learn more about how competition benefits consumers, file an antitrust complaint, or comment on a proposed merger. For the latest news and resources, follow the FTC on social media, subscribe to press releases and read our blog.
title: FTC Secures Fair Pricing Protections by Taking Action Against Major Wholesale T-Shirt Distributors

NASA is launching two new science and technology initiatives to deepen scientific understanding and accelerate the innovation that will shape America’s future in space.
The initiatives are announced in conjunction with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s (OSTP) “Science: A Golden Age Summit” in Washington on Thursday with top U.S. agency leaders. The programs reflect NASA’s commitment to pioneering research and transformative technologies and advancing the Trump Administration’s vision as outlined in the July report to the President, Science: A New Golden Age. One focuses on peer review and the other on fellowship researchers.
“NASA has a proud history of pursuing bold ideas and achieving the near impossible,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are building on that legacy by creating new opportunities for great science, experimenting with how we evaluate and accelerate the best ideas, and investing in the next generation of researchers through the Genesis Mission Fellowships. We are entering a new Golden Age of American innovation and discovery, and NASA will be at the forefront.”
During a fireside chat, Isaacman and Michael Kratsios, assistant to the President for science and technology and director of OSTP, will discuss the following:
- Establishing a coordinated metascience initiative within NASA’s Science Mission Directorate to strengthen the reliability, efficiency, transparency, and overall productivity of the agency’s scientific practices. As part of this effort, NASA is expanding the agency’s use of dual anonymous peer review to ensure proposals are evaluated solely on their intrinsic scientific merit. This approach enhances fairness and supports innovative and unconventional research ideas. Started as a pilot program during the first Trump Administration, this initiative has helped position NASA as a leader in advancing best practices in scientific review.
- NASA will support 10 Genesis Mission Fellows, who are accelerated doctoral students with dual competencies in super intelligence (SI) and science or engineering. Fellows will work directly on NASA mission areas and conduct research at NASA laboratories, advancing SI-enabled scientific discovery. The fellowships will be based on NASA’s successful Future Investigators in NASA Earth and Space Science and Technology program.
NASA leads the nation in space exploration, scientific discovery, and technological innovation. Through these new initiatives, NASA will continue to inspire the world and drive progress in science and technology.

Gov Watchdog Finds Geothermal Developers Lack Permitting Tools Oil and Gas Companies Already Have
Washington, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a new report showing that companies trying to build geothermal power on public lands lack basic permitting tools that oil and gas companies already have and face confusing rules with no way to see where their permits stand, even as demand for geothermal development has grown more than fortyfold since 2020.
The watchdog report, requested by U.S. House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Susie Lee (D-Nev.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) found that the permitting process can be inconsistent and lacks transparency, creating uncertainty for geothermal developers and federal land managers. Oil and gas companies file permits online, track them through a dedicated system, and work from public handbooks, while geothermal developers submit permit applications in writing, wait on unpublished handbooks, and have no system tracking their permits.
The report comes as Congress has shown bipartisan interest in expanding geothermal energy development and private-sector interest in federal lands has grown significantly. According to GAO, nominations of federal lands for geothermal development increased from approximately 25,000 acres in 2020 to more than one million acres in 2025.
Despite this growing interest, geothermal developers reported to GAO inconsistent permitting decisions for exploration activities. BLM has developed handbooks intended to clarify terminology and provide consistent guidance, but those documents have remained in draft form since at least 2022. 
GAO also found that BLM lacks a comprehensive mechanism for tracking geothermal permitting activity. BLM shut down its geothermal tracking system in 2021, and the system that took its place has no way to track geothermal permits. Oil and gas wells, however, are tracked in a dedicated system from initial permitting through final closure. As a result, BLM has limited visibility into permitting timelines and workloads, making planning more difficult for both developers and federal officials to anticipate project timelines and resource needs.
The House has already voted to address these problems. The bipartisan Geothermal Energy Advancement Act (H.R. 5631), which passed the House in June, includes legislation sponsored by Rep. Lee, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, and Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.). Rep. Ansari’s Geothermal Gold Book Development Act would require the Bureau to publish standard permitting procedures, in line with GAO’s recommendation.
Read the full report and recommendations here.

Sanctions Target Iran’s Remaining Illicit Fleet and its Global Support Network
WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury is targeting the remnants of Iran’s shadow fleet: the aging network of tankers the regime relies on to move billions of dollars’ worth of petroleum and petroleum products to foreign markets. Today’s action effectively neutralizes the vast majority of Iran’s remaining shadow fleet network.
“Treasury is starving the tyrannical regime in Tehran of the money it uses to wage war in the region, and we will continue exposing those who enable the regime’s oil sales,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “No enabler of Iranian sanctions evasion is safe from the full force of Treasury’s authorities.”
With the success of the U.S. military’s blockade, dwindling Iranian oil shipments outside the blockade line, and intensifying economic pressure across sectors from Operation Economic Outcast, the regime is running out of options to stabilize Iran’s failing economy.
OFAC is taking action against remaining shadow fleet vessels that are continuing to evade U.S. sanctions by transporting Iranian petroleum and petrochemicals. The vessels involved, registered across more than a dozen jurisdictions and operated by an intricate web of international front companies, underscore the global scale of Iran’s illicit shipping architecture and the sophistication with which the regime attempts to mask its sanctions evasion. By dismantling these maritime nodes and the companies behind them, Treasury is severing core channels the Iranian regime has long relied on to circumvent U.S. sanctions, sustain its petrochemical sector, and funnel resources to destabilizing actors. Because this illicit maritime ecosystem is fluid, with vessels routinely entering and exiting the network, Treasury will continue to monitor, identify, and disrupt any attempts at sanctions evasion.
The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum sector, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy.
OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME
Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror. Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds.
Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran. Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here.
SHADOW FLEET VESSELS
Treasury today took action against 17 shadow fleet vessels responsible for transporting millions of barrels of Iranian crude oil and petroleum and petrochemical products to a variety of markets in South and East Asia.
- The Comoros-flagged asphalt/bitumen tanker PARITOSH (IMO 9383352), owned by Marshall Islands-registered Paritosh Shipping Inc, has transported over 100,000 barrels of Iranian bitumen/asphalt in 2026.
- The Panama-flagged asphalt/bitumen tanker BITU (IMO 9531765), owned by Marshall Islands-registered Ornella Shipping Inc, has transported over 170,000 barrels of Iranian bitumen/asphalt in 2026.
- The Panama-flagged STARWAY (IMO 9273246), owned by China-based Hechuang International Group, has transported over three million barrels of Iranian naphtha since 2025.
- The Bahamas-flagged liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker GAS LUCKY (IMO 9177557), owned by China-based Shunhang Ship Management Ltd, has transported over 500,000 barrels of Iranian ethylene since 2025.
- The Mongolia-flagged LPG tanker G SPRING (IMO 9040118), owned by Hong Kong-registered JLS Dragon Co Ltd, has transported the equivalent of over one million barrels of Iranian LPG to China since 2021.
- The Palau-flagged products tanker KANHA (IMO 9308766), owned by Marshall Islands-registered Kanha Shipping Inc, has transported over three million barrels of Iranian high sulfur fuel oil to various ports in the Middle East and India since 2021.
- The Cameroon-flagged oil products tanker KING CHAIN (IMO 9277761), owned by the United Kingdom-registered and China-based Saint Abundant International Co Limited, has transported several millions of barrels of Iranian methanol to China since 2023.
- The Zanzibar-flagged LPG tanker POLAR (IMO 9050187), owned by Marshall Islands-based Terra Nav Shipping Ltd, has transported over 100,000 barrels of Iranian propane/butane to Pakistan since 2025.
- The Panama-flagged chemical/oil products tanker MACKEREL (IMO 9234628), owned by Marshall Islands-based Betta Shipping Inc., has transported over 500,000 barrels of Iranian high sulfur fuel oil since December 2025.
- The Sierra Leone-flagged LPG tanker GAS MARAKUA (IMO 9240421), owned by British Virgin Islands-based Makarua Shipping Limited, has transported over one million barrels of Iranian propane/butane since late 2025.
- The Vanuatu-flagged LPG tanker ZIXUAN (IMO 9317298), owned by Marshall Islands-based Goddess Shipping Corp., has transported over one million barrels of Iranian propane/butane since October 2025.
- The Hong Kong-flagged chemical/oil products tanker AVA 6 (IMO 9226140), owned by Hong Kong-based Standwill Shipping Limited, has transported over one million barrels of Iranian naphtha since September 2025.
- The Vanuatu-flagged crude oil tanker TINA 5 (IMO 9237761), owned by Marshall Islands-based Nostalgia Company Limited, transported over 1.5 million barrels of Iranian crude oil in August 2026.
- The Comoros-flagged LPG tanker SOGL (IMO 9208227), owned by Marshall Islands-based Gravion Maritime Company, has transported more than two million barrels of Iranian propane/butane since September 2025.
- The San Marino-flagged LPG tanker NOBLE SEA (IMO 9343118), owned by Hong Kong-based Brich Shipping Co. Limited, has shipped over two million barrels of Iranian ammonia and propane/butane since mid-2025, most recently completing a shipment of 200,000 barrels of Iranian methanol in June 2026.
- The Cameroon-flagged crude oil tanker SHENZHEN (IMO 9276561), owned by Marshall Islands-based Northport Navigation Inc., has transported more than 3.5 million barrels of Iranian crude oil since November 2025.
- The Gambia-flagged oil products tanker EXFLAME (IMO 9294678), owned by Marshall Islands-registered Science Ru Trading Co. Limited, has transported more than 400,000 barrels of Iranian methanol since mid-2026.
The following companies are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum or petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy:
- Paritosh Shipping Inc.;
- Ornella Shipping Inc.;
- Hechuang International Group Limited;
- Kanha Shipping Inc;
- Terra Nav Shipping Ltd;
- Betta Shipping Inc.;
- Makarua Shipping Limited;
- Goddess Shipping Corp.;
- Standwill Shipping Limited;
- Gravion Maritime Company;
- Nostalgia Company Limited;
- Brich Shipping Company Limited; and
- Northport Navigation Inc.
The following companies are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy:
- Shunhang Ship Management Limited;
- JLS Dragon Co Ltd;
- Brich Shipping Company Limited;
- Saint Abundant International Co Limited; and
- Science Ru Trading Co. Limited.
As a part of today’s action, OFAC is also removing two vessels from the sanctions list. The HAKUNA MATATA (IMO 9354167) and PINOCCHIO (IMO 9400112) were previously identified in June 2025 as part of Iran’s shadow fleet. Following a demonstrated change in circumstances, namely the removal of these vessels from the shadow fleet and their sale to non-sanctioned/U.S.-aligned operators, OFAC has effectuated their removal from the SDN List, and these vessels will be able to reintegrate into the ranks of licit maritime operators.
SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS
As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.
Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions. Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons.
Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions. OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.
The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.
