CISA, FBI, NSA and International Partners Warn of China-based Cybersecurity Company Enabling Threat Actors to Target Multiple Critical Infrastructure Sectors Worldwide
WASHINGTON – Today the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), National Security Agency (NSA), and international partners issued a joint Cybersecurity Advisory warning that Integrity Technology Group (Integrity Tech), a China-based cybersecurity company, is enabling threat actors to target multiple critical infrastructure sectors worldwide using a range of sophisticated tools, such as large-scale botnets, virtual private network infrastructure and living off the land. Based on real-world investigations and observed activity in North America, Southeast Asia and Africa, this advisory provides recommended mitigations and information to help network defenders detect and respond to this malicious activity.
With ties to the Chinese government, Integrity Tech is a key enabler of malicious cyber activity by acquiring or developing cyber tools, hosting infrastructure, and compromising networks globally. These Integrity Tech-enabled threat actors are using tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) consistent with the activity publically known as Flax Typhoon, Ethereal Panda, and Red Juliett. To maintain long-term, stealthy access to networks, these actors are targeting edge devices that are not closely monitored by the targeted organization. The advisory includes a range of actionable steps for network defenders to secure edge infrastructure and protect their networks which includes patching the listed known exploited common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs).
“Chinese government-affiliated actors continue to position themselves within critical infrastructure networks, including operational technology (OT) systems, with the aim of disrupting critical functions at a future time of their choosing,” said Acting Executive Assistant Director for Cybersecurity Chris Butera. “CISA urges organizations to review this advisory to be aware of the wide range of tactics used by these actors and implement recommended actions and mitigations. The advisory underscores the critical role of collaboration between government agencies and the private sector.”
"Under the FBI Cyber Strategy, we pursue both the actors who threaten critical infrastructure and the enterprises that support them," said Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI's Cyber Division. "Integrity Technology Group, a China-based company with ties to the Chinese government, is one of those enterprises, acquiring or developing cyber tools and hosting infrastructure for actors targeting networks worldwide. We urge every organization to apply this advisory's mitigations and report suspicious activity to their local FBI field office."
The advisory highlights that Chinese government-linked cyber actors targeted critical infrastructure across sectors to include government, critical manufacturing, healthcare. They also targeted victims in US law enforcement, and education organizations.
CISA, FBI and partners strongly urge all organizations, especially those in critical infrastructure to review the advisory, hunt for signs of compromise, and implement the recommended mitigations.
For more information, please visit China Threat Overview and Advisories.
###
About CISA
As the nation’s cyber defense agency and national coordinator for critical infrastructure security, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency leads the national effort to manage, uncover, and reduce risk to our digital and physical infrastructure Americans rely on every hour of every day.
Visit CISA.gov for more information and follow us on X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram.

Justice Department Files Complaint Against the City and County of Denver, Colorado Challenging Mask Ban and Identification Requirements for Federal Officers
Today, the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against the City and County of Denver, Mayor Michael C. Johnston, City Attorney Michiko Ando Brown, and Police Chief Ronald Thomas, challenging their unconstitutional attempt to regulate federal law enforcement officers by prohibiting them from wearing masks and by requiring identification in the manner prescribed by D.R.M.C. §§ 28-300–28-303.
Not only does this law represent an illegal attempt to regulate the Federal Government, but, as alleged in the complaint, the law threatens the safety of federal officers who are already facing an unprecedented wave of harassment, doxxing, and even violence. Threatening officers with prosecution for simply protecting their identities and their families chills the enforcement of federal law and compromises sensitive law enforcement operations.
“Under the U.S. Constitution, the Supremacy Clause makes clear that states and localities do not have the authority to regulate the Federal Government,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. “And they certainly cannot enact laws that place the safety of federal law enforcement at risk and undermine federal operations. We will never tolerate the doxxing or harassment of federal officers, or any law like those in Denver that enable violent behavior against federal law enforcement officers and their families.”
“The Denver masking and identification ordinance directly regulates federal law enforcement operations and threatens severe consequences for officers and public safety alike,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The Federal Government gets to decide which equipment federal officers may or may not wear when performing their official duties.”
Attorney General Blanche has instructed the Department’s Civil Division to identify state and local laws, policies, and practices that facilitate violations of federal laws or impede lawful federal operations. Today’s lawsuit is the latest in a series of lawsuits brought by the Civil Division targeting illegal policies designed to thwart federal law enforcement across the country, including in Maryland, New York, Virginia, Connecticut, New Jersey, California, Philadelphia, and Milwaukee. Through this filing, the Department reaffirms that federal law enforcement operations cannot be compromised by state or local measures that violate federal law.
Press Release Number: 26-1161
title: Justice Department Files Complaint Against the City and County of Denver, Colorado Challenging Mask Ban and Identification Requirements for Federal Officers

GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION TASK FORCE CHAIR THOMPSON, JUDICIARY COMMITTEE RANKING MEMBER RASKIN AND REP. MCBATH LEAD 174 MEMBERS CALLING ON DOJ TO ENFORCE YOUTH HANDGUN LAW
Washington – Gun Violence Prevention Task Force Chair Mike Thompson, Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin, and Rep. Lucy McBath lead a bipartisan letter with 174 members calling on the Department of Justice (DOJ) to enforce the 1968 law which prohibits licensed gun dealers from selling handguns to 18-20-year-olds.
“DOJ’s decision to block the enforcement of the 1968 law which prohibits 18-20-year-olds from buying handguns is unconstitutional, and will make our communities, and especially our schools less safe,” said Mike Thompson. “It is outrageous that DOJ would unilaterally overturn the law and allow an 18-year-old high school student to buy a handgun, buy a silencer, and have them shipped to their house without ever leaving their basement. That is just wrong.”
“For generations, the landmark provision prohibiting the sale of handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds has saved countless lives. Yet, now, the Trump Department of Justice has released a baseless opinion that this provision is unconstitutional and cannot be enforced. This reckless decision will allow young adults to obtain the firearms most often used in crime, jeopardizing public safety and putting those most at risk for gun violence in greater danger. Brady thanks Chair Thompson and Ranking Members Raskin and McBath for leading the effort to oppose this senseless decision and for their dedication to protecting America’s youth from gun violence,” said Mark Collins, Director of Federal Policy, Brady.
“The math here is simple: 18- to 20-year-olds commit gun homicides at triple the rate of people 21 and older, which is why more than 80% of Americans want 21 to be the minimum age to buy a gun,” said John Feinblatt, president of Everytown for Gun Safety. “Trump’s MAGA DOJ is handing the gun industry something it could never win in Congress or at the ballot box, and America will pay for it in lives lost and communities shattered.”
"The Office of Legal Counsel has no authority to erase a federal gun law and put more handguns in the hands of teenagers. This decision disregards clear evidence that minimum-age laws save lives,” said GIFFORDS Executive Director EmmaBrown. “The Trump administration must immediately reverse this dangerous action. I thank Representatives Jamie Raskin, Lucy McBath, and Mike Thompson, as well as the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, for their leadership in defending this lifesaving law.”
The Gun Control Act of 1968 (GCA) passed the House of Representatives and the Senate with bipartisan support and was signed into law by President Johnson in response to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy, and others, and to address a startling increase in gun crimes. For almost six decades, the GCA as a whole has saved countless lives by helping keep firearms out of the hands of high-risk groups, including not only Americans in the 18-to-20-year-old cohort but people who pose a danger to themselves or others. Expanding access to concealable firearms like handguns creates a significant public safety risk as the majority of gun crimes involve handguns.
The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.
Dear Attorney General Blanche,
We urge the Department of Justice to immediately rescind its opinion illegally declaring that a 1968 law prohibiting the sale of handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds by federally licensed firearms dealers “may not be enforced.”
Since the passage of the Gun Control Act of 1968 some 58 years ago, the Department of Justice (DOJ) has faithfully enforced it according to clear congressional intent and defended its constitutionality. The Supreme Court has never questioned, much less invalidated, this statute. Its policy rationale—that 18-to-20-year-olds lack the cognitive judgment required to safely own and handle handguns has only grown more compelling with advancements in our understanding of brain development over the last six decades and the record of gun violence already associated with that age group.
The Gun Control Act of 1968 (GCA) passed the House of Representatives and the Senate with bipartisan support, and was signed into law by President Johnson in response to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy, and others, and to address a startling increase in gun crimes. For almost six decades, the GCA as a whole has saved countless lives by helping keep firearms out of the hands of high-risk groups, including not only Americans in the 18-to-20-year-old cohort but people who pose a danger to themselves or others.
DOJ’s sudden epiphany that this essential law, which has been enforced by Democratic and Republican Attorneys General continuously for more than a half-century, is unconstitutional would override the judgment of the last 29 Congresses, which have staunchly stood by the law. Your personal reinterpretation would now allow 18-to-20-year-olds to purchase easily concealable handguns, a kind disproportionately used in violent crimes.
We already have a problem with young men in the 18-20 year range obtaining a firearm from family, friends or the criminal underground and using it to conduct a mass shooting. Millions of Americans remember when a 20-year-old gunman in Newtown, Connecticut killed 27 people, overwhelmingly children, in the deadliest elementary school massacre in American history. According to a study published in the American Journal of Public Health, one in eight mass shooters was between 18 and 20 years old.[1] Indeed, 18-to-20-year-olds have already been shown to be responsible for a disproportionate share of school shootings. [2] In fact, they comprise just 4 percent of the US population, but account for 17 percent of known gun homicide offenders generally. [3]
Teens and young adults are also already at higher risk for firearm suicide. Limiting access to firearms has been a proven and effective way of lowering rates of firearm suicide. One study demonstrated that when states restricted handgun sales to individuals under the age of 21, the firearm suicide rate declined 12 percent among 18-to-20-year-olds. [4]
Expanding access to concealable firearms like handguns creates a significant public safety risk as the majority of gun crimes involve handguns. FBI crime statistics from 2020 to 2024 show that 92 percent of firearms identified in murders were handguns, 6 percent were rifles, and 2 percent were shotguns. The lack of legal access to handguns by people under the age of 21 explains why crime guns traced to 18-, 19-, and 20-year-olds remain relatively low compared to the next age cohort of 21-, 22-, and 23-year-olds. The rate at which firearms recovered in crimes are traced back to young purchasers jumps 10-fold at age 21 before peaking at age 22.[5] This sharp increase tracks with the legal minimum age to purchase handguns and would therefore begin rising earlier after DOJ’s baffling new refusal to enforce the 1968 law.
Young adults engage in crime at a higher rate than the rest of the adult population and lowering the age to purchase a handgun would make an even larger percentage of youths vulnerable to coercion or cooption by traffickers. According to the ATF, “The most frequent age of a purchaser of a crime gun was 22 years old, with purchasers between 21 and 25 years old accounting for almost as many traced crime guns as all purchasers ages 45 and older.” One reason most crime guns are purchased by people in this age group is because traffickers frequently use, and often force younger individuals who don't have criminal backgrounds to straw-purchase their weapons for them.
DOJ’s reckless U-turn interpretation of the 1968 law is made exceptionally more dangerous when combined with ATF’s proposed rule that would allow Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs) to engage in more “non-over-the-counter” gun sales than ever before. In other words, with this new opinion and if ATF’s rule is finalized as proposed, FFLs will be able to sell handguns to purchasers between the ages of 18 and 20 without them ever setting foot in a gun store and then deliver those guns directly to their door. This would eliminate critical opportunities for responsible FFLs to observe suspicious behavior that may indicate criminal intent and to exercise their discretion to decline such sales. This would be inconsistent with congressional intent and unnecessarily endanger public safety.
The sensible restriction on FFLs from selling handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds is constitutional and is helping save lives every day. Your duty is to enforce the law as Congress writes it, not to make up new laws you prefer and substitute them for the public will as expressed through Congress. We urge you to immediately rescind your unlawful and dangerous opinion.
Sincerely,
[1] Joshua D. Brown and Amie J. Goodin, “Mass Casualty Shooting Venues, Types of Firearms, and Age of Perpetrators in the United States, 1982–2018,” American Journal of Public Health 108, no. 10 (2018): 1385–138.7
[2] Paul M. Reeping et al., “State Firearm Laws, Gun Ownership, and K-12 School Shootings: Implications for School Safety,” Journal of School Violence 21, no. 2 (2022): 132–146.
[3] Eighteen to 20 year olds commit 18% of gun homicides, despite comprising just four percent of the US population. Giffords Law Center analysis of FBI Supplementary Homicide Report (SHR) data, 2016–2020.
[4] Emma E. Fridel et al., “Examining the Impact of Minimum Handgun Purchase Age and Background Check Legislation on Young Adult Suicide in the United States, 1991–2020.” American Journal of Public Health 0 (2024).
###
Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12), and Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) are expressing concerns about workplace safety at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan and across other Southeast Michigan USPS Facilities. Since May 2026, employees have raised safety concerns and offered solutions to management, but to date employees report that nothing has been done to rectify the situation. 
“On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate,”
 the lawmakers wrote. 
The lawmakers continued:
“According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan. This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.” 
In a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, the lawmakers noted that the USPS has a responsibility to ensure that employees are safe and protected on the job.
A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:
Dear Postmaster General Steiner:
This letter is regarding workplace safety concerns at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan. We are concerned by the reports of unsafe practices at this facility and across Southeast Michigan.
On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate.
According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan.  This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.
Given the USPS’s role in ensuring worker safety, we request clarification on this matter and written responses to the following questions:
1. Was USPS aware that a non-maintenance supervisor had knowledge of and used a maintenance bypass code on multiple occasions, which could have led to serious, life-threatening consequences?
2. What steps will USPS take to ensure that only qualified employees have access to the maintenance code?
3. Have any disciplinary actions been taken, and if not, what correctional actions will USPS pursue?
4. How often are program evaluations, service talks, safety observations, and inspections conducted at this facility, as described in the Employee and Labor Relations Manual, and how will USPS adapt the safety training and protocols to address this problem at the facility?
5. What are the appropriate procedures for employees to communicate complaints or concerns with the appropriate staff when a supervisor is involved in an unsafe practice?
6. What future actions will USPS put in place to ensure a similar situation does not recur?
Ensuring worker safety remains our top priority. Thank you, and we look forward to your full and prompt response.
title: Dingell, Colleagues Express Concern Over Workplace Safety at Pontiac USPS Facility

HHS’ Office for Civil Rights Settles HIPAA Privacy Rule Investigation with Dr. Linda L. Shen d/b/a Shen Smiles, P.C.
Settlement Marks OCR’s 56th HIPAA Right of Access Enforcement Action to Advance Individual Access to Medical Records
WASHINGTON — October 8th, 2026 — The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Oﬃce for Civil Rights (OCR) today announced a settlement with Linda L. Shen d/b/a Shen Smiles, P.C. (Shen Smiles), a Pennsylvania-based healthcare provider that offers dental services, for potential violations of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) Privacy Rule. The settlement resolves an investigation of a complaint alleging a failure to provide timely access to an individual’s protected health information (PHI).
“The Privacy Rule’s administrative requirements are essential to protect not only PHI from impermissible use or disclosure, but also to ensure that covered entities are able to meet their obligations related to individual rights, such as the right of access,” said OCR Director Paula M. Stannard.
OCR initiated an investigation after receiving a complaint that Shen Smiles failed to provide an individual with timely access to her PHI despite receiving multiple requests. During OCR’s investigation, Shen Smiles asserted that it could not provide the individual with access to her PHI because a workforce member stole the records from the practice. OCR’s investigation determined that Shen Smiles failed to implement policies and procedures with respect to PHI that are designed to comply with the Privacy and Breach Notification Rules, including a failure to have right of access policies and procedures, and that Shen Smiles did not reasonably safeguard PHI from any intentional or unintentional use or disclosure that would violate the requirements of the Privacy Rule.
On July 31, 2024, OCR issued a Notice of Proposed Determination proposing to impose a civil money penalty, and Shen Smiles subsequently requested a hearing before an administrative law judge. On August 11, 2026, prior to an administrative hearing, OCR and Shen Smiles resolved this enforcement action with a resolution agreement. Under the terms of the resolution agreement, Shen Smiles agreed to pay $140,000 to OCR.
The HIPAA Privacy Rule’s “Right of Access” provisions require that individuals, or their personal representatives, have timely access to health information within 30 days, with the possibility of one 30-day extension. OCR enforces the HIPAA Privacy Rule, which establishes national standards to protect individuals’ health records; sets limits and conditions on the uses and disclosures of PHI; and gives individuals certain rights, including the right to timely access and to obtain a copy of their health records for a reasonable cost.
The Notice of Proposed Determination may be found here.
The Resolution Agreement may be found here.
OCR is committed to enforcing the HIPAA Rules that protect the privacy and security of people’s health information. Guidance about the Privacy Rule, Security Rule, and Breach Notification Rule can be found on OCR’s website.
If you believe that your or another person’s health information privacy, civil rights, or conscience rights have been violated, you can ﬁle a complaint with OCR.
Follow HHS OCR on X at @HHSOCR.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

CNO Visits German Navy in Wilhelmshaven, Focuses on Fleet Readiness
WILHELMSHAVEN, Germany – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle visited German naval leaders, toured the guided-missile frigate FGS Sachsen (F 219), and observed ship maintenance facilities in Wilhelmshaven, Germany, Oct. 8, highlighting shared priorities in fleet readiness, shipbuilding and maintenance.
During the visit, Caudle received briefings from German Navy Flotilla Adm. Sven Beck, commander of Flotilla 2, and Rainer Sacher, director of the German Naval Arsenal, on the state of the German Navy, operational priorities and naval infrastructure.
“Our relationship with the German Navy is built on decades of trust, shared sacrifice and a common commitment to maritime security,” said Caudle. “Strong alliances require more than operating together at sea. We also have to learn from one another and find better ways to build, maintain and sustain the warships our Sailors need to fight and win.”
The discussions included ship maintenance, repair capacity and lessons learned in sustaining operationally ready fleets.
“Both of our navies understand that readiness doesn’t begin when a ship gets underway,” said Caudle. “It begins in our shipyards, our maintenance facilities and with the skilled people who keep our ships operational. By studying what each of us does well, we can identify smarter, faster and more effective ways to return ships to the fleet and keep them in the fight.”
Caudle, joined by Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, also toured FGS Sachsen, a German Navy Sachsen-class air-defense frigate. During the tour, the Navy’s senior leaders met with the ship’s crew and thanked German Sailors who participated in the United States’ 250th Independence Day celebrations in New York City in July.
“It meant a great deal to have German Sailors standing alongside our own as America celebrated 250 years of independence,” said Caudle. “Your presence in New York was a powerful reminder that the friendships we’ve built across the Atlantic extend well beyond our military missions. We’re proud to serve alongside you, and we’re grateful for the professionalism and friendship you bring to this partnership.”
Perryman also met with Sachsen’s enlisted leadership and crew, discussing the importance of professional development, leadership and the role enlisted Sailors play in maintaining operational readiness. The engagement provided an opportunity to exchange perspectives on the challenges facing Sailors in both navies and reinforce the professional relationships that underpin successful allied operations.
“Whether you’re serving aboard an American destroyer or a German frigate, the foundation of a strong Navy is its Sailors,” said Perryman. “We may wear different uniforms, but we share the same commitment to our shipmates, our mission and getting the job done. These opportunities to connect with our German counterparts, exchange ideas and learn from one another make us better Sailors and stronger partners.”
The CNO concluded his visit with a tour of shipyard facilities supporting German naval vessel maintenance and repair. The engagement highlighted the importance of maintenance capacity, industrial expertise and efficient repair processes as both navies sustain increasingly complex warships.
“We cannot afford to have ships sitting pierside when they should be at sea,” said Caudle. “Building warships is only part of the equation. We have to sustain them throughout their service lives, and that means having the right infrastructure, workforce and processes in place. Our German partners face many of the same challenges, and there is tremendous value in comparing approaches and applying lessons learned to improve readiness across both fleets.”
The visit reinforced the U.S. Navy’s commitment to working with Germany and other NATO allies to strengthen maritime security, improve naval capabilities and deter aggression across the European theater and beyond.
The visit to Wilhelmshaven marked the final stop of Caudle’s trip through the U.S. European Command area of responsibility, which began with engagements at Naval Air Station Sigonella, Italy, followed by participation in the Trans Regional Support Squadron (TRSS) in Venice, Italy, and meetings with leadership and Sailors at U.S. Africa Command in Stuttgart, Germany. Throughout the trip, Caudle reinforced the importance of forward-deployed naval forces, operational readiness and strengthening partnerships to address shared security challenges.
title: CNO Visits German Navy in Wilhelmshaven, Focuses on Fleet Readiness

Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon Visit Oakland Head Start Facility and Community Health Center, Condemn Republican Cuts to Childcare, Healthcare, and Education Programs
OAKLAND, CA – This week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12) hosted, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA-05), the highest-ranking woman in the House of Representatives, in Oakland’s Fruitvale neighborhood. They visited the Unity Council’s Head Start and Early Head Start Preschool facilities and La Clínica de La Raza, a federally qualified health center, to meet with families, frontline health care staff, and care workers who have been impacted by Republicans’ devastating federal aid cuts.
President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ “One Big, Cruel, Ugly Bill” has made deep cuts to federal funding for healthcare, childcare, education, and food assistance programs. In California’s 12th Congressional District, it is estimated that 31,000 people are experiencing rising healthcare costs and 35, 595 people will lose health coverage because of Republican cuts to Medi-Cal and decision to end enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits. In Congress, Congresswoman Simon has consistently fought against cuts to Medicaid/Medi-CAL and SNAP and attempts to gut Head Start.
“My daughter was a Head Start child, and I know intimately that federally supported childcare and healthcare is a lifeline for many families. It allows children to learn safely and be healthy while their parents attend school or work in our local businesses,” said Congresswoman Simon. “Whip Clark and I are taking everything we heard from our visit back to D.C., where we are hell bent on fighting this Administration and reversing their harmful policies so our Head Starts, our community health centers, our care workers, our families have everything they need to continue growing and being brilliant.”
"Congresswoman Lateefah Simon is an unrivaled champion for working families," said Democratic Whip Katherine Clark. "It was a privilege to join her in Oakland to see firsthand what communities need from the federal government: investments in healthcare, childcare, and the wellbeing of regular people, not giveaways to the ultra-rich. While the Republican Party continues to bend its knee to the billionaire class, Democrats are ready to take back the People's House and get to work for the working class.”
“We are honored to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark to Fruitvale and share firsthand the impact of The Unity Council’s work,” said CEO of The Unity Council, Chris Iglesias. “From giving our youngest learners, a strong foundation at our De Colores Head Start, to bringing La Catrina de Oakland to Fruitvale as a powerful celebration of culture and community, our work is rooted in creating opportunities and strengthening families. Their visit underscores the importance of continued investment in the people, programs, and places that allow communities like Fruitvale to thrive."
“At our De Colores Head Start Center, we see every day how a strong start can shape not only a child’s future, but an entire families’,” said Chief Early Learning Officer of The Unity Council, Luis Arenas. “Head Start creates opportunities for children to learn and grow while giving parents the support and resources they need to move their families forward. We were proud to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark into our classrooms and share the real, lasting impact this work has on families throughout our community.”
“We are deeply grateful to Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon for visiting La Clínica and for their tireless advocacy on behalf of the communities we serve. Their visit shows what federal investment looks like on the ground, and highlights what is at risk when coverage and resources for community health centers are reduced,” said La Clínica CEO, Jane García. “What’s at stake is whether parents can get their children to the doctor, whether patients can access dental and behavioral health care along with primary care, whether families can afford their medications, and whether community health centers have the resources to keep the staff who provide this care. La Clínica thanks Whip Clark and Congresswoman Simon for listening to our patients and staff and for bringing their voices back to Washington. The decisions made there have very real impacts here in the Bay Area.”

EDGEWOOD, MD – Amtrak has achieved a major milestone for two bridge replacement projects in Maryland: Bush River Bridge and Gunpowder River Bridge. Amtrak has selected HNTB for architectural and engineering services for both projects, which will include community engagement to inform the final design.
These bridges span a critical section of the Northeast Corridor (NEC) between Baltimore and Wilmington, each carrying over 100 Amtrak, MARC commuter, and freight trains per day. Full replacement of both bridges will help improve safety and reliability, while enabling Amtrak and MARC to add more train service in the future as needed to accommodate record growth.
Amtrak Executive Vice President, Capital Delivery Laura Mason:
“Today marks a critical step in the long journey to replace both the Bush River and Gunpowder River Bridges, key to improving the travel experience as record Amtrak ridership is projected to continue growing over the next decade. These projects are two important examples of Amtrak’s long-term vision to modernize the Northeast Corridor’s century-old tunnels, bridges, and more.”
Why it matters: The Bush and Gunpowder River Bridges serve over 100 trains from Amtrak, MARC and Norfolk Southern every day. This aging infrastructure restricts train speeds, demands constant maintenance, and bottlenecks both intercity and commuter services. Adding to the unreliability, the outdated structure of the moveable Bush River Bridge requires a 20-person crew during summer weekends to open for marine traffic, an extensive resource strain.
About the projects: Replacing the Bush and Gunpowder River Bridges will address critical state-of-good repair needs and deliver modern, reliable structures featuring several benefits, including:
- Upgrades to track alignment, signal systems, and electric traction over a 10-mile stretch of the NEC, expanding track capacity once both projects are constructed;
- Higher speeds of up to 145 miles per hour for Gunpowder River Bridge and 160 for Bush River Bridge (compared with 125 mph today); and
- A fixed-span Bush River Bridge structure that better supports marine traffic needs and no longer requires a crew.
Schedule details: Preliminary engineering is on track to conclude in 2029. HNTB has supported Amtrak on several bridge projects along the NEC in the past, including ongoing work for replacement of the Susquehanna River Bridge in Maryland and Portal North Bridge in New Jersey.
About the bridges: Completed in 1913, Gunpowder River Bridge is located between Chase and Joppatowne, Maryland. To the north is Bush River Bridge, another 113-year-old bridge located between Edgewood and Perryman, MD. Due to their age and deteriorating condition, the bridges experience reliability issues. Bush River Bridge must open for boat traffic, and its outdated infrastructure requires a team to hand crank open the structure. When the bridge has failed to close in the past, Amtrak trains between New York, Philadelphia, and Washington face massive delays. In 2019 alone, more than 72 hours of train delays for Amtrak and MARC trains were caused directly by the Bush River Bridge.
How it’s paid for: This step in the planning process is primarily funded by a grant from the Federal Railroad Administration, along with contributions from Amtrak and the Maryland Transit Administration. Both bridges are listed as key priorities on the FRA’s NEC Project Inventory. Work is currently funded through preliminary engineering and NEPA review; additional future funding would be required for final design and construction.
The big picture: Amtrak and partners are advancing several major infrastructure projects. Recent milestones across Amtrak’s portfolio of major bridge projects include:
- Portal North Bridge: Amtrak and NJ TRANSIT opened the first track on the new bridge earlier this year. The second and final track will open this fall, providing increased reliability to rail customers for generations to come.
- Dock Bridge: Amtrak will soon begin work to rehabilitate this nearly century-old bridge in New Jersey after awarding key construction and project management contracts this summer.
- Sawtooth Bridges: Amtrak and NJ TRANSIT are moving forward with initial construction for the Sawtooth Bridges Replacement Project. This $133 million Federal-State Partnership grant for “enabling components” will support critical improvements along the Northeast Corridor, delivering long-term reliability and operational benefits for more than 200,000 daily customers.
- To learn more about recent progress on other Amtrak projects, visit our infrastructure updates page.

ICYMI: Pappas-Backed AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act Passed House
The House passed the bipartisan AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, legislation cosponsored by Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01). This legislation would ensure Americans continue to have access to AM radio in all new vehicles.
“In addition to being a source of news, music, and community connection, AM radio is a lifeline in emergencies for Americans to get important information and stay safe. This bipartisan legislation will help make sure people do not lose access to this free service in their cars,” said Congressman Pappas.
More than 50 million Americans listen to AM broadcast radio every month, and it remains one of the most reliable ways to reach the public during emergencies because it can travel long distances and reach broad geographic areas. AM radio is the backbone behind America’s National Public Warning System, which provides emergency-alert and warning information to the public during major natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, chemical incidents, health emergencies, and other domestic threats, often when cellular and Internet networks fail.
Despite the clear public safety uses of AM broadcast radio, many manufacturers stopped including it in their vehicles because they did not want to spend the minimal funds to ensure public safety during emergencies.
The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act will require the Department of Transportation to issue a rule mandating that all automakers include AM radio as standard equipment in their vehicles, at no additional cost to consumers.
title: ICYMI: Pappas-Backed AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act Passed House

Statement of the Department of Justice Antitrust Division on the Closing of Its Investigation of Arrive AS’s Proposed Acquisition of Passport Labs Inc.
The U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the closing of the Antitrust Division’s investigation into Arrive AS’s (Arrive) proposed acquisition of Passport Labs Inc. (Passport):
“The Antitrust Division is committed to protecting competition while also preserving the Department’s finite resources,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. “A phased approach to merger review serves those objectives. The Antitrust Division conducted a targeted review of the proposed transaction and has decided to close the investigation.”
On March 4, Arrive announced its intent to acquire Passport. Both firms offer mobile parking payment solutions (MPPs), among other products and services. Municipalities across the United States procure one or more MPPs to allow their citizens to pay for municipal parking, particularly on-street parking, using their phones rather than meters or kiosks. The Antitrust Division opened an investigation and issued Second Requests to the companies.
Based on the particular facts surrounding Arrive and Passport’s proposed merger, the Antitrust Division and the merging parties entered into a timing agreement that prioritized the production of evidence related to MPP competition. The Antitrust Division used this and other material to more expeditiously reach a conclusion about the likely competitive effects of the transaction.
Over the past five months, the Antitrust Division conducted a thorough investigation, reviewing documents from the parties and numerous third parties, analyzing data, and interviewing industry participants, including many municipalities. In particular, the Antitrust Division analyzed whether the proposed merger may result in a substantial reduction in competition for MPPs.
The Antitrust Division concluded that a substantial reduction in competition was unlikely given current competitive dynamics in this industry. For example, smaller vendors outside of Arrive, Passport, and PayByPhone have recently won municipal contracts, suggesting a number of viable alternatives exist outside Arrive and Passport. Moreover, Passport has declined to bid for or has lost some recent notable MPP contracts.
Given the facts surrounding this investigation, the Antitrust Division anticipates that municipalities are likely to continue to have meaningful MPP alternatives in the current environment, including PayByPhone, in the event the merged firm attempts to exercise market power.
Following this review, the Antitrust Division decided that its investigation could be closed.
title: Statement of the Department of Justice Antitrust Division on the Closing of Its Investigation of Arrive AS’s Proposed Acquisition of Passport Labs Inc.

HHS Launches Agency-Wide Actions to Strengthen Vaccine Injury Research, Reporting, and Patient Care
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 8, 2026— The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) this week launched a series of actions to strengthen how the federal government identifies, documents, investigates, and responds to health problems reported following vaccination, with a focus on improving patient care and generating better evidence about potential vaccine-related injuries.
To address health problems Americans report after vaccinations, HHS:
- Opened a new National Institutes of Health (NIH) clinic dedicated to studying and caring for patients experiencing health problems following vaccination;
- Proposed reimbursing physicians for reporting suspected vaccine-related injuries to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) through a new Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) policy, bringing vaccine reporting in Medicare in line with typical Medicare reimbursement policies;
- Will require electronic health records to capture vaccine-related adverse events so that information can follow patients across the health care system; and
- Is modernizing the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) VAERS to make reporting simpler and improve the tools available to researchers and medical professionals investigating potential safety signals.
“We must listen to patients and families who report vaccine injuries—not dismiss or gaslight them,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “President Trump and I are building a health system that takes them seriously, follows the evidence, and uses what we learn to make vaccines safer. This is how we earn back trust in our public health institutions.”
NIH Opens Clinic for Patient Care and Research
On October 5, NIH opened a new clinic dedicated to studying and caring for patients experiencing health problems following vaccination. HHS and NIH leaders marked the opening with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at NIH’s Bethesda campus.
The clinic brings specialized patient care and scientific investigation together, allowing NIH clinicians and researchers to evaluate patients, study their experiences, investigate potential causes, and identify better approaches to care. By connecting patients directly with clinicians and researchers, NIH will expand access to evaluation and care while advancing scientific understanding of health problems reported following vaccination.
CMS Proposes Reimbursing Physicians for VAERS Reporting
For the first time, CMS has proposed reimbursing physicians for the time they spend submitting reports of suspected vaccine-related injuries to VAERS, bringing vaccine reporting in Medicare in line with typical Medicare reimbursement policies.
VAERS relies on reports from health care professionals, patients, caregivers, vaccine manufacturers, and others to help identify potential vaccine safety concerns. CMS proposes the reimbursement policy to reduce barriers to physician reporting and encourage health care professionals to document suspected adverse events following vaccination.
Electronic Health Records to Capture Vaccine-Related Adverse Events
Federal health information technology standards overseen by the HHS Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology will now require electronic health records to capture vaccine-related adverse events so that this information can follow patients across the health care system.
The requirement will give health care professionals a more complete picture of a patient’s medical history and reduce the need for patients to repeatedly recount the same information when receiving care from different providers.
CDC Modernizing VAERS
CDC is modernizing VAERS to make adverse-event reporting simpler, more accessible, and easier to use.
In August, CDC solicited bids for a new contract to overhaul the system. On September 28, CDC announced a new contract to make VAERS accessible on mobile devices and improve the tools available to researchers and medical professionals investigating potential safety signals. Earlier this year, CDC also added a VAERS QR code to Vaccine Information Statements provided to parents and patients for each vaccine administered.
Together, these Department-wide actions will connect patient care, physician reporting, medical records, clinical research, and federal safety monitoring. They will help HHS better identify and investigate potential vaccine injuries, improve care for patients, and use what it learns to strengthen vaccine safety.

The groundbreaking kicks off over one million new square feet of facilities that will support the B-21 Raider production-capacity expansion announced earlier this year. The effort is part of the agreement between the DAF and Northrop Grumman that increases annual B-21 production capacity by 25% while maintaining focus on cost, schedule and performance.
“This groundbreaking represents more than construction; it represents a sustained commitment to delivering the capability our nation needs at the speed the security environment demands,” said Gen. Dale White, director, Critical Major Weapon Systems and Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager to the Deputy Secretary of War. “The B-21 Raider is foundational to the Air Force’s future long-range strike capability, and this investment strengthens the industrial capacity required to field that capability faster.”
The DAF is applying $4.5 billion in funding previously authorized and appropriated under fiscal year 2025 reconciliation legislation to accelerate production of the approved B-21 acquisition profile of 100 aircraft, building on the program’s demonstrated performance to compress delivery timelines for the next-generation stealth bomber fleet.
The B-21 Raider is a long-range, penetrating strike aircraft designed to operate in highly contested environments. It integrates advanced stealth, resilient networking and modern, data-driven command-and-control architecture to support the Joint Force’s ability to deter and, if necessary, defeat emerging threats.
Currently in flight test, the B-21 program remains on track to have aircraft on the ramp at Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota, in 2027. The expansion at Plant 42 will support the transition from demonstrated program performance to increased production capacity and more rapid fielding of operational capability.
title: DAF, Northrop Grumman break ground on B-21 production facility

NSF–UKRI metascience statement
The United States National Science Foundation (NSF) and United Kingdom Research and Innovation (UKRI) have long advanced knowledge through the ingenuity of our researchers and the institutions that enable them.
Both UKRI and NSF intend to build on the metascience principles that the United States have outlined in the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science, and that both agencies have articulated in, respectively, the "NSF Leadership in a New Golden Age of Science" memorandum and the UKRI Strategy 2026-31.
The NSF and UKRI will collaborate on metascience, to apply the experimental and analytical process of science to the funding, practice, and orchestration of our respective science and technology enterprises. The NSF and UKRI recognize that the methods by which research is funded, conducted, and evaluated can themselves be studied and improved, and we can learn from our respective programs, data, and institutional experience. We intend to explore metascience cooperation in areas including:
- Measuring research productivity and impact;
- Improving research review and funding;
- Assessing how new methods and tools are used in research; and
- Enabling responsible analysis of metascience-relevant data.
The partnership between the NSF Office of Metascience and the UK Metascience Unit also supports the development of an international network of metascience units, which will bring together like-minded countries to exchange ideas, share best practices, and explore coordinated experiments and challenges regarding applied metascience.
In the coming months, NSF and UKRI intend to formalize this collaboration to put this partnership into practice and identify initial concrete, ambitious opportunities for joint metascience work.
title: NSF–UKRI metascience statement

WASHINGTON—Today, Congressman James P. McGovern (D-MA) released the following statement calling for the release of detained Egyptian journalists:
“As the Democratic Co-Chair of the bipartisan Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, I condemn the arrest of six journalists affiliated with the independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash and call on the government of Egypt to release them immediately. 
"On September 28, Egyptian security forces raided the homes of and arrested Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira and Abdullah Qadri, both of whom are editors at Matsadaash. Later that day, Egyptian state security arrested four additional journalists, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud, and Mohamed Adel, constituting the entirety of the newsroom. Authorities have not publicly issued charges against the journalists or justification for their arrest. 
"This comes after the Trump Administration shamefully released $320 million in military aid to Egypt which had been withheld due to human rights concerns.  
"Matsadaash has repeatedly been targeted by Egyptian authorities for its open-source investigative reporting. The recent arrest of its newsroom represents an alarming escalation of repression against independent media and freedom of expression in Egypt, particularly as some of the detainees report having been tortured.  Pursuant to its obligations as a state party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the Convention Against Torture, Egypt must respect the rights of its citizens to freedom of expression and freedom from arbitrary detention and torture. 
"As a partner in the Defending Freedoms Project, which campaigns to free prisoners of conscience around the world, I demand that the Egyptian government release the six detained journalists immediately. I also call on authorities to refrain from further targeting of members of the Matsadaash platform and other press workers.”
title: McGovern calls for the release of detained Egyptian journalists

text:
Justice Department and FBI Seize Vulnerability Scanning and Spear Phishing Tools Operated and Used by China-State Sponsored Hackers
Today the Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorized seizures to deny malicious cyber actors access to two hacking tools, “Microscan” and “FishHub,” used to scan and, in some cases, hack, U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure systems and other networks. As alleged in court documents unsealed in the Western District of Pennsylvania, malicious cyber actors working for Integrity Technology Group (Integrity Tech), a company based in the People’s Republic of China (PRC), operated and used the tools. Integrity Tech has contracts with the PRC government.
“The United States will not allow China or its proxies to operate against United States interests with impunity in cyberspace,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will continue to respond decisively and use every tool at our disposal to disrupt the Flax Typhoon threats, dismantle the infrastructure sustaining them, and protect the critical networks that power our daily lives and on which our Nation’s security depends.”
“These state-sponsored hackers continue to aggressively target and access networks and systems throughout the world in an effort to identify and steal files and otherwise exploit victims’ vulnerabilities,” said U.S. Attorney Troy Rivetti for the Western District of Pennsylvania. “These seizures, our second disruption of Integrity Tech’s massive operations in as many years, send another clear message to cybercriminals from the PRC and elsewhere of the Department’s dedication to defending and maintaining cybersecurity in the United States and abroad.”
“Integrity Technology Group provided China-linked threat actors with capabilities used to conduct widespread vulnerability scanning and, in some cases, intrusions targeting U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure,” said Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Division. “The PRC relies on contractor and enabling companies to expand the reach and scale of its malicious cyber activity. By exposing and disrupting these enablers, we make it harder for the PRC to target American networks and infrastructure.”
“Today’s seizures underscore the FBI’s unwavering commitment in disrupting PRC state-sponsored cyber criminals who threaten our critical infrastructure and national security,” said Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily of the FBI San Diego Field Office. “FBI San Diego and our law enforcement partners around the world will continue to employ the full force of our investigative authority to protect the American people and safeguard our networks from malicious foreign cyber actors.”
According to court documents, Integrity Tech created and used a botnet of internet-of-things devices infected with a variant of Mirai malware. Among other things, this botnet facilitated Integrity Tech’s computer vulnerability scanning using Microscan. Integrity Tech developed Microscan to conduct reconnaissance, via the botnet and otherwise, of victim computer networks for vulnerabilities that its clients would later exploit. Targets of Microscan vulnerability scanning include a U.S. power company based in South Carolina, a multi-national Non-Governmental Organization, Japanese and Polish airports, Taiwanese critical infrastructure companies in the natural gas and power sectors, and two Taiwanese universities. Integrity Tech accessed Microscan through one of the seized domains, c0cc[.]cc.
A second Integrity Tech tool, FishHub, is alleged to have facilitated the exploitation of computer networks through spear phishing. After an initial network compromise, FishHub downloaded additional malware to the victim network. This malware provided Integrity Tech’s clients with unauthorized remote access to the victim network or searched for specific files and sent them to servers controlled by Integrity Tech. Confirmed victims of FishHub activity included approximately 20 Taiwanese universities. Five of the seized domains helped deliver this malware: 98aicai[.]com, 98aicode[.]com, outlook3650[.]com, youtubecard[.]com, and linkedinns[.]net.
Today’s action marks the Department’s second public technical disruption of Integrity Tech’s hacking infrastructure. In September 2024, the Justice Department announced the court-authorized disruption of Integrity Tech’s Mirai malware botnet which consisted of more than 200,000 consumer devices in the United States and worldwide. In conjunction with the seizures announced today, the FBI, along with other U.S. and foreign-partner agencies, published a cyber security advisory. This advisory provides indicators-of-compromise associated with Integrity Tech intrusion activity and is designed to help network defenders identify and respond to Integrity Tech’s malicious activity.
The FBI San Diego and Baltimore Field Offices are investigating the case, in coordination with the FBI’s Cyber Division.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan McKenna for the Western District of Pennsylvania and Trial Attorney Jacques Singer-Emery of the National Security Division’s National Security Cyber Section are prosecuting the case. Substantial assistance was provided by Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas Sullivan for the District of Maryland and the National Police Agency of Japan.
Note: View the affidavit here.
View the seizure warrant here.
title: Justice Department and FBI Seize Vulnerability Scanning and Spear Phishing Tools Operated and Used by China-State Sponsored Hackers

On September 23, 2026, leadership from the National Weather Service (NWS) and Argonne National Laboratory (Argonne) formally signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to collaborate on artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) for advanced weather forecasting and atmospheric simulation workflows.
Strengthening Weather Prediction and AI Infrastructure
The MOU establishes a framework intended to encourage joint innovation, technical exchange, and exploration of AI-ready datasets and open-weight machine learning foundation models. By connecting NWS capabilities with DOE's Genesis Mission initiatives and Argonne's computing power, including the Aurora Exascale Supercomputer, the collaboration aims to bring together the unique expertise of both agencies to advance the development of capabilities to improve weather prediction across scales to better inform decision support tools.
Areas of Cooperation
Under the MOU, NWS and Argonne will explore and coordinate on several key areas:
	- AI and Environmental Modeling: The partnership will focus on advancing artificial intelligence and high-performance computing for atmospheric science and environmental prediction. This includes exploring AI subseasonal-to-seasonal forecast models, training open-weight machine learning foundation models, and leveraging exascale architectures like the Aurora Supercomputer.
- Technical Information Exchange and Data Readiness: Both organizations will work together to optimize the availability and impact of AI-ready data to support advanced research. Additionally, teams will share technical capabilities regarding modeling, data workflows, and decision-support tools.
- Forums, Knowledge Sharing, and Future Coordination: NWS and Argonne will jointly host and participate in technical exchange meetings. These discussions will help establish collaboration pathways and joint projects.
The signing ceremony took place during a joint NOAA and DOE Workshop on High-Resolution Reanalysis Data held at Argonne National Laboratory on September 22-23, 2026. The MOU was signed by Dr. Daryl Kleist, Deputy Director of the NWS Office of Modeling & Development, on behalf of the National Weather Service, and Dr. Kirsten Laurin-Kovitz, Associate Director for Nuclear Technologies and National Security, on behalf of Argonne National Laboratory.
title: October 8, 2026 - National Weather Service and Argonne National Laboratory Formalize Strategic Partnership in AI and Advanced Weather Forecasting

text:
After more than seven months aboard the International Space Station, NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission safely splashed down Thursday in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles. The crew members will discuss their science mission during a news conference at 3:30 p.m. EDT, Thursday, Oct. 15, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

“Jessica, Jack, Sophie, and Andrey spent 237 days living and working in orbit, traveled more than 100 million miles, advanced important science, and returned safely home because of the extraordinary expertise and competence of thousands across NASA, SpaceX, and our international partners,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Building the capability, experience, and confidence to do this repeatedly is exactly what will allow us to go farther, and I am grateful to Crew-12 and their families for their service to humanity’s greatest adventure.”

NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway , ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev returned to Earth at 8:34 a.m. PDT. Teams aboard SpaceX recovery vessels retrieved the spacecraft and its crew shortly after. Following standard postflight medical screenings, the crew will fly to shore before returning to NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

“NASA’s activities supporting the International Space Station — transporting crew, conducting impactful research, and maintaining critical national assets — enable the science, engineering, and risk‑reduction needed for future missions across the solar system,” said Dana Weigel, manager of NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program at the agency’s Johnson Space Center. “We’re grateful for the dedication across the human spaceflight team that makes this possible, and we’re thrilled to welcome Jessica, Jack, Sophie, and Andrey home.”

During their 237-day mission, the four crew members traveled more than 100 million miles and completed more than 3,792 orbits around Earth. The mission was the second for Meir and Fedyaev and the first for Hathaway and Adenot. Crew-12 lifted off at 5:15 a.m. EST on Feb. 13 and docked to the orbiting laboratory a day later.

Crew‑12 logged hundreds of hours of scientific research to support human exploration beyond low Earth orbit and advance benefits for people on Earth. The crew members’ work included testing stem cell production for cell‑based therapies, demonstrating on‑demand IV fluid generation for future missions, and studying how the bacteria that causes pneumonia can lead to long‑term heart damage. The crew also conducted nutrition-focused research and examined how physical characteristics may affect blood flow during spaceflight to help keep astronauts safe and healthy on future missions. Research conducted aboard the space station advances knowledge and demonstrates new technologies that enable us to prepare for human exploration of the Moon and Mars.

Meir completed four spacewalks, bringing her career total to seven. That places her third all-time in total spacewalks among women at NASA, behind former agency astronauts Peggy Whitson and Suni Williams. Adenot completed three spacewalks, becoming the first French woman to venture outside the orbital outpost.

United States-based media interested in attending the crew news conference in person with Meir, Hathaway, and Fedyaev, must contact the NASA Johnson newsroom no later than 5 p.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, at jsc-newsroom@mail.nasa.gov . Media joining by phone must request dial-in details by 9:30 a.m., Oct. 15. To ask a question, media must join no later than 15 minutes before the start of the news conference. The agency’s media credentialing policy is available online. Adenot will return to Europe and not be available during the news conference.

NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program provides reliable access to space, maximizing the use of the International Space Station for research and development by partnering with private U.S. companies, including SpaceX, to transport astronauts to and from the space station.

Learn more about NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 at:

https://www.nasa.gov/commercialcrew

-end-

Editor’s note: This release was updated Oct. 8, 2026 with the formal name of the summit.

As the Golden Age of deep-space exploration begins, NASA and the U.S. Department of Energy are advancing the development of safe, reliable, next-generation nuclear technologies for space.

Together, the agencies will supercharge civil space exploration, unlock bold scientific discovery, and solidify American leadership in space nuclear power and propulsion.

“We are entering the ‘Nuclear NASA-era,’ which represents a major transformation for space exploration,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Nuclear power will allow us to go farther, operate longer, and field more capable spacecraft and instruments than ever before. The work we’re doing today is laying the foundation for the fission-powered spacecraft of tomorrow and opening an entirely new frontier for exploration and discovery.”

The new Memorandum of Understanding, “Accelerating American Leadership in Space Nuclear Power and Propulsion,” was signed Thursday between NASA and DOE, and establishes a framework for end-to-end collaboration. The agreement unites both agencies across the full spectrum of space nuclear development, spanning advanced research and fuel production to rigorous testing, launch integration, and operations. Across all these efforts, an uncompromising commitment to safety remains the central pillar.

The signing took place between Isaacman and U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright during the Science: A Golden Age Summit, hosted by the Office of Science and Technology Policy at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace in Washington, and is effective Sunday, Nov. 1.

“Thanks to President Trump, America’s nuclear renaissance is reaching a new frontier,” said Wright. “The Energy Department is proud to partner with NASA as we help American space missions reach uncharted territory.”

President Trump’s December 2025 Executive Order on Ensuring American Space Superiority directs NASA to develop a launch-ready lunar surface reactor by 2030, a goal toward which NASA, partnering with DOE, is making steady progress. This pivotal agreement fortifies existing collaborations on fission and radioisotope power systems, propelling NASA’s vision for a sustained human presence on the Moon and accelerating the breakthrough technologies to enable our mission.

When NASA’s Space Reactor‑1 Freedom launches in 2028, nuclear propulsion will advance from laboratory research to operational deep‑space application. This milestone paves the way for Lunar Reactor‑1, the fission surface power system that will sustain the future Moon Base through darkness and shadow. Nuclear power will energize habitats, communications, instruments, rovers, resource usage, and critical lunar infrastructure, and it will be essential for the demanding energy needs of future Mars missions.

Together, SR‑1 and LR‑1 form the foundation of a robust domestic nuclear‑space industrial base. These programs are poised to power permanent lunar outposts, enable exploration of distant worlds, and cement American leadership in space for generations. These endeavors will expand humanity’s reach toward Mars, reinforce American preeminence in deep space, and pioneer innovative technologies that yield benefits here on Earth.

In addition to fission power, NASA continues to expand its use of radioisotope power systems. The Dragonfly mission to Saturn’s moon Titan, scheduled for launch in 2028, will rely on a Multi‑Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator and 24 Light Weight Radioisotope Heater Units to power and warm the car‑sized rotorcraft. Dragonfly will fly to various locations on Saturn’s moon Titan and investigate the moon’s habitability.

NASA and DOE additionally plan to support ESA’s (European Space Agency) Rosalind Franklin Mars rover studying the potential for past and current life on the Red Planet, by providing 24 similar heater units to maintain instrument temperatures in the extreme cold of the Martian environment.

To learn about Nuclear NASA, visit:

https://www.nasa.gov/ignition

-end-

Media are invited to join NASA for a media teleconference at 4 p.m. EDT, Thursday, Oct. 15, to preview the agency’s contributions to JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission. The mission is scheduled to launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan on Monday, Oct. 19 EDT (Tuesday, Oct. 20 JST).
Audio of the media teleconference will stream on the agency’s website at:

Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald Issues Memorandum on the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Comprehensive Approach in the Fight Against Fraud
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (the Fraud Division) today released Directive 26-13, outlining the Division’s comprehensive approach in the fight against fraud.
Expanding on earlier guidance regarding the Division’s priorities (available here) and corporate enforcement policy (available here), Directive 26-13 sets out the Division’s prosecutorial methodology for investigating, disrupting, and prosecuting fraud. This directive marks a significant operational shift, requiring the Division’s prosecutors to attack fraud from all angles using the Division’s tax, securities fraud, consumer fraud, and cybercrime authorities.
This directive also requires Division prosecutors to deploy early, pre‑indictment asset seizures and digital‑infrastructure takedowns to halt fraud schemes and freeze assets in real time. Finally, this directive urges Division prosecutors to develop practice cooperators, zealously prosecute corporate bad actors, seek arrest and detention in appropriate cases, and deliver fulsome advocacy at sentencing. This new, comprehensive approach will drive the Division forward in its mission to preempt, disrupt, and dismantle fraudulent networks before they can inflict widespread harm.
Read the full memo here.
The Fraud Division has a clear mission: to prosecute fraud in the United States, no matter its size or complexity. This mission is critical to restoring public confidence in the federal government’s ability to responsibly steward taxpayer dollars. The Government Accountability Office recently estimated that the federal government loses between $233 billion to $521 billion annually to fraud — with other models showing even higher annual losses. Accordingly, Fraud Division personnel will work tirelessly to bring to justice individuals and corporations who have defrauded the public fisc, and threaten the health, safety, security, and prosperity of Americans.
The public may contact the Corporate Enforcement Section with information about corporate fraud at corporate.enforcement@usdoj.gov.

Justice Department Files Motions Defending a Rule Rescinding the Regulatory Definitions of “Harm” As It Relates to the Endangered Species Act
The Justice Department’s Energy and Natural Resources Division (ENRD) yesterday filed motions for summary judgment in four cases defending challenges to a rule rescinding the regulatory definition of “harm” in U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) and National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) regulations implementing the Endangered Species Act (ESA). These cases, in the Northern District of California and the District of South Carolina, are the first in a series of similar challenges across the country to reach this stage of litigation.
“Regulatory overreach burdens American families and businesses, and these now-rescinded Endangered Species Act regulations are a prime example,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of ENRD. “The Department of Justice will continue vigorously defending President Trump’s efforts to uphold the Act as written and protect economic growth.”
According to the filings, what is at issue in all four cases is whether the ESA’s restriction on “take” of listed species requires an intentional, purposeful act directed against a particular animal. In the ESA, Congress defined “take” to include 10 verbs centered on intentional actions against individual animals, like hunt, shoot, wound, kill, and trap. But the FWS and NMFS interpreted one of those verbs, “harm,” in a way that allowed them to regulate actions that modify a species’ habitat.
The filings go on to say that the Supreme Court’s since-overruled Chevron doctrine deferred to certain agency interpretations of statutes, which led to the court’s decision to uphold the prior regulatory definitions of “harm” in the ESA. A dissent to that decision stated how the ESA’s plain language, structure, and history cut against such an overly broad reading. After the Supreme Court’s rejection of Chevron deference in its decision in Loper Bright Enterprises, the FWS and NMFS should interpret the statute according to its plain terms — which adopts the reasoning of that prior dissent — and decide to rescind the regulatory definitions of “harm” to return to the statutory text as written.
Attorneys from ENRD’s Wildlife and Marine Resources Section and Natural Resources Section are handling the matters.
title: Justice Department Files Motions Defending a Rule Rescinding the Regulatory Definitions of “Harm” As It Relates to the Endangered Species Act

ST. LOUIS – Three St. Charles County, Missouri residents have been sentenced for their roles in the forced labor of an Indian national.

U.S. District Judge John A. Ross on Thursday sentenced Venkatesh Sattaru, 38, to 50 months in prison. Judge Ross ordered that sentence to run concurrently with a 5-year sentence for second-degree domestic assault in St. Charles County Circuit Court. Sattaru has also paid a forfeiture money judgment of $74,634 to the Department of Homeland Security, restitution of $83,776 to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and restitution of an agreed upon sum to his victim.

Sattaru pleaded guilty in April to one count of confiscating or concealing immigration paperwork while obtaining the labor or services of a person by means of serious harm or threats of serious harm and one count of theft of government funds. The victim is Sattaru’s cousin, an Indian national who arrived in St. Louis on Dec. 16, 2022. The victim lived in Sattaru’s O’Fallon home and was required to perform household chores, run errands and work in a company owned by Sattaru, the plea agreement says. In February 2023, Sattaru moved the victim into a home that was being renovated for eventual rental on Daniel Drive in O’Fallon. Around September 2023, Sattaru moved the victim into a different home being renovated on Highway D.

When the victim failed to perform his duties, he was punished with the confiscation of his immigration paperwork as well as sleep deprivation, physical abuse and restricted access to the bathroom, bathing and food. Sometimes Sattaru punished the victim himself. At other times, Sravan Penumetcha and Nikhil Penmasta punished the victim, either at Sattaru's request or on their own initiative, Sattaru’s plea agreement says. The physical abuse included the use of dangerous weapons and resulted in serious bodily injury to the victim.

During some of this time, Sattaru, a U.S. Army veteran, was also exaggerating his VA disability to increase his compensation under the Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers, also known as the Caregiver Support Program. The PCAFC provides monthly financial compensation to caregivers, who are typically relatives, to care for qualified veterans or service members. Sattaru fraudulently caused his caregiver to receive $83,776 in extra compensation from the Department of Veteran Affairs.

Penmatsa, 30, of Defiance, pleaded guilty on April 2 to one count of knowingly confiscating or concealing immigration paperwork. He is Sattaru’s brother-in-law. He was sentenced in August to 37 months in prison, consecutive to the 3-year sentence he received in St. Charles County Circuit Court.

Penumetcha, 26, pleaded guilty on March 13 to the same charge and was sentenced in June to 30 months in prison.

The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Inspector General and the St. Charles County Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Dianna Edwards prosecuted the case.
title: St. Charles County Residents Sentenced to Prison in Forced Labor Case

AGUADILLA, Puerto Rico — U.S. Border Patrol agents assigned to Ramey Sector, working in coordination with the Puerto Rico Police Department’s Fuerzas Unidas de Rápida Acción, seized approximately 562 pounds of suspected cocaine and arrested two U.S. citizens during a maritime enforcement action near Aguadilla early Monday.
On Oct. 5, law enforcement personnel identified and intercepted a suspicious vessel operating in waters west of Aguadilla. During the subsequent investigation, authorities discovered 231 packages containing a substance that field-tested positive for cocaine.
The vessel, suspected narcotics, and two individuals were transferred to the Ramey Border Patrol Station for further investigation and processing. The Drug Enforcement Administration is in charge of the investigation and prosecution.
“This seizure demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the vigilance of the men and women protecting Puerto Rico’s coastal borders,” said Ramey Sector Chief Patrol Agent Reggie Johnson. “Working alongside the Puerto Rico Police Department and FURA, our agents prevented a significant quantity of dangerous narcotics from reaching our communities. We remain committed to disrupting transnational criminal organizations and safeguarding the public.
The investigation is ongoing.
Ramey Sector is one of the twenty Sectors spread out across the United States. Encompassing the U.S. territorial islands of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands, it is the only Border Patrol Sector located outside the continental United States. The Sector’s entire border area is made up of coastline and its area of responsibility is made up of some 6,000 square miles of land and water area, including the twelve-mile band of territorial water surrounding the Islands.
title: Border Patrol, Puerto Rico Police Seize More Than 560 Pounds of Cocaine Near Aguadilla
