MEDFORD, Ore.—A Grants Pass, Oregon, man pleaded guilty today to illegally possessing a gun he stole in a burglary, announced U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford for the District of Oregon.

Matthew Bertrand, 45, pleaded guilty to felon in possession of a firearm. Bertrand is a felon, having been previously convicted five other times for burglary and theft.

According to court documents, on January 5, 2024, Central Point Police responded to a burglary in progress. A witness told police that the witness saw a man wearing a black ski mask, a black jacket, and blue jeans jump the fence and go inside a home.

When police arrived and spoke to the homeowner, they saw Bertrand flee through the back of the home. Police caught Bertrand after chasing him through multiple backyards. Bertrand had a black ski mask. Police recovered the gun belonging to the homeowner in the area where Bertrand ran.

Bertrand admitted to "rob[bing] the house", stealing the gun, and being in the victim's house on a prior occasion because the owner had "lots of toys."

On June 6, 2024, a federal grand jury in Medford returned a two-count indictment charging Bertrand with felon in possession of a firearm and possession of a stolen firearm. He will be sentenced on March 11, 2027, before U.S. District Court Judge Kasubhai.

Bertrand faces a maximum of life with a mandatory minimum of fifteen years’ imprisonment as an armed career criminal. He also faces a fine of $250,000, up to three years of supervised release, and a $100 fee assessment.

The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Medford Police Department, and Central Point Police Department are investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Judi Harper is prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: Grants Pass Man Pleads Guilty to Felon in Possession of a Firearm

WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement after an investigation by the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), led by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), resulted in the sentencing of an illegal alien who had been convicted on drug trafficking charges.
On October 1, Jose Luis Mata-Cedillo, an illegal alien from Mexico, was sentenced to 20 years in prison after he had previously been convicted for cocaine trafficking, possessing a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, being a felon in possession of a firearm, and illegal re-entry after deportation as an aggravated felon. The investigation into Mata-Cedillo began when an HSI Task Force Officer intercepted a courier transporting 27 kilograms of cocaine bound for St. Louis, Missouri, which led to the subsequent seizure of approximately 13 kilograms of cocaine, $121,280 in cash, and a loaded 9-millimeter Glock handgun.
Following his conviction, Mata-Cedillo was turned over to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) and will face deportation proceedings upon his release.
Jose Mata-Cedillo
Mata-Cedillo’s criminal history includes prior convictions for TWO counts of selling, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance, conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance, and unlawfully transporting firearms in Washington.
“This illegal alien will now spend 20 years behind bars after being convicted for cocaine trafficking, firearm charges, and illegal re-entry,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “Thanks to our partners through the Homeland Security Task Force, this criminal is now off our streets and will be removed from our country once his sentence is complete. We will never apologize for putting the safety of the American people first.”
Mata-Cedillo first illegally entered the United States through Texas in 2008 and was deported the same day. He then illegally re-entered the United States – a felony – at an unknown date and location. After serving his prison sentence for the prior convictions, he was deported a second time by the Trump Administration in August 2020. He then illegally entered the country for a THIRD time at an unknown date and location.
This investigation was led by HSI St. Louis.

Trump’s Executive Order 14159, DHS and the Department of Justice (DOJ) are taking a whole of government approach by setting up Homeland Security Task Forces across the nation. USDA Announces $1.8 Billion in 2026 Conservation Program Payments
(Washington, D.C., October 8, 2026) — The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced today it is issuing approximately $1.8 billion in Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) payments to agricultural producers and landowners for their participation in key conservation programs for 2026. These payments include Grassland CRP payments that play an important role in the Trump Administration’s Ranchers First Initiative announced by USDA Secretary Brooke L. Rollins that includes sweeping actions focused on rebuilding the Great American Cattle Herd and putting America’s ranchers back at the center of our nation’s food supply.
This year, USDA’s Farm Service Agency (FSA) accepted offers on nearly 1 million new acres of Grassland CRP, providing ranchers with rental payments and cost share assistance to maintain rangeland and pastureland as grazing areas. After 2026 enrollment, Grassland CRP acreage is anticipated to account for more than 40% of all CRP enrolled acres.
“Under the Trump Administration we have committed to putting American farmers and ranchers first. As we continue to work to rebuild the American cattle herd, today’s announcement will help continue this effort by protecting nearly one million acres of grazing land for our ranchers,” said Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “This change will encourage greater growth of our cattle industry, while preserving our nation’s natural resources.”
“These conservation payments play a key role in helping landowners preserve and protect natural resources, while also promoting working lands conservation,” said Under Secretary for Farm Production and Conservation Richard Fordyce. “Enrollment in our conservation programs has been a highly competitive process. These payments support landowners with an interest in voluntary land stewardship, helping them drive conservation efforts on their land to keep their operations moving forward while protecting our nation’s natural resources and supporting rural communities across the country.”
Conservation Payments
The $1.8 billion in annual rental payments are being made to agricultural producers and private landowners through the Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) and Grassland CRP. These annual rental payments are made to eligible farmers and ranchers who establish long-term, resource-conserving vegetative covers. Additionally, annual rental payments provide a steady income stream for participants, helping to stabilize farm income.
CRP helps reduce soil erosion, improve water quality, and increase wildlife habitat, contributing to the overall health of ecosystems. Grassland CRP is a working lands conservation program that enables participants to conserve grasslands while also continuing most grazing and haying practices.
For fiscal year 2027, a total of 26.8 million acres will be enrolled in CRP after FSA accepts offers on 2.2 million acres through Grassland, General and Continuous CRP signups for 2026.
The following states rank in the top five for CRP payments for 2026: Iowa, Illinois, Minnesota, South Dakota, and Missouri.
More Information
For more information on conservation programs, producers and landowners can visit fsa.usda.gov/crp or contact their local FSA county office.

Trump EPA Continues to Clear Backlogged State Implementation Plans in Oklahoma
DALLAS, TEXAS (Oct. 8, 2026) – Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) approved final revisions to Oklahoma’s State Implementation Plan (SIP) for the interstate transport of Sulfur Dioxide (SO2) that was submitted in 2021, marking the 15th SIP approval for the state in 2026. This action further reduces the backlog of SIPs left by the Biden Administration and confirms that Oklahoma’s plan meets all Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements for SO2 transport. Approving SIPs on time provides certainty to local businesses, strengthens cooperative federalism, and advances EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment, while allowing the economy to continue to grow.
“Over the past year, EPA Region 6 has worked diligently to clean up the mess left behind by the Biden Administration and give Oklahoma more control over its air program,” said Regional Administrator Scott Mason. “Today’s action is a perfect example of Administrator Zeldin’s efforts to promote cooperative federalism, give Oklahoma businesses more certainty, and provide all Americans with clean air to breathe.”
EPA’s approval confirms Oklahoma’s SIP has provisions to ensure emissions of SO2 in the state will not significantly affect air quality in neighboring states. To support this decision, EPA considered air quality, emission sources, modeling, and emission trends in Oklahoma and bordering states to identify any sources and emission activities that could potentially impact the downwind air quality in other states. EPA found that Oklahoma’s SIP complies with the CAA requirements and there are no SO2 nonattainment concerns in any other state as a result of emissions from Oklahoma sources or emission activities. EPA will continue to work with the state of Oklahoma to develop and approve common sense environmental plans that protect Americans and provide regulatory certainty for businesses.
The final notice and docket materials are available at regulations.gov under docket ID EPA-R06-OAR-2025-2270.
Background
The Clean Air Act (CAA) requires states to develop State Implementation Plans (SIPs). The SIP is a general plan to attain and maintain the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) in all areas of the country, and a specific plan to attain the standards for each area designated nonattainment for a NAAQS. The core purpose of a SIP is to enforce air standards, reduce pollution, and demonstrate compliance with CAA standards.
Earlier this year, EPA cleared over two decades of backlogged SIPs in Oklahoma by acting on 13 SIP revisions submitted between 2002 and 2025. Clearing the enormous SIP backlog left over from previous administrations is key to achieving EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin’s mission to protect the environment and grow the economy.
For more information on SIPs, visit our webpage.
Connect with the Environmental Protection Agency Region 6 on Facebook, X, Instagram, or visit our homepage.
title: Trump EPA Continues to Clear Backlogged State Implementation Plans in Oklahoma

Twelve newly selected Phase II and six Phase I projects to advance the frontiers of Super Intelligence (SI) for science, capping a first-year cohort of 297 projects across the Genesis Mission portfolio.
October 8, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced 12 Phase II Genesis Mission project awards totaling $159 million. Building on the Genesis Mission’s growing portfolio of projects, first announced in July, these Phase II project awards will unleash scientific discoveries with Super Intelligence (SI).
President Trump launched the Genesis Mission in November 2025 to accelerate discovery and strengthen U.S. leadership in science, medicine, and technology.
“These projects represent a critical step in turning the promise of Super Intelligence for science into transformative scientific capability,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Dr. Darío Gil. “The Phase II teams have already demonstrated what is possible when SI is integrated with scientific expertise, data, and computing. These awards give them the opportunity to take that work to the next level. By bringing together our National Labs, universities, and industry partners, we are building on extraordinary work already underway and accelerating the pace of discovery.”
The Phase II awards are developing new, powerful capabilities to tackle the Nation’s most complex National Science and Technology Challenges. By connecting America’s leading scientists with advanced SI, supercomputing, scientific data, and DOE’s world-class research infrastructure, the Genesis Mission is strengthening U.S. leadership at the frontiers of science and technology.
Awarded Projects
Through DOE’s Office of Science, the 12 newly awarded projects are:
- Accelerating the path to commercial fusion energy via an AI-enabled digital twin platform for SPARC: Led by Commonwealth Fusion Systems, this project will build a digital twin to simulate and optimize operations of a fusion demonstration device.
- Decoding the RNA Structurome to Secure AI Advantage for the Bioeconomy: Led by the University of California San Diego, the project will expand the RNA structure database five-fold for training SI models to unlock the ability to engineer resilient crops and sustainable microbes.
- Lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (LQCD) at the Intelligence Frontier: Led by MIT, this project will integrate Super Intelligence with supercomputing calculations of fundamental particle physics to dramatically accelerate discoveries about the basic building blocks of our universe.
- Multi-agent AI Expert for Subsurface Reasoning and Optimization (MAESTRO): Led by the University of California Irvine, MAESTRO will establish an SI platform to accurately map, stimulate, and manage deep underground reservoirs to unleash vast resources of reliable geothermal energy.
- AI-extended Interfacial Separations (AXIS): A Multiscale Framework for Redox-Active Ligand Design: Led by the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, AXIS will harness SI to design more efficient electrochemical processes for extracting critical rare-earth elements from domestic sources.
- Overcoming barriers in computational enzyme design through improved sequence-structure ensemble modeling: Led by the University of Washington Seattle, this project will build foundational SI tools to predict and design functional enzymes.
- Accelerating Extreme Environment Specs-to-Silicon (AXESS): Led by Fermilab, AXESS will use SI to rapidly design rugged, high-performance microchips capable of operating in extreme conditions such as space, high-radiation, and ultra-cold environments.
- The Multi-office Accelerator Team Core (MOAT-Core): Led by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, MOAT-Core will develop a shared SI platform across National Laboratories to autonomously run and design particle accelerators faster and more efficiently.
- Application-Aware Error Correcting Codesign for Scientific Quantum Computing (ASQC): Led by Harvard University, ASQC combines SI with advanced quantum hardware to tackle quantum computing error correction.
- An Iterative Framework of AI-Assisted Scientific Development and Optimization (AI4HPC): Led by Argonne National Laboratory, AI4HPC will create an SI framework to modernize, optimize, and verify supercomputing scientific software.
- AI-empowered Design of Functional Quantum Magnets: Led by Oak Ridge National Laboratory, this project will develop a physics-informed SI framework to design new quantum magnets by working backward from desired properties, with applications in quantum sensing, low-power electronics, and quantum technologies.
- Agentic Assistance for Advanced Rare Isotope Separator Operations at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB): Led by Northeastern University, this project will develop an intelligent, automated assistant to safely streamline the operation and tuning of the FRIB particle separator, unlocking hundreds of hours of research time annually.
These new selections bring the total number of Phase II projects to 14, alongside previously announced awards for GridFM 2.0 under the Office of Electricity and Prometheus under the Office of Nuclear Energy.
DOE is also issuing six new Phase I awards, expanding the Genesis Mission’s initial round of selections. More information about these and previously awarded projects is available here.
title: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Advance Super Intelligence for Science

MURRIETTA, Calif. – San Diego Sector U.S. Border Patrol agents stopped another smuggling attempt of hard narcotics along Interstate 15.
On Sept. 29 at 11 a.m., agents conducted a vehicle stop on a northbound semi-truck, traveling without a trailer, on Interstate 15 approximately a quarter mile north of the California Highway Patrol scales. During the encounter, a Border Patrol agent assigned to the Newton-Azrak Border Patrol Station and his K-9 partner, Loki, led agents to discover characteristics of liquid methamphetamine concealed inside at least one of the truck's fuel tanks.
The vehicle and the driver were transported to the Newton-Azrak Station for further processing. Hazardous response specialists were called in to safely extract the liquid contents from the fuel tank. The recovered liquid tested positive for methamphetamine, yielding a staggering total weight of 962 pounds (approximately 115 gallons) with an estimated street value of $1 million.
Agents turned the driver, a Mexican national, over to Homeland Security Investigations and local authorities for state prosecution. The semi-truck was seized by the U.S. Border Patrol.
“This massive seizure of liquid methamphetamine highlights the lengths these transnational criminal organizations will go to smuggle hard narcotics into our communities,” said Justin M. De La Torre, chief patrol agent for the U.S. Border Patrol’s San Diego Sector. “The vigilance of our agents, the reliability of our K-9 units, and our strong multi-agency partnerships are vital to dismantling these illicit smuggling operations and keeping deadly drugs off our streets.”
Under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, the dedicated men and women of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, alongside our law enforcement partners, have arrested and removed thousands of criminal aliens from the country - including gang members, rapists, kidnappers, and drug traffickers - to make our communities safer.
To prevent the illicit smuggling of humans, drugs, and other contraband, the U.S. Border Patrol maintains a high level of vigilance on corridors of egress away from our Nation’s borders. To report suspicious activity to the U.S. Border Patrol, contact San Diego Sector at (619) 498-9900.

Nearly two decades after the U.S. Air Force retired the airframe from combat, one F-117A Nighthawk had the rare opportunity to take to the skies once more: this time, in the cargo hold of a C-5M Super Galaxy. The historic stealth aircraft, bound for the Smithsonian Institution’s National Air and Space Museum’s Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center in Chantilly, Virginia, would soon join the institution’s permanent collection.
The two-day, cross-country mission required precise weight distribution and millimeter-level clearances to fit the 29,500-pound load into the C-5M’s cargo compartment. For the 512th Airlift reservists, executing high-consequence, strategic airlift operations is business as usual—even when the payload is a piece of aviation history. 
    
    
“Growing up in the ‘90s and 2000s, I remember thinking of the F-117 as the most unique plane,” said Maj. Billy Hafker, 709th Airlift Squadron instructor pilot and aircraft commander for the mission. “Being able to move it to the Smithsonian to preserve it for future generations is an incredible opportunity, and we’re all honored to do it.”
Cargo-bearing missions in the Super Galaxy require mission-ready Airmen from various career fields spanning from flying crew chief to pilot, according to Hafker. Each Airmen’s proficiency in the generation and sustainment of airpower ensures the Air Force Reserve is ready to move fast, think creatively and disrupt the status quo when reacting to crises on the global stage.
Upon landing in Palmdale, California, the Dover-based crew began conducting pre-loading operations to stage the aircraft for cargo. Within two hours of landing, the loadmasters had carefully maneuvered and secured the detached Nighthawk’s wings into the cargo hold while maintaining ample room for the fuselage.
However, the F-117’s cockpit upload was unexpectedly delayed overnight due to a coordination breakdown regarding the required number of tie-down points on the fourth-generation fighter. With both aircraft grounded on the tarmac, the Lockheed Martin Skunk Works mechanical team worked through the night to resolve the issue. Their efforts to fabricate and install the points ensured the entire plane was successfully delivered to the Smithsonian team on October 6.
“It was a little difficult to load in, but we got the job done,” shared Senior Airman Lucas Richard, 709th Airlift Squadron loadmaster. “This is probably one of the coolest pieces of cargo that I’ve ever seen.”
As of January 2021, the Air Force has retained approximately 48 F-117As in its inventory and has disposed of approximately four aircraft each year since grounding the fleet in April 2008. The demilitarization process required to deem an aircraft worthy of museum display requires immense cooperation between the Department of War and its industry partners.
“There’s a lot of people that participate in a project like this,” said Jeff Corbets, program manager at Lockheed Martin Skunk Works, who led the restoration. “Demilitarization was the most difficult piece, but I think it went really smoothly, all things considered.”
The stealth fighter that will soon be on display at the Udvar-Hazy Center earned the nickname “The Overachiever” after being the only F-117A to fly in all four major conflicts in which Nighthawks flew combat operations: Just Cause, Desert Storm, Allied Force and Iraqi Freedom. During its 1991 participation in Iraq, it flew 1,271 sorties, achieving an 80% mission success rate while suffering no battle damage. The jet retired in 2007.
As the historic aircraft takes its place on the museum floor to be marveled at by more than a million visitors each year, the mission itself serves as a proud victory for the 512th AW and its C-5 squadron. Beyond preserving history, the operation successfully showcased the advantage of the Air Force Reserve in action—delivering unprecedented combat capability and professionalism to the Joint Force.
title: Legendary fighter takes final flight, Air Force Reserve delivers F-117A to Smithsonian

Rep. Summer Lee Receives Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services
PITTSBURGH, PA – OCTOBER 8, 2026 — Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) received the Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services (RHLS), joining housing advocates, nonprofit developers, legal aid leaders, and community partners from across Pennsylvania at the organization’s annual awards reception in Downtown Pittsburgh.
Rep. Lee was recognized for her work advancing affordable housing and tenant protections in Congress and delivering federal investments for housing across Western Pennsylvania.
“I am proud to receive this award, but this one belongs to the tenants fighting to stay in their homes, the families trying to keep a roof over their heads, the organizers, lawyers, advocates, and nonprofit developers doing the hard work to keep our communities whole,” said Rep. Lee. “In Congress, I have been focused on putting federal dollars and federal protections behind that work, from bringing millions home for affordable housing to fighting for legal representation for tenants facing eviction and taking on Wall Street investors buying up our homes for profit. Nobody should have to watch their neighborhood finally get investment just in time to be priced out of it. We are going to keep fighting until staying in the community you helped build is something every single family can count on.”
Rep. Lee has brought millions of federal dollars home for affordable housing and community development, including $3 million for affordable housing projects across Allegheny County and $1 million to help convert underused office buildings in Downtown Pittsburgh into housing through her Community Project Funding initiatives.
Rep. Lee also helped advance the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a sweeping housing package that passed Congress with overwhelming bipartisan support and included provisions to limit additional single-family home purchases by large institutional investors, support home repairs and housing preservation, improve small-dollar mortgage access, and strengthen protections for homeowners challenging inaccurate appraisals. When President Trump initially withheld his signature from the bill, Rep. Lee publicly pushed for the housing relief to move forward without delay.
Her work in Congress has also focused on keeping families in their homes and preventing displacement. Rep. Lee introduced the Eviction Right to Counsel Act, which would help guarantee legal representation for low-income tenants facing eviction, and has fought to preserve affordable housing in historically underserved communities.
Rep. Lee also helped reintroduce the Stop Wall Street Landlords Act, legislation aimed at ending federal tax advantages that help large institutional investors buy up single-family homes and compete with working families.
During the event, Rep. Lee was honored alongside Pennsylvania Senate Minority Leader Jay Costa, Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato, State Rep. Lindsay Powell, and State Rep. Brandon Markosek.
To view photos/video from the event, please click HERE.
Congresswoman Summer Lee serves on the House Committee on Judiciary and the Committee on Education and Workforce. Since taking office in January 2023, she has delivered historic levels of federal investment totaling over $2.7 Billion brought back to Western PA, including over $580 million for infrastructure, over $110 million for affordable transit, over $500 million to keep clean energy manufacturing at home in Pennsylvania, and over $55 million on clean energy efforts in and around schools to help keep our kids and communities safe. These investments will help improve Western Pennsylvania’s infrastructure and transit, ensure cleaner air and drinking water, lower housing costs, fund research institutions, fuel clean manufacturing, fund STEM innovation and entrepreneurship, boost workforce development, and create thousands of good paying union jobs. Lee and her team have also delivered casework and constituent services to over 4,000 constituents with issues ranging from helping our seniors and disabled community access Medicare and social security to helping folks secure housing and helping families with immigration support and passports.
title: Rep. Summer Lee Receives Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Paulo Rangel, Portuguese Foreign Minister

Palacio das Necessidades

Lisbon, Portugal

October 8, 2026

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon. We’re going to start the press conference. I will give the floor now to His Excellency Minister of State and Foreign Affairs Paulo Rangel.

FOREIGN MINISTER RANGEL: Welcome to Lisbon, Secretary Marco Rubio.

(Via interpreter) Portugal and the United States are historic allies which together have enjoyed a lengthy relationship which defends state of law, democratic values which represent the free world, and we have strong links in economy, defense, economy, and culture.

Obviously, I want to once again highlight the 250 years of American independence, remembering that the independence was done with Portuguese wine from Madeira, and we were the third country in the world which recognized the independence of the United States of America. This historic friendship of allies consolidated in ‘95 with the cooperation agreement and defense agreement, which brings together the bilateral commission, which is functioning on a permanent basis. And this bilateral commission has been a diplomatic channel of privilege for dialogue with a legal basis on many areas of our relationships, and with the military presence of the United States in the Lajes air base.

This visit takes place at a time of great, big developments in our bilateral relations, especially in key areas like the economy and tourism. The interest of the United States and of United States citizens and their companies to Portugal continues to grow. In ‘25, United States visitors brought in 11 percent of revenue from tourism, and in the first quarter of ‘26, U.S. citizens were ranked third as visitors to Portugal.

In the economy, our companies increasingly present in the United States, whether in renewable energies, pharmaceuticals, car industry. And we have also increased investment of – United States investment in Portugal like Goldman Sachs, Aquaterra, UPS, IBM, AWS, Google have a very strong presence in our country and obviously the United States, for us, our strategic partner. And as a member of the EU, Portugal is surely one of the countries which is a champion of the priorities that Europe should give to the transatlantic relationship.

As part of that transatlantic relationship, Portugal agrees and agreed with your appeal from the United States for Europeans, members of NATO, to guarantee their responsibilities for their defense. And so we have been made a effort in our budget, which has reached 2 percent of GDP in ‘25, and so a transition of 1.6 to 2 percent in a very difficult year. And we will continue to comply with objectives of NATO, which are the 5 percent objective in medium-term future, with 3.5 in defense and 1.5 in investments related to defense sector. For us, NATO is a fundamental pillar of our defense and our safety, our security, and so is one of our priorities in foreign policy.

Obviously, we continue to believe that our relationship with the United States is fundamental. We have always supported Ukraine, and we believe that the contribution of the United States is decisive in that conflict to reach a long-lasting and fair peace. In the Middle East, we recognize the threats and the risks created by Iran and their proxies. We defend full respect for the integrity of our friends, states in the Gulf, and we have to – essential to recover free maritime movements in Hormuz and total respect for the rule of the sea. And the contribution of the United States is essential to solve this conflict.

When we prepared our mandate for the Security Council, we established relations and contacts with all members of the Security Council and other states of the United Nations, and obviously we have been discussing and preparing our presence with the United States, where obviously the majority of our positions converge.

Today, which is so important for our bilateral relationship, I’d like to welcome you especially – the important Portuguese community that lives in the United States; and they’ve been from one coast to the other – and welcome the new, enormous, and dynamic, visible U.S. citizen community in Portugal that have contributed to a new stage, a new dynamic thrust to our 50-year relationship – 243, in fact. Thank you, Marco Rubio.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you. I almost understood everything he said. I almost – like, I got very close because it’s very similar to Spanish. And so I almost turned this thing off but I said no, let me just finish it. So anyway, but thank you. I appreciate you having me here in your beautiful country, and I’m glad to be here. It’s my first visit ever and I hope it will not be my last. And I appreciate the welcome you’ve given us – not just in this extraordinary setting but the opportunity to meet with you and obviously, of course, to meet previously with – before this meeting with the prime minister.

Our two countries have accomplished many things together in the past, and we look forward to deepening and building that relationship in the future. In the past, for example, we’ve worked very closely on forging the arsenals of our allied forces. We together built your F-16 fleet, strengthening not just our two nations’ security and defense, but frankly strengthening NATO as a result of it. This is through decades of shared maintenance and training and joint operations, and we know that that will continue.

We applaud you, by the way, on the work – and I know it’s difficult, but the commitment that you’ve made that you’re living up to in spending more – and I don’t even want to use the term spending more – in investing more on defense, and for being on track to meet all of the commitments that were made at The Hague in – by the year 2035. And I always highlight this, because people sometimes view this call to invest more in defense as a hostile thing. It is not a hostile thing. On the contrary, what we are arguing is that NATO is important. For NATO to matter, NATO has to be strong. For NATO to be strong, NATO’s member-states need to be strong. And for members – for NATO’s member-states to be strong, they have to have capabilities.

Now, every country is of a different size and proportion. Some countries can contribute more than others. But every country in NATO needs to be as strong as they can possibly be. Because the stronger the members of NATO are, the stronger NATO is, the stronger the Alliance is, and the stronger the deterrence is. NATO exists, more than anything else, as a defensive Alliance that acts as a deterrent against hostility, and it has served us well for decades. And if we want it to continue to serve us, we need to make sure that it is strong.

So we look forward to the burden – to the – we look to share the burden of defense in the future, and we look forward to collaborating on constructing the next generation of weaponry that’s going to be needed and advanced military technology that’s going to be needed in order to deter the adversaries of the future. I believe working together, along with all of our Allies and partners in NATO, we can make our nations and our continents safer from foreign threats and more secure for our people.

Now, I don’t want to focus this relationship solely on our defense cooperation, because what happens between our countries goes far beyond that. And I want to talk a little bit about the economic realm, where Portugal plays an integral role in fostering U.S. commerce and in delivering U.S. technology to the European continent and beyond. As an example, Portugal’s undersea cables, affordable energy, critical mineral reserves, and hyperscale data centers make it the ideal gateway – the ideal gateway from a geographic and economic perspective – the ideal gateway for American technology companies to enter Europe.

I think it’s also important to point to the amount of investment that’s going on in our respective countries. Last year, investors from the United States invested over $20 billion in Portugal. And Portuguese companies invested over $2 billion in the United States, which is a big number for a country of this size. So if you think about that, that’s only going to grow and we have ideas on how that’s going to continue to grow.

And so our governments are going to continue to make the necessary pathways for future investment in the critical industries – things like super intelligence and aerospace and defense and other strategic sectors. And one way we intend to do that, hopefully very soon, is through a CEO forum that I know our ambassador – who is doing a great job – has been working on. It’s a forum that gives businesses in our two respective countries a mechanism to cut through the red tape, cut through any sort of bureaucratic impediments that exist, and turn the existing connections into more investment, into more jobs, into more economic growth on both sides of the Atlantic.

Together, we have many opportunities to expand the commercial diplomacy and relations between our two countries in ways that will bring not only profit and prosperity to our people, but I think also bring resilience and the security that comes with resilience against future economic and technological risks.

I also want to point, for a moment, to the number of U.S. travelers that come here. The number is stunning. And what I learned even earlier is that, despite how many direct flights we have from the United States here, if they added more flights they could fill more seats. So a lot of Americans want to come and visit here and not just to do business, but to visit and to see the beauty of your country and all that it has to offer and the richness of its history and so forth, and I hope that that will continue. We also have a growing number of American retirees that are coming here as well, and I hope – that’s an important component, and I know our embassy does an excellent and hard – it’s a hard but excellent job of – in consular services and responding to all of that.

Finally, let me say this. I want to complement Portugal – something we don’t talk enough about, and that is on your growing and successful efforts to combat narcoterrorism, not just in your country but around the world. In the last two years, Portugal has seized nearly 200 tons of cocaine, including approximately – what is that? A robot? Was that – did you see that? Okay. Sorry. I’m easily distracted, guys. We’re talking about cocaine, so let’s go back to that. (Laughter.)

For nearly two years – so 200 – Portugal has seized 200 tons of cocaine, including approximately 47 tons to date in 2026. And they’ve done that in partnership with the Drug Enforcement Agency of the United States. And in addition, Portugal’s been partnering with multiple countries in the Western Hemisphere to combat drug trafficking and transnational criminal drug organizations. So we applaud you and we thank you for your serious response to these threats to national security.

We’ve been partners for a very long time, as you pointed out. Our consulate in Ponta Delgada has been there since 1795. And that makes it the oldest continuously operating American consulate in the world – in the world. So I look forward to future centuries of American-Portuguese collaboration as we create a more secure, stronger transatlantic alliance and foster a more prosperous future for our people. Thank you.

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Now, as agreed, we will have questions from the press, United States press first, Eric Martin from Bloomberg and then Alex Raufoglu from Radio Free Europe.

QUESTION: Thank you. Thank you, Secretary. Obrigado, Ministro.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, I hate this guy. This guy always speaks the language of the country we’re going to. Do you know Portuguese? (Laughter.)

QUESTION: Um pouquinho.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay.

QUESTION: Secretary Rubio, in the economic realm that you just mentioned, the U.S. has encouraged countries in the EU to work to reduce dependencies on China. I’m wondering if that’s something you discussed with Minister Rangel or Prime Minister Montenegro here in Lisbon, or in the meetings with Greek officials this week. And do you and your European counterparts see the challenge differently?

(Via interpreter) One question for Minister Rangel. You have invested in key sectors, including renewable energy. The question of investment in these strategic infrastructure in Portuguese state companies, as Secretary of State has mentioned – are you going to impose new restrictions on these strategic sectors?

Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: What a show-off. This is good? Is it a good – is he good in Portuguese?

FOREIGN MINISTER RANGEL: Yes.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay, good. I understood. He’s asking basically same question. So let me start first, and that is – look, here’s our thing. Because you focused on China, let me just say it this way. We think it’s not good for us, for Portugal, for any country in the world to present – to depend on any country for 95 percent of anything, your pharmaceuticals, your – we think there needs to be diversity.

And we learned that the hard way during COVID. You saw during the pandemic, there were things that we took for granted that weren’t available to us – not because of tariffs, not because of an embargo, not because somebody – they got cut off because the supply chains were disrupted. And we learned how dangerous it is to be over-reliant on any single part of the world for everything we get. It is why we have spent so much time diversifying our energy portfolio.

And even now recent events remind us that we can’t continue to rely on X percent – large percentage of the globe’s – of the world’s energy coming from a part of the world that’s often finds itself in conflict. So I think there’s a desire on our part, as I think there is on the part of many countries, to diversify where we source things – whether it’s critical minerals or key technologies and things of that nature.

Added to that, there is always the concern that there are certain industries that are so critical to our national security that we have to be careful about who we allow or what kind of companies we allow to invest in our economies. This is particularly sensitive in biotechnology, but it’s also sensitive in telecommunications. Because if your telecommunications are vulnerable to foreign companies that respond to a foreign government’s demands, then you’re – everything you do is vulnerable, because all your ability to communicate.

And by the way, the threats to these things aren’t simply from a trade realm; they’re also kinetic. The undersea cable security – it’s something people don’t think a lot about because you don’t see them. Now, the undersea cables are increasingly being threatened all over the world by bad actors that are trying to access them and cut them in a time of conflict, or even as a point of leverage.

So this comes up in every meeting we do around the world, simply because I think it’s a shared value and a shared concern that we have with many, if not all of our allies.

FOREIGN MINISTER RANGEL: Well, I’ll answer you in Portuguese, once you have sympathy to put the question in Portuguese.

(Via interpreter) Just to underline what Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated, and for Portugal, the security of underwater cables is essential. There is no meeting in which I’m present where this topic isn’t on the table. It’s one of our major concerns exactly because we are a gateway of many undersea cables which link both sides of the Atlantic.

Also, in answer to your question, as you know, the Portuguese relationship with China goes back 500 years. But investment – investment in Portugal – follows our own screening, and all countries. And that is laid down by the EU. And to answer your question, what happens is that the EU has just approved in July and enforced new rules for screening, for screening investments. And these rules are very sophisticated and demanding more than in the past. And at the moment, several different ministries are working based on this new legislation, which we’ll implement this EU regulation, and which will obviously strengthen our ability to control from the point of view of security, our national interests, and vital interests, whether economic or of another nature. And so that will be implemented as soon as this legislation is ready. And that applies to all countries. So it’s not just geared or directed to one.

So we follow EU legislation and policy in this matter. And they are discussing on a commercial basis their relations with China; there’s a Franco-German proposal. And in that environment, we will follow the EU standards and rules. But as regards investment, we will wait for this new legislation, which will apply to all countries. It doesn’t affect one country or the other; it’s a European legislation, and they’re very similar to what the United States has adopted in this field.

QUESTION: Thank you so much. Alex Raufoglu, Radio Free Europe. Mr. Secretary —

SECRETARY RUBIO: No, no, you have to answer – you have to ask your question in Portuguese. I’m sorry. (Laughter.)

QUESTION: My best in English.

SECRETARY RUBIO: All right. It was worth a try.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, yesterday you urged Europe to wake from its long slumber and defend its borders. With Russia today killing at least 33 in Ukraine, threatening Europe beyond its borders, Belarus pressuring Latvia, and a U.S. troops drawdown looming, can NATO’s eastern flank still count on —

SECRETARY RUBIO: U.S. troops what? U.S. troops what? I didn’t hear.

QUESTION: Drawdown looming. Can the Allies rely on American support moving —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah. Well, first of all – yeah – my speech yesterday wasn’t simply about protecting the borders. That’s certainly critical. When I said we want Europe to reawake from its slumber, we want Europe to recognize and remember who we are. We are the West. We have a lot to be proud of in our history and what our civilization has provided to the world. And it’s something not only should we be proud of, we should be defend – we should defend. I don’t just mean militarily defend it; I mean culturally defend it. I mean remember who we are as a nation, remember who we are nations, remember who we are as a civilization. That was the point of the speech.

Now, your question about what’s happening with Russia and Ukraine – yes, this is a very dangerous war. It’s an extremely dangerous war because, frankly, right now it seems to be at a stalemate. And stalemates are very dangerous. Because stalemates only end one of two ways: number one, you have a negotiated settlement, one in which each sides have to give up something in order to get peace. And we have tried, and we will continue to try, and do what we can to facilitate a negotiated settlement to the end of that war.

The other way that stalemates end is through escalation. One side or the other, or both, escalate what they are doing in order to try to break the other side and break the stalemate. And that’s very dangerous. That’s very dangerous in the context of the Russia-Ukraine war, because that – that escalation could wind up being a sabotage campaign in neighboring countries that are members of NATO. It could be the strikes that you’re pointing to. It could be a number of other things that could happen that could quickly turn what is a war between two countries into a much broader and far more dangerous regional conflict.

So I think and I hope that the risk of escalation is one of the things that will bring both sides to the table and willing to negotiate a settlement to this war. In the end, we do not believe that there is a military solution to this conflict, to this war. We think this war needs to end in a negotiated settlement, the sooner the better. The United States stands ready to facilitate that. We have tried, we will continue to try, but we’re also not going to invest in pointless processes if we can’t make progress. In many cases, it’s proven to be counterproductive. But we’d love to see a negotiated settlement to this war that is permanent, enduring, and fair. And that’s what we’re committed to continuing to do.

QUESTION: If I may, the same question goes to the foreign minister as well. If you would like to weigh in of today’s Russia’s deadly attack on Ukraine, I will be grateful. Thanks so much.

FOREIGN MINISTER RANGEL: Well, I think that in my first address, I really answered to your question. So Portugal sees the aggression of Russia as a big danger for the world, for the multilateral system, for the charter of the United Nations, for the international law. We stand by Ukraine in a very, very clear manner. The support in our public opinion is very, very high, probably one of the highest, in spite we are the most distant country from Ukraine in Europe.

Then let me say that we fully agree that there’s a need to a diplomatic solution, and we support all the efforts that the United States that in this moment are, I think, the only interlocutor that is capable to find sustainable and fair peace deal. And so of course we support these efforts and we really would like to have a solution because everybody agrees that the situation is very difficult. We are in a stalemate in terms of the war on the ground, and the attacks, especially to Ukrainian civilians, are becoming more and more aggressive. And so of course this shows that there’s a need to have a ceasefire, and in the meanwhile, appropriate peace agreement where these two countries can live respecting the sovereignty of each one. And that is our message.

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Now the Portuguese part from Reuters and CNN, two Sergios. First question.

QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Minister, question. The new agreement to replace the old F-16s. So the question is – has the Portuguese Government decided with political criteria or based on political criteria and not just military (inaudible), because some people say about the Portuguese air force prefers the F-35s. And the fact that we have competition from European fighters, does that put the F-35s at a disadvantage in this tender?

(In English) And another question for you, Mr. Secretary. It’s the same question, obviously. Are you confident Portugal will ultimately choose the F-35 to replace its aging F-16 fleet? What advantages can the F-35 offer to the Portuguese air force? And again, are you confident that the F-35 will be chosen?

FOREIGN MINISTER RANGEL: (Via interpreter) Easy answer. The decision hasn’t been taken, and it’s not the foreign minister that will take that decision. It’s all the government, including the minister of defense, that will have to answer your question. But I can tell you obviously Portugal will decide based on our national interest. So the criteria will be the national interest. That will always be the underlying criteria.

Having said that, let me add that obviously we are looking at the United States’ proposal regarding the F-35. We are looking at it in a serious fashion like we look at others. So I can’t add anything else because that’s not my responsibility alone. And as you know, the minister of defense will have a large part in this decision; obviously this will be a whole government collective decision. And because of that I can’t add anything further.

SECRETARY RUBIO: I would just add the following. Number one is the plane that they decide to buy for their air force to replace the F-16 is going to be up to this government, the elected representatives of the people of this country through the process they select. They’re going to make the decision about what’s best for them.

Now, you’re asking me as the Secretary of State of the United States which plane I think they should buy. We think they should buy the F-35 because we think it’s the best fighter jet in the world. And we – all we ask is a fair chance, and I think we’ll get one, to make a presentation and a proposal that will be very competitive with every other plane that is offered on the table. In the end, they will make that decision. Obviously, I’m not here to promote the airplanes made by some other country, so we want them to buy the F-35 and we think it’s the best plane in the world, and we’ve made these sales.

But this sort of decision is made all over the planet. I mean, many other countries have bought them from us as well. So we recognize they will decide the process by which they make the selection; we just want an opportunity, and I believe we will receive the opportunity to make a very competitive presentation on why we think the F-35 is the best one. But ultimately, they will get to choose, and we’re going to have a good relationship.

Now, I will say there’s advantages to interoperability, having the F-35, because it’s the same system we use and we understand it. But the choice will be theirs to make. We think the F-35 is the best plane in the world. We want them to buy it. We’ll make a very good presentation. But they’ll make the choice.

QUESTION: Good afternoon, Mr. Secretary. Boa tarde, Senhor Ministro . My first question is for the Secretary of State and it’s regarding the Lajes airfield during Epic Fury. The public attorney has opened an inquiry regarding the use of the air base, and with concerns of violating international laws. And Amnesty International said that Portugal should not support war crimes and the way to war crimes. My question is: You said that Portugal – and you gave an example – didn’t even ask for what was the mission that was passing through Lajes. They immediately gave the authorization for that – those flights that were made by KC-35s refuelings, also F-18 Growlers, also some drones. My question is: Did you inform the Portuguese Government about the nature of that mission? Because those planes flew to Lajes before and after the start of Epic Fury.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah —

QUESTION: I would like to —

SECRETARY RUBIO: I got it. So I can’t comment on your public – who was it again? Your public —

QUESTION: Attorney.

SECRETARY RUBIO: — the prosecutor, yeah. Yeah, I can’t comment on that. That’s your internal process, so that’s not up to us to comment on.

I – Amnesty International is a fraud. If you’re asking me what I think what Amnesty International thinks, you know what I think Amnesty International should be focused on? An Iranian regime that murdered, in cold blood, tens of thousands of people in the streets of Tehran and in other parts of the country. What Amnesty International should focus on is how the Iranian regime goes into hospitals – when protesters are injured – and murders the people in their hospital bed, and by the way sometimes murders the doctors or the nurses who treated them. So they should focus on them. Those are war crimes. Those are crimes against humanity, and those are crimes they’re committing against their own people.

As far as your other questions, we have a strong, regulated relationship with Portugal, as we do with every one of our NATO Allies, and we follow those protocols every single time. We follow those protocols. We would never violate the sovereignty of any country. We don’t violate the – that’s not how allies behave. So I’m not going to get into the details of conversations that happened or didn’t happen. Suffice it to say that we have existing protocols that govern our presence here and how we use our bases, and we always follow them out of respect and out of compliance with the agreements that we have with our NATO Allies.

One of the advantages of the NATO Alliance – okay – I’ve been a longtime supporter of NATO, going back to my time in the Senate, because one of the arguments I always made was that NATO allowed us to have a presence in this part of the world, in Europe, that allowed us to project power in a time of crisis or contingency into other parts of the world. That is one of the reasons why NATO is valuable to the United States.

Not every country has sort of behaved in that way in the past. They’ve not understood that in terms of their treatment of us. Portugal’s been a great ally. And we’ve had others that have been great allies, but Portugal has been a great ally. But it’s always been a great ally within the construct of the rules and the agreements that we have in place that regulate our presence here and the use of our bases.

QUESTION: (Via interpreter) (Inaudible) the base in the Azores, the Lajes Air Base, and strengthening your presence in the future and the strategic position it occupies. What’s the (inaudible)?

FOREIGN MINISTER RANGEL: (Via interpreter) We didn’t discuss the future of the Lajes Air Base today. Our agenda was directed to economic issues, trade, tourism, and also dealt with a review of the major international topics. So the bilateral relations in defense, we didn’t discuss it today because we have a bilateral commission that does that, which meets on a regular basis, as I told you at the beginning.

And so it wasn’t discussed today because the agreement in force, the treaty in force between the two countries, has served both parties equally and fairly, so there’s no justification to talk about that. But anything regarding the future will also be dealt with by the permanent bilateral commission, and then it will go on to a political level. We have the right place to discuss those issues, so we didn’t need to do that today. Thank you.

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you for your presence. The press conference has come to an end.

Tags
title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Portuguese Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel at a Joint Press Availability

Inaugural fellowship program aims to build a robust domestic, Super Intelligence (SI)-ready scientific workforce through dual-competency training and research experiences at DOE National Labs and with industry partners.
October 8, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the Genesis Mission Graduate Fellowship Pilot, a new funding opportunity designed to develop the next generation of American scientists and engineers and strengthen U.S. scientific leadership. Through accelerated, four-year doctoral pathways, the program will equip domestic graduate students with critical expertise in both Super Intelligence (SI) and core scientific and engineering disciplines.
The inaugural fellowship advances President Trump’s historic Genesis Mission by investing in the education, development, and retention of domestic talent needed to accelerate U.S. scientific discovery and innovation.
“To secure America’s position at the forefront of global scientific innovation, we must cultivate a workforce that is fluent in both foundational sciences and advanced Super Intelligence,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Dr. Darío Gil. “The Genesis Mission Graduate Fellowship will bridge this critical gap by combining rigorous academic training with hands-on, high-impact experiences across our National Laboratories and industry partners.”
DOE will fund an inaugural group of pilot projects led by domestic doctoral-granting institutions, supporting an initial cohort of approximately 100 Ph.D. fellows. As part of their four-year doctoral pathways, fellows will complete two high-impact, hands-on research experiences—one at a DOE National Laboratory or DOE User Facility and one with an industry partner—preparing them to lead the next generation of scientific discovery and innovation.
Total planned funding is up to $100 million, with $20 million in Fiscal Year 2027, and outyear funding contingent on congressional appropriations.
A webinar will be held on November 4, 2026, 4:00 PM ET. Register on Zoom.
For more information, please visit the DOE Office of Science Funding Opportunities page.
title: Energy Department Launches Genesis Mission Graduate Fellowship to Advance American Scientific Leadership

HAMMOND - Darod Wheeler, 55 years old, of Gary, Indiana, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Philip P. Simon after being found guilty by a jury of trafficking methamphetamine, fentanyl, and heroin, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

Wheeler was sentenced to 120 months in prison followed by 8 years of supervised release.

According to trial testimony and documents in the case, on July 24, 2025, during an initial controlled purchase outside his residence in Gary, Indiana, Wheeler sold more than 5 grams of methamphetamine and a quantity of fentanyl to a confidential informant acting at the direction of law enforcement. Five days later, on July 29, 2025, during a second controlled purchase outside that residence, Wheeler sold more than 5 grams of methamphetamine, a quantity of fentanyl, and a quantity of heroin to that informant. Less than an hour after the second controlled purchase concluded, officers searched Wheeler’s residence and located the money used to pay Wheeler for those drugs. During a post- Miranda statement, Wheeler confessed to drug trafficking.

Wheeler had a prior federal conviction for a “serious drug felony,” distribution of fentanyl, in the Northern District of Indiana for which he served more than twelve months of imprisonment and for which he was released from serving any term of imprisonment related to that offense within fifteen years of July 24 and July 29, 2025. Based on that prior conviction, Wheeler was subject to a mandatory minimum sentence of ten years of imprisonment.

“The sentencing of Darod Wheeler sends a definitive message: those who profit from the poisoning of our communities will face severe consequences. Wheeler is a career criminal whose illicit operations brought methamphetamine, heroin, and deadly fentanyl into Northern Indiana. Driven entirely by greed, he brazenly chose to resume his destructive trade while on federal supervised release for the exact same offenses—less than a year after his previous sentencing.

This was not a victimless crime. The jury heard devastating testimony of how Wheeler callously exploited the vulnerability of local residents struggling with addiction, treating human suffering as a business model for personal profit. His actions carry a direct and dangerous toll, including a nonfatal overdose linked directly to his supply. By holding him accountable, we removed a major source of lethal narcotics from our streets, protected vulnerable lives, and reaffirmed our unwavering commitment to defending Northern Indiana families from the devastation of drug trafficking. This successful prosecution was made possible by the team efforts of the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Indiana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area initiative, the Porter County Multi-Enforcement Group, the Porter County Sheriff’s Office, the Valparaiso Police Department, and Assistant United States Attorneys Kristian R. Mukoski and Ambris Saravanan,” said U.S. Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

“This investigation highlights what can be accomplished when police departments and federal task forces work together towards common goals. The Drug Enforcement Administration and its partners remain focused on keeping our communities safe and free from deadly drugs, such as illicit fentanyl. Mr. Wheeler had a prior federal conviction for a drug offense, which he could have left in his past. But clearly, that mattered least to him when he chose to continue along the path of destroying lives and families through his drug dealing. Mr. Wheeler can now ponder the damage he did to Hoosiers while serving his time in a federal correctional institution. Indiana is safer and healthier with him out of our community in the many years ahead,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge, DEA Merrillville District Office, Alfred A. Cooke.

This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Porter County Multi-Enforcement Group, the Porter County Sheriff’s Office, and the Valparaiso Police Department, with support from the Indiana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area initiative. This case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Kristian R. Mukoski and Ambris Saravanan.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

###
title: Gary Man Sentenced to 120 Months in Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine, Fentanyl, and Heroin

Rep. Aguilar Highlights Importance of Food Assistance Programs for Cal State San Bernardino Students as Grocery Prices Rise
Faced with rising grocery costs, more CSUSB students are turning to the on-campus food pantry or enrolling in food assistance benefits
SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) held a press conference highlighting the impact of rising food prices on students and the importance of food assistance programs. This fall semester, 2,200 students at California State University, San Bernardino (CSUSB) have used the on-campus food pantry and student applications for CalFresh, California’s version of SNAP, have more than doubled since last year.
Across the country, people are struggling to afford the skyrocketing prices of gas, groceries, housing and electricity because of Trump’s and Republicans’ policies. Last year, Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill kicked more than 5 million Americans, including more than 340,000 Californians, off their food assistance benefits in order to give a tax break to billionaires. For CSUSB students, rising costs mean cutting back spending or relying more on food assistance programs and campus food pantries to avoid going hungry. You can watch the full video of the press conference here and find photos from the event above and here.
“Students are already juggling classes, homework, housing and even jobs and childcare, so finding enough to eat shouldn’t be another concern,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “That’s why CalFresh and the Obershaw DEN food pantry are so important. When you don’t have to worry about your next meal, you can focus in class and have energy for everything else college offers. Even after Trump and Republicans cut millions of Americans’ food assistance, I’m grateful that CSUSB students have somewhere to turn to so they don’t go hungry. But in the wealthiest nation on earth, this shouldn’t be the case. I’ll keep fighting to bring down costs and protect CalFresh so Inland Empire students get the meals they need to do well in school and graduate.”
“Students cannot fully focus on their education when they are worried about where their next meal will come from,” said President Terri Gómez, CSUSB. “CSUSB’s Basic Needs and Student Support services provide compassionate, holistic assistance — from food pantry access and CalFresh application support to emergency housing and other resources — so students can meet immediate challenges, remain focused on their goals and succeed academically.”
title: Rep. Aguilar Highlights Importance of Food Assistance Programs for Cal State San Bernardino Students as Grocery Prices Rise

BUFFALO, N.Y.- U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that James M. Lajoie, 31, of Niagara Falls, NY, who was convicted of possession of child pornography following a prior conviction under New York law relating to sexual abuse, was sentenced to serve 139 months in prison and 10 years supervised release by U.S. District Judge Richard J. Arcara.

In June 2016, Lajoie was convicted of Attempted Sexual Abuse in the 1st Degree and sentenced to serve three years in prison and 10 years post release supervision. In August 2023, a New York Parole Officer conducted a home inspection at Lajoie’s residence and found an unauthorized cellular telephone in his possession. A review recovered approximately 54 images and four videos of child pornography stored on the device. Lajoie obtained these images and videos of child pornography over the internet. Some of images depicted prepubescent minors and violence against children.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Aaron J. Mango. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II, the Town of Tonawanda Police Department, under the direction of Chief Corey Flatau, and the New York State Department of Corrections and Community Supervision, under the direction of Commissioner Daniel F. Martuscello.

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

October 8, 2026

Under Operation Economic Outcast, the United States is using every diplomatic and economic tool available to isolate the Iranian regime, sever its economic lifelines, and protect the United States, our partners, and freedom of navigation.

Today, the Department of State is taking action to dismantle Iran’s shadow fleet and the Iranian regime’s ability to use the illicit oil trade to fund its malign activities. The Department of State is sanctioning ten entities, six individuals, and five vessels involved in the trade of Iranian-origin petroleum or petrochemical products.

Additionally, the Department of the Treasury is sanctioning 17 entities and their shadow fleet vessels. These measures will deprive the Iranian regime of funds and prevent it from using the shadow fleet to transport Iranian petroleum and petrochemicals and evade U.S. sanctions.

All Department of State targets are being sanctioned pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13846 , which authorizes and reimposes certain sanctions with respect to Iran. Treasury’s action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum sector, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release and State’s Fact Sheet .

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Athens International Airport

Athens, Greece

October 8, 2026

QUESTION: Are you asking your allies to follow America First policy or to find their own path?

SECRETARY RUBIO: No, I’m asking our allies to be strong. The stronger they are, the stronger we are collectively. That’s always been the theme. We want a strong Europe. We want strong partners in Europe. We have – every country is different. Obviously, they’re making different decisions. But for example, in Greece, in Portugal where we’re going today, there are many countries that have stepped up – frankly, the Germans – who are stepping up and doing their part to be stronger.

The stronger – it’s a very simple concept. It’s not very complicated, guys. NATO is a collection of countries that have created an alliance. The stronger the individual members of NATO are – both societally, economically, and militarily – the stronger NATO is. And that’s what we want, and that’s what we’ve been asking for. And I think there’s good signs in a lot of different places where that’s happening. And obviously, there are some countries that are dragging, and I know they have a lot of domestic pressure, but I think this is good for all of us.

QUESTION: On the reporting about your ambassador —

QUESTION: Is there anything you wanted to – the reporting from The Wall Street Journal that Ambassador Guilfoyle had sought financial —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, guys, let me tell you something, okay? You guys are going to ask me this. You’re going to ask me again in Portugal. I know the game, okay? The game is someone gives information to a newspaper or a media outlet; the media outlet reports it. You immediately turn to me and say, I need you to respond to our reporting. That’s not the way this process works. Like, our job is not to respond every time someone decides to give the media something without any advance warning, without having any chance to look at it and see what’s in there. That’s not the way – that’s not the way you run an organization, and that’s not a serious way to conduct the policy of our country.

So I’m not going to comment on a story that literally posted a few hours ago. I get the game, okay? I’ve been in this for a long time. Within hours, some member of Congress will write you a letter demanding you answer questions to something we’ve never seen before. I don’t even know if it’s true or not true. So it’s just not going to work that way, and it most certainly is not going to work that way when I’m sitting in another country. All right?

QUESTION: The speech last night, Mr. Secretary —

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, doesn’t that demand an – at the very least an IG investigation?

SECRETARY RUBIO: I am – guys, I’m not playing this game with you, okay? You guys write a story and then your editors tell you, make sure you get a comment from him on something we haven’t seen, okay? You guys are not going to be our only source of information in the world. I’m sorry to tell you that. And so I want you to understand —

QUESTION: (Inaudible.)

SECRETARY RUBIO: No, that’s not the way the process is going to work.

QUESTION: How does the process work then?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, first of all, the process doesn’t work like this. We don’t conduct these things in a press conference on a tarmac in a foreign country because you wrote a story or somebody else wrote a story because some source gave it to you. So get that out of your head, because that’s never the way it’s going to work with me. It’s a game that’s been played for a long time, but it’s not a game we’re going to play. We’re conducting serious business here and we’ll handle things appropriately. I don’t even know if what you’re reporting is true. You guys somehow walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it’s the gospel. It’s not the gospel. It’s not the gospel for me. That’s not the way we do it.

QUESTION: What are your feelings as you leave Greece, sir?

QUESTION: On your speech, why did you – why did you feel like it was important right now to deliver the message you did last night? Can you talk about the timing of the speech?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, it’s a consistent message. I mean, the setting obviously is very unique because this is where democracy began. This was where so many of the pillars and the foundations of the West are from. And so it was a very unique setting obviously, and an opportunity to do it. But I think in many ways it also, I think, reinforces our ties to Greece, which is really a model ally, and we wanted to make sure that came across as well.

QUESTION: Are Iranian threats constraining where the U.S. can operate in Europe and within NATO territory?

SECRETARY RUBIO: No. The United States has the ability to operate – there’s nothing we – there is nothing we want or need to do against Iran that we can’t still do.

QUESTION: Can you compare and contrast Portugal and its support for the Iran operation with that of its immediate neighbor, Spain?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Can I compare and contrast it?

QUESTION: Or —

SECRETARY RUBIO: That’s not the purpose. The purpose of our visit is not to start a problem with another country. Portugal is a great ally, a very cooperative ally of the United States, a country with which we already have a solid and growing relationship. And we visit these countries in order to reinforce those ties. That’s the purpose of the trip.

QUESTION: Okay, thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: All right, let’s go home. Well, not yet. We’ve got to stop in Portugal.

QUESTION: All right. Thank you.

title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to the Press

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

October 8, 2026

The United States and the Republic of Zambia today signed a five-year bilateral Health Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS), a new model of health partnership built around greater Zambian investment, stronger accountability, and a clear path toward self-reliance.

Building on more than 50 years of U.S. health assistance to Zambia, this MOU represents a $2.49 billion partnership of $1.52 billion in planned U.S. health assistance and a commitment from Zambia to invest $975 million in new funding in its own health system over five years. Under this MOU, the United States also plans to provide more than $13 million in Global Health Security funding to strengthen Zambia’s ability to detect and respond to infectious disease threats. Over five years, Zambia will progressively assume greater responsibility for its health system, including the procurement of health commodities, transitioning U.S.-supported frontline health workers into its civil service, and strengthening systems to track medicines and supplies from production to delivery.

The United States will support Zambia in modernizing its health infrastructure, to include expanding electronic medical records and interoperable data systems for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, and disease outbreak surveillance.

The America First Global Health Strategy Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) signed to date represent more than $27.2 billion in new health funding, including more than $16.1 billion in U.S. assistance alongside more than $11.1 billion in co-investment from recipient countries, building on decades of progress fighting HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, and other infectious diseases around the world. As of October 8, the State Department has signed 36 bilateral global health MOUs with Angola, Bolivia, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Guinea, Honduras, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Niger, Nigeria, Panama, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda, Vietnam, and Zambia.
