BLM Streamlines Winter Exploration in Alaska’s National Petroleum Reserve
Organization:
Media Contact:
ANCHORAGE, Alaska — Today, the Bureau of Land Management established a categorical exclusion to improve predictability and reduce burdens for companies seeking permits for wintertime oil and gas exploration in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska. This action enables important winter exploration projects—such as exploratory seismic surveys, exploration wells, and plugging and abandonment— to move forward efficiently, advancing American Energy Dominance and national security.
The BLM developed this categorical exclusion after analyzing the dozens of previous environmental assessments the agency has conducted for wintertime exploration in the Petroleum Reserve. Those analyses show that those exploration activities result in no significant impacts on human health or the environment when conducted under established operating procedures and mitigation measures. Wintertime exploration relies on temporary ice roads, ice pads, and snow routes where the only potential sign of exploration after the snow melts is generally the well-head, if drilled.
“The BLM has decades of experience analyzing the effects of exploration in the Petroleum Reserve and permitting responsible exploration,” said BLM Alaska State Director Kevin Pendergast. “This categorical exclusion builds on that record to allow developers to more nimbly locate energy resources in the Petroleum Reserve, ultimately increasing domestic energy supply, leading to stable energy costs and more revenue for Alaskan communities and the American public.”
Categorical exclusions are categories of actions that have been determined to not typically result in significant environmental impacts, eliminating the need conduct a full environmental review. Streamlining National Environmental Policy Act compliance through categorical exclusions removes regulatory burdens and speeds up the process, saving time, and resources.
Before relying on a categorical exclusion for a proposed project, an agency must verify that there are no extraordinary circumstances, such as potential impacts to endangered species or cultural resources, that may result in the project having any significant environmental effects.
This new categorical exclusion supports the goals of Executive Order 14153, “Unleashing Alaska’s Extraordinary Resource Potential,” Executive Order 14154, “Unleashing American Energy,” and the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. The action builds on the BLM’s extensive work to improve regulatory certainty in the Petroleum Reserve, including rescission of the 2024 rule that restricted leasing and development in the Petroleum Reserve and reopening nearly 82% of the area to oil and gas leasing through an updated Integrated Activity Plan. It also complements BLM’s ongoing work to streamline permitting for qualifying production sites in the area.
About 3.5 million acres are currently leased in the Petroleum Reserve following the historic lease sale held in March 2026. That sale resulted in 187 tracts receiving bids and $163,696,722 in total receipts, generating the most revenue ever, the most tracts receiving bids and the second most acreage sold in a single sale for the area.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM Streamlines Winter Exploration in Alaska’s National Petroleum Reserve

text:
RELEASE: Squeezed by High Costs, Gottheimer Hosts Agriculture Roundtable with Sussex County Farmers
Farmers Hit with by High Diesel, Fertilizer, Equipment Costs, Tariffs, and Losses from Winter Freeze Announces New FROST Relief Act to Help Farmers Recover from April Freeze Outlines Farm Bill Priorities to Lower Costs, Help Specialty Crops and Give Farmers Certainty Continued Support for 4-H, FFA, and the Next Generation of Agriculture Leaders
Above: Gottheimer hosts agriculture roundtable.
AUGUSTA, NJ — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted an agriculture roundtable with farmers from across New Jersey’s Fifth District to hear how rising diesel, fertilizer, and equipment costs, low dairy prices, and a shrinking number of farms in the Garden State are putting family farms under pressure, along with concerns about fewer cooperative plants and fewer meat processing facilities, and concerns about shrinking access to milk haulers. Gottheimer also laid out his priorities for the final Farm Bill, focusing on specialty crops, dairy, and agritourism, and asked farmers what they need to see in the final bill.
“It’s because of all of you, and the more than 1,000 farms in New Jersey’s Fifth District, that families across our state and nation have fresh, high-quality, nutritious meals on the table,” said Gottheimer (NJ-5). “You do your part, every single day, rain or shine. The question for Washington is whether they’re doing everything they can for you. And right now, the clearest test of that is the Farm Bill.”
Farmers are getting squeezed from every direction. For a family farm already running on razor-thin margins, those costs add up fast. When it costs more to fuel the tractor, buy supplies, and get the crop to market, even a good harvest may not be enough.
Then came the freeze. Last April, a hard freeze hit right as crops were budding and blooming. Many growers lost a huge share of their harvest, including peaches, cherries, apples, strawberries, blueberries, and more, adding up to estimated losses of $300 million. For too many farmers, the help has not been there. New Jersey’s Fifth District is home to more than 1,000 farms, and New Jersey is a top-ten specialty crop state. Right now, a specialty crop grower can lose a season to a freeze and find that crop insurance does not fit the risk.
Meanwhile, the Farm Bill, which last became law in 2018, has been kicked down the road with one extension after another, leaving farmers unable to plan their planting season, equipment purchases, or hiring.
At the roundtable, he announced the Farmer Recovery Opportunity and Support for Temperatures (FROST) Relief Act, new federal legislation to help growers recover from the April freeze that caused an estimated $300 million in losses.
The FROST Relief Act and the TEMP Act will:
- Create a Block Grant Program for Freeze Losses: The FROST Relief Act would create a block grant program for farmers in the 13 states hit by the April freeze: Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia.
- Get Resources to Farmers Without Red Tape: The money goes to the states that were hit, so it can reach the farmers who lost their crops without months of red tape.
- Develop Temperature-Based Crop Insurance: The TEMP Act directs federal crop insurance to develop an affordable, temperature-based policy that covers freeze and cold-weather losses for specialty crop growers.
Gottheimer’s additional actions:
- Fight to Expand Rural Eligibility: In April, Gottheimer offered an amendment to the Farm Bill to raise the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) population cap for “rural” eligibility from 20,000 to 50,000, so more North Jersey communities can qualify for broadband and infrastructure support. It did not make it into the House bill, and it remains a top priority for the final bill.
- End the Hiring Freeze at the Farm Service Agency: Gottheimer offered amendments to end the hiring freeze at the Farm Service Agency (FSA), so loans and assistance get processed faster, especially for new and beginning farmers.
- Restore Local Food Resources: The Administration cut more than $1 billion from the Local Food for Schools and Local Food Purchase Assistance programs. Because of those cuts, New Jersey lost $26 million in commitments that would have supported 46 local farms and food producers, including 11 in the Fifth District. Gottheimer has demanded the resources be restored and offered a Farm Bill amendment to do it.
- Fix the SNAP Provisions in the House Bill: As written, the House bill would force New Jersey to cover 5 percent of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and raise the state’s share of administrative costs, adding up to $200 million a year in new costs for Jersey taxpayers. It would also push families off SNAP, stripping their children of automatic eligibility for free school meals. Gottheimer is urging the Senate to fix it, and he introduced the Feed Our Kids Act, which would provide free school meals to every student and push schools to buy nutritious food locally when they can.
- Back Specialty Crops and Rural Communities: Gottheimer is backing more resources for the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program, more help fighting invasive species including the spotted lanternfly, more investment for meat and poultry processors, and reliable, affordable broadband for rural communities.
- Stand Up for Jersey Dairy Farmers: After farmers raised the issue at a previous roundtable, Gottheimer backed whole milk in schools, and the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act was signed into law in January. He is also a member of the Dairy Caucus, so he can continue working across the aisle on commonsense solutions for dairy producers and sellers.
- Support the Next Generation of Jersey Agriculture: Ahead of National 4-H Week, celebrated annually during the first full week of October, Gottheimer reaffirmed his support for 4-H and USDA’s Positive Youth Development programs.
- Lower Costs and Go After Price Collusion: Gottheimer is pushing an All-of-the-Above Energy Plan to boost domestic capacity and bring down diesel and fertilizer costs, and he helped pass legislation to go after meat and poultry companies that collude to rig prices on the backs of hard-working families.
Gottheimer was joined by Ed Wengryn, New Jersey Secretary of Agriculture; Senator Parker Space, LD24 Senator; Louis Crescitelli, Chief of Staff to Senator Space; Commissioner Alan Henderson, Sussex County Commissioner; Commissioner Jill Space, Sussex Director Board of County Commissioners; Ken Schwemmer, Confidential Assistant to Commissioners; Liz Thompson, NJ Farm Bureau Executive Director; Paul Hlubik, USDA NJ Farm Service Agency State Committee Chair and NJ Agricultural Society President; Dave Foord, 4-H Senior Program Coordinator, RCE Sussex County, State 4-H Enrollment Coordinator; Holly Systema, Member of New Jersey State Board of Agriculture and the owner of The Farm at Windy Flats; Rocky Hazelman, President of the Passaic County Board of Agriculture and the Chairman of the Passaic County Agriculture Development Board; Stacey Kennedy, NJ Agricultural Society Director; Joe Atchison III, NJ Department of Agriculture Assistant Secretary and NJ Department of Agriculture Marketing and Development Director; Mike Burger, Sussex County Board of Agriculture President; Lindsay Caragher, USDA NJ Farm Service Agency Deputy State Executive Director; Rich Byma, Dairy Farmer at By-Acre Holsteins; Phil and Keri Brodhecker, Beef and Grain Farmers at Brodhecker Farms; Jason Swarts, Dairy Farmer for Deckertown Holsteins; Pete Southway, Springhouse Creamery; Mitchell Jones, Mountain Top Farm in Warren County.
Below: Gottheimer hosts agriculture roundtable.

WASHINGTON, D.C./October 8, 2026 – A whistleblower disclosure to the U.S. Office of Special Counsel (OSC) has prompted the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to restore its coordination function, provide training, and update its procedures for tax filings tied to foreign ownership of U.S. real estate.
The disclosure concerned tax filings related to the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980 (FIRPTA). When a foreign person sells a U.S. real property interest, the buyer generally must withhold tax—ordinarily 15 percent of the amount realized—unless a reduced rate or an exception applies or the IRS issues a withholding certificate reducing or eliminating withholding. The IRS’s Ogden, Utah, team processes applications for FIRPTA withholding certificates as well as a cluster of related filings. IRS employees refer to this group of related submissions as “Weird FIRPTA.”
The whistleblower alleged that, after a specialized international-tax unit in Cincinnati was dissolved about 16 years ago, the IRS assigned this work to tax examiners in Ogden without sufficient training or a functioning FIRPTA coordinator, contrary to the Internal Revenue Manual. The whistleblower also reported that, as of February 26, 2026, the team had 7,435 related filings awaiting processing and that its principal written guidance was a three-page job aid issued in 2014.
OSC referred the disclosure to the Secretary of the Treasury. The Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) concluded that the work was appropriately within the Ogden team’s authority but confirmed the operational gaps. The previous FIRPTA coordinator retired in March 2025. The employee who subsequently assumed the role had not received training and was not widely known to examiners as a technical resource. The IRS had no formal training program for several types of FIRPTA-related work, and examiners relied on informal instruction and the 2014 job aid. TIGTA confirmed the backlog of unprocessed FIRPTA-related submissions and found that the IRS lacked an official system for tracking the inventory. Because some submissions had not been processed for more than a year, TIGTA could not determine whether required withholdings, penalties, or interest went uncollected.
In June 2026, after TIGTA identified the coordination gap, the IRS designated a FIRPTA coordinator and a backup and began providing training and resource materials. The IRS updated Internal Revenue Manual section 21.8.5. It also stated that it would incorporate the updated guidance into examiner training by October 31, 2026, revise related taxpayer correspondence, and address the outstanding inventory. TIGTA’s Office of Audit plans to review applications to reduce FIRPTA withholdings and related submissions in fiscal year 2027.
“OSC thanks the whistleblower for bringing a detailed disclosure that identified longstanding gaps in FIRPTA coordination and training,” said Special Counsel Charles Baldis. “We also appreciate that Treasury appears to be taking this issue seriously and that the IRS has taken steps to restore the coordination function, update its manual, and schedule the needed training. This is the kind of outcome that the whistleblower disclosure process is intended to produce.”
title: Whistleblower Disclosure Leads to Restored IRS Oversight of Tax Filings Related to Foreign Ownership of U.S. Real Property

Gov Watchdog Finds Geothermal Developers Lack Permitting Tools Oil and Gas Companies Already Have
Washington, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a new report showing that companies trying to build geothermal power on public lands lack basic permitting tools that oil and gas companies already have and face confusing rules with no way to see where their permits stand, even as demand for geothermal development has grown more than fortyfold since 2020.
The watchdog report, requested by U.S. House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Susie Lee (D-Nev.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) found that the permitting process can be inconsistent and lacks transparency, creating uncertainty for geothermal developers and federal land managers. Oil and gas companies file permits online, track them through a dedicated system, and work from public handbooks, while geothermal developers submit permit applications in writing, wait on unpublished handbooks, and have no system tracking their permits.
The report comes as Congress has shown bipartisan interest in expanding geothermal energy development and private-sector interest in federal lands has grown significantly. According to GAO, nominations of federal lands for geothermal development increased from approximately 25,000 acres in 2020 to more than one million acres in 2025.
Despite this growing interest, geothermal developers reported to GAO inconsistent permitting decisions for exploration activities. BLM has developed handbooks intended to clarify terminology and provide consistent guidance, but those documents have remained in draft form since at least 2022. 
GAO also found that BLM lacks a comprehensive mechanism for tracking geothermal permitting activity. BLM shut down its geothermal tracking system in 2021, and the system that took its place has no way to track geothermal permits. Oil and gas wells, however, are tracked in a dedicated system from initial permitting through final closure. As a result, BLM has limited visibility into permitting timelines and workloads, making planning more difficult for both developers and federal officials to anticipate project timelines and resource needs.
The House has already voted to address these problems. The bipartisan Geothermal Energy Advancement Act (H.R. 5631), which passed the House in June, includes legislation sponsored by Rep. Lee, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, and Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.). Rep. Ansari’s Geothermal Gold Book Development Act would require the Bureau to publish standard permitting procedures, in line with GAO’s recommendation.
Read the full report and recommendations here.

Congressman Krishnamoorthi to Honor Captain Smit Machchhar in Congressional Record for His Heroism During Flydubai Hijacking Attempt
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) announced today that he will enter a statement into the Congressional Record on Friday honoring Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery aboard Flydubai Flight 1073 on September 30, 2026. After being attacked by the flight’s first officer, who attempted to seize control of the aircraft, Captain Machchhar’s actions helped save the lives of 172 passengers and his fellow crew members.
Congressman Krishnamoorthi’s full statement follows:
“Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize Captain Smit Machchhar of India, a husband, father, and pilot with 17 years of flying experience, including 11 as a captain, whose extraordinary bravery on September 30, 2026, helped save the lives of 172 passengers and his fellow crew members aboard Flydubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, including 4 United States citizens and 27 children.
Midway through the flight, the first officer attacked Captain Machchhar with the aircraft's emergency crash axe and attempted to seize the flight controls. The aircraft plunged approximately 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds. Despite grave injuries, Captain Machchhar fought his way to the cockpit door and opened it, allowing passengers and crew members to enter and overpower his attacker. Two reserve Flydubai pilots traveling aboard the aircraft then took control and landed it safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
Even as Captain Machchhar fought for his own life, he understood that the lives of everyone aboard depended on what he did next. Despite his injuries, his years of experience told him that the aircraft was going down, and he found the strength to reach that door. His presence of mind, determination, and courage gave the passengers and crew the chance they needed to stop the attack and avert a catastrophe.
Behind every person aboard Flight 1073 is a family that was spared an unimaginable loss. Because Captain Machchhar refused to give up, the passengers and crew aboard that aircraft had the chance to return to the people who love them.
Mr. Speaker, I ask my colleagues to join me in honoring Captain Smit Machchhar, whose extraordinary courage helped save hundreds of lives aboard Flight 1073. We extend our warmest wishes to him, his wife Sonal, their two children, and their entire family, and we hope for the captain’s full-speed recovery from his injuries at the earliest.”
Congressman Krishnamoorthi’s Congressional Record Entry is available here.
title: Congressman Krishnamoorthi to Honor Captain Smit Machchhar in Congressional Record for His Heroism During Flydubai Hijacking Attempt

Spirit Airlines to Sell Employee Data to Train Google AI, Horsford and Warren Lead Call for Worker Privacy Protections
NORTH LAS VEGAS – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Elizabeth Warren led 119 Members of Congress in a letter to Spirit Airlines CEO, Dave Davis, and Google CEO, Sundar Piachi, urging the companies to protect the privacy of thousands of former Spirit employees. The letter responds to the proposed $10 million sale of Spirit’s internal data to Google for the purpose of training artificial intelligence systems.
Court findings revealed that the proposed sale would include approximately 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages, employee records, timecards records, payroll and tax information, and employment contracts. Workers created and provided this information as a condition of their employment, and it may contain highly sensitive details, including medical information and accommodation requests.
“Spirit’s workers handed over this information because their jobs required it, not so it could be sold to train a different company’s AI,” said Rep. Horsford. “In Las Vegas alone, nearly 1,000 people were laid off from Spirit. They should not have to worry about their payroll records, disciplinary files, and private messages being used by a company they never worked for. Innovation cannot come at the expense of workers’ privacy, and no employee data should move until real, enforceable safeguards are in place.”
"Spirit Flight Attendants and other former employees are on the tip of the spear of this new threat to workers' rights," said Sara Nelson, president of the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, representing 55,000 Flight Attendants at 20 airlines including Spirit." Senator Warren, Representative Horsford and 119 of their colleagues, with very little time and without either chamber in session, acted quickly to urge protections for workers as they face immediate risk in the bankruptcy court. But the outcome of conditions on this proposed sale to Google carries tremendous implications for workers across the economy. We thank the lawmakers for their swift action in their oversight role, as they recognize the immediate concern for our Spirit members. Flight Attendants across the industry and workers across the economy also thank them for recognizing the dangerous precedent it could set in this new frontier of unregulated AI and the intrusion of privacy for all Americans."
“Spirit Airlines workers deserve better than having their private information become a bargaining chip in a $10 million AI data deal. We are demanding that Spirit and Google exclude employee information wherever possible and keep confidential safety reporting out of this transaction. Removing names is not enough—workers deserve a voice in the safeguards and enforceable protection against profiling or misuse of their information. The IAM Union is at the forefront of protecting workers in the age of AI and big data, and we will keep fighting to ensure new technology respects our members’ rights, privacy and dignity,” said IAM Union Air Transport Territory General Vice President Richie Johnsen.
Google has stated it will not receive personally identifiable information and that the data will undergo third-party scrubbing before transfer. The Members warn that removing names, email addresses, and other direct identifiers does not necessarily make a dataset anonymous, particularly when modern AI systems can identify patterns across large datasets and connect seemingly unrelated pieces of information. The National Institute of Standards and Technology has recognized that de-identified data can be re-identified in certain circumstances.
“Spirit Airlines caused economic damage to workers, and now they are trying to hurt them even more by sharing sensitive data without proper safeguards," Transport Workers Union of America International President John Samuelsen said. "The least Spirit can do as it settles debts and gives Big Tech more data to train their AI models is to fully protect workers who gave years of hard work to the airline.”
This letter urges Google and Spirit to take specific actions before employee-related information is approved for transfer: exclude employee information from the transaction to the greatest extent possible, including records, timecards, payroll information, and Microsoft 365 content containing flight attendant information; establish a meaningful de-identification protocol developed with input from affected workers; maintain heightened protections for sensitive records such as disciplinary files, medical or accommodation requests, and compensation information, even after de-identification; conduct an independent employee confidentiality review and set enforceable limits on downstream use, disclosure, retention, and transfer; and establish a former review protocol that expressly prohibits using the data to identify, profile, evaluate, or draw inferences about identifiable groups of workers.
"As the nation’s largest transportation labor federation, we represent hundreds of thousands of workers who build, operate, and maintain transportation network across the United States," said Greg Regan, President of the Transportation Trades Department, AFL-CIO (TTD). "As our society confronts a new technology era, regulators, legislators, and organizations have a responsibility to set guardrails around its use. That includes privacy guardrails for employee data that is collected by employers and whether this sensitive information can be transferred or sold to another party. Employers are entrusted with highly sensitive employee records and communications, and workers deserve to have their data protected instead of being exposed to privacy risks. We commend Congressman Horsford and Senator Warren for leading this letter urging Spirit and Google to commit to guidelines for handling sensitive employee information if a data transfer occurs."
"Spirit's workers shared personal information because their jobs required it, not so it could be sold to train AI," said Capt. Jason Ambrosi, President of ALPA. "Our safety system works because pilots and other airline workers trust that when they speak up, it stays confidential. Break that trust and people stop reporting. We thank Senator Warren and Representative Horsford and dozens of Members of Congress for acting quickly to seek answers before this sale is final. Google and Spirit must put real, enforceable protections in place before a single employee record changes hands."
The Members are calling for no employee-related information to be transferred until protections are in place to ensure that workers’ sensitive information cannot be identified, profiled, or misused.
The full text of the letter can be found HERE.
119 members co-signed the letter with Rep. Horsford and Senator Warren, including Reps. Amo, Ansari, Barragán, Bell, Blair, Bonamici, Boyle, Brownley, Brown, Budzinski, Carson, Carter (GA), Casar, Castor, Chu, Clarke, Cohen, Conaway, Courtney, Craig, Crockett, Davids, Davis (IL), Davis (NC), DelBene, Deluzio, DeSaulnier, Dexter, Dingell, Elfreth, Espaillat, Fitzpatrick, Fletcher, Foster, Foushee, Frankel, Frost, Garamendi, García (IL), Garcia (CA), Garcia (FL), Goldman, Gomez, Grijalva, Hernández, Hoyle, Huffman, Jackson (IL), Jacobs, Jayapal, Johnson (GA), Kamlager-Dove, Kaptur, Kennedy, Khanna, Krishnamoorthi, Landsman, Larsen, Lee (PA), Lee (NV), Levin, Lieu, Lynch, Magaziner, Matsui, McBath, McClain Delaney, McClellan, McGovern, Mejia, Menefee, Meng, Mfume, Morrison, Norcross, Norton, Ocasio-Cortez, Omar, Pappas, Pingree, Pocan, Pou, Ramirez, Ryan, Sánchez, Schakowsky, Sherman, Simon, Stansbury, Stevens, Strickland, Takano, Thanedar, Thompson (MS), Titus, Tlaib, Tonko, Torres (NY), Trahan, Vargas, Velázquez, Walkinshaw, Warnock, Wasserman Schultz, Waters, Watson Coleman, Williams, Wilson, and Sens. Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Cantwell, Cortez Masto, Duckworth, Kelly, Markey, Merkley, Sanders, Slotkin, Van Hollen, and Warnock

SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, released the following statement regarding the Trump administration’s actions to suspend Microsoft’s ability to sponsor workers through the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program.
“This is a crucial issue for me as the top Democrat on the Immigration Subcommittee, the only member of Congress to have actually had an H-1B visa, and the Representative for tens of thousands of Microsoft workers. The administration has been consistently working to take away legal pathways for immigrants to contribute their talents to our country, and this is yet another of those attacks.
“The PERM program is the first step toward an employment-based green card for countless workers who want to contribute to this country, and it lays out a clear process with steps to ensure that this is a net benefit to our economy and does not harm American jobs. Our economy, our communities, and our families depend on immigrants in many sectors, including the tech sector, and heavy-handed attacks like this only hurt efforts to build a strong, stable, and diverse base of workers who have legal pathways to come and be in the United States while also protecting U.S. workers from unscrupulous employers.
“You don’t fix a broken immigration system by taking a hammer to legal immigration. Microsoft has been a leader in advocating for comprehensive immigration reforms that modernize an antiquated immigration system and provide more — not fewer — legal pathways for immigrants from all over the world to work here and be with their families. Targeting Microsoft or the PERM program in this way simply undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate.”
title: Jayapal Statement on Trump Suspending Microsoft from the PERM Program

text:
BLM’s Third Quarter Oil, Gas and Geothermal Sales Generate Nearly $400 Million in Revenue
Organization:
Media Contact:
WASHINGTON — The Bureau of Land Management generated nearly $400 million in total receipts from oil, gas and geothermal sales held in the third quarter of 2026. These revenues reflect the Trump administration’s ongoing focus on unleashing domestic energy and supporting job growth, and promoting efficient, streamlined permitting and leasing processes.
“This quarter’s sales demonstrate our unwavering commitment to fostering American energy dominance and reducing reliance on foreign resources, in a transparent and balanced way that considers community needs,” said BLM Director Steve Pearce. “By building on the commonsense, pro-growth policies of the Trump administration, we’re ensuring that we strengthen the partnership between BLM and the energy sector for the benefit of the American people.”
Oil and Gas
From July through September 2026, BLM oil and gas lease sales generated $372.1 million. The sales were held in Montana/Dakotas, New Mexico, Wyoming, Colorado, Eastern States, Nevada, and Utah, offering a total of 344 parcels across 293,963 acres. BLM sales have generated $5.1 billion in 2026, with first quarter sales of $592.7 million from January through March, and second quarter sales of $4.1 billion. A record second-quarter oil and gas lease sale in May generated more than $4 billion in total receipts in New Mexico and Texas, underscoring strong industry demand for domestic energy development on public lands. In that sale, the BLM sold 74 parcels on 33,530 acres.
The combined bonus bids and rentals from the leases will be distributed between the federal government and the states where the parcels are located. Oil, gas, and geothermal lease sales support domestic energy production and American energy independence while contributing to the nation’s economic and military security. Consistent with Executive Order 14154, “Unleashing American Energy,” BLM's lease sales help meet the energy needs of U.S. citizens and solidify the nation as a global energy leader long into the future.
Geothermal
From July through September 2026, the BLM generated $25.8 million for geothermal sales. In August, the BLM set records for the bureau’s highest parcel bid at $4,168,725, and highest per-acre bid at $1,207, and it was the second largest lease sale in total dollars in the Bureau’s history. The BLM accepted winning bids on 32 parcels in Utah totaling 72,398 acres for $24,706,280 in total receipts for a geothermal lease sale. Another August sale in Oregon brought in more than $1.1 million on two parcels totaling more than 9,500 acres.
So far in 2026, the BLM has reported $42.4 million in geothermal lease sales, which reflects continuing industry interest. This includes another successful sale in June in New Mexico that generated $16.6 million on 47 parcels totaling 152,381 acres.
The BLM is planning for more geothermal lease sales this fall in Nevada, Idaho, and California.
The combined bonus bids, rentals, and subsequent royalties from the geothermal leases will be distributed among the U.S. Treasury, the states and counties where the leases are located. Geothermal is an abundant resource, especially in the West, and the BLM has authority to manage geothermal leasing, exploration, and development on approximately 245 million surface acres of public lands and the 700 million acres where the United States owns the subsurface mineral estate.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM’s Third Quarter Oil, Gas and Geothermal Sales Generate Nearly $400 Million in Revenue

Rep. Panetta Stands with Local Community Leaders to Call on the United States Postal Service to Restore Mail Service to Brookdale
To watch his remarks, click HERE.
For additional photos and b-roll, click HERE.
Brookdale, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) brought together local elected leaders and community members at the Brookdale Lodge to voice their unified opposition to the U.S. Postal Service’s (USPS) proposed permanent closure of the Brookdale Post Office. Rep. Panetta was joined at the press conference by Santa Cruz County Supervisor Monica Martinez, Jason Patel of the Brookdale Lodge, and other concerned Brookdale residents. With more than 30 community members present, the group called on USPS to restore mail service as soon as they can to Brookdale.
After nearly two years of delays, missed deadlines, and inconsistent statements, USPS recently launched a discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office without proposing an alternative location in the community or expanded local service. The proposed closure would leave the people of Brookdale without local postal services in a community that already lacks USPS home delivery.
“For nearly two years, the people of Brookdale have waited in good faith while USPS sat on its hands, missed deadlines, and failed to provide a reliable timeline for restoring service,” said Rep. Panetta. “Now, instead of finding a new location or restoring local service, USPS is studying whether to permanently close the Brookdale Post Office. We are standing shoulder to shoulder to call for USPS to halt the study and restore postal services for the Brookdale community.”
“It is unfair for USPS to further burden Brookdale residents, who have already had to assume additional costs in the aftermath of the CZU Lightning Fire Complex, by asking them to travel out of town to access their mail during work hours. If they won’t reestablish a post office, USPS should offer home delivery in Brookdale, like it does in neighboring towns,” said Santa Cruz County Supervisor Monica Martinez.
“After nearly two years without local postal service, Brookdale residents deserve a solution, not a permanent closure. Brookdale residents don’t get home mail delivery, making the post office their only way to receive their prescriptions, ballots, and bills. Since the fire, they have had to drive to Boulder Creek or Ben Lomond to pick up their mail. I stand with Congressman Panetta and Brookdale residents in calling on USPS to restore postal service in Brookdale,” said Assemblymember Gail Pellerin.
“We, the residents of Brookdale, respectfully request the restoration of a permanent U.S. Post Office in the community of Brookdale, Zip Code 95007,” said Brookdale Resident Sally Lussier.
USPS plays a fundamental role in making sure Americans stay informed and participate in our democracy, receive essential government services, pay their bills, and maintain access to lifesaving medication. However, postal services in Brookdale have been suspended since a fire damaged the community’s post office in December 2024. Since then, Brookdale residents have had to travel to Boulder Creek to receive essential mail and conduct the everyday business of their lives. That burden falls especially hard on seniors, people with disabilities, working families, and residents without reliable transportation.
With USPS closing the study’s comment period on October 11, Rep. Panetta and local leaders urged residents to submit their questionnaires and feedback before the deadline. Rep. Panetta also collected comment cards from Brookdale residents expressing their opposition to the proposed permanent closure, which he will submit directly to USPS this week. Those who could not attend the event in person can complete the form linked here by October 9 to have their concerns submitted by Rep. Panetta’s office.
USPS was invited to attend the event but declined to participate, citing its September 11 virtual meeting on the discontinuance feasibility study.
Rep. Panetta has repeatedly pressed USPS leadership to restore postal services in Brookdale. Last week, Rep. Panetta wrote to Postmaster General David Steiner demanding that USPS immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office, identify a new location in Brookdale, and expand appropriate postal services to serve the community. In a February 2026 letter to the Postmaster General, he called on USPS to repair and reopen the facility with a clear project timeline and provide temporary postal service within the community in the interim. After USPS missed its promised May 1 reopening date, Rep. Panetta sent a May 2026 letter requesting that the USPS Inspector General review the agency’s management, communication, and decision-making, the adequacy of interim services, and the feasibility of restoring service through a temporary or alternative facility.
Rep. Panetta will continue to oppose the USPS proposal to permanently close the Brookdale Post Office and demand a permanent postal facility that serves the Brookdale community.
For additional photos and b-roll, click HERE.
###
title: Rep. Panetta Stands with Local Community Leaders to Call on the United States Postal Service to Restore Mail Service to Brookdale

Larson Joins Bipartisan Colleagues to Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
Washington, D.C. - Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Jim Costa (CA-21), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H. Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day." National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.
As Co-Chair of the bipartisan Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Caucus, Rep. Larson has long championed fuel cell technology and has been a forceful advocate for extending the Investment Tax Credit for fuel cells and linear generators, securing its extension in both 2018 and 2022 as part of the Inflation Reduction Act. He co-led introduction of the bipartisan Technology for Energy Security Act to extend the tax credit for another eight years and the American Affordability Act, to bring down costs for households, including a plan to spur the development of American-made clean energy by providing a tax credit to companies that reduce carbon emissions by producing "green" and "blue" hydrogen and fuel cells.
"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."
The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power. Larson, Costa, Tonko, Valadao, Fitzpatrick, and Bilirakis are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Reps.Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) led the introduction of the Senate Resolution, with Senators Bill Cassidy (R-LA), Chris Coons (D-DE), and Chris Murphy (D-CT) joining as original cosponsors.
"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."
"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," said Tonko. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."
"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Valadao.
"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Fitzpatrick.
"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of the Fuel Cell and Hydrogen Energy Association (FCHEA). "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large.”
title: Larson Joins Bipartisan Colleagues to Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day

text:
The Department of War (DoW) today announced a series of initiatives to advance President Donald J. Trump's vision for a New Golden Age of American science. Building on the recommendations in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios's report Science: A New Golden Age, these initiatives will modernize how the Department supports and evaluates scientific research, bring new talent to work on critical scientific challenges in defense of the nation, and strengthen partnerships across the science ecosystem between discovery, innovation, and national defense to ensure American warfighters are supported with cutting edge technology and capabilities.
"President Trump has made it clear that technological dominance requires us to move faster, safeguard our research, and build right here in America," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. "We are answering that call by dismantling barriers to commercialization, modernizing our labs, and ruthlessly securing taxpayer-funded research from foreign exploitation. The Department of War will continue to turn the President's vision of a new golden age of science into unrivaled capability for our warfighters."
"Maintaining our technological edge requires balancing rapid innovation with responsible program protection," said Joseph Jewell, Ph.D., Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology. "As we accelerate how we move concepts from the lab to the field, we are equally committed to safeguarding federally funded research and ensuring domestic investments deliver tangible capabilities. By modernizing our testing facilities, empowering industry through initiatives like the Defense Patent Holiday, and expanding pathways for domestic scientific talent, we are safeguarding our nation's economic vitality and national security, ensuring this new golden age drives lasting domestic strength and unrivaled technological capabilities for our warfighters."
The Department's execution of the White House strategy includes major lines of effort led by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology:
1. Revitalizing America's Defense Research Enterprise
- Department of War and National Science Foundation Establish Memorandum of Understanding to Advance Science, Technology, and Innovation: The Department of War and the National Science Foundation (NSF) have established a broad memorandum of understanding (MOU) to pursue mutually beneficial collaborative activities in science, technology, and innovation. The MOU establishes a framework for the Department and NSF to explore and coordinate opportunities that strengthen the nation's research ecosystem, accelerate the transition of promising technologies, and promote collaboration among government, academic, industry, and other research partners. Initial areas of joint interest include X-Labs, the Programmable Cloud Laboratories Network, and AI Forge ($40 million), among other initiatives that advance experimentation, modernize research infrastructure, build the workforce, and push the development of emerging technologies. As part of this effort, the Department of War is dedicating $200M to Programmable Cloud Labs in Fiscal Year 2028 across the Future Years Defense Program (FYDP).
Through this partnership, the Department of War and NSF may identify opportunities for information exchange, joint workshops, research collaboration, pilot activities, and other initiatives consistent with each organization's authorities, priorities, and available resources.
- Department of War Advances Metascience-informed Framework to Strengthen the Defense Research Enterprise: Consistent with Science: A New Golden Age and the recommendations of the Defense Research Enterprise Review, the Department of War is establishing a new enterprise-wide framework to measure and improve the performance and effectiveness of its in-house laboratories, Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs) and University-Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs).
Implementing Recommendation 14 of the Department's recently published "Defense Research Enterprise Review," the initiative will apply metascience-informed principles to create measures of performance (MOP) and measures of effectiveness (MOE) as metrics.
The initiative reflects a metascience-informed approach to research management: using evidence and rigorous evaluation to improve how research organizations are assessed, governed, and resourced. Rather than impose a single scorecard on organizations with different missions, the Department will develop category-specific measures anchored to each institution's mission, comparative advantages, and enduring technical capabilities.
The framework will be designed to:
- Focus on outcomes: Assess whether portfolios achieve mission-relevant results commensurate with their resources and responsibilities
- Support independent verification: Use measures that can be audited and substantiated
- Measure progress over time: Track long-term performance consistent with the timelines of scientific research and engineering
- Respect institutional differences: Enable appropriate comparisons while recognizing that laboratories, warfare centers, medical research organizations, federally funded research and development centers, and university affiliated research centers have distinct missions and operating models
- Reduce distorted incentives: Avoid overreliance on narrow activity metrics that can encourage organizations to report volume instead of mission outcomes
- Inform leadership decisions: Strengthen the evidence base for portfolio management, resource allocation, and performance improvement
The Defense Research Enterprise Review found that existing enterprise measures, including activity counts and obligation and expenditure rates, remain useful for financial stewardship and oversight but do not independently capture portfolio-level outcomes. The new MOP/MOE framework is intended to complement—not replace—appropriate financial management and program oversight tools.
The Department is launching the framework with a limited pilot across representative research organizations to validate measures before engaging in a broader implementation.
- New Department of War Research Center Unites Academic Researchers with Broader Industry, Venture Capital, Non-Profit Ecosystem: The Department of War is catalyzing the university research ecosystem through the new Center for Defense Academic Research's (CeDAR) two complementary initiatives: the Problem-Based Basic Research Consortium (PBR-C) and the Translational Research Initiative for Academia and Defense (TRIAD) Partnership. Through PBR-C, the Department will unite multidisciplinary university research teams and world-class individual investigators to solve pressing scientific challenges, leveraging partnerships with non-profit research foundations, selective international collaborations, and participation from industry and venture capital observers. In parallel, TRIAD pairs transdisciplinary academic research teams with Service laboratories to develop actionable solutions for Combatant Command and Joint Interagency Task Force mission priorities.
2. Investing in America's Scientific Talent to Support the Warfighter
- Expansion of Hands-On Technical Learning: Fulfilling the White House directives to invest in individual researchers and elevate technical apprenticeships, the Department is expanding premier human capital programs. Celebrating its 20th anniversary, the Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship for Service Program welcomed its largest cohort of more than 750 scholars this year.
The DoW's SMART Program provides merit-based scholarships to bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students in STEM fields. In exchange for full tuition, stipends, and internship opportunities, scholars commit to a one-to-one service period as civilian employees with the DoW. Since its inception in 2006, the SMART program has awarded over 6,500 scholarships, with 91 percent of scholars successfully completing the program.
Beginning this fiscal year, the Department of War will explore a talent exchange initiative that would connect the Department of Energy's (DOE's) Genesis Mission Fellowship program to the DoW's SMART and National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate (NDSEG) programs. This partnership enables DoW and DOE scholars to intern with each other's laboratories and industry partners, putting opportunities in academia, government laboratories, and companies under one umbrella.
The Department's flagship SMART and NDSEG programs are producing a new generation of scientific leaders. To date, the two programs boast over 5,000 Ph.D. graduates between them; these graduates have gone on to fill critical roles within the Department, drive innovation in the private sector, and advance the frontiers of knowledge in academia.
Complementing this talent pipeline, the NDSEG program has cultivated the nation's scientific minds since 1989, awarding nearly 4,900 fellowships. The program offers full tuition and a generous stipend for up to three years to individuals pursuing doctoral degrees, with no service obligation. This provides fellows with the flexibility to pursue careers across academia, industry, and government, with 90 percent of graduates entering research and development roles, broadly strengthening the U.S. innovation ecosystem.
The SMART SEED Innovation Award supports SMART scholars as they begin their DoW employment after completing their doctorates. The technical work completed through SEED, which provides funding of up to $155,000 per year for up to three years, aligns with Department missions or critical technology areas.
The Department of War is proud to announce the Fiscal Year 2026 SMART SEED Innovation Award principal investigators:

- Maile McCann, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Coastal Hydraulics Laboratory, Duck, NC

- Trent Schreiber, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Construction Engineering Research Laboratory, Champaign, IL
- Varsha Swamy, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Geotechnical and Structures Laboratory (GSL), Vicksburg, MS
- Juliet Swinea, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – GSL, Vicksburg, MS
- Amani Webber-Schultz, Naval Undersea Warfare Center- Newport Division, Newport, RI
- Daniel Weitsman, U.S. Army DEVCOM Aviation Missile Center – Technology Development Directorate, Fort Eustis, VA
- Ethan Wright, Naval Surface Warfare Center- Panama City Division, Panama City, FL
Since Fiscal Year 2020, SMART SEED awards have invested $41 million in 140 projects, resulting in new patents, publications, and advanced defense technologies. Ultimately, these programs ensure the long-term sustainability of an agile, highly capable STEM workforce equipped to safeguard national security and maintain America's enduring technological edge.
3. Accelerating and Safeguarding American Defense Innovation
- Enforce Robust Research Security and Program Protection: The Department has strengthened its Science & Technology Program Protection and Maintaining Technology Advantage frameworks to support implementation of National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 (NSPM-33). The Department conducts rigorous risk-based reviews of fundamental research, screens against National Defense Authorization Act Section 1286 foreign-risk entity lists, ensures strict compliance with Section 1062 foreign institution limits, and executes mandatory foreign ownership due diligence. This ensures technological advancements made in America can be translated into operational capabilities for the United States and our allies.
- Dismantle Commercialization Barriers via the Defense Patent Holiday Initiative: The Department is responding to the White House's mandate to reform intellectual property licensing and open federal innovations to non-traditional builders through the Defense Patent Holiday Initiative. This initiative directly supports White House priorities by rapidly accelerating the transition of Department-funded technologies into the commercial sector. By granting royalty-free licensing windows to federally developed patents, the Department empowers private-sector innovators to commercialize breakthrough defense hardware without navigating months of legal friction.
- Leverage R&D to Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing: The Department of War's ManTech Program celebrated its 70th anniversary this year and serves as the Department's primary bridge from prototypes to programs of record, shaping not just what the military designs, but how it is produced affordably, securely, and at scale. The Department's Manufacturing Innovation Institutes (MIIs) include a network of nine active, defense-led institutes across the nation, including the latest addition, the FutureTEX institute in Belmont, North Carolina.
These unified lines of effort strengthen the American innovation pipeline and deliver unmatched capabilities to our warfighters.
title: Department of War Executes White House Strategy for a New Golden Age of Science

Rollins Urges Federal Land Ranchers to Put June Grazing Directive to Work
(WASHINGTON, D.C., October 8, 2026) — Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins sent a letter to all livestock ranchers holding grazing permits on U.S. Forest Service allotments, outlining the Department’s June 12, 2026 Grazing Directive and inviting producers to put it to work on their allotments.
The letter builds on the October 20, 2025 USDA Plan to Fortify the American Beef Industry and the March 31, 2026 Advancing Grazing on Forest Service and BLM Lands Memorandum of Understanding signed by Secretary Rollins and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum. Together with the Grazing Directive issued by Secretary Rollins and Under Secretary for Natural Resources and Environment Michael Boren, the three documents describe Administration policy to streamline and expand livestock grazing on federal lands, elevate grazing as a priority, and strengthen support for America’s ranchers within the framework of existing law and regulations.
“You embody the ethos of our nation’s founding 250 years ago,” said Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “For the past 19 months, USDA has worked tirelessly to defend and promote our nation’s ranchers and give you the tools to help rebuild our Great American Cattle Herd. I encourage you to familiarize yourself with the Grazing Directive as we work together to accomplish shared goals on your respective allotments.”
For more information, see the full letter (PDF, 312 KB).
Background:
The U.S. Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management administer approximately 240 million acres of rangelands across 28 states, supporting more than 23,000 permittees and lessees. Secretary Rollins noted that restoring the nation’s beef and sheep herds will, by necessity, include both Forest Service and BLM lands.
The June Grazing Directive directs the Forest Service, consistent with applicable law and regulation, to:
- Take appropriate measures to restore at least 500,000 head months across National Forest System lands within two years;
- Implement a policy of no net loss of Animal Unit Months within allotments;
- Make vacant and closed allotments available for grazing;
- Improve wildfire planning, coordination, and recovery, including the use of virtual fencing;
- Improve National Environmental Policy Act efficiencies; and
- Improve coordination and build positive relationships with ranchers.
The letter also points to the new USDA Ranchers First webpage at www.usda.gov/ranchers-first, which details actions taken under the Trump Administration to support grazing, processing, and the long-term strength of the American cattle herd.
Producers who believe they have been subjected to agricultural lawfare may submit information through the Farmer and Rancher Freedom Framework at www.usda.gov/lawfare. Grazing-specific concerns may be sent to grazing@usda.gov.

EPA Approves Removal of Burdensome Permitting Requirements Following Georgia’s Air Quality Attainment Status
ATLANTA (October 8, 2026) — Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) approved revisions to Georgia’s State Implementation Plan (SIP), removing unnecessary permitting requirements. Following the entire State of Georgia coming into attainment for National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) in 2022, EPA has determined that permitting requirements previously in place to help reach air quality standards are no longer required or needed under the Clean Air Act (CAA). This milestone will help promote economic growth across Georgia by removing burdensome requirements that slow energy construction and discourage reshoring of manufacturing, all while maintaining clean air within the state.
“EPA is proud to put cooperative federalism into action and work with the State of Georgia to remove these obsolete permitting requirements. By clarifying the regulatory landscape, businesses in Georgia will have certainty as they look to invest in the Peach State,” said EPA Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber. “Years of work have gone into reaching this point, and we are confident that the state continues to have the tools to maintain clean air for all Georgians.”
Today’s action will remove all nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) requirements, certain provisions related to the use of emission reduction credits, and other mandated programs in Georgia’s SIP that were put in place when areas were still in nonattainment for the NAAQS. Under the best reading of the CAA, EPA determined that removing these permitting programs from Georgia’s SIP will not interfere with attainment or maintenance of the NAAQS or any other applicable statutorily obligations. Georgia’s SIP will continue to include permitting programs designed to protect the state’s attainment with the NAAQS.
On background:
EPA proposed to approve the removal of the NNSR program from the Georgia SIP on September 2, 2025, and held a 30-day comment period.
Georgia has not had any designated nonattainment areas since EPA’s approval of the redesignation of the Atlanta area for the 2015 ozone NAAQS on October 17, 2022.
title: EPA Approves Removal of Burdensome Permitting Requirements Following Georgia’s Air Quality Attainment Status

HUD Announces Arrests of Nearly 500 Fraudsters and Fugitives
Nationwide Crackdown Restores Safety to HUD Housing and Communities
October 8, 2026
WASHINGTON – Secretary Turner applauded the work of Operation Clean House, a multi-agency, multi-month law enforcement initiative targeting fugitives living in HUD-assisted housing, for arresting 491 criminal fugitives. HUD Office of Inspector General (OIG) Special Agents partnered with the U.S. Marshals Service and state and local law enforcement across 12 cities to carry out this mission.
“We will not allow criminal predators and fraudsters to use HUD housing as a haven or live freely on the taxpayer’s dime,” said Secretary Turner, a member of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. “Operation Clean House removed dangerous drug traffickers, rapists, and sex offenders and delivered real accountability. President Trump promised to restore once-great American cities, and we are fulfilling that promise by making our communities safer.”
“These arrests are only one part of our strategy. Our investigators, auditors, evaluators, and analysts are attacking threats to HUD programs from every direction. Whether it is violent criminals hiding in HUD-assisted housing, fraudsters stealing taxpayer dollars, or weaknesses that leave federal housing programs vulnerable to abuse, we will use every authority and every tool available to protect these programs and the people they serve,” said Acting Inspector General Brian D. Harrison.
“Public housing is for the needy, not criminals. Thankfully, Secretary Turner will not sleep until all crooks and fraudsters are kicked out,” said Scott Brady, Executive Director of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.
Operation Clean House carried out arrests in Memphis, Tennessee; New York City, New York; Newark, New Jersey; Chicago, Illinois; Los Angeles, California; Kansas City, Missouri; Kansas City, Kansas; New Orleans, Louisiana; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; Cleveland, Ohio; Minneapolis, Minnesota; Columbus, Ohio; and others.
Working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, HUD is rooting out waste and holding fraudsters accountable with real consequences.
- In June, HUD held Los Angeles’ homeless industrial complex accountable and suspended the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) from receiving further taxpayer funds. LAHSA has received over $1 billion in tax dollars since 2013 despite its record of fraud.
- In September, Secretary Turner announced the arrests of LA fraudsters who stole $14 million, including taxpayer funds received through LAHSA, instead of serving the homeless.
- In July, HUD suspended funding to the Virgin Islands Housing Finance Authority, which received $1.9 billion, due to widespread financial mismanagement and improper payments.

Congresswoman Gwen Moore Leads Effort to Crack Down on Corrupt, Taxpayer-Funded Settlements
Congresswoman Gwen Moore introduced the Executive Settlement Review Act to provide stronger oversight and independent review and approval of any legal settlements that occur between the President, his political allies, or personal associates, and the federal government they oversee. This legislation comes as the Trump administration has sought to use taxpayer funds for a $1.8 billion slush fund, which could have paid violent January 6th insurrectionists.
“Trump has attempted to use sham government settlements to enrich himself and protect his family from legal scrutiny. And it likely doesn’t stop at him. I’m dismayed by recent reports that Treasury Secretary Bessent may be negotiating sweetheart deals with the IRS for himself. Congress and the Judiciary must work to prevent corruption and grift in the executive branch. My bill, the Executive Settlement Review Act, fulfills a need for a fair and comprehensive process to ensure that our tax dollars aren’t misused and that the public and Congress are aware of the details of any settlement that are at a heightened risk of abuse,” said Congresswoman Gwen Moore.
The provisions of this bill would apply to pending lawsuits brought against the United States by the currently serving President, Vice President, Cabinet members, certain senior federal officials, their families, and their businesses, with exemptions for those seeking small claims.
Key Provisions of the bill:
    - Formal filing of the proposed agreement by the Department of Justice with a federal district court, led by a panel of three judges.
- A 60-day period in which the public can and submit comments on any proposed settlements, comments that the government must address and which the court must consider. 
- Submission of written briefs to the court by both parties outlining the merits and rationale of the agreement, including the disclosure of any documents or communications that informed their decision to settle.
- Review of the settlement by the three-judge district court panel, who will assess whether the settlement agreement is lawful, factual, and settles a legitimate legal dispute, among other criteria.
title: Congresswoman Gwen Moore Leads Effort to Crack Down on Corrupt, Taxpayer-Funded Settlements

Suozzi Convenes Long Island Robotics Roundtable
      Image    
Convenes Roundtable with CEO of Standard Bots, Largest Manufacturer of Industrial Robots in America, and Other Leaders
Pushes to make region a hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing
Glen Cove, NY—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today convened business, technology, and workforce development leaders for a roundtable discussion on how to position Long Island to become a national hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing. The roundtable was held at Standard Bots in conjunction with CEO Evan Beard, the largest manufacturer of industrial robots in the United States.
“Standard Bots is a great example of why Long Island has the talent, the universities, the skilled workforce, and the entrepreneurial spirit to be the nation’s leader in robotics and advanced manufacturing. We need to bring all those pieces together and make sure we are competing for the businesses and jobs of the future,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Robotics and advanced manufacturing are going to play an increasingly important role in our economy, not only because of their effectiveness but because the industry creates high-skilled, high-tech jobs that have good wages for the people of Long Island.”
The roundtable brought together leaders from the robotics, manufacturing, financial, and economic development sectors to discuss the rapid growth of the domestic and international robotics industry, the role of robotics in strengthening American manufacturing, the future of robotics and physical AI on Long Island, and the opportunities for Long Island to attract robotics companies, develop a skilled local workforce, and improve its existing strengths in technology, manufacturing, engineering, and research. Participants also explored federal initiatives that could promote robotics, including tariffs, grant opportunities, research and development supports, expansion of workforce development initiatives, tax credits, safety standards for newer AI-powered robots, and more.
The roundtable was held at Standard Bots in Glen Cove, the largest manufacturer of industrial robots in America. Suozzi opened the event and moderated a discussion featuring Evan Beard, Co-Founder, CEO and Chief Engineer of Standard Bots; Robert Kufner, President and CEO of Designatronics; Tommy McNulty, Head of Platform Sales at Erebor Bank; Cara Longworth, VP, Long Island Regional Director of Empire State Development; and Amy Erickson, Executive Director of Long Island Manufacturing Extension Partnership.
Beard delivered the keynote address on the state of the domestic and international robotics industry and the opportunities ahead for Long Island and the United States. 
“The next era of manufacturing will be won by the countries that build their own robots, and we believe America should lead it. That's why we design and build our robots right here in Glen Cove, with some of the most talented engineers, machinists, and builders anywhere in the world. Long Island has a proud manufacturing legacy, and we're grateful to Congressman Suozzi for bringing industry, government, and investors together to make this region a home for American robotics,” said Evan Beard, CEO & Co-founder, Standard Bots.
“Robotics is the fastest growing market in the world. It will fundamentally change how work gets done in your home and in nearly all business segments. Unfortunately, much of the global supply of robots has come from outside the U.S., but the through the good work of Rep. Suozzi and leaders across industries on Long Island that have the capability to build robots, it has been recognized that future supply can and must be made domestically with American made products. Long Island’s proximity to New York City where hundreds of robotics startups are being nurtured gives it a distinct advantage to support their growth as well as the thousands of other robotics companies across the country that are getting ready to scale. Long Island has a long history in advanced manufacturing and already has all the components to become a national hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing with the right amount of coordination,” said Robert Kufner, President and CEO, Designatronics.
“As Executive Director of the Long Island MEP (LIMEP) at Stony Brook University, I see a tremendous opportunity for our small and mid-sized manufacturers to strengthen their competitiveness through the adoption of advanced technologies, particularly robotics. LIMEP is committed to helping manufacturers understand how automation and robotics can improve productivity, efficiency, and long-term growth. Today’s event at Standard Bots, hosted by Congressman Suozzi and Evan Beard, CEO and Founder of Standard Bots, was an excellent example of how industry, government, and the manufacturing community can come together to advance this mission. Evan also served as a keynote speaker at our LIMEP–College of Engineering robotics event, helping regional manufacturers see the practical opportunities that robotics can bring to their operations. We thank Congressman Suozzi and Evan Beard for their continued leadership and support of the NY MEP Network—and especially LIMEP at Stony Brook University—as we work to strengthen Long Island’s manufacturing ecosystem and position our companies for the future,” said Amy Erickson, Executive Director, Long Island Manufacturing Extension Partnership.
title: Suozzi Convenes Long Island Robotics Roundtable
