NIH announces record number of grants to support early career investigators, launches new recruitment initiative for intramural research
Thursday, October 8, 2026
NIH announces record number of grants to support early career investigators, launches new recruitment initiative for intramural research
NIH highlights actions to strengthen American biomedical science at White House Science: A New Golden Age Summit.
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) today announced significant accomplishments that underscore the agency’s progress in strengthening the U.S. biomedical research enterprise. The agency announced that 1,648 early-stage investigators are receiving NIH support through R01-equivalent extramural research grant awards in fiscal year 2026, the most ever recorded. The agency also launched Generation Discovery, a new initiative to recruit 100 early-career Principal Investigators into NIH’s Intramural Research Program.
The NIH shared these and other recent accomplishments as part of the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, an event hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) to highlight the comprehensive rethinking of the U.S. science and technology enterprise in the Science: A New Golden Age report and to showcase significant areas of progress.
“NIH is building the future of American biomedical science,” said NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya. “That means demanding the highest standards of rigor, giving exceptional scientists the freedom to pursue bold ideas, attracting new talent, and putting powerful, innovative technologies to work. These actions will help turn scientific possibility into discoveries that improve and save lives.”
The Trump Administration places a high priority on increasing opportunities for early-stage investigators to receive funding support to test new ideas. NIH has found that the average age of an extramural researcher serving for the first time as a principal investigator on a R01-equivalent grant has climbed in recent decades, from 38 years old in FY1995 to 42 in FY2025. The 1,648 R01-equivalent grants awarded to support early-stage investigators in FY2026 represented a 25% increase over the ten-year average of 1,323.
With NIH’s Intramural Research Program (IRP), Generation Discovery is a concerted effort to connect talented early-career researchers with the unparalleled resources and research opportunities found within the IRP.
Beyond these two announcements, NIH highlighted several other initiatives and accomplishments designed to reinvigorate American biomedical science.
Strengthening Scientific Rigor and Reproducibility
A cornerstone of NIH’s efforts is strengthening replication and reproducibility — the ability to test scientific findings and determine whether they hold up when examined again. Because new discoveries build on earlier research, ensuring that findings are reliable is critical to advancing science and directing time and resources toward the most promising paths.
As part of this agency-wide initiative, NIH plans to establish its first metascience office. The office will serve as a central hub for studying and improving how biomedical science is conducted and coordinating NIH efforts to make rigorous, reproducible research a more integral part of the scientific enterprise.
Those efforts include the launch of a new NIH-wide program, known as Rigor, Replicability, & Reproducibility to Promote Excellence, Accuracy, & Translation in Science, or R3PEATS, that will support research, partnerships, infrastructure and training to improve the reliability of biomedical science. They also include NIH’s Linked Discoveries, an experimental PubMed tool recently launched to help researchers see how individual findings fit within the broader body of biomedical evidence.
New Models for Tackling Complex Challenges
NIH is creating new ways to tackle complex scientific and technical challenges. In partnership with the National Science Foundation (NSF), NIH will advance X-Labs, a research model that brings together full-time, interdisciplinary teams with the resources, flexibility and operational independence to pursue ambitious technical goals that are difficult to address through traditional research approaches. NIH and NSF will seek input from the research community to identify potential X-Labs topics focused on priority biomedical research challenges.
Accelerating AI-Enabled Discovery
NIH is leading the Bio-Genesis Mission, part of the national Genesis Mission, to harness Super Intelligence (SI), data, and advanced computational approaches to accelerate biomedical discovery. Efforts include challenges focused on using SI and data to advance pediatric cancer research and repurpose generic drugs, work with the Department of Energy to build the cross-agency Genesis Mission Platform, and a new partnership with Biohub on virtual cell models for the Predicting Living Systems Challenge. NIH will also explore opportunities to develop scientists with expertise in SI and other scientific disciplines and connect trainees with Genesis Mission research opportunities at NIH and partner laboratories.
Developing Scientific Talent
NIH is expanding opportunities for scientists to pursue ambitious ideas and build independent research careers. In fiscal year 2026, NIH supported 1,648 early-stage investigators, the highest number in a single year in NIH history, as part of its commitment to helping early-career researchers establish independent scientific programs. NIH will also broaden its use of Investigator-Focused Awards (R35), which provide greater stability and flexibility to pursue promising scientific directions, and continue using prizes and challenges to spur new approaches to priority scientific and health problems.
NIH is extending that commitment to its own laboratories through Generation Discovery, a new initiative to recruit 100 outstanding investigators to the NIH Intramural Research Program over the next three years to pursue ambitious biomedical research.
Looking Ahead
Together, these efforts reflect NIH’s commitment to strengthening the foundations of American biomedical research while creating new opportunities for discovery. By advancing rigorous and reproducible science, investing in the future of the research workforce, and developing new ways to tackle complex scientific challenges, NIH is working to accelerate discoveries that improve health and strengthen U.S. leadership in biomedical research.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
title: NIH announces record number of grants to support early career investigators, launches new recruitment initiative for intramural research

The Hurricane Hunters will continue flying weather reconnaissance missions into Isaias from Kelly Field, Texas, collecting data for the National Hurricane Center to improve storm track and intensity forecasts.

“We are relocating our aircraft as a prudent measure to protect these critical assets while preserving our ability to conduct weather reconnaissance,” said Col. Although El Niño conditions have contributed to a slower-than-normal Atlantic hurricane season, Fish said one storm can still have significant consequences for communities and military installations in its path.
A hurricane warning is in effect for part of the Mississippi Gulf Coast. The National Hurricane Center forecasts hurricane conditions Friday night into early Saturday, along with potentially dangerous storm surge, heavy rainfall, flooding and isolated tornadoes. Personnel and residents should monitor local weather information and follow instructions from local emergency-management officials.
Wing leadership encourages all Airmen and their families to review personal hurricane preparedness plans, complete appropriate protective actions and remain attentive to official installation messaging.

BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – A North Carolina man appeared in federal court this week following allegations that he voted multiple times in the same election across two states, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr.

A one-count indictment returned by a federal grand jury charges Forrest Scott Woody, 68, of Hendersonville, North Carolina, with illegally voting more than once.

According to the indictment, Woody voted twice in the 2024 general election. In particular, he voted in Calhoun County, Alabama, after having already voted in the same election in Henderson County, North Carolina.

“Every election is an important opportunity for eligible voters to make their voices heard, and the integrity of the election depends on voters following the law,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “As we approach the upcoming election, we will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to ensure that election laws are respected and that every lawful vote is counted.”

“Maintaining the sanctity of our country’s election system is one of the highest callings of federal law enforcement, and this indictment is yet another example of how seriously our office takes that mission,” said Assistant U.S. Attorney and Election Crimes Coordinator Brett A. Janich.

“Ensuring public confidence in our elections is a responsibility we take seriously,” said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. “When individuals attempt to undermine that process, the FBI will work with our partners to safeguard the integrity of every vote.”

“I appreciate the U.S. Attorney Phil Williams and his team in the U.S. Attorney’s Office and all other federal agencies who are assisting in the investigation and prosecution of this case,” said Secretary of State Wes Allen. “I want to also thank the team in my office. Election integrity is a top priority of mine.”

FBI investigated the case, with the assistance of the Alabama Secretary of State’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Brett A. Janich is prosecuting the case.

An indictment contains only charges. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
title: North Carolina Man Arraigned in Federal Court for Voting More Than Once in a Single Election

Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.
For the first time, on August 1, the National Weather Service upgraded a Red Flag Warning for fire weather conditions to a Particularly Dangerous Situation, which is very rare and typically reserved for extreme fire weather conditions. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane: the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead. The Spokane Complex Fires forced 67,000 people to evacuate, burned nearly 10,000 acres, with damages predicted to exceed $1 billion.
This was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and threatening lives, property, businesses, and livestock. In Okanogan County, the Kaiser Canyon, Modrite, and Sinlahekin fires burned over 350,000 acres total.
“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” the lawmakers wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”
The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.” 
“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.
Joining DelBene in the letter to President Trump were Washington Senators Patty Murray and Maria Cantwell, and Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Dan Newhouse (WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (WA-05), Emily Randall (WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Kim Schrier M.D. (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10).

Reps. Tlaib and Green lead letter demanding release of DACA recipient in ICE custody
Ya’akub Ira Vijandre has now been in ICE custody for a year for ‘liking’ a social media post
WASHINGTON – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Al Green (TX-09) joined by 21 Members of Congress demanded the release of Ya’akub Ira Vijandre, who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a year ago as of yesterday. In a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Acting Director David Venturella, the Members pressed for answers regarding Ya’akub’s unconstitutional arrest and prolonged detention after a federal judge allowed his habeas challenge to proceed.
Ya’akub, a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipient, has lived in the U.S. since he was 14 years old. He spent a decade working for American Airlines as a senior safety specialist and was recognized for supporting grieving families after a helicopter crashed into a plane in Washington, D.C. Despite having no criminal record and not being charged with any crime, he was targeted and arrested at gun point for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza and for “liking” a social media post with Quranic verses–both of which are protected by the First Amendment.
“The administration’s stated basis for [Ya’akub’s] detention has been inconsistent and appears to rely substantially on his speech and social media activity,” the Members wrote. “DHS has sought to justify his detention by citing his social media commentary regarding the prosecutions of the Holy Land Foundation Five, his criticism of the treatment of Guantanamo detainees, his advocacy for Palestine, and his engagement with religious Islamic content, including ‘liking’ Instagram posts containing Quranic verses. We are deeply concerned that constitutionally protected political and religious expression is being used as a basis for his continued detention or deportation.”
The letter renews concerns and questions from a letter Rep. Green sent in June. Rep. Tlaib also spoke on the House floor urging for Ya’akub’s release in August.
“We are also concerned by reports, previously flagged in Congressman Green’s June letter, that the FBI approached Mr. Vijandre in November 2023 seeking his cooperation as a confidential informant and that he declined,” the Members continued in their letter. “His DACA status, renewed as recently as May 2024 through May 2026, was subsequently revoked. The proximity and sequence of these events—an FBI approach he declined, followed by a DACA termination and detention grounded largely in the government’s characterization of his religious and political speech—continue to raise serious questions about possible retaliation that Congress has not yet received satisfactory answers to.”
The letter, led by Reps. Tlaib and Green, was signed by 21 other Members of Congress: Greg Casar (TX–35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús "Chuy" García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

ROCHESTER, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Stephen Odiboh, 53, of Stone Mountain, Georgia, who was convicted of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, was sentenced to serve 33 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Charles J. Siragusa. He was also ordered to pay $196,500 in restitution.

Between 2023 and March 2025, Odiboh conspired with co-conspirators to defraud four victims. The total loss and attempted loss were $356,500.

In 2023, Odiboh contacted Victim 1, a 77-year-old woman in the Western District of New York, on Facebook. Posing as “Oliver Wilson,” he falsely represented that he was a United States Citizen, a widower, and currently living in Norway. Over the course of approximately a year and a half, “Wilson” fostered a romantic, online relationship, stating that he needed gift cards to “stay online” and continue talking. As a result, Victim 1 sent “Wilson” approximately 30 $500 gift cards, totaling approximately $15,000. In addition, between January and July of 2024, “Wilson” induced Victim 1 to mail eight checks totaling over $162,000.00 to specific individuals and entities, including two checks to Stephen Odiboh. In December 2024, “Wilson” stated that he was being held by customs authorities in Norway and needed to pay a fine of $158,000. He directed Victim 1 to mail two checks totaling $158,000.00 but Victim 1’s bank detected fraud and stopped payment of the checks before they could be cashed.

In April 2024, a co-conspirator contacted Victim 2, a caterer, claiming to be “Alex Alberto,” and in need of catering services. Victim 2 requested a deposit of $800. To pay the purported deposit, “Alberto” sent Victim 2 a check for $2,800, and instructed Victim 2 to cash the check and send the extra $2,000 to the defendant via Zelle. Victim 2 realized he was being defrauded and did not deposit the check.

In 2024, a co-conspirator, claiming to be “William Rivera,” contacted Victim 3 through an online dating website. After gaining Victim 3’s trust, “Rivera” convinced Victim 3 to send $2,000 to Odiboh via CashApp, which Victim 3 did on August 14, 2024.

In March 2025, a co-conspirator, claiming to be “Alec Jonas,” contacted Victim 4 on a dating website, leading Victim 4 to believe that they were starting a romantic relationship. Once he gained her trust, “Jonas” stated that he was working in Bahrain and needed money to ship goods from Bahrain to Texas, prompting Victim 4 to wire $17,525 to a bank account he controlled.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Meghan K. McGuire. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II and the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Harry Chavis.

Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act would help veterans in New Hampshire and across the country connect with community and strengthen their well-being
Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) and Congressman Jeff Hurd (CO-03) introduced the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act, legislation to help veterans in New Hampshire and across the country access outdoor recreation programs that support their mental and physical well-being.
The Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act would establish a grant program through the Department of Veterans Affairs for state veterans’ agencies to develop, administer, and expand outdoor recreation programs for veterans. States could operate programs directly or partner with local outfitters, guides, nonprofit organizations, and community-based outdoor recreation providers.
“Our obligation to those who served doesn’t end when the uniform comes off. In New Hampshire, our mountains, lakes, and trails offer veterans opportunities to build community and strengthen their physical and mental well-being,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “I’m proud to help introduce the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act with Congressman Hurd to make those opportunities available to more veterans. By helping cover equipment, transportation, and program costs, our bill would help more veterans get outdoors, connect with one another, and find the support they’ve earned.”
“For many veterans, the transition from military service can mean losing the sense of purpose, community, and connection that came with serving alongside others,” said Congressman Hurd. “Colorado’s public lands and outdoor spaces offer opportunities to rebuild those connections while supporting veterans’ physical and mental well-being. This bipartisan legislation gives states more tools to work with local organizations and expand outdoor recreation opportunities so that more veterans can benefit from time outdoors and with one another.”
Under the legislation, grant funding could be used to reduce financial barriers that may prevent veterans from participating in outdoor recreation programs, including the costs of equipment, program fees, and reasonable transportation expenses. Funding could also support outreach to veterans and the expansion of existing programs.
The bill would also encourage state veterans’ agencies to work with federal land management agencies, including the National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Forest Service, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, to expand veterans’ access to outdoor spaces, reduce administrative barriers, and identify appropriate locations for organized activities.
The legislation defines eligible outdoor recreation programs broadly as nature-based activities designed to improve veterans’ mental and physical well-being through physical engagement, peer connection, skill-building, or therapeutic benefit. Programs may also include adaptive or accessible activities for veterans with disabilities.
Each eligible state entity whose application meets the bill’s requirements would receive at least $200,000 per fiscal year, subject to available appropriations. The legislation authorizes $10 million annually for the grant program. Participating states would also report information including the number of veterans served, types of activities offered, participation frequency, and observations related to veterans’ well-being, social connectedness, and physical activity.
Read the full bill text here. Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) leads the Senate companion to this bill.

title: Goodlander Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Expand Outdoor Recreation for Veterans

WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY-09) and Julia Letlow (R-LA-05) introduced a bipartisan, bicameral resolution to establish October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18th as World Menopause Day. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced the resolution’s companion in the Senate.
These observances will contribute to the spread of global awareness and access to care during menopausal transition and post-menopause, as well as provide organizations and individuals around the world with an opportunity to advocate for resources and support for the 75 million American women in perimenopause, menopause, and post-menopause.
“Throughout our lives, women deserve the support we need to confront every trial and embrace every triumph each of our chapters has in store for us. Menopause is a natural experience that we all must face, yet the stigma that follows it continues to inflict needless ridicule and shame on women at a time when all we ask for is acceptance and understanding,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “World Menopause Awareness Month and World Menopause Day will be the bridges to normalizing menopause and ensuring the women confronting it have the resources, care, and confidence they need to tackle their new horizons head on, and I am proud to lead this bipartisan legislation to see both codified as national observances.”
“Through any stage of life, women need access to reliable information to make educated decisions about their health. World Menopause Awareness Month shines a light on the millions of women undergoing menopause every year, highlighting the need for women to have a better understanding of the treatments and options available to them,” said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.
“Generations of women have faced the transition to menopause, yet for too long this experience has been overlooked, under-researched, and treated as taboo,” said Lisa Senator Blunt Rochester. “It’s far past time we ensure women have the care and support they need to feel their best in all phases of life. I’m proud to introduce the World Menopause Awareness Month Resolution to elevate the challenges of menopause and encourage further investments into research that will help women meet this transition with confidence.”
“Our health care system has failed women struggling with menopausal symptoms that disrupt their livelihoods, and this unfortunate reality disproportionately affects Black and Hispanic women,” said Senator Cory Booker. “This resolution is a reminder that we must do more to support women navigating menopause and provide them with the resources they need. Menopause should not be a barrier to the quality of life every woman deserves.”
“The resolution introduced by Congresswoman Yvette Clarke represents another important step toward breaking down the barriers that have too often left women without the information, care, and relief they need throughout the menopause transition,” said Donna Klassen of Let’s Talk Menopause. “We proudly support this resolution and applaud Congresswoman Clarke’s leadership in bringing greater attention to menopause, expanding access to trusted health information and care, and ensuring women have the resources they need to navigate this stage of life with confidence and support.”
“Menopause is a universal experience for women, and yet, for too long menopause has been understudied. This has left us with significant knowledge gaps about menopause itself, including its symptoms and treatments, but also about the effects of menopause on overall health and healthy aging. Fortunately, we now have momentum to course correct. The Society for Women’s Health Research thanks Representative Clarke for her leadership on the resolution designating October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18 as World Menopause Day. We must collectively continue raising awareness about menopause, which can help shape research priorities and ensure women and health care providers have the evidence and information needed to make informed decisions about menopause care,” said Lindsey Miltenberger of the Society for Women’s Health Research.
Menopause is more than a personal, biological transition—it has lasting implications for women’s health and well-being, and for families, workplaces, and society. The Black Women’s Health Imperative endorses this resolution to recognize October as World Menopause Awareness Month and expand awareness, provider education, and access to the resources and care that women, particularly Black women, need for a healthy, dignified menopause, ” said Ifeoma Udoh, Ph.D. of the Black Women’s Health Imperative.
The resolution is endorsed by the American Medical Association, Astellas, Greater New York Hospital Association, Healthcare Association of New York State, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Mount Sinai Health System, National Medical Association, National Minority Quality Forum, Novo Nordisk, Inc., NYU Langone Health, One Brooklyn Health System, Reproductive Health Access Project, Ritual, The Fibroid Foundation, and The White Dress Project.

DOE’s Early Career Research Program (ECRP) Supports the Next Generation of American Scientific Leadership Across Universities, National Laboratories, and User Facilities.
October 8, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Science today announced the selection of 67 early career scientists to receive a combined $96 million through the 2026 Early Career Research Program (ECRP). Today’s announcement advances President Trump’s Executive Order Restoring Gold Standard Science by supporting exceptional researchers pursuing rigorous, mission-driven research in areas critical to America’s scientific and technological leadership, including Super Intelligence (SI), fusion energy, and quantum science.
“Groundbreaking science begins with empowering extraordinary people,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Dr. Darío Gil. “These 67 early career researchers represent the very best of American ingenuity. DOE is proud to invest in their vision as they push the boundaries of knowledge and cement U.S. leadership in the technologies that will define our century.”
The 2026 Early Career Research Program (ECRP) selectees represent 39 universities, 11 DOE National Laboratories and Office of Science User Facilities, and 26 states. By investing in exceptional researchers at a pivotal stage in their careers, ECRP empowers the next generation of STEM leaders to pursue bold, innovative research that drives DOE’s mission and ensures America continues to lead the world in science and innovation. Since its inception in 2010, the program has made 1,238 awards, including 797 to university researchers and 441 to DOE National Laboratory researchers.
Awards to scientists at institutions of higher education are approximately $875,000 over five years, while awards to scientists at DOE National Laboratories or Office of Science User Facilities are approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
Information about the 67 selectees and their research projects is available on the Office of Science Awards page.
Profiles of previous award recipients, including information about how the program helped advance their research and careers, are available on the Early Career Program profiles page.
Selection for award negotiations is not a commitment by DOE to issue an award or provide funding. Before funding is issued, DOE and the applicants will undergo a negotiation process, and DOE may cancel negotiations and rescind the selection for any reason during that time.

DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a Dallas man has been charged with repeatedly flying a drone into restricted airspace around both Dallas Love Field and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

On Sept. 16, a federal grand jury returned a four-count indictment against Pujan Prashantkumar Gajjar, 24, on offenses related to the unauthorized operation of an unmanned aircraft in protected airport airspace.

“Safe and secure air travel depends on strict compliance with federal aviation rules,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Unauthorized drone incursions into protected airport airspace jeopardizes aircraft and endangers pilots, passengers and the entire community. This office will continue working with our law enforcement partners to ensure the safety of our airspace.”

“Safe and secure air travel depends on strict compliance with federal aviation rules,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Unauthorized drone incursions into protected airport airspace jeopardizes aircraft and endangers pilots, passengers and the entire community. This office will continue working with our law enforcement partners to ensure the safety of our airspace.”

"Operating a drone in restricted airport space threatens the safety of pilots, passengers, and crew in the air as well as communities on the ground,” said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “The FBI is committed to working with our partners to investigate these types of violations and ensure those who endanger our airspace are held accountable .”

According to the indictment, Mr. Gajjar allegedly flew a drone into the runway exclusion zone at Dallas Love Field around 11:30 p.m. on June 26, 2025, with the drone allegedly crossing an active runway. The following night, he allegedly flew the same drone into restricted airspace surrounding Dallas-Fort Worth Airport. The indictment further alleges that, in connection with the same flights, Mr. Gajjar knowingly and willfully served as an airman without the required airman’s certificate.

Federal agents arrested Gajjar Sept. 22. He made his initial appearance the same day before U.S. Magistrate Judge Renee Harris Toliver. If convicted, Gajjar faces up to eight years in federal prison.

The FBI Dallas and the Federal Air Marshal Service conducted the investigation with the assistance of the Federal Aviation Administration. Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward L. Hocter from the National Security Section is prosecuting the case.

An indictment is merely an allegation of criminal conduct and defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

WASHINGTON—The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah (bank), for deficiencies in the bank’s Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

The OCC determined that the bank failed to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations. Deficiencies in the Bank’s BSA/AML program involved inadequate resources, including staff without sufficient expertise, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and weak BSA/AML training for employees and directors.

The OCC found that the bank failed to tailor its BSA/AML risk assessment to its business activities. The bank focused on the risks in its relatively narrow demand deposit account products and services and insufficiently on the risks in its more dominant credit and charge card products. In addition to its ineffective risk assessments, the bank’s customer due diligence processes and customer identification program procedures contributed to the bank’s monitoring and reporting failures. The bank experienced systemic breakdowns in its suspicious activity monitoring and reporting processes, resulting in a failure to timely identify, evaluate, and sufficiently report approximately $13 billion of suspected trade-based money laundering activity that took place over the past decade.

“The OCC expects banks of American Express’s size and complexity to devote sufficient resources to ensure compliance with laws and regulations designed to detect and prevent money laundering, which are critical to both economic and national security,” said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould. “American Express failed to maintain a BSA/AML compliance program properly aligned with the money laundering risks of its operations, which resulted in the bank’s failures to timely identify and report significant missed suspicious activity and to provide important information to law enforcement. Today’s actions will serve to focus American Express on properly addressing such risks as it continues to serve its customers.”

The OCC is taking these actions in coordination with a concurrent cease-and-desist order against American Express Company and American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc., by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The OCC-assessed penalty will be directed to the U.S. Treasury.

Reps. Carter, Thompson Reintroduce the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act to Address the Evolving Challenges Posed by AI
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA), Member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee, and Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee, re-introduced the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Securing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Task Force Act.
This legislation will establish a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) dedicated to addressing safety and national security challenges posed by AI. The task force and reporting requirements will ensure effective DHS coordination as AI threats and challenges evolve. Recently, Rep. Carter appeared on CNBC to discuss how to regulate AI while preserving innovation.
“As technology advances in sophistication and use, our commitment to safeguarding against emerging threats and ensuring the responsible advancement of AI technologies must grow stronger too,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m introducing the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Securing AI Task Force Act to take an essential step towards managing the impact of AI on our cybersecurity landscape.”
“Advancements in AI technology are expanding by the day and we need to make sure our cybersecurity defenses are moving with it,” said Ranking Member Thompson. “This bill creates a dedicated CISA task force so the agency can better understand the risks that come with AI and make sure we are prepared to protect the systems and infrastructure Americans rely on every day. I am proud to work alongside Representative Carter to reintroduce this critical legislation and help ensure our defenses are ready for what comes next.”
Background
The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act would:
- Establish a Task Force - Within one year of enactment, the Director of CISA will establish a Task Force comprised of personnel from various offices and divisions to coordinate AI-related directives and activities.
- Address AI Challenges - The Task Force will ensure coordination of efforts to improve the safe and secure design, development, adoption, and deployment of AI. It will assess relevant safety and security initiatives, advise stakeholders on potential cyber risks associated with AI deployment, and identify workforce gaps.
- Increase Accountability - The Task Force will provide biannual briefings to the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate on its activities.

Customers benefit from $8 million in federal investments
NORMAN and PAULS VALLEY, Okla. – Amtrak passengers have a more welcoming experience at two Oklahoma stations following about $8 million in improvements. Amtrak Heartland Flyer trains stop in Norman and Pauls Valley twice daily on the route between Fort Worth, Texas, and Oklahoma City.
“Amtrak is committed to making our stations accessible to all customers and we are actively working on accessibility across the national network where more than 80 stations have accessibility projects under construction.” said Amtrak Vice President of Accessibility Dr. David Handera. “We want all of our stations to provide a welcoming environment for every passenger.”
Improvements enhance the passenger experience by providing a level surface for wheeled mobility devices, strollers and users of rolling luggage.
Twenty-two stations were brought into compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act in the 12 months ending Sept. 30 and another 58 stations are targeted for completion in the next year at a forecasted investment of $300 million. These improvements focus on supporting Amtrak’s goals to enhance the customer experience and bring greater integrated and comprehensive accessibility to stations across the country.
Norman (NOR) $3 million
- The station was built for the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railroad in 1909. Sitting in the heart of historic Norman, the Santa Fe depot is a well-preserved example of Mission Revival architecture, built in brick and limestone, with a cross-gable and clay tile roof. The station now features a 300-foot-long platform with reinstalled brick pavers and accessible paths of travel to and from the station building. Complete are sloped accessible walkways and safety barriers, energy efficient LED light fixtures that provide full coverage lighting at the platform, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
- The designer of record for the project is WSP USA, one of the world’s leading engineering, science and infrastructure solutions firms, bringing together top experts across disciplines and geographies. Centennial Contractors Enterprises provided general contractor services for the project. Oklahoma contractors were Olsson Engineering, Streets Mechanical, Terracon and Greenshade Trees (Oklahoma City), Jesco Electric (Yukon) and Cantera Concrete Company (Tulsa).
Pauls Valley (PVL) $5 million
- Pauls Valley opened its station in 2002 with funding assistance from the Oklahoma Department of Transportation through the Federal Transportation Equity Act for the 21st Century. Built to match the original depot in style, it incorporates a climate-controlled waiting area and restrooms. The station now features a 290-foot-long concrete boarding platform with an embedded brick paver surface. Complete are sloped accessible walkways and safety barriers, energy efficient LED light fixtures that provide full coverage lighting at the platform, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
- The designer of record for the project is HDR Inc., specializing in architecture, engineering, environmental and construction services. George Allen Construction provided general contractor services for the project. Oklahoma contractors were WW Builders and Smith Dressler Electric Services (Duncan) Greenshade Trees (Oklahoma City), Tolbert Tree Care (Pauls Valley), Mills Fene Services (Glenpool), Attaboy Striping and Parking Lot Services (Tecumseh) and Ark Welding & Fab (Ardmore)
Amtrak has invested more than $1 billion since 2011 in accessibility upgrades and improvement projects at 169 stations across the national network to ensure a safe, efficient, and comfortable travel experience for customers. The ADA Stations Program is advancing 116 station designs and 85 station construction projects as part of Amtrak’s ongoing commitment to providing accessibility by working toward 100% completion by 2029.
These Amtrak projects receive specific Congressional funding directed by the Federal Railroad Administration. The Amtrak Heartland Flyer (Trains 821 & 822) are sponsored by the Oklahoma and Texas state transportation departments.
Reactions:
“Amtrak’s improvements to both the Norman and Pauls Valley stations in Oklahoma will enhance accessibility for wheeled mobility devices, strollers, and users of rolling luggage. As the representative for both stations, I am excited to see infrastructure accessibility being enhanced throughout my district and am grateful to see Amtrak make this investment,” said Cong. Tom Cole (Okla. 4th)
“The improvements to Norman’s historic Santa Fe Depot will help ensure that this important transportation connection is accessible and welcoming to everyone who travels through our community. The Heartland Flyer is an integral part of Norman’s transportation network, and we’re grateful to see this investment in a station that has served our community for more than a century,” said Norman Mayor Stephen Tyler Holman.
“We appreciate the work Amtrak has done to improve the station here in Pauls Valley and the investment they have made in our community. These improvements help create a welcoming place for residents and visitors and support our efforts to bring more people into our downtown. We see Amtrak as an important economic driver for Pauls Valley, connecting travelers to our local businesses, attractions, and events. We value this partnership and look forward to continuing to work together to grow ridership and create more opportunities for our community,” said Pauls Villey City Manager Joe Livingston.

HUNTSVILLE, Ala. – Three individuals have been charged in separate but related indictments for illegal firearms possession and threats of violence, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr.

A two-count indictment filed in U.S. District Court charges Levi Clifton Belcher, 18, of Huntsville, Alabama, with possession of an unregistered National Firearms Act Weapon and interstate transmission of threatening communications.

In separate but related indictments, Tadashi Ereckson, 38, and Anthony Elijah Slota, 28, both of Huntsville, Alabama, were charged with possession of an unregistered National Firearms Act Weapon.

“My office will take every available step to prosecute credible threats against law enforcement,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. I’m grateful for the partnership between FBI, ATF, HSI, and the Huntsville Police Department. Their diligent investigation led to these prosecutions.”

“I’m proud of the men and women of our FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force and all our partners across North Alabama," said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. "Their partnership and dedication are vital to Protecting (capital P) the Homeland. Together, we will swiftly confront any threat to public safety in full defense of the U.S. Constitution.”

“The relationships that the ATF has fostered with our state, local, and federal law enforcement partners allows us to rapidly investigate reports of federal violations and threats of violence,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge James VanVliet. “This case is another example of those collaborative and unified efforts to protect the communities that we serve.”

“HSI is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to identify and investigate credible threats of violence against federal law enforcement personnel and the communities we serve,” said Ellen Johnson, Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI in Georgia and Alabama. “This case demonstrates the importance of information sharing and coordinated action to address alleged threats before they can escalate. HSI will continue to work alongside our federal, state, and local partners to protect public safety and uphold the rule of law.”

According to court documents, on December 18, 2025, the FBI’s National Threat Operations Center was alerted by an individual to a social media post by Belcher that contained threats of violence against Immigration and Custom Enforcement agents.

According to court documents, on September 10, 2026, ATF agents and Intelligence Research Specialists located Belcher’s vehicle in Decatur, Alabama and began surveillance. During the surveillance, agents observed Belcher and Slota wearing body armor, carrying multiple firearms, and in possession of military-style backpacks. Belcher and Slota were observed entering Belcher’s vehicle, which then traveled toward Huntsville. Officers with the Huntsville Police Department conducted a traffic stop on the vehicle. Belcher and Slota who were armed with rifles and two 3D printed pistols. Officers searched the vehicle and located rifle and pistol magazines with various anti-government sentiments written on them, along with hundreds of rounds of ammunition. Belcher and Slota were arrested.

Officers then obtained a search warrant for the residence that Belcher and Slota were known to stay at in Huntsville, Alabama. During the execution of the search warrant, Erekson was arrested after attempting to reach for a concealed pistol on his ankle while being detained.

FBI, ATF and Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case along with the Huntsville Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney John M. Hundscheid is prosecuting the case.

An indictment contains only charges. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
title: Three Individuals Indicted on Firearm Charges After One Allegedly Made Threats of Violence

WASHINGTON — The Office of the United States Trade Representative has invoked the Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRM) in the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) to review whether workers at GLM Components Mexico, S.A. de C.V. (GLM Components), located in Puebla, Mexico, are being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. The United States has suspended liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the GLM Components facility, which manufactures auto parts.
Background
The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On September 8, 2026, the ILC received an RRM petition from the Sindicato Regeneración Nacional de Trabajadores y Empleados de la República Mexicana “Morenas,” a Mexican independent union. The petition alleges that GLM Components is violating workers’ rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining, including by interfering with union activity and unlawfully firing workers in retaliation for union activity.
The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. After conducting this review, the ILC determined that there is sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms under the USMCA. As a result, the Trade Representative has submitted a request to Mexico under Annex 31-A of the USMCA that Mexico review whether workers at GLM Components are being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. The Trade Representative has also directed the Secretary of the Treasury to suspend liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the GLM Components facility.
Mexico has 10 days to agree to conduct a review and, if it agrees, 45 days from today to complete the review.
A copy of the request for review can be found here.
A copy of the letter to the Secretary of the Treasury can be found here.
Information about previous requests can be found here.
###
title: United States Seeks Mexico’s Review of Alleged Denial of Workers’ Rights at GLM Components Mexico

Rep. Torres Introduces the Improving Access to WIC Act to Ease Access to Nutrition Support for Moms and Children
With More Than 4 in 10 WIC-eligible families Not Enrolled, Legislation Closes Gap by Helping States Strengthen Partnerships with Healthcare Providers, Lower Barriers to Participation, and Boost Outreach Efforts
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) introduced the Improving Access to WIC Act, legislation to make it easier to enroll in and stay connected to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). As families struggle with the ongoing affordability crisis, WIC helps feed mothers from the moment they find out they are pregnant to when their children are five years old. WIC not only helps moms access free, healthy foods, but also helps with breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health resources.
Nearly 25,000 mothers, infants, and children benefit from WIC in California’s 35th Congressional District. Nationwide, in fiscal year 2025, WIC served 6.9 million participants every month. The program is proven to save lives and improve lifetime health outcomes. Despite this, the most recent data show that more than 4 in 10 eligible individuals do not participate in WIC, and WIC utilization is lower for pregnant mothers and 1- to 4-year-olds. This legislation will tackle this participation gap.
The Improving Access to WIC Act would establish a federal grant program for states, tribes, and territories to improve access to, participation in, and retention in WIC. States that opt into the program would receive flexible funding to help strengthen partnerships between WIC agencies and healthcare providers, modernize the enrollment experience, improve community outreach, and help enroll mothers and children on SNAP and Medicaid who already qualify for WIC but do not yet participate.
“WIC provides critical nutrition assistance to moms, babies, and young children, and getting enrolled should not mean jumping through unnecessary hoops,” said Congresswoman Torres. “Moms are already juggling doctor’s appointments, work, child care, and countless responsibilities. We should be making it easier, not harder, for eligible families to access the support they need. My Improving Access to WIC Act will help states integrate WIC enrollment with healthcare providers, reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork, and make it easier for families to enroll and stay on WIC.”
“Despite the incredible public health benefits of WIC, we are still reaching only a little more than half of eligible families. Investing in targeted outreach, data sharing, and healthcare linkages will make it easier for families who qualify to connect with WIC. We thank Rep. Torres for her leadership and support for WIC.” Georgia Machell, President & CEO, National WIC Association
“WIC is an evidence-based, time-limited program with proven positive outcomes for families and communities, yet there is a significant portion of eligible families not connected to services. Supporting innovative outreach methods and healthcare linkages to improve access to the program is an important investment. We appreciate Rep. Torres’s support for WIC and young families.” Megan Esparza, Executive Director, California WIC Association
“The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC) is one of the most critical tools pediatricians have to ensure infants and young children can receive proper nutrition support in their earliest years. The Improving Access to WIC Act would provide states with resources to make enrolling eligible families in WIC easier, more efficient, and more effective. The American Academy of Pediatrics thanks Representative Torres for introducing this important legislation and calls on Congress to advance it,” said Andrew D. Racine, MD, PhD, FAAP, President of the American Academy of Pediatrics.
“The American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists has a long history of supporting the WIC program and is proud to endorse the Improving Access to WIC Act,” said ACOG President Camille A. Clare, MD, MPH, CPE. “Families are facing growing financial pressure, and putting healthy food on the table can be especially difficult during pregnancy and after a baby is born. With significant changes to SNAP under H.R. 1, making WIC easier to access is more important than ever. This bill would help eligible families get the nutrition support they need instead of getting stuck in red tape. ACOG thanks Rep. Norma Torres for her leadership and commitment to strengthening the WIC program.”
"WIC is a proven intervention that supports the health of women, babies, and young children. Yet far too many eligible families are missing out on the many benefits of the program. We applaud Rep. Torres for introducing the Improving Access to WIC Act. Establishing a federal grant program to help states improve access to and participation in WIC would make it easier for eligible families to connect with this critical support. We urge Members of Congress to co-sponsor this legislation, so more families are connected to the nutrition they need to thrive." - Crystal FitzSimons, President of the Food Research & Action Center (FRAC).
The bill is supported by: National WIC Association (NWA), California WIC Association (CWA), American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), Food Research and Action Center (FRAC), Alliance to End Hunger, Coalition on Human Needs.
Bill Summary:
The Improving Access to WIC Act authorizes $50 million for Fiscal Years 2027 through 2031 for the grant program. States, tribes, and territories that choose to opt in would receive, to the maximum extent practicable, $200,000 and an additional amount based on each participating state’s national share of WIC participants.
The bill also requires the U.S. Department of Agriculture to publicly report on the program’s outcomes, including its impact on WIC participation and retention, and share best practices that states can use to improve enrollment and access.
Under the legislation, participating states could use grant funding to:
- Connect more eligible families with WIC by: 
  - Improving outreach in clinical settings and building up systems to make it easier for doctors and health care providers to directly refer patients to WIC, including through statewide referral systems, and
  - Expanding outreach in trusted community settings, including at Head Start and Early Head Start programs, preschools, schools, and other places to meet WIC-eligible families where they are.
- Improve secure data sharing between health care providers and WIC agencies to streamline WIC referrals and certification, while protecting privacy, requiring individual consent, and maintaining federal confidentiality protections.
- Reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork by making it easier for health care providers, consistent with applicable laws and with individuals’ consent, to securely provide WIC agencies with information such as height, weight, hemoglobin measurements (blood tests), and other documentation needed for WIC certification.
- Modernize the enrollment process, including by establishing or expanding online WIC applications.
- Help reach and enroll moms and children on Medicaid (Medi-Cal) or SNAP (CalFresh) who already qualify for WIC, but are not participating.
Original Cosponsors: Nanette Barragán (CA-44); Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01); Yvette Clarke (NY-09 ); Jim Costa (CA-21); Jasmine Crockett (TX-30); Chris Deluzio (PA-17); Debbie Dingell (MI-06); Sylvia Garcia (TX-29); Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04); Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07); Glenn Ivey (MD-04); Pramila Jayapal (WA-07); Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37); Robin Kelly (IL-02); Tim Kennedy (NY-26); Kelly Morrison (MN-03); Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00); Chellie Pingree (ME-01); Lateefah Simon (CA-12); Melanie Stansbury (NM-01); Juan Vargas (CA-52);

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Colin Reece Neher, age 22, of Ardmore, Oklahoma, entered a guilty plea to one count of Possession of Certain Material Involving the Sexual Exploitation of a Minor, punishable by up to 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

The Indictment alleged that beginning in or about February 2022, and continuing until on or about May 21, 2026, Neher knowingly possessed and accessed with intent to view one or more matters which contained visual depictions of a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The Honorable Gerald L. Jackson, Magistrate Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, accepted the plea and ordered the completion of a presentence investigation report.

A U.S. District Court Judge will determine the sentence to be imposed after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Neher was remanded into the custody of the United States Marshals Service pending sentencing.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Morgan Muzljakovich and Nicole Paladino represented the United States.
title: Ardmore Resident Pleads Guilty To Possessing Child Sexual Exploitation Material

The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) announced today a $150 million conditional loan commitment to PsiQuantum, Corp. to enhance the company's advanced manufacturing and prototyping capabilities in the United States. Building on OSC's ongoing collaboration with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)'s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, the proposed loan follows recently awarded funding agreements with DARPA and CHIPS and supports PsiQuantum's novel photonic approach to developing the world's first commercially useful fault-tolerant quantum computer (FTQC).
The potential financing executes on President Donald J. Trump's mandate to drive and sustain U.S. leadership in the strategically important field of quantum information science and technology. Quantum computing is now regarded, alongside Super Intelligence (SI) and semiconductors, as a foundational technology for future economic and military advantage.
"OSC's proposed transaction with PsiQuantum directly aligns with President Donald J. Trump's mandate to accelerate development and commercialization of quantum computing. Quantum computing will provide transformational capabilities, and the Department of War's investment into PsiQuantum serves the mission of securing U.S. leadership in quantum computing in full alignment with Department of War objectives set forth by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth," said David A. Lorch, Director of the Office of Strategic Capital and Senior Advisor to Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg.
"Funding the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing is a national security imperative,"added Peter B. Zuckerman, Senior Managing Director at OSC. "We must scale this critical technology to secure our technological edge and deny adversaries a decisive strategic advantage."
"I applaud OSC for this strategic collaboration with DARPA and CHIPS, which demonstrates how the Department of War is moving at breakneck speed to meet President Trump's directive that the United States must lead in quantum. Quantum computing will shape the future of warfare and fundamentally change how the Joint Force solves its most complex operational challenges," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
The conditional loan commitment between OSC and PsiQuantum specifies customary additional steps the company must take to proceed toward financial close, including satisfying financial, legal, technical, due diligence, and other requirements.
title: Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital Signs $150 Million Conditional Loan Commitment With PsiQuantum

Rep. Vasquez Leads Effort with State and Local Officials to Push for Federal Coordination in Response to Recent Flooding
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 8, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) led a delegation of federal, state, and local leaders in a letter to federal agencies urging them to tour the damage and provide all available resources to those affected by the recent flooding across southern New Mexico.
The letter asks the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC) to visit affected communities, work with local leaders, and provide assistance to homes, communities, farms and businesses impacted by the flooding.
“It is imperative that your agencies act now to cut red tape, reduce bureaucratic barriers, increase communication and responsiveness, and act as a partner in this recovery,” wrote Vasquez. “Due to the nature of this area, the complex patchwork of federal land, critical agricultural areas, and proximity to the border, this response will require your agencies to work hand-in-hand with state, county, and local leaders on both short-term recovery and long-term mitigation efforts.”
The letter is joined by State Senator Jeff Steinborn, State Representative Nathan P. Small, Hatch Mayor Dennis Torres, and Caballo Soil and Water Conservation District Chairman Harvey Morrow.
On October 4th, Rep. Vasquez hosted a meeting in Doña Ana County with local elected officials and visited families and farms impacted by the recent flooding. He visited Hatch, the McLeod/Garfield Dam, and surrounding areas to assess the impact of the flooding and what the community needed for recovery firsthand. During this visit, Rep. Vasquez also discussed Hatch’s immediate recovery needs, available state and federal resources, and opportunities for continued coordination to support the community’s recovery and infrastructure needs.
Read the full letter HERE.

title: Rep. Vasquez Leads Effort with State and Local Officials to Push for Federal Coordination in Response to Recent Flooding

Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.
2026 was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and devastating lives. Weather conditions, exacerbated by extended drought, heat, and wind, caused over 900,000 acres, or 1,400 square miles, to burn across Washington state – taking homes and lives. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead.
In the Eighth District, the Little Giant, Three Queens, Sisi, King, Goat, and West Fork fires – among others – devastated communities, property, livestock, and businesses. The damages from this wildfire season continues to overwhelm state, local, Tribal, nonprofit, and private-sector capabilities.
“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” members of the delegation wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”
Joining Congresswoman Schrier in the letter to President Trump were Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), and U.S. Representatives Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Dan Newhouse (R, WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (R, WA-05), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10).
The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”
“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.
The full letter is available HERE.
title: Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State

Winning the race for quantum leadership is essential to preserving the United States' technological edge and securing its national security. President Trump made American leadership in quantum information science a national priority through Executive Order 14413, ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation. Today, building on the call to renew bold, ambitious national missions in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios' report Science: A New Golden Age, the Department of War is accelerating its efforts to identify, develop, and prepare for quantum computing capabilities that will underpin future national security missions.
In support of President Trump's mandate for American leadership in quantum, the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (R&E) today announced new initiatives and programmatic updates totaling approximately $350 million to strengthen U.S. leadership in quantum computing capabilities that support national security.
"Dominance in quantum information science is a critical priority for both President Trump and the Department of War. Maintaining American leadership in this field is essential to preserving our technological edge, and R&E is uniquely positioned to drive the innovation needed across academia and industry," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
R&E will direct greater attention across the Department of War's innovation ecosystem toward identifying mission-relevant applications of quantum computing, particularly as sufficiently capable quantum computers become available. R&E expects that quantum-enabled applications in disciplines such as chemistry, materials science, and physics will enable the development of next-generation weapons, platforms, and other critical capabilities that are more lethal, cost-effective, and manufacturable.
This new effort will build on existing Department of War programs and complement related national initiatives led by the Department of Energy (DOE), particularly its recently announced Quantum Genesis Priority Applications and the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, as well as initiatives led by the National Science Foundation (NSF) and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). In coordination with DOE's Office of Science, the National Nuclear Security Administration, and the Laboratory for Physical Sciences, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) will host a series of application workshops beginning before January 2027. The workshops will bring together end users and quantum-algorithm experts to identify high-value use cases, accelerate industrially relevant quantum advantage, create economic opportunity, and strengthen national defense.
DARPA is also advancing the technical validation needed to determine whether prospective quantum computing systems can deliver utility at scale. Through its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, DARPA announced the advancement of four prospective quantum-computing providers to Stage C of the initiative, representing approximately $200 million in new funding that builds on more than $650 million in investments from DARPA in prospective quantum-computing providers. During Stage C, participants will work with DARPA to verify and validate that their utility-scale quantum-computer concepts can be constructed as designed and operated as intended. Advancement to Stage C indicates that each participant has demonstrated a research and development plan capable of realizing a utility-scale quantum computer; characterized key program risks and mitigation measures; and developed prototype requirements to retire those risks.
A strong quantum industrial base is essential to maintaining U.S. leadership in science and technology. To help build that foundation, the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital today announced an approximately $150 million conditional loan commitment to support PsiQuantum's advanced manufacturing and prototyping capabilities in the United States.
Together, these efforts will advance the Department's understanding of quantum computing's future national security applications and strengthen avenues for companies to deliver systems capable of executing them.
title: Department of War Announces $350 Million in Quantum Computing Initiatives
