Ranking Member Raskin, Rep. Dean Demand DOJ Investigate Former Bard College President After Uncovering His Email Asking Whether Young Woman Was “for Me” or Epstein Himself, Reveal History of Sex Abuse Coverup at Bard
Records Indicate Epstein Was Trafficking the Young Woman Across State and International Lines When He Sent Her to Meet Botstein, Who Asked Epstein: “Is [She] for Me or Are You Keeping Her for Yourself?”
Evidence Contradicts DOJ Insistence That Epstein Trafficked Only to “Himself,” and Clearly Meets the Standard for Launching a Criminal Investigation; DOJ and FBI’s Inaction Left Possible Epstein Co-Conspirator in a Position of Power Over Young Students and Faculty
More Than a Dozen Whistleblowers Describe Decades of Unpunished Sexual Misconduct at Bard, Including Allegations Botstein Groped Women and Intervened in Title IX Proceedings to Protect Offenders
Raskin and Dean Call on DOJ and FBI to Investigate Botstein and Other Potential Epstein Co-Conspirators, Release Complete Files, and Protect Survivors’ Identities
Washington, D.C. (October 7, 2026)—Today, Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Madeleine Dean demanded a federal investigation into former Bard College President Leon Botstein after reviewing an email in which Botstein asked Jeffrey Epstein about a young woman Epstein was trafficking: “Is [Jane Doe] for me, or are you keeping her for yourself.” In a separate letter to Bard’s leadership, Ranking Member Raskin sought records concerning Epstein’s use of the college to advance his trafficking activities and allegations from more than a dozen whistleblowers about sexual misconduct at Bard, including allegations that Botstein personally engaged in misconduct and intervened in Title IX proceedings to protect offenders.
The letters—to Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel, and to Bard Board Chair Brandon Weber and Acting President Jonathan Becker—detail communications concerning a young foreign model and aspiring vocalist whom Epstein sent to Botstein in May 2014. They also question why DOJ exposed her name hundreds of times and released photographs showing her face while redacting Botstein’s email address.
“[T]his evidence, and the facts laid out in the Epstein files, surely meet and exceed the federal law enforcement standard for initiating a criminal investigation: the existence of evidence that a crime ‘may have occurred.’ These facts strongly indicate that a crime may have occurred. Yet, you have done nothing, and launched no investigation, about this incident which you and your staff must have known of for at least 18 months. In so doing, you have effectively permitted a potential co-conspirator of Jeffrey Epstein to stay in a position of power over young students, faculty and staff for an additional year at least,” wrote Ranking Member Raskin and Rep. Dean to Blanche and Patel.
Emails and messages reviewed by the Committee show that Epstein groomed the young woman throughout 2014, offering advice and assistance with her education and career in the United States. After meeting Jane Doe in Paris, Epstein directed his assistant, Lesley Groff, to arrange private flights from her home country to destinations including Canada, New York, Florida, New Mexico and his island. A message to Epstein included a photograph of Jane Doe giving a woman, possibly Ghislaine Maxwell, a nude massage.
That May, Epstein sent Jane Doe to meet Botstein, ostensibly to assess her musical abilities and provide educational guidance. In an email from his Bard account, Botstein asked whether Jane Doe was “for me”. As he did with other survivors, Epstein relied on Botstein to assuage parental concerns about the sex offender, in this case by requesting orchestra tickets for the young woman’s parents to attend a Bard concert abroad. Epstein also asked Botstein to give them special treatment.
The evidence uncovered by the Committee contradicts the July 2025 DOJ–FBI memorandum and numerous follow-up claims by FBI Director Patel and Attorney General Blanche asserting that investigators found no evidence warranting an investigation of Epstein’s uncharged associates. Ranking Member Raskin demanded answers about why DOJ exposed the young woman’s identity while redacting Botstein’s email address, who directed that disparate treatment, and whom they were seeking to protect. Committee staff identified documents that still expose her name and provided the list separately to DOJ for redaction. The letters omit citations to DOJ documents to protect her identity.
Separately, more than a dozen whistleblowers have provided Committee staff information about a culture of sexual misconduct at Bard spanning decades. Multiple reports accuse Botstein of groping women and asking sexualized questions during tenure interviews. Whistleblowers described Botstein personally overseeing Title IX adjudications for the majority of his tenure as president and faculty being told that certain individuals accused of abuse were “protected by Botstein.”
The Bard letter also details allegations involving a senior tenured professor who remains on campus, including that he invited a male student into his bed and supplied alcohol to the point of alcohol poisoning. That allegation appeared in a sworn federal complaint and was corroborated by whistleblower statements.
“I write to share damning evidence that Botstein likely enabled and possibly even participated in Epstein’s abuse while serving as Bard’s President, as well as deeply troubling whistleblower reports that Botstein used his influence on Bard’s campus to influence Title IX proceedings and protect sexual predators on the Bard faculty,” wrote Ranking Member Raskin to Weber and Becker.
The letters follow Ranking Member Raskin’s June 17 inquiry into Bard’s Epstein ties, which questioned the scope and adequacy of WilmerHale’s internal review. Raskin commended new Bard leadership for their initial cooperation and reiterated his requests for all Bard and Smolny College records relating to Epstein and his associates, along with the records WilmerHale reviewed. He also sought sexual misconduct complaint and Title IX investigation records involving specific faculty and administrators, with detailed requests provided separately. Botstein continues to reside in the President’s House and conduct a Bard orchestra, with concerts scheduled with students this fall and next spring.
Ranking Member Raskin demanded that DOJ and FBI investigate Botstein and other potential Epstein co-conspirators, including Leon Black, Jes Staley, Les Wexner, Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem, Richard Khan, Darren Indyke, Lesley Groff and Larry Visoski, and release the complete Epstein files with victims’ identities protected and congressional staff granted access to unredacted versions. DOJ and FBI’s refusal to investigate is part of a broader effort to protect President Donald Trump.
“Ultimately, we understand that your outrageous abandonment of your responsibilities is not about Leon Botstein. It is about protecting another individual who appears frequently in the Epstein files who also may have been a co-conspirator in Jeffrey Epstein’s brutal and sickening sex trafficking operation. And yet you continue to show the world that you would rather let a dozen, even 100, or 1,000 human sex traffickers go free than allow the possibility of an honest investigation of the conduct of one man,” concluded Ranking Member Raskin and Rep. Dean.

DeLauro’s Urgent Message to CT Farmers: Don’t Miss Out; Apply Today!
Today, Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro urged Connecticut’s farmers to apply for disaster relief funding she secured for their recovery:
“I wrote the Farm Recovery and Support Block Grant for farmers who too often get left behind when disaster strikes. Today, I am urging every one of them to apply. Round One closes tonight at 11:59 PM. The earlier you apply, the faster you’ll get the money you’re owed. Busy on the farm? No problem, the application portal will remain open after today.
“Applying is simple: go to portal.ct.gov/FRS today. You will find the application, eligibility details, and partner organizations ready to help you fill it out. Whether you run a few acres of vegetables, an orchard, or a family dairy, this money is meant for you. Don’t miss out; apply today!”
title: DeLauro’s Urgent Message to CT Farmers: Don’t Miss Out; Apply Today!

Over $10 million invested in North Carolina station accessibility improvements
HAMLET AND ROCKY MOUNT, N.C., Oct. 7, 2026 – Amtrak joined federal, state and local officials this week to celebrate the completion of accessibility improvement projects at its stations in Hamlet and Rocky Mount, marking more than $10 million in investments to improve accessibility, safety and the customer experience for rail travelers in North Carolina.
“These investments demonstrate Amtrak’s commitment to providing safe, accessible and convenient rail travel for all customers,” said Amtrak Vice President of Accessibility, Stations & Facilities Dr. David Handera. “Stations like Hamlet and Rocky Mount are important community assets, and these enhancements will help ensure they continue serving residents and visitors for many years to come.”
At Hamlet Station, Amtrak completed approximately $3.2 million in improvements, including construction of two 200-foot accessible boarding platforms, accessible pathways and walkways, safety barriers, LED platform lighting, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
At Rocky Mount Station, Amtrak completed approximately $7.3 million in improvements, including construction of an 840-foot accessible boarding platform, accessible pathways connecting the station, public right-of-way and parking areas, LED platform lighting, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
Together, these projects improve accessibility for customers of all abilities and support better travel experiences. The improvements were made possible through strong collaboration among Amtrak, the North Carolina Department of Transportation, the Federal Railroad Administration, local officials, and community partners.
These efforts support Amtrak’s broader efforts to modernize stations and create a more seamless travel experience for customers nationwide. Amtrak continues to advance station accessibility projects across the country as part of its long-term commitment to achieving a fully accessible national passenger rail network.
REACTIONS
Jason Orthner, NCDOT Rail Division Director
“Continued investments in stations like Hamlet and Rocky Mount make it safer and easier for passengers of all abilities to access rail service and continue their journeys These improvements strengthen the passenger experience today while supporting the continued growth and future of intercity passenger rail across North Carolina.”
Hamlet Mayor, Amy Guinn
“Amtrak’s recent substantial investment in our historic train depot demonstrates their continued commitment to rural communities. Enabling passengers of all abilities to access travel enhances the experience and ensures everyone can enjoy the freedom of travel by rail. The City of Hamlet greatly appreciates the collaboration of all the departments working together to accomplish these improvements.”
Rocky Mount Mayor, Sandy Roberson
“As much as any place in North Carolina, Rocky Mount is a railroad town. We are grateful to Amtrak in partnership with the NC Department of Transportation and the Federal Railroad Administration for the improvements that will make our historic train station more accessible, more welcoming, and more convenient for everyone who uses it.”
title: Amtrak Celebrates Completion of Accessibility Improvements at Hamlet and Rocky Mount Stations

Boyle Statement on Nonpartisan Watchdog Finding Trump Administration Illegally Withheld Health Research Funding
PHILADELPHIA, PA — Congressman Brendan F. Boyle (PA-02), Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee, issued the following statement after the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that the Department of Health and Human Services violated the Impoundment Control Act by withholding congressionally appropriated funding for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ). The finding comes after Boyle raised concerns about cuts affecting research at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) and the University of Pennsylvania and demanded answers from the Trump Administration:
“GAO has made clear that the Administration violated the law by withholding funding Congress provided for critical health research. In Philadelphia, these cuts threaten lifesaving work, along with good-paying jobs and one of the most important drivers of our regional economy. I will continue fighting to protect Philadelphia’s research institutions and ensure the funding Congress provides is actually put to work.”
BACKGROUND
In August, Boyle joined researchers from CHOP and Penn to oppose the Administration’s cuts to AHRQ-supported programs and highlight their impact on Philadelphia. Researchers warned that the funding losses threatened ongoing medical research, research jobs, and programs training the next generation of scientists.
Boyle also sent a letter to Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought and AHRQ Director Roger Klein seeking information about the canceled and withheld funding, including whether the Administration intended to fully obligate funding appropriated by Congress. To date, the Administration has not responded to Ranking Member Boyle's questions about withholding this money.
GAO concluded that HHS violated the Impoundment Control Act when it refused to spend appropriated AHRQ funds, without submitting the special message to Congress required by law.
The stakes extend beyond individual research grants. Philadelphia is one of the country’s leading life sciences hubs, with more than 88,000 life sciences workers across the Greater Philadelphia region, and recent data show employment in biotechnology research and pharmaceutical manufacturing reaching record levels. Federal research investments help support that broader ecosystem of hospitals, universities, scientists, startups, and high-skilled jobs.
As the top Democrat on the House Budget Committee, Boyle has made protecting Congress’s constitutional power of the purse a central focus of his oversight work, repeatedly challenging efforts by the Executive Branch to freeze or withhold funding approved by Congress. Congressman Boyle’s Congressional Power of the Purse Act strengthens Congress’s authorities under the Impoundment Control Act (ICA) and creates criminal penalties for violations of the ICA.

Elfreth Leads Colleagues in Urging $11 Million in Additional Funding for Mental Health Support at Cyber Command Following Suicides
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (D-MD-03), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, led her colleagues on the Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation (CITI) Subcommittee of the House Armed Services Committee and the Maryland Delegation in requesting an additional $11 million in funding for mental health support at U.S. Cyber Command following reports of multiple suicides earlier this year. On the letter from the CITI members, Elfreth was joined by Representatives Don Bacon (R-NE-02), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Rich McCormick (R-GA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06), Herbert Conaway (D-NJ-03), Eugene Vindman (D-VA-07), and Pat Ryan (D-NY-18). On the letter from the Maryland members, Elfreth was joined by her Maryland delegation colleagues, including Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), who co-led the letter, along with Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), and Representatives Steny Hoyer (D-MD-05), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02), and April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06). Both letters were directed to the heads of the House and Senate Appropriations Committees.
“We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training… Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions,” wrote the CITI members.
“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” wrote the Maryland lawmakers. “Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively ‘deployed in place’ for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.”
“One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at NSA and Cyber Command has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again,” wrote the CITI members.
In last year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Elfreth specifically secured a provision, H.R. 6630, the Expanding Mental Health Access for Cyber Command Personnel Act (Sec. 1506), requiring U.S. Cyber Command and the Cyber Mission Force to hire mental health professionals with security clearances at each of their operating locations. The amendment also requires quarterly briefings on the status of the initiative, validating the clearances, challenges carrying out the initiative, and efforts to improve awareness among troops regarding the cleared physicians. The $11 million in funding would ensure full funding of this provision.
Elfreth continues to work alongside U.S. Cyber Command to bring additional mental health resources to Fort Meade. Elfreth is working to rectify the reporting requirements and include civilian employees in DoD’s suicide data, especially at installations like Fort Meade where civilian and uniformed officers work side by side on the same projects.
Elfreth is also working to address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses from out of state. During conversations with mental health professionals, Elfreth heard that the transfer of licenses can take several months to almost a year before these professionals can begin practicing in Maryland and on military bases. At the state level, she is working with partners, including Senator Dawn Gile and Secretary Ed Rothstein of the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, to address delays and barriers to military-connected mental health professionals transferring or obtaining professional licensure in Maryland.
The full CITI letter can be accessed HERE. The full Maryland letter can be accessed HERE.
###
title: Elfreth Leads Colleagues in Urging $11 Million in Additional Funding for Mental Health Support at Cyber Command Following Suicides

Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (CA-26) joined 189 Members of Congress in demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.
In the House, the letter is led by Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08), Early Childhood and Elementary and Secondary Education Subcommittee Ranking Member Bonamici (D-OR-01), and Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13). In the Senate, the letter is led by Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Sanders (I-VT), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA), and Senator Ben RayLuján (D-NM).
The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.
“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”
Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely. These actions serve the Trump Administration’s goal to end the Head Start program as laid out on page 482 of Project 2025.

Representative John W. Mannion Announces $500,000 Federal Grant for Brownfield Cleanups and Infrastructure Investments in the City of Utica
UTICA, N.Y. – Representative John W. Mannion today announced that the City of Utica will receive $500,000 in federal funding to support environmental cleanup projects and infrastructure initiatives. 
Representative John W. Mannion said, “This funding will provide the City of Utica with additional resources to turn vacant sites into safe, productive spaces. This brownfield grant will protect public health, create new opportunities for growth, and strengthen our neighborhoods. I will continue working with our local leaders to ensure our communities get the support they deserve, and I look forward to seeing this project drive lasting change in the region.” 
The City of Utica will use the award to conduct assessments, cleanups, and revitalize polluted brownfield areas. These investments will support the local economy, support redevelopment, and protect public health for Utica residents. Utica plans to conduct over a dozen site assessments and hold almost 20 community meetings throughout the process. 
The funding was awarded by the Environmental Protection Agency through the Brownfields Multipurpose, Assessment, Revolving Loan Fund, and Cleanup Cooperative Agreements. The program provides federal resources to address sites contaminated by hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants and petroleum. 
# # #
title: Representative John W. Mannion Announces $500,000 Federal Grant for Brownfield Cleanups and Infrastructure Investments in the City of Utica

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 7, 2026

The following is the text of a joint statement by the United States of America and the Hellenic Republic on the occasion of the sixth U.S.-Greece Strategic Dialogue.

Begin text:

On October 7, 2026, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs George Gerapetritis presided over the 6th round of the U.S.-Greece Strategic Dialogue and held discussions on a wide area of global issues. The two sides reaffirmed their steadfast, long and deep bilateral relations in the context of shared democratic values and Greece’s role as an active NATO ally. Anchoring their discussions in shared priorities, both sides committed to deepen defense ties, bolster trade and investment, and promote cultural ties.

DEFENSE AND SECURITY COOPERATION

Greece and the United States reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen their longstanding defense and security cooperation. The United States and Greece announced $4 billion in Foreign Military Sales in support of Greece’s long-term defense plan to deepen our interoperability, and to explore future opportunities for defense industrial base cooperation, including on innovative technologies. They finalized Greece’s participation in the U.S. National Guard Bureau’s State Partnership Program with Florida, and enhanced interoperability through the provision of Stryker vehicles to Greece. Both sides reaffirmed the strategic value of our defense cooperation in support of bilateral and NATO security objectives. They expanded law enforcement and counterterrorism cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to address illegal migration.

ECONOMIC AND TRADE COOPERATION

Greece and the United States reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening two-way trade and investment. They recognized the importance of economic security and intend to partner to strengthen investment screening and protect critical infrastructure procurements. With Greece’s status as a Pax Silica signatory, the two sides welcomed growing cooperation in super intelligence, high-performance computing, cybersecurity, and advanced technologies. They highlighted deepening energy ties, building on the November 2025 P-TEC ministerial, the Vertical Gas Corridor, and hydrocarbon exploration. They underscored the significance of maritime collaboration and signed an agreement on certification for U.S. seafarers on Greek vessels.

CULTURAL TIES

The governments also signed an extension of their Cultural Property Agreement, reaffirming their commitment to protect cultural heritage and combat illicit trafficking networks. In addition, they announced the United States’ first project in Greece under the Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation to highlight shared democratic traditions.

End Text.

WASHINGTON, D.C.— As the Trump Administration prepares propaganda signage to adorn the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, Representative Jamie Raskin (MD-08) introduced legislation to ensure future generations learn about President Donald Trump’s commitment to censoring, whitewashing and fictionalizing American history. The Preserving and Remembering the History of Trump and other Tyrants Act directs officials from the Smithsonian Institution to collect and preserve artifacts reflecting the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism during the Trump presidencies as the basis for a permanent exhibition in the National Museum of American History.
Last month, the Department of the Interior—under orders from President Trump—created propaganda signage to place outside of the National Museum of American History, warning visitors of curators’ “personal, radical ideologies.” Preserving these signs will educate Americans on how authoritarians attempt to control media, government and culture.
“Unlike President Trump’s project of censoring, whitewashing and fictionalizing American history, my legislation will forever preserve his manifestations of authoritarian narcissism and his propagandistic assault on American history and American democracy,” said Rep. Raskin. “To avoid repeating this descent into authoritarianism, we must study this corrupt President’s actions and allow the public to learn about the numerous tools he deployed while attempting to remake American history in his own image and according to his own autocratic and white nationalist beliefs.”
The legislation directs officials from the Smithsonian Institution to preserve the banners bearing President Trump’s face that are currently displayed outside of certain federal agencies; still images and videos from the media; personal narratives of American citizens who resisted and opposed the rise in authoritarianism in the United States; and other artifacts that the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution determines to have historical significance. The legislation also directs officials from the National Park Service to remove any signage that was erected near the National Museum of American History without the consent of Congress.
Rep. Raskin has drawn on his expertise as an American constitutional scholar as he speaks out against the Trump Administration’s authoritarian tactics. This month, he introduced a Resolution condemning President Trump and MAGA’s campaign of book bans and censorship and advocating for the American freedom to read and think freely.
Read the full text of the legislation here.

title: Raskin Introduces Legislation to Preserve and Document Trump Propaganda and Educate Future Generations on Resistance to Corruption and Authoritarianism

Congresswoman Simon, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Landmark Olmstead Court Decision Supporting Americans with Disabilities on 27th Anniversary
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Simon (CA-12) alongside Reps. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-05), Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), and Tom Kean (R-NJ-07) introduced a bipartisan resolution commemorating the 27th anniversary of the landmark Supreme Court decision, Olmstead v. L.C.. The Olmstead decision prohibits the unnecessary institutionalization of people with disabilities and ensures Americans with disabilities can live full, independent lives and categorized the unjustified institutionalization of people with disabilities as discrimination under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). As the Olmstead decision comes under attack from the Trump Administration, this bipartisan resolution reaffirms the right that people with disabilities have to live, work, and participate in their own homes and communities with independence and dignity.
As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, Congresswoman Simon is committed to defending the disability community from attacks by the Trump Administration and advancing policies that expand accessibility. Congresswoman Simon recently condemned the Trump Administration’s Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services’ move to dispute the Olmstead integration mandate and undermine the key protections outlined by the Olmstead decision.
"Community-based services and supports work. They are more cost-effective, produce better health and quality-of-life outcomes, and honor people with disabilities’ autonomy and self-determination. The consequences of weakening the integration mandate would be profound and impact millions of Americans’ ability to access home and community-based services that allow them to remain among their families, maintain employment, pursue education, and participate in civic life," said Congresswoman Simon. "That's why as the first congenitally blind Member to serve in Congress, I am proud to join my colleagues to reaffirm our bipartisan commitment to the Olmstead decision and fight any attempts to diminish the civil rights of the disability community."
"It is essential that people with disabilities continue to have the right to live, work, and thrive in their own communities with dignity," said Congresswoman Dingell. "This bipartisan resolution reaffirms that we will not allow hard won progress to be rolled back, and that we will continue to protect and support the rights enshrined by the Olmstead decision for every person whose lives it has changed for the better."
"Although the Olmstead decision was issued more than twenty‑five years ago, its significance remains just as strong today. I am pleased to join my colleagues in introducing this resolution, reaffirming our commitment to ending discrimination based on disability," said Congressman Kean.
"For 27 years, the Supreme Court’s decision in Olmstead v. L.C. has informed the advancement of policies to empower individuals with disabilities to live and work independently in our communities," said Congresswoman Scanlon. "Recent attempts to undermine the Olmstead integration mandate and roll back those policies raises new opportunities for discrimination against our friends and neighbors with disabilities, and harms the larger community. I’m proud to join my House colleagues in recognizing Olmstead’s anniversary and recommitting ourselves to protecting community integration for the good of all."
"Olmstead affirmed a fundamental principle: every American deserves the freedom and opportunity to build a full life in the community they call home. As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Disabilities Caucus, that principle has always been at the heart of my work to break down barriers, strengthen independence, and ensure all Americans with disabilities have the resources, support, and opportunities they need to thrive. Twenty-seven years later, our responsibility is not simply to recognize the progress Olmstead made possible, but to protect it, build upon it, and ensure that progress is never reversed," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.
The resolution is endorsed by the Caring Across Generations, United Spinal, ANCOR, Autism Self Advocacy Network, National Council on Independent Living, American Association of People with Disabilities, and the National Disability Rights Network.
A copy of the resolution can be found HERE.

Developed as a Partnership Between Wichita Northwest High School Students and the Drug Free Communities Support Program
WICHITA, KS – Today, the Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, or “Drug Czar,” Sara Carter and Senator Roger Marshall (R-KS) announced a new partnership between the Drug Free Communities Support (DFC) program and Wichita Northwest High School to develop the first youth-led primary prevention toolkit. This toolkit will guide primary prevention efforts throughout the nation by providing evidence-based best practices recommendations adapted to the best suit today’s youth. The toolkit is expected to be released around the back-to-school season in 2027.
“The DFC program has been successful because it empowers local leaders- those who know their communities best- with federal resources to make a difference in the lives of countless young Americans. Among those leaders, and some of our most powerful advocates, are youth themselves,” said Drug Czar Sara Carter. “The students developing this toolkit know better than anyone the pressures their peers face, and how to best overcome them. I look forward to the release of their work.”
“We don’t want the next generation to inherit the drug crisis we are fighting today. We need to empower young people to take this crisis on head-on because they know what their friends and classmates are facing,” said Senator Marshall. “I appreciate Director Carter and ONDCP for putting young people at the center of this effort and giving them the tools to lead. It’s great to see a Kansas school setting an example and empowering students to take ownership in this fight.”
“We are excited that students of our district were selected to help create this national toolkit, giving young people a voice in shaping youth engagement efforts nationwide,” said Superintendent Kelly Bielefeld.
Primary prevention is a cornerstone of President Donald J. Trump’s 2026 National Drug Control Strategy, which governs the Administration’s approach to defeating the drug crisis. This latest partnership comes as the most recent reports indicate drug use among students is now at a near-record low, now the lowest since 1992 and the second-lowest since reporting began.
The White House Office of National Drug Control leads and coordinates U.S. drug policy, develops and implements the President’s the National Drug Control Strategy, and supports communities through the Drug Free Communities Support (DFC) and High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) programs.

Department of Justice Announces Phase Three of Compensation Process for Western Union Fraud Victims
The Department of Justice announced that it has begun the third phase of the remission compensation process to provide recovery for Western Union fraud victims.
In 2017, Western Union entered into a deferred prosecution agreement (DPA) with the Department of Justice and agreed to forfeit $586 million. The Department of Justice previously distributed over $436.9 million to more than 180,000 victims. Because additional forfeited funds remain available in this case, the Department of Justice has reopened the petition process to potential victims who did not previously submit a petition for remission.
“The Department is pleased to announce the third and final phase of the Western Union remission process,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Thousands of victims have already obtained over $430 million in compensation in the first two phases, and this third phase represents the Criminal Division’s continued dedication to taking the profit out of crime and compensating victims of fraud.”
“This additional $3.4 million in remission to 1,294 victims and the opening of the Victim Portal represents the U.S. Postal Inspection Service’s commitment to ensuring all victims of consumer fraud are protected,” said Inspector in Charge Christopher Nielsen of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service’s Philadelphia Division. “We are proud of our efforts recovering over $400 million for victims of this fraud, and we thank our partners for their contributions to this cooperative effort.”
Victims of fraud who sent a money transfer through Western Union between Jan. 1, 2004, and March 9, 2020, can file a petition for remission and receive compensation for their fraud losses. Individuals who believe they may be victims may file a petition online or may obtain a petition form online at www.westernunionremissionphase3.com/. The deadline to file a petition for remission is Dec. 31. More information regarding the remission process, including eligibility criteria, updates, and frequently asked questions, is available at www.westernunionremissionphase3.com/ or by calling 1-833-419-4677.
Pursuant to the DPA, Western Union acknowledged responsibility for its criminal conduct, which included violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and aiding and abetting wire fraud, and agreed to forfeit $586 million. This money has been made available to compensate victims of an international consumer fraud scheme. Western Union simultaneously resolved a parallel civil investigation with the Federal Trade Commission.
According to court documents, fraudsters targeted consumers, including seniors, through multiple scams and convinced their victims to send money through Western Union. Three specific scams directed towards seniors included the so-called grandparent scam, where the fraudster would pose as the victim’s relative in purported need of immediate money to avoid personal harm; lottery or sweepstakes scams, where the fraudster would tell the victim that he or she had won a large cash prize but had to pay fees, such as taxes, to claim the prize; and romance scams, where the fraudster would pose as an online love interest and request funds for a visit or for another purpose.
Certain owners, operators, or employees of Western Union locations were complicit in the scheme. Western Union aided and abetted the scheme by failing to suspend or terminate complicit agents and by allowing them to continue to process fraud-induced monetary transactions. Western Union fulfilled its obligations under the DPA, and the court granted the motion to dismiss the criminal information against Western Union in 2020.
The Department of Justice, through the Asset Forfeiture Program, works diligently to restore lost funds to victims of crime and acknowledges the significant assistance of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service Philadelphia Division’s Harrisburg Office in the victim compensation process and in conducting the criminal fraud investigation. Since fiscal year 2000, the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF), which has overseen the remission process, has successfully used its specialized expertise to return more than $13 billion in forfeited assets to victims of crime.
The victim compensation payments in this case would not have been possible without the extraordinary efforts of MNF and the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices for the Middle District of Pennsylvania, the Central District of California, the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, and the Southern District of Florida. The FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, IRS-Criminal Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Reserve Board, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Office of Inspector General, and the Department of the Treasury Office of Inspector General provided valuable assistance. The FTC conducted the civil fraud investigation. MNF Attorney Advisor Brittany R. Van Camp with the section’s Program Management and Training Unit is leading the remission process.
Verita Global LLC (formerly known as Gilardi & Co. LLC) is serving as the remission administrator in this matter. Verita Global LLC and the Department of Justice will not ask for any payment to participate in this remission process.
Neither the Remission Administrator nor the Department of Justice will ask for any payment to participate in this remission process. Please be cautious of any individual or organization claiming to represent the Remission Administrator or the federal government in this matter. If you are a victim, any communications will come directly from the Remission Administrator or from government representatives with whom you have already had contact.
PSA: FBI Warns of the Impersonation of Law Enforcement and Government Officials: www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250418
How To Avoid a Government Impersonation Scam: consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-avoid-government-impersonation-scam
For more information on how to protect yourself from fraud, please visit www.uspis.gov or www.consumer.ftc.gov.
title: Department of Justice Announces Phase Three of Compensation Process for Western Union Fraud Victims

United States Files Civil Suit to Recover Customs Duties and Fraud Penalties exceeding $280M Against Importer and Retailer of Kitchen and Bath Construction and Remodeling Products and Its Chief Executive Officer
The United States has filed a civil fraud lawsuit in the United States Court of International Trade against importer Uni-Tile & Marble Inc., and its chief executive officer, Xin Mian Pan, jointly and severally, to recover $67.9 million in unpaid customs duties on merchandise imported from the People’s Republic of China (China). The government also seeks $222.5 million in fraud penalties from the defendants.
“This filing reflects the Justice Department’s unwavering commitment to enforcing the nation’s trade laws and holding accountable those who attempt to evade them,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “We will continue to use every enforcement tool at our disposal to ensure that U.S. manufacturers and American workers are competing on a level playing field.”
“CBP remains firmly committed to safeguarding the U.S. economy, enforcing fair trade standards, and defending American jobs from unlawful commercial practices,” said Acting Executive Director Salvatore Ingrassia of Cargo and Conveyance Security, Office of Field Operations. “These civil penalties demonstrate that attempts to undermine our economy and American businesses carry serious consequences.”
Specifically, the government alleges that from September 2018 to August 2023, defendants fraudulently transshipped, undervalued, and misdescribed merchandise via a scheme that involved multiple shell companies. As a result of this alleged conduct, defendants made or caused to be made materially false statements and omissions to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) in 503 declared shipments of imported merchandise or “entries” of wooden cabinets and vanities, quartz surface products, ceramic tiles, and other merchandise that deprived the United States of lawful duties.
On Dec. 18, 2025, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California announced criminal conspiracy charges, among other charges, including wire fraud, smuggling, and international money laundering, against Mr. Pan, Uni-Tile, and several other parties involved in defendants’ ongoing scheme to evade custom duties and to violate U.S. trade and finance laws. See Bay Area Businessmen, Chinese National, And Three Companies Charged With Scheme To Evade Millions In Customs Duties, U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of California, (Dec. 18, 2025).
In the civil complaint, the government seeks to enforce CBP’s demand that defendants pay additional duties and penalties because the conduct alleged against defendants in the criminal case also violated 19 U.S.C. § 1592(a), which is a provision of the Tariff Act of 1930.
To combat trade fraud, including avoidance of import duties, the Justice Department created a Trade Fraud Task Force. The Task Force partners with CBP and other law enforcement agencies to ensure compliance with Untied States trade laws
The case is being handled by Civil Division’s Commercial Litigation Branch, National Courts Section and the United States is represented by National Courts Section Trial Attorney Anna Walker.
The claims in the complaint are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability.
Press Release Number: 26-1151
title: United States Files Civil Suit to Recover Customs Duties and Fraud Penalties exceeding $280M Against Importer and Retailer of Kitchen and Bath Construction and Remodeling Products and Its Chief Executive Officer

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07), a 25-year Army veteran, and Raja Krishnamoorthi (Ill.-08), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, introduced legislation that would require the Pentagon to study and apply lessons from Ukraine’s battlefield innovations to U.S. military doctrine and training.
The Learning Effective Strategies and Systems Optimization for National Security (LESSONS) from Ukraine Act would require the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress within 120 days on lessons the U.S. military can draw from the Russia-Ukraine War, including the use of drones and other unmanned systems, electronic and cyber warfare, air defense, operations without GPS or satellite communications, battlefield medicine, and Ukraine’s efforts to expand and decentralize weapons production. The Pentagon would also be required to develop a plan and timetable for incorporating those lessons into U.S. military doctrine and training.
“Ukraine’s defense against Russia has shown just how rapidly modern warfare is evolving. I saw that firsthand during my trip to Ukraine last month, where drones, electronic warfare, cyber operations, and defense manufacturing are reshaping the battlefield in real time,” said Vindman. “As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our military must constantly learn, adapt, and innovate to maintain our strategic advantage and protect our service members. The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will ensure the Department of Defense learns from Ukraine’s hard-earned experience and applies those lessons to our doctrine, training, and capabilities so our military is prepared for the threats of tomorrow.”
“During my visit to Ukraine, I saw firsthand how the Ukrainians are rapidly adapting to a battlefield where drones and electronic warfare are changing how wars are fought,” said Krishnamoorthi. “The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will make sure our military learns from what Ukraine has discovered through years of defending itself against Putin’s invasion, from countering drone swarms and operating through electronic warfare to sustaining weapons production under attack. We need to put those lessons to work to strengthen our own military, protect our servicemembers, and ensure we are prepared to deter aggression across the world.”
BACKGROUND
Vindman first announced the legislation following a bipartisan congressional delegation visit to Ukraine, where he visited a Ukrainian drone production facility and met with officials to discuss the battlefield and Ukraine’s rapidly evolving defense innovations.
In September 2026, Vindman voted to pass legislation that would impose sanctions on Russia.
Following his retirement from the U.S. Army, Vindman spent 18 months investigating war crimes in Ukraine, completing 14 trips as a senior consultant for a Department of State-funded program. Since coming to Congress, he has returned to Ukraine twice on bipartisan congressional delegation trips. Vindman is a recognized expert in international criminal law and has published extensively on national security and international relations.
###
title: Vindman, Krishnamoorthi Introduce Legislation to Strengthen U.S. Military Readiness Through Lessons from Ukraine

Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (D-CA) and Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN) announced the introduction of a resolution recognizing October 2026 as National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month. Observed annually in October, National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month raises public awareness of learning disabilities, promotes early and accurate diagnoses, and highlights the importance of ensuring individuals have access to the resources, tools, and support they need to succeed in school, the workplace, and their communities.
“Having a learning disability should never stand in the way of a person’s ability to pursue their goals and achieve success,” said Congresswoman Brownley. “I began my career in public service to ensure that individuals like my daughter, who has dyslexia, have access to the resources and tools that empower them to learn and grow with confidence. I am grateful for Congresswoman Houchin’s partnership in recognizing National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month as we work to foster positive and supportive learning environments and improve learning outcomes and lived experiences for people with learning disabilities.”
“Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, and that starts with the early identification of learning disabilities,” said Congresswoman Houchin. “Students who struggle quickly fall through the cracks of our education system. That’s why I am proud to recognize National Learning Disabilities Awareness Month alongside Congresswoman Brownley. We can, and should, do more to screen children as early as possible for learning challenges, like dyslexia, and this resolution brings awareness to the issue.”
This resolution is endorsed by the National Center for Learning Disabilities, a leading non-profit organization focused on building community, sharing resources, and shaping policy to help individuals with learning and attention issues.
The full text of the resolution can be found here.

Comptroller affirms support for community banks to combat fraud; Reemphasizes banks’ role on the front lines of protecting consumers

WASHINGTON—Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould convened a panel of community bankers in Minneapolis, Minnesota, October 6 to discuss ongoing efforts to combat financial fraud.

The Comptroller’s visit supports the Trump Administration’s priority to eliminate fraud and protect Americans from illicit activity. In a discussion with local community bankers, the Comptroller discussed recent financial fraud in Minnesota, the role of banks to identify and combat fraud, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC) commitment to support banks in their efforts.

“Minnesota has seen fraud spiral out of control in recent years. Non-mortgage fraud reports in Minnesota more than doubled between 2020 and 2024, and filings of suspicious activity reports related to check fraud increased nearly 300% during that same period,” said Comptroller Gould. “Billions of dollars intended for hungry children, housing for disabled seniors, and services for children with special needs were diverted to people who cheated the system, some of whom are not even American citizens. The OCC is committed to supporting community banks in the fight against fraud and participating in a whole-of-government effort to stop those who seek to exploit the U.S. financial system or prey on American families and taxpayers.”

In his discussion with community bankers, Comptroller Gould discussed the OCC’s tools and resources to support bank efforts to report fraud and keep their customers and communities safe. Comptroller Gould announced the launch of a new tool for community bankers to directly report suspected payments fraud involving OCC-regulated institutions to an OCC fraud taskforce. He also reminded banks of the OCC’s bulletin on the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network 314(b) guidance that enhances information sharing across institutions and helps banks detect and thwart fraud more effectively.

He also highlighted the success of Treasury’s Do Not Pay program to prevent fraud and improper payments to better protect taxpayer dollars. In the last fiscal year alone, Treasury screened more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling approximately $3.7 trillion. Through these screenings, Treasury identified and returned approximately 13,500 payments totaling $175 million that would have gone to deceased individuals.

The OCC remains committed to addressing fraudulent activities that can harm banks and consumers.

DeGette, Matsui, Beyer Statement on Illegal Impoundment of Health Research Funds
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representatives Diana DeGette (CO-01), Doris Matsui (CA-07), and Don Beyer (VA-08) released the following statement after the Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued a legal determination confirming the administration illegally impounded $78 million in Fiscal Year 2025 funding for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ). The decision comes more than a year after Reps. DeGette, Matsui and Beyer sent the initial request for a nonpartisan legal opinion on the matter.
“The GAO’s decision today confirms what we have known for over a year: Donald Trump is stealing taxpayers’ dollars that Congress set aside to improve Americans’ health. The administration’s unilateral dismantling of the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality’s grantmaking operations is an illegal impoundment of Congressionally appropriated funds.
“Under Article I of the Constitution, the power of the purse rests strictly with Congress, not the executive branch. Trump’s administration cannot simply refuse to spend the resources we authorized for lifesaving health care research. Republicans must join Democrats in demanding that the Constitution is upheld.”
Background:
The Trump administration’s massive cuts at the Department of Health and Human Services beginning April 1, 2025, disrupted grant funding for health care research across the country, including in Colorado. AHRQ suffered particularly devastating impacts to its grants supporting more efficient, effective, and safe health care. Grantmaking at AHRQ halted: from April 1 to September 5, 2025, AHRQ did not issue a single grant. The agency would typically issue up to 73 grants during a comparable time period.
In September 2025, Representatives DeGette, Matsui and Beyer sent a request to GAO for their legal opinion on whether disruptions of AHRQ’s grantmaking process represented illegal withholding of funds in violation of the Impoundment Control Act, which regulates the president’s ability to delay or withhold Congressionally appropriated spending. The GAO is often called the “Congressional watchdog” for its role in investigating federal government spending and performance.
Today, after a lengthy nonpartisan investigation, the GAO announced its findings that the Trump administration did illegally withhold—or impound—$78 million Congress directed to support healthcare research.
###
title: DeGette, Matsui, Beyer Statement on Illegal Impoundment of Health Research Funds

Ranking Member Khanna Joined by Democratic Lawmakers to Raise Alarm Over DOE Cancellation of Transmission Corridors, Warns Decision Could Undermine U.S. Manufacturing and Competitiveness with China
WASHINGTON – Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, joined Rep. André Carson (D-IN), Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA), Rep. Paul Tonko (D-NY), and Rep. Mike Levin (D-CA), to raise serious concerns about the Department of Energy’s decision to abandon three proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors (NIETCs), warning that the move could undermine U.S. manufacturing, increase electricity costs for American families, and weaken the nation’s ability to compete with China.
In a letter to Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Tuesday, the lawmakers questioned the Department’s August 12 decision not to move forward with the Lake Erie-Canada Corridor, Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and Tribal Energy Access Corridor. He also pressed the Department to explain how it plans to address the nation’s urgent transmission needs and accelerate permitting for critical grid infrastructure.
The letter comes as the Department’s own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study found a “pressing need” for additional transmission infrastructure driven in part by expanding domestic manufacturing, large industrial loads, data centers, and a growing economy.
“Arbitrary cancellations like these set back the U.S. in the strategic race with the CCP, hamstring a U.S. manufacturing buildout, and drive up costs for American families,” the lawmakers wrote.
The Members further raised concerns about the impact of inadequate transmission capacity on American consumers. As electricity rates continue to rise, transmission constraints are driving up wholesale power costs and limit the ability of regions to bring new generation online, putting additional pressure on families and businesses already struggling with higher energy bills, the lawmakers wrote.
The Members are calling on Secretary Wright to provide detailed answers to the following by October 26, 2026:
- Please provide a detailed account of any analysis conducted by the Department of the opportunity cost of cancelling the Lake Erie–Canada Corridor, the Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and the Tribal Energy Access Corridor, including projected effects on ratepayer costs, grid reliability, and industrial electricity supply in the affected regions.
- Did the Department assess the impact of these cancellations on potential manufacturing and energy-intensive development in the regions associated with these cancelled corridors? Please provide a detailed account of that analysis.
- How does the Department reconcile these cancellations with the findings of its own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study?
- What stakeholder feedback did the Department evaluate when deciding to cancel these NIETC designations and did the Department engage with utilities, regional transmission organizations, or the North American Electric Reliability Corporation?
- What steps, if any, will the Department take to address the transmission needs in these three corridors, or in other transmission constrained areas across the country (especially those identified in the 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study)?
Read the full letter to Energy Secretary Wright HERE.

title: Ranking Member Khanna Joined by Democratic Lawmakers to Raise Alarm Over DOE Cancellation of Transmission Corridors, Warns Decision Could Undermine U.S. Manufacturing and Competitiveness with China

USDA Announces Record Payments of $13.8 Billion for 2025 Crop Year Revenue and Price Safety Net Programs
(WASHINGTON, D.C., October 7, 2026) — Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins announced that the Farm Service Agency’s Agriculture Risk Coverage (ARC) and Price Loss Coverage (PLC) will generate approximately $13.8 billion in gross payments to eligible agricultural producers for the 2025 crop year; the largest annual payout by far since these key safety net programs were established in the 2014 Farm Bill.
“President Trump has been the biggest champion for American farmers, and today's announcement delivers nearly $14 billion in funding for rural America,” said Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “Last July 4th President Trump signed the Working Families Tax Cuts Act into law and today we are acting on it, this will strengthen reference prices to better reflect today’s farm economy. This historic economic support provides producers critical liquidity to cover operating costs, prepare for the next crop year and invest in their operations. Thank you to all the Republicans who unanimously voted for this law and put food security and rural America first.”
The 2025 crop year stands alone in the history of ARC and PLC since Congress created the programs as key components of the commodity safety net in the Agricultural Act of 2014. Since 2015, no previous crop year has generated payments approaching this level. While ARC and PLC payments total $13.8 billion, producers are reminded that this does not account for payment limitation reductions and the 5.7% sequestration rate required by statute that will be applied to all ARC and PLC payments.
Working Families Tax Cuts Act Improvements
The Working Families Tax Cuts Act (WFTCA) strengthens ARC and PLC beginning with the 2025 crop year, including higher statutory reference prices and improvements to the effective reference price calculation. Additionally, for the 2025 crop year only, producers will automatically receive the higher payment rate of either ARC or PLC, regardless of their program election. The WFTCA also increases the ARC and PLC payment limit from $125,000 to $155,000, starting with the 2025 crop year with annual adjustments based on inflation. The payment limit for the 2025 crop year is $160,000.
The following 16 crops triggered a PLC payment for the 2025 crop year: Chickpeas (small and large), canola, corn, dry peas, flaxseed, grain sorghum, lentils, peanuts, rice (long grain, medium grain, japonica), safflower, seed cotton, soybeans, and wheat. ARC-County (ARC-CO) payments are based on county-level revenue and therefore trigger at the county level. FSA will issue payments to eligible producers as calculations are completed.
2026 ARC and PLC Enrollment
As a reminder, the ARC and PLC election and enrollment period for the 2026 crop year is now open.
The WFTCA added an additional 30 million new base acres to farms nationwide. Because eligible acres exceeded the nationwide 30-million-acre cap, FSA applied an across-the-board, prorated reduction of 3.69% to all newly allocated base acres. These additional base acres impact ARC and PLC starting with the 2026 and future crop years, further improving the farm safety net.
Producers should make an appointment with their FSA county office to complete their 2026 ARC and PLC election and enrollment.
ARC and PLC Safety Net
ARC and PLC protect producers from substantial declines in crop prices or revenues. Producers annually elect and enroll for ARC or PLC coverage for eligible commodities.
PLC provides income support when the effective price for a covered commodity falls below its effective reference price. ARC provides income support when actual crop revenue falls below a guaranteed level. Depending on the coverage elected, ARC protection is based on either county-level revenue or the revenue of an individual farm.
Producers with questions about their ARC-CO or PLC enrollment or payments should contact their local FSA county office. Producers who selected ARC‑Individual (ARC‑IC) and want to know which crops on the farm triggered a payment, should contact their local FSA county office. ARC‑IC protects the entire farm’s revenue rather than individual crops.
More Information
For more information about ARC and PLC, including eligibility and payment calculations, producers can visit fsa.usda.gov/arc-plc or contact their local FSA county office.
###
title: USDA Announces Record Payments of $13.8 Billion for 2025 Crop Year Revenue and Price Safety Net Programs

Human lung organoids with a built-in immune system could transform respiratory disease research
Wednesday, October 7, 2026
Human lung organoids with a built-in immune system could transform respiratory disease research
In NIH-funded study, the models orchestrated adaptive immune responses to viral infection.
A new organoid model built with human lung fragments may help us answer key questions about one of the body’s first lines of defense against respiratory pathogens. In a National Institutes of Health (NIH)-supported study, researchers at the Stanford University School of Medicine elicited virus-specific immune responses from these organoids and showed that administering a virus booster weakened subsequent infections.
The findings suggest the lung mucosa’s immune system alone may provide significant protection, which adds to growing evidence that vaccination strategies designed to train up the body’s frontline defenses are a worthwhile pursuit. The models may also be ideal testing grounds for such interventions.
“These organoids retain key immune cells and functions of lung mucosa long-term, allowing investigators to examine local tissue immunity separately from the other parts of the body’s immune system,” said John H. Powers III, M.D., acting director of NIH’s National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). “This platform may provide a replacement for animal models for some types of evaluations and may provide insights that tests in animal models could not capture.”
In the new study, the researchers transferred pieces of intact distal lung tissue from more than 220 patient volunteers into a unique cell culture system that simulated the lung’s life-sustaining gas exchange. The authors sustained organoids within this 3D air-liquid interface for up to several months, during which they found many critical immune cell populations thriving. More specifically, they confirmed that the T cells present were permanent residents of the tissue and maintained their virus-sensing capabilities.
With these components of the immune system present in the model, the team next sought to determine whether it was also fully functional. Infecting organoids with SARS-CoV-2, the researchers saw that the lung models countered with not only generic immune reactions such as inflammation, but also adaptive responses, as T cells became reactive to SARS-CoV-2 specifically.
They also tested the impact of pre-stimulating the organoids with fragments of the virus prior to infection, essentially simulating a kind of vaccination. Again, the organoid’s immune cells learned how to better detect and dispatch SARS-CoV-2, which diminished future infections.
“The exact role of local immunity in human lungs has long been a hotly debated subject, but we believe these organoids will be a conduit for clear answers. Already, we’ve unveiled indications that resident T cells may be much more persistent than previously thought,” said corresponding author Calvin Kuo, M.D., Ph.D., a professor of hematology at Stanford Medicine.
The authors believe that their findings and future work in these models could provide a strong basis for local vaccination, which may complement or replace traditional vaccines that induce adaptive immunity systemically.
Their scope may also widen greatly in the future. The researchers believe their models could potentially help elucidate the role of tissue-resident immune responses in a variety of other pulmonary diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, and bacterial infections.
NIH supported this research through NIAID grants T32AI007502, K08AI163369, U19AI057229, R01AI127877, R01AI130398, and U19AI116484, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) grant T32HL129970, National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS) grant T32GM007365, National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) grant R01DK130414, and National Cancer Institute (NCI) grant OT2CA278713.
About the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID): NIAID conducts and supports research to study the causes of infectious and immune-mediated diseases, and to develop better means of preventing, diagnosing and treating these illnesses. News releases, fact sheets and other NIAID-related materials are available on the NIAID website.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®

title: Human lung organoids with a built-in immune system could transform respiratory disease research

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Giorgos Gerapetritis, Greek Foreign Minister

Ministry of Foreign Affairs

Athens, Greece

October 7, 2026

FOREIGN MINISTER GERAPETRITIS: Dear Secretary, dear colleagues, it is a great pleasure to welcome and your delegation to Athens for the sixth round of the Greece-U.S. Strategic Dialogue. Your presence here speaks to the enduring strength of our relationship and to the importance both our countries attach to its future.

Since the launch of the Strategic Dialogue back in 2018, our cooperation has grown steadily in scope and ambition, encompassing defense, energy, infrastructure, digital technologies, law enforcement, maritime affairs, and the close ties between our peoples. The three agreements signed today are tangible evidence of that progress. Our partnership has never been stronger, deeper, or more consequential. It rests on shared values and a common determination to advance peace, stability, security, and prosperity for our peoples, for our regions, and beyond.

We meet at a time of profound geopolitical change. The ongoing war in Ukraine, instability in the Middle East, threats to maritime security in the Red Sea, and the resurgence of a revisionist rhetoric demand resolve, coordination, and a clear sense of purpose. In this uncertain environment, Greece remains a reliable ally and an anchor of stability in the Eastern Mediterranean. During the 2025-‘26 term on the United Nations – of the Security Council – and as we prepare to assume the presidency of the Council of the European Union second semester of 2027 – we bring that same sense of responsibility to our work. Respect for international law is a guiding principle for our foreign policy and an essential condition for lasting peace.

Greece’s geography places us at the meeting point of three continents. Our history, our longstanding relationships across the region, and the enduring influence of Hellenism allow us to engage with a wide range of partners in good faith and with credibility. This gives Greece a particular responsibility and a practical capacity to connect countries, facilitate dialogue, and build understanding. It also gives our partnership strategic value. Strengthening Greece’s role strengthens the security of the wider region and advances interests we share with the United States.

The Strategic Dialogue allow us to translate this convergence into concrete action. Today, we have an opportunity to carry that world forward across its core pillars. Our defense cooperation has reached unprecedented levels. The Mutual Defense Cooperation Agreement has deepened our strategic partnership and strengthened our capacity to address common security challenges.

Alexandroupolis exemplifies the value of this cooperation. A sovereign Greek port and a vital logistical hub for the United States, it contributes directly to the security of nations – of NATO’s eastern flank. Greece’s consistently high defense expenditure and longstanding contribution to the Alliance reflect a simple conviction: Collective security requires every Ally to shoulder its responsibilities. We are committed to further strengthening our defense cooperation, including through procurement, industrial partnerships, and advanced technologies. Our growing collaboration in law enforcement and counterterrorism is equally important to the security of our citizens.

On energy, Greece is emerging as a vital hub for Southeastern and Central Europe infrastructure, such as the Alexandroupolis FSRU. Together with our leading role in the Vertical Corridor, this diversifying supply is strengthening resilience and giving our neighbors greater energy security. The growing engagement of U.S. energy companies, including Severn and ExxonMobil, underscores confidence, increases potential, (inaudible) the opportunities our partnership offers.

Our maritime strength are the third strategic dimension. With Greek-owned vessels accounting for almost one-fourth of global energy shipping capacity globally, Greek shipping plays a pivotal role in connecting energy producers with consumers and sustaining transatlantic energy flows. The transformation of the Greek economy has opened a new chapter in our bilateral relationship. Renewed growth and investment confidence are creating opportunities for American businesses to participate in Greece’s progress.

Investment by leading U.S. technology companies in data centers’ digital infrastructure is helping to establish Greece as a regional center for innovation. Our ambition is to build on this momentum through partnerships that create skilled jobs, support research, and bring new opportunities to the next generation.

At the heart of this relationship, however, are our people. The Greek American community has helped shape America while sustaining a close and abiding connection with Greece. Its achievements in business, science, public service, and the arts are a source of pride for both our nations. Greek Americans have made Greece’s heritage part of America’s success. They embody a relationship rooted in the ideals of liberty, democracy, and the rule of law, ideals that inspired America’s Founding Fathers and continue to give our partnership purpose. Our expanding education and cultural exchanges carry this connection forward, allowing young Greeks and Americans to learn from one another and to build relationships of their own.

Mr. Secretary, I look forward to our discussions today and to the practical results that we deliver. We have a strong foundation and a clear sense of what we can achieve. Today’s discussion will help us turn that shared ambition into practical results. Our alliance draws strength – draws strength from all we have achieved together. Its promise lies in what we choose to do next. Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you. Thank you for this opportunity to be here today for the sixth time a U.S. secretary of state gathers with their counterparts in Greece for this Strategic Dialogue. And I’m happy to be here in Greece for that dialogue. It’s my first trip to the country ever; I didn’t even have a chance to come as a senator. And so I’m happy to be here and to be a part of this Strategic Dialogue.

I want to begin by saying that I hope our presence here today and our work that we’re about to do – and continue to do together – highlights something very important, and that is how critical the historic alliance between Greece and the United States is. And this is especially true now at a time of great global uncertainty, whether it’s the war between Russia and Ukraine, whether it’s what’s happening in the Middle East, whether it’s – meaning in the Straits of Hormuz and, increasingly now, in the Red Sea because of the Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

At a time of extraordinary global tumult and global instability, we need anchor partners rooted in a common history. And that is what Greece has meant for the United States and, I hope, what the United States has meant for Greece and what we will continue to mean for each other. This strong partnership, it’s a relationship that spans a variety of fronts – obviously defense and security, our mutual defense and security as allies and partners, but it extends to trade, to investment, to energy. There literally is no – it’s a cultural exchange. There are literally no areas of our societies or of our countries that are not part of the U.S.-Greece relationship, and we seek to build and expand on every single one of them.

Let me begin by saying what is obvious to everyone but should continue to be obvious: Greece is an indispensable NATO partner, an indispensable NATO Ally. It is a pillar of stability in this region, it is a pillar of the U.S.’s presence in this region, and it is a pillar of how we secure our national interest as well as Greece’s in the region. So we are thrilled – part of that, some of the things that aren’t heavily perceived but we’ll be able to be a part of announcing again later today, is we’re thrilled that Greece joins the

U.S. National Guard Bureau of State Sponsorship [1] Program, and they’re doing so with the guard from my home state of Florida. It’s another milestone in our deepening defense relationship.

The U.S.-Greece Economic Security Declaration commits both nations to continue to work with likeminded allies as well to develop secure supply chains. That includes – including critical mineral productions, again another area of very strong cooperation in which our mutual interests are aligned but also in which we’re taking concrete action.

Our energy relationship is reaching new heights, and it continues to expand and grow, and it’s something we’re going to be building on. The Vertical Gas Corridor expansion has cemented in Greece, has cemented Greece as an energy hub and as a secure energy hub, and has facilitated increase in U.S. LNG exports to Europe. That’s something we continue to build on.

Our bilateral relationship as countries, of course, at the end, is founded not just in a common history but in enduring ties of family, of culture, of religion, of a shared heritage. As I’ll speak about later today in what I think is a pretty historic setting, from what I read – (laughter) – it – we are indebted to ancient Greece for its role in shaping not just our country but, frankly, our civilization.

And we – so we’re here today to remember the past because that’s the foundation upon which our relationship is built, but also to focus on the future, because we have incredible things that we can do together. And I’m very grateful to be a part of this, to be – excited to be a part of the Strategic Dialogue and happy to be here on my first visit to Greece but hopefully not my last.

[1] Partnership
