Congressman Brad Sherman Marks Three Years Since October 7th Attack on Israel
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), Co-Chair of the House Israel Allies Caucus, Ranking Member Emeritus of the Middle East Subcommittee, and senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement marking three years since Hamas’s October 7th, 2023 terrorist attack on Israel:
“Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists launched a barbaric and unprovoked attack against Israel, murdering more than 1,200 innocent men, women and children, including Americans, and taking some 250 people hostage in the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust.
Today, we must continue to remember those who were murdered, honor their memories, stand with the survivors and families whose lives were forever changed, and recommit to ensuring that Hamas and any like-minded terrorist entity can never be allowed to govern again.
Last October, after more than two agonizing years of captivity, the remaining twenty living hostages held in Gaza finally returned home. Their release brought enormous relief, but it did not erase the suffering inflicted upon the hostages and their families, nor diminish our obligation to ensure that every terrorist organization that participated in the October 7th attack is held accountable.
The acts of brutality committed on that day – including rape and torture – should have inspired global solidarity. Instead, 3 years later, we are witnessing the return of extreme vilification of the Jewish people and the Jewish state, including through the manufactured and libelous accusation of genocide.
The United States must reject this disinformation campaign and remain steadfast in supporting Israel’s security. Hamas can never again carry out such an attack and Gaza must be governed not by terrorists, but by legitimate leadership committed to peace. This is critical to ending the tragic cycle of violence and finally allowing innocent Israelis and Palestinians to live in security.
The U.S.–Israel partnership has endured because of our shared democratic values and common determination to confront terrorism and pursue lasting security and peace. We must stand up to the antisemitism and coordinated disinformation that threatens this alliance. On this solemn anniversary, we remember the victims of October 7th and reaffirm our commitment to building a future of greater peace and security for Israelis, Palestinians, and the region.”
Since the October 7th attack, Congressman Sherman has led and co-sponsored numerous measures to support Israel’s security and hold Hamas and other terrorist organizations accountable, including legislation to sanction the Popular Resistance Committees for their participation in the October 7th massacre, strengthen Israel’s missile-defense capabilities, and counter the flow of Iranian funds to terrorist proxies.

A 42-year-old woman has been ordered to federal prison for her role in a multimillion-dollar pandemic loan fraud conspiracy.
Trenikia Lashae Banks pleaded guilty Sept. 22, 2025.
U.S. District Judge Kenneth M. Hoyt ordered Banks to serve 18 months in federal prison to be followed by three years of supervised release. Banks was also ordered to pay more than $400,000 in restitution to the Small Business Administration. In handing down the sentence, Judge Hoyt cited the aggravated nature of the crime and Banks’ lack of moral fortitude. He emphasized there is no such thing as “free money” and described her conduct as intentional, not a mistake.
In 2020 and 2021, Banks and Shawn Nicholas Young conspired with approximately 70 others to submit fraudulent applications for funds through the Paycheck Protection Program and Economic Injury Disaster Loan funds intended to help small businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Young submitted more than 100 loan applications from his Missouri City residence, including one for his fake business All Day Money Crew LLC.
The group attempted to obtain more than $14 million in pandemic loan funds and successfully received approximately $4.5 million.
Through Young, Banks obtained three pandemic loans for fake businesses in her name and paid him kickbacks from the proceeds. She also falsified documents at Young’s request for submission with 15 loan applications for other co-conspirators. Young paid Banks to falsify the documents even when the loan applications were unsuccessful.
Banks was permitted to remain on bond and voluntarily surrender to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future.
Young, 43, Missouri City, also pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud for his role in the scheme and is set for sentencing Feb. 9, 2027.
Federal Housing Finance Agency - Office of Inspector General, Treasury Inspector General for Tax Agency, SBA - OIG, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation - OIG, and Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations conducted the investigation, with the assistance of Fort Bend County Sheriff’s Office and Harris County Constable’s Office Precinct 1.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephanie Bauman prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division which is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal benefit programs.
title: Houston Resident Sentenced in $14 Million Pandemic Loan Fraud Conspiracy

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Small Business Administration Inspector General and Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC) Chairman William W. Kirk welcomed Treasury’s announcement of expanded fraud prevention and payment verification safeguards, emphasizing the importance of a whole-of-government approach to protecting taxpayer dollars. Treasury reported expanding access to Do Not Pay data and screening approximately $3.7 trillion in federal payments during fiscal year 2026.
“Protecting taxpayer dollars requires us to identify fraud risks before funds go out the door,” said Kirk. “Treasury’s announced progress represents an important step in moving from ‘pay and chase’ to prevention. As SBA Inspector General and PRAC Chairman, I support this governmentwide effort and am committed to ensuring our oversight work helps agencies strengthen safeguards, identify risks early, and prevent losses.”
SBA OIG’s oversight of pandemic assistance programs illustrates the importance of early screening and effective follow-through. In its management alert on Paycheck Protection Program recipients identified through Treasury’s Do Not Pay data, SBA OIG collaborated with Treasury’s Do Not Pay Business Center to identify loans to potentially ineligible recipients and recommended stronger screening before awards and payments.
The PRAC’s Blueprint for Enhanced Program Integrity reinforces complementary principles, including strong internal controls, access to data, verification of applicant identity and eligibility, and coordinated oversight across government. These principles support efforts to prevent fraud while ensuring assistance reaches eligible recipients.
“Our contribution is to turn oversight findings into fraud prevention,” Kirk said. “By sharing lessons learned, identifying vulnerabilities, and working across organizational boundaries, inspectors general and the PRAC help strengthen the government’s defenses against fraud. We welcome Treasury’s reported progress and will continue doing our part alongside our federal, state, and local partners.”
According to Treasury, approximately 99 percent of federal programs can now access the Do Not Pay data sources for which they are legally authorized, compared with approximately 4 percent at the end of fiscal year 2025. Treasury also reported screening more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling approximately $3.7 trillion during fiscal year 2026.

Georgia's Congressional Democrats Push Back on State Board’s 'Unsubstantiated Claims' in DOJ Letter
ATLANTA, GA — Today, four of the five members of the Georgia U.S. House of Representatives Democrat delegation and Rep. Joe Morelle of New York, the Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration that oversees federal elections, sent a letter to the Georgia State Election Board pushing back on its Sept. 30 letter to the Department of Justice seeking their intervention in the state’s voting machines ahead of the November midterms elections, which are now in just 27 days.
“We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law — and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice — is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.”
Read the full letter HERE and below.
Georgia State Election Board
2 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive SE
Floyd West Tower
Suite 324
Atlanta, Georgia 30334
Dear Mr. Mills:
We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law—and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice—is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.
There is absolutely no ambiguity on this point: The voting system used by Georgia voters complies with state and federal law. Your unsubstantiated claim that Georgia’s voting system is “inconsistent” with the requirements of the Help America Vote Act (“HAVA”) is deeply troubling; one would expect that someone in your position would have some basic understanding of applicable federal election law. HAVA mandates that the United States Election Assistance Commission (“EAC”) “provide certification, decertification, and recertification of voting systems, as well as the accreditation of voting system testing laboratories.” The EAC also issues Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (“VVSG”), which cover “pre-voting, voting, and post-voting operations consistent with the definition of a voting system in HAVA Section 301(a).” And, as you should know, a state’s voting devices and software “must meet [VVSG specifications] in order to receive certification from the EAC.” Of course, Georgia’s voting system has undergone the EAC’s thorough testing process, as evidenced by the fact that the EAC has certified Georgia’s voting system, as required by Georgia’s statutory and regulatory regime.
The intent of your letter is clear—to serve as a pretext for undermining public confidence in Georgia’s election results this November. Americans should know that the State Election Board does not administer Georgia’s elections. That responsibility rests with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of State’s Elections Division. The SEB has important statutory oversight and rulemaking responsibilities, but those responsibilities should not be conflated with the actual administration and certification of Georgia elections. Nor should any erroneous SEB communication to the Department of Justice concerning Georgia’s elections be understood as anything more than partisan political actors’ attempt to justify future attempts to overturn a free and fair American election—an extraordinarily serious, and cynical, misuse of official communication.
Public confidence in elections depends in substantial part upon public officials communicating accurately, responsibly, and within the scope of their statutory authority—and without incompetently, or intentionally, mischaracterizing the law. Georgians have used the state’s voting system for three straight federal elections—elections won by both Republicans and Democrats. And Georgia has one of the most rigorous, robust post-election audit regimes in the country—this is how we know that Georgia’s elections are free, fair, and secure. You should therefore promptly clarify the record, correct any inaccurate characterization of HAVA or Georgia’s voting-system requirements, and make clear that Georgia’s elections are administered by the Secretary of State and conducted using voting systems that have satisfied the certification requirements established by state and federal law.
Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.
Sincerely,
Reps. Joe Morelle (NY-25), Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Everton Blair (GA-13).
###
title: Georgia's Congressional Democrats Push Back on State Board’s 'Unsubstantiated Claims' in DOJ Letter

As Colorado begins mailing ballots for the November election, Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) is demanding answers from the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) regarding reported deployments of armed and unarmed guards at Colorado postal facilities.The deployments follow repeated Trump administration efforts to restrict mail voting, sow confusion, and undermine confidence in our elections—raising urgent concerns about whether voters will face intimidation simply for casting a ballot. In the 2024 general election, more than 92% of Colorado voters cast their ballots by mail—making reliable delivery and intimidation-free access essential for the state to conduct this and future elections. 
“Coloradans should be able to cast their ballots without fear or intimidation. Deploying armed guards at postal facilities just as voting begins demands an explanation and urgent action,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen. “We need clear answers about why these guards are here, what authority they have, and how voters and election mail will be protected. Coloradans deserve confidence that their ballots will be delivered and their voices heard. Voter intimidation is an attack on our democracy, and here in Colorado, we will fight to ensure every vote is counted.”
Armed guards have reportedly been deployed at postal facilities even though USPIS says no credible security or operational threat prompted the increased presence. A memo distributed to the American Postal Workers Union says guards will monitor entrances and parking lots, verify IDs, and report purportedly suspicious activity at public Post Offices and restricted mail-processing plants. USPIS calls this a longstanding security plan, but has not explained why these deployments are happening now, identified the affected facilities, or detailed safeguards to prevent voter intimidation and interference with election mail.
In the letter to Chief Postal Inspector Barksdale, Pettersen writes, “Postal workers have a crucial responsibility to deliver election mail safely and on time. We support appropriate measures designed to protect them and their ability to carry out this responsibility. At the same time, the presence of armed guards at facilities where voters may deposit ballots runs the real risk of making voters feel intimidated. Federal law prohibits voter intimidation, which is defined as the use of threats, coercion, or attempts to intimidate for the purpose of interfering with the right of another person to vote or to vote for the person of their choosing. Voters should feel assured that they can send their ballots without being questioned, monitored, or deterred by armed guards.” 
Congresswoman Pettersen demands that USPIS disclose:
    - Who authorized the deployments,
- Which Colorado facilities are affected, and 
- Whether guards can demand identification, restrict public access, inspect ballots, or influence whether election mail is accepted and delivered. 
- She also asks whether the White House, the Department of Justice, or the Department of Homeland Security had any role in the decision.
Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen has consistently defended Coloradans’ access to secure, accessible elections. She introduced an amendment to protect eligible voters from disenfranchisement under the SAVE Act and opposed a Republican budget resolution that included $10 billion for election grants tied to SAVE America Act voter-ID requirements. Building on her work in the state legislature to strengthen Colorado’s mail-ballot system, she has also pressed USPS to ensure timely ballot delivery, particularly for rural communities, and pushed back against federal efforts to restrict mail voting.
The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.
Dear Chief Postal Inspector Barksdale,
 
We write in response to recent reporting that the United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) has deployed armed and unarmed guards to postal facilities in Colorado and across the country just as millions of Americans are preparing to cast their ballots by mail ahead of the 2026 General Midterm Elections. 
 
In a memo distributed to the American Postal Workers Union, the USPIS has indicated that the guards will monitor entrances and parking areas, verify IDs, and observe and report purportedly suspicious activity in and around key postal facilities, including both Post Offices – which are open to the public – and US Postal Service processing plants – which are not open to the public. These deployments come despite the agency’s repeated assurances that no credible security or operational threat has necessitated the heightened presence, with USPIS characterizing this initiative as part of a longstanding, multiyear security plan. Yet the agency has provided little public information for the timing of this deployment, failed to identify which facilities will be affected, and offered no detail regarding the safeguards that will be implemented to ensure that the presence of law enforcement personnel does not disrupt, intimidate, or otherwise interfere with postal workers, election officials, or votes during a critical period of the election cycle. 
 
Postal workers have a crucial responsibility to deliver election mail safely and on time. We support appropriate measures designed to protect them and their ability to carry out this responsibility. At the same time, the presence of armed guards at facilities where voters may deposit ballots runs the real risk of making voters feel intimidated. Federal law prohibits voter intimidation, which is defined as the use of threats, coercion, or attempts to intimidate for the purpose of interfering with the right of another person to vote or to vote for the person of their choosing. Voters should feel assured that they can send their ballots without being questioned, monitored, or deterred by armed guards.
 
This issue is particularly poignant for Colorado, where over 90% of voters cast their ballots by mail. Colorado’s 2024 General Election Fact Sheet shows that every audit demonstrated a 97% rate of statistical certainty that voting tabulation equipment worked correctly, demonstrating the strength and soundness of Colorado’s election security system which has multiple layers of physical and network security measures designed to prevent unauthorized access and ensure accurate vote counts. Leading up to the 2026 General Midterm Election, the United States Postal Service (USPS) has disseminated best practices for voting by mail, which includes guidance that if and when feasible, voters should deliver their mail-in ballot to a postal facility or USPS retail facility to receive same-day stamping. The presence of armed and unarmed guards already deployed at postal facilities is not a hypothetical concern; it is a reality that voters and postal workers are confronting right now. Deploying armed and unarmed personnel at key mail-processing and ballot-return locations during an election, without a clear and compelling public justification, risks intimidating voters, discouraging ballot return, and eroding public confidence in both the Postal Service and the integrity of the electoral process.
As such, we request answers to the following questions to help us understand the circumstances surrounding this deployment and its potential impact on voter access:
    - When was the decision to deploy additional guards made, who approved it, and what prompted the deployment at this time?
- How many armed and unarmed guards have been deployed nationwide and in Colorado? At which facilities, and for what anticipated duration?
- What are the guards’ duties and limits of authority? May they ask members of the public for identification, inspect mail or ballots, direct postal employees, restrict access to facilities, or interact with election officials?
- What steps has USPIS taken to consult postal workers, their unions, state and local election officials, and USPS election mail personnel about the deployment and its potential effect on ballot processing?
- Has USPIS received any request, direction, or input concerning this deployment from the White House, the Department of Justice (DOJ), the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or any other federal agency? 
- Will these guards have any role or authority in determining whether election mail is accepted, processed, or delivered?
- What specific steps has USPIS taken to ensure that the presence and conduct of these guards do not intimidate voters or discourage them from mailing their ballots?
 
Coloradans deserve certainty that every eligible voter can return a ballot free from intimidation, disruption, or interference, and that every piece of election mail will be handled and delivered securely and on time. Postal workers, election officials, and voters alike are entitled to clear assurances regarding the scope, purpose, and conduct of these deployments of armed and unarmed guards. In light of the urgency and significance of these concerns, we request a prompt and comprehensive response no later than October 16th, 2026.
 
Sincerely, 
Brittany Pettersen
Member of Congress
title: Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen Demands Answers on Armed Guards Trump Admin Has Reportedly Deployed to Ballot Drop Off Facilities As Colorado Begins Mail-In-Voting

Italian Alien Charged With Voting in 2024 General Election and Lying About It
TAMPA, Fla. —U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided critical assistance in the investigation that led to a federal indictment charging Andrea Catanese, 60, an Italian national, with voting by an alien, attempting to unlawfully procure naturalization, and making a false statement in connection with naturalization. If convicted on all counts, Catanese faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in federal prison. U. S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.
According to the indictment, Catanese voted in the 2024 general election despite not being a U.S. citizen. The indictment further alleges that Catanese later falsely stated on a Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, that he had never voted in a federal election and repeated that false statement to a USCIS official reviewing the application.
An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty.
This case was investigated by U.S. Immigration and Custom Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS and the Pasco County Supervisor of Elections. It will be prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark E. Andreu.
To report suspected immigration benefit fraud or abuse to USCIS, please use the USCIS Tip Form.
For more information on USCIS and its programs, please visit uscis.gov or follow us on X, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and LinkedIn.

Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Bennet Demand Answers on Childhood Vaccines EO, Measles Deaths, & Delayed Vaccine Access
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Senator Michael Bennet (D-CO) led 25 colleagues in a letter to Dr. Erica Schwartz, the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to call out efforts to reject settled vaccine science and demand answers about the CDC’s efforts to implement President Trump’s childhood vaccine Executive Order (EO), underreport measles-associated deaths, and delay access to childhood immunizations.
“[...] As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule. At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health,” began the lawmakers.
The United States is facing a decline in childhood immunization rates. Recently, the CDC reported that 280,000 kindergartners did not complete their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine series. This comes as the Trump Administration has actively worked to lower the number of recommended immunizations, break up safe and effective combination shots, and promote legal action against states unaligned with such efforts.
Additionally, the CDC has a long-standing agency precedent and prides itself on “objective data collection and reporting.” At the beginning of September, numerous reports exposed that four measles-associated deaths verified and reported by the Pennsylvania Department of Health were excluded from the CDC’s public outbreak tracker for weeks, even as internal CDC systems continued to track these fatalities. This omission breaks with agency standards, and raises serious questions about the CDC’s willingness to resist political pressure over settled science.
“The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient. We look forward to your response and to seeing whether the CDC under your leadership honors the commitments you made at your confirmation hearing,” concluded the lawmakers.
The text of the letter is available HERE.
###
title: Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Bennet Demand Answers on Childhood Vaccines EO, Measles Deaths, & Delayed Vaccine Access

BLM Timber Sales Generate Nearly $30 Million, Support American Jobs in Third Quarter
Organization:
Media Contact:
WASHINGTON – The Bureau of Land Management generated $29.8 million in revenue from timber sales during the third quarter of 2026, supporting American jobs and increasing domestic timber supply.
During July, August, and September, the BLM sold about 121 million board feet of timber across 5,300 acres in Oregon, Washington, Wyoming, and Idaho. That amount of lumber is enough to build about 7,600 homes. The sales support local economies with well-paying jobs in logging, milling, and construction.
“I’ve met the people whose livelihoods depend on this work, from foresters in the woods to employees at local mills,” said BLM Director Steve Pearce. “These timber sales have a real impact in rural communities, and that’s something that goes well beyond the numbers in a quarterly report.”
The BLM plans to hold nine timber sales in October 2026 to offer about 46 million board feet of timber across more than 1,200 acres.
The BLM manages 58 million acres of forests—including 2.4 million acres in western Oregon. The bureau is committed to supplying a reliable, secure, and resilient domestic supply of timber. BLM forestry supports economic security, reduces risks from wildfire, conserves fish and wildlife habitat, and decreases costs of energy production. Local communities rely on jobs that come from BLM forests, and timber from public land feeds local industry.
More than 20% of BLM-managed lands are forest and woodland ecosystems. The BLM ensures the health and resilience of these public forest lands as well as the availability of traditional forest products, such as timber.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM Timber Sales Generate Nearly $30 Million, Support American Jobs in Third Quarter

NIH joins effort to build SI-ready data for predictive models of human biology
Wednesday, October 7, 2026
NIH joins effort to build SI-ready data for predictive models of human biology
NIH-led Bio Genesis Mission will leverage existing biomedical data resources to accelerate SI-enabled discovery and improve human health.
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is coordinating with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Biohub and other partners to develop the data and resources needed to develop Super Intelligence (SI) models that can better predict how cells and biological systems respond to disease and potential interventions. Through its Bio Genesis Mission, NIH will bring together existing biomedical datasets, national data infrastructure, and research programs to help build SI-ready resources for the broader scientific community.
Developing predictive models of biology requires enormous amounts of high-quality, SI-ready data capturing how cells respond to interventions across different cell types and conditions. NIH’s extensive investments in biomedical research provide a foundation for this work; resources include national biomedical repositories catalogued by NIH’s National Library of Medicine (NLM) and the National Center for Biotechnology Information, as well as NIH Common Fund programs that are already developing coordinated biological atlases, shared data standards and SI-ready biomedical datasets.
“By combining resources and expertise, we can accelerate the development of universal cell models with sufficient biological complexity to predict how any cell responds to an intervention,” said Nicole Kleinstreuer, Ph.D., NIH Deputy Director for Program Coordination, Planning, and Strategic Initiatives (DPCPSI). “The return from these models could be broad and profound, resulting in substantially faster timelines for medical breakthroughs as compared with attempting to attain the same results through laboratory experiments alone.”
NIH will coordinate with Biohub to help standardize appropriate datasets for SI model training. Training these models requires obtaining measurements of how cells respond to intervention across many more cell types and conditions than have yet been studied, and building technologies for studying cells at scales and speeds that current instruments cannot capture.
“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally. The insights that come from this could unlock a far greater understanding of disease and open up completely new paths for cures,” said Biohub Head of Science, Alex Rives. “Because of this potential, the creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together. We invite the worldwide scientific community to join us in this project.”
The joint effort aligns with the Predicting Living Systems National Science and Technology Challenge and seeks to make high-quality biological data more useful to researchers developing predictive models of living systems. These models could ultimately help scientists explore biological questions computationally, identify promising drug targets and interventions, and prioritize the most promising ideas for laboratory and clinical testing, accelerating the translation of biomedical discoveries into better health for all Americans.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
title: NIH joins effort to build SI-ready data for predictive models of human biology

Grant Extends Microloans and Business Support for Refugee Entrepreneurs
BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) today announced a $62,500 federal grant from the Office of Refugee Resettlement for the Westminster Economic Development Initiative (WEDI), extending its Refugee Microenterprise Development project through September 2027. The award will fund the project’s upcoming year, continuing WEDI’s microloans and business-development support for refugees and other eligible newcomers who are starting and growing small businesses in Western New York.
“Refugees and new Americans bring ambition, skill, and strong determination to build a better future for themselves and their family, and a small business is one of the best ways to help them put down roots here in Buffalo,” said Congressman Kennedy. “WEDI has spent years supporting these entrepreneurs with the capital and guidance they need to start a successful business. I’m thrilled to see this funding carry that work forward, and I know that WEDI will use it to make sure that Buffalo continues to live up to its reputation as the City of Good Neighbors.”
“At WEDI, we see every day what can happen when talented, determined entrepreneurs have access to the right resources and capital,” said WEDI Interim Executive Director Courtney Yonce-Swain. “This funding from the Office of Refugee Resettlement has helped us support more than 100 businesses since 2022, giving refugee entrepreneurs greater opportunity to start, stabilize, and grow their businesses. We are incredibly grateful for this additional support and for the opportunity to continue investing in entrepreneurs who strengthen their families, their neighborhoods, and the Western New York economy"
WEDI first received this award in 2022. Through March 31, 2026, the most recent reporting period, it has helped 105 businesses, including more than $94,000 in microloans for start-up, stabilization, and expansion. Founded in 2007, WEDI is a certified Community Development Financial Institution and also operates the West Side Bazaar, a small business incubator on Niagara Street.
 
###
title: Kennedy Announces $62,500 Federal Grant for Buffalo’s Westminster Economic Development Initiative

text:
RELEASE: On Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly, Gottheimer Marks Third Anniversary of October 7th
Introduces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember 10/7, Combat Terror
Above: Gottheimer announces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember October 7th in Tenafly alongside Alexander Family.
TENAFLY, NJ — Today, Wednesday, October 7, 2026, on the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined local leaders, community members, and the family of former hostage Edan Alexander on Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly to remember the victims, honor the hostages and their families, and announce new efforts to combat terror. Gottheimer, along with U.S. Representatives Lois Frankel (FL-22), Joe Wilson (SC-2), and Young Kim (CA-40), and dozens of their colleagues, introduced a bipartisan resolution marking the third anniversary of October 7th.
Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here and here.
“We will speak the truth about October 7th. We will stand up to hate, wherever it rears its ugly head. And we will never stop fighting for the day when Hamas lays down its arms for good, and communities can live in peace free from terror,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “We cannot pretend the work is done. Hamas has not disarmed. The terrorists who carried out October 7th still hold weapons and still hold power in Gaza, and they will keep threatening Israel, and the Palestinian people until that changes.”
Gottheimer also announced new and continuing efforts to combat terror and antisemitism:
- October 7th Remembrance Resolution: The bipartisan resolution honors every person murdered on October 7th, condemns the attacks as the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust, and honors the hostages and their families. It also supports Israel’s right to defend herself, a durable cease-fire, and the full implementation of the framework, including Hamas disarmament, humanitarian aid and reconstruction for Gazans, and a future for Gaza without Hamas. The resolution also condemns the rise in antisemitism at home, including in schools and on college campuses. The House resolution is endorsed by the American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), Hadassah, Jewish Women International, and the Israel Allies Foundation.
- Holding the United Nations accountable: New legislation with Congressman Lawler (NY) that would bar U.S. funds from going toward U.S. contributions to the United Nations until the U.N. has designated Hamas and Hezbollah as terrorist organizations. This is critical as UNRWA currently does not screen for Hamas ties in its hiring of teachers and other employees, leading to Hamas terrorists infiltrating its ranks. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
- October 7th Gold Medal Act: Bipartisan legislation introduced last year with Congressman Lawler (NY) to award the Congressional Gold Medal to the American victims and hostages of October 7th, including Americans like Edan who survived captivity in Gaza. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Hostages and Missing Families Forum, American Jewish Committee (AJC), the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Jewish Women International, the Weitzman National Museum of Jewish American History, and the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
- October 7th Remembrance Education Act: Bipartisan legislation introduced last year with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA) to direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to build a model curriculum for schools to teach the attacks committed on October 7 and the antisemitism that followed. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Jewish Women International, and the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
The announcement builds on Gottheimer’s work since the attacks, including securing $100 million in the defense bill for his U.S.-Israel Anti-Killer Drone Act to counter drone attacks from Iran and its proxies, along with a provision to stop Hamas weapons smuggling on the Gaza-Egypt border; House passage last month of his bipartisan bill to cut off funds to colleges that enable BDS on their campuses; and legislation with Congressman Lawler to dismantle UNRWA and replace it with humanitarian assistance out of the hands of Hamas terrorists. At home, Gottheimer continues to work across the aisle to boost funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program so that every synagogue, church, mosque, and temple has the resources to protect itself.
Gottheimer noted the sharp rise in antisemitism since October 7th: the ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States last year, a 68 percent increase since 2022, with New Jersey ranking third highest in the country and Bergen County recording 139 incidents, the most in the state.
“Three years later, the horror of October 7th remains seared into our hearts,” said Congresswoman Lois Frankel. “We remember those who were murdered, honor the survivors and hostages and their families, and stand firmly against antisemitism and terrorism. Now we must build a future where Hamas is disarmed, Israel is safe and secure, and Palestinians and Israelis can live in peace and dignity.”
“Today marks the third anniversary of the massacre of 1,200 and kidnapping of 251 innocent men, women, and children in Israel by the Iranian terrorist puppet, Hamas. This cowardly act will forever be remembered around the world, but no more meaningful than to the families and friends who lost loved ones. I am grateful for the leadership of President Donald Trump, with the support of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and our allies, for ensuring that all hostages, living and deceased, were brought home,” said Congressman Joe Wilson.
“Three years ago, the world witnessed unspeakable evil as Hamas carried out the deadliest massacre of the Jewish people since the Holocaust. We remember the 1,200 innocent lives lost, the hostages who faced unimaginable suffering in Hamas captivity, families whose lives were irrevocably changed, and the extraordinary courage and selflessness shown by ordinary Israelis on that day,” said Congresswoman Young Kim. “We will never forget the darkness of October 7th or allow the world to forget what happened. As antisemitism continues to rear its ugly head around the world, the United States must stand firmly with the Jewish people and confront this hatred in all its forms.”
“Three years after Hamas’s October 7th attack on Israel, we remember and mourn the more than 1,200 innocent people brutally murdered, honor the hostages who have finally returned home and the families who endured unimaginable pain, and stand with all those whose lives were forever changed. American Jewish Committee proudly supports this bipartisan resolution introduced by Representatives Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Young Kim (R-CA), Lois Frankel (D-FL), and Joe Wilson (R-SC), which ensures the atrocities of October 7 are never forgotten and reaffirms America’s commitment to Israel’s security and the fight against antisemitism,” said Ted Deutch, CEO of American Jewish Committee.
“The tragedy of October 7 and the surge in antisemitism that followed that day will forever be etched in the memory of the Jewish people,” said ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt. “On this solemn third anniversary of the attack, we remember the innocent lives lost, the hostages who were taken, and the survivors whose lives were changed forever. We thank Reps. Gottheimer, Wilson, Frankel, and Kim for introducing this bipartisan resolution and for honoring the victims and survivors of October 7, and reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that ‘Never Again’ truly means never again.”
“Three years after October 7, we honor the memory of every person murdered by Hamas and its terrorist allies, and we honor the hostages and their families who endured unimaginable suffering. This resolution is an important affirmation that complete disarmament of Hamas and dismantling of its terrorist infrastructure are essential to ensuring that October 7 can never happen again and to building a future of security, peace, and dignity for Israelis and their neighbors. It also reinforces that we must confront the dangerous rise of antisemitism that has followed October 7 and continue to work hand-in-hand with government to ensure that our communities are secure in the face of this violent threat,” said Eric D. Fingerhut, President & CEO of Jewish Federations of North America.
“On the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, we pray for the innocent lives lost and renew our resolve to thwart future threats to peace. Hamas has yet to capitulate and disarm in Gaza, and terror groups continue to operate alongside Israel’s borders, sustained by state sponsors of terrorism. On this solemn day, we recognize that peace has not yet been achieved, and that further efforts are needed to safeguard civilians and demilitarize those bent on perpetuating violence,” said Tyler Stapleton, Senior Director of Government Relations, FDD Action.
“As we mark three years since Hamas terrorists carried out the deadliest attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust, we remember and honor all those who were murdered, injured, tortured, raped or held captive by Hamas. We thank Representatives Lois Frankel, Josh Gottheimer, and Joe Wilson for introducing this resolution, which condemns the atrocities of October 7, 2023, affirms Israel’s right to self-defense and supports the critical conditions of the ceasefire, including the disarmament of Hamas. We urge members of Congress to support this bipartisan resolution and to continue to confront the rise in violent antisemitism across the country and around the world,” said Carol Ann Schwartz, National President, Hadassah, The Women’s Zionist Organization of America.
“I listened with horror to whispers of the sexual atrocities committed by Hamas. I watched with horror the video of young women, pulled from their beds and pushed bloodied into trucks to be taken into Gaza. I saw with horror the photo of a naked, bound woman surrounded by terrorists raising guns in victory. I sat with horror in the silence of the world, in the silence of the feminist organizations. In the three years since, the silence, the denial, the distortion, and the hate not only continue; they grow. It is virulent and dangerous. Resolutions like this are critical in the fight against hate and disinformation. We are grateful to Representatives Gottheimer, Frankel, and Joe Wilson for standing up to hate and amplifying the truth. For those who died, and those who survived, we owe them as much,” said Meredith Jacobs, CEO of Jewish Women International (JWI).
Gottheimer was joined by Tenafly Mayor Mark Zinna, Tenafly Councilwoman Lauren Dayton, Tenafly Councilwoman, Jenny Jackson, Adi and Yael Alexander, and Rabbi Kirshner of Temple Emanu-El, Debra Mazon and her colleagues from Hadassah, Rabbi Levy from AJC, Brandi Katz Rubin from the ADL, and Shlomo Schorr from Agudath Israel, Rabbi Shmuel Bergman from Young Israel of Fort Lee, Rabbi Genack and his wife Sarah from Englewood, Tenafly Police Chief Michael Greenly, Rabbi Krishner with Temple Emanu-El, Rabbi Zev Reichman from East Hill Synagogue, and the Alexander family.
Below: Gottheimer Announces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember October 7th in Tenafly.
Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:
Good morning. Thank you all for joining us on this solemn day as we mark three years since October 7th, the deadliest attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust. As many of you know, for 842 days the posters of every single hostage held in Gaza hung on the wall outside my office in Washington – right next to the Israeli flag.  
It was a reminder to everyone who visited the United States Capitol of the responsibility we held here in the United States to do our part, not only for our key ally, but for what is right, until every hostage was returned to their families. The hostage photos were not just Israelis. They were of Americans. Of Thais. French. British. Filipinos. They were young and old. L’dor vador, from generation to generation. We all had a responsibility to do everything in our power, in every corner of the globe, to bring them home. It is a relief that this anniversary is the first without the need to wear yellow ribbons calling for the return of those being held.
Yet, as I walk past the empty wall into my office every day, I can still see those images, staring at me. It’s almost a reminder to me that we must never forget what happened – and of the work that lies ahead to heal and bring us back together. As it’s said in Isaiah, “Your ancient ruins shall be rebuilt; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations; you shall be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of streets to live in.”
Let’s be honest. We have a great deal of repairing and restoration ahead of us.
But, on this third anniversary of October 7th, while we mourn those we lost, we also have much to be grateful for – for all the hostages who were reunited with their loved ones, who are rebuilding their lives. Among those taken that day, and who came home, was our very own Edan Alexander, a young man from right here in Tenafly. A graduate of Tenafly High School, who swam on the swim team and biked on these streets, a Jersey boy through and through. Today, we are standing here on Edan Alexander Way, a street we named last year in honor of his unshakable strength and courage.
To Adi and Yael Alexander: thank you for being with us today. I know Edan can’t be here, but I know he is living his life to the fullest today in Israel. I met your family on October 23rd, 2023, just over two weeks after the attack, and you have been like family to me and Marla ever since. For nearly two years, while Edan endured the unimaginable, you never — not for a single moment — surrendered hope. You called for action, and you would not be quieted until your son came home.
You pressed me, as you pressed so many others in our community, for action and for answers. And, I was proud to carry the courage and conviction you gave me, both on my trips to the Middle East and in the halls of Congress every single day.
I especially want to thank the people of Tenafly. Three years ago today, the world changed, and this community was asked to carry something unimaginable. But, you never recoiled – you never looked away. You stood here with the Alexander family while Hamas terrorists held their son for 584 days.
You stood in Huyler Park at five o’clock in the morning to watch him be released – I was there – and you filled these streets by the thousands to welcome Edan home in May of last year. You showed what a town can do when it stands together.
You’ve also shown us the importance of never forgetting.
That’s especially important today when some are actually glorifying Hamas terrorists as martyrs – or trying to justify the actions that day, when Hamas terrorists brutally murdered, raped, burned alive, decapitated, and kidnapped more than twelve hundred people – including innocent babies, children, women, men, and elderly people, and dozens of Americans, while taking 251 hostages into tunnels in Gaza. It’s unfathomable.
Some may try to bury their head in the sand or rewrite history. But, anybody who has seen the videos and images of those heinous and unthinkable acts knows what Hamas and its accomplices are capable of. They sowed terror at the Nova music festival, in the kibbutzim, in cities across Southern Israel. Like many of you, I traveled to Israel afterward to see their path of destruction with my own eyes – to give me the first-hand knowledge to confront the haters.
But, despite the truth, since Hamas’s devastating attack, we have unfortunately witnessed a tidal wave of antisemitism that has only grown more persistent, starting just hours after the terrorists attacked Israel. Instead of empathy from people and organizations around the globe, there was a flood of criticism and blame, and it hasn’t stopped.
Just days after the October 7 attack, during the “Day of Rage” in New York City, someone shouted at a group of Jewish people: “I wish Hitler was still here; he would’ve wiped all of you out.” Other protestors said: “Say it loud, say it clear, we don’t want Zionists here!”
At Columbia University, Jewish students were chased out of their dorms, received death threats, were spat upon, stalked, and pinned against walls. People in masks screamed, “Go back to Poland!” and “Globalize the Intifada.” On October 8th, the day after the largest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust, a faculty member at Rutgers declared October 7th “awesome.”
Three years later, the protests continue – including today – against Jews simply practicing their religion in America.
Recently, at one just outside a synagogue chanting hateful slogans like “We are all Hamas,” “Death to Zionists,” and “Long live October 7th” at worshippers. Businesses have even boycotted my Jewish colleagues – refusing to serve them.
Last year, the ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States. That’s a 68 percent increase since 2022, before October 7th. And here in New Jersey, we ranked third highest in the entire country. Right here in Bergen County, we had 139 incidents, the most in New Jersey.
No other county in our state had more than 80. That’s our backyard. And, now you have internet personalities like Hasan Piker and Candace Owens spreading misinformation and hate to millions of followers online, with comments like calling a Jewish reporter a “Pig Dog,” justifying the violence on October 7th as “resistance”, blood libel, and conspiracy theories about Jewish control.
I say this not only as your Congressman, but also as a member of the Jewish community. This is deeply personal for me.
But, even in those moments of despair, we have also seen moments that give us hope. Light through the darkness.
Just a month ago, I joined the Chancellor of Vanderbilt, along with leaders from colleges ranging from the University of Alabama to Washington University to the University of Texas, in saying that hatred and religious discrimination against anyone isn’t welcome on their campus. We’ve had leaders in business, nonprofits, in the arts, in Hollywood, and in government stand strong against antisemitism, even though it has cost them personally.
Nations like the UAE and Argentina have bucked their own history and doubled down to protect the Jewish people.
And, of course, the greatest light. On May 12th of 2025, Edan came home. I will never forget the moment I first met him after his release. His humility, poise, and self-assurance stopped me in my tracks. He told me he was not a hero, that the real heroes were the ones still there … those who gave their lives. And, then he said something that will echo in my heart forever: “My story doesn’t end with survival. It continues with service.”
He meant it. Edan returned to the Israel Defense Forces and has since been promoted to Sergeant First Class. Just this summer, he stood before the world at the opening ceremony of the Maccabiah Games to explain why he went back into uniform. He has refused to let evil triumph. So neither can we.
A year ago this month, the remaining twenty living hostages came home. And in the months since, the remains of the fallen were returned, including Americans Omer Neutra and Itay Chen, whose families waited and waited until the last were finally brought home in January. Today, we remember every one of them.
We cannot pretend the work is done. Hamas has not disarmed. The terrorists who carried out October 7th still hold weapons and still hold power in parts of Gaza, and they will keep threatening Israel, and the Palestinian people until that changes.
That is why today, three years later, I am proud to announce new efforts to combat terror.
First, I’ve introduced a bipartisan resolution marking the third anniversary of October 7th. It honors every person murdered by Hamas. It condemns the attacks as the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust.
It honors the hostages and their families. It supports Israel’s right to defend herself, a durable cease-fire, and the full implementation of the framework, including Hamas disarmament, humanitarian aid and reconstruction for Gazans, and a future for Gaza without Hamas. And, it condemns the rise in antisemitism here at home, including in our schools and on our college campuses. I’m proud to be joined by Representatives Lois Frankel, Joe Wilson, and Young Kim, as well as fifty of my colleagues in introducing this resolution.
Second, I’m introducing legislation to hold the United Nations accountable.
Here’s the simple, shocking truth: the UN has never designated Hamas or Hezbollah as terrorist organizations. Not before October 7th. Not after. The Security Council maintains sanctions lists for ISIS and al-Qaeda, but not for Iran’s proxies. And, because Hamas isn’t on the list, UN agencies, including UNRWA, don’t even screen for Hamas membership when they hire. The USAID Inspector General has found more than 100 UNRWA staff with Hamas affiliations, even though we believe there are far more, and only nine have been fired for direct involvement in the October 7 attacks. That is unacceptable.
So, my bill is straightforward. No U.S. funds can go toward our contributions to the United Nations until the Security Council has designated Hamas and Hezbollah as the terrorist organizations that they are.
Today, we are also recommitting to two bipartisan bills I introduced last year, and that I am continuing the fight to pass them.
The October 7th Gold Medal Act, with Congressman Lawler from New York, will award the Congressional Gold Medal to the American victims and hostages of October 7th, including Americans like Edan who survived captivity in Gaza.
And, the October 7th Remembrance Education Act, with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick from Pennsylvania, will direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to build a model curriculum for schools to teach the heinous and brutal attacks committed on October 7th, and the antisemitism that followed.
We can’t afford for our children to learn history – and be filled with anti-American, antisemitism-filled disinformation — from TikTok. From Hasan Piker. The truth and the facts – history – should be taught in every classroom across America.
This builds on the work we’ve been doing since that terrible day. This summer, I secured $100 million in the defense bill for my U.S.-Israel Anti-Killer Drone Act to counter drone attacks from Iran and its proxies, along with a provision to stop Hamas weapons smuggling on the Gaza-Egypt border.
Just last month, the House passed my bipartisan bill to cut off funds to colleges that enable BDS on their campuses. With Congressman Lawler, I also introduced legislation to dismantle UNRWA and replace it with humanitarian assistance we can trust, out of the hands of Hamas terrorists.
Here at home, we’re going to keep working across the aisle to boost funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program, so every synagogue, church, mosque, and temple has the resources to protect itself.
This is not a red or blue issue. It’s about the safety of our families. Our Jersey Values mean that we don’t allow our communities to be torn apart. We stand together and protect one another. That’s exactly what we’re doing here today in Tenafly, just feet from Edan Alexander.
So today, we remember. We honor those we lost. We thank the heroes. And we recommit ourselves to the work ahead.
We will speak the truth about October 7th. We will stand up to hate, wherever it rears its ugly head.
And we will never stop fighting for a day when Hamas has laid down its arms for good, and Israelis and Palestinians alike can live in peace.
If we keep doing that, I know that here, in the greatest country in the world, antisemitism and hate will lose, and our best days will be ahead of us.
Thank you. God bless. And may God continue to bless and watch over the United States of America.
###

Man Arrested and Charged for Role in Plotting to Conduct a Mass-Shooting Event in Support of ISIS at the Mall of America
Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, of Richfield, Minnesota, was charged today by complaint with one count of knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition in order to commit a federal crime of terrorism.
The FBI arrested the defendant on Oct. 6, and he made his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright on Oct. 7.
“This individual allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Once again this FBI is moving more effectively than we ever have before at stopping terrorists before they can attack Americans – with over 1,100 individuals prevented from conducting attacks, over 4,000 foreign terrorist organization related disruptions and arrests, a 38% increase, and more. We will continue to use every resource we have to detect and prevent acts of terrorism and wipe out their networks all over the country. Thank you to FBI Minneapolis who did an outstanding job in the investigation and likely saved lives.”
“Mohamud allegedly sought to carry out a mass-casualty shooting at the Mall of America, expressing a desire to emulate some of the most horrific ISIS-inspired attacks in the United States, including the atrocities at Pulse Nightclub and 2025 New Year’s Day attack in New Orleans,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will continue to work closely with the FBI and Joint Terrorism Task Force to track down and prosecute ISIS-inspired terrorists in the United States.”
“As alleged in the criminal complaint, Mohamud took substantial steps to plot to murder innocent people in the name of ISIS,” said U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota. “Such threats are taken seriously, and I commend the committed public servants of the Joint Terrorism Task Force, the FBI, and my office, who work every day to stop them.”
According to the complaint, beginning in or about December 2024, Mohamud exchanged hundreds of messages through multiple social media and messaging applications with a confidential source. Mohamud expressed his desire to travel to Somalia to join a designated foreign terrorist organization to fight on its behalf. Mohamud also expressed a desire to commit a mass-casualty event in Minnesota by acquiring and using a firearm and ammunition. The defendant stated many times that if he was unable to travel overseas because of a lack of funds, he planned to carry out a mass-casualty event in Minnesota in support of ISIS.
In July 2026, Mohamud sent messages discussing his intent to carry out a mass-casualty shooting attack at the Mall of America because he claimed it was owned by Jews. He wrote that wanted to kill 30 to 60 people so no one would go there.
In August and September 2026, Mohamud continued to send messages discussing his intentions, including his plans to purchase a firearm and to recruit others to join him in committing the attack. Mohamud sent a selfie-style video of himself pledging allegiance to ISIS:
Screenshot of Mohamud’s Video Pledging Allegiance to ISIS
During the course of his communications, Mohamud stated that he wanted to commit an attack similar to those of the Pulse Nightclub mass-shooting in Orlando, the Bondi Beach mass-shooting in Australia, and the New Year’s Day vehicle-ramming attack in New Orleans.
In September 2026, Mohamud expressed a desire to kill “kuffar” — a term used to refer to a non-Muslim. Mohamud identified Oct. 24 as the date of his planned attack. When the confidential source asked if there was a big gathering on Oct. 24, Mohamud indicated that there were would be numerous Asians and other “kuffar” celebrating at the Mall of America. Mohamud then sent a link to a “Hmong Arts Celebration” at the Mall of America.
In September 2026, Mohamud continued to send propaganda videos to the confidential source. A still shot from one of the propaganda videos sent by Mohamud is depicted below:
Still Shot of Propaganda Video Sent by Mohamud
On Oct. 6, the FBI arranged to sell to Mohamud, through an undercover FBI employee, an AK-47 assault rifle, four 30-round magazines, and approximately 200 rounds of ammunition. The FBI rendered the AK-47 rifle inert prior to the transaction. The FBI arrested Mohamud shortly after he paid about $600 cash for the rifle, magazines, and ammunition and had those items in his possession. During the sale of the firearm and ammunition, Mohamud reaffirmed his plan to use the firearm and ammunition to shoot people at the Mall of America.
This case was the result of an investigation by the FBI, the Joint Terrorism Task Force, and the Bloomington Police Department, with assistance from IRS Criminal Investigation.
This case is being prosecuted by Trial Attorney Ryan White of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Bejar for the District of Minnesota.
A complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Man Arrested and Charged for Role in Plotting to Conduct a Mass-Shooting Event in Support of ISIS at the Mall of America

USITC Makes Determinations in Five-Year (Sunset) Reviews Concerning Small Vertical Shaft Engines from China
The U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) today determined that revocation of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on imports of small vertical shaft engines from China would likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury within a reasonably foreseeable time.
As a result of the USITC’s affirmative determinations, the existing orders on imports of these products from China will remain in place.
Chairman Brett W. Doyle and Commissioners Jason E. Kearns, Peter-Anthony Pappas, Bart Thanhauser, and David Foley Jr. voted in the affirmative. Commissioner Samuel T. Negatu did not participate in today’s vote.
Today’s action comes under the five-year (sunset) review process required by the Uruguay Round Agreements Act. See the attached page for background on these five-year (sunset) reviews.
The USITC’s public report, Small Vertical Shaft Engines from China (Inv. Nos. 701-TA- 643 and 731-TA-1493 (Review), USITC Publication 5801, October 2026), will contain the views of the USITC and information developed during the reviews.
The report will be available on the USITC website by November 13, 2026.
BACKGROUND
The Uruguay Round Agreements Act requires the Department of Commerce to revoke an antidumping or countervailing duty order, or terminate a suspension agreement, after five years unless the Department of Commerce and the USITC determine that revoking the order or terminating the suspension agreement would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping or subsidies (Commerce) and of material injury (USITC) within a reasonably foreseeable time.
The USITC’s institution notice in five-year reviews requests that interested parties file responses with the USITC concerning the likely effects of revoking the order under review as well as other information. Generally, within 95 days from institution, the USITC will determine whether the responses it has received reflect an adequate or inadequate level of interest in a full review. If responses to the USITC’s notice of institution are adequate, or if other circumstances warrant a full review, the USITC conducts a full review, which includes a public hearing and issuance of questionnaires.
The USITC generally does not hold a hearing or conduct further investigative activities in expedited reviews. Commissioners base their injury determination in expedited reviews on the facts available, including the USITC’s prior injury and review determinations, responses received to its notice of institution, data collected by staff in connection with the reviews, and information provided by the Department of Commerce.
The five-year (sunset) reviews concerning Small Vertical Shaft Engines from China were instituted on April 1, 2026.
On July 6, 2026, the USITC determined to conduct expedited five-year reviews. Commissioners David S. Johanson, Jason E. Kearns, and Amy A. Karpel concluded that the domestic interested party group responses were adequate and the respondent interested party group responses were inadequate and voted for expedited five-year reviews.
Chairman Brett W. Doyle and Commissioners Peter-Anthony Pappas, Bart Thanhauser, David Foley Jr., and Samuel T. Negatu did not participate in the adequacy votes, as they were not members of the USITC at the time.
A record of the USITC’s vote to conduct expedited reviews is available on the investigations page for Small Vertical Shaft Engines from China; Inv. No. 701-TA-643 and 731-TA-1493 (Review).
title: USITC Makes Determinations in Five-Year (Sunset) Reviews Concerning Small Vertical Shaft Engines from China

text:
ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Local Community Members to Raise Alarm Over Marana Detention Facility
Marana, Arizona — Yesterday, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva joined local community members in Marana for a press conference addressing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s new contract with Management and Training Corporation (MTC) to open an immigration detention facility in Marana within the next 60 days.
The press conference brought together community members and local voices to raise concerns about the proposed facility and the record of MTC, the company contracted to operate it. MTC has previously operated correctional facilities in Arizona that faced allegations and documented concerns involving conditions including sexual abuse, inadequate food, extreme heat, and prison riots. The State of Arizona has terminated previous contracts with MTC under both Democratic and Republican governors.
Earlier this year, Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem. This comes after Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem and joined community members earlier in the year at a press conference alongside Reps. Stanton and Ansari.
A copy of her remarks are below: 
“Buenas tardes. Thank you to PRICE for organizing this press conference.
We’re here today because DHS is once again rushing to open another private detention facility in Arizona.
Eso no está bien. Nuestra comunidad merece respuestas.
This is happening as deaths in ICE custody reach record levels – and as the agency fails to provide even the most basic care for the people already in its custody.
Just today, I learned about another disease outbreak - this time at a facility in Eloy.
Yet instead of addressing these conditions, this Administration is marching full steam ahead to fuel its cruel mass-deportation agenda.
And there is another reason we should be deeply concerned about this particular facility: Management & Training Corporation, or MTC, has a long and documented history of serious problems at facilities it has operated.
Here in Arizona, that history includes allegations of sexual abuse that were not properly reported, chronic understaffing and inadequate training, major security failures, and destructive prison riots.
In 2010, three inmates escaped from an MTC-operated prison in Kingman due to serious security failures.
While on the run, two of the escapees brutally murdered an elderly couple in New Mexico, leading to a large wrongful death settlement between the state of Arizona and the victims’ family.
Five years later, after riots at the same prison, an investigation found a “culture of disorganization, disengagement, and disregard.”
Those aren’t my words. Those are the findings that led Republican Governor Doug Ducey to terminate the state’s contract with MTC.
In 2017, at an MTC-operated ICE Processing Center in New Mexico, the DHS Office of the Inspector General raised concerns about the treatment and care of detainees.
Two people detained there died after pleading for medical help from facility staff.
This is the company the federal government is entrusting with the lives of hundreds of people here in Marana.
And they are moving fast. MTC says it plans to have this facility up and running within 60 days of signing its contract with ICE.
Sixty days.
That should alarm every person in this community, especially when there are still so many unanswered questions.
First and foremost: How many people are actually going to be held here?
A document earlier this year suggested more than 1,300, but the contract MTC signed says up to 775. Both of these numbers are significantly above the 513-bed capacity the state prison previously operated under.
Regardless of what the final number is, one thing is abundantly clear: local residents do not want this facility.
La gente de Marana merece tener voz.
Since President Trump returned to office, at least 56 people have died in ICE custody, including four in Arizona.
And now the federal government has awarded MTC a contract with a potential value of more than $355 million to operate this facility.
That is a drop in the bucket of the nearly $261 BILLION Congress has approved for immigration enforcement under Trump.
Our communities are tired of our taxpayer dollars being wasted on these private detention centers to meet arbitrary deportation quotas.
We are tired of seeing private companies profit off Trump’s cruel and inhumane immigration agenda.
No queremos más dinero para compañías privadas
While the federal government operates in secrecy, local residents and their elected officials across the country are pushing back against these facilities, using zoning, public nuisance laws, and other means.
MTC’s history of poorly-run facilities, combined with the track-record of abuses at DHS, underscore the concerns of Marana residents.
Unfortunately, the responsibility of oversight has fallen on local governments because the federal government is willfully asleep at the wheel.
We will continue asking questions.
We will continue demanding accountability.
And we will continue fighting to ensure that the people of Marana have a voice in what happens in their own community.
Vamos a seguir luchando por nuestra comunidad.
Thank you. Muchas gracias.”
###
title: ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Local Community Members to Raise Alarm Over Marana Detention Facility

Comisionado Residente solicita nuevas respuestas tras revisar documentos sobre contrato de generación temporera
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó nueva información y documentación sobre el proceso de adquisición y contratación de generación temporera adjudicado al consorcio encabezado por Power Expectations, LLC, tras identificar interrogantes en los documentos producidos al Congreso sobre la investigación y el manejo de alegaciones surgidas durante el proceso competitivo.
En una carta dirigida al Zar de Energía, Josué Colón Ortiz, y al presidente del Third Party Procurement Office (3PPO), Osvaldo Carlo Linares, el Comisionado Residente solicita información para esclarecer qué se investigó sobre la alegada firma no autorizada de Enchanted Rock, quién realizó esa revisión, con qué autoridad, y por qué transcurrieron casi más de siete semanas antes de referir el asunto a las autoridades competentes.
La gestión da seguimiento a una carta enviada por el Comisionado Residente el 3 de septiembre. Tras examinar los informes, referidos y comunicaciones producidos al Congreso, su oficina identificó que un informe de 3PPO del 8 de agosto describió una “revisión exhaustiva” de las alegaciones, mientras que una comunicación enviada al día siguiente indicó que la revisión se había limitado a evaluar la suficiencia de la documentación sometida durante el proceso competitivo.
“Desde nuestra primera solicitud hemos estado revisando cuidadosamente los documentos y siguiendo los hechos. La información que recibimos nos permitió avanzar, pero también levantó preguntas adicionales que ahora corresponde aclarar”, expresó el Comisionado Residente. “Queremos entender con precisión qué se revisó, qué se determinó y cómo se tomaron las decisiones durante este proceso.”
A partir de esa revisión, el Comisionado Residente identificó varias áreas que aún requieren aclaración y, en esta carta, busca precisar:
- El propósito y alcance de la revisión realizada por 3PPO y qué asuntos permanecían sin resolver.
- La cronología de las gestiones realizadas entre el 17 de junio y el 10 de agosto.
- Qué información y hallazgos existían cuando el asunto fue referido al Departamento de Justicia de Puerto Rico y a las autoridades federales.
- Cuándo fueron informadas la AEE y la Junta de Supervisión Fiscal, y cómo se tomaron las decisiones de informarles.
- Las comunicaciones y documentos internos relacionados con la revisión y el manejo de las alegaciones.
La información deberá ser entregada no más tarde del 15 de octubre de 2026.
“Estamos dando seguimiento a lo que surge de los propios documentos y vamos a continuar procurando las respuestas que aún están pendientes”, concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

title: Comisionado Residente solicita nuevas respuestas tras revisar documentos sobre contrato de generación temporera
