Aurora Sentinel: Rep. Crow introduces bill to extend TPS protections for Ukrainian immigrants
AURORA | Aurora Democratic Congressperson Jason Crow is behind a House bill that would extend through 2029 temporary immigration protections for Ukrainian nationals living in the United States.
Crow’s bill would extend Temporary Protected Status, or TPS, for Ukrainians currently in the U.S. The protections are scheduled to expire Oct. 19, 2026, according to a press statement from Crow.
“Russia continues its illegal and unprovoked attacks on Ukraine,” Crow said in a statement. “America must continue to stand with the people of Ukraine.” The legislation would make the extension part of federal law rather than leaving the protections subject to presidential action, the release said.
President Donald Trump and his administration has created intense worry and consternation among immigrants living in the United States and benefiting from TPS protections.
“I think that TPS should be a part of a long overdue comprehensive immigration reform by Congress but until then, we owe it to those who are in the country under TPS to extend their status,” Aurora Mayor Mike Coffman said in a statement. “It would be heartless to force the Ukrainians back into a war zone. So I applaud Congressman Crow’s efforts to extend their status, although having been a member of Congress for 10 years, I know how difficult it will be to pass and… to have President Trump sign it into law when he already has the authority to extend it, unilaterally, without Congressional approval. “
On Sept. 9, Trump let expire TPS protections for hundreds of thousands of immigrations, primarily from Venezuela and El Salvador. The Supreme Court earlier this year ruled that, under current U.S. law, the president has authority to end TPS protections for protected groups without justification.
TPS allows nationals of designated countries experiencing armed conflict, natural disasters or other extraordinary conditions to remain temporarily in the United States and obtain work authorization. The program requires recipients to undergo screening, according to the release.
Crow introduced the bill with representatives Bill Keating, D-Mass., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa. In the Senate, the legislation was introduced by senators Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska; Chris Coons, D-Del.; and Bill Cassidy, R-La.
Crow serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Armed Services Committee, according to the release.
He has been a supporter of U.S. assistance to Ukraine since before Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022. Crow traveled to Kyiv in December 2021 and later advocated for U.S. military and humanitarian assistance to Ukraine, according to his office.
The legislation would apply to Ukrainian nationals already covered by TPS and extend their protections through June 2029.
The measure does not address another TPS warranty, covering immigrants from Sudan, also set to expire Oct. 19.
Colorado is home to about 17,000-18,000 Ukrainian immigrants, according to the U.S. Census records. The Aurora-Denver metro area is home to as many as about 5,000 of those immigrants, according to Census records.
Temporary legal protections for about 200,000 immigrants from El Salvador — including more than 4,000 in Aurora — was in limbo Wednesday as a deadline neared for the Trump administration to decide if they should end, as it has done for hundreds of thousands from Venezuela, Haiti and other countries.
The Temporary Protected Status designation expired in September, but the statute does not give a specific time for when that happens. If the Department of Homeland Security takes no action, protections are automatically extended for six months. This rare reprieve happened in May, when the protections were automatically extended to about 11,000 Lebanese, allowing them to stay and work in the U.S. for another 180 days.
DHS said in a statement in early September that it will announce a decision on El Salvador “at the appropriate time” and that protections would remain in place until then.
The push against Salvadoran immigrants drew a rebuke from Coffman, a Republican.
“I fully support the Trump administration’s successful effort at controlling our borders to combat illegal immigration,” Coffman said earlier this year in a social media post. “But this is not a question about illegal immigration because the Salvadorans, living in Aurora under TPS, came here legally and have had children and even grandchildren here, own homes in our city, and have not only started but expanded small businesses here.”
About 200,000 people from El Salvador have lived in the U.S. since 2001 under TPS, which allows people already in the country to remain with work permits for renewable periods of up to 18 months, if the secretary of homeland security determines conditions are unsafe for return. They are eligible for work permits.
Crow agreed with Coffman at the time that the situation of the El Salvadoran immigrants and refugees stands apart.
“Immigrants and asylum seekers who come here legally – including through Temporary Protected Status – work, pay taxes, and contribute greatly to Colorado,” Crow said. “It’s important for Coloradans to remember how we got here. President Trump and Republicans cut healthcare and food assistance to give tax breaks to billionaires and hire thousands of poorly trained ICE agents. Their aggressive immigration tactics and mass deportations have hurt our economy, terrorized our communities, and separated families. Coloradans deserve a secure border, an orderly asylum process for those fleeing violence, and a path for workers, families, and children to earn citizenship.”
During President Donald Trump’s second term, Homeland Security has ended TPS for more than 1 million people from 14 countries, including El Salvador, Venezuela, Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Afghanistan and Syria. Only about 103,000 from three countries remain protected with termination dates in October for Ukraine and Sudan, and November for Lebanon.
The Trump administration obtained a major victory when the Supreme Court ruled in June that Homeland Security acted within its authority by ending TPS for about 350,000 Haitians and 6,000 Syrians. The impact of the decision extends far beyond Haitians and Syrians, potentially affecting nearly 1.3 million people from 17 countries on TPS.
TPS was created by Congress in 1990 to prevent deportations to countries suffering from natural disasters or civil strife.
It was granted to El Salvador following two devastating 2001 earthquakes that left hundreds of thousands of people homeless. Just before leaving office, President Joe Biden extended TPS for El Salvador for 18 months to Sept. 9, 2026.
The vast majority of Salvadoran TPS holders have children born in the U.S. Many have lost their jobs and fear being detained, separated from their American family members, and deported to a country they barely know.
— The Associated Press contributed to this story.
title: Aurora Sentinel: Rep. Crow introduces bill to extend TPS protections for Ukrainian immigrants

ICYMI | Wall Street Journal: “Wells Fargo Faces Regulator Probe Over Efforts to Boost Black Homeownership”
October 7, 2026
WASHINGTON - Today, Secretary Turner launched an investigation into Wells Fargo’s initiatives to increase homeownership for Black Americans, which may be a violation of the Fair Housing Act.
“Even if Wells Fargo did not violate the law, its practice of dividing Americans based on race is immoral, unethical and un-American,” said Secretary Scott Turner. “Wells Fargo and all of its employees that engaged in race-based decision-making should be ashamed of themselves.”
“The Trump Administration will not stand for un-American and unlawful race-based mortgage lending practices from any financial institution,” said Deputy Secretary Andrew Hughes. “This investigation is another important step in the agency’s work to restore justice to fair housing enforcement.”
“The Fair Housing Act forbids racial discrimination in housing. It does not say: discriminate, so long as the discrimination is called a ‘special purpose credit program’ and justified as advancing ‘racial equity in homeownership,’” said Assistant Secretary for Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity Craig Trainor. “No matter an institution’s size, wealth, or power, if there is reasonable cause to believe it has violated Americans’ civil rights, the Trump Administration will hold it to account.”
Read the full letter here.
Read the exclusive story from the Wall Street Journal:
Trump administration housing officials are launching an investigation into Wells Fargo over programs and commitments the bank made over nearly a decade to increase homeownership among Black Americans.
The Department of Housing and Urban Development on Wednesday sent Wells Fargo Chief Executive Charlie Scharf a letter saying it would examine whether the bank violated fair-lending laws by favoring Black or other minority homeowners, according to a copy viewed by The Wall Street Journal.
Wells Fargo didn’t have an immediate comment Wednesday.
The investigation provides another example of corporate America finding itself in the crosshairs for programs that were encouraged during prior administrations, either by the government or socially conscious investors.
The Trump administration has opened investigations into companies for so-called diversity, equity and inclusion programs. It has also launched attempts to find evidence of “debanking,” where banks closed the accounts of businesses or individuals operating in politically controversial industries, from fossil fuels to firearms.
Wells Fargo’s campaign to help Black homeowners goes back years. In 2017, the bank said it was committing $60 billion in loans in an effort to help add at least 250,000 Black homeowners by 2027.
In 2022, the bank expanded the program to put the company’s own money to work refinancing minority homes. That followed criticism the bank faced over a Bloomberg report that it had rejected half of all refinancing applications by Black families in 2020.
“These efforts are an important next step and will help close the homeownership gap between white and minority families created by decades of systemic inequities,” Wells Fargo said in 2022.
In early 2023, Wells Fargo scaled down its mortgage business broadly, focusing on lending to existing customers, but again reiterated a pledge to advance racial equity in housing.
In 2024, only 24% of Black households owned the home they lived in, compared with 73% of White households, according to the Pew Research Center.
Now, Trump officials are considering whether the bank’s efforts to help Black families were a violation of the Fair Housing Act. In its letter, HUD said Wells Fargo had adopted a strategy of “sorting” homeowners and offering different products or terms based on their race.
HUD Secretary Scott Turner said that he plans a full investigation into Wells Fargo’s statements. The agency is also reviewing similar initiatives by other banks, according to a senior HUD official.
“Even if Wells Fargo did not violate the law, its practice of dividing Americans based on race is immoral, unethical and un-American,” Turner said. “Wells Fargo and all of its employees that engaged in race-based decision-making should be ashamed of themselves.”
The HUD probe follows investigations by the Justice Department examining whether government contractors violated antifraud laws by implementing what the administration has called “unlawful” DEI practices. Such programs proliferated amid social unrest in the aftermath of a wave of police violence against Black Americans, including the 2020 murder of George Floyd.
Last year, International Business Machines and Deloitte paid multimillion-dollar fines to resolve claims they defrauded the government by considering diversity when hiring and making promotion and staffing decisions.
The diversity programs and corporate initiatives responding to environmental issues became the subject of intense political backlash from conservatives. Since Trump’s election in 2024, many companies have moved away from their diversity goals, scrubbing websites and investor disclosures.
Wells Fargo achieved about 40% of its initial $60 billion lending commitment and had helped refinance about 5,100 customers—representing an average monthly payment savings of about $100—when it commissioned a racial-equity assessment in late 2023.
It has since gone silent on its racial-equity initiatives, removing the 2023 assessment from its website.
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.

WASHINGTON — On the margins of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Trade Committee, the Office of the United States Trade Representative convened a meeting of senior officials of 14 economies to begin work to address structural excess capacity and production in key manufacturing sectors. Building on the productive discussions at the G20 Trade Ministerial in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, these fourteen economies joined the United States in signing a Joint Ministerial Statement that expresses our collective resolve to work together in new, dedicated sectoral platforms to examine and take effective actions that address structural excess capacity and production in several key sectors of concern. The Joint Ministerial Statement also calls on all countries to take steps to end the use of non-market policies and practices that distort markets and perpetuate structural excess capacity and production. The signatories include the Trade Ministers of Argentina, Australia, Canada, the European Union, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Poland, Türkiye, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
“Over the course of the U.S. G20 presidency, numerous economies raised instances of structural excess capacity and production in economies that persistently exceeded global demand and were sustained by foreign government’s non-market policies and practices,” said Ambassador Greer. “Left unchecked, these issues will continue to cripple domestic industries, displace local production, and hinder our ability to raise the standard of living for workers and their families. The Trump Administration will continue to engage with our trading partners to defend our domestic industries, workers, and economy from distortions resulting from these pervasive policies and practices.”

WASHINGTON, DC – In July 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) issued its first civil penalty under the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP). Treasury penalized Amidi, LLC (Amidi) $200,000 for failing to submit a required notification of an investment by its controlled foreign entity into a Chinese embodied artificial intelligence company. The OISP, which became effective on January 2, 2025, currently requires notification to Treasury of certain types of investments and prohibits certain other types of investments by U.S. persons into entities in or connected to the People’s Republic of China, the Special Administrative Region of Hong Kong, and the Special Administrative Region of Macau that are engaged in certain activities in the quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and semiconductor sectors. In addition, a U.S. person is required (a) to file a notification with Treasury regarding any transaction by its controlled foreign entity if the transaction would be notifiable if engaged in by a U.S. person and (b) to take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent transactions by its controlled foreign entity if the transaction would be prohibited if engaged in by a U.S. person.
On April 19, 2025, Amidi’s subsidiary, a Chinese fund, invested approximately $92,478 in Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology Company Limited (Noematrix). Amidi is also the parent entity of the organization that does business as Plug and Play Tech Center. Noematrix is a private Chinese company that develops artificial intelligence, robotics, and embodied intelligence.
“Today’s penalty announcement under the Outbound Investment Security Program underscores Treasury’s commitment to safeguarding U.S. national security through robust investment security measures that preserve America’s technological leadership and advance President Trump’s America First Investment Policy,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.
“The Outbound Investment Security Program is an important tool aimed at addressing the advancement of key technologies by countries of concern that could pose risks to U.S. national security,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton. Pilkerton added, “We will continue to ensure that investors comply with the requirements established under the program.”
The issuance of the penalty highlights Treasury’s commitment to compliance with OISP rules. Treasury identified this transaction as part of its regular and ongoing compliance and market monitoring efforts. On December 18, 2025, Congress passed the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025 (COINS), which will expand OISP jurisdiction to include investments in additional countries and technology sectors. In assessing compliance and whether to bring an enforcement action in connection with a particular transaction, Treasury will evaluate the facts and circumstances surrounding the conduct, including the aggravating and mitigating factors described in the Outbound Investment Security Program Enforcement Overview and Guidance.
If anyone believes that a violation may have occurred, the Treasury Department encourages them to submit tips, referrals, or other relevant information to the Outbound Program tips line: Outbound.Tips@treasury.gov.
###
title: Treasury Announces Enforcement Penalty for Violation of Outbound Program

SOUTH BEND – Kumar Bishop, 47 years old, of South Bend, Indiana, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Damon R. Leichty after pleading guilty to conspiracy to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine.

Bishop was sentenced to 121 months in prison followed by 7 years of supervised release.

According to documents in the case, between September 2025 and November 2025, Bishop conspired with DeCarlos L. Smallwood and Sanena Williams to distribute methamphetamine to others in the Northern District of Indiana.

“Kumar Bishop will spend more than the next ten years in federal prison. This sentence holds him accountable for supplying large quantities of methamphetamine that poisoned our communities for profit. Methamphetamine is a destructive drug that tears families apart and ravages entire neighborhoods. Thanks to the relentless dedication of our partners on the Homeland Security Task Force, a major source of this poison has been removed from Northern Indiana. This office remains steadfast in its commitment to disrupting drug trafficking networks and protecting our communities from those who exploit addiction for personal gain,” said U.S. Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

“The Drug Enforcement Administration, along with its law enforcement partners, will continue to hold accountable those responsible for bringing drugs into our Indiana communities. Mr. Bishop maintained southwest border drug connections, which he used to supply the South Bend region with methamphetamine. His actions brought suffering and addiction to our neighbors and neighborhoods. Today, the South Bend region is safer and healthier with Mr. Bishop off the streets; he is no longer a threat to our communities.”

“Strong partnerships are at the heart of every successful law enforcement investigation. The more than ten-year sentence in this case demonstrates what is possible when we work collaboratively to investigate and prosecute drug traffickers which in turn disrupts the flow of dangerous drugs into our communities. ATF will continue to work closely with our HSTF partners towards our shared goal of reducing violent crime and making America safer.” – ATF Chicago Field Division Special Agent in Charge Christopher Amon

“Meth dealers should know this: You can’t hide from us, and you can’t profit from poisoning our neighborhoods without consequences,” said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Timothy J. O’Malley. “The Homeland Security Task Force and our partners are going after the people who bring this poison into our communities. We will find them, we will put them out of business, and we will put them behind bars.”

The U.S. Postal Inspection Service works tirelessly with our federal, state and local partners to combat the distribution of illicit substances. The sentencing of Kumar Bishop is an example of law enforcement working together towards the common goal of securing our communities from dangerous individuals.

This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, including the DEA Merrillville District Office, DEA Chicago Special Response Team, DEA Detroit Special Response Team, DEA St. Louis Special Response Team, and DEA North Central Laboratory, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the United States Postal Inspection Service, with assistance from the Indiana State Police, South Bend Police Department, St. Joseph County Sheriff’s Office, Mishawaka Police Department, and the St. Joseph County Prosecutor’s Office. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Lydia T. Lucius and Joel Gabrielse.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Indianapolis comprises agents and officers from FBI, HSI, DEA, ATF, IRS, Indiana State Police, and other partners, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Offices for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

Maryland Delegation Pushes for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade
Lawmakers press for funding following reports of severe mental health concerns among service members, civilian employees at Cyber Command, including several recent deaths by suicide
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02) joined the Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation (CITI) Subcommittee of the House Armed Services Committee and the Maryland Delegation in requesting an additional $11 million in funding for mental health support at U.S. Cyber Command following reports of multiple suicides earlier this year. Olszewski joined Representatives Sarah Elfreth (D-MD-03), Don Bacon (R-NE-02), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Rich McCormick (R-GA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06), Herbert Conaway (D-NJ-03), Eugene Vindman (D-VA-07), and Pat Ryan (D-NY-18). On the letter from the Maryland members, Elfreth was joined by her Maryland delegation colleagues, including Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), who co-led the letter, along with Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), and Representatives Steny Hoyer (D-MD-05), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), and April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06). Both letters were directed to the heads of the House and Senate Appropriations Committees.
“We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training… Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions,” wrote the CITI members.
“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” wrote the Maryland lawmakers. “Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively ‘deployed in place’ for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.”
“One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at NSA and Cyber Command has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again,” wrote the CITI members.
The full CITI letter can be accessed HERE. The full Maryland letter can be accessed HERE.
title: Maryland Delegation Pushes for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade

Federal partners seize 90 fuel shipments valued at over $2.8 million bound for sanctioned Cuban entity
Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Miami and HSI Houston, working with Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), seized 90 biodiesel fuel shipments valued at over $2.8 million dollars. These shipments were part of an attempt to unlawfully export fuel to Cuba in violation of federal export laws.
HSI Miami, HSI Houston, CBP and BIS developed information indicating that the Cuban government used ENETEC S.A. to receive fuel illegally exported from the United States. In early September 2026, CBP, through coordinated intelligence and trade data analysis, identified shipments of biodiesel fuel being illegally exported from the United States, specifically from Port Everglades (PEV) and the Port of Houston to ENETEC S.A, in Cuba. HSI Miami and HSI Houston, in coordination with CBP and BIS requested the detention of these shipments. A total of 71 shipments containing approximately 496,000 gallons of biodiesel fuel at Port Everglades were seized and 19 additional shipments containing approximately 119,000 gallons at the Port of Houston are currently being detained.
HSI requested the seizure of the shipments based on suspected violations of federal export laws, including exportation contrary to law; the International Emergency Economic Powers Act; and regulations governing merchandise subject to the Export Administration Regulations.
“This seizure underscores HSI Miami’s commitment to stopping fuel and other goods from the United States from being illegally exported to Cuba through sanctioned entities or deceptive commercial networks.” said HSI Miami Special Agent in Charge Jose R. Figueroa. “Working with our federal partners, we will continue to identify, disrupt and investigate efforts to evade U.S. sanctions, protect the integrity of U.S. export controls and deny the Cuban government access to resources obtained in violation of U.S. law.”
“U.S. Customs and Border Protection is steadfast in enforcing the laws of the United States across all domains, encompassing both incoming commerce and outbound shipments,” said Daniel Alonso, Director of Field Operations. Through vigilant outbound operations, our officers successfully intercepted these shipments and took appropriate action. Trade enforcement is a collaborative mission; by working closely with the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the Department of Commerce, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and our federal partners, we ensure that commercial shipments comply with U.S. sanctions and export laws, safeguarding our national security and foreign policy interests.”
“The Bureau of Industry and Security is aggressively enforcing our export control laws, including with respect to Cuba, and this will continue,” said Jeremy Shein, Special Agent in Charge for BIS Miami.
HSI Miami, HSI Houston, CBP and BIS continue to investigate the matter.

On the third anniversary of the brutal attack on Israel, the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights (OCR) is expanding its investigation into Swarthmore College over complaints that it has not adequately and promptly responded to particularly egregious antisemitic propaganda on campus. OCR will determine whether the institution violated Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title VI) by allowing or failing to meaningfully respond to antisemitic harassment.
Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists tortured, raped, burned alive, and otherwise brutally massacred roughly 1,200 innocent people, and kidnapped roughly 250 more, locking them in underground dungeons and subjecting them to further abuse. Near the anniversary of this fateful day, the Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP) at Swarthmore College saw fit to release a video depicting an Israeli soldier being doused in gasoline and burnt in effigy.
With the backdrop of this burning soldier, SJP displayed the message “Long Live Al-Aqsa Flood,” using the term Hamas terrorists coined to describe the horrific October 7th massacres. The video then shows the burning Israeli soldier under a Palestinian flag and proceeds to call on supporters to go “All Out” at rallies on October 6 and October 7, 2026. “On the third anniversary of October 7th, these new allegations underscore that radicalism and antisemitism are incompatible with safe learning environments,” said Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kimberly Richey. “If Swarthmore has in fact turned a blind eye to such provocation—using the most horrific acts of violence against Jews since the Holocaust as a propaganda tool—someone is asleep at the wheel. Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces $90 Million Loan to Eliminate Traffic Bottlenecks, Accident Hotspots on I-81 in Virginia
Upgrades will cut travel delays, add truck climbing lanes, replace aging bridges, and enhance freight flow along major Mid-Atlantic commerce corridor
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced Virginia’s Commonwealth Transportation Board (CTB) will receive two Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) loans totaling up to $89.7 million from the Build America Bureau. The package funds vital capacity and safety upgrades along 325 rural miles of I-81, a key East Coast freight route carrying 43% of Virginia's interstate truck traffic.
The projects will transform I-81 by:
- Adding dedicated truck climbing lanes in Washington County and Augusta County, allowing slow-moving heavy trucks to climb steep hills without blocking passenger cars;
- Fixing dangerous merging bottlenecks by extending exit ramps in Wythe County and adding merge lanes around Wytheville to give drivers more room to speed up or slow down safely; and,
- Replacing aging bridges over Peppers Ferry Road and the I-81 northbound bridge over I-77 to guarantee long-term corridor reliability.
“President Trump understands strong roads mean strong supply chains—that’s why he is investing in big, beautiful upgrades along the I-81 corridor in Virginia,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “By upgrading the commonwealth’s transportation infrastructure, reducing dangerous bottlenecks, and separating freight and passenger traffic, Virginia families and freight will move more safely and efficiently across the entire Mid-Atlantic region.”
The package supports Virginia’s $4 billion I-81 Corridor Improvement Program, which is projected to generate $5.2 billion in economic activity, supporting regional growth and job creation. Construction on many projects is already underway, with completion slated for late 2035.
“By securing a TIFIA loan at half the standard interest rate, the Commonwealth of Virginia is delivering these critical improvements faster and more affordably,” said Build America Bureau Executive Director Morteza Farajian, Ph.D. “By cutting interest costs in half and stretching taxpayer dollars, this project serves as a national blueprint. It proves that innovative financing can help rural communities deliver vital corridor improvements faster while freeing up resources for future infrastructure needs.”
“As a vital commercial corridor not only for Virginia but the entire east coast, additional travel lanes, new bridges and interchange improvements are enhancing safety and reducing congestion on I-81,” said Virginia Transportation Secretary Nick Donohue. “The TIFIA loans will help Virginia stretch its transportation dollars and continue building the interstate corridor all travelers deserve.”
Additional Information:
The two loans, totaling up to $47.6 million and $42.1 million respectively, take advantage of low interest rates made possible by the TIFIA Rural Project Initiative and build on Secretary Duffy’s broader campaign to eliminate traffic bottlenecks across America.
###
The Build America Bureau accelerates investment in transportation infrastructure by lending federal funds to qualified public and private borrowers; clearing roadblocks for creditworthy projects; and providing technical assistance services and grants to build local and regional capacity and implement best practices and innovative solutions in project planning, funding, financing, delivery, and operations. The Bureau draws on expertise across DOT to serve as the point of coordination for states, municipalities, private partners, and other project sponsors seeking federal financing.
title: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces $90 Million Loan to Eliminate Traffic Bottlenecks, Accident Hotspots on I-81 in Virginia

Reps. Davis, Bergman, Van Drew, Golden Introduce SMILE for Veterans Act
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Reps. Don Davis (NC-01), Jack Bergman (MI-01), Jeff Van Drew (NJ-02) and Jared Golden (ME-02) have introduced the SMILE for Veterans Act, bipartisan legislation which will create a Department of Veterans Affairs Pilot Program to pay for local dentists providing care to America's rural veterans.
"Too many rural veterans experience difficulty obtaining necessary dental care, and quality dental care is essential for maintaining overall health," said Rep. Don Davis. "The SMILE for Veterans Act provides community-based providers with a means to provide that care closer to home. We owe it to our veterans to maintain our promise to provide them with the best care possible.”
At this time, only approximately 15 percent of the nearly 9 million veterans receiving their healthcare through the VA are eligible for VA-funded dental care. In most cases, eligibility for dental care is based on whether a veteran has a service-connected dental issue, a 100 percent disability rating, or was a former prisoner of war.
The SMILE for Veterans Act addresses the lack of accessibility to quality dental care in rural areas by allowing local dentists already in place to be reimbursed for treating rural veterans. The legislation would allow for increased access to dental care in underserved areas using the current provider base and infrastructure, without creating additional costs or requiring the VA to develop new dental systems.
“For too many veterans in rural communities, basic dental care is either too far away or simply out of reach,”said Rep. Jack Bergman.“The SMILE for Veterans Act offers a practical solution by connecting veterans with trusted dental providers already serving their communities. Rather than building an expensive new federal system from the ground up, this legislation uses existing local providers to deliver care efficiently and closer to home.”
“I spent 30 years as a dentist, and I can tell you that putting off dental care usually only makes things worse,”said Rep. Jeff Van Drew.“For veterans living in rural communities, sometimes the hardest part is simply finding a dentist close enough to get the care they need. That should not be the case. The SMILE for Veterans Act is a practical way to connect veterans with that care closer to home. To me, that is common sense.”
“VA health care is an essential benefit for our nation’s veterans, but for too long a lack of dental coverage has been a massive gap in care. The mouth is part of the body, and our veterans shouldn’t have to jump through hoops to get basic dental care. I’m proud to work with Reps. Bergman, Davis and Van Drew on the SMILE Act, which takes a smart first step toward more comprehensive coverage by focusing on rural areas where barriers to care are the highest and community providers that can help close the gap,”said Rep. Jared Golden.
The SMILE for Veterans Act is supported by AMVETS, the National Rural Health Association, and the CareQuest Institute for Oral Health.

title: Reps. Davis, Bergman, Van Drew, Golden Introduce SMILE for Veterans Act

Man Arrested and Charged for Role in Plotting to Conduct a Mass-Shooting Event in Support of ISIS at the Mall of America
Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, of Richfield, Minnesota, was charged today by complaint with one count of knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition in order to commit a federal crime of terrorism.
The FBI arrested the defendant on Oct. 6, and he made his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright on Oct. 7.
“This individual allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Once again this FBI is moving more effectively than we ever have before at stopping terrorists before they can attack Americans – with over 1,100 individuals prevented from conducting attacks, over 4,000 foreign terrorist organization related disruptions and arrests, a 38% increase, and more. We will continue to use every resource we have to detect and prevent acts of terrorism and wipe out their networks all over the country. Thank you to FBI Minneapolis who did an outstanding job in the investigation and likely saved lives.”
“Mohamud allegedly sought to carry out a mass-casualty shooting at the Mall of America, expressing a desire to emulate some of the most horrific ISIS-inspired attacks in the United States, including the atrocities at Pulse Nightclub and 2025 New Year’s Day attack in New Orleans,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will continue to work closely with the FBI and Joint Terrorism Task Force to track down and prosecute ISIS-inspired terrorists in the United States.”
“As alleged in the criminal complaint, Mohamud took substantial steps to plot to murder innocent people in the name of ISIS,” said U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota. “Such threats are taken seriously, and I commend the committed public servants of the Joint Terrorism Task Force, the FBI, and my office, who work every day to stop them.”
According to the complaint, beginning in or about December 2024, Mohamud exchanged hundreds of messages through multiple social media and messaging applications with a confidential source. Mohamud expressed his desire to travel to Somalia to join a designated foreign terrorist organization to fight on its behalf. Mohamud also expressed a desire to commit a mass-casualty event in Minnesota by acquiring and using a firearm and ammunition. The defendant stated many times that if he was unable to travel overseas because of a lack of funds, he planned to carry out a mass-casualty event in Minnesota in support of ISIS.
In July 2026, Mohamud sent messages discussing his intent to carry out a mass-casualty shooting attack at the Mall of America because he claimed it was owned by Jews. He wrote that wanted to kill 30 to 60 people so no one would go there.
In August and September 2026, Mohamud continued to send messages discussing his intentions, including his plans to purchase a firearm and to recruit others to join him in committing the attack. Mohamud sent a selfie-style video of himself pledging allegiance to ISIS:
Screenshot of Mohamud’s Video Pledging Allegiance to ISIS
During the course of his communications, Mohamud stated that he wanted to commit an attack similar to those of the Pulse Nightclub mass-shooting in Orlando, the Bondi Beach mass-shooting in Australia, and the New Year’s Day vehicle-ramming attack in New Orleans.
In September 2026, Mohamud expressed a desire to kill “kuffar” — a term used to refer to a non-Muslim. Mohamud identified Oct. 24 as the date of his planned attack. When the confidential source asked if there was a big gathering on Oct. 24, Mohamud indicated that there were would be numerous Asians and other “kuffar” celebrating at the Mall of America. Mohamud then sent a link to a “Hmong Arts Celebration” at the Mall of America.
In September 2026, Mohamud continued to send propaganda videos to the confidential source. A still shot from one of the propaganda videos sent by Mohamud is depicted below:
Still Shot of Propaganda Video Sent by Mohamud
On Oct. 6, the FBI arranged to sell to Mohamud, through an undercover FBI employee, an AK-47 assault rifle, four 30-round magazines, and approximately 200 rounds of ammunition. The FBI rendered the AK-47 rifle inert prior to the transaction. The FBI arrested Mohamud shortly after he paid about $600 cash for the rifle, magazines, and ammunition and had those items in his possession. During the sale of the firearm and ammunition, Mohamud reaffirmed his plan to use the firearm and ammunition to shoot people at the Mall of America.
This case was the result of an investigation by the FBI, the Joint Terrorism Task Force, and the Bloomington Police Department, with assistance from IRS Criminal Investigation.
This case is being prosecuted by Trial Attorney Ryan White of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Bejar for the District of Minnesota.
A complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

Reps. Davids (D), Crane (R) Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Eli Crane (R-AZ-02) introduced bipartisan legislation to improve how unused housing vouchers are managed and distributed. The legislation would allow Tribes to voluntarily give back vouchers they do not plan to use, so the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) can redirect assistance to Tribal communities facing a shortage.
"Native veterans hold a special place in my heart,” said Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation of Wisconsin. “My mom and grandfather both served in the Army, and as a Native person, I know how much our communities value the veterans who have served our country. Tribal Nations know best what their communities and veterans need, and respecting Tribal sovereignty means giving them the flexibility and resources to meet those needs. I'm grateful to work with Rep. Crane on this bipartisan effort to ensure more Native veterans get the housing they need after returning home.”
"The Tribal HUD-VASH program helps house Tribal veterans in need, but the current system is not as efficient as it should be,” said Representative Eli Crane (R-AZ-02). “Some Tribes have leftover vouchers they cannot use while others lack the resources to take care of our veterans. Our legislation aims to resolve this longstanding issue by getting unused vouchers into the hands of Tribes that can put them to use. This is a sensible approach that makes better use of existing support without expanding the size and scope of the federal government. As the representative for more than half of the Tribes in Arizona, I'm honored to advocate for these heroes by reforming and modernizing this process. I appreciate Rep. Davids' willingness to work across the aisle. We've made real progress together before, and I look forward to building on that success with this bill.”
Native American veterans experience some of the highest rates of homelessness in the United States. To address this, Congress created the Tribal HUD-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (Tribal HUD-VASH) demonstration program, which provides rental assistance and supportive services to Native veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
Although the program has helped many veterans secure stable housing, it lacks a clear process for Tribes to return vouchers they cannot use or to request additional ones. As a result, valuable housing support sits idle while veterans in other Tribal communities wait for help.
The new Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act directs HUD to establish a voluntary program for reallocating unused Tribal HUD-VASH vouchers to Native veterans who need them most. Under the bill, Tribes and Tribally Designated Housing Entities (TDHEs) can notify HUD via digital, phone, or mail correspondence if they have surplus vouchers or request additional assistance for their communities without impacting their future allocations.
Required to launch within 180 days of enactment, the program creates a streamlined process to strengthen Tribal HUD-VASH and expand Native veterans' access to earned housing assistance. Within that same timeframe, HUD must submit a congressional report detailing voucher usage and shortfall metrics, distribution recommendations, and an assessment of whether to increase overall program funding.
This is not the first time Davids and Crane have partnered on legislation to assist Tribal communities. Davids previously introduced the Native American Entrepreneurial Opportunity Act, which would bolster U.S. Small Business Administration outreach to Tribal entrepreneurs navigating the unique complexities of running a business on a reservation. Crane co-led the measure, and it has twice passed the House with strong bipartisan support.
title: Reps. Davids (D), Crane (R) Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans

BOISE, Idaho—In a proactive step to reduce wildfire risk and invest in healthy, resilient public lands, the Bureau of Land Management Boise District in southwestern Idaho, partnering with the U.S. Wildland Fire Service, will conduct the following aerial herbicide treatments:
- Approximately 9,800 acres of lands managed by the BLM Bruneau Field Office within Owyhee County.
- Approximately 6,000 acres of lands managed by the BLM Owyhee and Four Rivers Field Offices within Ada and Owyhee Counties.
Treatments are scheduled to begin the second week of October 2026, depending on weather, wildfire activity and other operational conditions. They are intended to reduce invasive annual grasses and hazardous fine fuels, maintain strategic fuel breaks, support vegetation recovery following wildfire, and improve the establishment and long-term success of desirable perennial vegetation. By strengthening landscapes before wildfire strikes, the work helps reduce wildfire risk and the potential costs of large, damaging fires while protecting wildlife habitat, rangelands, watersheds and other public resources.
Treatments will use the BLM-approved herbicide imazapic. Application rates will vary by project area based on vegetation and management objectives.
The public may see low-flying aircraft over designated treatment areas and should avoid those areas while applications are underway. USWFS employees will be present in project areas before and during application. Federal officials appreciate the public’s cooperation as these treatments invest in the long-term health and resilience of public lands and reduce wildfire risk.
Rangelands in Idaho and across the West have been heavily impacted by destructive wildfires, exacerbated by drought, insects, and disease, leaving millions of acres vulnerable to future wildfires. Since 2000, wildfires have burned an average of 7.3 million acres annually, with BLM lands seeing an average of 236,530 acres affected each year. This year alone, wildfires have devastated over 3.3 million acres of BLM-managed lands, and 9 million acres of all jurisdictions nationwide.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM Targets Invasive Weeds to Reduce Wildfire Risk in Southwestern Idaho

Rep. Sykes Announces $33,000 for Canal Fulton-Lawrence Township Fire Department
CANAL FULTON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Canal Fulton – Lawrence Township Fire Department is receiving two Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) grant awards that will fund new firefighting equipment and a community fire safety training tool. Congresswoman Sykes supported both grant applications with letters of support.
The City of Canal Fulton received the following awards:
- $17,055.55 in federal funding for a regional fire hose replacement, with a local share of $852.78, for a total project investment of $17,908.33. The project will replace attack and supply hose within the departments' shared response system.
- $16,737.14 in federal funding for a fire extinguisher training system, with a local share of $836.86, for a total project investment of $17,574.00. The project will provide an augmented-reality training system that allows hands-on public education without live fire, smoke, chemical discharge, or cleanup.
Together, the awards provide $33,792.69 in federal funding toward a total investment of $35,482.33 in public safety projects.
“Our firefighters and EMS crews show up to keep our neighbors safe every day, and they must have the tools to do their jobs safely. I am proud to have supported Canal Fulton's grant applications, and I congratulate Chief Yerian and the entire department on these well-earned awards,”said Congresswoman Sykes.
“Receiving these FEMA awards is tremendous news for the Canal Fulton community and our regional fire service,” said Shawn Yerian, Fire Chief of the Canal Fulton – Lawrence Township Fire Department. “The funding will allow us to replace outdated fire hose that our firefighters rely on every day, while also providing a new fire extinguisher training system that addresses one of the most frequent safety-training requests we receive from local businesses.
“These are important investments in both firefighter safety and community education, and they are projects we would not have been able to move forward with at this time without federal assistance. We are extremely grateful for Congresswoman Sykes' support of our applications and her continued support of local fire and EMS services. Her assistance helped make it possible for us to bring these resources back to the community we serve.”
Congresswoman Sykes congratulates Chief Yerian and the entire Canal Fulton - Lawrence Township Fire Department on these awards and thanks them for their service to the community.
title: Rep. Sykes Announces $33,000 for Canal Fulton-Lawrence Township Fire Department

text:
Speech

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

The Pnyx

Athens, Greece

October 7, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO: There are great ruins all across the world. In many cases, they are places where history seems to have exhausted itself: remnants of distant cultures that have long passed beyond living memory.

But the Acropolis is different.

For thousands of years, the civilization that built what stands behind me has captivated the imagination of the Western world. Generations of our statesmen, artists, and philosophers have looked to it – they’ve looked to it with wonder and they’ve looked to it with awe.

Now time has a tendency to dull the senses: great victories and catastrophic defeats, they seem to shrink to becoming like a footnote in a textbook, another fact for our schoolchildren to memorize and forget. But the Greeks of antiquity, they seem to have an almost mystical hold on our memory. They call us back to them, again and again.

480 years before Christ, the armies of Xerxes arrived in this city and they put its sanctuaries to the torch. Most Athenians had by then evacuated by ship to a nearby island. But there was a handful of them that refused to leave their home. So instead, they barricaded themselves in the rocky fortress of the Acropolis to fight an extraordinary last stand, heaving massive stones down the cliffs onto the Persian invaders and holding the greatest empire of the age at bay for days. They were eventually overwhelmed. The Persians plundered the temples, burned the shrines, and razed the Acropolis to the ground but when the Athenians returned, they gathered the broken remains of the old Acropolis and buried them in the hill where it had stood. And decades later, under Pericles, they raised the Parthenon.

For 25 centuries since, the Parthenon has stood. Empires have risen and fallen beneath its shadow. And the progeny of the men who built it – the sons of Athens and Rome – have carried their civilization with them to the ends of the Earth.

Two and a half centuries after the founding of the American republic halfway across the world from where I stand now – I stand here today as the Secretary of State of that republic, and a great-grandson of settlers who arrived in the new world from Spain – I stand here to testify to a debt that no lapse of time, no distance of space can ever extinguish.

The history of America, the history of my country, is covered with the fingerprints of antiquity. Greece is literally carved into the architecture of our government: in the towering columns, in the domes and the monuments across our capital city. The city where our Constitution was born – Philadelphia – is itself a Greek name.

The men who founded my country were fascinated by the heritage we inherited from yours. They were exceptionally well-read in history – they were vividly aware of their unique place in it – but no other age of the past held their attention or their imagination quite like that of antiquity. Many, many people are surprised to learn that the most commonly cited author in the Federalist Papers was not an Enlightenment philosopher or political theorist. No, the most commonly cited author in the Federalist Papers was Plutarch, the Greek biographer of Greece and Rome’s great men.

Now, much has been written and said about the influence of ancient Greece on the ideas of the American Founders – and, for that matter, on all of the Western philosophers and statesmen that preceded them. Most of us are familiar with the basic history. Athens gave us democracy. Plato and Aristotle gave us Western philosophy. Our ideas of law, of virtue, of citizenship, and republican government were shaped in the Greek city-states. Even much of our political vocabulary – words like democracy, tyranny, the word “politics” itself – found its origins here.

Now, all of that is true. But the things we owe to this place – as Americans, and as Westerners – are actually far far deeper. These institutions and ideas – these institutions and ideas were the outward expression of more fundamental qualities we see in the ancient Greeks – qualities that can’t be reduced to any particular political system or theory.

Here, in Athens, we found the first full realization of all the essential traits that would come to define the West: fierce individuality and relentless ambition; daring exploration and invention; a yearning for discovery, for adventure, risk and glory. An insatiable curiosity about the world and the principles by which it operates, a hunger to know the mysteries of nature and grasp the secrets of the cosmos. An impatience with the notion of impossibility, chafing at all boundaries and limits, straining to peer into the depths of the unknown.

These were not just the formulas or precepts of a particular school of philosophy. They were the characteristic of a people – expressed in their traditions, their stories, their imagination; in the qualities they demanded of their citizens; in the things they lived and fought and died for.

To know them is to know ourselves.

What blossomed here in this place was the Western desire to uncover all that ignorance, darkness, and distance had kept hidden from the mind of man. The Greeks did not just shape history; the Greeks gave us history itself. Much about – much of what we know about many ancient civilizations comes almost entirely from the records of Greek explorers and historians, explorers and historians who didn’t just chronicle the histories of their own people, but ventured outwards to observe and record the sagas of foreign peoples and cultures all across the world.

Where others looked inward, the Greeks were the first to direct their focus outward, to chase the thrill and glory of seeing all that was strange and new. It was this trait – it was this trait that would push the West to create and build things that others could not, marking us out from so many other cultures and civilizations where stability and subsistence were the highest ends of life.

But it is not just the ambition to explore the unknown that we inherit from the Greeks; it is the conviction that the unknown canbe known. The confidence that the world can be charted and measured and mapped and understood – and that there is a rational order to the cosmos, governed by certain fundamental laws, laws that men can observe and the mind can come to understand.

This was the foundation of the Western mind: our math, our science, our medicine. Our philosophy, ethics, and religion. It paved the way for the gospel of Jesus Christ to find fertile soil in Europe and flourish into the empire of Christendom. It was the foundation of the riches of Christian theology – of Augustine and Aquinas and the whole tradition of natural law.

It gave birth to a civilization marked not just by a common culture, it was marked by a common anthropology – a common view of man and his place in the universe. Its descendants would share not just the idea of a natural order, but a distinctive understanding of virtue; of destiny and fate; of truth, goodness, and beauty; of a code that dictates how men ought to live; of objective standards and ideals to strive towards.

For the Greeks of antiquity, the pursuit of excellence was the very principle of man’s existence. They organized all of civic life around contest, ambition, competition: in philosophy and poetry, in sculpture and drama, in athletics and art, in war and statecraft. The classical Greek city was an arena for great men to test and prove themselves, to hone their potential through perpetual struggle – to be the best, the strongest, the most beautiful, straining to inch ever closer to perfection.

Now I know that to modern ears, what I just described, this way of life, may sound odd; it may even sound cruel. The ideal of many ideologies in our time has, frankly, become a world of perfect safety, devoid of risk or failure, with neither the glory of victory nor the shame of defeat. Too often these days, we build downwards. We design our standards to ensure no one will lose; we preoccupy ourselves more with the comfort of the worst than the potential of the best. We hold the most exceptional things among us hostage to the average, the ordinary, the mediocre.

The men who made the Parthenon, they built upwards. They held that the highest and most noble aspiration in life was to surpass all others, to strive to be the best in all things. The ancient Greek city-states were filled. They were filled with intense passion and rivalry and faction and conflict. But from that constant struggle for distinction – from that came the great flowering of art and philosophy and political and intellectual energy that would transform a collective of Mediterranean cities into the birthplace of the greatest civilization in the world.

The thumos , as the ancient Greeks called it – the fire of passion, strength, courage, pride – is the heart of great civilization. And without it? Without it, nations lose their will to fight, the will to strive, the will to survive.

Today, too much of the West has forgotten this quality. Over time, we in the West came to feel ashamed of the very things that made us exceptional. We felt embarrassed that our achievements set us apart from the rest of the world. Our prosperity somehow became a source of guilt. We no longer believed we deserved and had earned our greatness.

The word “nationalism” became a dirty word. And so we tore down our monuments; we condemned our own history. And in too many places, we taught our children to be ashamed of the countries they would inherit. In the process, we opened our borders and outsourced our industry, and allowed our militaries to wither and to decay.

And with every passing year, we seemed to outsource more of our sovereignty, transferring our decisions to global bureaucracies far beyond the reach of our control.

But others were all too happy to fill the vacuum that we left – the vacuum left behind by our weakness. And as the West’s confidence faltered, its adversaries and its rivals only grew more assertive, building up their own wealth and their own power in our stead.

And now, today, we find ourselves at a crossroads. Because the next decade and the decisions we make will write the story of the next century. The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline. We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.

Under President Trump, the United States has made its choice. We choose the unapologetic pursuit of national power: to take back control of our critical supply chains, to reindustrialize our economy, to rebuild our defense, to fight for dominance of the technologies and industries of the future.

We choose to reach for new frontiers: in advanced manufacturing and super intelligence; in drones, weapons, and warfare; in chips, minerals, cyber, and every other domain of human possibility. To unleash our energy, to rebuild our factories, to return our astronauts to the moon and launch a new age of exploration in space.

Now for all their lofty ideals, the ancient Greeks were not naive. They understood that nations have interests. They understood that statecraft requires prudence and diplomacy, but they also understood that it requires the ability to wield force when prudence and diplomacy fail. They understood that power requires not only having the means to defend yourself, it requires the credibility that you are willing to use it.

This is the classical understanding of politics and of statecraft that the Trump Administration hopes to reclaim – reclaim not just for our country, but for the whole of our civilization.

We believe that Europe can awaken from its long slumber and rekindle the fire that was lit here millennia ago.

There are already signs.

Across this continent, we are witnessing what we hope will be the beginnings of a generational shift: skyrocketing defense spending, a flurry of new partnerships and programs, expanded manufacturing and production, following on the historic defense commitments made last year in The Hague.

Greece has been at the center of this shift. The people of this nation have proved themselves once again to be an indispensable friend to Europe and to the United States alike, on everything from energy to migration to defense, where Greece has been a model ally.

And it’s our sincerest hope that all of Europe will follow your example.

Though passions may, at times, have strained the bonds of affection between the United States and Europe, it must not be allowed to break them. Together, we must strengthen an alliance capable of confronting threats of our age.

And we can. Because we do not believe the transatlantic friendship should be zero sum. Quite the opposite: our vision is of an alliance whose strength is greater than the sum of its parts. It is a vision we saw in action just last month, in an unprecedented new agreement between the United States, Denmark, and Greenland – an agreement that will reshape the Arctic and bolster the security of all of NATO. All three partners in that deal emerged victorious. All of Europe – and NATO and the United States emerged safer, stronger, and more secure because of it.

We want to win together. We must win together.

Now it’s has become fashionable today to believe that enlightened foreign policy means prioritizing the global community over one’s own people. And I think here, too, we have much to learn from the men of ancient Greece because they knew that there was nothing selfish or wrong about loyalty to your nation, nor anything selfish or wrong about fighting to defend its interests above all else.

They believed – fiercely – in the ideal of the great man: the exceptional individual who obtains immortality through his own deeds. But they believed that glory and fame, those things were won through striving, sacrificing and achieving greatly for something larger than yourself. The recurring hero of the ancient Greek world was the man who was willing to pay any cost for a cause worthy of his loyalty.

We see this in Socrates, who refused to abandon the inquiry into truth even at the cost of his own life. We see it in the legendary stand of 300 Spartans – surrounded and hopelessly outnumbered by the vast armies of Persia – who refused the chance to save themselves, choosing to fight to the last man rather than abandon their post or abandon their duty. And we see it in the epic myth of Achilles, who is offered the choice to return home and live a long and peaceful life – but chooses instead to remain at Troy and perish in pursuit of eternal glory.

These – these are the qualities that would shape the Western moral imagination. From the Christian martyr who refused to betray his faith to the patriot who gave his life for his country; from Saint Thomas More to the Battle of the Alamo, running through the immortal closing words of the Declaration of Independence of the United States which says, “We mutually pledge to each other our Lives, our Fortunes and our sacred Honor.”

It is from the Greeks that the West inherited its sense of duty – an unbreakable loyalty to one’s code, one’s cause, one’s country. Our heroes, the heroes of the West are those who choose to remain faithful to their duty precisely when it is most difficult and painful to do so: the man who is bound by his word, the soldier who will not abandon his post, the captain, the proverbial captain, who goes down with his ship.

This is wholly different from what we see, even now, for example from fanatics like the radical mullahs of Iran, whose cult of death hails child suicide bombers as national heroes, and portrays martyrdom as an end to itself.

Our heroes – our heroes may be willing to die for their cause; but our heroes do not worship death. It is precisely because we value life that we come to recognize the heroism in those who would sooner sacrifice it than to betray their principles. Now, we take the West’s conception of these things – heroism, honor, duty – we take these things for granted. We assume that these somehow are universal to all people in all times and in all places. They are not. They are the product of a distinct character, a distinct character which arose here and shaped the whole story of the civilization that came after it. A civilization that we must fight to defend today with the same passion as our forefathers did.

The men who built the Parthenon were succeeded by the architects of European Christendom, who raised the cathedrals of Milan, Cologne, and Florence. The quest to perfect the human form that moved the ancient Greek sculptors found a new expression in Michelangelo. The Greek philosophers’ search for the structure of the universe was inherited by Copernicus, and then Galileo, then Kepler, and in Newton.

The hunger for new knowledge, that’s what gave birth to Magellan’s first expedition around the world, to Columbus’ discovery of the Americas, and ultimately to Apollo 11’s journey to the moon. And the qualities that led Alexander to conquer the entire known world reappeared in Caesar, then Charlemagne, and Cortes.

And in America, that same tradition rediscovered itself anew. An open and wild land became the site of a great revival of Western imagination and ambition. The Greek aspiration for new horizons became the American frontier spirit. The civilization of Athens and Rome transformed an infant seaboard republic into a continental empire.

The greatest Americans of every generation have carried the unmistakable features of their forefathers – born in Athens, formed by Rome, baptized in Christendom, hardened in the furnace of medieval Europe, endowed with the English genius for liberty, and then carried across the Atlantic to be reborn on the shores of a new world.

Together, we must now rediscover that spirit. We are at an inflection point – an inflection point not only in the history of my nation, but an inflection point in the whole of our civilization.

The threats we face today are every bit as real as they were on the dramatic stage of antiquity.

National interests did not vanish in the face of international institutions. War did not disappear simply because we preferred peace. Other states continued to arm, to seek influence, to compete for territory, and technology, and resources, and markets, and energy, and power.

And now, there is war again. There is new competition between great powers again. There is vulnerability, aggression, terrorism, a whole universe of new threats and attacks again.

And so we must rebuild our institutions and our alliances to face these threats together – understanding that the purpose of these things is not to abolish the sovereignty of the nations that constitute them; it is to defend them. And that nations need not abandon their distinct identities in order to recognize their common interests.

We have built a model of that with our partners here in Greece. In our defense partnerships, in energy and technology, in our shared ambition to secure Europe’s borders from the threats of mass migration.

Our friendship dates back to the earliest years of my nation. When Greece rose in 1821 to recover its independence after centuries of Ottoman rule, Americans recognized something familiar in that struggle. Three years later, the great American statesman Daniel Webster, he delivered a famous address to Congress, helping bring the cause of the Greek Revolution before the representatives of the young American republic.

And he began by calling their attention to everything around them. This is what he said in his speech; he said: “This free form of government, this popular assembly… this practice of free debate, and public discussion, the contest of mind with mind… even the edifice in which we assemble, these proportioned columns, this ornamented architecture, all remind us that Greece has existed, and that we, like the rest of mankind, are greatly her debtors.”

Those words are as true today as they were when he said them. And all of us – not just Americans, but Europeans and our friends across the West – must relearn the lessons our forefathers took from this place and from its history.

The history of Greece – the history of Greece does not just offer us a glimpse – it does not offer a glimpse of our institutions in their earliest forms. The history of Greece shows us an image of ourselves.

It shows us that ours is the inheritance of great heroes, and that we should be proud – that we should be intensely proud – of where we come from. We should marvel at what our forefathers carved out of this countryside. The story of our civilization is the greatest story ever known to man. And it began here, with the first men and women of the West. From them – from them – we can rediscover the virtues, the courage, and the strength to confront the dangers that we face in our time.

Thank you.

(Applause.)
