Top Air Force and Space Force leaders, joined by their spouses, offered observations during a panel at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference into the lives of military families and how that dynamic contributes to readiness and defense of the nation.
The discussion included Chief of Staff of the Air Force Gen. Ken Wilsbach and his wife, Cindy; Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess and his wife, Debbie; Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David Wolfe and his wife, Dr. Doniel Wolfe; and Chief Master Sergeant of the Space Force John Bentivegna and his wife, Cathy. Retired U.S. Air Force Lt. Gen. Burt Field, president and CEO of the Air and Space Forces Association, moderated the panel at the association’s conference on Sept. 16.
The panelists underscored a central theme: “Readiness begins at home.” They agreed that strong families build strong units and a stronger national defense.
Evolving Perspectives on Leadership
Wilsbach explained how his view of leadership has changed over his 41-year career and 26 moves with his spouse. “When you start out earlier in your career, you’re very focused on the mission,” he said. “As I’ve gained rank and responsibility the people piece really expands.”
Mrs. Wilsbach shared a memorable example from their time at Kadena Air Base in 2009. While meeting with deployed spouses, she noticed one woman who answered she was “fine” when asked by her husband but clearly was not.
“After watching the interaction, I knew she wasn’t fine, so I stepped back and said, ‘Is everything okay?’, and it wasn’t okay. She had a child with a health problem and was far away from family,” she recounted. “That shows me the value of what I bring to this table. I sometimes see things, and I’m told things that he’s not.”
“All our family members are part of a team. When John gets deployed, that's his away game and he's busy taking care of his away-game family,” Mrs. Bentivegna said. “But the other teammates are still at home with roles to play. We still have our own goals, and in order to keep a successful team, we have to have good communication. We have to understand the mission, what's going on, and keep everyone, especially our kids, involved to feel part of the team."
Dr. Wolfe highlighted the power of simple kindness, quoting a lesson she learned: “If you treat everybody you meet as if they are going through some big trouble in their life, more than half the time you’ll be right.” She encouraged everyone to make saying “hello” a regular practice.
Family Stability Equals Warfighter Readiness
The panelists stressed that families directly impact the ability of Airmen and Guardians to focus on the mission. Gen. Schiess noted the unique challenges for a large portion of Space Force personnel who are employed in place.
"I learned early on that if I understand 'the why,' then I can invest more and I can support better as a spouse,” Mrs. Schiess said. “And so, taking the time to fill me in, even if he can't give me the details, to say, 'there's something big going on at work and stress levels are high.' Those kind of pieces of information help me to better support him, and I encourage other military members to do the same."
The spouses and their counterparts in the other services are members of the Military Spouse Commission, which President Donald Trump established to advise and assist the president on policies that affect military spouses and families.
Panelists discussed multiple programs aimed at supporting military families, notably the Global Military Spouse Connection, STARBASE, and the AFPASS Card Initiative.
Global Military Spouse Connection
The Global Military Spouse Connection is a pilot initiative designed to strengthen connections between qualified Department of the Air Force spouses and federal employment opportunities. It is being tested at the following installations across the world:
- Luke Air Force Base, Glendale, Arizona
- Goodfellow AFB, San Angelo, Texas
- Laughlin AFB, Del Rio, Texas
- Mountain Home AFB. Mountain Home, Idaho
- Travis AFB, Fairfield, California
- Patrick Space Force Base, Satellite Beach, Florida
- Ramstein AB, Ramstein-Miesenbach
- RAF Croughton, United Kingdom
- RAF Mildenhall, U.K.
- RAF Lakenheath, U.K.
- RAF Feltwell, U.K.
- Kadena AB, Okinawa, Japan
The program is designed to target military spouse unemployment, which currently has rates around 20%, largely due to frequent permanent change of station moves. GMSC aims to improve career continuity by connecting qualified spouses with DAF civilian employment opportunities before they arrive at their new duty station.
“It is a good start,” said CMSAF Wolfe. “With the four spouses here being involved in the [Presidential] Military Spouse Commission, we have an opportunity to make some real change to laws that currently prevent us from hiring people fast enough and putting people in positions and jobs.”
STARBASE and STEM Support for Military Children
Another family-oriented program mentioned during the panel was STARBASE, a Department of War STEM education program that delivers hands-on, immersive experiences primarily to fifth grade students from military-connected, at-risk and underserved communities. The program seeks to spark interest and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and future defense professionals.
“Our kids have to live with the decisions of their parents, and I think we owe them the best we possibly can provide,” said CMSAF Wolfe. He stressed the importance of the Air Force investing in educational opportunities for military children, using Starbase as a positive example. The program exposes military youth to the technological environments and positive civilian and military roles found on active, Guard, and Reserve military bases and installations.
AFPAAS Card for Spouse Roster
Each spouse discussed the challenge in spouse outreach, especially during times when connecting with family is most essential such as deployments and crises.
One solution mentioned was an Air Force Personnel Accountability and Assessment System Card, which provides unit leaders with instructional pocket cards and guidance for accessing current personnel and family contact information through the AFPAAS, maintaining accurate recall rosters and securely sharing appropriate roster data with key support liaisons.
Improving access to timely contact information, the initiative supports faster outreach to newly arriving spouses and families of deployed Airmen and Guardians, strengthens assistance during permanent change of station moves, deployments, exercises and emergencies and closes gaps in family-support communication. Participation respects privacy, as spouses may opt out of routine contact, while enabling stronger grassroots support networks and unit resilience.
Advice to the Next Generation
Panelists were asked what advice they would give to young Airmen, Guardians, and their spouses who are just beginning their military journey:
- Take every opportunity to grow professionally and personally
- Build and nurture strong relationships
- Recognize that military service is a family service to the nation
- Prioritize physical fitness, financial responsibility and emotional resilience
- Understand the “why” behind the mission to support one another more effectively
- Never underestimate the power of simple human connection
"You have to really embrace the preciousness of time because you can't get it back,” said CMSSF Bentivegna. “We're always focusing on that next assignment, next rotation, or the next deployment. You think, 'I've got plenty of time to focus on my finances, education, family, relationships … but you can't get that time back. Make the most of it."
title: DAF leaders, their spouses highlight families’ role in mission success

Rep. Sykes Announces $493,000 for TRIO Programs at the University of Akron
AKRON, OHIO — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced the Department of Education has awarded the University of Akron $493,314 as part of the TRIO talent search program. This grant will be awarded annually for five years, beginning in 2026, and is expected to serve nearly 900 students each year.
“Programs like TRIO provide deserving students with the opportunity to pursue higher education,” said Rep. Sykes. “I congratulate the University of Akron for supporting first generation college students participating in the TRIO program who will go on to make a meaningful impact in our community. I am a proud supporter of TRIO and other programs that help our families in Ohio’s 13th Congressional District reach higher heights.”
“The University of Akron Educational Talent Search Program is honored to continue this important work for another five years.” said Dr. Fedearia Nicholson, Vice Provost for Student Pathways and Dean of the Williams Honors College. “This investment from the U.S. Department of Education will create meaningful opportunities for Akron and Summit County students to prepare for college, careers, and the workforce. We are grateful to Congresswoman Emilia Sykes, Provost Gwen Price, Dr. Sandie Crawford and Akron Public Schools for their leadership, partnership, and continued support. I also want to recognize and thank our dedicated ETS team, Meiyah Hill, Amber Lambing, Shananne Lewis, and Roy Rosario, whose commitment to our students and families makes this work possible. Together, we are investing in the future of our students and our community.”
The TRIO Program is mandated by Congress and helps students from disadvantaged families receive the support they need to send their children to college. Two-thirds of TRIO students must come from families with combined incomes of no greater than 150% of the federal poverty line, and the student’s parents cannot have attended college. Schools that offer TRIO programs give students tutoring, counseling, financial guidance, and other forms of assistance.
title: Rep. Sykes Announces $493,000 for TRIO Programs at the University of Akron

The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) announced today a $1.5 billion conditional loan commitment to Wolfspeed, Inc., a vertically integrated U.S. manufacturer of silicon carbide (SiC) wafers, SiC power devices, and gallium nitride (GaN)-on-SiC wafers. The proposed loan, combined with private capital, would help strengthen the U.S. supply chain for wide bandgap materials and power devices, which have critical military and commercial applications.
The contemplated financing builds on President Trump's mandate to accelerate the onshoring of semiconductor production and bolster the associated supply chain. SiC and GaN are advanced wide bandgap semiconductor materials used in next-generation power and radio frequency applications across defense, Super Intelligence (SI), critical infrastructure, and other strategically important areas.
"Securing U.S. military and economic superiority requires bold domestic investments in critical dual-use capabilities. By strengthening our nation's wide bandgap industrial base, the contemplated transaction would achieve important national security objectives while advancing U.S. supremacy in the SI era," said Peter B. Zuckerman, Senior Managing Director at OSC.
"OSC's proposed transaction directly aligns with President Donald J. Trump's strategy to enhance domestic semiconductor manufacturing by supporting the development and production of wide bandgap capabilities in the United States," said David A. Lorch, Director of the Office of Strategic Capital and Senior Advisor to Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg. "The contemplated investment advances U.S. military and economic security by helping build a secure, reliable domestic supply chain for SiC and GaN that benefits the Department of War, the U.S. defense industrial base, and the broader U.S. economy."
With this proposed strategic financing, OSC would help the company strengthen domestic access to wide bandgap materials and devices used in high-performance propulsion systems, directed energy weapons, drones, electronic warfare systems, radars, and missile defense systems. The financing would also help advance U.S. economic security as SiC and GaN are expected to play an increasingly important role in the SI revolution.
"The Office of Strategic Capital is advancing President Trump's priority of supporting the domestic semiconductor supply chain to achieve American dominance in the era of Super Intelligence," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
The conditional loan commitment specifies additional steps Wolfspeed must complete before financial close, including satisfying various financial, legal, technical, investment, and due diligence requirements.
title: Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital Announces $1.5 Billion Conditional Loan Commitment to Wolfspeed, Inc.

U.S. Navy and AUKUS Partners Launch Landmark Maritime Big Play Pacific Demonstration
07 October 2026
SAN DIEGO — The U.S. Navy, alongside international military and research partners from Australia and the United Kingdom, recently initiated active testing for the AUKUS Pillar II Maritime Big Play Pacific (MBP-P) demonstration in the Southern California (SOCAL) operating area.
Sponsored by the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, Critical Technologies (OUSW(R&E) CT) and hosted by Naval Information Warfare Center (NIWC) Pacific, U.S. Pacific Fleet as well as the U.S. Marine Corps, this experimentation event is expected to achieve milestones in integrating mature robotics and autonomous systems within AUKUS coalition maritime operations. Running from October 05 - 25, 2026, the event will showcase more than 40 government and industry technologies from across all three partner nations, including multi-domain autonomous, crewed, and uncrewed systems (UxS).
The MBP-P demonstration builds off three years of intensive trilateral collaboration, advancing common command and control solutions for generating overwhelming combat mass, as well as delivering secure ‘stratosphere to seabed’ communications that enable AUKUS to act in coordination across the entire maritime domain. The event will feature live-fire operational vignettes focused on increasing mission effect and delivering force multipliers during strike operations, contested resupply, and undersea warfare.
"This demonstration represents a significant step forward as partners to integrate and fight together in future conflicts,” said Gerry Tighe, U.S. Lead for AUKUS Maritime Big Play. "This effort strives for seamless integration of autonomous systems with our conventional maritime fleet, and further as part of a greater combined partner force.”
“We’ve brought together cutting-edge systems from across our shared industrial base, put those solutions into the hands of AUKUS Warfighters so they can train together, and removed the technical barriers for integrating those advanced capabilities into no-kidding operations,” he said. “Maritime Big Play underscores the shared commitment of Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States to maintaining security, stability, and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific region."
title: U.S. Navy and AUKUS Partners Launch Landmark Maritime Big Play Pacific Demonstration

text:
Florida Laboratory Vice President and Marketer Convicted of Medicare Fraud for COVID-19 Testing Scheme
Yesterday, a federal jury in the Southern District of Florida convicted a Florida man who was the Vice President of a testing laboratory and owned and operated a separate marketing company for his role in a fraud scheme that took advantage of patients who wanted COVID-19 tests during the pandemic and were instead given additional blood tests they did not want or need, for which Medicare was billed for over $15 million.
“The defendant took advantage of patients desperate for COVID-19 tests at the height of the pandemic to bill Medicare for unnecessary blood tests,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “Such egregious conduct in the face of a global pandemic cannot stand and will be prosecuted. The Fraud Division remains committed to holding the perpetrators of such schemes accountable.”
“This case highlights a troubling scheme that took advantage of vulnerable patients who sought COVID‑19 testing during a national public health crisis, only to be subjected to additional and unnecessary blood tests intended to increase profits,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “By placing personal gain above the well‑being of elderly individuals, the defendant violated their trust and threatened the integrity of our health care system. HHS‑OIG remains steadfast in its mission to protect public health and ensure that individuals who abuse federal health care programs and the people they serve are held fully accountable.”
“This guilty verdict holds Joseph Rodriguez accountable for his role in a scheme that exploited patients and fraudulently billed Medicare for millions of dollars," said FBI Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles. “The jury’s verdict reflects the strength of the evidence and underscores that those who seek to profit through fraudulent schemes will be held accountable. The FBI and our law enforcement partners remain committed to protecting patients, safeguarding taxpayer dollars, and pursuing those who defraud federal health care programs.”
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Joseph Rodriguez, 58, of Coral Springs, perpetrated a scheme that exploited elderly patients at residence country clubs in the West Palm Beach area who were desperate for COVID-19 nasal swab and blood antibody tests. When those patients signed up to receive just swab and antibody tests at drive-through testing events at their residence clubs organized by Rodriguez through his marketing company, Phoenix Health, they were, in addition to the COVID-19 tests they wanted, subjected to tens or even hundreds of unnecessary blood tests that they did not want or need, and that no doctor ordered as required. These tests, which ranged from hormone tests to heavy metal tests for arsenic, mercury, and cadmium, were then billed to Medicare as if they were medically necessary and ordered by a treating physician.
Rodriguez marketed these drive-through COVID-19 events to the residence country clubs, set up the testing events, directed his staff to draw extra blood for the unnecessary tests, and caused a doctor’s name to be fraudulently listed on the claims submitted to Medicare. As a result of these claims — for tests conducted at nine different clubs over approximately four months involving almost two thousand patients — Medicare was billed more than $15 million and paid over $500,000. Evidence at trial included patient complaints sent to Rodriguez, complaints from one of the doctors who supposedly ordered such tests wondering why Medicare had been billed thousands of dollars for blood tests in the doctor’s name, and managers from the residence country clubs asking Rodriguez why these extra blood tests were being done on their club members when all they wanted were COVID-19 tests.
Image of one of the COVID-19 testing events managed and advertised by the defendant to the residence country club managers.
The jury convicted Rodriguez of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and six substantive counts of health care fraud. Rodriguez faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for each count. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled by the Court at a later date in January 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
FBI and HHS-OIG are investigated the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief James V. Hayes and Trial Attorney Claire Horrell of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
title: Florida Laboratory Vice President and Marketer Convicted of Medicare Fraud for COVID-19 Testing Scheme

190 Members of Congress Slam HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start
WASHINGTON –One hundred ninety Members of Congress demanded that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.
In the House, the letter is led by Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08), Early Childhood and Elementary and Secondary Education Subcommittee Ranking Member Bonamici (D-OR-01), and Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13). In the Senate, the letter is led by Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Sanders (I-VT), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA), and Senator Ben RayLuján (D-NM).
The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.
“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”
Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely. These actions serve the Trump Administration’s goal to end the Head Start program as laid out on page 482 of Project 2025.

text:
WASHINGTON — The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced a proposed rule that, if finalized, would implement new fees for F-1 nonimmigrant students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), a temporary employment authorization connected to a student’s field of study, in order to reduce the flow of cheap labor into the United States and make it easier for American citizens to compete in the job market.
The proposed rule would establish a $70,000 fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for initial OPT and a $30,000 fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for any subsequent OPT. DHS is proposing the fees to combat fraud and abuse, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect U.S. workers.
“Optional Practical Training was never meant to be a back door into the American workforce, a subsidy for cheap labor, or a prize for those who game the system,” said a DHS Spokesperson. “DHS is upskilling OPT to require foreign students to justify their worth to employers. American workers should not have to compete against a program that has been turned into a pipeline for cheap foreign labor.”
Existing federal regulations allow eligible F-1 nonimmigrant students to engage in OPT if the OPT is directly related to the student’s major area of study. To participate, F-1 nonimmigrant students must receive a recommendation from their designated school official (DSO) and apply for employment authorization with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).
F-1 nonimmigrant students may apply for OPT during their academic program (pre-completion OPT) or after completing their program (post-completion OPT). Eligible F-1 nonimmigrant students may receive up to 12 months of OPT at each education level. Those who earn degrees in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics fields may be eligible for an additional 24-month extension.
DHS is proposing the rule in response to fraud and abuse identified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP). As more F-1 nonimmigrant students have participated in OPT, SEVP has encountered schools, designated school officials, employers, and F-1 nonimmigrant students engaged in schemes to exploit current regulations, including problematic worksites and “pay-to-stay” visa schemes.
DHS believes the proposed fees would encourage schools to exercise greater oversight and selectivity when recommending F-1 nonimmigrant students for OPT, helping reduce fraud and strengthen program integrity.
The proposed rule also aligns with recent executive orders and other presidential directives emphasizing the protection of U.S. workers and the integrity of employment-based immigration programs. The increased fees would support program oversight and help ensure schools, F-1 nonimmigrant students, and employers use OPT consistent with its intended purpose and applicable regulatory requirements.
Under the proposed rule, SEVP-certified schools must pay the fee before designated school officials recommend F-1 nonimmigrant students for OPT in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) and before F-1 nonimmigrant students apply for employment authorization with USCIS. USCIS would not grant employment authorization to F-1 nonimmigrant students if schools have not paid the required fee.
The proposed fee would not be tied to a specific employer. Instead, it would apply when schools recommend an F-1 nonimmigrant student for any type of OPT. Collected fees would be deposited in the Treasury of the United States.
DHS will accept public comments on the proposed rule from October 8 through November 9. Additionally, the Paperwork Reduction Act section of the rule will have a 60-day public comment period. Members of the public should refer to the Federal Register notice for instructions on how to submit comments for DHS consideration. After the public comment period closes, DHS will review all properly submitted comments and materials and may revise the rule based on public feedback.
SEVP will provide additional communications about the proposed rule through its communications channels, including SEVIS Broadcast Messages, Study in the States, and field representatives.
For more information, refer to the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) in the Federal Register, the Practical Training page on ICE.gov/SEVP, and the Training Opportunities in the United States page on Study in the States.

title: DHS Proposes Fees for Foreign Student Work Program to Protect American Jobs

text:
Crow Introduces Bill to Extend Temporary Protected Status for Ukrainians
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and House Armed Services Committee, introduced legislation that will protect Ukrainian nationals already in the U.S. against the threat of deportation by extending their Temporary Protected Status (TPS).
Crow’s bill provides certainty and stability for Ukrainians currently in the U.S. by extending TPS for this group through June 2029. TPS for Ukrainian nationals is currently set to expire on October 19, 2026, despite continued threats facing the country from Russian aggression. Passing Crow’s legislation would ensure that temporary protections for Ukrainian nationals are codified into law past October and not solely up to the whims of any President.
TPS allows foreign nationals who cannot return home due to violence, conflict, and instability to live and work in the U.S. Under TPS, individuals are rigorously and continuously vetted before and after they receive this status.
Crow introduced the bill alongside Congressmen Bill Keating (D-MA) and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA). It was introduced in the Senate by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Chris Coons (D-DE), and Bill Cassidy (R-LA).
“Russia continues its illegal and unprovoked attacks on Ukraine. Vladimir Putin is attacking Ukrainian schools, homes, hospitals, and energy infrastructure across the country with drones, ballistic missiles, and aerial bombs. Millions of Ukrainian women, children, and refugees have fled the violence fearing for their lives. America must continue to stand with the people of Ukraine,” said Congressman Crow.
Congressman Crow has been a strong supporter of the Ukrainian people. In December 2021, just before Russia’s full-scale invasion, Congressman Crow led a delegation to Kyiv to reaffirm America’s commitment to Ukraine. When the invasion began, he immediately called for the U.S. to send military and humanitarian support to Ukraine, for international sanctions against Russia, and for a stronger NATO alliance to meet these new security threats. Weeks later, as Ukrainians fled their homes, Congressman Crow and other members advocated for an expedited immigration status for Ukrainians to the U.S. Crow has visited Ukraine several times since Russia’s invasion. The Congressman has been one of the earliest and strongest supporters of military, development, and humanitarian assistance for Ukraine. He voted for, and strongly advocated for, every supplemental package provided to Ukraine.
Full text of the bill is available here.
###
title: Crow Introduces Bill to Extend Temporary Protected Status for Ukrainians

Ranking Member Khanna Joined by Democratic Lawmakers to Raise Alarm Over DOE Cancellation of Transmission Corridors, Warns Decision Could Undermine U.S. Manufacturing and Competitiveness with China
WASHINGTON – Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, joined Rep. André Carson (D-IN), Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA), Rep. Paul Tonko (D-NY), and Rep. Mike Levin (D-CA), to raise serious concerns about the Department of Energy’s decision to abandon three proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors (NIETCs), warning that the move could undermine U.S. manufacturing, increase electricity costs for American families, and weaken the nation’s ability to compete with China.
In a [democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/2026.10.06-letter-to-doe-on-nietc-cancellations.pdf]letter to Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Tuesday, the lawmakers questioned the Department’s August 12 decision not to move forward with the Lake Erie-Canada Corridor, Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and Tribal Energy Access Corridor. He also pressed the Department to explain how it plans to address the nation’s urgent transmission needs and accelerate permitting for critical grid infrastructure.
The letter comes as the Department’s own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study found a “pressing need” for additional transmission infrastructure driven in part by expanding domestic manufacturing, large industrial loads, data centers, and a growing economy.
“Arbitrary cancellations like these set back the U.S. in the strategic race with the CCP, hamstring a U.S. manufacturing buildout, and drive up costs for American families,” the lawmakers wrote.
The Members further raised concerns about the impact of inadequate transmission capacity on American consumers. As electricity rates continue to rise, transmission constraints are driving up wholesale power costs and limit the ability of regions to bring new generation online, putting additional pressure on families and businesses already struggling with higher energy bills, the lawmakers wrote.
The Members are calling on Secretary Wright to provide detailed answers to the following by October 26, 2026:
- Please provide a detailed account of any analysis conducted by the Department of the opportunity cost of cancelling the Lake Erie–Canada Corridor, the Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and the Tribal Energy Access Corridor, including projected effects on ratepayer costs, grid reliability, and industrial electricity supply in the affected regions.
- Did the Department assess the impact of these cancellations on potential manufacturing and energy-intensive development in the regions associated with these cancelled corridors? Please provide a detailed account of that analysis.
- How does the Department reconcile these cancellations with the findings of its own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study?
- What stakeholder feedback did the Department evaluate when deciding to cancel these NIETC designations and did the Department engage with utilities, regional transmission organizations, or the North American Electric Reliability Corporation?
- What steps, if any, will the Department take to address the transmission needs in these three corridors, or in other transmission constrained areas across the country (especially those identified in the 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study)?
Read the full letter to Energy Secretary Wright HERE.
###
title: Ranking Member Khanna Joined by Democratic Lawmakers to Raise Alarm Over DOE Cancellation of Transmission Corridors, Warns Decision Could Undermine U.S. Manufacturing and Competitiveness with China

text:
Kamlager-Dove, Meeks Push State Department for Answers on Brazil
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Co-Chair of the Congressional Brazil Caucus, and Gregory W. Meeks (NY-05), Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, led 10 Members of Congress in demanding answers from the State Department about its decision to revoke Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti’s diplomatic visa.
In their letter, the lawmakers condemned the decision as an unnecessary escalation that threatens U.S.-Brazil relations and undermines American interests in the Western Hemisphere. They emphasized Brazil’s importance as a major democracy and regional security and trading partner.
“This unnecessary escalation is the latest of a series of actions that has driven a rupture in our relationship with the largest democracy and economy in South America. At a time when the Trump Administration claims to be prioritizing the Western Hemisphere, this misguided decision further damages America’s reputation in the region and pushes Brazil closer to the hands of our adversaries,” wrote the lawmakers.
The lawmakers also criticized what they described as the Trump Administration’s sustained effort to influence Brazil’s 2026 elections. They cited State Department officials’ meetings with former President Bolsonaro, sanctions against Supreme Court Justice de Moraes, and statements questioning the integrity of Brazil’s elections as actions threatening the country’s democratic institutions and electoral processes.
“Congress therefore has an obligation to understand why the Department of State departed from established practices and took the extraordinary step to revoke the Brazilian Ambassador’s visa,” concluded the lawmakers.  
The letter can be viewed in full here. 
In addition to Reps. Kamlager-Dove and Ranking Member Meeks, the letter was signed by James P. McGovern, Pramila Jayapal, Nydia M. Velázquez, Jonathan L. Jackson, Sylvia R. Garcia, Dina Titus, Yvette D. Clarke, Mike Quigley, Jasmine Crockett, and Madeleine Dean.

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

October 7, 2026

Today, the Department of State is publicly designating Zhao Fugang, the Director of the Overseas Chinese Service Center located in Fiji, for his involvement in significant corruption on behalf of China-based actors. This action renders Zhao and his immediate family members generally ineligible for entry into the United States.

Zhao abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance China-based government, business, and criminal interests. His actions constituted significant corruption and adversely affected U.S. interests in Fiji.

The United States will hold accountable those who abuse power for personal gain, and continue to fight corruption that fuels drug trafficking, enables transnational criminal organizations, and threatens U.S. interests around the world.

These public designations are made under the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (Div. F, P.L. 119-75)(“Section 7031(c)”). Section 7031(c) requires the Secretary of State to publicly or privately designate foreign officials and their immediate family members about whom the Secretary has credible information of involvement in significant corruption or a gross violation of human rights.

Maryland Delegation Members Push for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives April McClain Delaney, Steny Hoyer, Sarah Elfreth, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Glenn Ivey, and Johnny Olszewski were joined by Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) in requesting $11 million for U.S. Cyber Command as Congress works to complete the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense appropriations. In the letter to Appropriations Committee leadership, the lawmakers stressed the importance of the health and wellbeing of the service members and civilian employees of U.S. Cyber Command, as well as the importance of their work to our national security. The $11 million program increase would fund U.S. Cyber Command’s high-performance team training, an operation aimed at improving care for service members, including helping commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, care, and resilience practices.
The lawmakers begin, “We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent military operations missions.”
“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” they continue.
On the need for funding for High Performance Team Training at Cyber Command, the lawmakers note, “The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.”
“Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families,” the lawmakers conclude.
The full text of the letter is available here and below.
Dear Chairman Cole, Ranking Member DeLauro, Chair Collins, and Vice Chair Murray:
We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions.
As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear.
Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively “deployed in place” for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.
These challenges are particularly relevant at Fort Meade, where U.S. Cyber Command, the National Security Agency, military cyber components, and other national security organizations operate within a highly secure and interconnected environment. Although Maryland has a significant network of military, federal, and civilian health resources, traditional centralized-care models do not always give cyber personnel timely access to appropriately cleared professionals in the facilities where they work.
Congress and the Department have already recognized this gap. Congress previously directed a review of the psychological and occupational demands placed on cyber operators, and the Department subsequently acknowledged that existing resources did not fully meet the needs of the U.S. Cyber Command. The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) also expanded mental health services intended to address the U.S. Cyber Command’s unique requirements by integrating behavioral health professionals with security clearances within cyber units. Nevertheless, dedicated support teams and embedded care have not been implemented consistently across the force.
The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.
This represents a modest investment compared with U.S. Cyber Command’s broader annual budget and the strategic value of its highly trained workforce. Recruiting, clearing, and developing cyber operators takes years. Losing experienced personnel harms Maryland families, disrupts operational teams, increases replacement and training costs, and reduces the Nation’s ability to defend critical systems and conduct cyber missions.
Accordingly, we respectfully request that the final Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act retain the following program increase:
12D CYBERSPACE OPERATIONS
High Performance Team Training ........................................ $11,000,000
Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again.
We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families.
title: Maryland Delegation Members Push for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade

Rep. Mike Levin Pushes Administration to Adopt Critical Reforms to Improve Access to SNAP Benefits for Veterans
Washington, D.C.—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) applauded a new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report outlining recommendations to improve veterans’ access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). In January 2024, Rep. Levin served as the Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity with Chair Derrick Van Orden (WI-03) and requested GAO to examine how states with reported high and low rates of food insecurity have targeted veterans in the state annual outreach plans. On October 1, 2026, GAO published the report, “Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Federal Actions Needed to Help Veterans Access Benefits,” which highlights the importance of conducting veteran-specific SNAP outreach to increase awareness and use of food resources.
According to a 2023 RAND report, more than one million veterans faced food insecurity each year from 2015 to 2020. Eligible veterans can use SNAP benefits to access healthy foods, but they’re less likely to participate than non-veterans. In the report, GAO reviewed states’ efforts to target SNAP outreach to veterans and work with veterans’ organizations to help connect veterans to the program. GAO also examined state and federal efforts to improve the type of SNAP outreach conducted to veterans. The report makes four recommendations for the Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to more effectively tackle veteran food insecurity.
“More than one million veterans face food insecurity in this country. That is one million too many. That is why, when I served as Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity, I asked GAO to investigate how states and the federal government can better help veterans get the support they need. I am encouraged by the report’s findings on successful state outreach efforts, but I am deeply troubled that USDA has still not updated its website to inform veterans about new requirements that could result in them losing their benefits,” said Rep. Levin. “One of the many reasons I opposed H.R. 1 was because it eliminated the work requirement exemption for veterans and created additional barriers to accessing food assistance. I am also concerned that, following staffing cuts in 2025, USDA has failed to fill critical positions that support coordination with the Department of Veterans Affairs on veteran hunger. That is unacceptable. USDA must take these findings seriously and act quickly to address the gaps identified by GAO. I plan to work with my colleagues to hold the Administration accountable for implementing GAO’s recommendations as quickly as possible and ensuring veterans can access the support they have earned.”
GAO made three recommendations to USDA and one to VA, including:
- The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure Food and Nutrition Administration’s (FNA) SNAP eligibility website includes up-to-date information about exceptions to the SNAP time limit.
- The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure FNA develops and disseminates additional SNAP outreach materials tailored to veterans, in collaboration with Veterans Health Administration (VHA).
- The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure a formal mechanism is in place to collaborate with VA on efforts to address veteran food insecurity. This could include reviewing the memorandum of agreement (MOA) and updating the agreement as needed.
- The Secretary of Veterans Affairs should ensure a formal mechanism is in place to collaborate with VA on efforts to address veteran food insecurity. This could include reviewing the MOA and updating the agreement as needed.
Rep. Levin will continue working with the relevant federal agencies to ensure they implement GAO’s recommendations and address reducing barriers for veterans seeking access to SNAP.
###
title: Rep. Mike Levin Pushes Administration to Adopt Critical Reforms to Improve Access to SNAP Benefits for Veterans

WASHINGTON — The Department of Veterans Affairs today launched a new pilot program at six VA facilities to help Veterans establish VA.gov accounts faster than ever before, which means speedier access to VA services, care and benefits.
VA has worked with technology and security company CLEAR to deploy CLEAR pods at six VA hospitals across the country. Veterans who want to create a new account on VA.gov can use these pods to sign up in a matter of minutes with the assistance of VA staff.
Starting today, this faster option for setting up a VA.gov account is available at VA medical centers in Atlanta; Brooklyn, New York; Orlando, Florida; Palo Alto, California; San Juan, Puerto Rico; and Washington, D.C. VA will consider expanding this system to other facilities pending the results of this pilot program.
CLEAR uses the same scanning technology used at airports and other secure locations to create an easier way to establish a VA.gov account for Veterans who may have mobility, connectivity or other challenges when they try to sign up at home. Here’s how it works:
- Veterans can visit any participating medical center with a valid, non-expired government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, state ID, or passport, along with a phone number and personal email address.
- VA staff will help Veterans quickly enter their information and have Veterans take a photo at the CLEAR pod, which sets up the account in a matter of minutes.
- Veterans can set up face ID or other recognition tools so they can use CLEAR to access their VA accounts at home in a matter of seconds.
This process for creating and signing into VA.gov accounts will make it easier for Veterans to take full advantage of their VA benefits online, including:
- Scheduling healthcare appointments both in VA and in the community and finding nearby facilities for community care.
- Reviewing after-visit summaries of their healthcare appointments.
- Sending and receiving secure messages with their healthcare providers.
- Refilling prescriptions.
- Applying for disability compensation.
- Submitting for routine benefits, like healthcare-related travel reimbursements.
- Checking the status of benefits applications, including disability compensation and burial/memorial benefits.
“Veterans want better customer service and convenience, and under President Trump, VA is delivering,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “This technology is another way we’re changing VA to put Veterans first and make it easier for those who have worn the uniform to get the care and benefits they’ve earned.”
Using CLEAR to gain secure access to VA.gov is free and optional. Veterans can continue using existing options if they prefer. Choosing not to log in to VA.gov with CLEAR will not affect Veterans’ ability to access VA benefits or services. Veterans’ personal health information stays with the VA. CLEAR does not receive or access it and does not sell biometric or sensitive personal data.
This new pilot program is one of several ways the Trump Administration is making VA work better for Veterans. since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
- Enrolled more than 290,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
- Opened 43 new VA healthcare facilities, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country.
- Completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in fiscal year 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024.
- Completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024.
- Offered Veterans more than 3.2 million appointments outside of normal operating hours, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.
title: VA launches pilot program to speed Veterans’ access to services, care, benefits

HUD Announces the Next Generation Housing Action Plan
Outlines modernization of HUD Code and opportunities for manufactured housing innovation
October 7, 2026
WASHINGTON - Following the successful Sixth Annual Innovative Housing Showcase, HUD unveiled its Next Generation Manufactured Housing Action Plan to communicate its plan to modernize and support updated codes and guidance to define the next fifty years of affordable, factory-built housing.
Fifty years after the creation of the Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards, commonly known as the HUD Code, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act removed the longstanding permanent chassis requirement. Now, HUD is paving the way for new designs and construction innovations for affordable, manufactured housing.
“For 50 years, the HUD Code has provided a national framework for safe, quality, affordable housing,” said Secretary Turner. “Now, HUD is building on that foundation to expand innovation in design and construction for the next generation of manufactured homes to unleash the American Dream for even more families.”
“Removing the permanent chassis requirement is more than a technical change,” said Joe Gormley, who oversees the Office of Housing and FHA. “It creates an opportunity to reconsider how manufactured homes are designed, transported, assembled, and regulated, so we can increase supply for first-time homebuyers.”
The Next Generation Manufactured Housing Action Plan outlines how HUD will:
- Update energy efficiency standards for manufactured homes.
- Remove barriers to build by addressing the design and construction of manufactured homes built without a permanent chassis.
- Maintain safety by addressing foundation, anchoring, and installation requirements for chassis-free homes.
- Create construction pathways to explore innovative housing types that work within the federal manufactured housing regulatory framework and that factories can realistically complete.
- Develop a performance-based code for larger-scale buildings to examine a federal construction and safety framework for larger factory-built residential structures.
- Develop resources for chassis-free construction to provide stakeholders with information on early projects, including design, transportation, foundations, installation, zoning, appraisal, lending, insurance, and market acceptance.
- Allow more manufacturers on board to increase housing supply by providing resources for existing modular and other off-site construction manufacturers who comply with the federal system.
The action plan preserves the core strengths of the federal manufactured housing system while welcoming the next generation of factory-built housing.

title: HUD Announces the Next Generation Housing Action Plan

CNO Strengthens Global Maritime Partnerships at 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium
VENICE, Italy – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle joined senior naval leaders from around the world at the 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium in Venice, Italy, Oct. 6-7, underscoring the importance of international partnerships, maritime security and innovation in addressing shared challenges at sea.
VENICE, Italy – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle joined senior naval leaders from around the world at the 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium in Venice, Italy, Oct. 6-7, underscoring the importance of international partnerships, maritime security and innovation in addressing shared challenges at sea.
Hosted by the Italian Navy, the symposium brought together the heads of nearly 80 navies from around the world, along with experts from industry, academia, science and technology, to examine how regional maritime challenges increasingly produce global consequences.
Caudle said the symposium provides an important forum for building the relationships needed to confront challenges that transcend national boundaries.
“For 30 years, this symposium has brought naval leaders together here at Venice’s historic Arsenal, a place with centuries of maritime history behind it,” said Caudle. “The challenges we face at sea don’t stop at national borders, and no nation, no matter how capable, can address them alone.”
The 2026 symposium, themed “From Regional Waters to Global Influence: generating effects across the midland seas of the world,” focused on the relationship between regional security challenges and the broader global maritime system. Discussions examined how events in strategically important seas, straits and waterways can affect international trade, economic security, freedom of navigation and global stability.
Caudle participated in the working session “Future Seas: Industrial Scale, Decisive Mass and Innovation, and Securing the Maritime Domain,” joining fellow maritime leaders from Australia, France, Great Britain and Italy to discuss how navies must adapt their forces, industrial capacity and approach to innovation to meet rapidly evolving threats.
The discussion highlighted the growing importance of unmanned systems, autonomy, resilient logistics, advanced manufacturing and closer cooperation between navies and their industrial and technological partners.
For the U.S. Navy, Caudle emphasized that capability and capacity depend not only on what a navy can field, but also on its ability to sustain operations alongside allies and partners around the world.
“We have to be able to pull into [ports] and get the same kit that I can get in the United States,” said Caudle. “We need these solutions to be staged all around the world. That’s how our navies get force multiplication.”
Caudle said achieving that level of interoperability requires relationships and cooperation to be established well before they are tested in a crisis.
“Relationships and cooperation has to begin long before a crisis, not during one,” Caudle said.
The symposium’s other working sessions explored global and regional geopolitical dynamics, maritime regional security, the role of navies in protecting sea-based flows, the changing strategic environment in the Arctic and the leadership skills required to prepare future maritime commanders and Sailors for increasingly complex operating environments.
The gathering comes as naval leaders confront security challenges that increasingly connect once-distinct geographic regions. Disruption or instability in one maritime chokepoint can rapidly affect shipping, supply chains and economies thousands of miles away, making cooperation among maritime nations increasingly important.
Caudle also stressed that responding to those challenges requires navies to make deliberate choices about readiness while maintaining the ability to regenerate forces as operational demands change.
“We can’t surge everywhere indefinitely, so we have to make big decisions on readiness, said Caudle. “You have to not only build and certify those forces, but you have to be able to regenerate them and do that in timing and tempo as the situation demands.”
Throughout the symposium, Caudle engaged with fellow heads of navy and maritime leaders to reinforce relationships and discuss opportunities for greater cooperation and interoperability.
He said future naval forces must also be flexible, sustainable and capable of combining traditional platforms with emerging technologies to generate greater combat power.
“Together, we have to be adaptable. We have to be tailorable. There’s got to be a high-low mix. It’s got to be sustainable in forward places and force multiplied through robotic and autonomous systems. That’s why I’m investing so hard to build my endurance in directed energy and containerized payloads,” said Caudle.
The Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium traces its history to 1996, when the Italian Navy established what was then known as the Regional Seapower Symposium as a forum for multinational naval dialogue and cooperation. It has since grown from delegations representing 23 countries at its first gathering to approximately 70 navies today.
Caudle also continues a longstanding tradition of U.S. Chiefs of Naval Operations participating in the Venice symposium.
Former CNO Adm. Michael Mullen attended in 2006, followed by Adm. Gary Roughead in 2008, Adm. Jonathan Greenert in 2012 and Adm. John Richardson in 2015. Adm. Mike Gilday participated in both the 2019 Regional Seapower Symposium and the 2022 Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium, and Adm. Lisa Franchetti attended the 14th T-RSS in 2024.
Caudle’s participation makes him the seventh U.S. Chief of Naval Operations to attend the symposium and marks the eighth CNO appearance at the forum since 2006.
The symposium has evolved alongside the maritime environment it was created to address, expanding beyond its original regional focus to examine the increasingly interconnected nature of global maritime security.
Three decades after the first gathering in Venice, Caudle said its fundamental purpose remains unchanged: bringing naval leaders together before they are called upon to confront a crisis together.
He said those relationships strengthen deterrence by giving navies the trust and familiarity necessary to operate effectively alongside one another.
“We train together, we exercise together, we operate together,” Caudle said. “And we build the trust that allows us to act together when it matters most.”
title: CNO Strengthens Global Maritime Partnerships at 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium

RELEASE: Gottheimer Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Flydubai Flight 1073 Heroes
Condemns Attempted Terrorist Attack
Resolution Honors Captain, Crew, Passengers Who Saved All Lives
Calls for a Full Investigation
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10), and Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2) introduced a bipartisan resolution honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on the flight.
“Captain Machchhar is a hero. While gravely wounded, he fought off a terrorist attack and saved every soul on that plane, including 27 children and four Americans,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Congress must honor his extraordinary courage, and we must be clear that this was an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international air travel. I’m proud to lead this resolution with Congressman McCaul and Congressman Bacon, and we wish Captain Machchhar and everyone injured a full recovery.”
“I’m proud to co-lead this resolution, which condemns the attempted terrorist attack, calls for a full investigation, and honors the brave crew and passengers. The world owes a debt of gratitude to these heroes — especially Captain Smit Machchhar, who sustained injuries fighting the attacker and still managed to unlock the cockpit door and allow others to land the plane,” said Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10). “Were it not for his extraordinary courage, this story could have ended in horrific tragedy. I wish Captain Machchhar, the crew, and all the passengers healing and strength as we await a comprehensive investigation into this harrowing incident.”
On September 30, Flight 1073 departed Dubai for Tel Aviv carrying approximately 174 passengers and six crew, including 4 U.S. citizens and 27 children. Midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain with the aircraft’s emergency crash axe and tried to seize the controls, sending the plane plunging more than 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Despite grave injuries, Captain Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and unlocked the cockpit door so off-duty pilots could enter and land the plane, and so crew and passengers could restrain the first officer. The aircraft landed safely in Saudi Arabia with everyone accounted for. On October 3, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the investigation had determined the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act.
The resolution:
- Honors Captain Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft;
- Commends the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down;
- Wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery;
- Condemns the attack as an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international civil aviation;
- Calls for a full and expeditious investigation by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.

U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), and House Natural Resources Committee top Democrat Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), led 30 of their colleagues in calling on House and Senate Armed Services Committee leaders to reject the Hunt Amendment’s provision (Section 2835) in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which would grant unprecedented eminent domain authority to the federal government to benefit Sable Offshore Corporation.
 “The NDAA has long served as a bipartisan vehicle to strengthen our national security and support our servicemembers. However, we are deeply concerned by the inclusion of Section 2835, which would grant extraordinary eminent domain authority to the federal government to circumvent established environmental protections for the benefit of a single private company. Given the sweeping implications of this provision, we believe this policy rider does not belong in the NDAA and, therefore, should be removed from the final conference agreement,” wrote the lawmakers. 
 The lawmakers explain how this provision would jeopardize the California coastal economy and do little to strengthen our nation’s energy security. 
“California’s coastal economy supports roughly 511,000 jobs and generates over $51.3 billion in GDP from marine-economy activities — largely in tourism and recreation. Another oil spill from a corrosion-prone pipeline that has spilled before would jeopardize the economic security of everyday Americans that rely on our coastal economy for their livelihoods,” the lawmakers continued. “In addition, there is no evidence that this provision would meaningfully advance our nation's energy security. Recent spikes in gasoline prices driven by market uncertainty surrounding the war in Iran underscore that global oil markets—not a single offshore project—continue to dictate prices at the pump.”
The letter goes on to highlight the unprecedented nature of Section 2835, which would grant the federal government extraordinary powers to seize property for the sole benefit of a single private organization. 
“The NDAA should not be used to circumvent established permitting processes or create special authorities for individual projects that have failed to secure the approvals required under existing law. The federal government's power of eminent domain is among its most significant authorities and should be exercised only when there is a clear and compelling public purpose—not to resolve private infrastructure disputes or increase the profitability of a single company—at the expense of communities who have to live with the consequences of an oil spill,” said the lawmakers. 
The full letter is available HERE.
Joining Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, and Huffman the letter is co-signed by U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (D-CA-43), Dave Min (D-CA-47), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Mike Thompson (D-CA-04), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA-11), John Garamendi (D-CA-08), Gil Cisneros (D-CA-31), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Derek Tran (D-CA-45), Mike Levin (D-CA-49), Juan Vargas (D-CA-52), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Laura Friedman (D-CA-30), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12), Kevin Mullin (D-CA-15), Mark Takano (D-CA-39), Ami Bera, M.D. (D-CA-06), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Scott Peters (D-CA-50), Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Pete Aguilar (D-CA-33), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37), George Whitesides (D-CA-27), Luz Rivas (D-CA-29), and Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51). 
Background
Sable Offshore acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024. The pipeline had been out of service since the 2015 Refugio oil spill. In March 2026, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the Defense Production Act and ordered Sable to restore pipeline operations. 
Carbajal has been a leader in opposing the Sable pipeline’s forced restart. 
In September 2026, Carbajal led a bicameral group of colleagues in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright to challenge the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along the California Central Coast. The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority.
In July 2026, Carbajal spoke on the House floor against the NDAA’s Hunt amendment, which would grant the federal government unprecedented access to California-owned public lands associated with the Santa Ynez Unit and Las Flores Pipeline System.
 In May 2026, Carbajal, Schiff, and members of the California congressional delegation launched an inquiry into Sable’s efforts to restart oil drilling off the California coast and demanded answers on the company’s collaboration with the Trump administration to invoke the DPA in relation to this project.
Last year, Carbajal, Schiff, Padilla, and members of the California congressional delegation demanded answers from the Trump administration on its involvement in Sable’s attempts to restart the pipeline.
title: Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, Huffman Lead Colleagues in Urging Removal of Hunt Amendment from Annual Defense Bill

Reps. Cisneros, Castro Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
WASHINGTON D.C. — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.
Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most-watched and financially successful productions.
El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.
“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”
“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country,” said Congressman Castro. “Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”
“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”
“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”
“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen,” said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. “Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”
“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”
“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”
Read the full text of the resolution here
Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.
###
title: Reps. Cisneros, Castro Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
