AIDS Healthcare Foundation Agrees to Pay $1.44M to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
AIDS Healthcare Foundation, a non-profit organization based in Los Angeles, California, has agreed to pay $1.44 million to resolve allegations that it violated the False Claims Act by submitting or failing to delete false or invalid diagnosis codes in order to increase payments that it received from the Medicare Advantage program.
“The government relies on Medicare Advantage participants to submit accurate, substantiated diagnosis codes that are adequately documented in a medical record to ensure proper payment,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The Justice Department will continue to protect the public fisc and hold accountable those who receive inflated payments by knowingly providing or failing to correct false information.”
“The integrity of our federal healthcare programs, including Medicare Advantage, must be preserved,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “We will not tolerate companies undermining the interests of Medicare patients for financial gain.”
“Medicare Advantage organizations have a responsibility to ensure the accuracy of diagnosis codes they submit for payment. When entities fail to correct information they know is wrong, they undermine the integrity of a program millions of seniors rely on,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS‑OIG). “HHS‑OIG will continue to safeguard taxpayer funds by holding organizations accountable when their failures inflate federal payments and compromise program trust.”
Under the Medicare Advantage (MA) Program, also known as Medicare Part C, Medicare beneficiaries may opt out of traditional Medicare and enroll in private health plans offered by insurance companies known as Medicare Advantage Organizations, or MAOs. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) pays the MAOs a fixed monthly amount for each Medicare beneficiary enrolled in their plans. CMS adjusts these monthly payments to account for various “risk” factors that affect expected health expenditures for the beneficiary. In general, CMS pays MAOs more for sicker beneficiaries expected to incur higher healthcare costs and less for healthier beneficiaries expected to incur lower costs. To calculate the payment amounts, CMS uses a health-based risk adjustment model — the Hierarchical Conditions Category (HCC) model — that takes into account diagnoses reported by healthcare providers. In general, the more severe the diagnosis or costly the associated treatment, the higher the risk score and the higher the corresponding payments to the MAO. Diagnosis codes submitted to CMS must be supported by the beneficiaries’ medical records and be accurate, complete, and truthful, based on the best knowledge, information, and belief of the MAO making the submission.
AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) provides care and services to HIV patients in the United States and other countries. AHF’s Managed Care Division (doing business as Positive Healthcare Partners) operated special needs MA plans for Medicare beneficiaries who have HIV and lived in Florida, Georgia, or California.
The settlement announced today resolves allegations that, for payment years 2017 to 2023, AHF failed to timely investigate and delete diagnosis codes that were either inaccurate or not documented in medical records. Beginning in around 2017, AHF’s risk adjustment coders conducted chart reviews to identify inaccurate or unsupported diagnosis codes for deletion. As part of this process, AHF’s risk adjustment coders maintained “Delete Research” spreadsheets, which listed diagnosis codes they identified as potentially lacking support in the medical record but needing further research. Although AHF knew that it was required to investigate and delete inaccurate and unsupported diagnosis codes within 60 days, AHF failed to timely investigate and delete the codes. AHF did not delete most of the inaccurate or unsupported diagnosis codes in the “Delete Research” spreadsheets until 2024 or 2025 — well after AHF was on notice that the codes potentially lacked support and only after being notified of the United States’ investigation.
The United States further alleges that, for payment year 2017, AHF knowingly submitted diagnosis codes for HIV (ICD-10 B20) where the diagnosis was not documented in any medical record for a face-to-face visit, in violation of CMS requirements that all diagnosis code submissions must be documented as a result of a face-to-face visit.
The civil settlement resolves claims brought under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act by Donna Irons, a former risk adjustment coder at AHF. Under the qui tam provisions, a private party can file an action on behalf of the United States and receive a portion of any recovery. The qui tam case is captioned United States ex rel. Irons v. AIDS Healthcare Foundation d/b/a Positive Healthcare Partners, Civil Action No. 23-cv-2160 (C.D. Cal.). Ms. Irons will receive $259,200 as her share of the federal recovery.
AHF received credit under the Department of Justice’s guidelines for taking disclosure, cooperation, and remediation into account in False Claims Act resolutions, Justice Manual § 4-4.112. In addition to cooperating in the government’s investigation and enhancing its compliance program, AHF proactively remediated its conduct during the course of Department’s investigation by submitting deletes for diagnosis codes that, based on review of medical records, were not supported.
The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the Justice Department’s Civil Division, Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California, with assistance from the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General.
The investigation and resolution of this matter illustrate the government’s emphasis on combating healthcare fraud. One of the most powerful tools in this effort is the False Claims Act. Tips and complaints from all sources about potential fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, can be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services at 800-HHS-TIPS (800-447-8477).
This year the Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the Administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect, and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s FCA enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. FCA matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s FCA work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
Trial Attorney Tiffany L. Ho of the Civil Division’s Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney S. Desmond Jui for the Central District of California handled this case.
The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.

Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) announced an award of $1.5 million in federal grants for the mansion and outbuildings of the fifth President of the United States, James Monroe. Oak Hill, located in Loudoun County, has been preserved for hundreds of years and provides the local community and visitors access to American history and educational programming. Earlier this year, the Virginia General Assembly approved Governor Spanberger’s budget amendment to designated Oak Hill as a State Park. That amendment was championed by Senator Russet Perry and Delegate John McAuliff.
“Oak Hill is an important part of our history and has survived hundreds of years. This funding will ensure it can continue to live on for generations. I am proud that federal funding will help maintain and preserve this historical landmark. I look forward to seeing people of all ages in our community and across the world visit Oak Hill for many years to come,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanayam.
“For more than two years, we fought in Richmond to make Oak Hill a state park and protect more than 1,200 acres of Loudoun County and President Monroe’s historic home. We got it done, and now the work is making sure Oak Hill has what it needs to thrive for the long term. This $1.5 million in federal funding will help us do that, and I’m grateful to Congressman Subramanyam for securing these resources and being a partner in Oak Hill’s future. I’m looking forward to continuing this work and getting Oak Hill State Park open to the public,” said Senator Russet Perry.
"Oak Hill will be an enormous investment in the quality of life and conservation of Western Loudoun by opening up over 1,200 acres of farm and forestland for recreational use. The new funding secured by Congressman Subramanyam and State budget language provided by Gov. Spanberger ensures this land and history will be treasured by generations to come," said Delegate John McAuliff.
“Oak Hill stands as a powerful reminder of our nation’s founding story, and these grants ensure that story will be preserved for generations to come. We’re grateful to Rep. Subramanyam and our federal partners at the National Park Service for recognizing what this site means – not just to Loudoun County, but to the story of our nation as we mark 250 years of independence,” said Heather Richards, Mid-Atlantic Vice President, The Conservation Fund.
Of the $1.5 million in grants for preservation and restoration, $750k from Save America’s Treasures and $750k from Semiquincentennial grants. View the NPS announcements of funding here and here.

title: Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill

HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.

ICYMI: OPM Director Kupor Discusses American Leadership in Super Intelligence on Fox Business
WASHINGTON, DC – US Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Director Scott Kupor joined Varney & Co. on Fox Business for his first television appearance since President Trump announced his appointment as Vice Chair of the White House Super Intelligence Task Force. Kupor discussed the President’s vision for maintaining American leadership in superintelligence, protecting national security, and holding industry accountable while advancing innovation.
On advancing President Trump’s vision for American leadership in super intelligence:
“We are going to do exactly what the President has talked about, which is we all recognize that leading in super intelligence is the most important economic issue, security issue, for the country. And the President has asked us to do that. At the same time, the President recognizes that, yes, there are risks. Like any new technology, there’s new things we have to figure out. We have to figure out the energy cost, water cost, utilities, all these other things, security, of course.”
On developing a comprehensive plan to advance innovation and address risks:
“So the main thing for the task force to do will be to come back to the President with a comprehensive plan that balances those two issues and make sure that we have the precondition that will allow the U.S. to continue to win, which we are and we will continue to do so. And also make sure that all the other players in the ecosystem recognize and understand how do we address and how do we appropriately handle issues that may arise in the course of this development in the technology.”
On independent oversight and accountability for industry commitments:
“So, this is not just a bunch of engineers sitting around and grading themselves. This is actually them going outside to a third-party auditor, that auditor reporting to an independent committee of the board. It actually has real legal teeth in a way that I think people who haven’t been on a public company board before, they don’t quite appreciate and understand. I think this was the genius of what the President was able to get these industry leaders to commit to, is something that truly does have teeth.”
On protecting American innovation while enforcing existing laws:
“One of the key members of the task force is Andrew Ferguson, the head of the FTC. There are lots of things, obviously, the FTC can do. The President has mentioned the DOJ has lots of existing rules and regulations. So, nobody is going to get a free pass here. The question, though, is do you want to make sure you don’t introduce a regulatory scheme that will slow down or impact the ability of the inventiveness of this country to win what is an incredibly important technology. And I think the President is trying to strike the right balance here.”
On touring the new White House ballroom with President Trump:
“The President did a great job. He literally told us down to the thickness of the glass and the strength of the steel there. It looks awesome. It’s going to be fantastic. It has been well reported and not only adds to the functionality of the White House but obviously creates an entirely robust security infrastructure that’s been long needed. So, it was a great tour. It’s very clear that the President is a builder.”

NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland is seeking Phase 1 proposals for the design and construction of the Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory. The principal purpose of this procurement is to deliver a laboratory facility to support the testing and development of power systems, with associated site work, infrastructure, and systems.

The laboratory will provide modern test facilities to advance power research and enable NASA to meet current and future mission needs. Glenn’s expertise in power is crucial to the Artemis program , the Moon Base , and the exploration of Mars and beyond.

Proposals submitted in response to this solicitation are due no later than Oct. 30, 2026, at 1 p.m. EST.

NASA will conduct this acquisition as a full and open competition. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, and the small business size standard of $45 million.

The anticipated contract award date is Dec. 16, 2026. The contract will be performed on-site at NASA Glenn and off-site at the contractor’s facilities.

Proposals for this solicitation are required to be submitted through NASA’s Enterprise File Sharing and Sync Box (EFSS Box), a FedRAMP Moderate certified platform.

All questions regarding this request should be submitted electronically, in writing, to John Christel, contracting officer, at john.a.christel@nasa.gov on or before Oct. 12, 2026. Offerors are encouraged to submit questions as soon as possible for consideration.

For more information about NASA and agency programs, visit:

https://www.nasa.gov

Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) announced that the Scio Rural Fire Protection District has received a $1.19 million federal grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency to support firefighter safety and fire prevention. Congresswoman Bynum advocated for the funding by writing a letter to FEMA in support of Scio Rural Fire’s grant application.
“When you call 911, you shouldn’t have to wonder if there are enough firefighters to answer,” said Rep. Bynum. “This $1.19 million is a big deal for Scio, Jefferson, and the communities they serve. It means more support for the people running toward emergencies and a stronger response when our neighbors need help most. This is exactly what bringing federal dollars home should look like.”
"These grants are a significant opportunity and an important first step in building the capacity our Fire & Life Safety Division needs," said Albany Fire Chief Chris LaBelle. "A community our size, with the growth and unique industries we have, requires a more proactive approach to risk reduction. This position moves us in that direction and supports our mission to Prevent and Protect from Harm."
"Redmond Fire & Rescue would like to thank Senators Merkley and Wyden and Congresswoman Bynum for their support,” said Redmond Fire Chief Ryan Herrera. "With members of our organization having navigated a past cancer diagnosis, and with the recent passing of Firefighter/Paramedic Michael Kienzle from a Line-of-Duty cancer, this funding marks another meaningful step forward in our commitment to carcinogen reduction and improving the long-term health and safety of our firefighters."
"As costs continue to rise faster than available revenue, small fire districts like ours face difficult choices about how to best use limited resources. Recruiting, training, and retaining volunteer firefighters can too often be delayed as we focus on meeting the immediate costs of providing emergency services,” said Scio Fire Chief Kevin White. "This grant is an important investment in the future of our department and our community. It will strengthen our efforts to recruit and retain volunteers, grow our membership, and ensure we have the people and resources needed to provide the high-quality emergency services our community depends on. We are grateful for this support and the opportunity to build a stronger, more sustainable fire department."
FEMA awarded the funding through its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant Program, which helps fire departments hire additional firefighters and strengthen recruitment and retention efforts.
FEMA also issued funding under the SAFER Grant Program to the following areas:
- More than $2.3 million to Boise Fire Department in Boise, Idaho
- More than $1.7 million to South Kitsap Fire and Rescue in Port Orchard, Washington.
- More than $1.7 million to Spokane County Fire District 9 in Mead, Washington.
- More than $1.1 million to Umatilla Rural Fire Protection District in Umatilla, Oregon.
- $1 million to North Whidbey Fire and Rescue in Oak Harbor, Washington.

title: Bynum Secures Over One Million for Scio Rural Fire

Rep. Gillen Announces More Than $500,000 in New Federal Funding for Nassau County Fire Departments
GARDEN CITY, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) announced that four fire departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District have been awarded more than $500,000 total in federal funding for improved equipment, training and recruitment. Three departments were awarded Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG), including the Inwood Fire Department for emergency vehicle acquisition as well as the Bellerose Terrace Fire Department and the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department for operations and safety. Stewart Manor Village received funding through the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant to help recruit and retain more volunteer firefighters.
“Firefighters across Long Island put their lives on the line every day to protect our families and communities. They should have the resources of a modern firefighting force,” said Rep. Gillen. “I’m proud to help secure more than $500,000 in federal funding for Nassau County fire departments to support critical equipment, vehicle and recruitment needs. I will continue working with our local fire departments to deliver federal dollars and ensure they have the tools and support they need to keep our communities safe.”
“The chiefs, officers and members of the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department thank Congresswoman Gillen very much,” said Chief Joseph McHugh, Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department. “This will help keep our members safe and take a big financial burden off of us.”
- The Inwood Fire Department received $220,476 through the AFG program to assist with the purchase of new vehicles for the department.
- The Stewart Manor Village Fire Department received $119,500 through the SAFER program to help recruit and retain trained volunteer firefighters.
- The Bellerose Terrace Fire District received $96,666 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.
- Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department received $72,857 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.
During the FY25 grant application process, Rep. Gillen urged all departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District to apply for funding through the AFG and SAFER programs and wrote letters of support. As a member of the bipartisan Congressional Fire Services Caucus, Rep. Gillen has also pushed for increased funding for the AFG and SAFER Programs to help ensure Long Island fire departments have the federal resources to improve emergency response and support their firefighters.
The AFG program, administered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), provides funding to local fire departments to help obtain needed equipment, protective gear, vehicles and training. The SAFER grant is a federal program administered by FEMA that provides direct funding to local fire departments and volunteer firefighter organizations to help increase or maintain the number of trained firefighters.

As part of its nationwide initiative to crack down on “Pass the Trash” practices, the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights (OCR) today opened investigations into various school districts based on allegations of staff-on-student sexual misconduct. OCR will determine whether the districts’ handling of alleged sexual harassment, including sexual assault, by district teachers, administrators, and other school personnel violated Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (Title IX).
OCR launched a directed investigation into the New York City Department of Education for its alleged systemic and disturbing pattern of enabling abuse in schools. According to reporting, nearly two thousand complaints filed under the state’s Child Victims Act accuse a school, educator, or staff member of sexual abuse. What is most chilling is that instead of protecting the students to ensure these incidents would never happen again, the schools allegedly allowed the accused to evade punishment and resign. Or, even worse, New York City allegedly let educators named in complaints remain in their job, even after a settlement.
Additionally, OCR is opening an investigation into Jefferson County Public Schools, which has faced intense scrutiny and parent-led protests regarding systematic staff misconduct, including at least four recent staff arrests for sexually assaulting students on campus.
OCR is opening additional investigations into school districts in California, Georgia, North Carolina, Missouri, Texas, and Virginia, alleging that the districts failed to respond as required to reports of staff-on-student sexual misconduct allegations. These investigations will examine reports across these districts that include allegations that a teacher touched the private parts of young elementary school girls in the classroom; a paraprofessional assigned to work with a student with a disability sexually harassed the student in question; a coach groped female student athletes; a staff member groomed a middle school student; and more unsettling accounts.
“Sexual misconduct in schools, especially by the adults entrusted with students’ care, is insidious. Schools have a duty to protect students from sexual harassment in schools and to respond appropriately when sexual misconduct occurs, especially when the predatory behavior is committed by school staff,” said Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kimberly Richey. “Parents and families should be able to send their kids to school without fear that they will be targeted by school staff. By opening these investigations, our message is clear: we will always protect our children so parents should never have to wonder if their kids are safe at school.”
Background
The Office for Civil Rights enforces Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex in education programs and activities receiving federal financial assistance. Title IX requires schools with knowledge of sexual harassment or sexual assault to respond promptly and in a manner that is not deliberatively indifferent.
The Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) also requires states and school districts receiving federal funds to maintain policies that prohibit school employees, contractors, agents, and educational agencies from assisting individuals believed to have engaged in sexual misconduct involving a student in obtaining new employment with another educational institution. These protections are intended to prevent the practice commonly known as “passing the trash.”
The U.S. Department of Education will vigorously enforce ESEA and Title IX to ensure schools fulfill their legal obligations, protect students from sexual misconduct, and provide every child with a safe learning environment. Institutions that fail to comply with federal law may face enforcement action, including the potential termination of federal financial assistance.
Anyone who believes that a school, school district, or state educational agency has failed to comply with ESEA or Title IX may file a complaint with OCR. Information about filing a complaint is available on OCR’s website.
title: U.S. Department of Education Launches Multiple Investigations Based on Reports of Staff-on-Student Sexual Misconduct

text:
Ambassador Mike Waltz
U.S. Representative to the United Nations
New York, New York
AS DELIVERED
Danny, thank you for your kind words. It’s so good to be with you all again.
I just had the opportunity to meet Eliya and Ziv just outside, and I want to start today with talking about you all. What you two endured is just—I think it’s completely unimaginable to any normal human being.
And Eliya, there is one part of your story—I hope I’m pronouncing your name right. My Hebrew’s not the best—but it’s one in your story that I haven’t able to get out of my head that the night before you were released after 505 days in captivity, chained, starved, tortured, believing that the love of his life, Ziv, had been murdered because that’s the psychological torture that the terrorists impose on people. The night before, Hamas tried to make him record one of their propaganda videos, saying all was well, he had been treated magnificently, that it was all fine. He refused. He held firm. He said no.
And the next day, as they were finally handing him over, Hamas tried to turn his release again into a propaganda moment. They put him on a stage, surrounded him with cameras, told him to raise his hands for the spectacle. He refused again.
Eliya, we salute you. I salute you. You are a proud, strong Jew. You’re undefeated. You stood strong, man, and I’m deeply—deeply admirable. And I admire you.
Ziv, when all that’s happening underground, you were living through your own nightmare. You survived the music festival, one of peace and hope and fun, underneath the bodies of people who had been murdered. You watched Eliya being taken away, not knowing whether you would ever see him again.
At 505 days, neither of you knew what had happened to the other, and thankfully, we now obviously know how it ends. Both were freed just a few weeks ago, as Danny just celebrated with you, that you both got married. And from what I hear about your wedding, it was beautiful, and you used it to celebrate new life and to honor those that can no longer celebrate life.
And there’s others—that I think their stories should be heard, and we should take these opportunities and these moments to tell their stories. Ziv’s nephew, Amit, who was murdered at the Nova Festival. And like Aner, who protected God knows how many innocents. Do you know how they protected them? By picking up and throwing Hamas’ hand grenades that they were throwing at a civilian crowd at a music festival. They picked them up and threw them back. Not once, not twice—seven times. I mean, that’s a medal of honor. That’s multiple in our system. Sadly, it was the eighth grenade that Hamas threw at these civilians that killed him.
Folks, I’ve had the honor over these last few years of getting to know many of these hostages and their desperate, desperate families, hearing many of these stories firsthand. The one thing that struck me as a veteran again and again is their extraordinary ability to kind of hold two things at once: to carry the memory of this immense loss, the suffering and pain, but at the same time moving forward and living such beautiful lives, building families, going back to work, telling your stories through art and through love and through peace.
I want to recognize Oriya Berlin, who’s also here today for her unbelievable courage. She finished her IDF training on October 5, a brand new recruit, just two days on the job, when Hamas attacked her base. She was wounded in combat. Obviously survived, but what I found so admirable: she didn’t go home, she didn’t rest, she didn’t stay in the hospital, she went back to her duty, she stood with her fellow brothers and sisters in arms. Thank you, Oriya, for your bravery, and I salute you too.
I have to commend someone else who you just saw, Alon Ohel. Alon didn’t just kind of magically arrive on the USS Nimitz. He was facilitated by and helped by my good friend Ambassador Jeff Bartos, who, as many of you know, and is here for us and a real fighter for the U.S.-Israel relationship.
Alon was taken from the same shelter as Eliya, and for much of their captivity, they were held together underground. To go from that to a year later, standing on the deck of the USS Nimitz, just as it returned on its last voyage from combat operations in the Middle East against the Iranian regime on America’s 250th in front of the Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor to sing that song with another great friend and fighter for the U.S.-Israel relationship, John Ondrasik of Five for Fighting, was a surreal and amazing, just an amazing experience.
Here is a young man who spent 738 days in Hamas captivity. He had been held underground, away from his family, away from daylight, away from his piano that he loved, been such a huge part of his life. To see him playing on that deck was just an absolute beautiful symbol of freedom, and it struck me then, like how much it changed in just a year.
A year ago, 48 hostages underground, including two Americans, held in those Hamas terror tunnels. Their families were still waiting, calling us, begging for something to change, they were fighting every day.
And now today, for the first October 7 commemoration since that terrible morning, every hostage out, the living are back with their families, those who were sadly murdered are home for a proper burial. Even Hadar Goldin and Oron Shaul, who have been held by those depraved terrorists since 2014, were out and back home, which no one said was possible.
President Trump thought it was possible, and he told his envoys, he told me, he told Secretary Rubio, he told Steve and Jared to never stop pushing until we got them home—and we did.
And I just can’t tell you how amazing it was. I can tell you this: firsthand from the moment we started transition in my previous role as National Security Advisor, from that first day, he was talking about these hostages. They were always top of mind for the President and his charge to all of us, I can tell you, he was like, “I don’t want to see you guys again until we get them home.”
But that wasn’t the end of the job. The President was determined, and is still determined, that we do not go back to that cycle of violence. That we don’t go back to that old cycle where Hamas rearms, Iran feeds its proxies with weapons and money, then we have another war, we have another attack, we have another generation of Israelis and Palestinians who pay the price.
Colleagues, October 7 can never ever happen again, and it will not ever happen again, and certainly not under this President’s watch. And that’s why he fought so hard and put together and put forward his 20-Point Peace Plan.
He then charged us to do what seemingly was another impossible task to bring that plan to the UN of all places. Well, you know what? We got it done. Resolution 2803 passed through the UN Security Council 13-0. The UN endorsed that plan. It provides a framework for what? A Gaza without Hamas rule, a demilitarization of the Strip, an international stabilization force and a path towards reconstruction and peaceful coexistence.
It’s not guaranteed to work, folks. But what everything we’ve tried in the past was guaranteed to fail and had failed. And so, the terrorist aimed to isolate Israel and destroy any hope for peace.
Let’s take stock just for a minute of all the things that the media and the experts said couldn’t be done. The biggest thing that they said couldn’t be done was the Abraham Accords.
Look, folks, October 7, completely, and I think irreversibly has backfired on Iran and all of their terrorist proxies.
The Shia Crescent that Iran spent decades and billions building has shattered. Assad is gone. Syria is no longer Iran’s pawn. Lebanon is actually talking to Israel to break free from Hizballah. Iraq is turning westward. All of these things, you never know this by reading any of the headlines. But most importantly, Hamas, its friends, and its backers are in shambles.
And meanwhile, despite all of the experts that said it was impossible that the Abraham Accords would never survive all of these tests and conflict—meanwhile, the Abraham Accords are actually expanding.
You wouldn’t know that, but today, right now as we speak, Iron Dome technology is protecting cities like Abu Dhabi and Dubai. I mean, that folks, just was completely unthinkable. Israelis and Arabs are standing shoulder to shoulder to defend the region from Iranian attacks.
And just as recently as this month, Danny and I were able to host the Foreign Minister of Israel and the Foreign Minister of Morocco together as they expanded their relationship. They upgraded their embassies. They have direct flights. They’re upgrading their trade and tourism. They’re establishing new avenues for investment.
So, folks, my bottom line is—and I know I went a little long, but I think it’s so important for everyone to hear: have hope. Peace is possible. America will stand with the Jewish people. The terrorists are on their back foot. Be strong, be resilient, be wise, and know that what you’re doing is right. Stand with your moral compass, and know that this administration, the United States of America, stands with you.
Thank you. It’s good to be with you.
###
title: Remarks at a UN High-Level Event Marking Three Years Since the October 7th Attack Against Israel

SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Former Western Asset Co-CIO Ken Leech in Cherry Picking Case
Washington D.C., Oct. 6, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission today moved for entry of a final judgment by consent against Stephen Kenneth Leech II, the former co-chief investment officer of registered investment adviser Western Asset Management Company LLC, whom the SEC previously charged with a multi-year cherry-picking allocation scheme.
As alleged in the SEC’s November 2024 complaint, from at least January 2021 through October 2023, Leech placed trades and then routinely delayed allocations until near or after futures markets set daily settlement prices, allowing him to observe price movements and disproportionally allocate hundreds of millions of dollars in realized and unrealized first‑day gains to favored portfolios and a similar amount of realized and unrealized first‑day losses to disfavored portfolios.
Without admitting the allegations in the SEC’s complaint, Leech consented to entry of a final judgment, subject to court approval, that would order him to pay a $3 million penalty, impose an officer-and-director bar and permanently enjoin him from violating antifraud provisions of federal securities laws. Leech also agreed to a forthcoming associational bar against him.
In June 2026, the Commission instituted settled public administrative proceedings against Western Asset, ordering the firm to pay a $100 million civil penalty and establishing a Fair Fund to distribute money to affected investors in the disfavored portfolios.
“The conduct by Leech and Western Asset was an egregious breach of fiduciary obligations to their clients,” said Brent Wilner, Associate Director of the SEC’s Los Angeles Regional Office. “Together, the resolution with Leech, if approved by the court, and the SEC’s prior settlement with Western Asset will return $103 million and provide meaningful relief to harmed investors, and reinforce that advisers must put clients first, every time.”
Also in June 2026, Leech pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in the Southern District of New York to obstruction of justice charges related to false and misleading testimony he provided to the SEC during its investigation; sentencing will take place in the coming weeks.
The SEC acknowledges the assistance of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York and the FBI.
###
Last Reviewed or Updated: Oct. 6, 2026
title: SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Former Western Asset Co-CIO Ken Leech in Cherry Picking Case

Neal, Wyden Object to Treasury’s Proposed Boost for Private School Tax Credits
New provision continues Trump’s pattern of ignoring clear Congressional mandates in an effort to benefit the wealthy and well-connected

Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military
WASHINGTON — On Monday, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07), a 25-year Army veteran, introduced the Learning Effective Strategies and Systems Optimization for National Security (LESSONS) from Ukraine Act, legislation requiring the Pentagon to study and apply lessons from Ukraine’s battlefield innovations to U.S. military doctrine and training.
“During my visit to Ukraine, I saw firsthand how the Ukrainians are rapidly adapting to a battlefield where drones and electronic warfare are changing how wars are fought,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will make sure our military learns from what Ukraine has discovered through years of defending itself against Putin’s invasion, from countering drone swarms and operating through electronic warfare to sustaining weapons production under attack. We need to put those lessons to work to strengthen our own military, protect our servicemembers, and ensure we are prepared to deter aggression across the world.”
“Ukraine’s defense against Russia has shown just how rapidly modern warfare is evolving. I saw that firsthand during my trip to Ukraine last month, where drones, electronic warfare, cyber operations, and defense manufacturing are reshaping the battlefield in real time,” said Vindman. "As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our military must constantly learn, adapt, and innovate to maintain our strategic advantage and protect our service members. The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will ensure the Department of Defense learns from Ukraine’s hard-earned experience and applies those lessons to our doctrine, training, and capabilities so our military is prepared for the threats of tomorrow.”
The LESSONS from Ukraine Act would require the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress within 120 days on lessons the U.S. military can draw from the Russia-Ukraine War, including the use of drones and other unmanned systems, electronic and cyber warfare, air defense, operations without GPS or satellite communications, battlefield medicine, and Ukraine’s efforts to expand and decentralize weapons production. The Pentagon would also be required to develop a plan and timetable for incorporating those lessons into U.S. military doctrine and training. Congressman Krishnamoorthi first announced the legislation following an August official visit to Ukraine, where he visited a Ukrainian drone production facility and met with officials about the battlefield and Ukraine’s rapidly evolving defense innovations.
The text of the legislation is available here.
title: Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military

Hoyer, Comptroller Lierman Visit Nonprofit Organizations Across Maryland's Fifth Congressional District
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) and Maryland Comptroller Brooke E. Lierman visited nonprofit organizations in Prince George's and Charles Counties to discuss each group's commitment to serving Southern Marylanders within their communities.
"Maryland's Fifth Congressional District is home to a multitude of nonprofit organizations that deliver critical resources and create opportunities for the region. From Westbrook Horse Farm to LifeStyles of Maryland, each advocate and organization we met with has an invaluable role in shaping the lives of Marylanders. I enjoyed seeing their work up close and discussing their contributions to our communities. I thank each organization for welcoming us, and I will continue to support their efforts during the remainder of my term in Congresss," said Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05).
“The three organizations we visited – all nonprofits but each doing work in its own way - play an essential role in strengthening our communities, supporting Marylanders in need, and creating opportunities for individuals to build better futures,” said Comptroller Brooke E. Lierman. “I am grateful for the dedicated people behind these organizations and the difference they make across our state. From supporting young people to helping individuals find stable housing, to supporting economic development and job creation, the work of these organizations makes Maryland a better place for everyone.” 
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with Brian Westbrook and his father, Roy Westbrook at the Westbrook Farm.
Starting off in Prince George's County, Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman visited the Westbrook Horse Farm in Upper Marlboro, Maryland. Owned and operated by Brian Westbrook, former NFL player and founder of The Brian Westbrook Foundation, the farm's programming provides hands-on skills training, riding lessons, and mentorship for youth to teach them responsibility and instill a greater sense of purpose in their lives. Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman received a tour of the farm and learned more about the community outreach initiatives Westbrook plans to implement in the near future.
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with board members of the
Charles County Military Alliance Council.

The group discussed strategy and ongoing investments to connect residents and local businesses with opportunities to support defense activities and boost the economy. Congressman Hoyer and the Comptroller continue working to maintain an effective relationship between military facilities, elected officials, and the greater Southern Maryland community.
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with LifeStyles CEO Sandy Washington and
Support Staff at the LifeStyles Headquarters in LaPlata, Maryland.
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman spent the rest of their afternoon at the LifeStyles Inc. headquarters in LaPlata, Maryland to receive an update on the around-the-clock support services provided at this location. During their tour, LifeStyles CEO Sandy Washington highlighted their work to deliver food, clothing, and housing assistance and workforce training for nearly 3 decades. LifeStyles of Maryland has 8 offices and distribution centers across the state to help meet the needs of underserved communities in the region.

HAMMOND – Dagoberto Padilla-Castro, 44 years old, of Honduras, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Philip P. Simon after pleading guilty to felony reentry of removed alien, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

Padilla-Castro was sentenced to time served, followed by 1 year of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 Special Assessment. The supervised release term would go into effect should the Defendant remain in, or return to, the United States within that period following expected removal proceedings.

“The Defendant was previously removed from the United States twice, in 2003 and 2004. By illegally reentering the United States again, he violated our nation’s laws, borders, and sovereignty. Once he is released, the Defendant needs to leave and not return again to the United States illegally,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Mildred.

This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from the Hobart Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Emily A. Morgan.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $413 Million Investment to Upgrade Rail Safety Across Florida, Build New Multimodal Station for the Space Coast
Instead of funding California’s train to nowhere, President Trump & Secretary Duffy are fixing over 900 highway-rail grade crossings throughout the Sunshine State
COCOA, FL – The U.S. Transportation Department’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) today joined the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) to celebrate $413 million in federal funding for essential rail safety upgrades across the Sunshine State and the construction of a new multimodal station in Cocoa. The state of Florida is providing an additional $100 million to support the projects.
The federal package will provide:
- $356 million for Florida DOT to deploy safety upgrades – which include new high-tech signage, lighting, and physical barriers – to 910 highway-rail grade crossing locations to better protect passengers, motorists, and pedestrians.
- $57 million for the City of Cocoa to build a new Brightline in-line rail station, multi-use access road, and new segment of double-track.
The $356 million in federal support from the FRA is a key pillar of Secretary Duffy’s “Golden Age of Rail” package announced in August. Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.
FRA Administrator David Fink joined FDOT Secretary Jared W. Perdue, P.E., U.S. Congressman Mike Haridopolos, railroad industry leaders, and local and state officials in Brevard County today to share details about the safety upgrades as well as plans for the new Brightline Cocoa station.
"Defunding California’s train to nowhere is producing tangible safety upgrades and real infrastructure projects that will benefit millions of Floridians for years to come,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “President Trump is delivering transformational results for the Sunshine State, and we’re just getting started.”
“This is a monumental leap in rail safety for the state of Florida, and it was only made possible by President Trump and Secretary Duffy,” said FRA Administrator David Fink. “By investing these dollars where they matter most, President Trump and Secretary Duffy are ushering in a Golden Age of Rail that will make Florida’s rail corridors safe, modern, and more efficient.”
“Here on the Space Coast, we continue to build for the future,” said U.S. Congressman Mike Haridopolos. “This new station will make it easier for people to travel to and from the Space Coast while supporting our growing community. It is expected to have up to a $350 million annual economic impact and support 3,500 jobs, bringing even more opportunity to our region. Thank you to the FRA, FDOT, and our local partners for working together to make rail travel safer and more accessible for Floridians.”
Additional Information:
Of the railroad crossing enhancements to be installed at over 900 locations across Florida, nearly a quarter of the sites will be in Central Florida – in Brevard, Orange, Osceola, Seminole, and Volusia counties.
The types of safety features to be added include:
- Upgrades of pedestrian-activated warning systems at pedestrian rail crossings, including lights, gates, and audible warnings for pedestrians.
- Refinement and enhancement of pavement markings to ensure only rail-related markings are used (including Dynamic Envelopes). Raised reflective markers and solid lane lines will provide motorists, pedestrians, and bicyclists with clear, consistent visual cues.
- Installation of overhead-mounted signals to enhance motorists’ awareness of rail crossings.
- Enhanced lighting to heighten the visibility of rail crossings for pedestrians and motorists.
- Installation of LED-enhanced “DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS” signage at high-speed rail crossings to reinforce safe driving behaviors for motorists.
- Addition of “ANOTHER TRAIN COMING” warning signs at locations with at least two tracks to help prevent potential conflicts with pedestrians and vehicles with an unexpected additional train.
- Installation of physical barriers such as double gates to further deter vehicles from going around rail crossing gates.
###
title: Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $413 Million Investment to Upgrade Rail Safety Across Florida, Build New Multimodal Station for the Space Coast

Pou Statement On Release of Martin Soto from ICE Detention
PATERSON, NJ – Tonight, U.S. Representative Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) celebrated the release of Martin Soto, a resident of the Ninth Congressional District who was held in ICE custody for several months.
“I am so overjoyed that Martin Soto is finally freed from ICE custody,” stated Rep. Nellie Pou, a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security. “Martin was undeniably targeted and mistreated, being moved from Delaney Hall to the Elizabeth Detention Center and held in solitary confinement. ICE remains out of control in our state and we must continue to oppose its rampant abuses. Initially detained in Newark, Martin Soto was moved to the Elizabeth Detention Center in retaliation for his role in the hunger and labor strike to highlight the deplorable conditions at Delaney Hall. There, Martin experienced harsh retribution including isolation.

“I am so happy Martin is finally being released from ICE custody,” said Gabby Soto, wife of Martin Soto. “I want to thank Congresswoman Nellie Pou for all of her work on his case. Her efforts were critical to us finally reaching this moment.”

WTAS: New Regulations Make It Easier to Find, Compare, and Report Healthcare Pricing and Coverage Information
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 6, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), on Monday announced that Americans will have access to more reliable, accessible, and actionable information about what their health coverage includes and what they are likely to pay before receiving care under new regulations that strengthen federal healthcare price transparency requirements. The actions taken today to create a more transparent healthcare marketplace also ensure employers can make more informed decisions; researchers can better understand healthcare markets; and innovators can build better tools.
Here is how government officials, medical professionals, advocates, the media, and others are responding:
Government Officials:
- Rep. Davidson via X: “When patients can compare prices, health plans and providers have to compete for their business, and that competition brings costs down. This final rule puts Americans in charge of choosing the health care that works best for them and their families.”
- Rep. Harshbarger via X: “For too long, the corporations that pay for our care have gone to great lengths to hide costs and bury patients in complexity. For the first time, insurers will have to attest that their pricing data is accurate and complete. Transparency drives competition, and competition lowers costs. That's a win for patients, employers, and taxpayers!”
- Rep. Fine via Newsmax: “I think it's going to be a massive help,’ Fine said. ‘When people are getting an X-ray or they're going to get a shot or some other service, they don't realize that the 10 providers in their community could charge massively different prices. If you're willing to drive an extra mile down the street to save a nickel a gallon on gas, you certainly ought to know if a procedure is going to cost $50 or $100 less at one place or another.”
- White House via X: “The Trump Administration is putting Americans first with healthcare price transparency, ensuring healthcare price data is clear and reliable. @HHSGov is making healthcare transparency useful for patients. Americans should know exactly how much their healthcare options cost.”
- White House Rapid Response via X: “@DrOzCMS: ‘Our rule is going to empower all these transparency sites in the room today to sync up and deliver a one-stop shop for cost comparison — using data that has always been out there but has purposely been obfuscated.’”
- White House Rapid Response via X: “@SecKennedy: In his first term, President Trump succeeded in demanding healthcare price transparency — but the industry took evasive action to obscure the process. Today, we are fixing that so Americans know exactly what their healthcare procedure will cost.”
- Department of Labor via X: “The American People have a right to compare healthcare prices and thanks to @POTUS — now they can. CHOICE DRIVES COMPETITION — it’s the opposite of Socialism — IT IS THE AMERICAN WAY. Together with @HHSGov, @USTreasury, and @CMSGov — we are delivering on healthcare transparency so ALL AMERICANS can make the best choices for themselves and their families.”
- Republican Study Committee via X: “President Trump started the fight for healthcare price transparency in his first term, and now @SecKennedy and @DrOzCMS are finishing what he started by giving American families the CLEAR, ACCURATE, and ACTIONABLE prices they need to make the best decisions for their health.”
- Republican Study Committee via X: “For too long, Big Healthcare overcharged vulnerable patients and kept Americans in the dark about what their care would cost. Thanks to the leadership of @CMSGov, new transparency rules will cut bloated pricing files by roughly 70%, strip out useless and duplicative data, and make personalized cost estimates far easier to access. America FIRST means American patients FIRST, and the Trump administration is keeping that promise.”
- Pennsylvania State Senator Dawn Keefer via X: “A win for health care transparency! The federal govt is strengthening price transparency so patients can compare costs. That's a step in the right direction! One we should build on here in PA.”
Medical Professionals & Academics:

Closing some loopholes, requiring plans to attest that the prices are accurate, allowing patients to get REAL price info by phone in advance. And much more. Amen. Thanks @HHSGov @USDOL @USTreasury @FTC”
Advocates & Organizations:
- Patient Rights Advocate Founder and Chairman, Cynthia A. Fisher, via The Center Square: “…[A] transformative step to lower health care costs, stop overcharges, and hold insurers and hospitals accountable... added requirement of executive attestation that published prices and other information are true, accurate, and complete as of the date in the machine-readable file is a breakthrough for compliance… Real price transparency means patients can shop for better care at lower prices and employers can demand a better deal.”
- America First Works via X: “@SecKennedy announces more TRANSPARENCY in healthcare costs: ‘If you went to a car dealer and you said, 'How much does that cost?' and they said, 'We're not going to tell you until after you make the purchase,' you wouldn't do it—but that's how the healthcare system in this country [worked].’”

- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@AFergusonFTC hits it out of the park: ‘Arming consumers with the knowledge they need to shop around will foster competition and drive down healthcare costs.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@Sonderling47 explains how price transparency is critical to lowering healthcare costs for employers and employees: ‘When workers and employers can compare prices, providers have to compete for their business... putting more money back in your pocket.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@CMSGov’s Peter Nelson announces the upcoming schema for the Prescription Drug File, requiring insurers to post exactly what they pay for prescription drugs. This long-overdue step is essential to helping patients better understand and lower their drug costs!”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@SecKennedy nails it: ‘One lesson from the first generation transparency requirement is that publishing enormous quantities of data does not necessarily produce useful information.’ The new Transparency in Coverage final rule requires health plans to publish the data actually needed to deliver clear and upfront prices to patients.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “The final Transparency in Coverage rule announced today is a significant step toward holding insurers accountable and securing actual, upfront prices in dollars and cents for consumers. This rule makes the data usable by a general audience. For large employers that provide coverage to tens of millions of workers and their families, better data means we can spot when one hospital charges more than another for the same procedure, negotiate harder, build better networks, and cut waste that drives up costs for employers and employees alike.”
- Purchaser Business Group on Health CEO, Elizabeth Mitchell, via Healthcare Dive: “We believe that these new rules are going to make a really significant difference, this has the potential to meaningfully address the affordability crisis in the commercial market.”
- State Financial Officers Foundation CEO, OJ Oleka via The Center Square: “…[R]eal dollar prices, standardized reporting, and greater accountability is meaningful progress for employers, patients, and taxpayers trying to understand what healthcare actually costs… Accountability and transparency go hand in hand, but transparency only works if the data is actually usable.”
- David Kochel, campaign strategist via The Center Square: “[T]he Trump Administration is taking action on healthcare price transparency ahead of the midterm elections, showing Republicans are willing to lean forward on an issue that hits Americans’ wallets every day. Real prices give patients the freedom to choose lower-cost, high-quality care and give employers the power to audit spending, negotiate better deals, and hold insurers accountable…The administration's work on price transparency puts power in the hands of patients and employers to stop overcharges, demand a better deal, and keep more of their hard-earned money."
- Families USA Executive Director, Anthony Wright, via press release: “Cleaner, more useable pricing data from insurers will help employers, researchers and other purchasers see what health care actually costs.”
- Save Our States Executive Director, Trent England, via The Center Square: “That it has taken this long to guarantee patients and employers actual prices is absurd…Fortunately, President Trump is standing strong for common-sense and putting the American people ahead of hospital and insurance executives and other insiders…With real price transparency, patients can plan ahead, find the best care at the best price, fight overcharging, and avoid price gouging and surprise bills…Employers can finally see the receipts and use real pricing data to negotiate better deals, lowering healthcare costs for employees and freeing up resources for higher wages, more jobs, and better returns for investors, including pensioners and retirees…All this is long overdue.”
- Andrew Bremberg, Former Director of the Domestic Policy Council via The Center Square: “…[R]equiring insurance executives to attest that their machine-readable files are true, accurate, and complete will unleash actual transparency and accountability… These commonsense reforms are a testament to President Trump's commitment to 'maximum transparency' and shifting the power from the big business of healthcare to the American people.”
Media & Influencers:
- Laura Ingraham via Fox News broadcast: “America is frustrated with these indecipherable medical bills. Anytime you go to the doctor, especially you go to the hospital. Now look at Riley Gaines. She gave birth a year ago and is still getting a constant stream of bills in the mail…This happens to everyone and that’s why President Trump is taking on the machine. Today, the administration is finalizing new rules requiring hospitals and health insurers to disclose prices up front, so patients know exactly what they’re paying for.”
- Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) via X: “BREAKING: In a massive win, HHS Sec. Bobby Kennedy is moving to FORCE Big Healthcare to disclose all pricing to Americans UP FRONT rather than dump JUNK DATA as a loophole, which was totally unusable. Pricing files will be slashed by -70% and Americans will actually be able to SHOP AROUND with all necessary information before they receive care. THIS IS COMMON SENSE.”
- Terrence Williams (@w_terrence) via X: “Give Dr. Oz credit on this one. This is what I voted for. Saving people money and cutting unnecessary waste. Here is what has been going on. Medicare has been paying twice for overlapping work when someone has an office visit and a procedure on the same day. Those extra costs can eventually mean higher premiums and more out of pocket costs for patients. @DrOzCMS is pushing a fix so Medicare is not paying full price twice for the same overlapping work. This is the kind of change I want to see in healthcare”
- One America News Network (@OANN) via X: “Dr. Oz: ‘Our rule is going to empower all these transparency sites in the room today to sync up and deliver a one-stop shop for cost comparison — using data that has always been out there, but has purposely been obfuscated.’”
- Morse Report (@MorseReport) via X: “HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. says the Trump administration is fixing healthcare price transparency after the industry took evasive action to obscure first-term rules. HHS and CMS finalize regulations so Americans can see what a procedure will cost before they receive care. Kennedy says patients will get clearer information to compare costs, understand coverage, and make informed decisions.”

RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Leads Los Angeles Delegation and Entertainment Unions in Push for National Film Tax Credit
Bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act brings production jobs back to the U.S.
Levels international playing field against 65 countries that offer incentives America does not match
Above: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.
GLENDALE, CA – Today, October 6, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) led Members of the Los Angeles congressional delegation, and the major unions representing film and television workers at the Alex Theatre in a new push for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. This bipartisan legislation creates a national film tax credit on qualified labor expenses to bring production jobs back home.
A recording of the rally can be found here and here.
For decades, the United States has offered no national filming incentive, leaving American crews to compete against roughly 65 countries that do. The result has been hundreds of thousands of lost jobs for the drivers, grips, electricians, carpenters, caterers, and crew members.
WHAT THE BILL DOES:
- A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.
- Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.
- Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.
- Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.
- Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.
- A one-pager with more details can be found here.
“When a production leaves this country, the stars still work. The crew is who gets left behind,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “65 countries offer incentives we don’t match, and no single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. Our bipartisan bill is built on labor costs, which means it only pays off when American workers get hired. These are good paying union jobs with benefits and pensions, and I won’t stop fighting until they come home.”
“You won’t see the carpenters, electricians and camera crews on screen, but they are the backbone of the film industry,” said Congresswoman Linda T. Sánchez (CA-38). “Many live in my district and have watched their jobs move overseas as other countries use incentives to lure production away. Our bipartisan bill will level the playing field to bring good-paying union jobs back to Southern California and keep them here.”
"Southern California has been the heart of America’s film and television industry, but today, too many productions are leaving the United States for countries offering better incentives," said Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28). "That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which would provide a long-overdue federal tax credit to incentivize production here in the United States. Our creative workforce is the backbone of this industry. It's time we must invest in them and bring American film and television production back home.”
“Movie magic is central to the California story, and we need to keep it that way,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33). “Our state is losing good-paying, union jobs because filming in this country has become far too expensive. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act will bring jobs back to America, boost wages for workers and keep productions at home.”
“California is the heart of film and television production, in large part because of the workers and technicians who bring the magic to life,” said Representative Tran (CA-45). “Yet the U.S. is rapidly losing jobs in this industry to competitors overseas. When productions relocate outside the U.S., it’s the American-based crews that suffer the most. California’s workforce deserves better. This bill incentivizes American-based productions, strengthens California’s production workforce, and brings jobs back to the U.S.—where they belong.”
“Southern California is the birthplace of the modern film and television industry. From the movies and television shows that have entertained audiences around the world to the hardworking people behind them, this industry is a vital part of our community and economy,” said Congressman Lieu (CA-36). “We can’t let the United States’ film industry lose ground to foreign competitors. I am pleased to be an original co-sponsor of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. It’s time to strengthen our domestic film industry and protect American jobs.”
“American performers and entertainment workers should not have to leave the country to find work in an industry that was built here. Film and television are more than entertainment — they are a major American industry that supports hundreds of thousands of good-paying union jobs and generates significant economic activity in communities across the country. For decades, foreign governments have recognized the economic value of production and successfully used incentives to attract these jobs overseas. States across the country have shown what targeted incentives can do to attract and retain production, and a federal incentive would build on those efforts and give the United States a stronger tool to compete. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is an investment in American workers, American industry and American communities. SAG-AFTRA is proud to stand with Congresswoman Friedman and our labor partners in support of this important legislation,” said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.
“The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will benefit entertainment industry workers, as well as the supporting businesses and local economies that rely on a robust domestic entertainment industry. Lawmakers have an opportunity to invest in an important American industry and preserve middle-class jobs, by passing the first-ever federal film and television tax incentive program,” said WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta.
"Let’s not overthink this. The world is a complicated place, but this legislation is a no-brainer. It's going to get people back to work, and everyone just wants an opportunity to work in the industry they love in this country. Everyone will benefit from this – Republicans, Democrats, workers, audiences -- because our industry touches everyone," said Mike Farah, an Emmy-winning producer and a President of the Producers Guild of America.
“I’ve worked aggressively with labor and entertainment industry leaders, and together we've already expanded state-level tax incentives and reduced filming fees locally. A federal tax credit is critical so our local incentives remain competitive with countries that offer larger benefits and have drawn productions out of the United States,” said Mayor Bass. “I want to thank the bipartisan leadership of Representatives Laura Friedman, Brian Jack, Linda Sánchez, and Nathaniel Moran and Senators Adam Schiff and Tim Scott for understanding the importance of investing in an industry that is so critical to Los Angeles and the country. As a former Member of Congress, I'll continue leveraging my relationships in Washington to ensure this bill is passed into law.”
U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (CA-30) was joined by Senator Adam Schiff (CA), U.S. Representatives Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Pete Aguilar (CA-33), Ted Lieu (CA-36), David Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45), Glendale Mayor Ardy Kassakhian, IATSE International Vice President and Director of the Motion Picture and Television Department Mike Miller, SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta, DGA Associate National Executive Director and Western Executive Director Rebecca Rhine, Teamsters At-Large Vice President and Motion Picture Division Director Lindsay Dougherty, LiUNA Business Manager Alex Aguilar, Jr., and producer and three-time Emmy winner Mike Farah.
Below: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.
###
title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Leads Los Angeles Delegation and Entertainment Unions in Push for National Film Tax Credit

Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett (TX-30) sent a letter to Governor Greg Abbott, Attorney General Ken Paxton, and Education Commissioner Mike Morath demanding answers and accountability over the use of excessive force against children in Texas public schools.
“Texas is failing our kids. Our children deserve to go to school in an environment that fosters learning and growth, not environments where ordinary student behavior can end with a child in handcuffs, hogtied, shocked with a Taser, or pepper-sprayed.”
Crockett expressed concern regarding the expansive presence of police in school, putting Texas students in unnecessary contact with the criminal system, further opening the door to the school-to-prison pipeline.
In her letter, Crockett highlights how officers using excessive force to respond to student behavior could ordinarily be addressed through school discipline. The letter cites a New York Times investigation documenting more than 2,600 school-based use-of-force incidents across Texas from January 2022 through December 2025.
Crockett is demanding answers regarding police involvement in routine student discipline, incident reporting, accountability for police misconduct, and potential changes to state law training.
“The number of “incidents” is alarming. Our kiddos should not be treated like criminals. They are the future of this country, and we owe it to them to protect them from cruel and abusive behavior. I am urging our Texas leaders to exercise immediate oversight and ensure accountability for these horrific reported actions. This is unacceptable, and it has to stop.”
The full letter can be found here.
title: Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools
