Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce Disaster Declaration from U.S. Small Business Administration for Homeowners, Renters, and Businesses Impacted by September Flooding
Declaration Enables Impacted Individuals, Families, Businesses, and Nonprofits to Apply for Low-Interest Loans to Aid in Their Recovery
Hartford, CT – Today, members of the Connecticut Congressional delegation joined Governor Ned Lamont to announce a disaster declaration from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) for Fairfield County and the contiguous counties of New Haven County and Litchfield County in response to the flash flooding event that impacted the region on September 13, 2026. The approved declaration means that homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits in the impacted counties can apply for low-interest loans from the SBA to aid in their recovery.
“This declaration makes low-interest loans available to homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits so they can recover and rebound from these flash floods,” Governor Lamont said. “I am glad that we’ve been able to secure this funding and encourage anyone who was impacted by this storm to look into this assistance and determine whether it can help you in the recovery process.”
“As communities continue to recover from severe flooding that hit our state last month, I am glad that the Small Business Administration granted our request for a disaster declaration," said Congressman John B. Larson. "This declaration is a crucial step forward, so small businesses, local organizations, and homeowners can get the help they need to repair and rebuild after incurring damage—including in Litchfield County. Our delegation will keep working with the governor and state leaders to ensure the federal government is responsive to the towns and cities that were impacted by this storm.”
“This disaster declaration is a strong step toward bringing federal aid to Connecticut following severe floods last month. This step allows Connecticut state agencies to work with federal partners like the SBA to continue recovery efforts and potentially unlock more federal assistance to rebuild local businesses. I am grateful to the SBA for their swift response to Governor Lamont and our delegation’s request,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal.
“Connecticut communities were hit hard on September 13 by sudden and intense flooding. I encourage all small business owners in the counties covered by this disaster declaration to take advantage of the available assistance from the Small Business Administration,” said Congressman Joe Courtney.
“Extreme weather events like flash flooding are damaging our communities more often and more unexpectedly. I am glad that federal support is on its way through this SBA disaster declaration for the businesses, residents, and communities that were impacted by devastating flash floods last month. I will continue to fight for federal resources so that Connecticut has the support necessary rebuild after disasters like this one,” said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro.
“I’m glad the federal government is stepping up to assist Connecticut residents and businesses, especially those in Fairfield County, in recovering from last month’s flooding. I encourage anyone whose residence or business was impacted by the severe weather to look into these resources. I will continue fighting alongside the rest of Connecticut’s Congressional delegation to bring home the federal support our constituents need to rebound,” said Congressman Jim Himes.
“Extreme weather continues to impact our state. I am pleased to see the U.S. Small Business Administration approve federal assistance for parts of the Fifth District and our state. These federal resources will help alleviate the financial losses of business leaders and homeowners from the recent flooding,” said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes.
The following groups may be eligible for low-interest SBA disaster loans:
- Homeowners: Up to $500,000 to repair their primary residence.
- Homeowners and renters: Up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.
- Business owners: Up to $2,000,000 for the replacement of real property, inventories, machinery, equipment, and other physical losses.
- Businesses and nonprofits: Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2,000,000 to provide necessary working capital until normal operations resume after a disaster.
“We know there are people with uninsured losses. These low-interest SBA loans are a means for people to rebuild and recover from the flooding. Additionally, our Volunteer Organizations Active in Disaster—independent faith-based and nonprofit groups—remain engaged in helping people needing cleanup,” saidConnecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection Commissioner Ronnell A. Higgins.
How to apply for low-interest SBA disaster loans
Under this declaration, the application deadline for physical damage loans is December 1, 2026, and the application deadline for economic injury loans is July 2, 2027.
Applications may be submitted to the SBA through the following methods:
- In-person: A temporary, in-person SBA Disaster Loan Outreach Center will open at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center at 999 Broad Street in Bridgeport beginning October 7, 2026.
  - It will operate Mondays through Fridays from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Saturdays from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; and it will be closed on Sundays.
  - Due to prior engagements, it will have adjusted hours of 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on October 9, 2026; and 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on October 20 and 21, 2026.
  - It will be closed on October 12, 2026, due to the Columbus Day holiday.
  - It is expected to permanently close at 4:00 p.m. on October 21, 2026.
- Online: The MySBA Loan Portal at provides applicants with the ability submit applications online, view loan details, check balances, make payments, and access statements.
For further assistance, applicants can contact the SBA’s Customer Service Center by email at disastercustomerservice@sba.gov or by phone at 1-800-659-2955. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
title: Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce Disaster Declaration from U.S. Small Business Administration for Homeowners, Renters, and Businesses Impacted by September Flooding

October 6, 2026
“The Grande Arbor” Manufactured Home by Cavco Homes and UMH Properties
CALIFORNIA - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations and resources from the West Coast during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.
“Expanding affordable housing options is important for communities across the Pacific region,” said Region IX Administrator Will Spencer. “At the Innovative Housing Showcase, I saw how private companies are working alongside HUD and local communities to make housing easier to build and more affordable for American homebuyers.”
HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.
Examples from the West Coast Region
A fully furnished, enterable tiny home, manufactured using Azure Printed Home's (California) proprietary factory-based 3D printing technology and advanced modular construction.
“The Grande Arbor,” a two-bedroom manufactured home from Cavco Homes (Arizona) and UMH Properties. This home is the first manufactured house built to the HUD code without a permanent steel chassis.

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces Five Actions to Accelerate Commercial Space Licensing
Proposed rules represent the USDOT SPACE Task Force’s first pillar to cut red tape & supercharge American space dominance
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is proposing five rules to streamline and modernize the commercial space launch and reentry regulations. The rules were developed in concert with the recently launched the USDOT Space Policy Administration, Coordination, and Execution (SPACE) Task Force.
Key changes to the Part 450 commercial space licensing process include:
- Allowing operators to submit launch applications electronically
- Providing greater flexibility to demonstrate an equivalent level of safety
- Combining three required safety analyses into a single submission
- Eliminating duplicative safety analyses when a safety requirement is already addressed through other approved methods.
What we’re doing: The proposed rules would make the Part 450 licensing process more efficient, less burdensome, and more flexible for operators while maintaining the FAA’s safety standards.
Why it matters: Simplifying these critical rules will ensure American space operators can continue leading the world in commercial launch growth while maintaining the FAA’s highest safety standards. These actions also support President Trump’s space policy goals in his Enabling Competition in the Commercial Space Industry Executive Order and National Space Transportation Policy to enhance American greatness in space by enabling a competitive launch marketplace and substantially increasing commercial space launch cadence to 1,000 per year by 2030.
“We can’t unlock the final frontier if we let red tape hold American innovators back from leading the way,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “By making simple, common-sense changes to modernize the commercial licensing processes, we can strengthen the United States’ position as a powerhouse for commercial space transportation while maintaining the highest safety standards in the world.”
“The SPACE Task Force is moving quickly to execute on President Trump’s vision to achieve America’s continued superiority in space,” said U.S. Under Secretary for Transportation Ryan McCormack. “The commercial space industry is moving at lightning speed, and our regulations need to keep pace. I’m proud of the work the Task Force has already done to hit the ground running and create the conditions that will revolutionize America’s commercial space industry.”
“These proposed rules are just the beginning of the FAA’s effort to reduce unnecessary burdens on the U.S. commercial space industry,” said Acting Deputy FAA Administrator Liam McKenna. “These changes will give operators greater flexibility and make the licensing process more efficient, while ensuring the safety of the National Airspace System remains our top priority.”
Reminder:
The U.S. was responsible for 217 of the 329 commercial space launches worldwide in 2025 and we expect to see that number will soar to 10,000 FAA-licensed launches and reentries a year by 2035.

Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands
The proposed revision of the 2005 Travel Management Rule poses serious risk to conservation and safety on public lands
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 6, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Under Secretary Michael Boren and U.S. Forest Service (USFS) Chief Tom Schultz strongly opposing the Administration’s proposed rule expanding vehicle access to public lands and trails that are already facing maintenance backlogs. Vasquez was joined by 28 of his House and Senate colleagues in his call to keep the 2005 Travel Management Rule in place.
“New Mexicans deserve public lands that are safe and well-managed. Ending the long-established Travel Management Rule would put public safety at risk and open the door to damage that will take generations to undo,” said Vasquez. “Hikers, hunters, and ranchers alike shouldn’t have to worry about more folks driving through the spaces they use for recreation and grazing. Instead of opening more of our public lands to vehicle access in places where access already exists, the Forest Service should focus on maintaining existing trails and roads. This broad reversal is unnecessary."
The USFS and the Bureau of Land Management have separate but similar rules requiring our public land agencies to provide clear, consistent guidance for how public lands are used, including where motorized vehicles, including cars and ATVs, can travel. For those who enjoy our public lands, whether on foot or on wheels, these rules help keep trails open, accessible, and responsibly managed. They also require public input before designating routes, produce Motor Vehicle Use Maps that show visitors where they can go, give rangers clear standards to enforce, and allow exceptions for emergency, military, and law enforcement vehicles.
Changing the 2005 rule, as proposed by USDA, could endanger public safety, reduce quality access to our public lands, and degrade the quality of trails, lands and waters that support our nation’s wildlife and outdoor recreation economy.
The letter demands that any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule preserve the following core principles:
- Maintain the current default of keeping routes and areas closed to motorized use unless expressly designated as open.
- Carry forward criteria that guide local land management decisions and protect critical public land values, including soil, watersheds, vegetation, and wildlife habitat, as well as reduce conflicts between public land uses such as camping, hiking, hunting, and grazing.
- Travel management decisions should continue to be informed by robust public engagement and local input.
- The agencies must retain the ability to protect fish and wildlife habitat, riparian areas, water quality, and cultural resources.
- The agencies should continue to clearly identify where motorized travel is permitted.
- The agencies should consider the long-term cost of properly maintaining, staffing, and administering their transportation system before adding new routes or expanding access.
“This is yet another egregious attack in the systematic dismantling of public lands management of our national forests,” said Paul Sanford, director for equitable access policy advocacy at The Wilderness Society. “Travel management provides the basic guardrails that let hikers, hunters, anglers, and riders share the same forest without chaos; removing those guardrails threatens the freedom of all public lands users to safely enjoy our national forests the way they choose. Paired with the proposed repeal of the Roadless Rule, this destructive agenda sells out future generations’ enjoyment of our forests in order to hand them over for corporate profits.”
“We’re grateful to see Congressional Leaders pushing back on federal agency proposals to gut travel management regulations and prioritize off-road vehicles at the expense of wildlife, cultural sites, desert waterways and other recreationists, proposals that will make visiting Utah’s canyon country worse for everyone,” said Laura Peterson, Senior Attorney at the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance (SUWA). “The Trump Administration’s vision for public lands is not about balance or reasonable access, it is about blanketing landscapes with off-road vehicle routes, transforming quiet, wild places into motorized playgrounds.”
"We stand with Rep. Vasquez and his urgent request to keep the Travel Management Rule intact,” said Taylor Rush, government relations representative at Defenders of Wildlife. "For more than two decades, this rule has protected our cherished wildlife, outdoor recreationists, clean water supply and local communities from the harmful impacts of unmanaged motorized vehicle use. Weakening the framework used to reduce habitat damage and social conflict would result in dangerous degradation of our wild places and wildlife."
###
title: Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands

JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s Air and Marine Operations marked the final operational flight of its last P-3 Airborne Early Warning aircraft Sept. 30, 2026, at the National Air Security Operations Center in Jacksonville.
For decades, Jacksonville-based P-3 AEW aircraft supported the nation’s border security mission by conducting wide-area aerial surveillance over the Caribbean, the Gulf of America and transit zones across Central and South America.
Known by flight crews as the “Dome,” the P-3 AEW paired the long-range capabilities of the Lockheed P-3 aircraft with radar, communications and command-and-control systems. Operating from NASOC Jacksonville and NASOC Corpus Christi, Texas, the aircraft functioned as an airborne command center. It tracked multiple air and maritime targets and supported complex operations to stop illicit activity with partners, including Joint Interagency Task Force South.
“The P-3 AEW platform carried out a critical mission for decades,” said a NASOC Jacksonville aircrew member. “It's crews monitored millions of square miles of air and maritime approaches, helping identify airborne threats, counter illicit drug trafficking and disrupt networks facilitating illegal migration before they reached U.S. borders.”
During their service, Jacksonville-based P-3 AEW aircraft logged tens of thousands of flight hours supporting counter-narcotics and border security missions. NASOC Jacksonville crews also deployed in support of domestic and international emergency response operations, including humanitarian relief and emergency communications coordination after major natural disasters in the Caribbean.
Although the P-3 AEW aircraft are retiring from AMO’s active inventory, the P-3 Long Range Tracker will continue to operate and support AMO’s maritime domain awareness, detection, monitoring and interdiction missions. The experience and technical expertise of P-3 AEW aircrews, maintenance specialists and flight engineers also will continue to support AMO’s aviation mission.
As AMO modernizes its fleet, it will add C-130J aircraft to help sustain long-range operational capabilities and mission readiness.
AMO safeguards the nation by anticipating and confronting threats through aviation and maritime law enforcement expertise, innovative capabilities and partnerships at the border and beyond. AMO is an operational component of CBP. It works alongside federal, state and international partners to disrupt smuggling operations and safeguard national security.
title: CBP retires aircraft following final operational flight

Lynch (MA-08) led 24 of their colleagues from Northeastern states in pressing the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran. In their letter, the lawmakers urged the DOE to support an immediate end to the war and prioritize lowering energy costs for the winter, warning that rising prices will force families to choose between heating their homes and paying for basic necessities. 
“Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs,” wrote the lawmakers.
The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year.
In addition to increasing the cost of heating oil, the Trump administration has made or attempted to make heating costs for the upcoming winter even higher by: 
    - Attempting to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.
- Effectively increasing taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.
- Cutting more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families. 
“As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families,” the lawmakers continued. 
“To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP,” the lawmakers concluded. 
The lawmakers were joined by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.); and Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Bill Keating (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Chris Pappas (D-N.H.), Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.).

For the first time, the Air Force Office of Special Investigations has certified a cadre of special agents to both operate and instruct others on the Skydio X10D as part of a broader effort to expand small unmanned aircraft system operations across the agency.
Last month, six personnel completed a weeklong course at AFOSI headquarters in Quantico, Virginia, creating the first group of instructors positioned to bring the capability back to technical operations units in the field.
“We not only learned how to operate the drones, but also how to properly instruct other individuals on how to fly successfully to meet mission needs,” said Special Agent Logan Trigg, assigned to the 2nd Field Investigations Squadron Technical Operations Program.
That instructor qualification is what gives the course its broader impact. Rather than returning to their units as individual operators, the six graduates can now begin building additional capacity across AFOSI.
“My plan is to train the entire 2 FIS Technical Operations flight on drone operations because it enables every member to carry out the mission regardless of where or when the capability is needed,” Trigg said. “Having everyone certified creates the ability to attack the mission effectively.”
That train-the-trainer model is central to how AFOSI intends to grow the program. The capability could support surveillance, outdoor crime scenes, protective-service support and other missions requiring what Trigg called an “an eye in the sky.”
The work to build AFOSI’s agency-level capability has been an ongoing effort since early 2024, with Detachment 111 at Edwards Air Force Base, California, serving as a working pilot program well before the five X10Ds will be used by Technical Operations agents in January 2027.
Creating multipliers
The course was structured around more than basic flight instruction. Agents first completed roughly 16 hours of classroom work covering airspace, Federal Aviation Administration requirements, mission planning and the administrative requirements behind government sUAS operations.
“After the classroom portion, we transitioned to the field for hands-on flight operations,” said Special Agent Scott Zawacki, AFOSI Technical Operations program manager. “We focused on the fundamentals of takeoff and landing, then progressed to the system’s autonomous capabilities and how those features can be applied to meet operational requirements.”
Once students were comfortable with the aircraft, the training shifted to approximately 16 hours of flight scenarios built around AFOSI missions.
In one exercise, students lifted to roughly 400 feet, identified a vehicle’s license plate and tracked the vehicle for roughly a mile. In another, they used the aircraft’s thermal camera at night to locate a person concealed in a wooded area.
“The real advantage is our ability to design highly specialized training scenarios that directly support AFOSI’s unique mission requirements,” Zawacki said.
By the end of the week, all six had qualified as both operators and instructors. The course was the latest step in an effort that began years earlier at Edwards AFB.
Building the program
At Edwards AFB, Anthony Zutten, AFOSI Det. 111 criminal indexing and investigations specialist, in coordination with Zawacki, developed a sUAS capability before AFOSI moved to establish a broader program in 2024.
To do this, Zutten worked through the approvals, funding and training requirements needed to stand up the local effort, which soon moved beyond demonstration flights.
Prior to the latest training, agents at Edwards AFB used drones to support reconnaissance related to illegal marijuana growing operations near the installation, map the site of a recent B-52 crash for the 412th Test Wing and assist with search-and-rescue efforts across the installation’s expansive operating area.
In one case, Zutten said a drone helped narrow the search area for a 12-year-old believed to be in danger before the child was eventually located. Those missions gave AFOSI early proof of concept for how sUAS could support investigations and other operational needs.
Meanwhile, at AFOSI headquarters, Zawacki examined the same capability from an agency-wide perspective. The two efforts eventually converged.
“Det. 111 helped establish the proof of concept for a broader expansion,” Zawacki said.
As AFOSI’s new MAJCOM sUAS program manager, Zawacki, in collaboration with Zutten, brought the Edwards AFB effort under the developing AFOSI structure, building on roughly two years of policy work, testing, coordination and funding efforts to establish a broader command capability. Zutten’s experience also made him a natural choice to lead AFOSI’s first broader operator-instructor course.
“He did a lot of the legwork in finding the policy, finding the people to talk to, coordinating everything and helping get this off the ground,” Zawacki said.
Drone technology also shows potential for detailed crime-scene documentation, he said. In one demonstration, operators captured 126 images that were stitched together to develop two- and three-dimensional crime-scene models.
“When reviewing crime-scene map captures, the detail is so clear you can zoom in and see each individual bullet casing, easily identify placards and see exactly where key evidence rests in relation to the scene,” Zutten said.
With compatible software, agents can also mark evidence and measure distances using spatial data captured through the drone’s imagery, incorporate telemetry data and upload the information directly into AFOSI’s case management system.
“By utilizing sUAS to assist with crime scenes, we can effectively cut tens of hours of work from our field agents by digitizing everything on scene in real time,” Zutten said.
AFOSI has not yet used that capability in an actual case. For now, demonstrations are helping officials determine where the technology can best support field operations.
“Our job is to give agents the capabilities they need to accomplish the mission,” Zutten said. “If this technology can help us collect detailed information faster, reduce risk to our people and better support a case or operation, then that’s where its value shines.”
title: AFOSI certifies first drone operator-instructor cadre ahead of X10D fielding

text:
Elected leaders who hailed the reopening of the state’s second freestanding birth center earlier this year may have celebrated prematurely.
The Cambridge Health Alliance Birth Center, which closed in March 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic, was scheduled to reopen on July 6 with the aim of welcoming 100 babies in the first year. CHA said the center would serve all patients but have a “special focus on vulnerable and underserved populations who will benefit most from midwifery care and a birth center experience.”
But no deliveries happened this summer, even as supporters of the 2024 maternal health law tried to create new urgency around bolstering access to care and removing healthcare disparities for people of color.
“The Birth Center has been open for prenatal and outpatient visits,” CHA spokesperson David Cecere told the News Service Thursday. “We are anticipating our first delivery this week — they had been on hold as we worked through a leadership transition.”
Cecere said that “unexpected turnover” prompted the center to “hold deliveries until we established a plan to ensure high quality care and an exceptional patient experience.”
A spokesperson for the Department of Public Health, asked whether it was aware of any paused operations or staffing issues, said DPH had called the birth center and was told it was “taking clients.”
CHA has said the reopening would not have been possible without $1 million in state funding, which Cambridge Rep. Marjorie Decker helped secure in the fiscal 2024 budget. The center also received a grant from Beth Israel Lahey Health to help cover training, equipment, and community education and outreach.
The birth center, situated in a Victorian home with three renovated birthing rooms, held an open house on June 17 with more than 200 attendees, according to CHA. Speakers included Decker, U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark, Sen. Sal DiDomenico, Cambridge Mayor Sumbul Siddiqui and Public Health Commissioner Robbie Goldstein.
“Too often we are talking about the closure of maternity services, but today we get to celebrate a spectacular rebirth – and one that I hope will be followed by many more,” Goldstein said in a statement at the time. “Expanding access to community-based, relationship-centered care is key in advancing health equity. The reopening of the CHA Birth Center supports families who deserve more options for culturally responsive maternity care.”
Clark said the reopening was a “signal to women everywhere that we can and will keep making progress on maternal health.”
“We’re going to keep fighting for a healthcare system worthy of every mother in this community and a future worthy of the children who will begin their lives at CHA,” she said.
Michele Helgeson, a member of the Community Coalition for the Cambridge Birth Center, said everything had seemed “very positive” and “very, very upbeat” surrounding the open house. The coalition has met with CHA leaders to advocate for community interests and promote a midwifery model of care.
“There was no indication that there was any reason to stop or pause at that point,” said Helgeson, who added she wants to see CHA conduct community outreach and assure patients about available services at the birth center.
Birth centers are seen as alternatives to hospital deliveries, particularly in low-risk pregnancies. The facilities offer a home-like environment and are staffed by midwives who can provide more personalized care.
The 2024 law removed regulatory barriers to opening freestanding birth centers and created a pathway for certified professional midwives to become licensed. The state started accepting applications for temporary CPM licensure last month, as DPH expects to issue regulations for “standard” licensure in early 2027.
Until the CHA Birth Center returned to the maternal health landscape, Massachusetts was home to only one such freestanding facility in Northampton. But Seven Sisters Midwifery and Community Birth Center faces intense financial pressure due to low reimbursement rates compared to services provided in hospitals, according to owner and clinical director Ginny Miller.
Legislation (S 784) to ensure that certified nurse midwives, certified professional midwives and licensed freestanding birth centers are not paid less than physicians and hospitals delivering the same services has been lodged in the Senate Ways and Means Committee since April.
Kimberly Amsley-Camp was the CHA’s director of midwifery from August 2025 through September 2026, and she managed a staff of 20 certified nurse midwives and nurse practitioners, according to her LinkedIn profile. Working with a “multi-disciplinary” team, Amsley-Camp wrote she “planned and developed reopening of a hospital owned freestanding birth center.”
Amsley-Camp did not respond to a News Service request for comment.
Cecere said consultant and certified nurse midwife Erin Stein is now overseeing “daily operations” of the CHA Birth Center. She’s working alongside Dr. Tara Singh, chief of obstetrics and gynecology, and Allisyn Brady, senior director of OB/GYN.
Helgeson said the coalition wants to meet with CHA leaders and get an update on birth center operations, though she expects that won’t happen until November due to scheduling logistics.
“There is definitely support for the sustainability of the birth center, and that’s really what we’re hoping to achieve in the long run,” Helgeson said. “The opening is important, but we really want it to succeed in the long-term as well.”

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández visitó Vimenti, en el Residencial Ernesto Ramos Antonini en San Juan, donde presentó $1,031,000 en fondos federales que aseguró para desarrollar el Next Generation STEM Learning Lab Accelerator. La iniciativa ampliará las oportunidades de educación STEM para estudiantes de Vimenti School y otras tres escuelas del programa de Escuelas Comunitarias de Servicio Completo.

El Comisionado Residente aseguró los fondos mediante una solicitud de Financiamiento para Proyectos Comunitarios (Community Project Funding) presentada ante el Comité de Asignaciones de la Cámara de Representantes. Los recursos serán canalizados a través de la Oficina de STEM Engagement de la NASA.

“Llevo semanas diciendo que tenemos que priorizar lo básico, y la educación es básica. Nuestros niños fracasan en las materias básicas de español, inglés, ciencias y matemáticas. Este tipo de asignación ayuda a resolver ese problema.”, dijo el Comisionado Residente.

“Agradecemos al comisionado residente, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, y a su equipo, por la confianza depositada en este proyecto. Este logro reafirma nuestro compromiso de seguir identificando y allegando recursos que permitan que más escuelas públicas de Puerto Rico cuenten con espacios, herramientas y oportunidades educativas de excelencia para sus estudiantes, maestros y familias”, expresó Bárbara Rivera Batista, directora ejecutiva de Vimenti.

“Esta subvención confirma lo que puede lograr el modelo de Escuela Comunitaria de Servicio Completo cuando se le brinda el respaldo necesario. Nuestro compromiso es que estos recursos y espacios STEM se queden en cada escuela, sostenidos por sus propios equipos, mucho después de que termine el financiamiento”, indicó Lola Yglesias Quiñones, directora de Expansión de Vimenti.

A través del proyecto, las escuelas podrán desarrollar nuevos espacios educativos con herramientas de robótica y programación, astronomía y ciencias espaciales, ciencias de la Tierra, análisis de datos e inteligencia artificial. La iniciativa también contempla capacitación y acompañamiento para maestros, con el objetivo de fortalecer la capacidad de las escuelas para mantener y ampliar estos programas a largo plazo.

Durante su visita, el Comisionado Residente también sostuvo un conversatorio con estudiantes, familias y maestros sobre el modelo de Vimenti, los resultados que ha alcanzado la organización y la importancia de ampliar el acceso a oportunidades educativas en áreas STEM.

Según datos provistos por Vimenti, durante el año escolar 2023-2024 sus estudiantes alcanzaron un 54% de dominio en matemáticas, frente a un 11% a nivel de Puerto Rico. Entre los estudiantes con discapacidades, el dominio en matemáticas alcanzó un 63%, comparado con tasas de entre 10% y 18% a nivel estatal.

Vimenti atiende a estudiantes y familias mediante un modelo de dos generaciones que integra educación, salud y bienestar, desarrollo laboral, capacidad financiera, emprendimiento y mentoría. De acuerdo con su estudio de impacto de siete años, la organización ha generado cerca de $59 millones en impacto económico mediante sus operaciones y proyecta otros $97 millones asociados a iniciativas futuras.

title: Comisionado Residente entrega más de $1 millón para ampliar educación STEM en San Juan

EXIM Announces $547 Million Loan Guarantee to Support Tele-Fonika Cable Americas Proposed Manufacturing Facility in Texas
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) announced a $547 million loan guarantee to support Tele-Fonika Cable Americas’ (TFCA) growing manufacturing investment in the United States. Santander and Erste Bank Polska acted as sole arrangers for this financing. EXIM’s loan guarantee will support TFCA’s inaugural production of rubber-insulated cables in the United States. The cables, which will be made in Waller, Texas, are the arteries of modern infrastructure, carry power through the data centers, mines, and industrial facilities on which the American economy runs. TFCA’s cables will be manufactured by American workers for customers in the United States and around the world. The loan guarantee will be provided under the Bank’s Make More in America Initiative, which extends EXIM financing to export-oriented domestic manufacturing projects, especially in sectors critical to national security, to compete on a global scale.
“EXIM’s innovative tools like Make More in America help U.S. workers win around the globe and at home. Winning means building, and President Trump is delivering at unprecedented speed and scale. This financing will help Tele-Fonika Cable Americas reshore U.S. jobs and put Americans to work building the industries of the future,” said EXIM Chairman Jovanovic.
“EXIM’s approval of the $547 million loan guarantee is a key step for Tele-Fonika Kable Group’s investment in Waller, Texas,” said Bartłomiej Zgryzek, CFO of Tele-Fonika Kable Group. “This investment is a clear result of the Make More in America Initiative. Building a manufacturing facility in the United States from the ground up is a significant operational challenge, and we are taking it on. We expect continued growth in the U.S. market, particularly in data centers, mining and industrial infrastructure, and we intend to serve that demand with cables made in Texas.”
Tele-Fonika Cable Group is the third-largest electrical cable manufacturer in Europe and one of the largest in the world, employing more than 2,500 people and selling its products in more than 80 countries. The proposed Waller, Texas facility would be the company's first manufacturing operation in North America and reflects confidence in American workers and the U.S. industrial base. The facility is expected to boost employment in Texas, employing up to 500 people and several hundred construction workers.
EXIM’s first loan guarantee under the Make More in America Initiative is an important milestone in supporting export-oriented domestic manufacturing and strengthening the U.S. industrial base. The investment remains subject to all required regulatory approvals and permits, the securing of financing, compliance with all applicable conditions.
ABOUT EXIM:
As the United States government’s official export credit agency, the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) supports American jobs by facilitating U.S. exports. As an independent agency, EXIM plays a critical role in supporting economic growth, securing critical supply chains, and ensuring American businesses are given a fighting chance. To achieve this mission, EXIM offers financing including export credit insurance, working capital guarantees, loan guarantees, and direct loans. Learn more at www.exim.gov.

text:
Reps. Castro, Cisneros Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
WASHINGTON D.C. — Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.
Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most watched and financially successful productions.
El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.
“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country," said Congressman Castro. "Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”
“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”
“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”
“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”
“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen," said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. "Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”
“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”
“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”
Read the full text of the resolution here.
###
title: Reps. Castro, Cisneros Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers

Editor’s Note: This advisory was updated Oct. 8, 2026, to reflect revised timing for the Cygnus XL spacecraft’s deorbit and information about its departure .

After delivering more than 11,000 pounds of supplies, science experiments, and other cargo to the International Space Station for NASA, Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus XL spacecraft is scheduled to depart Friday, Oct. 9, as part of the company’s Commercial Resupply Services-24 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-24.

Watch NASA’s live coverage of departure beginning at 12:30 p.m. EDT through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:

https://www.nasa.gov/live

Flight controllers on the ground will send commands for the space station’s Canadarm2 robotic arm to detach the Cygnus XL spacecraft from the Unity module’s Earth-facing port and maneuver it into position for release at 12:45 p.m. NASA astronaut Luke Delaney will monitor the operation from aboard the orbital complex.

Loaded with thousands of pounds of disposal items and other unneeded cargo, Cygnus XL will deorbit Monday, Oct. 12, for a destructive re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere, where it will safely burn up. NASA will not provide coverage of the spacecraft’s deorbit.

The resupply spacecraft launched on April 11 on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

Learn more about this NASA commercial resupply mission at:

https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-northrop-grumman-crs-24/

Congresswoman Scholten Introduces COIN Act to Help Small Businesses Evaluate Uses of Digital Assets
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03), member of the House Small Business Committee, introduced the Currency Options, Information, and Navigation (COIN) Act. This legislation would direct the Small Business Administration (SBA) to create learning modules to help small businesses learn how to evaluate the use of digital assets, such as cryptocurrency, for their operations. According to PayPal, 39 percent of American merchants currently accept cryptocurrency at checkout, and 84 percent believe payments using cryptocurrency will become common within the next five years.
“Small businesses keep our state and country running, but too many owners are being asked to navigate rapidly changing technology without clear, reliable guidance or learning opportunities,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “Digital assets like cryptocurrency are becoming more and more common at checkout counters, which is why I’m proud to introduce the COIN Act to make sure Main Street businesses have what they need to adapt and succeed.”
The bill requires these learning modules to be made with detailed information on the benefits and drawbacks of digital assets, and would provide entrepreneurs information on the logistics involving this technology, including tax implications and security risks if they choose to adopt any kind of digital asset. Additionally, this bill directs the SBA Administrator to work with relevant agencies to achieve accuracy in the information provided, with the goal of creating a comprehensive resource for small businesses. Finally, the bill establishes an Advisory Working Group made up of members from academia, industry, and financial consumer advocates to inform the creation of these learning modules.
This bill reflects the Congresswoman’s ongoing efforts to support small business owners in Michigan and across the country. Earlier this year, Congresswoman Scholten’s bipartisan Investing in All of America Act was signed into law, and her Main Street Competes Act, AI WISE Act, and AI for Main Street Actall passed the House.
###
title: Congresswoman Scholten Introduces COIN Act to Help Small Businesses Evaluate Uses of Digital Assets

Moore, Bonamici, Frost, Grijalva, and Pocan Blast Regulations Paving the Way for National Voucher Scheme
The Treasury Department recently released regulations on their national voucher scheme, which was established through the Republicans’ Big Ugly Bil (HR 1). That law allowed Americans to receive a tax credit, up to $1,700, for donations to eligible scholarship-granting organizations, including religious schools. These regulations will double the credit amount for married couples. Representatives Gwen Moore (WI-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), and Mark Pocan (WI-02) have introduced HR 9289, the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, which would repeal the H.R .1 voucher scheme.
In states across the country, taxpayer supported voucher programs operate with little oversight and fund private schools who lack civil rights and other protections for students. In Wisconsin, the current voucher program at the state level will cost state taxpayers more than $700 million this year alone. Nearly all the students receiving a voucher in Wisconsin attend private, religious schools. 
Republicans are working to enact and expand this flawed system at the national level. So far, six states have resisted, including Wisconsin. 
“Despite what Republicans claim, these regulations make it clear this voucher scheme is designed to prop up private schools– at the expense of our public schools. Public schools serve every student who walks through its doors. Our tax dollars should not be funneled to schools that can discriminate against students who try to enroll. That is why I am proud to spearhead legislation to reverse this voucher scheme,” said Representative Gwen Moore (WI-04).
"The Treasury Department's school voucher regulations clearly demonstrate that the Trump administration has no interest in supporting public schools or the students they serve," said Representative Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01). "Diverting public resources into private schools - including religious schools -  that can pick and choose which students they enroll is unjust and irresponsible. Alarmingly, the regulations actually prohibit states from implementing additional oversight, reporting, accountability, or civil rights protections. The vast majority of students in this country attend public schools. We should be strengthening public education, not destroying it."
“This voucher scheme sends public money to private schools with less accountability for how that money is spent," said Representative Maxwell Frost (FL-10)."We’ve already seen the consequences in Florida, where the state struggled to track hundreds of millions of dollars in voucher funds and cases of fraud surfaced. Now the Treasury Department and Trump administration want to take that same model nationwide. We shouldn’t be making it easier to lose track of taxpayer dollars; we should be making sure every dollar is accountable to the public.” 
“Arizona’s fraud-ridden school voucher program should serve as a warning to the rest of the country. Instead, the Trump Administration is moving full steam ahead with a national voucher scheme while failing to include even basic safeguards to prevent taxpayer dollars from being wasted or abused. Arizona has already seen where this road leads. That’s why Congress must act to ensure federal taxpayer dollars strengthen the public schools that serve the overwhelming majority of America’s children, not subsidize privatization schemes rife with fraud,” said Representative Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).
“As a proud public school graduate, I know firsthand the value and importance of our public education system,” said Representative Mark Pocan (WI-02). “Fixing this blatant abuse of the tax system will help kids across the country, not just those whose parents are members of Mar-a-Lago. I applaud my friend, Rep. Moore, for spearheading this legislation, and I’m glad to be part of this effort to keep public funds in public schools.”
title: Moore, Bonamici, Frost, Grijalva, and Pocan Blast Regulations Paving the Way for National Voucher Scheme

Do Not Pay Reaches 99% of Federal Programs and New Safeguards Verify Over $3.7 Trillion in Payments
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service announced significant Fiscal Year 2026 results from Treasury’s efforts to prevent fraud and improper payments to better protect taxpayer dollars, fulfilling key requirements of Executive Order 14249, Protecting America's Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse, issued by President Trump on March 25, 2025.
“Treasury continues to transform how the federal government protects taxpayer dollars by using better data, stronger controls, and advanced technology to stop fraud and improper payments before money goes out the door,” said Secretary Scott Bessent. “In the past year alone, Treasury built and deployed new safeguards that verified more than $3.7 trillion in federal payments and increased Do Not Pay access from 4 percent of programs to 99 percent, ensuring agencies have access to the data they need. We are moving beyond ‘pay and chase’ and making prevention the federal government’s first line of defense.”
Over the past year, Treasury streamlined access to Do Not Pay’s fraud prevention tools, added nine new data sources to the Do Not Pay program, and deployed a new government-wide payment verification process.
MORE THAN TWENTYFOLD INCREASE IN DO NOT PAY REACH
Treasury significantly expanded the reach and capabilities of the Do Not Pay program, which provides federal agencies and federally funded state-administered programs with data and tools to help verify identity and eligibility for the purpose of preventing fraud and improper payments.
During FY2026, Treasury:
- Expanded Federal Programs’ Access to Do Not Pay Data by More Than Twentyfold. Approximately 99 percent of federal programs can now access all Do Not Pay data sources for which they are legally authorized, compared with approximately 4 percent at the end of FY2025. Most remaining programs are on track to complete onboarding in early FY2027. Treasury achieved this progress by streamlining the Do Not Pay onboarding process and partnering with federal agencies to accelerate the data-sharing and privacy compliance work necessary to expand access. All access to and use of Do Not Pay data is governed by strict privacy, security, and user access controls.
- Screened Over 2.3 Billion Records Against Do Not Pay Data Sources, a nearly four-fold increase from the 641 million records screened in FY2025. The increase reflects expanded use of Do Not Pay across the federal government, the implementation of payment verification, and additional screenings conducted for states through the Public Assistance Reporting Information System (PARIS).
- Added Nine New Datasets, expanding the breadth and depth of information available to agencies for payment, identity, and eligibility screening. New sources include company registration information through OpenCorporates, select verification against the Social Security’s Numident data, and grantee audit findings from the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, among others.
MOVING FROM “PAY AND CHASE” TO PREVENTION AND VERIFICATION
Treasury also implemented a new payment verification process during FY2026, establishing additional safeguards to verify critical payment information before federal payments are disbursed. During the fiscal year, Treasury screened more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling approximately $3.7 trillion. Through these screenings, Treasury identified and returned approximately 13,500 payments totaling $175 million that would have gone to deceased individuals.
Treasury developed and implemented these safeguards in close collaboration with federal agencies, with controls designed to protect legitimate payments while ensuring payment data is used responsibly and securely.
Treasury piloted additional verification capabilities during FY2026 to validate bank account ownership and the presence and format of Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TINs) associated with federal payments. These capabilities became fully operational on September 30, 2026, enabling Treasury to identify and return payments that fail established verification requirements before funds are disbursed.
Together, these improvements provide agencies with earlier access to authoritative and high-value data, strengthening their ability to identify potential fraud and improper payments before awards are made and payments are issued. Treasury will continue working with federal agencies to expand the data available through Do Not Pay, strengthen payment verification capabilities, and further embed fraud prevention into government-wide payment and program integrity controls.
###
title: Treasury Reports Major Progress in Preventing Fraud and Improper Payments

Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) — the only Virginian on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee — joined Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04) in sending a letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins opposing the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, commonly referred to as the “Roadless Rule.”
Since its implementation in 2001, the Roadless Rule has protected 45 million acres of forest lands across the country, including nearly 394,000 acres in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Under the Trump Administration, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Forest Service filed a proposal in August of this year to repeal the Roadless Rule, which could have devastating impacts on water quality, biodiversity, economic development and more for these regions.
The letter was also signed by U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.), and U.S. Representatives Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) and James Walkinshaw (Va.-11).
“This proposal would strip protections from approximately 84% of Virginia’s roadless areas, opening these lands to road construction, logging, and other industrial activities. The consequences for Virginia’s environment, economy, and public health would be severe, falling squarely on the families and communities we represent,” wrote the lawmakers. “With more roadless acres than any other state east of the Mississippi River, Virginia has an outsized stake in decisions regarding the Roadless Rule. Once lost, these ecosystems and the countless benefits they provide to clean air, clean water, and climate resilience cannot be easily restored, if at all.”
The letter outlines the risks this rescission would pose to Virginia by jeopardizing Virginia’s drinking water and ecosystems, threatening economic activity driven by recreation and tourism activities, increasing wildfire risk and straining public resources.
“For 25 years, the Roadless Rule has demonstrated that protecting America’s national forest lands is both effective and widely supported. Rescinding the Roadless Rule would ignore this overwhelming public consensus while undermining Virginia’s drinking water, biodiversity, local economies, and public safety,” the lawmakers concluded. “We urge the Department to withdraw this dangerous proposal and maintain the Roadless Area Conservation Rule of 2001 in its entirety.”
Read the full letter text here.
###
title: Vindman Stands Up for Roadless Rule to Protect Virginia’s Natural Resources, Local Economies

Davids Helps Launch Bipartisan Agenda to Cut Red Tape, Boost Local Economies, Lower Everyday Costs for Kansas Families
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids, a member of the Build America Caucus, helped announce the Build More Agenda — a major bipartisan policy platform designed to fix federal gridlock, strengthen local economies, create jobs, and lower everyday prices for hardworking families. By streamlining approval processes for energy, housing, and infrastructure, the roadmap directly targets the bureaucratic delays that slow down construction, drive up utility and housing costs, and prevent critical projects from getting built.
“Kansans don’t want D.C. talking points — they want lower utility bills, homes they can actually afford, and roads that aren't falling apart,” said Davids. “The problem isn't a lack of good ideas; it's the bureaucratic red tape slowing projects down for years. I’m supporting the bipartisan Build America Caucus’ new agenda because it would help cut through government gridlock and start building these projects now, not a decade from now.”
The bipartisan Build America Caucus was established to give pro-growth, pragmatic policymaking a permanent foothold in Congress. Over the past year, the Caucus helped negotiate and pass major bipartisan housing reform legislation and led bipartisan efforts to deliver permitting certainty for energy and infrastructure projects. Spanning seven core policy areas and over 60 legislative proposals, the Build More Agenda builds on those successes, establishing a comprehensive framework to spur domestic production, bring manufacturing home, create good-paying jobs, and lower the cost of living for Kansans.
“Not enough homes or energy, shortages of doctors and daycares, cures that take too long to reach patients, and infrastructure projects that drag on for decades. That’s what life in America looks like today because we’ve lost the ability to build the things we need,” said CaucusCo-Chairs Harder and Maloy. “We used to believe that America was the only place in the world where the boldest dreams could be realized, and we need a new politics of action to restore that national ambition and trust in government. The Build America Caucus was founded a little over a year ago with that goal in mind, and the Build More Agenda is our bipartisan roadmap to make growth and prosperity the cornerstone of American life once again.”
The solution to systemic dysfunction is to build our way to prosperity:
- Lowering Housing Costs: With the nation facing a shortage of five million homes, the agenda reduces regulatory delays, unlocks new project financing, and fully implements the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to expand homeownership options and bring housing prices back within reach for young families and working Kansans.
- Cutting Healthcare Costs & Red Tape: We spend more on healthcare than any other nation, but that care is unaffordable, inaccessible, and archaic. It reallocates physician training investments and slashes mountain-high administrative paperwork, so doctors spend time on patient outcomes rather than bureaucracy — cutting health system waste and lowering out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.
- Cheaper, Reliable Energy: Electricity rates have jumped more than 30 percent in recent years. The platform fixes broken permitting rules, so grid upgrades and energy projects don't take longer to approve than to actually construct, bringing down monthly electricity bills for households and small businesses.
- Building Infrastructure Faster: It establishes dedicated fast-track approvals and smarter federal funding models to ensure roads, bridges, and water systems are completed on schedule and under budget — ending costly construction delays that waste taxpayer dollars.
- Accelerating Medical Cures: America is losing its scientific edge because our scientists spend half their time on paperwork and research dollars aren’t geared toward modern discovery. It saves American medical researchers over one million hours a year spent on bureaucratic paperwork, redirecting resources toward breakthrough science and AI technology to accelerate cures for cancer, Alzheimer's, and chronic conditions.
- Expanding Childcare & Workforce Pipelines: It strengthens workforce development programs that directly match workers to high-paying local jobs, while expanding accessible childcare options so parents can stay in the workforce without breaking their household budgets.
- Modernizing Government to Save Taxpayer Dollars: It cuts redundant D.C. red tape, updates archaic federal technology systems, and builds a skill-focused public workforce that manages taxpayer funds efficiently.
Read the full agenda here. Read a section-by-section here.
“America knows how to build, we just have to get out of our own way and start doing it,” said Rep. Janelle Bynum (D-OR-05). “More homes, better roads and bridges, new technology, and good jobs – this agenda is about turning big ideas into things people can actually see and feel in their communities. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and help get it done.”
“Americans are tired of Washington making it harder and more expensive to build, innovate, and grow,” said Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA-01). “The Build More Agenda brings Republicans and Democrats together around commonsense solutions to cut red tape, lower costs, strengthen American energy, improve access to healthcare, and get critical projects built. I’m proud to work with the Build America Caucus to turn good ideas into real results for the American people.”
“The Build More Agenda reflects what we can accomplish when we work across the aisle to tackle challenges facing American families and businesses,” said Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12). “I’m proud to join my colleagues in the bipartisan Build America Caucus to advance practical solutions that cut unnecessary red tape, lower costs, and help America build faster and smarter. By modernizing infrastructure and creating opportunities for American workers and manufacturers, we can strengthen our economy, make taxpayer dollars go further, and deliver lasting results for our communities.”
“America used to pride itself on accomplishing big things — winning world wars, sending man to the moon, or discovering the next medical breakthrough,” said Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA-50). “Today, our challenges have not gone away, but our capacity to achieve great things has. Our constituents are counting on us to put politics aside and invest in our country’s future to make their lives better. The bipartisan Build More Agenda includes ways to do exactly that: lower costs, create good-paying jobs, strengthen communities, and restore America as a global leader in progress and innovation.”
“Folks in Western and Southern Colorado know how to build things, create jobs, and get things done,” said Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-03). “Too often, Washington just gets in the way. The Build More Agenda is about cutting unnecessary red tape so we can produce more American energy, build the housing and infrastructure our communities need, and bring down costs for working families. Republicans and Democrats aren’t going to agree on everything, but we ought to be able to agree that it shouldn’t take years of paperwork and bureaucracy to build something in this country.”
“A housing shortage is a tax on working people, and they pay it every month in rent,” said Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15). “For decades, we have piled on rules and caps that make it slower and costlier to build homes, and few places have paid a higher price than the Bronx. The surest way to bring down the cost of housing is to bring up the supply of housing. The Build More Agenda is built on that principle, because a pro-growth agenda is a pro–working class agenda. Progress should be measured not by how many projects we regulate but by how many we deliver.”
“Congress passed a housing abundance bill this term,” said Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04). “It's seriously debating a bipartisan energy abundance bill. Build America has momentum in its mission to lower prices by building more, faster & better – next up are unlocks to lower prices in medicine, transportation, and childcare.”
“As a senior member of the Housing, Transportation, and Urban Development Subcommittee, I’m proud to be a member of the bipartisan Build America Caucus. My constituents tell me every day they want to see their representatives in Washington take actions that will make their lives better – lower the cost of housing, healthcare, and energy,” said Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). “At a time of deep political division, we have the unique opportunity to come together as Democrats and Republicans to lower costs and solve the housing crisis.”
“Whether it’s rebuilding a bridge over I-95 in record time or passing landmark housing legislation, we know that government can still get things done, if rarely,” said Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT-04). “I’m in the Build America Caucus because this group of lawmakers fundamentally believes government needs to get things done — not as the exception, but as the rule. Our agenda reflects that belief, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to turn our group’s governing principle into law.”
What they’re saying about the Build More Agenda:
“For too long, we’ve treated a four-year college degree as the default path to a good career. The Build America Caucus’s push to get more apprenticeships and higher-quality workforce training programs off the ground is a critical step forward. If we want to build more in America, we need to make it easier for more Americans to learn how to do the building,” said Zach Boren, Senior Vice President, Apprenticeships for America.
“Getting lawmakers from both parties to agree on what's holding the country back is no easy feat, and we applaud the Build America Caucus for assembling a genuinely bipartisan coalition around these questions. BPC Action has long argued that the problems on this list — the cost of building housing, the time it takes to approve energy projects, and a broken childcare system — are solvable ones. We look forward to working with the caucus and its members as they move from agenda to legislation,” said Michele Stockwell, President, BPC Action.
“Through their work with the Build America Caucus, Reps. Harder and Maloy have asked how we can build more of what Americans actually need and answered it across housing, childcare, energy, and more. We applaud this effort and its goal to build 5 million homes, add millions more new childcare slots, modernize the energy grid, and get infrastructure built faster. This comprehensive plan demonstrates that pragmatic, actionable solutions can still be ambitious. This Agenda, written by a Democrat from California and a Republican from Utah, also shows the strength of abundance solutions in building coalitions. I urge Congress to take action on these solutions,” said Derek Kaufman, President, Inclusive Abundance Action.
“The Build More Agenda is an innovative, bipartisan framework for creating a more abundant future in America. The priorities laid out in this agenda have the potential to make a massive difference in areas from science and innovation to housing, transportation, and energy. For example, we were thrilled to see X-Labs and metascience units highlighted as vehicles to accelerate scientific discovery and increase the return on investment for R&D. Similarly, the Agenda’s focus on reducing land use regulations, building transit at lower cost, and achieving energy abundance is crucial for letting America build again and innovate in the world of atoms,” said Alec Stapp, CEO, Institute for Progress.
“For the past year, the Build America Caucus has worked across the aisle to notch key policy wins, making it easier, cheaper, and faster to build in America. The Build More Agenda strengthens that foundation, with over sixty policy proposals covering seven different policy areas. NAIA looks forward to working with the Caucus to back the builders,” said the New America Industrial Alliance.
“Finding childcare that's both affordable and meets their family’s specific needs is nearly impossible for far too many American parents. This agenda from the Build America Caucus offers an innovative menu of reforms to identify and remove the barriers to a more abundant supply of childcare options that fit family preferences without sacrificing quality or safety,” said Josh McCabe, Director of Social Policy, Niskanen Center.
“The housing affordability crisis is the result of many different factors, and solving it requires an all-hands-on-deck approach. The Build America Caucus agenda delivers this, with solutions that make it easier and less expensive to build housing. Critically, it does the same for transportation infrastructure and buses, because abundant housing and effective transportation options work together to connect people to economic opportunity,” said Kimberly Burnett, Deputy Director of Housing and Transportation, Niskanen Center.
“America's healthcare affordability crisis is fueled by a scarce and consolidated supply side of the market. This agenda from the Build America Caucus rightly targets solutions that increase care availability and cut out the incentives that drive consolidation,” said Lawson Mansell, Senior Health Policy Analyst, Niskanen Center.
“We applaud the Build America Caucus for its energy agenda focused on more power and lower bills. Getting transmission right and having neighboring regions connected is how you build a grid Americans can afford,” said Sarah Iskander, Government Affairs Manager, Niskanen Center.
“Whether it's housing, transportation, energy, or infrastructure, the federal government needs the tools and capacity to deliver for the American people. Meeting those demands requires a government whose systems and processes make delivery possible, and right now ours is not built to keep pace with changes in the workforce, technology, and the public's needs. The Build America Caucus's policy agenda takes this challenge head-on, rightly recognizing state capacity as essential to unlocking a prosperous future for our country,” said Max Stier, President and CEO, Partnership for Public Service.
“Getting the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into law was a major accomplishment, and Congressman Josh Harder and Congresswoman Celeste Maloy deserve a lot of credit for helping build the bipartisan coalition that got it done. Now we have to make it work. That means making sure HUD has the people and resources to implement the law well, while continuing the bipartisan work of finding the next set of solutions to get more homes built. The Build America Caucus’ Build More Agenda carries that work forward by keeping the focus on implementation and putting new ideas on the table. Up for Growth supports that direction, and we look forward to bringing our members and policy expertise to the work ahead,” said Mike Kingsella, Chief Executive Officer, Up for Growth.
