Washington, DC – Legislation led Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.) and Chairman of the U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) has passed the Senate unanimously and is headed to the President’s desk to be signed into law. The bipartisan, bicameral Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act is led by Senators Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.).
This bill directs the Department of Labor (DOL) to train its employees to identify human trafficking and refer suspected trafficking crimes to law enforcement. While DOL employees are on the ground conducting workplace inspections, they will be able to spot human trafficking behavior in real time.
“Human trafficking is a devastating crime that preys on the most vulnerable and robs victims of their freedom and dignity. We have a responsibility to ensure that those on the front lines in our communities and across the federal government have the tools necessary to help combat this crime and provide survivors with a path to safety. Strengthening training for Department of Labor employees is an important step toward recognizing the signs of human trafficking, protecting victims, and connecting them with the resources they need. I thank my colleagues for their support,” said McBath.
“Human trafficking is a national tragedy, and we need to do everything we can to stop it. This law will help ensure federal workers are equipped to spot the signs of human trafficking and refer suspected crimes to law enforcement. I’m proud this bill will be my fourth bill signed into law since I took office. This is a great example of the bipartisan work we can accomplish for the American people, and I look forward to the lives this law will help save,” said Husted.
“The fight against human trafficking should never be a partisan issue. Survivors and victims in Michigan and across the country are owed justice, accountability, and meaningful action to prevent these crimes from happening in the first place. Our bipartisan bill, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, provides the Department of Labor with the necessary framework to address these unthinkable crimes head-on. I am proud to have worked alongside my colleagues to get this important legislation passed and look forward to seeing it signed into law,” said Slotkin.
“Human trafficking can hide in plain sight, and this bill will help more people recognize the warning signs. I’m glad the Senate unanimously passed my bill and sent it to President Trump’s desk. By giving Department of Labor employees the right training, we can help identify victims sooner and get potential cases to law enforcement,” said Walberg.
McBath and Walberg introduced the companion bill to the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking in the House of Representatives, where it passed on March 3, 2026.
Full text of the bill is available here.
title: McBath Bill to Stop Human Trafficking Passes Senate, Heads to President’s Desk

EPA Implements Updated Cleanup Approach to Address Groundwater Contamination at Baird & McGuire Superfund Site
BOSTON (Oct. 5, 2026) – U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has selected an interim cleanup plan for groundwater at the Baird & McGuire Superfund Site located in Holbrook, Massachusetts.
After approximately 25 years of active site remediation, contaminant levels at the site have decreased, but groundwater remains impacted. In 2023, EPA began a Focused Feasibility Study (FFS) to evaluate additional cleanup options, and in 2026 selected a new cleanup approach based on the evaluations performed during the FFS.
"We've made real progress at the Baird & McGuire Site, but we need a different approach to address the groundwater contamination that remains," said EPA Regional Administrator Mark Sanborn. "This updated plan will move the cleanup forward and put us on a better path toward restoring the groundwater to drinking water standards."
The updated cleanup plan is based on past investigations, a pilot test, updated human health and ecological risk assessments, the 2026 FFS, and comments received on EPA's Proposed Plan during a 37-day public comment period. This cleanup plan is formally called an Interim Record of Decision Amendment for Operable Unit 1 (Groundwater and Surface Water).
EPA's interim cleanup plan includes:
- Treating polluted groundwater directly underground. This includes injecting sulfate into groundwater to help naturally break down harmful chemicals and to trap arsenic so it cannot spread.
- Additional cleanup options for reducing arsenic contamination may involve:
  - Cleaning groundwater using filters designed to remove arsenic, and/or
  - Underground treatment using air or a special barrier that helps capture arsenic until groundwater conditions improve.
EPA will continue to track groundwater and see whether pollution outside the treatment areas is decreasing enough for groundwater to achieve drinking water standards. EPA will also watch for any signs that contamination is spreading to the bedrock groundwater.
EPA will also continue to use groundwater use restrictions and engineered barriers that prevent people from using contaminated groundwater and keep activities from disturbing the pollution plume. These protective measures will remain in place until cleanup goals are met.
EPA estimates the interim cleanup plan including construction, operation, maintenance, and long-term monitoring will cost about $7.1 million.
More information
A copy of the interim cleanup plan, the Administrative Record supporting the cleanup plan, and other background information about the Baird & McGuire Superfund Site can be found at: www.epa.gov/superfund/baird
Background
The Baird & McGuire Superfund Site is located at 775 South Street in Holbrook, Massachusetts. Baird & McGuire Company, Inc. operated a chemical mixing and batching operation at the Site for approximately 71 years. Manufactured products included herbicides, pesticides, disinfectants, soaps, floor waxes, and solvents.
Operations from the facility resulted in contaminant releases to soil and groundwater. Site-related contamination includes various volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (VOCs and SVOCs), pesticides, and arsenic.
Record of Decision Administrative Record:  
Baird & McGuire Interim Record of Decision Amendment Administrative Record
title: EPA Implements Updated Cleanup Approach to Address Groundwater Contamination at Baird & McGuire Superfund Site

SEC Coordinates with Global Financial Regulators to Raise Fraud Awareness During World Investor Week
Washington D.C., Oct. 5, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission, in coordination with other U.S. and global financial regulators, today issued a joint investor bulletin as part of World Investor Week (WIW). The bulletin encourages investors to be resilient in changing economic conditions and to be vigilant in the face of rising relationship investment and impersonation scams.
World Investor Week is a global effort by the International Organization of Securities Commissions to bring together regulators across six continents to raise awareness about the importance of investor education and investor protection. This year marks WIW’s tenth anniversary. The SEC, coordinating U.S. efforts, worked with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Securities Investor Protection Corporation, National Futures Association, and North American Securities Administrators Association to issue the joint Investor Bulletin.
“Investor protection is a core tenet of the SEC’s mission, and World Investor Week provides another important opportunity for U.S. financial regulators and international counterparts to raise awareness together and encourage investor resilience across the globe,” said SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins. “This week, as always, I urge investors to take advantage of the resources on the SEC’s Investor.gov website and to remain vigilant against potential scams.”
“Investors can use the principles of resiliency that the SEC and our partners highlight this week to help protect themselves against fraud and weather market volatility,” said John Moses, Director of the SEC’s Office of Investor Education and Assistance. “We encourage investors to visit Investor.gov, which provides free, accurate, unbiased information and financial planning tools to help individuals invest wisely and better protect themselves against investment fraud.”
The SEC’s WIW page highlights resources on investor education and protection.
###
Last Reviewed or Updated: Oct. 5, 2026
title: SEC Coordinates with Global Financial Regulators to Raise Fraud Awareness During World Investor Week

New Regulations Make It Easier to Find, Compare, and Report Healthcare Pricing and Coverage Information
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 5, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), today announced that Americans will have access to more reliable, accessible, and actionable information about what their health coverage includes and what they are likely to pay before receiving care under new regulations that strengthen federal healthcare price transparency requirements. The actions taken today to create a more transparent healthcare marketplace also ensure employers can make more informed decisions; researchers can better understand healthcare markets; and innovators can build better tools.
“Americans should know what their healthcare will cost before they receive it,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “President Trump directed us to bring real price transparency to healthcare, and HHS is delivering. These rules give patients clearer, more reliable information to compare costs, understand their coverage, and make informed decisions before they receive care.”
“Greater transparency drives competition, reduces price disparities, and helps lower healthcare costs, a key priority for the Trump Administration,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “At the heart of this rule is a simple idea: People should know what their health insurance will cover and what they will need to pay before receiving medical care, not after the bill arrives.”
Updates to the Transparency in Coverage (TiC) rules, finalized today by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), in partnership with the Departments of Labor and the Treasury (the Departments), build on the historic health care price transparency rules established during President Trump’s first term.
The final rules improve the underlying healthcare pricing data by reducing duplicative and unnecessary information, providing more context about in-network prices, increasing available out-of-network pricing information, and strengthening accountability for the completeness and accuracy of published data. Reporting frequency for pricing information will change from monthly to quarterly, maintaining meaningful transparency while lowering administrative burden.
The rules also require group health plans and health insurance issuers to provide consumers with personalized cost-sharing information by phone, in addition to existing online tools.
These improvements will help technology developers build better consumer tools, give consumers more reliable information when comparing costs before receiving care, and enable employers and researchers to better analyze healthcare markets, all of which will help drive competition across the healthcare industry.
“Transparency is a pillar of the Trump Administration’s efforts to drive better value in healthcare,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling, “Today’s final rules will enhance the Transparency in Coverage (TiC) files already in existence, giving workers and employers alike a clearer view of their true healthcare costs.”
“Healthcare price transparency is common sense,” said FTC Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson. “But only President Donald Trump, with assists from Secretary Kennedy, Secretary Sonderling and Dr. Oz, decided to actually make it happen. Today’s announcements follow a basic but important principle: Consumers should always have as much information as possible.”
“Under President Trump’s leadership, this Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen transparency and accountability across America’s healthcare system,” said Deputy Secretary of the Treasury Francis Brooke. “This rule helps improve the standardization, accuracy, and accessibility of pricing disclosures to put Americans and their families in a better position to understand the cost of their health care coverage and make informed decisions about their own care.”
The Departments plan to begin development of the initial schema for the Prescription Drug File in November 2026 and will finalize it on or around May 2027. Plans and issuers will be expected to publish their Prescription Drug Files using this schema starting in December 2027 and monthly thereafter.
Today’s announcement builds on the original TiC regulations established during President Trump’s first term. This work allowed for continued refinement to TiC requirements that have improved the usability of pricing data, enabling developers to build more accurate tools for consumers, employers, researchers, and industry. Recent data have found that the top 25% of the most expensive healthcare service prices have dropped by 6.3% per year following the initial implementation of price transparency requirements on hospitals and health plans.
Today’s final rules support Executive Order 14221, Making America Healthy Again by Empowering Patients with Clear, Accurate, and Actionable Healthcare Pricing Information.
To view the final rules, visit: https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-20447/transparency-in-coverage
To read the CMS fact sheet, including implementation dates, visit: https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/transparency-coverage-final-rules-cms-9882-f
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

title: New Regulations Make It Easier to Find, Compare, and Report Healthcare Pricing and Coverage Information

Reps. Ramirez, Salinas Introduce Legislation to Require the Federal Government to Share Evidence with Local Law Enforcement in DHS Use-of-Force Incidents
Washington, DC – Recently, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee, and Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) introduced H.R.10698, the ICE Shootings Transparency Act, to provide local and state law enforcement agencies unfettered access to evidence in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer-involved shootings and other use of force incidents.
“DHS lies to avoid accountability. DHS agents use reckless and unlawful force, and then DHS issues public statements justifying the use of force that are repeatedly proven false or highly misleading,” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “That’s why I’m joining Rep. Salinas to require DHS and the Attorney General to share evidence related to shootings by ICE and CBP officers with local law enforcement agencies to carry out investigations. We will not stop until we have justice for every person who was killed or harmed at the hands of DHS agents. We will reimagine true safety, abolish ICE, dismantle DHS, and hold all perpetrators accountable.”
“When an ICE or CBP agent kills or injures someone in our community, transparency needs to be the bare minimum,” said Rep. Salinas. “Since the start of the second Trump Administration, the federal government has often refused to provide local law enforcement with critical evidence in shootings and other use-of-force incidents involving ICE and CBP officers. My bill would ensure that when these incidents occur, state and local law enforcement agencies would have unrestricted access to this evidence to deliver full justice to victims and their families.”
In January 2026, when ICE killed Renee Good, Minnesota’s Bureau of Criminal Apprehension was tapped to conduct a joint investigation with the FBI. However, shortly after the announcement, the state agency said that they had been kicked out of the investigation, leaving the investigation in the hands of the Trump Administration. Several months later, ICE agents killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas and have also refused to work with state and local law enforcement. The administration’s actions have included blocking local and state law enforcement officials from accessing investigatory materials, such as Salgado Araujo’s work van and the scene of the incident.
The members introduced the ICE Shootings Transparency Act to address issues that some local agencies and prosecutors have encountered with ICE and CBP officers-involved shootings that result in the injury or death of a civilian. Their bill would require the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Attorney General to share evidence on an ongoing basis with appropriate local law enforcement agencies related to shootings by ICE and CBP officers that injure or kill someone.
Additionally, this bill would require DHS and the Attorney General to provide access to the location of the incident to state and local law enforcement agencies with jurisdiction over the area to carry out regular investigative functions.
The ICE Shootings Transparency Act is cosponsored by Reps. Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-At Large), Jim Costa (CA-21), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Steven Horsford (NV-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), and Sylvia Garcia (TX-29).
The legislation is endorsed by the National Immigration Law Center (NILC).
 
BACKGROUND:
Congresswoman Ramirez has led the calls for accountability of DHS and its leadership. In September 2026, Ramirez stood with Illinois public officials, civil society, and community members to announce the Reimagining Safety Act. The landmark community-led legislation would create a new human- and community-centered federal department that promotes collective safety, repeal the authorities that give the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) its power, and redirect DHS funds to programs that working families rely on. Additionally:
- In January 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez and Congressman Seth Magaziner (RI-02) announced the DHS Use of Force Oversight Act to statutorily require a DHS policy on the use of force and de-escalation by agents.
- In January 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez led 71 members of Congress to demand the House Committee on the Judiciary immediately start investigation hearings on Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem’s unlawful and potentially impeachable actions.
- In January 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez introduced the Melt ICE Act to end DHS’s funding to detain or monitor immigrants, disrupt immigration enforcement, and redirect funding toward wrap-around services for communities affected by immigration enforcement.
- In July 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez and Congressman Takano (CA-39) launched an investigation into reports that VA delayed processing ICE medical reimbursement claims.
- In August 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez led 28 colleagues in opening an investigation into a new data-sharing agreement between TSA and ICE that has resulted in a spike in immigration enforcement activities at airports across the country.
- In September 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez and Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) introduced the No Shock Act to ban the use of “shock gloves” by ICE.
- In September 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez and Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) led 22 colleagues in opening an investigation into the fraud, corruption, and coercion of DHS’s “Project Homecoming.”
- In September 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez led 8 members of the Illinois Congressional delegation in requesting that the Office of the Inspector General investigate Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) agents for a pattern of misconduct, unconstitutional uses of force, and potential criminal violations during immigration enforcement operations, including “Operation Midway Blitz.”
- In September 2026, Congresswoman Ramirez joined Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11) and Ranking Member Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02) to introduce the CISA Force Structure Assessment Act.
title: Reps. Ramirez, Salinas Introduce Legislation to Require the Federal Government to Share Evidence with Local Law Enforcement in DHS Use-of-Force Incidents

Rep. Kelly and Rep. Latimer Introduce Food Access in Community Health Centers Act of 2026
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Congresswoman Robin Kelly (D-IL) and U.S. Congressman George Latimer (D-NY) introduced the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act of 2026, a bill to create and expand partnerships between community health centers and emergency feeding operations to provide access to food at these centers.
In the face of unprecedented cuts to SNAP and Medicaid, emergency feeding operations and community health centers have provided critical support to countless Americans. Partnerships between community health centers and emergency feeding operations have enabled underserved populations to reduce food insecurity. It is well established that access to food is critical to primary health. As Americans continue to struggle with access to food and healthcare, partnerships between organizations like these are vital tools to alleviate these crises. This bill would enable these existing partnerships to be expanded and for new ones to be created.
Congresswoman Kelly and Congressman Latimer previously championed this cause by sending a letter to the leadership of the Labor-HHS-Education Appropriations subcommittee urging them to include report language in the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bill encouraging the expansion of partnerships between emergency feeding operations and community health centers.
Congresswoman Kelly stated, “What makes us sick, or keeps us well, starts long before we ever walk into a doctor's office. Over 40 million Americans have limited access to affordable groceries, and the Big, Ugly Law has now gutted SNAP and Medicaid on top of that. Community health centers and emergency feeding operations are already stepping up. This bill helps them do it together, through on-site food pantries and mobile distribution, so patients can get both the care and the healthy food they need. I'm proud to partner with Congressman Latimer to ensure that everyone has access to nutritious food, no matter their zip code.”
Congressman Latimer stated, “I am proud to introduce this critical legislation alongside Congresswoman Robin Kelly at a time when far too many across our country are facing food insecurity and the rising cost of living. Food access is directly linked to health outcomes, and this bill aims to address the food insecurity that patients experience when seeking essential care. I am grateful to the national, statewide, and local partners who stand alongside us to ensure patients receive the comprehensive care. I look forward to working alongside our stakeholders as we work towards passing this necessary legislation.”
Judith Watson, RN BSN MPH, HD, CEO of Westchester Community Health Center, stated, “Congressman Latimer came to our health centers, met our staff and patients, and saw firsthand how food insecurity affects our community. Then he did something about it. That is what leadership looks like, and it is truly inspiring. Hunger is a pressing issue that impacts the health of our community, including our patients and many neighbors who are not our patients. You cannot manage diabetes or high blood pressure without access to healthy food. Our partnership with Feeding Westchester has shown what a health center and a food bank can do together. We are grateful to Congressman Latimer and Congresswoman Kelly for introducing the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act, which would help health centers across the country bring nutritious food to their communities.”
Kristine Borok, President and CEO of Feeding Westchester, stated, “At Feeding Westchester, we believe food is a fundamental right, and access to nutritious food is fundamental to our health. When people lack reliable access to nutritious food, chronic conditions become harder to manage, preventable health problems escalate, and too often the result is a medical crisis. Food as Medicine addresses this by recognizing that our food and healthcare system cannot operate in isolation. We are grateful to Congressman Latimer, who saw this work firsthand at our Food as Medicine partner sites and responded with the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act. This bill would create a grant program to help community health centers provide food pantry access to their patients, bringing nutritious food to the very places people go for care.”
Rose Duhan, President and CEO of the Community Health Care Association of New York State, stated, “Community health centers see every day how food insecurity can affect a patient’s health and make chronic conditions harder to manage. By bringing health centers and local food providers together, the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act would make it easier for patients to access both the care and the resources they need in their communities. Good health starts with having access to the basics, and CHCANYS appreciates Representatives Latimer and Kelly for recognizing the important connection between food access and health.”
Jerome Nathaniel, Director of Policy and Government Relations at City Harvest, stated, “Food security and health are directly connected, which is why community health centers and food access organizations should be collaborating more deeply, especially at a moment when rates of food insecurity are staggeringly high. The Food Access in Community Health Centers Act would help bring those systems together, making it easier for organizations like City Harvest to make nutritious food more accessible where people already receive trusted health care and helping address food insecurity as part of supporting healthier communities.”
Anne Kauffman Nolon, MPH, CEO of Sun River Health, stated, “As New York's largest community health center network, we know firsthand that no prescription can make up for an empty refrigerator. The Food Access in Community Health Centers Act would help health centers and food banks provide food right where patients receive care. With federal SNAP cuts taking hold, this model has never mattered more. We are proud to support it and grateful to Congressman Latimer for recognizing that food access is health care.”
Leslie Gordon, President and CEO of Food Bank For NYC, stated, “We applaud Representatives Latimer and Kelly for introducing the Food Access in Community Health Centers Act and are proud to join the bill’s coalition of supporters. By investing in partnerships between community health centers and food banks, this legislation recognizes a simple truth: access to nutritious food is essential to good health. This grant program would help deliver meaningful support to families while strengthening the community infrastructure they already trust and rely on.”
The Food Access in Community Health Centers Act of 2026:
●    Directs the HHS Secretary to establish a grant program to facilitate food access in CHCs.
●    Enables emergency feeding operations and CHCs to apply jointly for these grants.
●    Eligibility for these grants includes projects that involve creating or expanding a physical space in or adjacent to a CHC (e.g., an on-site food pantry or a mobile distribution vehicle) that assists with providing access to food.
●    Specifies the maximum award per partnership as $500,000.
●    Requires the HHS Secretary to report on 1) the effectiveness of the program, 2) the impact of the program on the food insecurity of patients of community health centers, and 3) recommendations to improve the program.
The bill has been endorsed by City Harvest, Community Health Care Association of New York State (CHCANYS), Feeding America, Feeding Westchester, Food Bank for NYC, Food Bank of the Southern Tier, Greater Chicago Food Depository, Sun River Health, and Westchester Community Health Center.

Today, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) and the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) sent a joint letter to all state Attorneys General reaffirming the Trump Administration’s commitment to protecting parental rights. The letter puts Attorneys General on notice that under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), parents have the right to know and be informed of the most sensitive and personal information pertaining to their children. ED and DOJ also announced a new enforcement action against the Los Angeles Unified School District in California (LAUSD) for policies that require staff to keep sensitive information hidden from parents.
The Trump Administration’s message is clear: the era of silencing, harassing, and targeting parents is over, and their rights under federal law are non-negotiable. Five years ago, the Biden Administration weaponized the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to investigate parents who attended school board meetings, including setting up a dedicated snitch-line. The infamous October 4th memorandum came after the Biden White House coordinated with the National School Boards Association to label parents as “domestic terrorists.” Today’s letter and enforcement action also come on the same day the DOJ’s Weaponization Working Group will release its report exposing the memorandum’s creation.
“Under the Biden Administration, parents were the enemy. They were labeled as terrorists, targeted, and investigated by a government weaponized against them,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “That era is over. The Trump Administration is acting with unprecedented energy and purpose to restore parents’ natural rights as the primary protectors of their children. The Department of Education is committed to fully enforcing FERPA and PPRA. We are grateful to the Department of Justice for partnering with us to hold rogue schools accountable, including the Los Angeles Unified School District, and urge all state Attorneys General to work with us in upholding the letter of the law.”
“Parents are children’s natural providers and protectors,” said Harmeet K. Dhillon, Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights. “The Biden-Harris DOJ labeled concerned parents as threats for exercising their right to know what was happening at their kids’ schools. This Civil Rights Division stands with parents, and we will continue to partner with the Department of Education to enforce parents’ rights under federal law.”
Additionally, ED partnered with DOJ to take enforcement action against LAUSD for policies that violate FERPA and PPRA. These policies direct district employees to “privately ask the student how they want to be referred to when communicating with parents/legal guardians” and to keep a students’ self-professed “gender identity” “private” or “confidential,” including from parents. LAUSD’s parental secrecy policies have allowed students to make life-altering decisions in secret, unbeknownst to their parents.
Compare this to the Biden Administration that opened several investigations into parents, some of which were led by the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division and Weapons of Mass Destruction Directorate. One FBI field office interviewed a mother because she was a member of Moms for Liberty, which it disparaged as a “right wing mom’s group.” Another FBI tip launched an investigation into a father opposed to mask mandates because he “fit the profile of an insurrectionist.”
Background:
FERPA and PPRA are federal privacy laws enforced by the Department's SPPO. FERPA protects the privacy of students’ education records and safeguards parents’ rights to access their children’s education records, seek amendments to those records, and exercise control over the disclosure of personally identifiable information. PPRA requires schools to provide notification and attain written parental consent when conducting surveys, analyses, or evaluations asking students for certain sensitive and private information such as sex behaviors and attitudes, religious beliefs, mental and psychological problems.
These statutory obligations were emphasized and clarified in the SPPO’s recent Dear Colleague Letters issued in March 2025 and August 2026.
In June 2026, the Department partnered with DOJ to provide more responsive and coordinated enforcement of our nation’s parental and civil rights laws with the goal of continuing investigations uninterrupted while also cutting red tape and expediting enforcement.
title: U.S. Department of Education and U.S. Department of Justice Reaffirm Parents Are Not Terrorists and Have the Right to Direct their Children’s Education

U.S. Department of Justice Obtains Settlement on Behalf of National Guard Medic for Alleged Employment Discrimination by Texas Memory Care Facility
A federal judge in Austin has approved a settlement between the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, on behalf of Army National Guard Combat Medic Specialist Maria Opara, and Texas-based University Village Memory Care (UVMC) to resolve allegations that UVMC violated the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act of 1994 (USERRA). The lawsuit arises from UVMC’s demotion, and ultimate termination, of Specialist Opara because she went on leave to fulfill military orders.
“It is unlawful to demote a servicemember because of her service in the National Guard, and also unlawful to terminate a servicemember because she refused to accept such a demotion,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “The Department is proud to vindicate servicemembers’ rights under USERRA and will continue to ensure that they can serve our country without fear of being demoted or losing their civilian jobs because of their service.”
“So many of our servicemembers call the Western District of Texas home, so we do all we can to protect their rights while they are out protecting our freedoms,” said U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. “Our servicemembers — the men and women who, along with their families, sacrifice so much to protect our nation and its citizens — can be confident the Justice Department will hold employers accountable for unlawful acts committed against our soldiers, sailors, airmen and Marines.”
The settlement agreement resolves Specialist Opara’s claim that UVMC violated USERRA when it demoted or attempted to demote her from her position as a night shift supervisor to a lower paying position because of her military service. The settlement also resolves Opara’s claim that UVMC violated USERRA when it terminated her employment when she refused to accept the forced demotion. The settlement includes monetary relief in the amount of $15,000 to Specialist Opara and requires UVMC to update its policies and procedures regarding employees’ USERRA rights, including training all UVMC employees on those updated policies and procedures.
USERRA protects the right of uniformed servicemembers to reemployment in their civilian jobs following absences due to military service obligations and provides that servicemembers shall not be discriminated against because of their military obligations. The Justice Department prioritizes the enforcement of servicemembers’ rights under USERRA. Additional information about USERRA can be found on the Justice Department’s website at www.justice.gov/servicemembers as well as on the Department of Labor’s website at www.dol.gov/vets/programs/userra.
title: U.S. Department of Justice Obtains Settlement on Behalf of National Guard Medic for Alleged Employment Discrimination by Texas Memory Care Facility

FAIRFAX, VA — Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25) and members of Virginia’s Democratic congressional delegation held a public shadow hearing Thursday in Fairfax to confront the Trump Administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Panelists outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation, and misinformation. 
The hearing examined the Administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. The experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
In his remarks and responses to lawmakers, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay outlined safeguards against duplicate voting, secured ballot drop boxes and the county’s use of paper ballots and scanners without internet connectivity. The discussion emphasized that protecting election integrity and ensuring access to the ballot go hand in hand.
“Where the Trump Administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.” 
"In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans’ right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.” 
"Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote," said Congressman Bobby Scott, Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. "Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone's right to participate in our elections, and this hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight."
“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.” 
“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Vindman. “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.” 
“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.
The panel included Chairman McKay; Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause; Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP; and Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States.
The experts urged voters to check their registration, make a plan to vote and consult trusted election officials.
View photo gallery here. 
Watch the full hearing: C-SPAN.

title: Walkinshaw, Morelle and Virginia Democrats Fight Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting, Pledge to Protect Every Vote

“Hometown Heroes!” Suozzi Honors Local Police Officers at 7th Hometown Heroes Ceremony
      Image    
Suozzi continues tradition of recognizing local law enforcement officers who have displayed exemplary heroism in service to their communities
This marks the seventh Hometown Heroes ceremony Suozzi has held to recognize and thank local police officers
Glen Cove, NY – Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today hosted his seventh “Hometown Heroes” ceremony, continuing a tradition he began to recognize, honor, and thank local law enforcement officers who have demonstrated extraordinary courage and heroism in the line of duty. At this year’s ceremony, held outside the Glen Cove Police Department, Suozzi honored nine officers across five police departments. He recognized five of the officers for protecting victims and apprehending their violent offenders, one for saving a life by de-escalating a mental health crisis, one for saving a child’s life, one for his vigilance and professionalism in removing an illegal firearm, and one for dedicating 20 years to the force, including 15 years handling domestic violence cases.
The nine recognized officers were from the Nassau County Police Department, Glen Cove Police Department, Brookville Police Department, and three precincts of the New York City Police Department: the 105th, 109th, 111th. Suozzi shared the stories of the officers’ heroic actions and the lives they helped save while serving their communities.
“I have made it a tradition to hold these Hometown Heroes ceremonies because the men and women who protect our communities every day deserve our support and our thanks,” said Suozzi. “Police officers have one of the toughest jobs there is. They run toward danger when the rest of us are running away, and too often the extraordinary things they do every day go unnoticed.”
“These Hometown Heroes represent the very best of law enforcement. Their courage, quick thinking, and willingness to put themselves at risk to help others saved lives. I am proud that this is now the seventh time we have come together to recognize these remarkable officers and, most importantly, to say: thank you for keeping us safe.”
Suozzi began his Hometown Heroes tradition to shine a spotlight on the often-unheralded acts of courage performed by local law enforcement officers and to underscore his longstanding support for the men and women who serve in local police departments. This year’s event marks the seventh Hometown Heroes ceremony Suozzi has hosted.
This year’s honorees include officers from the Nassau County Police Department 6th Precinct, Glen Cove Police Department, Brookville Police Department, and three precincts of the New York City Police Department: the 105th, 109th, 111th.
Suozzi presented each officer with an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol and a Congressional citation recognizing their service and heroism.
The following officers were honored by Suozzi at this year’s ceremony:
Police Officers Terrell Carter-Ballier and Matthew Russo 
Sixth Precinct 
Nassau County  
On April 25, 2026, the Sixth Precinct received a call from a woman screaming for help on an open line and a man yelling, “Shut up or I will keep choking you” and “I will kill both of us.” Upon arriving on the scene, Officer Russo heard screams coming from inside the locked house and kicked open the front door. He and Officer Carter-Ballier rescued the victim as she ran up the stairs away from the subject, her estranged husband. She told the officers that he was carrying a rope and a metal baton. The officers found him in the basement holding a lawn stake with 6-inch-long prongs to his chest, which he refused to drop. Both officers initially drew their firearms due to the confined space and the unstable subject who could have charged them with the stake, and tried for several minutes to deescalate the situation by working to get him to drop the stake. Both officers then put away their weapons, despite the precarious situation, in an attempt to gain compliance with the subject.   
Officer Russo continued speaking to the subject while Officer Carter-Ballier drew his taser. The subject threatened to take his life and tried to hide in a closet that was partially open. He continued to disobey commands and began stabbing himself in the stomach. At the appropriate time, Officer Carter-Ballier deployed his taser, causing the subject to fall backwards away from the object. 
Officers Russo and Carter-Ballier were able to make entry into the room, secure the lawn stake, and take the subject into custody after a struggle. Their apprehended the subject without major injury and potentially saved the victim’s life. 
Police Officers Sara Palagonia, Nicholas Zanfardino, and Jonathan Pesce 
105th Precinct 
New York Police Department 
On Wednesday, March 25, 2026, Officers Palagonia, Zanfardino and Pesce were conducting daily patrols in the 105th. They responded to a 9-1-1 call of an assault with a knife. Upon arrival, the officers discovered the victim inside, bleeding heavily from multiple stab wounds all over his body. Officer Pesce immediately assessed the victim’s condition and rendered first aid by applying direct pressure to the wounds and applying a chest seal. He monitored the victim’s responsiveness until EMS arrived. Due to the officer’s quick actions and effective control of the bleeding, the victim was stabilized enough for transport, which was instrumental in saving his life.   
Officers Palagonia and Zanfardino did a thorough canvas and were able to successfully apprehend a male suspect at the corner of 115th Road and 229th Street. The suspect was in possession of a large kitchen knife with blood on the blade. The perpetrator was identified and arrested. 
Officers Palagonia, Zanfardino and Pesce are being recognized for their quick response, teamwork, and actions that contributed both to saving the victim’s life and apprehending the individual responsible. 
Police Officer Liang Lin 
109th Precinct 
New York Police Department 
On April 11, 2026 at approximately 5:30 pm, NYPD responded to a report of a woman threatening to jump off of a building. Upon arrival, Officer Lin went up to the roof of the building. The woman was on the ledge. Without hesitation, Officer Lin took swift and decisive action, safely pulling her off the ledge. He then secured the woman and made sure she was placed in custody so she could get the care she needed. 
Officer Lin is being recognized for his decisive action, saving a life and preventing a potential tragedy.
Detective Stephanie Tringali 
111th Precinct 
New York Police Department 
Detective Stephanie Tringali is being honored today for 20 years of dedicated service in the New York Police Department. Being in law enforcement is no ordinary career: it requires thousands of shifts, countless sacrifices, missed birthdays, birthdays, endless paperwork, and an unwavering commitment to keeping the peace.  
Detective Tringali started her career in the 115th Precinct. After about a year, she was assigned to the 111th Precinct, and for the past 15 years, has proudly worked in the Domestic Violence Unit, a position that not many could handle.
Domestic violence investigations are some of the most complex, emotionally exhausting, and critical calls handled by a police department. It takes a unique kind of person to step into the center of someone else's darkest moments day after day. Officers in the Domestic Violence Unit  don't just see the aftermath of a crime; they see people at the absolute lowest, most vulnerable moments of their lives. It takes a heavy toll for everyone involved. It requires a rare combination of an iron stomach and a massive heart. 
For the last decade and a half, Detective Tringali has been the voice for those who felt silenced. She has developed strong cases, brought offenders to justice and literally saved lives. Detective Tringali has been the shield for people who didn't think anyone was left to fight for them. She has guided survivors from fear to a place of safety, dignity, and hope. She is an irreplaceable asset to the 111th Precinct.  
Detective Vasilios “Billy” Rabie 
Brookville Police Department 
On March 14, while on routine patrol, Detective Vasilios Rabie observed a white 2023 Dodge Charger traveling northbound on Route 107 at a speed well above the posted limit and operating in an unsafe manner. After initiating a traffic stop, Detective Rabie encountered the driver, who was unable to produce a valid driver’s license. 
During the course of the investigation, the officer observed what appeared to be a black Glock-style handgun inside the vehicle’s glove compartment. The car’s operator was immiediately directed away from the weapon and safely detained. The firearm was later determined to be an imitation BB pistol designed to closesly resemble a real handgun.
Continuing the investigation and subsequent inventory search of the vehicle, the officer recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .38 Special revolver along with additional ammunition concealed inside. 
Through careful observation, sound judgement and adherence to officer safety tactics, this incident was resolved without injury and resulted in the recovery of an illegally possessed loaded firearm. Detective Rabie and the Brookville Police Department are being recognized for the detective’s professionalism, vigilance and commitment to public safety.
Sergeant Peter Michaleas 
Glen Cove Police Department 
On June 24, 2026, police responded to a 9-1-1 call from two 12-year-old boys reporting that their friend had severely cut his arm on a glass door. Sergeant Peter Michaleas was the first officer to arrive and immediately took command of a tense scene.   
While playing, the child had accidently thrust his arm through a glass windowpane, severing a major artery. Recognizing the severe blood loss and impending shock, Sgt. Michaeleas maintained complete composure, reassuring the terrified youth that help was here and their friend would be okay. Taking decisive, life-saving actions, Stg. Michaleas applied a tourniquet to halt the arterial bleeding and stabilized the child. He then coordinated aviation support to medevac the boy to the nearest trauma center for emergency treatment.   
Sgt. Michaleas’ leadership, calm demeanor under pressure, and immediate medical intervention directly saved the life of a child.
###
title: “Hometown Heroes!” Suozzi Honors Local Police Officers at 7th Hometown Heroes Ceremony

FDIC Issues List of Banks Examined for CRA Compliance
WASHINGTON—The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) today issued its list of state nonmember banks recently evaluated for compliance with the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA). The list covers evaluation ratings that the FDIC assigned to institutions in July 2026.
The CRA is a 1977 law that requires the FDIC to assess a bank’s record of meeting the credit needs of its entire community, including those of low- and moderate-income neighborhoods, consistent with safe and sound operations. As part of the Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery, and Enforcement Act of 1989 (FIRREA), Congress mandated the public disclosure of an evaluation and rating for each bank or thrift that undergoes a CRA examination on or after July 1, 1990.
You may obtain a consolidated list of all state nonmember banks whose evaluations have been made publicly available since July 1, 1990, including the rating for each bank, or obtain a hard copy from FDIC's Public Information Center, 3501 Fairfax Drive, Room E-1002, Arlington, VA 22226 (877-275-3342 or 703-562-2200).
A copy of an individual bank's CRA evaluation is available directly from the bank, which is required by law to make the material available upon request, or from the FDIC's Public Information Center.
title: FDIC Issues List of Banks Examined for CRA Compliance

WA Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
PNW records devastating 2026 wildfire season – Members voice concern USFS is misusing taxpayer funds by directing resources outside of USFS scope and mission
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congresswoman Emily Randall (D, WA-06), and Representatives Kim Schrier, M.D. (D, WA-08), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.
This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. As of October 5, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.
“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.
The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.
The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.
The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:
Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:
- Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?
- Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?
- To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.
- Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.
- What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?
- What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?
- Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?
- Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?
The full text of the letter is available HERE.

text:
Weaponization Working Group Releases Report on Garland Memo That Chilled Parental Rights and Warned Parents Could Be Domestic Terrorists
Today, the Justice Department’s Weaponization Working Group issued a report detailing how Biden Administration officials at the Department of Justice explored avenues to prosecute parents and protestors who spoke to school boards and school officials during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Today’s report focuses on the production and circulation of an October 4, 2021 memorandum sent from Attorney General Merrick Garland to the Director of the FBI, the Assistant Attorney General for the Criminal Division, the Director of the Executive Office for U.S. Attorneys, and United States Attorneys.
On January 20, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14147 to eliminate the political weaponization of federal agencies. To many Americans, Attorney General Garland’s memo embodied the misuse and weaponization of government power. This report fulfills the February 2, 2025 directive from Attorney General Pam Bondi to review the Memo and the report ordered by the President in EO 14147.
The report details how, despite being presented with very little evidence of actual violence or violent threats against school administrators and at school board meetings, Garland arrived at a memo which claimed, “in recent months, there has been a disturbing spike in harassment, intimidation, and threats of violence.”
The Working Group’s report makes clear that the ideological inspiration for the October 4, 2021 memo was a September 29, 2021 letter from the National School Boards Association to President Joe Biden in which the organization urged the federal government to consider that “these heinous actions” “could be equivalent to a form of domestic terrorism and hate crimes.”
The Working Group officially acknowledges what many Americans already assumed: that as Biden Administration actions chilled the exercise of parental and free speech rights, parents who lawfully exercised their parental rights and freedom of speech were often targeted by members of the educational establishment.
Among the most egregious findings, exhibits show that individuals in the Biden White House and Attorney General Garland’s advisors wanted to involve federal law enforcement and prosecutors in matters involving parents and school boards. Further, the Memo established a task force to find federal enforcement options for investigating and prosecuting parents and the FBI opened 25 “Guardian assessments” on parents. One FBI whistleblower disclosed that a mother was investigated because she “is a gun owner” and belonged to a “right-wing mom’s group.”
After thoroughly reviewing internal communications and investigative records, the Working Group found that more than a dozen DOJ and FBI personnel raised concerns with the Memo and its directive, including:
- “Stupid, stupid, stupid”
- “they might as well rename the damn thing the Anti-MAGA Task Force”
- “ridiculous,”
- “challenging from a First Amendment perspective”
- “potentially dangerous ground”
- “horrible”
- “confusing”
- “look[s] political”
- “a partisan exercise aimed at those who do not support the Administration”
- Would “tarnish reputation as an apolitical law enforcer”
- “very messy and political”
- “nothing remotely federal”
Despite internal pushback, emails show Attorney General Garland issued the Memo, influenced by White House officials. The Working Group confirms the Memo was the product of pressure exerted by the White House and wrongly weaponized the Department of Justice against parents.
The Trump Administration and Attorney General Todd Blanche have made securing parental and First Amendment rights a top priority. In addition to the investigative Report, the Department of Justice is taking the following steps:
- Parents and other participants at school board meetings who became the subject or target of an FBI Guardian assessment as a result of the Garland Memorandum will be offered the opportunity to review the Guardian.
- A disclaimer will be added to Guardian assessments associated with the Garland Memorandum. The majority of these Guardian assessments have been closed or discontinued, but this disclaimer will note that the Garland Memorandum raised serious constitutional concerns, and so any Guardian assessment resulting from it should be read with caution.
- The Department will review the files of anyone who was investigated under the Garland Memorandum to determine if their constitutional rights were violated. To the extent such a violation is found, the Department will issue a formal apology and institute internal controls as necessary to prevent repeating the violation.
- Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services, the Department is partnering with the National Association of School Resource Officers and awarding them $1.5 million to develop and deliver a series of training and technical assistance directly to our nation’s school resource officers. The goal of this grant is to increase the organization’s capacity to inform school employees regarding the rights of parents in our primary and secondary educational system.
- Through the Office of Justice Programs, the Department is prioritizing additional funding to provide resources and training to schoolteachers and staff about the First Amendment rights of parents and the rights of parents to direct and guide the upbringing and education of their children.
This report follows letters sent earlier today by Department of Justice and Department of Education leadership to all 50 state attorneys general on parental rights. The letters can be viewed here.
The Justice Department remains committed to defending Constitutionally protected civil liberties, especially the First Amendment rights of all Americans. Individuals with concerns about unconstitutional conduct are encouraged to come forward; the Department will evaluate such matters without fear or favor.
Read the full report here.
Press Release Number: 26-1138
title: Weaponization Working Group Releases Report on Garland Memo That Chilled Parental Rights and Warned Parents Could Be Domestic Terrorists

Blair: New SNAP Cut Hits Georgia Families as 5 Million Americans Have Already Lost Food Assistance
Congressman's office stands ready to help GA-13 residents keep their benefits and navigate new federal rules
Media Contact:
Allison Phipps, Allison.Phipps@mail.house.gov ; Amya Enlow, Amya.Enlow@mail.house.gov
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Everton Blair (GA-13) warned today that the latest SNAP cut in H.R. 1, the Republican Reconciliation Law, is now in effect, and announced that his office will help constituents across the 13th District keep the food assistance they are eligible for.
As of October 1, Washington pays half of what it used to toward the cost of running SNAP, leaving states to cover 75% of administrative costs. Nationwide, that is more than $16 billion in lost funding. For Georgia, it means an estimated $43.7 million hole this year and up to $58.3 million every year after.
"When Washington cuts the people who process SNAP applications and then piles new paperwork on families, the result is predictable: longer waits, more mistakes, and eligible people losing food they qualify for," said Congressman Blair. "This is about a mother in Clayton County waiting weeks for a renewal, a senior in Rockdale who can't get anyone on the phone, a veteran in Henry County who loses benefits over a missed form. Georgia had to put up more than $46 million of its own money just to keep the lights on, and that is a patch, not a plan. Families in our district should not go hungry to pay for tax breaks for big corporations and the wealthiest Americans. I will keep fighting to reverse these cuts. In the meantime, if you have lost benefits, received a notice you don't understand, or aren't sure what the new rules mean for you, call my office. We will help you."
What this means for Georgia and the 13th District
About 1.4 million Georgians rely on SNAP, and roughly seven in ten Georgia SNAP households include a child. Fewer administrative dollars mean fewer caseworkers to process applications, determine eligibility, and answer questions at the moment new federal rules are making the program harder to navigate.
State lawmakers temporarily filled the gap with $46.4 million in FY 2027, plus $18.2 million for error-rate reduction. But relying on state funds to backstop federal cuts is not sustainable, and it puts schools, public safety, and other state and local services at risk. A second cost shift, forcing states to pay a share of SNAP benefits themselves, begins as soon as October 1, 2027.
According to USDA data, more than 5 million Americans, including about 2 million children, have lost SNAP since H.R. 1 was enacted in July 2025. More than 150,000 of them are Georgians.
Help for GA-13 residents
H.R. 1 also expanded SNAP work requirements. Many adults up to age 64, parents of teenagers 14 and older, veterans, people experiencing homelessness, and young adults leaving foster care must now document 80 hours a month of work, training, or volunteering to keep their benefits. Congressman Blair's office can help constituents:
- Understand whether the new rules apply to them and whether they qualify for an exemption
- Resolve delayed applications, renewals, and notices with the Georgia Division of Family and Children Services
- Connect with local food banks and community partners
Residents should watch their mail and their Georgia Gateway account for notices and respond by the deadline. For help, contact the district office at (770)-210-5073 or visit the website.

Today’s announcement will deliver more reliable American energy, strengthen the grid, lower costs, and meet growing power demand across the 13-state PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. region.
October 5, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization across Vistra’s nuclear fleet in Pennsylvania and Ohio. Today’s announcement will deliver more reliable American energy, strengthen the grid, lower costs, and meet growing power demand across the 13-state PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) region.
The investment advances President Trump’s Executive Order Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base, and marks another major step in restoring American nuclear leadership.
“President Trump promised to unleash an American nuclear renaissance, and the Energy Department is delivering,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “By getting more power out of the nuclear plants we already have, we can deliver more affordable, reliable, around the-clock energy for American families and businesses.”
The projects will preserve nearly 4 gigawatts (GW) of reliable baseload power—enough to power more than 3 million homes—and add 433 megawatts (MW) of new nuclear capacity, helping meet growing electricity demand in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and across the PJM region. The investments will support approximately 3,000 project-related jobs in engineering, construction, and planned outage work while preserving thousands of permanent, well-paying jobs.
“President Trump and Secretary Wright have set a clear direction for America’s nuclear future, and EDF is financing the projects that advance that mission,” said EDF Director Gregory A. Beard. “These investments will extend the life of existing reactors, increase nuclear generation, and deliver abundant, around-the-clock power to lower costs and power American prosperity for decades to come.”
Vistra’s planned investments at Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania and Davis-Besse and Perry in Ohio will produce more electricity from existing nuclear plants without requiring new transmission corridors or equivalent new generation resources, while supporting the plants’ operation for an additional 20 years beyond their existing licenses. EDF’s conditional loan commitment also includes an option to finance potential future uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant in Texas.
While this conditional commitment indicates DOE's intent to provide a loan, Vistra must satisfy certain technical, legal, environmental, and financial conditions before the Department enters into definitive financing documents and funds the loan.
title: Energy Department Announces $4.2 Billion Investment to Boost Nuclear Power and Help Lower Energy Costs in Pennsylvania and Ohio

WASHINGTON — Last week, Ambassador Jamieson Greer hosted the G20 Trade Ministers in Milwaukee, Wisconsin for the G20 Trade Ministerial. During the ministerial, Ambassador Greer led discussions on a wide range of topics, including eliminating forced labor in global supply chains, updating the Most-Favored Nation (MFN) principle, denouncing the weaponization of trade in food, and addressing structural excess capacity and production.
To highlight the ministerial and the progress made on a variety of topics, Ambassador Greer hosted a press conference with the attending media. Watch here.
Here are some of the top headlines:
Here are some of the highlights:
- Fox Business: Jamieson Greer says Trump's tariff program is working as trade deficit declines
- WISN 12 News: UPFRONT: Trade rep defends Trump tariff policy in MKE
- Axios: The world opinion shifts on trade
- Milwaukee Business Journal: In Milwaukee, Trump's trade rep touts tariffs, suggests American manufacturers use domestic suppliers
- 620 WTMJ: Jamieson Greer on Milwaukee G20 trade meeting, tariffs and jobs
- Fox Business: Trump Trade Chief Hosts G20 Leaders in Wisconsin
- TMJ4 News: 'Big win for Milwaukee': G20 trade ministers meet in Milwaukee to discuss tariffs, global trade policy
- ANI News: US Trade Representative Greer calls for new global trading order
- Reuters: US trade chief Greer says new 'Milwaukee Framework' to combat global excess steel capacity
- Bloomberg: Greer Pushes Europe on Diesel Release as He Hosts G20 Partners
- CNBC TV18: G20 trade ministers agree on statement against weaponisation of food
- Milwaukee Business Journal: Why G20 Trade Ministers Picked Milwaukee for Summit
For decades, trade in food, agricultural products, and agricultural inputs has been weaponized to exert coercive pressure for economic or political reasons. After constructive negotiations during the G20 Trade Ministerial, Ambassador Greer announced that the G20 Trade Ministers reached a consensus on condemning the weaponization of food through coercive trade actions. This statement is an important step towards ensuring that agricultural products are not used as a tool for economic or political coercion.
To read Ambassador Greer’s statement as the Chair of the G20 Trade Ministerial, click here. To read the Trade Ministers of the United States, Mexico, and Argentina’s statement on eliminating forced labor in global supply chains on the margins of the G20 Trade Ministerial, click here.
At the historic Milwaukee Clock Tower, Ambassador Greer hosted a CEO roundtable with EU Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and Japanese State Minister Miyamoto to highlight the success of President Trump’s trade agenda in strengthening our economic resilience.
To kick off the G20 Trade Ministerial, Ambassador Greer joined the G20 Trade Ministers for a welcome reception hosted by Business Roundtable and National Association of Manufacturers, whose advocacy continues to support American businesses and expand opportunities for American workers.
Under President Trump’s leadership, the U.S. steel industry is undergoing a renaissance on the strength of tariffs, trade deals, favorable tax treatment, improved energy policy, and the American entrepreneurial spirit. On the sidelines of G20 Trade Ministerial, Ambassador Greer chaired the Ministerial Meeting of the Global Forum on Steel Excess Capacity, which reached consensus on a comprehensive framework for joint action (“the Milwaukee Framework”).
Walking the factory floor with the G20 Trade Ministers, Ambassador Greer toured Rockwell Automation and met with blue-collar workers and industry leaders to discuss how President Trump’s trade policies are supporting jobs and strengthening our supply chain resilience.
Watch Ambassador Greer’s interview with Fox Business’s Edward Lawrence from Rockwell’s headquarters here.
At the Milwaukee Art Museum, Ambassador Greer and Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins hosted a welcome dinner to share a bounty of American-grown food with the G20 Trade Ministers. As a direct result of President Trump’s trade actions, our agricultural trade deficit is trending in the right direction and the trade deals secured are unlocking foreign market access for U.S. agricultural exports.
To conclude the ministerial meetings about the future of trade, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Harley-Davidson President and CEO Artie Starrs joined Ambassador Greer to tour one of America’s most iconic brands, Harley-Davidson, underscoring the ingenuity of American innovation. Harley-Davidson serves as a prime example of what happens when people have the freedom, the determination, and the grit to build something new.

Nation’s Largest Law Enforcement Organization Endorses Figures’ Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for the Children of Police Officers
MONTGOMERY – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures announced that the National Fraternal Order of Police – the nation’s largest organization of sworn law enforcement officers – has endorsed his bipartisan bill, the Public Service Educational Assistance Act, to cover the cost of college and job training for the children of law enforcement officers, other first responders, educators, and social workers.
“Every day, our police officers put their lives on the line to keep our streets and communities safe,” said Figures. “They and their families make tremendous sacrifices for us, and we should be there to give back to them in any way that we can. That’s why I introduced this bipartisan bill to recognize the vital work of our law enforcement officers by investing in their families' future.”  
“Public servants are the backbone of America, serving in vital roles that ensure the safety and well-being of their communities every day. As law enforcement in America faces a critical recruitment and retention crisis, and as postsecondary education becomes more expensive and crucial in our modern world, it is vital that the Federal government ensures that our public servants have the necessary funding and opportunities to receive postsecondary education,” said Patrick Yoes, National President of the National Fraternal Order of Police. “On behalf of the more than 382,000 members of the Fraternal Order of Police, thank you both for your leadership on this important issue.” 
Figures’ bill establishes a federal education assistance program covering the full cost of postsecondary education and training opportunities – including those enrolled in trade schools and vocational programs – for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers who have completed at least 20 years of qualifying service.  
Congressman Figures is joined in introducing this legislation by Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Representatives Jahana Hayes (CT-05) and Mike Ezell (MS-04).  
In addition to the National Fraternal Order of Police, this bill is also endorsed by the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, the National Association of Social Workers, the International Association of Fire Fighters, the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians, and the Major Cities Chiefs Association.
title: Nation’s Largest Law Enforcement Organization Endorses Figures’ Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for the Children of Police Officers
