Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Senator Jeanne Shaheen, Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Representative Sara Jacobs, Ranking Member of the Africa Subcommittee, and Senator Jeff Merkley, Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, issued a statement following the release of a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report they requested on the Trump Administration’s hollowing out of U.S. foreign assistance.
The GAO found that the Department of State could not produce comprehensive data on its workforce, even in the wake of last year’s substantial Reductions in Force, which leaves the Department unable to adequately plan for the significant assistance responsibilities it assumed after the Trump Administration illegally dismantled the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID).
“The GAO’s report on the recent drastic changes to U.S. foreign assistance confirms what we’ve known all along: the Trump Administration dramatically reduced programming and staffing without a plan, and this continues to negatively impact the United States’ ability to manage taxpayer dollars effectively and help communities in need.
"Despite assurances that State would be able to subsume USAID’s responsibilities and an early commitment from Secretary Rubio to provide guidance for implementing the State Department’s foreign assistance review, the Department’s Reductions in Force have left it too understaffed to properly execute those functions.
"Meanwhile, State has produced no written rationale for determining which programs to maintain and which to terminate. The GAO notes this lack of guidance could lead State Department officials to ‘make inconsistent or ad hoc decisions or lack the information necessary for effective decision-making.'
"The Trump administration’s failure to plan for the responsible continuation of U.S. foreign assistance after it eviscerated USAID clearly demonstrates how poorly conceived and executed these actions were. The regrettable results include millions of preventable deaths and significantly diminished U.S. soft power and reputation around the globe.” 
The GAO report can be found here. 
###
title: Meeks, Shaheen, Jacobs, Merkley Issue Statement on Troubling GAO Report on Status of Trump Admin’s Foreign Assistance

Hartford, CT – Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to reporting from The Atlantic that President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia:

“When we voted against the Senate’s sanction bill this month, we warned that stripping out the enforcement language would leave every decision about punishing Putin to a president who keeps siding with the Kremlin. It took less than two weeks and President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia.

“Just last week President Trump went to the United Nations and bragged about the ‘enormous new tariff authorities’ this bill handed him. So, the one part of the law he seems eager to enforce will needlessly raise costs on Americans by continuing his reckless trade policies, while the power he was given to cripple Putin’s war machine he is already looking to sign away.

“That is exactly why the House-passed bill, H.R. 2913, required the president to act on sanctions. Without that requirement, sanctions are dependent on President Trump’s will to impose them – and President Trump has shown us time and time again he would rather be a friend to Putin than hold him accountable.

“We will keep fighting for military assistance for Ukraine and real sanctions that no president can waive away as a favor.”
title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on Reports President Trump is Seeking to Ease Russian Sanctions

Rep. Frank J. Mrvan Introduces Utility Affordability and Transparency Act to Protect Consumers from Higher Energy Costs
Washington, DC – Today, Congressman Frank J. Mrvan introduced H.R. 10687, the Utility Affordability and Transparency Act, legislation that would increase transparency for consumers and prevent federal taxpayers and utility ratepayers from being forced to bear the costs associated with reopening or preventing the closure of outdated or expensive power-generating facilities.
The legislation would prohibit the Department of Energy from issuing emergency orders that delay the retirement of power plants or require electric generation from facilities that have already been permanently closed.
The Utility Affordability and Transparency Act would also require the Department of Energy to study alternatives to emergency orders that could reduce net costs to consumers and utilities and publish a publicly available report detailing the estimated costs associated with any emergency order.
Additionally, the legislation would require affected electric utilities to provide customers with information on their monthly bills identifying the additional costs resulting from any federal emergency order.
“Northwest Indiana residents are struggling to make ends meet, and a major part of that burden is the cost of heating and cooling their homes,” said Congressman Frank J. Mrvan. “Consumers deserve transparency about what is driving their utility costs and what can be done to lower them.
“Hardworking families should not be forced to pay higher utility rates because the federal government is requiring energy companies to reopen or keep outdated coal-fired generating units operating beyond their planned retirement. When the government intervenes in private-sector business decisions and forces companies to operate facilities that are no longer economically viable, those costs ultimately get passed on to consumers.
“The Utility Affordability and Transparency Act will ensure that the federal government cannot simply prevent or delay the retirement of expensive power plants without accountability for the costs imposed on consumers. Families deserve to know when government policies are increasing their utility bills, why those costs are being imposed, and what alternatives exist to lower them.”
The full bill text of the Utility Affordability and Transparency Act is available here.
###
title: Rep. Frank J. Mrvan Introduces Utility Affordability and Transparency Act to Protect Consumers from Higher Energy Costs

Constituent Update - October 2, 2026
FSIS Announces the FY2027 Annual Sampling Plan
Today, FSIS posted the FY 2027 Annual Sampling Program Plan. Sampling of products and testing for microbiological contaminants or chemical residues is a key FSIS inspection verification activity. Each annual sampling plan identifies all current FSIS sampling programs, showing the breadth of microbiological and chemical residue sampling data that will be generated to inform the agency’s science-based and data-driven strategic planning efforts. A few notable changes in this year’s sampling plan include:
- FSIS is planning to implement a new paired environmental sampling program for Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) and non-Lm Listeria in ready-to-eat (RTE) establishments nationwide in January 2027. The new sampling project will add two food contact surface and two non-food contact surface samples to the RTE post-lethality exposed product samples that FSIS already collects. The goal of the new sampling project is to generate data verifying that establishments are effectively controlling Lm and maintaining sanitation in RTE establishments.
- FSIS will increase raw pork sampling starting in January 2027 to provide data to support the development and refinement of future policy initiatives. FSIS will also test broader pork product types with a higher risk for Salmonella
- FSIS will decrease the number of bob veal samples collected and analyzed under the National Residue Program to account for the nationwide reduction in slaughter volume over the past several years, preventing unnecessary burden on smaller establishments.
You can view the FY 2027 Annual Sampling Program Plan and find more information on FSIS’ sampling programs.
FSIS Leadership Update
FSIS is continuing to build its leadership team and announcing leadership appointments in the Office of Policy and Program Development (OPPD) and the Office of Field Operations (OFO).
Stephanie “Stevie” Hretz has been named deputy assistant administrator (DAA) for OPPD after serving as acting DAA since March 2026. Prior to the acting DAA role, Hretz served as director of the Risk Management and Innovations Staff since May 2023. Hretz began her FSIS career 25 years ago through a student program at FSIS’ Eastern Laboratory while studying microbiology at the University of Georgia.
Within OFO, Jeffery Barham was named executive associate for regulatory operations. Barham joined FSIS in 1995 as a food inspector and has served in many leadership roles within FSIS, most recently as the Springdale district manager. His previous roles include deputy district manager, frontline supervisor, and district case specialist.
Jeffery Jacobsen was named executive associate for regulatory operations after serving in an acting role since March 2026. Jacobsen joined FSIS in March 2000 as an intermittent food inspector and has served in numerous leadership roles across the agency, most recently, as the Des Moines district manager. His previous roles include deputy district manager, frontline supervisor, and an Enforcement Investigation and Analysis Officer (EIAO).
Dr. Robert Reeder has been named executive associate for regulatory operations after serving in an acting role since November 2025. Prior to this role, he served as Denver district manager since 2021. He joined FSIS in 2001 as a relief and in-plant supervisory public health veterinarian. Dr. Reeder held additional leadership roles as an FLS and Denver DDM. Dr. Reeder holds a Bachelor of Science from Arkansas Tech University and a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from Louisiana State University.
Robert Witte has been named deputy assistant administrator for OFO after serving in an acting role since February 2026. Prior to this role, he served as acting assistant administrator for the Office of Investigation, Enforcement and Audit (OIEA). Witte began his FSIS career in 2006 as a student intern and egg products inspector. He has served in many leadership roles including EIAO, senior staff officer, senior program analyst, deputy chief of staff for the Office of the Administrator and deputy assistant administrator for OIEA.
Barry Rhodes has been named acting deputy administrator for OFO. Rhodes joined FSIS in 2003 as a Food Inspector in a poultry slaughter establishment. Rhodes has served in multiple field and headquarters roles over the past 23 years including most recently as the Director of the Recall Management and Technical Analysis Staff.
You can find these updates and information about FSIS leadership on the FSIS website.
FSIS Posted Updated Datasets
On October 2, 2026, FSIS updated the individual establishment Salmonella performance standard category information for raw poultry carcasses, raw chicken parts, and comminuted poultry products on the Salmonella Verification Testing Program Monthly Posting page on the FSIS website. Additionally, FSIS posted the aggregate sampling results showing the number of establishments in categories 1, 2, or 3 for establishments producing young poultry carcasses, raw chicken parts, or not ready-to-eat comminuted poultry products at the location linked above.
The following datasets were also updated to include the latest quarter of data:
- Raw Poultry Product Sampling
- Egg Product Sampling
- Raw Beef Product Sampling
- Ready-to-Eat Product Sampling
- Raw Pork Product Sampling
- National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) Cecal Sampling Data
- Livestock Humane Handling Inspection Tasks
- Poultry Good Commercial Practices Inspection Tasks
FSIS Announces Addition of Product Name Field in Laboratory Sampling Datasets
FSIS is announcing the proposed addition of the product name data field to the primary table of publicly available product-sampling FSIS Laboratory Sampling datasets in January 2027. The product_name field is a free-text field entered by FSIS inspectors during sample collection and may include brand or product-specific details not captured in other data fields.
The addition of this field provides supplementary product-level detail, enhances data transparency, and increases the usefulness of FSIS’ datasets for regulatory partners, researchers, and the public. The product_name field is only applicable to product-sampling projects and will remain blank for environmental and other non-product sampling projects. Any corporate proprietary information will be redacted and replaced with ‘[REDACTED]’ prior to publication.
FSIS is accepting public comments on the proposed addition of the product_name field through November 6, 2026. Although the sample dataset reflects the Ready‑to‑Eat (RTE) Product & Risk‑based Listeria monocytogenes Sampling dataset, the product_name field will be added to all establishment‑specific laboratory sampling datasets involving product sampling.
A sample dataset is available on the FSIS Sample Datasets and Documentation webpage in JSON and CSV formats. The webpage also includes a document summarizing updates to the metadata, data dictionary, and the data limitation sections for convenience.
To submit a comment, email FSISDataDriven@usda.gov and include “Product Name Addition” in the subject line.
Available for Public Comment
FSIS seeks public comments on proposed rules and notices, which are viewable on the FSIS Federal Register & Rulemaking webpage. FSIS is currently seeking comments on the following:
- Until October 13: Notice of Request To Renew an Approved Information Collection: Egg Products Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point and Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures
- Until November 9: Notice of Request to Renew an Approved Information Collection: Mechanically Tenderized Beef Products
Policy Update
FSIS notices and directives on public health and regulatory issues are available on the FSIS Policy webpage. The following policy update was recently issued:
FSIS Notice 38-26: Cancellation of Directives
FSIS Notice 39-26: Federal Holidays in Calendar Year 2027
FSIS Notice 40-26: Leave Bank Program 2026 Open Enrollment Period for the 2027 Leave Year

The Library of Export Requirements has been updated for products for the following:
FSIS:
- Türkiye
APHIS:

Complete information for APHIS products can be found at Export Restrictions on U.S. Animal Products for Human Consumption website. Select the countries listed above from the drop down menu for complete information.

Rep. Vasquez Secures $96 Million to Build New Alamo Navajo Health Center
With HHS grant, Alamo Navajo Chapter will build a new, technologically advanced health center in their community
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) secured $96 million in federal funding from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to build a new, technologically advanced health center at the Alamo Navajo Chapter. The health center will serve over 2,600 Tribal residents living in the communities of Alamo, Magdalena, and Socorro.
“This $96 million investment is a major step toward ensuring the Alamo Navajo community has access to the quality health care it deserves,” said Vasquez. “For too long, Tribal communities have been denied access to reliable healthcare – being forced to drive incredibly long distances and go to great lengths just to see a doctor. This project will bring care closer to home, and I’m proud to deliver this funding and will continue working to ensure the federal government is serving New Mexico’s Tribal communities.”
The $96 million award will support the construction of a new 70,000 gross square feet (GSF) health center and will be a modern, state-of-the-art, advanced facility to provide health care services specifically designed to meet the needs of the Alamo Navajo Chapter.
This funding comes from the Interior Appropriations bill, which passed with strong bipartisan support. Congressman Vasquez also secured key funding and resources for New Mexico in the bill, including $1,092,000 for the Ramah Navajo Drinking Water Improvement project and over $3 million in projects to improve public safety and infrastructure in Southern New Mexico.
Vasquez has consistently worked to support New Mexico’s Tribal communities:
- Led the Tribal HUD-VASH Act to provide housing assistance and support services for Native American veterans.
- Voted to extend the Special Diabetes Program for Indians to help address health disparities in Tribal communities.
- Championed the bipartisan Indian Programs Advance Appropriations Act to fulfill the US government's trust and treaty responsibilities and provide full and consistent funding for IHS and BIE programs.
- Led the Parity for Tribal Law Enforcement Act to enhance public safety within Tribal communities.
###
title: Rep. Vasquez Secures $96 Million to Build New Alamo Navajo Health Center

Committee Democrats Issue Statement on State Department’s Partial Production of Venezuela Oil Deal Documents
Washington, DC — Reps. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Joaquin Castro, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, along with all Democratic Members of the Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, issued the following statement after the State Department provided the Committee with one document related to the Trump administration’s deal signed with Alejandro Betancourt to acquire a stake in North American Blue Energy Partners.
“We appreciate that State has provided this document, but a single document falls far short of the records Democrats have requested as we conduct oversight over the Trump administration’s Venezuela policy. When Democrats sought to subpoena the documents on September 15, Republicans, led by Chairwoman Maria Elvira Salazar, voted to shield the administration from accountability and protect Alejandro Betancourt and Delcy Rodriguez from scrutiny.
“Democrats will continue to examine the Trump administration’s actions with respect to Venezuela, and we call on Secretary Rubio to produce to the Committee all remaining requested documents, including the agreement between Delcy Rodriguez and Betancourt, as well as KPMG’s independent audits of the Foreign Government Deposit Funds, the account Trump established after his administration began seizing Venezuelan oil revenues.
“Congress cannot conduct meaningful oversight based on selective disclosures. Providing one document while withholding other central records raises further questions about what the administration is trying to conceal.”
Additional background: On February 13, 2026, HFAC Democrats requested information regarding the Trump administration’s decision to route Venezuela oil revenues into an offshore account in Qatar. On September 21, 2026, Committee Democrats demanded Secretary Marco Rubio release the results of long-promised audits of the Foreign Government Deposit Funds, the account established after the Trump administration seized Venezuelan oil revenues. 
###
title: Committee Democrats Issue Statement on State Department’s Partial Production of Venezuela Oil Deal Documents

WASHINGTON, D.C. -- On September 24, Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25) introduced H. Res. 1583 expressing support for the designation of October as National Promotoras Month. This is the first time the resolution has been introduced at the federal level.

Promotoras, sometimes known as community health workers, peer educators, health advocates, patient navigators, and cultural liaisons, are trusted messengers who connect families to the care they need. They serve rural towns, farmworker families, Tribal nations, border communities, and immigrant neighborhoods, delivering health education and prevention in the language and culture of the people they serve.

"As an Emergency Physician, I saw too many patients arrive when it was already too late. Promotoras change that. They knock on doors, speak our language, and earn the trust that keeps families healthy before a crisis hits. This resolution recognizes their work and thanks them for everything they do for our communities," said Congressman Raul Ruiz M.D.

Promotoras help reduce emergency room visits, increase preventive care, and improve management of chronic diseases like diabetes, asthma, and heart disease, lowering health care costs for everyone. Yet many remain underrecognized and underpaid, with limited training pathways and support.

The resolution:

Recognizes the essential contributions of promotoras and community health workers to the health of our communities

Acknowledges the need for sustainable funding, workforce development, and fair compensation for the promotora workforce

Encourages federal, state, Tribal, and community partners to invest in and expand promotora-led programs, especially in rural areas

"Promotoras are trusted community leaders whom families turn to for resources, information, and support. They show up during emergencies and celebrations alike, guided by the same deep commitment to provide “servicio de corazón”, service from the heart,” said Maria Lemus, Executive Director, Vision y Compromiso. “We are profoundly grateful to Congressman Ruiz for his leadership in presenting this federal resolution recognizing the vital contributions of Promotoras. Community members, as well as federal and state agencies, rely on Promotoras to advance the health, well-being, and resilience of communities across the country. Designating October as National Promotoras Month honors their leadership and ensures that their work receives the recognition it deserves."
title: CONGRESSMAN RAUL RUIZ, M.D. INTRODUCES RESOLUTION DESIGNATING OCTOBER AS NATIONAL PROMOTORAS MONTH

WASHINGTON, D.C. and KYIV – The U.S.–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF) today approved a number of new investments to advance the shared economic and strategic interests of the United States and Ukraine. These investments will help secure critical supply chains, strengthen Ukraine’s energy resilience, and develop its critical mineral sector.
“URIF’s first investment in March demonstrated that it was open for business. Today’s board approval of additional investments in Ukraine’s critical minerals and energy sectors signals investor support for Ukraine’s recovery and future prosperity,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.“These investments represent the continued realization of the vision behind the novel agreement that Prime Minister Svyrydenko and I signed in April 2025 to establish URIF and give America a direct stake in Ukraine’s long-term peace and prosperity”
“Today's Board meeting marks an important step forward for the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. These investments strengthen Ukraine's energy resilience, develop critical mineral resources, and support innovative Ukrainian companies. Together these projects are building the foundation for Ukraine's economic recovery and deepening the partnership between our countries,” said DFC CEO Ben Black.
“This round of investments shows the growing scope of the U.S.-Ukraine partnership, from energy and critical minerals to telecommunications and emerging technologies. For URIF, it is an important step in building a track record of investments that gives investors' confidence in Ukraine. We want to see more Ukrainian companies develop through this partnership and create new opportunities for the Ukrainian economy,” said Oleksii Sobolev, Deputy Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine.
The joint U.S.-Ukrainian URIF board of directors approved the following today:
- Expanding Investment in Ukraine’s Critical Minerals: URIF will establish a joint investment platform with Ukrainian company BGV Group Management. The platform will seek to build a diverse portfolio of early-stage mining projects across Ukraine, supporting the development of Ukraine’s critical minerals sector. Its initial focus will be on identified assets of rare earths, beryllium, and zirconium deposits. This platform aims to significantly scale up Ukraine’s critical mineral production, creating Ukrainian jobs and investment opportunities for U.S. and Ukrainian companies and international investors, while shoring up secure supply chains of these vital critical minerals for U.S. and allied markets.
- Restoring Heat and Power to Ukrainian Communities: URIF’s equity investment in a multi-site distributed combined heat and power (CHP) cogeneration platform will support the construction and operation of a series of community-scale energy hubs designed to restore electricity and heat supply damaged by the war. Once completed, the project is intended to provide heat and power to thousands of households, ensuring access to vital energy and heat in Ukraine as the conflict continues.
- Enhancing Ukraine’s Energy Security: URIF’s debt investment provides financing for DTEK’s 200 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage system across six sites in Ukraine. The system is operational, with enough capacity to supply electricity equivalent to approximately 600,000 Ukrainian homes for two hours and provide the country’s power grid with greater resilience and stability. The project is built by DTEK, Ukraine’s largest private energy company, and leverages American energy technology at the battery storage sites to provide backup power and enable faster grid restoration.
Today’s announcement comes one year after the United States and Ukraine established URIF’s initial capital base and launched the Fund’s operations, moving URIF from an institutional framework to capital deployment. The Fund made its first investment in emerging-technology company Sine Engineering in March of this year. In June, the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation signed a cooperation agreement with the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) to develop a political risk insurance framework that will catalyze and support private sector investment and capital mobilization in Ukraine in connection with URIF’s investments.
URIF is a joint U.S.–Ukrainian investment fund and a key pillar of the economic partnership between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine. The Fund harnesses American and Ukrainian talent, resources, and expertise to mobilize U.S. and aligned private capital and create strategic investment opportunities in Ukraine for the United States, its allies, multilateral development banks, and private investors. URIF focuses on investments that support Ukraine’s reconstruction, supply chain resilience, and the shared economic security and prosperity of Ukraine and the United States.
For more information and to submit a project proposal, please visit URIF’s website: https://urifinvest.com.
###
The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to U.S. economic statecraft. DFC mobilizes private capital to advance U.S. foreign policy and economic development. Our investments deliver strong returns for American taxpayers, drive meaningful economic development for our allies and partners, and secure supply chains to counter and outcompete our adversaries.
title: URIF Approves Additional Investments and Partnerships in Energy and Critical Minerals

Washington, D.C. –Congressman Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), and Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) led 50 members of the House in urging U.S. Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Scott Turner to release the delayed Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) grants and urged the Department to immediately expedite the process of awarding grant funding for the HOPWA program. The call is part of a bipartisan, bicameral effort led by U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen.

The letter comes as organizations across the nation are at risk of losing critical HOPWA funding that they rely on to serve those with HIV/AIDS. Many previously awarded HUD grants expire on September 30, yet HUD has not released a NOFO or communicated with grantee organizations relying on award renewals to continue providing critical housing and health care services nationwide.

For decades, Congressman Nadler has been the leading advocate in Congress for fully funding and effectively administering HOPWA. Each year, he has worked to secure robust HOPWA funding in the appropriations process and has pushed back against efforts to cut, withhold, or otherwise undermine the program’s resources. In April 2026, Congressman Nadler took to the House floor to oppose President Trump’s budget request to eliminate HOPWA funding entirely, a proposal that would have jeopardized critical housing assistance for people living with HIV/AIDS across the country.

In the letter to Secretary Turner, the lawmakers wrote, “We write to express our grave concerns regarding the delayed Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) program. For many organizations in our communities, this program is vital to ensuring individuals with HIV/AIDS have access to safe and stable housing. We urge you to release the NOFO immediately and expedite the awards so communities can continue to provide support and housing to those who need it.”

They continued: “Unfortunately, many competitive HOPWA awards will expire tomorrow on September 30, 2026. Your department still has not released a NOFO, and grantees have received no information regarding the renewal of their awards. HOPWA is the only Federal program dedicated to the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS, making any gap in funding detrimental for the organizations providing support and the individuals and communities that depend on this program.”

The lawmakers concluded: “We understand that the awarding process takes careful review, but because these applicants are all seeking renewals, they have already been vetted and approved by your department. We urge you to expedite this process immediately and release awards as soon as possible. Without these critical funds, individuals with HIV/AIDS will face the risk of homelessness, and the organizations that help them may have to close their doors.”

Over 30 percent of those with HIV are living below the poverty line, and 20 percent have experienced homelessness in recent years. As the only HUD program dedicated to housing support for those with HIV/AIDS, expiration of previous awards and a delayed grant process by HUD could lead to staff layoffs and cuts to health care and housing services—exacerbating homelessness for some of the country’s most vulnerable communities.

The full letter can be read here.

Members of the House signing the letter are Representatives Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Betty McCollum (MN-04), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Danny Davis (IL-07), Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Bennie Thompson (MS-02), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Haley Stevens (MI-11), Everton Blair (GA-13), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Troy Carter (LA-02), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Frederica Wilson (FL-24), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Sean Casten (IL-06), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Bill Foster (IL-11), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), William Keating (MA-09), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Angie Craig (MN-02) and Juan Vargas (CA-52).

Krishnamoorthi and Smith Introduce Legislation to Help Immigrants Strengthen Our Health Care Workforce
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) and Congressman Adam Smith (WA-09) introduced the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act and the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act, two bills to help immigrants enter the U.S. health care workforce and address the nation's growing shortage of health care providers. A 2022 study by the Migration Policy Institute found that 2.1 million college-educated immigrants are unemployed or underemployed, even as sectors like health care face mounting workforce shortages, including a projected shortfall of up to 48,000 primary care physicians by 2034, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges.\
“Skilled doctors, nurses, and other health professionals should have the opportunity to put their training and expertise to work caring for patients,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Our legislation would help qualified immigrants overcome unnecessary barriers to entering the health care workforce while helping communities address critical provider shortages. When we make better use of the talent already in our communities, we strengthen our health care system and expand access to care.”
“We have thousands of skilled nurses, doctors, and health professionals in this country whose training and expertise are going to waste because their professional expertise is not recognized and they face numerous barriers to achieve the needed licensure. At the same time, our health care system is stretched thin and patients are waiting longer for care,” said Congressman Adam Smith. “This bill package helps immigrants put their skills to work and serve their communities and will rebuild the health care system.”
Statements of Support
“Across the U.S., communities face critical health workforce shortages, yet immigrant and refugee health professionals—who possess in-demand skills—remain underemployed. Communities need this talent, and recognizing it is an essential step. By streamlining licensure and addressing unnecessary barriers, we can meet urgent labor needs and improve access to quality care. We support efforts, including at the state and federal levels, to advance policies that promote community prosperity by ensuring that immigrants can fully contribute their training and skills to their local economy.” - Kit Taintor, Head of US Policy and Practice, World Education Services (WES)
“We are proud to support these bills, which will expand opportunities for immigrant professionals while helping address critical workforce shortages in the healthcare sector,” said Alice Kang, President of Upwardly Global. “With demand for healthcare workers rising nationwide, we should be creating pathways that allow qualified immigrants and refugees to contribute their expertise. This legislation will strengthen our healthcare system, bolster the economy and support safer, more resilient communities. Upwardly Global will continue to stand with Rep. Smith in moving this work forward.”
“Many members of our team hold advanced education and expertise in medicine, nursing, and behavioral health. Yet they are unable to practice here due to costly additional education requirements and complex licensing procedures. At a time when we are confronted with a significant healthcare provider shortage—and as we work to diversify the healthcare workforce—it is critical to consider policies that create pathways for these highly skilled professionals to contribute to patient care,” said Tamara Cyhan Cunitz, MN, RN, Executive Director, Nashi Immigrants Health Board. “These bills introduced by Rep. Smith would expand opportunities for immigrant healthcare professionals to serve patients in our community and region. These measures would not only strengthen our workforce with qualified providers but also enable community members to receive care from clinicians who understand their language and cultural background.”
Background
The Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act would help immigrants, regardless of previous health care experience, enter the nursing and allied health workforce by:
- Creating grants for programs that provide training, licensing, certification, and case management for immigrants interested in entering the health care field; and
- Opening eligibility for the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) to non-U.S.-citizen immigrants.
An estimated 200,000 nurses per year will need to be hired to meet increased demand and replace retiring nurses. This bill supports immigrants entering nursing or an allied health profession, including dental hygienists, dietitians, medical technologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech language pathologists.
The Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act would help internationally trained physicians (ITPs) obtain a U.S. medical license by:
- Incentivizing states to create temporary licensing programs allowing internationally educated immigrants with medical degrees to practice under supervision while completing the training and certification needed for a U.S. medical license;
- Establishing guaranteed medical residency slots for ITPs to practice in predominantly medically underserved communities; and
- Providing grants to help cover the cost of exam preparation, testing, certification, ESL classes, and case management for ITPs in need of financial assistance.
Apart from Canada, internationally trained physicians cannot immediately apply to sit for the U.S. Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE), and the cost of licensing, test preparation, and certification often puts a U.S. medical license out of reach, even for highly trained professionals. Many states have created alternative licensure pathways, but more must be done at the federal level to support these reforms nationwide to expand high-quality health care access.
Endorsements: International Medical Graduates Academy (TIMGA), Nashi Immigrants Health Board, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Sea Mar Community Health Center, Seattle Indian Health Board, Spring Institute for Intercultural Learning, Talent Beyond Boundaries, Upwardly Global, World Education Services (WES)
title: Krishnamoorthi and Smith Introduce Legislation to Help Immigrants Strengthen Our Health Care Workforce

Washington, D.C. – As a member agency of the Financial Literacy and Education Commission (FLEC), the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) is proud to support the new National Strategy for Financial Literacy  to guide nationwide actions on building youth financial competency, developing good saving and investing habits, improving Americans’ knowledge of digital financial literacy, and learning how to avoid fraud and scams.
The CFPB has developed evidence-based financial education resources to help Americans increase their financial well-being. The CFPB’s youth financial education strategy is a research-based framework that outlines when and how children and youth acquire the knowledge, skills, and behaviors associated with adult financial well-being. The framework supports improving executive functioning skills, creating and encouraging positive financial habits, and building financial knowledge and decision-making skills, which are the three building blocks children develop in youth.
The National Strategy for Financial Literacy establishes four priority areas for the FLEC:
- Youth Financial Capability: Build a foundation of basic financial skills starting in childhood and young adulthood to improve financial outcomes for the next generation of Americans.
- Saving and Investing: Increase Americans’ knowledge of saving and investing to build financial
security and achieve their financial goals, including by promoting awareness of new savings and investment vehicles such as Trump Accounts for children.
- Digital Financial Literacy: Improve Americans’ knowledge and decision-making skills to enable
the safe and confident use of digital financial products and services.
- Scams and Fraud Education: Equip consumers with the knowledge to recognize and avoid scams and fraud and the tools to mitigate the impact of potential losses.
The National Strategy for Financial Literacy also identifies best practices for delivering effective financial education, including providing actionable and timely education at key financial decision points, tailoring education to life stages and individual situations, reinforcing concepts over time, incorporating experiential and hands-on learning, supporting high-quality instruction, and evaluating program effectiveness. The strategy was developed through consultation with FLEC-represented agencies, public input, and independent research on financial literacy and education.
The FLEC was established by the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act of 2003 to “improve the financial literacy and education of persons in the United States through the development of a national strategy to promote financial literacy and education.” The FLEC is composed of the heads of 23 federal agencies and the White House Domestic Policy Council and is chaired by the Secretary of the Treasury. The Vice Chairman is the Acting Director of the CFPB.
About us
The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is a 21st century agency that implements and enforces Federal consumer financial law and ensures that markets for consumer financial products are fair, transparent, and competitive.
title: CFPB Proud to Support the National Strategy for Financial Literacy

Rep. Salinas, Sen. Booker Lead Eight Lawmakers in Calling on RV Industry to Remove Deforestation-Linked Timber from Supply Chains
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06), alongside Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) led eight Members of Congress in a letter urging the nation’s leading recreational vehicle manufacturers to adopt more sustainable supply chain practices and shift their sourcing of hardwood away from producers that contribute to deforestation and other devastating environmental practices.
This effort comes after an alarming New York Times investigation that uncovered how Indonesian rainforest timber harvested from environmentally sensitive regions made its way into American RVs. That logging has driven vast rainforest and peatland destruction, displacing Indigenous communities, fueling labor abuses, and threatening orangutans and other wildlife. The lawmakers stressed that the RV industry has both the duty and the means to lead the outdoor recreation industry toward responsible sourcing and stewardship without delay. The letter encouraged RV manufacturers to accelerate their switch to domestic hardwoods or composite materials.
Congresswoman Salinas and Senator Booker are joined on their letter by Reps. Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), and Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), as well as Sens. Jeff Merkley (D-OR), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).
Click HERE
Dear Mr. Happe, Mr. Martin, Mr. Gaeddert, and Mr. Nemeth,
We write as Members of Congress with an interest in the health of America’s forest products industry and in responsible stewardship of natural resources.
Investigative reporting by The New York Times documents how Indonesian rainforest timber sourced from environmentally sensitive regions of Borneo has made its way into your supply chains and consequently into American recreational vehicles.
These findings are alarming. Tropical plywood, particularly meranti or lauan, has been harvested from the Mayawana Persada concession which contains carbon-rich peatlands and intact rainforest habitat critical to the survival of critically endangered Bornean orangutans, as well as other species. These actions violate Indonesia's national climate commitments and have been accompanied by egregious violations of the rights of Indigenous communities.
As the biggest consumer of tropical hardwood plywood in the United States, the RV industry bears particular responsibility for ensuring its supply chains are more suitably managed.
Many companies now vet their suppliers to eliminate deforestation from their supply chains, yet the RV industry lacks basic wood-sourcing standards. Voluntary sourcing standards have played an important role in the development of sustainable production in a wide variety of industries and, when successful, can obviate the need for stricter regulation. Retailers such as Lowe's and Home Depot, for example, have adopted wood sourcing policies that prohibit deforestation-linked timber. Outdoor recreation depends on healthy ecosystems, and sourcing deforested timber contradicts the industry’s stated values, especially when practical alternatives exist.
We strongly encourage your companies – as market leaders in your industry – to adopt robust supply chain traceability practices and wood sourcing policies that prohibit the use of timber linked to deforestation, peatland destruction, violations of Indigenous peoples' rights, or labor abuses. As part of that commitment, we urge you to require that all wood products used in your vehicles be independently certified as legal, sustainably managed, and deforestation-free – such as Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certification or an equivalent standard. The development by your companies of new due diligence guidelines, in consultation with expert stakeholder entities, can help ensure that such policies can be effectively implemented and monitored. We would also encourage you to accelerate the switch to domestic hardwoods or composite materials to avoid the use of tropical hardwoods altogether.
Thank you for your attention to this important issue. We look forward to hearing how your companies intend to lead the outdoor recreation industry toward a commitment to responsible sourcing and responsible stewardship.
###
title: Rep. Salinas, Sen. Booker Lead Eight Lawmakers in Calling on RV Industry to Remove Deforestation-Linked Timber from Supply Chains

PITTSBURGH, PA – OCTOBER 2, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined community organizers, researchers, environmental advocates, labor leaders, and policymakers at Carnegie Mellon University's Community-Centered AI Infrastructure Summit to call for stronger protections for Pennsylvania communities facing the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centers.

The statewide summit, hosted by Carnegie Mellon University in partnership with Data & Society, the Center for Coalfield Justice, and the Pennsylvania Climate Equity Table, brought together residents and experts to examine the growing demands AI infrastructure places on Pennsylvania's electricity grid, water resources, workforce, and environment. Participants also explored policy solutions and community organizing strategies to inform a Community Action Plan for AI Infrastructure.

Drawing on her experience growing up in the Mon Valley, Rep. Lee warned against repeating the mistakes of Pennsylvania's industrial past, when corporations generated enormous wealth while working-class communities were left to bear the costs of pollution, disinvestment, and broken promises.

“Here in the Pittsburgh area, we have communities that have been similarly sacrificed. I grew up in one of them,” said Rep. Lee. “ We know what it looks like when these choices are made for us, but not with us. I believe that we have to establish regulatory frameworks before we suffer its consequences. Leading on AI doesn't mean building more data centers at any cost or racing toward superintelligence without considering the consequences. It means making sure that AI actually improves life for all of us, not just the CEOs or oligarchs.”

During the summit, Rep. Lee highlighted her cosponsorship of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would temporarily pause new data center construction and the expansion of existing facilities until Congress establishes comprehensive federal safeguards addressing AI's economic, environmental, and safety impacts. She emphasized that the pause must give lawmakers time to establish meaningful protections for communities already facing the consequences of unchecked development.

Rep. Lee called for stronger federal, state, and local regulations to address rising electricity and water costs, establish labor standards, increase community transparency, and account for the cumulative environmental and health impacts of industrial development. Drawing on her visit to Memphis, Tennessee, where residents are organizing against the environmental and noise pollution associated with xAI's data center operations, Rep. Lee warned against repeating the mistakes of Pennsylvania's industrial past and allowing corporations to make decisions that affect communities without their input.

Rep. Lee also connected the expansion of AI infrastructure to broader concerns about civil rights, workers' livelihoods, environmental harms, and corporate influence in Washington. She warned that unchecked AI could reinforce existing discrimination in healthcare, employment, and policing, while the communities bearing the environmental and economic costs of its expansion are left without meaningful protections. She also highlighted her Abolish Super PACs Act, arguing that unlimited corporate spending in elections undermines Congress's ability to establish regulations that prioritize the public over corporate profits.

Footage of Rep. Lee’s remarks can be found here.

Rep. Lee has championed legislation to protect communities, workers, and civil rights as artificial intelligence expands. She is a cosponsor of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would temporarily pause new data center construction and expansion until Congress establishes comprehensive federal safeguards addressing AI's economic, environmental, and safety impacts. Alongside Senator Ed Markey, Rep. Lee introduced the Eliminating BIAS Act, which would establish dedicated civil rights offices in federal agencies that use or oversee AI to combat algorithmic discrimination. She also co-leads theAI Civil Rights Act, which would strengthen protections against AI-driven discrimination in housing, healthcare, employment, and other essential services.
title: At CMU Summit, Rep. Summer Lee Calls for Stronger Community Protections as AI Data Centers Expand Across Pennsylvania

Congressman Davis Helps Deliver New 100-Foot Ladder Truck to Williamston Fire Department
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) celebrated the delivery of a new 100-foot aerial ladder truck to the Williamston Fire Department, made possible in part by $1 million in community project funding he secured for the Town of Williamston. Congressman Davis secured the project for federal funding to help replace the department’s aging 1999 Pierce 75-foot ladder truck after nearly 30 years of service, and voted to approve it as part of H.R. 5371, Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-37).
The $1 million investment, delivered through the USDA Rural Development Community Facilities program, helped fund the new custom-built 2026 E-ONE HR 100-foot tandem aerial ladder truck, designated Ladder 26. The Town of Williamston covered the remaining $500,000 for the apparatus. Ladder 26 expands the department’s vertical reach by 25 feet and strengthens its firefighting and emergency response capabilities.
“Behind the wheel of Williamston’s new ladder truck are firefighters who train, prepare, and put themselves in harm’s way to protect their neighbors,” said Congressman Don Davis. “I am proud to have voted and secured $1 million to help deliver this new apparatus, and grateful to the firefighters who answer the call when our community needs them most.”
Congressman Don Davis secured nearly $54 million in Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding for eastern North Carolina through federal appropriations legislation he supported. The funding was included in the Senate amendment to H.R. 7148, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026; H.R. 6938, Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026; and H.R. 5371, Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), a member of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today introduced the Federal Employee Records Relief Act, legislation to help former federal employees obtain missing personnel records, fix administrative errors and navigate their earned benefits. Missing or inaccurate records can delay retirement processing, complicate health coverage and interfere with future employment.

“Federal employees have suffered enough under the Trump administration’s mass firings and attacks on our civil service. They should not have to chase down missing paperwork to document their service and access the benefits they earned,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “My bill would require the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and federal agencies to help former employees get their records, fix errors and get clear answers about their benefits. These public servants deserve better.”

The bill would require OPM, working with former employing agencies, to provide personnel records, correct administrative errors and offer written benefits information and coordination assistance, including information about health coverage continuation options.

Federal employees who separated for any reason on or after January 20, 2025, including retirees, would have four years after enactment to submit requests.

“Too often, federal employees leave government service only to find themselves trapped in bureaucratic limbo, waiting months for agencies and OPM to correct records or process paperwork they need to collect benefits, secure loans, or move on to their next job. This commonsense legislation creates a clear, centralized, and time-limited process to fix those problems so former federal employees are not forced to keep paying the price for administrative failures that are beyond their control,” said the National Federation of Federal Employees.

“Mass firings and pressure campaigns to force out federal employees have thrown thousands of dedicated civil servants into chaos. Now many are left hanging, trapped by botched personnel records and processing delays that stand between them and their next job, their retirement, and the benefits they earned. The Federal Employee Records Relief Act will give these workers a clear path to correct their records and move forward with their lives. NTEU applauds Rep. Walkinshaw for his work on this bill and for standing up for federal employees and their families,” said Doreen Greenwald, National President, National Treasury Employees Union.

Original cosponsors include Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D.C.), Don Beyer (VA-08), Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05), Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), Glenn Ivey (MD-04) and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).

Read the bill text here.

title: Walkinshaw Introduces Bill to Fix Personnel Record Errors Delaying Federal Workers’ Retirement and Benefits

The Lawmakers Also Renewed Their Call for Trump to Release the Transcript of His 2019 Call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Following Khashoggi’s Murder

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representatives Eugene Vindman (Va.-07), James Walkinshaw (Va.-11), Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) released the following statement on the eighth anniversary of the murder of Jamal Khashoggi.

“Eight years ago today, Virginia resident and journalist Jamal Khashoggi was brutally murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. His murder was an unconscionable attack on a journalist and a Virginia resident, and his family and the American people deserve the full truth about what happened and what followed.

“That includes transparency about President Trump’s 2019 call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Congressman Vindman reviewed the transcript of that call while serving as a lawyer on the National Security Council, and we believe the American people deserve to see it for themselves.

“As members of Virginia’s congressional delegation, we will continue pressing for the transparency and accountability that this case demands. If President Trump will not release the transcript now, we will force him to do it in the next Congress when Democrats are in charge.

“Eight years is far too long to wait for answers. President Trump should declassify and release the transcript and give the Khashoggi family and the American people the truth they deserve.”

BACKGROUND

Jamal Khashoggi, a Washington Post journalist and U.S. resident, was murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in October 2018 — an assassination that drew global condemnation and raised serious questions about Saudi Arabia’s leadership and the Trump administration’s response.

In November 2025, Vindman demanded that the White House release the transcript of a “shocking” 2019 call that took place between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman following Khashoggi’s murder. Vindman reviewed this call while serving as a staff lawyer on Trump’s National Security Council.

That same month, he led 37 lawmakers in sending a letter to President Trump calling for the immediate release of the transcript. He also hosted a press conference alongside Hanan Elatr Khashoggi — Khashoggi’s wife — and U.S. Representatives Jamie Raskin (Md.-08) and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-11) to urge President Trump to release the transcript of the call.

In October 2025, Congressman Walkinshaw and Senators Kaine and Warner introduced a bicameral resolution commemorating the seventh anniversary of Khashoggi’s murder and calling for accountability. The resolution also called for the Government of Saudi Arabia to release wrongfully detained individuals, respect the rights of Saudi citizens, and ensure the protection of the freedoms of assembly, association, and the press.

Khashoggi was a resident of Virginia’s 11th District, which was formerly represented by the late Congressman Gerry Connolly and is now represented by Walkinshaw.

###
title: Vindman, Virginia Democrats Release Statement on 8th Anniversary of Jamal Khashoggi’s Murder

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, amplió al sector hospitalario la discusión sobre el futuro de Medicaid en Puerto Rico durante su participación en la Convención de la Asociación de Hospitales, donde abordó los cambios que enfrenta el programa a partir de 2027 y la necesidad de que Puerto Rico llegue preparado a la próxima etapa de discusión en el Congreso.

El Comisionado Residente destacó que las decisiones que se tomen en Washington tendrán consecuencias directas sobre la estabilidad del sistema de salud, incluyendo la capacidad de los hospitales para sostener sus operaciones, retener profesionales de la salud y garantizar acceso a servicios de calidad para los pacientes.

“Nuestra prioridad es atender lo básico, y la salud es parte de eso. Trabajamos más allá de líneas partidistas para extender los fondos del Plan Vital.El 23 de septiembre reunimos en el Congreso a expertos, personal congresional y representantes del sector de la salud para discutir los retos que tenemos por delante, y el 25 de septiembre nos reunimos con la gobernadora y el grupo multisectorial en La Fortaleza para revisar los datos y afinar la propuesta que llevaremos a Washington. El 2027 está cada vez más cerca y queremos llegar a esa discusión preparados, con una agenda clara y con una propuesta sustentada en datos. En asuntos como este, la salud de los puertorriqueños no tiene colores políticos”, expresó el comisionado residente.

Durante su participación, el Comisionado Residente explicó que Puerto Rico enfrenta una estructura de Medicaid distinta a la de los estados, particularmente por el tope anual al financiamiento federal. Bajo la ley vigente, el porcentaje de participación federal también está programado para reducirse de 76% a 55% a partir del 1 de octubre de 2027, mientras que la asignación federal bajo la Sección 1108 enfrenta una reducción significativa al culminar las asignaciones temporeras.

Estos cambios coinciden en el tiempo y crean lo que se ha denominado el precipicio de Medicaid de 2027, un escenario que requiere atención y planificación antes de que comiencen a materializarse sus efectos.

Como parte de la discusión, el comisionado residente presentó la necesidad de evaluar una estructura de financiamiento más estable para el programa, incluyendo una propuesta para el próximo Congreso que eliminaría el tope de la Sección 1108 y permitiría que el financiamiento federal continúe respondiendo a los gastos elegibles de Medicaid, como ocurre en los estados, sujeto al límite estatutario aplicable al porciento de participación federal.

La conversación con el sector hospitalario también incluyó otros asuntos que inciden sobre la estabilidad del sistema de salud, entre ellos Medicare Advantage, la retención de profesionales, los hospitales y centros de salud 330, la salud mental, la prevención, la investigación, la salud materna y los servicios comunitarios.

El Comisionado Residente repasó además las gestiones que ha realizado durante los últimos meses para fortalecer la coordinación entre el gobierno de Puerto Rico, el sector de salud y los interlocutores en Washington. Entre estas se encuentran sus reuniones con funcionarios federales y congresistas, su testimonio ante el Comité de Energía y Comercio de la Cámara de Representantes, la coordinación de esfuerzos bipartidistas sobre Medicare Advantage y las reuniones recientes con la gobernadora y representantes del sector de salud para revisar datos y recomendaciones de política pública.

De cara al próximo Congreso, el comisionado residente señaló la importancia de que Puerto Rico llegue a Washington con información sólida sobre costos, utilización de servicios, necesidades de los pacientes y las condiciones que enfrentan los proveedores de salud.

La participación ante la Asociación de Hospitales forma parte de los esfuerzos de el Comisionado Residente para mantener la discusión sobre Medicaid y Medicare Advantage conectada con los hospitales, profesionales y demás sectores que sostienen diariamente el sistema de salud de Puerto Rico.

###
title: Comisionado Residente amplía la discusión del futuro de Medicaid al sector hospitalario

The Department of the Interior today announced the designation of Whittier, Alaska, as an American World War II Heritage City, recognizing the community’s extraordinary contributions to the nation’s World War II home front and its ongoing commitment to preserving that history.

“The Department of the Interior is honored to designate Whittier, Alaska as one of the 2026 American World War II Heritage Cities in recognition of its vital contributions to securing our Allied victory and steadfast dedication to preserving this important chapter in American history,” said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum . “By recognizing this region, the Trump administration is reaffirming our nation's commitment to preserving the legacy of the United States' involvement in World War II and ensuring that the sacrifices, services and contributions of those who served and the communities that supported them will be remembered, both locally and nationally, for generations to come.”

Whittier’s nomination highlighted its vital strategic role in the defense of Alaska during World War II, when the U.S. Army transformed a remote site on Prince William Sound into a secret major military port and transportation hub. Chosen for its deep, ice-free harbor and the natural protection of surrounding mountains, Whittier provided a second, strategically located military port that relieved pressure on the more vulnerable commercial port of Seward and provided a more secure route for moving wartime supplies into Alaska.

Beginning in 1941, the U.S. Army constructed a railroad connection through the Chugach Mountains, including a tunnel through Mynard Mountain, as well as docks, warehouses, rail yards and other essential facilities to move troops, fuel, equipment and war materiel into Alaska. When the rail connection was completed in 1943, Whittier emerged as a principal entry point for military personnel and supplies supporting the defense of Alaska and the Aleutian Campaign.

“The community of Whittier would not exist if it were not for World War II and the U.S. Army's decision to utilize its strategic location. Today, the port of Whittier supports over 700,000 visitors and remains a major logistics hub for Alaska," said Kara Moriarty, Senior Advisor to the Secretary of the Interior for Alaska Affairs . “This designation appropriately recognizes how Alaskans, through military service, wartime construction and industrial production, strengthened the war effort and continue to defend our freedoms today.”

The community that developed from this massive wartime undertaking remains a tangible reminder of the scale, ingenuity and strategic importance of Alaska’s role in World War II. Today, Whittier’s preserved World War II structures, historical markers and local museum continue to interpret and honor this significant chapter in American history.

About the American World War II Heritage City Program

Administered by the National Park Service, the American World War II Heritage City Program was signed into law by President Donald J. Trump in March 2019 as part of the John D. Dingell Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act (S. 47). The program recognizes communities for their contributions to the World War II home front and helps preserve the history of U.S. involvement in the war. It authorizes the secretary of the interior to bestow the honorary designation on only one city or local jurisdiction in each state and territory.

Since 2020, designations have been made in 38 states and one territory, strengthening public understanding of the war’s local impacts and advancing preservation of historically significant sites.

Nominate Your City

Any city or other local jurisdiction in a state without an existing designation, is eligible for this recognition. Nominations must be submitted by the highest locally elected official.

Nominations will open in early 2027. For more information, including program information and nomination guidance, please visit the American World War II Heritage Cities Program webpage.

The Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (R&E), through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies (CT), has announced an agreement to partner with the Central Intelligence Agency and In-Q-Tel (IQT), a not-for-profit strategic investor that has served the national security community since 1999.
The partnership gives the Department's research and engineering enterprise structured access to IQT's global technology-scouting platform and its portfolio of early-stage companies, with the explicit objective of compressing the timeline to transition and rapidly field mature commercial solutions from non-traditional performers to the warfighter.
The Department of War has mandated six Critical Technology Areas (CTAs) as the focus of its investment and transition efforts: Applied Artificial Intelligence, Biomanufacturing, Contested Logistics Technologies, Quantum and Battlefield Information Dominance, Scaled Directed Energy, and Scaled Hypersonics. Under the agreement, IQT will conduct technology scouting and technical due diligence across all six CTAs, as well as across enabling technology areas, while the Department identifies transition sponsors and pathways for validated technologies.
"In a contested global threat environment, technological superiority will not be determined by who invents a capability first, but by who delivers it to the warfighter fastest. The Department is fundamentally shifting its posture: we are moving from acting solely as a long-cycle technology developer to operating as an agile, credible, and rapid customer for America's most innovative non-traditional performers. Our partnership with In-Q-Tel eliminates bureaucratic friction across our six CTAs. Over the next 12 months, our benchmark for success is simple and unambiguous: moving validated commercial prototypes out of the lab and into active operational field evaluations with our combatant commands," said Hon. Michael Dodd, Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies.
The integration leverages In-Q-Tel's proven venture capital methodology to vet early-stage commercial solutions that align directly with the Department's urgent mission requirements. By combining CT's strategic transition pathways with IQT's deep-tech scouting infrastructure, the partnership aims to significantly de-risk the integration of commercial hardware and software for national security applications, signaling to the commercial tech sector that the Department of War is open for business.
Joint pilot programs under this new partnership will begin in the coming weeks, targeting immediate battlefield bottlenecks. By aligning IQT's venture ecosystem with the Department's rapid transition pipelines, both organizations aim to establish a permanent bridge that converts commercial ingenuity into deployed military capability at the speed of relevance.
title: Department of War's Critical Technologies Office Partners With In-Q-Tel to Accelerate Technology From Non-Traditional Performers to the Warfighter

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Greg Casar (D-TX), Ranking Member of the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) sent a letter demanding answers and transparency from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel on the FBI’s planned increase of mass surveillance systems, such as Flock.

In May 2026, the FBI issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to acquire automatic license plate readers (ALPR) systems, including Flock and Motorola Solutions, that offer the ability to search for license plate information “and other descriptive data such as vehicle description information, time/date criteria, and geo-location criteria.” Flock and Motorola Solutions, whose ALPR systems are used by local police departments, likely possess the capabilities to satisfy this RFP. While the FBI already runs a License Plate Reader (LPR) program through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) to facilitate LPR information sharing with and between its law enforcement partners, the FBI’s plan to obtain direct access to an extensive network of cameras—such as those operated by Flock and Motorola—would dramatically expand the license plate data currently held by the FBI and institute “near real time” surveillance of civilians.

The Members of Congress write: “The American people are clearly concerned about law enforcement having access to Flock data and about government surveillance more broadly. Entering into a contract that would give the nation’s largest law enforcement agency access to Flock data across the country would subvert the clear preference of the American people.”

The Oversight and Government Reform Committee Democrats are requesting information by October 16, 2026.

Read the full letter here.

###

Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.
title: Casar, Brown Demand Answers on FBI’s Plan to Buy Flock Cameras and Other Mass Surveillance Systems

WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury applauded the release of the 2026 update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy from the Financial Literacy and Education Commission (FLEC), which is chaired by the Secretary of the Treasury and is composed of the heads of 23 federal agencies and the White House Domestic Policy Council.
“The newest United States National Strategy for Financial Literacy is a roadmap to help every American build the knowledge and skills needed to achieve financial security for themselves and their families,” said Secretary Scott Bessent. “The advent of Trump Accounts demonstrates what this approach looks like in practice. By giving young Americans and their families an opportunity to save and invest together, we can make financial education tangible, help a new generation establish sound financial habits from an early age, and build the knowledge and confidence to participate in our financial markets.”
2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy
The Financial Literacy Strategy outlines the FLEC’s goals for advancing financial literacy and education across the United States and identifies priority areas and actions to help Americans build the knowledge and skills to make informed financial decisions, achieve their financial goals, and enhance their financial well-being.
The Financial Literacy Strategy establishes four priority areas for the FLEC:
- Youth Financial Capability: Build a foundation of basic financial skills starting in childhood and young adulthood to improve financial outcomes for the next generation of Americans.
- Saving and Investing: Increase Americans’ knowledge of saving and investing to build financial security and achieve their financial goals, including by promoting awareness of new savings and investment vehicles such as Trump Accounts for children.
- Digital Financial Literacy: Improve Americans’ knowledge and decision-making skills to enable the safe and confident use of digital financial products and services.
- Scams and Fraud Education: Equip consumers with the knowledge to recognize and avoid scams and fraud and the tools to mitigate the impact of potential losses.
The Financial Literacy Strategy also identifies best practices for delivering effective financial education, including providing actionable and timely education at key financial decision points, tailoring education to life stages and individual situations, reinforcing concepts over time, incorporating experiential and hands-on learning, supporting high-quality instruction, and evaluating program effectiveness.
The Financial Literacy Strategy was developed through consultation with FLEC-represented agencies, public input, and independent research on financial literacy and education.
Read Secretary Bessent’s letter as Chair of the Financial Literacy and Education Commission available here.
Read the full 2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy available here.
The Financial Literacy and Education Commission
The Financial Literacy and Education Commission (FLEC) was established by the Financial Literacy and Education Improvement Act, Title V of the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act of 2003 (P.L. 108-159). It provides a forum for its represented Federal entities to continue coordination and collaboration that advance financial literacy and education andincrease access to financial services for all Americans. FLEC-represented agencies develop consumer-friendly, trustworthy, and consistent educational materials and tools; conduct outreach to help consumers make informed and sound decisions that enhance their financial well-being; coordinate and implement research; and develop and implement policies to improve how financial education is delivered.
Learn more about FLEC and financial literacy resources at mymoney.gov.
###
title: The Financial Literacy and Education Commission Releases the 2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

October 2, 2026

Today’s designations by the U.S. Department of the Treasury target a Hamas military operative in Gaza and a France-based fundraising network that used sham charities and cryptocurrency to collect nearly $2 million for Hamas in recent years.

This action underscores the enduring U.S. commitment to dismantling Hamas’s global support networks and denying the group the resources it needs to plan and carry out terrorism that threatens the security of Americans, our partners, and the broader Middle East. It reflects close coordination between the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, and the FBI to expose how Hamas exploits humanitarian and charitable structures abroad to disguise terrorist financing as legitimate aid work.

The United States will continue working with partner governments, including France, to identify and hold accountable individuals and organizations that provide Hamas cover to raise and transfer funds internationally. Disrupting these networks is central to broader U.S. efforts to isolate Hamas, protect the integrity of legitimate humanitarian assistance to Gazan civilians, and support conditions for lasting regional stability.

We are committed to ensuring that humanitarian aid can be delivered by reliable and safe organizations that advance legitimate Palestinian interests and lasting peace in the region.

Today’s designations were issued pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886, the United States’ core counterterrorism sanctions authority. On October 31, 2001, the U.S. Department of State designated Hamas pursuant to E.O. 13224 for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals, or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States. Hamas is also designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release .

title: United States Cuts Off Hamas Financing Network
